67\. For the destruction of Dakṣa’s sacrifice, the crores of his attendants were ordered; and also the evil demons, the followers of Gajānana, the spirits, ghosts and fiends (were ordered).

## \|\| 5.68 \|\|

*tairgatvā vibudhāssarve yajñe nirjitya nāśitāḥ \|*  
*hate yajñe tadā dakṣo nirutsāho nirudyamaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Having gone (to the place of the sacrifice) they vanquished all gods; caused them to flee. When the sacrifice was destroyed, Dakṣa became devoid of energy and inactive.

## \|\| 5.69-70 \|\|

*upagamyābravīttrasto devadevaṃ pinākinam \|*  
*na jñātosi mayā deva devānāṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tvamasya jagatodhīśaḥ surāssarve tvayā jitāḥ \|*  
*kṛpāṃ kuru maheśāna gaṇānsarvānnivarttaya \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Being alarmed, he approached Śaṅkara, the god of gods, and said to him: “I did not know your true character as the lord and master of the gods. You are the lord of this world, and gods are conquered by you. O great lord, favour me and withdraw all your attendants.

## \|\| 5.71-77 \|\|

*gaṇairnānāvidhairghorairnānābhūṣaṇabhūṣitaiḥ \|*  
*nānāvadanadaṃtauṣṭhairnānā praharaṇodyataiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*nānā nāgeṃdrasaṃdaṣṭa jaṭābhāropaśobhitaiḥ \|*  
*sudṛḍhoddhata darpāḍhyairghorairghoranighātibhiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*kāmarūpairakāṃtaiśca sarvakāmasamanvitaiḥ \|*  
*anivāryabalaiścograiryogibhiryogagāmibhiḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*vyālolakesarajaṭairdaṃṣṭrotkaṭahasanmukhaiḥ \|*  
*karīṃdrakaraṭāṭopa pāṭavaiḥ siṃhadehibhiḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*kecitparamadāghrāṇa ghūrṇaddīpasamaprabhaiḥ \|*  
*vicitracitravasanairddhīradhīravāradibhiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*mṛgavyāghrasiṃharutaistarakṣvajinadhāribhiḥ \|*  
*bhujaṃgahāravalayakṛtayajñopavītakaiḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śūlāsipaṭṭiśadharaiḥ paraśuprāsahastakaiḥ \|*  
*vajrakrakacakodaṃḍakāladaṃḍāstrapāṇibhiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

71-77. The sacrifice has gone to the heaven after being caused to fly away by your brave attendants of various kinds, of various mouths, teeth and lips, ready with various kinds of weapons, shining with matted hair, being bitten (i.e. touched) by many great serpents, full of intense and excessive pride, terrible, and hitting terribly, taking forms according to their desire, ugly-looking, having all desires, having invincible power, fearful, having armours, and moving trickishly, having unsteady matted hair, their laughing faces looking fierce due to the fangs, having great energy like the cheeks of elephants (?), having bodies like lions, and some of them stinking with madness and staggering like lamp (-flames) having quivering brilliance. (They are) crying like beasts, tigers, and lions, wearing hides like hyenas, using the wreaths of sepents \[serpents?\] as sacred threads, holding lances, swords and sharp-edged spears, carrying in their hands hatchets and barbed missiles, and destructive weapons, saws, bows and (other) fatal missiles.

## \|\| 5.78 \|\|

*gaṇeśvaraiḥ sudurddharṣairvṛtaḥ sūryo grahairiva \|*  
*devadevamahādeva naṣṭo yajño divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Sacrifice, surrounded by very invincible powerful attendants like the sun with planets, O Śaṅkara, and taking the form of a deer, and being frightened, fled and went to heaven.

## \|\| 5.79-80 \|\|

*mṛgarūpadharo bhūtvā bhayabhītastu śaṃkara \|*  
*namaḥ śaṅkhābhadevāya sagaṇāya sanaṃdine \|\| 79 \|\|*

*vṛṣāsanāya somāya kratukālāṃtakāya ca \|*  
*namo dikcarmavastrāya namaste tīvratejase \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. My saluation to the god resembling a conch, accompanied by his attendants, and by Nandi. My salutation to Soma, seated on a bull, and the destroyer of the sacrifice and time, and to him having the quarters as his garments, and to him of strong lustre.

## \|\| 5.81-87 \|\|

*brahmaṇe brahmadehāya brahmaṇyāyāmitāya ca \|*  
*girīśāya sureśāya īśānāya namonamaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*rudrāya prativajrāya śivāya krathanāya ca \|*  
*surāsurādhipataye yatīnāṃ pataye namaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*dhūmrogrāya virūpāya yajvane ghorarūpiṇe \|*  
*virūpākṣāśubhākṣāya sahasrākṣāya vai namaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*muṃḍāya caṃḍamuṇḍāya varakhaṭvāṅgadhāriṇe \|*  
*kavyarūpāya havyāya sarvasaṃhāriṇe namaḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*bhaktānukaṃpinetyarthaṃ rudrajāpyastutāya ca \|*  
*virūpāya surūpāya rūpāṇāṃ śatakāriṇe \|\| 85 \|\|*

*paṃcāsyāya śubhāsyāya caṃdrāsyāya namo namaḥ \|*  
*varadāya varārhāya kūrmāya ca mṛgāya ca \|\| 86 \|\|*

*līlālakaśikhaṃḍāya kamaṃḍaludharāya ca \|*  
*viśvanāmnetha viśvāya viśveśāya namonamaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

81-87. My salutation to Brahmā, Brahmaṇya, having the body of Brahmā, to the unlimited one, to Girīśa, to the lord of gods, and to Īśāna, to Rudra, to him resembling the thunderbolt, to Śiva, to Krathana, to the lord of the gods, and of demons and sages; to Dhūmogra, Virūpa, Yajvan, to the one of a fearful form, to Virūpākṣa, Aśubhākṣa, and Sahasrākṣa; to Muṇḍa, Caṇḍamuṇḍa, the holder of an excellent club with a skull at the top, to Kavyarūpa, Havya, and the destroyer of all; my salutation to (the lord), compassionate to his devotees and to him praised by the muttered prayer (addressed) to Rudra; to Virūpa, Sarūpa, to him who takes hundreds of forms; my salutation to Pañcāsya, Śubhāsya and Candrāsya, to the giver of boons, to Varāha, to Kūrma and to Mṛga; to him having a sportive lock of hair, and to the holder of a water-pot, to Viśvanāman, to Viśva and to Viśveśa.

## \|\| 5.88 \|\|

*trinetratrāṇamasmākaṃ tripuraghnavidhīyatāṃ \|*  
*vāṅmanaḥ kāyabhāvaistu prapannasya maheśvara \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O three-eyed one, O destroyer of Tripura, give protection to us (and to me) who have taken refuge in you, through sincerity of speech, mind and body.”

## \|\| 5.89 \|\|

*evaṃ stutastadā devo dakṣeṇāpannadehinā \|*  
*divyenānena stotreṇa bhṛśamārādhitastadā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. The lord, thus praised by Dakṣa, with his body afflicted, and propitiated very much with this divine eulogy (said):

## \|\| 5.90 \|\|

*samagraṃ te yajñaphalaṃ mayā dattaṃ prajāpate \|*  
*sarvakāmaprasirddhythaṃphalaṃprāpsyasyanuttamam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. “O Prajapati, I have given you the entire fruit of the sacrifice. You will get its excellent fruit leading to the accomplishment of all (your) desires.”

## \|\| 5.91 \|\|

*evamukto bhagavatā praṇamyātha sureśvaram \|*  
*jagāma svaniketaṃ tu gaṇānāmeva paśyatām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Thus addressed by the lord, Dakṣa, having saluted the lord of gods, and being watched by śiva’s attendants, went to his residence.

## \|\| 5.92 \|\|

*patnyāḥ śokena vai devo gaṃgādvāre tadāsthitaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ satīṃ ciṃtayānastu kva nu sāmepriyāgatā \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. (And) then the lord, due to the grief for his wife Satī, and thinking of her—‘Where has (my) beloved gone?’—remained at Gaṅgādvāra.

## \|\| 5.93 \|\|

*tasya śokābhibhūtasya nārado bhavasaṃnnidhau \|*  
*sā te satī yā deveśa bhāryā prāṇasamāmṛtā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Nārada approached him who was overpowered by grief. (He said): “O lord of gods, that Satī, your wife, is dead.

## \|\| 5.94 \|\|

*himavadduhitā sā ca menāgarbhasamudbhavā \|*  
*jagrāha dehamanyaṃ sā vedavedārthavedinī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. She, the knower of the Vedas and their significance, has taken up another body as the daughter of Himavat, born from the womb of Mena.”

## \|\| 5.95 \|\|

*śrutvā devastadā dhyānamavatīrṇāmapaśyata \|*  
*kṛtakṛtyamathātmānaṃ kṛtvā devastadāsthitaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Having heard this, the lord saw her descending into his meditation. Regarding himself blessed, the lord then remained (there).

## \|\| 5.96 \|\|

*saṃprāptayauvanā devī punareva vivāhitā \|*  
*evaṃ hi kathitaṃ bhīṣma yathā yajño hataḥ purā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Attaining youth, the goddess married again. Thus, O Bhīṣma, I have told you how the Sacrifice perished in olden times.

## Chapter 6 - Birth of Devas, Daityas, Birds and Serpents etc.

## \|\| 6.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca gaṃdharvoragarakṣasām \|*  
*utpattiṃ vistareṇemāṃ guro brūhi yathāvidhi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. O sire, tell me duly and in detail, about the birth of gods, demons and of the Gandharvas, serpents and goblins.

Pulastya spoke:

## \|\| 6.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*saṃkalpāddarśanātsparśātpūrveṣāṃ sṛṣṭirucyate \|*  
*dakṣātprācetasādūrdhvaṃ sṛṣṭirmaithunasaṃbhavā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The creation in ancient times is said to be effected by volition, sight and touch; (but) the creation after Prācetasa Dakṣa is effected by coitus.

## \|\| 6.3-4 \|\|

*yathā sasarja caivāsau tathaiva śṛṇu kaurava \|*  
*yadā tu sṛjatastasya devarṣigaṇapannagān \|\| 3 \|\|*

*na vṛddhimagamallokastadā maithunayogataḥ \|*  
*dakṣaḥ putrasahasrāṇi tadāsiknyāmajījanat \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Listen, O Kaurava, as to how he created (gods etc.): When he was creating groups of gods, sages and serpents, the world did not grow. So Dakṣa generated thousands of sons on his young maid-servant.

## \|\| 6.5-6 \|\|

*tāṃstu dṛṣṭvā mahābhāgānsisṛkṣūnvividhāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*nāradaḥ prāha haryaśvāndakṣaputrānsamāgatān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvorddhamadha eva vā \|*  
*tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ viśeṣeṇa kurudhvamṛṣisattamāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Seeing those magnanimous ones (i.e. Dakṣa’s sons), desiring to create various kinds of beings, Nārada said to Dakṣa’s sons who approached him:

“O you best sages, knowing the entire measure of the earth up and down, you should (proceed to) create with discrimination.”

## \|\| 6.7 \|\|

*te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvatodiśam \|*  
*adyāpi na nivarttaṃte samudrādiva siṃdhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Having heard these words, they went in all directions; and even now have not returned as rivers from the sea.

## \|\| 6.8 \|\|

*haryaśveṣu praṇaṣṭeṣu punardakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vīriṇyāmeva putrāṇāṃ sahasramasṛjatprabhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. When Haryaśvas had disappeared, Dakṣa Prajāpati again produced a thousand sons on Vīriṇī.

## \|\| 6.9-10 \|\|

*śabalāśvā nāma te ca sametāḥ sṛṣṭikarmaṇi \|*  
*nāradonugatānprāha punastānpūrvavanmuniḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvā bhrātṝnatho punaḥ \|*  
*āgatya ca punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Those (sons) named Śabalāśva gathered in the act of creation. To them, who went after (i.e. approached) Nārada, the sage told as before:

“Having known the entire extent of the earth, and coming back, you will especially undertake the creation.”

## \|\| 6.11 \|\|

*tepi tenaiva mārgeṇa jagmurbhrātranugāstadā \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti na bhrātuḥ kanīyānmārgamicchati \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. They followed their brothers along the same path. Since then a younger brother does not desire(to follow) the path of the (elder) brother.

## \|\| 6.12-16 \|\|

*anveṣṭā duḥkhamāpnoti tena tatparivarjayet \|*  
*tatasteṣvapi naṣṭeṣu ṣaṣṭiṃ kanyāḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vīriṇyāṃ janayāmāsa dakṣaḥ prācetasastadā \|*  
*prādātsa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa \|\| 13 \|\|*

*viṃśatisapta somāya catasroriṣṭanemine \|*  
*dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dve caivāṃgirase prādāttāsāṃ nāmāni vistarāt \|*  
*śṛṇu tvaṃ devamātṝṇāṃ prajāvistāramāditaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aruṃdhatī vasurjāmirlambā bhānurmarutvatī \|*  
*saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. The one who follows, gets into trouble; therefore, one should avoid it. When they too disappeared, Prācetasa Dakṣa Prajāpati generated sixty daughters on Vīriṇī. He gave (in marriage) ten (daughters) to Dharma, and thirteen to Kaśyapa, twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi, two to Bhṛgu’s son, two to intelligent Kṛśāśva, and gave two to Aṅgiras. Hear in detail the names of these mothers of gods and the expanse of mankind from the beginning: Arundhatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, Saṅkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādehyā, and the beautiful Viśvā.

## \|\| 6.17 \|\|

*dharmapatnyaḥ samākhyātāstāsāṃ putrānnibodha me \|*  
*viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyā sādhyānajījanat \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. These are known to be the wives of Dharma. Know from me their sons; Viśvedevas were (the sons) of Viśvā, and Sādhyā gave birth to Sādhyas.

## \|\| 6.18 \|\|

*marutvatyāṃ marutvaṃto vasostu vasavastathā \|*  
*bhānostu bhānavo jātā mūhūrttāyā muhūrtajāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Marutvāns were born of Marutvatī, and Vasavas of Vasu; Bhānus of Bhānu and Muhūrtajas of Muhūrtā.

## \|\| 6.19 \|\|

*laṃbāyāṃ ghoṣanāmāno nāgavīthī tu jāmijā \|*  
*pṛthivītalasaṃbhūtamaruṃdhatyāmajāyata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Those known as Ghoṣa were born of Lambā and Nāgavīthīs were born of Jāmī. Pṛthvītala and Sambhūta were born of Arundhatī.

## \|\| 6.20-23 \|\|

*saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpā vasu sṛṣṭiṃ nidhāraya \|*  
*jyotiṣmataṃśca ye devā vyāpakāḥ sarvatodiśam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vasavaste samākhyātāsteṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu \|*  
*āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivānilonalaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavoṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*āpasya putrāścatvāraḥ śrāṃto vaitaṇḍa eva ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*api śāṃto munirvabhruryajñarakṣādhikāriṇaḥ \|*  
*dhruvasya kālaḥ putrastu varcāḥ somādajāyata \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. Saṃkalpas were born of Saṃkalpā. Understand (now) the progeny of Vasu. Gods, bright and pervading all quarters, are called Vasus. Hear their names from me: Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, Pratyūṣa and Prabhāsa are known as the eight Vasus. Āpa had four sons: Śrānta, Vaitaṇḍa and Śānta and the sage Babhru—(they were) the officers protecting the sacrifice. Kāla was the son of Dhruva, and Varcas was born from Soma.

## \|\| 6.24-25 \|\|

*draviṇo havyavāhaśca dhara putrāvimau smṛtau \|*  
*kalpāṃtasthastataḥ prāṇo ramaṇaḥ śiśiropi ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*manoharo dhavaścātha śivo vātha hareḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*śivo manojavaṃ putramavijñātagatipradam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Draviṇa and Havyavāha—these two are said to be the sons of Dhara. Hari’s sons were: Kalpāntastha and Prāṇa, Ramaṇa and also Śiśira, as well as the charming Dhava and Śiva. Śiva obtained a son, having the mind’s speed and giving (causing) unknown speed.

## \|\| 6.26 \|\|

*avāpa cānalaḥ putrānagniprāyaguṇāṃstataḥ \|*  
*tatra śākho viśākhaśca nigameṣu svayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Anala also obtained sons like Śākha, Viśākha—self-existent in (supreme authorities on?) the Vedas—having mostly the qualities of fire.

## \|\| 6.27 \|\|

*apatyaṃ kṛttikānāṃ ca kārtikeyastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pratyūṣasya ṛbhuḥ putro munirnāmātha devalaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then Kārtikeya was known to be the child of the Kṛttikās. Ṛbhu, Muni and Devala were the sons of Pratyūṣa.

## \|\| 6.28-34 \|\|

*viśvakarmā prabhāsasya putraḥ śilpī prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*prāsādabhavanodyāna pratimā bhūṣaṇādiṣu \|\| 28 \|\|*

*taṭākārāmakūpeṣu tridaśānāṃ ca varddhakiḥ \|*  
*ajaikapādahirbudhnyo virūpākṣotha raivataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*haraśca bahurūpaśca tryaṃbakaśca sureśvaraḥ \|*  
*sāvittraśca jayaṃtaśca pinākī cāparājitaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ete rudrāssamākhyātā ekādaśa gaṇeśvarāḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ mānasānāṃ tu triśūlavaradhāriṇām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*koṭyaścaturaśītistu tatputrāścākṣayā matāḥ \|*  
*dikṣu sarvāsu ye rakṣāṃ prakurvanti gaṇeśvarāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ete vai putrapautrāśca surabhīgarbhasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*kaśyapasya pravakṣyāmi putrapautrādi patniṣu \|\| 33 \|\|*

*aditirditirdanuścaiva ariṣṭā surasā tathā \|*  
*surabhirvinatā caiva tāmrā krodhavaśā irā \|\| 34 \|\|*

28-34. Viśvakarmā Prajāpati was the son of Prabhāsa. He was an architect (skilled) in (fashioning) palaces, houses, gardens, images, ornaments, lakes, parks and wells; he also was the carpenter of gods. Ajaikapāda, Ahirbudhnya, Virūpākṣa, Raivata, Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka the lord of gods, Sāvitra, Jayanta, Pinākin, and Aparājita—these eleven, the lords of (Śiva’s) attendants, are called Rudra. These mind-born ones and holders of tridents are said to have eighty-four crores of imperishable sons, who, being the principal attendants in all the directions, protect; these are the sons and grandsons born from the womb of Surabhi. I shall name the sons and grandsons of Kaṣyapa’s wives: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Ariṣṭā, Surasā, Surabhi, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā, Irā, Kadrū, Khasā, and Muni.

## \|\| 6.35-39 \|\|

*kadrū khasā munistadvattāsu putrānnibodha me \|*  
*tuṣitā nāma ye devāścākṣuṣasyāṃtare manoḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*vaivasvateṃtare caiva ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*indro dhātā bhagastvaṣṭā mittro'tha varuṇo'ryamā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vivasvānsavitā pūṣā aṃśumānviṣṇureva ca \|*  
*ete sahasrakiraṇā ādityā dādvaśa smṛtāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mārīcātkaśyapājjātāḥ puttrāste'ditinaṃdanāḥ \|*  
*kṛśāśvasya ṛṣeḥ putrā devapraharaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ete devagaṇāstāta pratimanvaṃtareṣu ca \|*  
*utpadyaṃte vilīyaṃte kalpekalpe tathaiva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

35-39. Hear now the (names of the) sons born from them: Those gods who were known as Tuṣita in the period of Cākṣuṣa Manu were known as the twelve Ādityas in the Vaivasvata period. Indra, Dhātā, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭā, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Vivasvān, Savitā, Pūṣan, Aṃśumān, and Viṣṇu—these twelve are thousand-rayed Ādityas. From Kaśyapa, the son of Marīca, were born the sons of Aditi. The sons of the sage Kṛśāśva are known as Devapraharaṇa. These groups of gods, O dear one, are born and perish in the Manu-periods and in each Kalpa.

## \|\| 6.40 \|\|

*ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuṃ caiva hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. We have heard that Diti got two sons, Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa, from Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 6.41 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipostadvajjātaṃ putracatuṣṭayam \|*  
*prahlādaścānuhlādaśca saṃhlādohlāda eva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Similarly, four sons were born from Hiraṇyakaśipu: Prahlāda, Anuhlāda, Saṃhlāda, and Uhlāda.

## \|\| 6.42 \|\|

*prahlādaputrā āyuṣmānśibirbāṣkalireva ca \|*  
*virocanaścaturthastu sa baliṃ putramāptavān \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The sons of Prahlāda were Āyuṣmān, Śibi, and Bāṣkali. The fourth son was Virocana by name. He got a son named Bali.

## \|\| 6.43 \|\|

*baleḥ putraśataṃ tvāsīdbāṇajyeṣṭhaṃ tato nṛpa \|*  
*dhṛtarāṣṭrastathāsūryyo vivasvānaṃśutāpanaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. O king, Bali had a hundred sons with Bāṇa as the eldest; and also Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sūrya, Vivasvān and Aṃśutāpana.

## \|\| 6.44 \|\|

*nikumbhanāmā gurvakṣaḥ kukṣirbhaumotha bhīṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*evamanye tu bahavo bāṇojyeṣṭho guṇādhikaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Nikumbha, Nāmāgu, Vakṣa, Kukṣi, Bhauma, and Bhīṣaṇa were many other (sons): but the eldest, viz. Bāṇa was preeminent in virtues.

## \|\| 6.45-47 \|\|

*bāṇassahasrabāhustu sarvāstraguṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*tapasā toṣito yasya pure vasati śūladhṛt \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mahākālatvamagamatsārthyaṃ yasya pinākinaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣasya putrobhūdaṃdhako nāmanāmataḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*bhūtasaṃtāpanaścaiva mahānāgastathaiva ca \|*  
*etebhyaḥ putrapautrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ saptasaptatiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. Bāṇa had a thousand arms, and was endowed with excellence (in the use) of all missiles; and in his city the Trident-holder, pleased by his (i.e. Bāṇa’s) penance lived, and his being the destroyer (Mahākāla) of the world became significant. Hiraṇyākṣa’s son was Andhaka by name. And Bhūtasantāpana, and Mahānāga also were (his sons). From these were born seventy-seven crores of sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 6.48 \|\|

*mahābalā mahākāyā nānārūpā mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*danuḥ putraśataṃ lebhe kaśyapādvaradarpitam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. They were very powerful, had gigantic bodies and many forms and were very vigorous. From Kaśyapa, Danu obtained a hundred sons proud of boons.

## \|\| 6.49-53 \|\|

*vipracittiḥ pradhānobhūdeṣāṃ madhye mahābalaḥ \|*  
*dviraṣṭamūrddhā śakunistathā śaṃkuśirodharaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ayomukhaḥ śaṃbaraśca kapilo vāmanastathā \|*  
*marīcirmāgadhaścaiva harirgajaśirāstathā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*nidrādharaśca ketuśca ketuvīryaḥ śatakratuḥ \|*  
*indramitragrahaścaiva vajranābhastathaiva ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ekavastro mahābāhurvajrākṣastārakastathā \|*  
*asilomā pulomā ca vikurvāṇo mahāsuraḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*svarbhānurvṛṣaparvā ca evamādyā danossutāḥ \|*  
*svarbhānoḥ suprabhā kanyā śacī caiva pulomajā \|\| 53 \|\|*

49-53. Among them Vipracitti, of great power, was the chief. (Others were) Dviraṣṭamūrdhā, Śakuni, Śaṅkuśirodhara, Ayomukha, Śambara, Kapila, Vāmana, Marīci, Māgadha, and Hari. Gajaśiras, Nidrādhara, Ketu, Ketuvīrya Taśakratu, Indramitragraha, Vrajanābha, Ekavastra, Mahābāhu, Vajrākṣa, Tāraka, Asiloman, Puloman, Vikurvāṇa, Mahāpura, Svarbhānu, and Vṛṣaparvan—these and others were also Danu’s sons. Suprabhā was Svarbhānu’s daughter, and Śacī was the daughter of Puloman.

## \|\| 6.54 \|\|

*upadānavī mayasyāsīttathā maṃdodarī kuhūḥ \|*  
*śarmiṣṭhā suṃdarī caiva caṃḍā ca vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Maya’s daughters were Upadānavī, Mandodarī and Kuhū. Vṛṣaparvan’s daughters were Sarmiṣṭhā, Sundarī and Caṇḍā.

## \|\| 6.55 \|\|

*pulomā kālakā caiva vaiśvanarasute ubhe \|*  
*bahvapatyo mahāsatvo mārīcasya parigrahaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Pulomā and Kālakā were the two daughters of Vaiśvānara; Mārīca’s very spirited wife had many children.

## \|\| 6.56 \|\|

*tayoḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi dānavānāṃ purābhavan \|*  
*paulomānkālakhaṃjāṃśca mārīcojanayatpurā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. From the two, sixty-thousand Dānavas were born in olden times; Mārīca generated the Paulomas and Kālakhañjas.

## \|\| 6.57 \|\|

*avadhyā ye narāṇāṃ vai hiraṇyapuravāsinaḥ \|*  
*caturmukhāllabdhavarā ye hatā vijayena tu \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. They, living in Hiraṇyapura, having obtained a boon from Brahmā, were incapable of being killed by men, but were killed by Arjuna.

## \|\| 6.58-60 \|\|

*vipracittiḥ siṃhikāyāṃ nava putrānajījanat \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśiporyevai bhāgineyāstrayodaśa \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kaṃsaḥ śaṃkhaśca rājendra nalo vātāpireva ca \|*  
*ilvalo namuciścaiva khasṛmaścāṃjanastathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*narakaḥ kālanābhaśca paramāṇustathaiva ca \|*  
*kalpavīryaśca vikhyāto danuvaṃśavivarddhanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Vipracitti begot nine sons on Siṃhikā. Hiraṇyakaśipu’s sister’s sons were thirteen: Kaṃsa, Śaṃkha, Rājendra, Nala, Vātāpi, Ilvala, Namuci, Khasṛma, Añjana, Naraka, Kālanābha, Paramāṇu and the well-known Kalpavīrya, who exalted Danu’s race.

## \|\| 6.61-63 \|\|

*saṃhlādasya tu daityasya nivātakavacāḥ kule \|*  
*avadhyāḥ sarvadevānāṃ gaṃdharvoragarākṣasām \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ye hatā balamāśritya arjunena raṇājire \|*  
*ṣaṭkanyā janayāmāsa tāmrā mārīcavīryataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugṛdhrīṃ gṛdhrikāṃ śucim \|*  
*śukī śukānulūkāṃśca janayāmāsa dharmataḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

61-63. In the family of the demon Saṃhlāda, (were) born the Nivātakavacas, incapable of being killed by all gods, Gandharvas, serpents and fiends, (but) who were killed in battle by Arjuna resorting to power. From the semen of Mārīca, Tāmrā gave birth to six daughters: Śukī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugṛdhrī, Gṛdhrikā and Śucī. Śukī lawfully gave birth to parrots and owls.

## \|\| 6.64 \|\|

*śyenī śyenāṃśca bhāsī ca kurarānapyajījanat \|*  
*gṛdhrī gṛdhrānsugṛdhrī ca pārāvatavihaṃgamān \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. śyenī gave birth to hawks and Bhāsī to ospreys, Gṛdhrī to vultures and Sugṛdhrī to birds like pigeons.

## \|\| 6.65-67 \|\|

*haṃsa sārasa kāraṃḍa plavānśucirajījanat \|*  
*ete tāmrāsutāḥ proktā vinatāyā niśāmaya \|\| 65 \|\|*

*garuḍaḥ patagaśreṣṭho'ruṇaśceśaḥ patatriṇām \|*  
*saudāminī tathā kanyā yeyaṃ nabhasi viśrutā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*saṃpātiśca jaṭāyuśca aruṇasya sutāvubhau \|*  
*saṃpātiputro babhruśca śīghragaścātiviśrutaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. Śucī gave birth to swans, cranes and ducks. These are said to be the sons of Tāmrā. Listen to (the names of the offspring) of Vinatā: Garuḍa, the best among birds, and Aruṇa, the lord of birds, and daughter Saudāminī well-known in the sky. Sampāti and Jaṭāyu were the two sons of Aruṇa; Sampāti’s son was Babhru, who was swift and very well-known.

## \|\| 6.68 \|\|

*jaṭāyoḥ karṇikāraśca śatagāmī ca viśrutau \|*  
*teṣāmasaṃkhyamabhavatpakṣiṇāṃ putrapautrakam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Jaṭāyu’s famous sons were Karṇikāra and Śatagāmin. From them innumerable sons and grandsons of birds were born.

## \|\| 6.69 \|\|

*surasāyāṃ sahasraṃ tu sarpāṇāmabhavatpurā \|*  
*sahasraśirasāṃ kadrūḥ sahasraṃ prāpa suvratā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A thousand serpents were formerly born on Surasā. Kadrū, of a good vow, obtained a thousand (sons), the Nāgas.

## \|\| 6.70-74 \|\|

*pradhānāsteṣu vikhyātā ṣṣaḍviṃśatirarindama \|*  
*śeṣavāsukikarkoṭa śaṃkhairāvatakaṃbalāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*dhanaṃjaya mahānīla padmāśvatara takṣakāḥ \|*  
*elāpatra mahāpadma dhṛtarāṣṭra balāhakāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*śaṃkhapāla mahāśaṃkha puṣpadaṃṣṭraṃ śubhānanāḥ \|*  
*śaṃkharomā ca nahuṣo ramaṇaḥ paṇinastathā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*kapilo durmukhaścāpi pataṃjalimukhāstathā \|*  
*eṣāmanaṃtamabhavatsarveṣāṃ putrapautrakam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*prāyaśo yatpurādagdhaṃ janamejayamaṃdire \|*  
*rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā sunāmānamajījanat \|\| 74 \|\|*

70-74. Of them, O subduer of enemies, twenty-six prominent ones are famous: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Karkoṭa, Śaṅkha, Airāvata, Kambala, Dhanañjaya, Mahānīla, Padma, Aśvatara, Takṣaka, Elāpatra, Mahāpadma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Balāhaka, Śaṅkhapāla, Mahāśaṅkha, Puṣpadamṣṭra, Śubhānana, Śaṅkha, Romāca, Nahuṣa, Ramaṇa, Paṇina, Kapila, Durmukha, and Patañjali. These had innumerable sons and grandsons, who were mostly burnt in the abode of Janamejaya. Krodhavaśā gave birth to the well-known group of demons.

## \|\| 6.75-76 \|\|

*daṃṣṭriṇāṃ niyutaṃ teṣāṃ bhīmasenādagātkṣayam \|*  
*daṃṣṭri gomāyu kākādīnmahiṣīrgovarāṅganāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*surabhirjanayāmāsa kaśyapātttritayaṃ purā \|*  
*munirmunīnāṃ ca gaṇaṃ gaṇamapsarasāṃ tathā \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. A lakh of these snakes perished at the hands of Bhīmasena. From Kaśyapa Surabhi formerly gave birth to snakes, jackals, crows etc. and the triad of buffaloes, cows and excellent ladies. Similarly, Muni gave birth to a group of sages and of the celestial nymphs.

## \|\| 6.77 \|\|

*tathā kinnaragaṃdharvānariṣṭā janayadbahūn \|*  
*tṛṇavṛkṣalatā gulmamirā sarvamajījanatat \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. In the same, way, Ariṣṭā gave birth to many Kinnaras and Gandharvas; Irā created all the grass, trees and clumps of creepers.

## \|\| 6.78 \|\|

*khasā tu yakṣarakṣāṃsi janayāmāsa koṭiśaḥ \|*  
*ete kaśyapadāyādāḥ śataśotha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Khasā gave birth to crores of Yakṣas and demons. These hundreds and thousands are Kaśyapa’s relatives.

## \|\| 6.79 \|\|

*eṣa manvaṃtare bhīṣma sargaḥ svārociṣe smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tatastvekonapaṃcāśanmarutaḥ kaśyapādditiḥ \|*  
*janayāmāsa dharmajña sarvānamaravallabhān \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. O Bhīṣma, this is known to be the creation in the Manu-period named Svārociṣa. Then, O you, conversant with religious law, Diti gave birth to forty-nine Maruts, all dear to gods.

## Chapter 7 - Description of Manu Periods

## \|\| 7.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*diteḥ putrāḥ kathaṃ jātā maruto devavallabhāḥ \|*  
*devairjagmuśca sāpatnaiḥ kasmātsakhyamanuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. How did Maruts, the sons of Diti; become dear to gods, and how did they have excellent intimacy with gods?

Pulastya spoke:

## \|\| 7.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*purā daivāsure yuddhe hateṣu hariṇā suraiḥ \|*  
*putrapautreṣu śokārtā gatā bhūlokamuttamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Formerly, in the war between the gods and the demons, when, by Hari and gods, her sons and grandsons were killed, Diti, afflicted with grief, went to the excellent terrestrial globe.

## \|\| 7.3 \|\|

*puṣkareṣu mahātīrthe sarasvatyāstaṭe śubhe \|*  
*bhartturārādhanaparā tapa ugraṃ cacāra ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. At the great sacred place in Puṣkara, on the auspicious bank of the Sarasvatī, Diti the mother of the Daityas, intent upon propitiating her husband, practised a severe penance.

## \|\| 7.4-6 \|\|

*ditirvai daityamātā tu ṛṣikāryeṇa suvratā \|*  
*phalāhārā tapastepe kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yāvadvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ jarāśokasamākulā \|*  
*tataḥ sā tapasā taptā vasiṣṭhādīnapṛcchata \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kathayaṃtu bhavaṃto me putraśokavināśanam \|*  
*vrataṃ saubhāgyaphaladamihaloke paratra ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. She, of a good vow, afflicted with old age and grief, subsisting on fruit, performed fully, for a hundred years, a penance, with vows like Kṛcchra-cāndrāyaṇa, for the sages. Then she, tormented by penance, asked Vasiṣṭha and others: “Tell me a vow that will remove my grief for my sons and will cause good luck in this and the next world”.

## \|\| 7.7 \|\|

*ūcurvasiṣṭhapramukhā jyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāvratam \|*  
*yasya prasādādabhavatsutaśokavivarjitā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Vasiṣṭha and others told (her) about the vow of the full-moon night of Jyeṣṭha, due to the auspiciousness of which she became free from the grief for her sons.

## \|\| 7.8 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*śrotumicchāmyahaṃ brahmanjyeṣṭhasya pūrṇimāvratam \|*  
*sutānekonapaṃcāśadyena lebhe punarditiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

8\. O brāhmaṇa, I wish to hear about the vow of the full-moon of Jyeṣṭha, by which Diti got back her forty-nine sons.

## \|\| 7.9 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*yadvasiṣṭhādibhiḥ pūrvaṃ dityai saṃkathitaṃ vratam \|*  
*vistareṇa tadevedaṃ matsakāśānniśāmaya \|\| 9 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

9\. Hear from me in details the vow which was formerly told by Vasiṣṭha and others to Diti.

## \|\| 7.10-13 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe paurṇamāsyāṃ yatavratā \|*  
*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kuṃbhaṃ sitataṇḍulapūritam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*nānāphalayutaṃ tadvadikṣudaṃḍasamanvitam \|*  
*sitavastrayugacchannaṃsitacaṃdanacarcitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nānābhakṣyasamopetaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ tu śaktitaḥ \|*  
*tāmrapātraṃ guḍopetaṃ tasyopari niveśayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tasmādupari brahmāṇaṃ sauvarṇaṃ padmakoṭare \|*  
*kuryātśarkarayopetāṃ sāvitrīṃ tasya vāmataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. In the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha, on the full-moon day, one, of a pure vow, should place an unbruised pitcher filled with white rice, and having many fruits and sugarcanes, covered with a couple of white clothes, and besmeared with sandal; then one should put on it a copper-vessel, containing gold according to one’s capacity, and various kinds of eatables and jaggery; in a hollow of a lotus, one should instal a golden image of Brahmā. To his (i.e. Brahmā’s) left, one should fashion (the image of) Sāvitri made of sugar.

## \|\| 7.14 \|\|

*gaṃdhaṃdhūpaṃ tayordadyādgītaṃ vādyaṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*tadabhāve kathaṃ kuryādyathā padme pitāmahaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. To them he should offer perfume and incense and have vocal and instrumental music. How can one do it without it since Brahma lives in the lotus?

## \|\| 7.15-18 \|\|

*brahmāhvayāṃ ca pratimāṃ kṛtvā guḍamayīṃ śubhām \|*  
*śuklapuṣpākṣatatilairarcayetpadmasaṃbhavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*brāhmāya pādau saṃpūjya jaṃghe saubhāgyadāya ca \|*  
*viriṃcāyoruyugmaṃ ca manmathāyeti vai kaṭim \|\| 16 \|\|*

*svacchodarāyetyudaramataṃdrāyetyuro vidheḥ \|*  
*mukhaṃ padmamukhāyeti bāhū vai vedapāṇaye \|\| 17 \|\|*

*namaḥ sarvātmane maulimarccayeccāpi paṃkajam \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte tatkuṃbhaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Having fashioned an auspicious image made of jaggery and called Brahmā, one should worship Brahmā with white flowers, sacred grains and sesamum; one should worship him, saying ‘Salutation to Brahmā’ while worshipping his feet; saying ‘Salutation to Saubhāgyada’ while worshipping his shanks; saying ‘Salutation to Viriñca’ while worshipping his hair of thinghs\[?thighs?\]; saying’ ‘Salutation to Manmatha’ while worshipping his waist; saying ‘Salutation to Svacchodara’ while worshipping his belly; saying ‘Salutation to Atandra’ while worshipping his chest; saying ‘Salutation to Padmamukha’ while worshipping his face; saying ‘Salutation to Vedapāṇi' while worshipping his arms: saying ‘Salutation to Sarvātman’ while worshipping his head; and one should also worship the lotus. Then in the morning one should present the pitcher to a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 7.19-20 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayedbhaktyā svayaṃ tu lavaṇaṃ vinā \|*  
*bhaktyā pradakṣiṇaṃ dadyādimaṃ maṃtramudīrayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*prīyatāmatra bhagavānsarvalokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye sarvalokānāṃ yastvānaṃdobhidhīyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. With devotion one should feed the brāhmaṇa and oneself eat saltless (food), and devoutly cicumambulate and recite this hymn: ‘The revered one, the grandsire of all the worlds, who lives in the hearts of all people, and who is called Ānanda (joy), may be pleased now’.

## \|\| 7.21 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsimāsi samācaret \|*  
*upavāsī paurṇamāsyāmarcayedbrāhmamavyayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. With this rite one should practise the vow every month; and observing a fast, one should worship the immutable Brahma on every full-moon day.

## \|\| 7.22-23 \|\|

*phalamekaṃ ca saṃprāśya śarvaryāṃ bhūtale svapet \|*  
*tatastrayodaśe māsi ghṛtadhenusamanvitām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*śayyāṃ dadyādviriṃcāya sarvopaskarasaṃyutām \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ kāṃcanaṃ kṛtvā sāvitrīṃ rajataistathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Eating one fruit (only) one should at night sleep on the ground. Then in the thirteenth month one should give a bed to Viriñca with ghee and a cow and with all ingredients, and fashioning a golden image of Brahmā and (an image of Savitri) of silver.

## \|\| 7.24-25 \|\|

*padmātmakaḥ sṛṣṭikarttā sāvitrīmupalabhyatu \|*  
*vastrairdvijaṃ sapatnīkaṃ pūjya bhaktyā vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śaktyā gavādikaṃ dadyātprīyatāmityudīrayet \|*  
*homaṃ śuklaistilaiḥ kuryādbrahmanāmāni kīrtayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. (One should say:) ‘May the creator born from a lotus obtain Sāvitrī.’ Honouring a brāhmaṇa with his wife, by (giving them) garments and ornaments, one should give a cow etc. according to one’s ability and should say: ‘Be pleased’. One should perform a sacrifice with white sesamum and utter the names of Brahma.

## \|\| 7.26 \|\|

*gavyena sarpiṣā tadvatpāyasena ca dharmavit \|*  
*viprebhyotha dhanaṃ dadyātpuṣpamālāṃ ca śaktitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. One, knowing the religious practices, should, along with ghee made from cow’s milk, give money and a garland of flowers to brahmaṇas according to one’s capacity.

## \|\| 7.27 \|\|

*yaḥ kuryādvidhinānena paurṇamāsyāṃ striyopi vā \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti brahmasātmyatām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. One, who—even ladies (can observe this vow)—observes (the vow) according to the rite on a full-moon day, being free from all sins, gets identity with Brahman.

## \|\| 7.28 \|\|

*ihaloke varānputrānsaubhāgyaṃ dhruvamaśnute \|*  
*yo brahmā sa smṛto viṣṇurānaṃdātmā maheśvaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In this world (such a) one certainly obtains excellent sons and good fortune. He, who is Brahma, is known to be Viṣṇu, to be the essence of joy, and Maheśvara.

## \|\| 7.29 \|\|

*sukhārthī kāmarūpeṇa smareddevaṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*evaṃ śrutvā cakārāsau ditiḥ sarvamaśeṣataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. One who desires happiness should remember the lord in any form one likes. Having heard this, Diti did everything fully.

## \|\| 7.30 \|\|

*kaśyapo vratamāhātmyādāgatya parayā mudā \|*  
*cakāra karkaśāṃ bhūyo rūpalāvaṇyasaṃyutām \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Kaśyapa, due to the great virtue of her vow, having come there with great joy, made that rough (lady) full of form and beauty.

## \|\| 7.31 \|\|

*varairāchaṃdayāmāsa sā tu vavre varaṃvaram \|*  
*putraṃ śakravadhārthāya samarthaṃ ca mahaujasam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. He persuaded her (to ask for) boons, and she chose an excellent boon: “I desire a powerful, very lustrous, magnanimous son, capable of killing all gods, to murder Indra.”

## \|\| 7.32-34 \|\|

*varayāmi mahātmānaṃ sarvāmaraniṣūdanam \|*  
*uvāca kaśyapo vākyamiṃdrahaṃtāramūrjitam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*pradāsyāmyahametena kintvetatkriyatāṃ śubhe \|*  
*āpastaṃbīṃ tu kṛtveṣṭiṃ putrīyāmadya sustani \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vidhāsyāmi tato garbhaṃ spṛṣṭvāhaṃ te stanau śubhe \|*  
*bhaviṣyati śubho garbho devi śakraniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Kaśyapa uttered these words: “With this (boon) I shall give you a powerful son who will kill Indra; but, O you auspicious one, do this: O you of beautiful breasts, I shall today perform the Āpastamba sacrifice for (obtaining) a son. Then I shall deposit my semen (into you) after touching your breasts, O auspicious one. O lady, you will have a son capable of killing Indra.”

## \|\| 7.35 \|\|

*āpastaṃbīṃ tataścakre putreṣṭiṃ draviṇādhikām \|*  
*iṃdraśatrobhavasveti juhāva ca havistvaran \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Then he performed the Āpastamba sacrifice with (i.e. spending) great wealth for (obtaining) a son, and hurriedly offered the oblation saying: “O enemy of Indra, be (conceived).”

## \|\| 7.36 \|\|

*devāśca mumurhurdaityā vimukhāścaiva dānavāḥ \|*  
*dityāṃ garbhamathādhatta kaśyapaḥ prāha tāṃ punaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The gods fainted and the demons and the fiends turned away their faces. Kaśyapa then put the semen into Diti, and again said to her:

## \|\| 7.37 \|\|

*mukhaṃ te caṃdrapratimaṃ stanau bilvaphalopamau \|*  
*adharau vidrumākārau varṇaścātīva śobhanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “Your face is like the moon; your breasts resemble the bilva-fruit (are stout). Your lips have the form of corals and your complexion is very lovely.

## \|\| 7.38 \|\|

*tvāṃ dṛṣṭvāhaṃ viśālākṣi vismarāmi svikāṃ tanum \|*  
*tadevaṃ garbhaḥ suśroṇi hastenoptastanau tava \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Seeing you, O you lady of large eyes, I forget my own body. Therefore, O lady, of charming hips, I have, with my own hand (i.e. myself), deposited my seed into your body.

## \|\| 7.39-41 \|\|

*tvayā yatne vidhātavyo hyasmingarbhe varānane \|*  
*saṃvatsaraśataṃ tvekamasminneva tapovane \|\| 39 \|\|*

*saṃdhyāyāṃ naiva bhoktavyaṃ garbhiṇyā varavarṇini \|*  
*na sthātavyaṃ na gaṃtavyaṃ vṛkṣamūleṣu sarvadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*nopaskareṣu niviśenmusalolūkhalādiṣu \|*  
*jalaṃ ca nāvagāheta śūnyāgāraṃ ca varjayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. You should, O lady, having an excellent face, take care of this foetus in a penance-grove for one hundred years. During pregnancy you should not eat in the evening; you should not remain under, or go to the roots of, trees. You should not resort to (i.e. handle) instruments like mortar, pestle etc.; you should not plunge into water, and should avoid a vacant dwelling.

## \|\| 7.42 \|\|

*valmīkeṣu na tiṣṭheta na codvignamanā bhavet \|*  
*na nakhena likhedbhūmau nāṃgāre na ca bhasmani \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. You should not remain on ant-hills; you should not be dejected in mind; you should not write (i.e. scratch) with nails on the ground, on charcoal, or ashes.

## \|\| 7.43 \|\|

*na śayāluḥ sadā tiṣṭhedvyāyāmaṃ ca vivarjayet \|*  
*na tuṣāṃgārabhasmāsthi kapāleṣu samāviśet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. You should not always be sleepy, and should avoid (acts causing) fatigue. You should not come to rest upon charcoal or ashes of husk or bowls of bones.

## \|\| 7.44 \|\|

*varjayetkalahaṃ loke gātrābhyaṃgaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*na muktakeśī tiṣṭheta nāśuciḥ syātkathaṃcana \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. You should avoid quarrel with people, and should avoid smearing your body with oily substances; you should not remain with loose hair and should never remain impure.

## \|\| 7.45 \|\|

*na śayītottaraśirāḥ na caivādhaḥ śirāḥ kvacit \|*  
*na vastrahīnā nodvignā na cārdracaraṇā satī \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. You should never sleep either by raising or lowering your head; should not be without garments (on your person); should not be dejected or with wet feet.

## \|\| 7.46 \|\|

*nāmaṃgalyāṃ vadedvācaṃ na ca hāsyādhikābhavet \|*  
*kuryācca gurubhirnityaṃ pūjāṃ māṃgalyatatparā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. You should not utter inauspicious words; you should not laugh excessively Intent upon auspiciousness, you should everyday perform worship along with the elders.

## \|\| 7.47-48 \|\|

*sarvauṣ̣adhībhiḥ sṛṣ̣ṭena vāriṇā snānamācaret*  
*kṛtarakṣ̣ā tu ṣ́uṣ́rūṣ̣ā vācāpūjanatatparā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sarvauṣadhībhiḥ sṛṣṭena vāriṇā snānamācaret \|*  
*tiṣṭhetprasannavadanā bhartṛpriyahite ratā \|*  
*na garhayecca bhartā raṃsarvāvasthamapi kvacit \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. You should take bath with water connected (i.e. mixed) with all herbs; having protected yourself and with a desire to serve, and intent upon worshipping with vows, you should keep a pleasing face, and be engrossed in the things dear to your husband; should never condemn (your) husband in any condition.

## \|\| 7.49 \|\|

*kṛśāhaṃ durbalā caiva vārddhakyaṃ mama cāgatam \|*  
*stanau me calitau sthānānmukhaṃ ca valibhaṃguram \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Should never say: ‘I am emaciated, weak; old age has come upon me; my breasts have moved (away) from their place, and face is curled with folds. You have made me like this’.” (Before departing, he said:) “may it be well with you. I shall go (now)”.

## \|\| 7.50-51 \|\|

*evaṃvidhā tvayā cāhaṃ kṛteti na vadetkvacit \|*  
*svastyastute gamiṣyāmi tathetyuktastayā punaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*tataḥ sā bhartṛvācoktavidhinā samatiṣṭhata \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. When she said “All right”, he, in the presence of all beings, vanished there only. Then she took to the vow as told by her husband.

## \|\| 7.52-57 \|\|

*atha jñātvā tatheṃdropi diteḥ pārśvamupāgataḥ \|*  
*vihāya devasadanaṃ tāṃ śuśrūṣuravasthitaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*diteśchidrāṃtaraprepsurabhavatpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*viparītoṃtaravyagraḥ prasannavadato bahiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*ajānanniva tattkāryamātmanaśśubhamācaran \|*  
*tato varṣaśatāṃte sā nyūne tu divasaistribhiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ prītyā vismitamānasā \|*  
*akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucaṃ śayānā muktamūrdhajā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nidrābharasamākrāṃtā divā paraśirāḥ kvacit \|*  
*tatastadaṃtaraṃ labdhvā praviśyāṃtaḥ śacīpatiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*vajreṇa saptadhā cakre taṃ garbhaṃ tridaśādhipaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sapta ca te jātāḥ kumārāḥ sūryavarcasaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

52-57. Knowing that and leaving gods’ residence, Indra came near her and remained there desiring to hear what she said. Indra wanted to know the weak points of Diti. He was acting in a false manner, distracted interanally and having a smiling face outwardly, as it were not knowing her mission and doing (only) what was good for him. She regarded herself as blessed, and with a proud mind, through joy, not cleansing her feet, lay anywhere by day, with hair let loose and with her head raised. when only three days were left for hundred years to be completed. Then, taking that opportunity, the lord of Śacī, and the ruler of gods, entering inside (her body), cut the foetus into seven parts with his bolt; then those (pieces) were born as sons, as bright as the sun.

## \|\| 7.58-59 \|\|

*rudaṃtaḥ sapta te bālā niṣiddhā dānavāriṇā \|*  
*bhūyopi rudamānāṃstānekaikānsaptadhā hariḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ciccheda vajrahasto vai punaḥ stūdarasaṃsthitān \|*  
*evamekonapaṃcāśadbhūtvā terurudurbhṛśam \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Those seven boys who were crying were suppressed (i.e. appeased) with the water of libation. Again Indra, with the bolt in his hand, cut each of the crying ones, who were in the womb, into seven pieces. Thus cut into forty-nine (in number) they cried very much.

## \|\| 7.60-62 \|\|

*iṃdro nivārayāmāsa mā rudadhvaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sa ciṃtayāmāsa vitarkamiti vṛtrahā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*karmaṇaḥ kasya māhātmyātpunaḥ saṃjīvitāstvamī \|*  
*viditvā puṇyayogena paurṇamāsīphalaṃ tvidam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*nūnametatpariṇatamathavā brahmapūjanāt \|*  
*vajreṇābhihatāḥ saṃto na vināśamupāyayuḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. Again and again Indra suppressed (i.e. appeased) them by saying, ‘Do not cry’. Then the killer of Vṛtra conjectured: ‘Due to the virtue of which act have they survived? He knew by means of (his) religious merit that this was the fruit of the Paurṇamāsī (vow), or indeed this happened as a result of the worship of Brahmā; (so) though struck by the bolt, they did not perish.

## \|\| 7.63 \|\|

*ekopyanekatāmāpa yasmādudaragopanam \|*  
*avadhyā nūnamete vai tasmāddevā bhavaṃtviti \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Even one became many. Since the foetus was protected, and they indeed could not be killed, let them be gods.

## \|\| 7.64-65 \|\|

*yasmānmā ruda ityuktā rudaṃto garbhasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*maruto nāma te nāmnā bhavaṃtu sukhabhāginaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tataḥ prasādya deveśaḥ kṣamasveti ditiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*arthaśāstraṃ samāsthāya mayaitadduṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. Since, when born from the womb, they were told not to cry, there fore, let them be named Maruts, and let them be happy’. Then the lord of gods, having propitiated Diti, (said to her): “Forgive me; resorting to the rule of need, I did this bad act.”

## \|\| 7.66 \|\|

*kṛtvā marudgaṇaṃ devaiḥ samānamamarādhipaḥ \|*  
*ditiṃ vimānamāropya sasutāmagamaddivam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. The lord of gods, making the group of Maruts equal to gods, and putting Diti along with her sons in an aeroplane, went to heaven.

## \|\| 7.67 \|\|

*yajñabhāgabhujaḥ sarve marutaste tatobhavan \|*  
*na jagmuraikyamasurairataste suravallabhāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Since then all the Maruts enjoyed a share in the sacrificial offerings. They did not have unity with the Asuras; therefore, they were dear to gods.

## \|\| 7.68 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*ādisargastvayā brahmankathito vistareṇa me \|*  
*pratisargaśca yo yeṣāmadhipāṃstānvadasva me \|\| 68 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

68\. O brāhmaṇa, you have explained to me in detail the initial creation. Tell me what is the second ary creation and (who are) the lords (and) of which (species).

Pulastya spoke:

## \|\| 7.69-70 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*yadābhiṣiktaḥ sakalepi rājye pṛthurddharitryāmadhipo babhūva \|*  
*tathauṣadhīnāmadhipaṃ cakāra yajñavratānāṃ tapasāṃ ca somam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nakṣatratārādvijavṛkṣagulmalatāvitānasya ca rukmagarbham \|*  
*apāmadhīśaṃ varuṇaṃ dhanānāṃ rājñāṃ prabhuṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ ca tadvat \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. When Pṛthu was crowned (as the king) of all the kingdom, he became the lord on the earth; Brahmā made Soma (the moon) having radiance within, the lord of the herbs, sacrificial vows, and austerities and of constellations, stars, brāhmaṇas, clumps of trees and spreading creepers. Similarly he made Varuṇa the lord of waters, and Vaiśravaṇa (i.e. Kubera) the lord of wealth.

## \|\| 7.71 \|\|

*viṣṇuṃ ravīṇāmadhipaṃ vasūnāmagniṃ ca lokādhipatiṃ cakāra \|*  
*prajāpatīnāmadhipaṃ ca dakṣaṃ cakāra śakraṃ marutāmadhīśam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He made Viṣṇu the lord of the suns and Vasus, and Agni the lord of the worlds; made Dakṣa the lord of Prajāpatis, and Śakra the lord of Maruts.

## \|\| 7.72 \|\|

*daityādhipānāmatha dānavānāṃ prahlādamīśaṃ ca yamaṃ pitṝṇām \|*  
*piśācarakṣaḥpaśubhūtayakṣavetālarājaṃ hyatha śūlapāṇim \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. He made Prahlāda the lord of the kings of Daityas, and of Dānavas. He made the trident-holder the lord of demons, fiends, beasts, spirits, Yakṣas and vampires.

## \|\| 7.73 \|\|

*prāleyaśailaṃ ca patiṃ girīṇāmīśaṃ samudraṃ saritāmadhīśam \|*  
*gaṃdharvavidyādharakinnarāṇāmīśaṃ punaścitrarathaṃ cakāra \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He made Himālaya mountain the lord of mountains, and ocean the lord of rivers. He made Citraratha the chief of the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras.

## \|\| 7.74 \|\|

*nāgādhipaṃ vāsukimugravīryaṃ sarpādhipaṃ takṣakamādideśa \|*  
*digvāraṇānāmadhipaṃ cakāra gajeṃdramairāvaṇanāmadheyam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. He appointed Vāsuki of strong power as the lord of serpent-demons, and Takṣaka as the lord of snakes. He made the lordly elephant, Airavata by name, the lord of the quarter-elephants.

## \|\| 7.75 \|\|

*suparṇamīśaṃ patatāmathārvatāṃ rājānamuccaiḥśravasaṃ cakāra \|*  
*siṃhaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gavāṃ ca plakṣaṃ punaḥ sarvavanaspatīnām \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. He made Suparṇa the lord of birds and Uccaiḥśravas the lord of horses. He made lion the lord of beasts, bull the lord of cows, and the fig tree with waving leaves the lord of plants.

## \|\| 7.76 \|\|

*pitāmahaḥ pūrvamathābhyaṣiṃcadetānpunaḥ sarvadiśādhināthān \|*  
*pūrveśa dikpālamathābhyaṣiṃcannāmnā suvarmāṇamarātiketuṃ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. Then Brahmā consecrated these as the lords of quarters: He consecrated Suvarman, eminent as a foe, as the lord of the eastern quarter.

## \|\| 7.77 \|\|

*tatodhipaṃ dakṣiṇataścakāra sarveśvaraṃ śaṃkhapadābhidhānam \|*  
*saketumaṃtaṃ digadhīśamīśaṃ cakāra paścādbhuvanāṃḍagarbhaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Then he made him—Śaṅkha by name—the lord of the south. Brahmā made Ketumanta the lord of the (western) direction.

## \|\| 7.78 \|\|

*hiraṇyaromāṇamudagdigīśaṃ prajāpatiṃ meghasutaṃ cakāra \|*  
*adyāpi kurvaṃti diśāmadhīśāḥ sadā vahaṃtastu bhuvobhirakṣām \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Then Prajāpati made Hiraṇyaroman, the son of Megha, the lord of the northern direction.

Even now, the lords of quarters always carrying upon them (the responsibility of the protection of the earth) protect the earth.

## \|\| 7.79 \|\|

*caturbhiretaiḥ pṛthunāmadheyo nṛpobhiṣiktaḥ prathamaḥ pṛthivyām \|*  
*gateṃtare cākṣuṣanāmadheye vaivasvataṃ cakrurimaṃ pṛthivyāṃ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Along with these four, he first installed as the king of the earth (a man) Pṛthu by name. When the period of Manu named Cākṣuṣa was over, he made this (period) of Vaivasvata (Manu) on the earth.

## \|\| 7.80 \|\|

*gateṃtare cākṣuṣanāmadheye vaivasvatākhye ca punaḥ pravṛtte \|*  
*prajāpatiḥ sosya carācarasya babhūva sūryānvayajaḥ sacihnaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. When the period of Manu by name Cākṣuṣa was over, and when the period called Vaivasvata set in, he, born in the solar family, became the king, with his insignia, of this movable and immovable (creation).

## \|\| 7.81-82 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*manvaṃtarāṇi sarvāṇi manūnāṃ caritāni yat \|*  
*pramāṇaṃ caiva kalpasya tatsṛṣṭiṃ ca samāsataḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*ekacittaḥ prasannātmā śṛṇu kauravanaṃdana \|*  
*yāmā nāma purā devā āsansvāyaṃbhuvāṃtare \|\| 82 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

81-82. O son of Kuru, listen, in short, with concentrated and gracious mind, to all the periods of Manus and their lives, the measure of a Kalpa, and the creation in it. Formerly in the period of Svāyambhuva Manu, there were gods called Yāmā.

## \|\| 7.83-84 \|\|

*saptaiva ṛṣayaḥ pūrvaṃ ye marīcyādayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*āgnīdhraścāgnibāhuśca vibhuḥ savana eva ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

*jyotiṣmāndyutimānbhavyo medhā medhātithirvasuḥ \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvasyāsya manordaśaite vaṃśavarddhanāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. And also seven sages only like Marīci and others were said to be there. These ten increased the race of Manu: Āgnīdhra, Agnibāhu, Vibhu, Savana, Jyotiṣmat, Dyutimat, Bhavya, Medhā, Medhātithi, Vasu.

## \|\| 7.85 \|\|

*pratisargamamī kṛtvā jagmuste paramaṃ padam \|*  
*evaṃ svāyaṃbhuvaṃ proktaṃ svārociṣamataḥ param \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. These, having brought about secondary creation, reached the highest place. Thus is described the Svāyambhuva period; after this comes the Svārociṣa.

## \|\| 7.86 \|\|

*svārociṣasya tanayāścatvāro devavarcasaḥ \|*  
*nabhonabhasya prabhṛtirbhāvanaḥ kīrtivarddhanaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Svārociṣa’s four sons, having god-like lustre were: Nabha, Nabhasya, Bhāvana, and Kiītivardhana.

## \|\| 7.87 \|\|

*dattogniścyavanastaṃbhaḥ prāṇaḥ kaśyapa eva ca \|*  
*arvā bṛhaspatiścaiva sapta saptarṣayobhavan \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. The seven sages were: Datta, Agni, Cyavana, Stambha, Prāṇa, Kaśyapa and Arvābṛhaspati.

## \|\| 7.88-93 \|\|

*tadā devāśca tuṣitāḥ smṛtā svārociṣeṃtare \|*  
*havīṃdrasuḥkṛto mūrtirāpo jyotirathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhasya sutāḥ sapta ye prajāpatayastadā \|*  
*dvitīyametatkathitaṃ manvaṃtaramataḥ paraṃ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*anyaccaiva pravakṣyāmi tathā manvaṃtaraṃ śubhaṃ \|*  
*manurnāmauttamistatra daśa putrānajījanat \|\| 90 \|\|*

*iṣaūrjastanūjaśca śuciḥ śukrastathaiva ca \|*  
*madhuśca mādhavaścaiva nabhasyotha nabhastathā \|\| 91 \|\|*

*sahaḥ sahasya eteṣāmuttamaḥ kīrtivarddhanaḥ \|*  
*bhānavastatra devāḥ syurūrjāḥ saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*kaukabhiṇḍiḥ kutuṇḍaśca dālbhyaḥ śaṃkhaḥ pravāhitaḥ \|*  
*mitiśca saṃmitiścaiva saptaite yogavarddhanāḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

88-93. Then, in the Svārociṣa period, gods were called Tuṣita. The seven sons of Vasiṣṭha were then the Prajāpatis: Havi, Indra, Sukṛta, Mūrti, Āpa, Jyotiratha, and Smṛta. This is said to be the second period of Manu.

After this I shall narrate the next auspicious period of Manu. In it the Manu named Auttami produced ten sons; Iṣa. Ūrja, Tanūja, Śuci, Śukra, Madhu, Mādhava, Nabhasya, Nabha, Saha, Sahasya and excellent Kīrtivardhana were the twelve Ādityas. Gods were (then) called Ūrja. The seven sages were:

Kaukabhiṇḍa, Kutuṇḍa, Dālbhya, Śaṅkha, Pravāhita, Miti and Sammiti; and these seven increased the contemplation of the supreme spirit.

## \|\| 7.94-95 \|\|

*manvaṃtaraṃ caturthaṃ tu tāmasaṃ nāma viśrutaṃ \|*  
*kapiḥ pṛthustathaivāgnirakapiḥ kavireva ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

*tathaiva janyadhāmānau munayaḥ sapta nāmataḥ \|*  
*sādhyā devagaṇā ye ca kathitāstāmaseṃtare \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. The fourth period of Manu is known as Tāmasa. The names of the seven sages in it (are): Kapi, Pṛthu, Agni, Akapi, Kavi, Janya and Dhāman. The hosts of gods in the Tāmasa period were called Sādhyas.

## \|\| 7.96-98 \|\|

*akalmaṣastapodhanvī tapomūlastapodhanaḥ \|*  
*taporāśistapasyaśca sutapasyaḥ paraṃtapaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*tāmasasya sutāḥ sarve daśavaṃśavivarddhanāḥ \|*  
*paṃcamasya manostadvadraivatasyāṃtaraṃ śṛṇu \|\| 97 \|\|*

*devabāhuḥ subāhuśca parjyanyaḥ samayomuniḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyaromā saptāśvaḥ saptaite ṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

96-98. All the ten sons of Tāmasa, viz. Akalmaṣa, Tapa, Dhanvi, Tapomūla, Tapodhana, Taporāśi, Tapasya, Sutapasya and Parantapa increased the race. Similarly, listen to the fifth, i.e. the Raivata:

Devabāhu, Subāhu, Parjanya, Samaya, Muni, Hiraṇyaroman, Saptāśva are said to be the seven sages.

## \|\| 7.99-102 \|\|

*devāśca bhūtarajasastathā prakṛtayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*avaśastatvadarśī ca vītimānhavyapaḥ kapiḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*mukto nirutsukaḥ satvo nirmohotha prakāśakaḥ \|*  
*dharmavīryabalopetā daśaite revatātmajāḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*bhṛguḥ sudhāmā virajaḥ sahiṣṇurnāradastathā \|*  
*vivasvānkṛtināmā ca sapta saptarṣayopare \|\| 101 \|\|*

*cākṣuṣasyāṃtare devā lekhānāmapariśrutāḥ \|*  
*vibhavotha pṛthakcānu kīrtitāstridivaukasaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

99-102. The gods Bhūtarajas are similarly said to be the elements. These ten are the sons of Raivata, (they are) endowed with piety, vigour and power:

Avaśa, Tattvadarśin, Vītimān, Havyapa, Kapi, Mukta, Nirutsuka, Sattva, Nirmoha, and Prakāśaka.

Bhṛgu, Sudhāma, Viraja, Sahiṣṇu, Nārada, Vivasvān and Kṛti were the seven sages in the Cākṣuṣa period; and the gods were known as Lekhā; and the Vibhus also were separately termed as gods.

## \|\| 7.103-104 \|\|

*cākṣuṣasyāṃtare prāpte devānāṃ paṃcamo janaḥ \|*  
*ruruprabhṛtayastadvaccākṣuṣasya sutā daśa \|\| 103 \|\|*

*proktāḥ svāyaṃbhuve vaṃśe ye mayā pūrvameva te \|*  
*antaraṃ cākṣuṣaṃ caiva mayā te parikīrtitaṃ \|\| 104 \|\|*

103-104. When the Cākṣuṣa period set in, the gods had the fifth world: and similarly Cākṣuṣa had ten sons—Ruru and others. They have already been mentioned by me in the Svāyambhuva family. Thus I have described the Cākṣuṣa period to you.

## \|\| 7.105-106 \|\|

*saptamaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi yadvaivasvatamucyate \|*  
*atriścaiva vasiṣṭhaśca kaśyapo gautamastathā \|\| 105 \|\|*

*bhāradvājastathā yogī viśvāmitraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*jamadagniśca saptaite sāṃprataṃ te maharṣayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

105-106. I shall (now) tell you about the seventh which is called Vaivasvata. Now the seven great sages are: Atri and Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa and Gautama, the contemplative Bharadvāja, the valorous Viśvāmitra and Jamadagni.

## \|\| 7.107 \|\|

*kṛtvā dharmavyavasthānaṃ prayānti paramaṃ padaṃ \|*  
*sāvarṇyasya pravakṣyāmi manorbhāvi tathāṃtaraṃ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. After setting the religious order, they will reach the highest place. I shall describe to you the future period of Sāvarṇya Manu.

## \|\| 7.108 \|\|

*aśvatthāmā śaradvāṃśca kauśiko gālavastathā \|*  
*śatānaṃdaḥ kāśyapaśca rāmaśca ṛṣaya smṛtāḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The sages (of this Manvantara) are said to be: Aśvatthāman, Śaradvān, Kauśika, Gālava, Śatānanda, Kāśyapa and Rāma.

## \|\| 7.109-110 \|\|

*dhṛtirvarīyānyavasuḥ suvarṇo dhṛtireva ca \|*  
*variṣṇuvīryaḥ sumatirvasuśśukraśca vīryavān \|\| 109 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasyārkasāvarṇermanoḥ putrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*raucyādayastathānyepi manavaḥ saṃprakīrtitāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Dhṛti, Varīyān, Yavasu, Suvarṇa and Dhṛti (again), Variṣṇu, Vīrya, Sumati, Vasu and powerful Śukra are said to be the sons of the future Sāvarṇi Manu. Raucya and others also are said to be Manus.

## \|\| 7.111 \|\|

*ruceḥ prajāpateḥ putro raucyo nāma bhaviṣyati \|*  
*manurbhūtisutastadvadbhautyo nāma bhaviṣyati \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Raucya, the son ef Prajāpati Ruci will be a Manu; and also Bhautya, the son of Bhūti, will be a Manu.

## \|\| 7.112 \|\|

*tatastu merusāvarṇirbrahmasunurmanuḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ṛbhuśca ṝtudhāmā ca viṣvakseno manustathā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Then Merusāvarṇi, son of Brahma, is said to be a Manu. And also Ṛbhu, Ṛtudhāman, Viśvaksena will (each) be a Manu.

## \|\| 7.113 \|\|

*atītānāgatāścaiva manavaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ yugasāhasramebhirvyāptaṃ narādhipa \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Past and future Manus are (thus) described (by me). O prince, a thousand yugas will be occupied by (each one of) these.

## \|\| 7.114 \|\|

*svesventare sarvamidaṃ samutpādya carācaraṃ \|*  
*kalpakṣaye nivṛtte tu mucyaṃte brahmaṇā saha \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Having created all these mobile and immobile beings in their own periods, they will, at the end of the kalpa, obtain release along with Brahmā.

## \|\| 7.115 \|\|

*amīyugasahasrānte vinaśyanti punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*brahmādyā viṣṇusāyujyaṃ tato yāsyaṃti vai nṛpa \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. At the end of a thousand yugas they will again and again perish, and led by Brahma will then be absorbed in Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 8 - Description of the Solar Race (Ādityavaṃśa or Sūryavaṃśa)

## \|\| 8.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*bahubhirddharaṇī bhuktā bhūpālaiḥ śrūyate purā \|*  
*pārthivāḥ pṛthivīyogātpṛthivī kasya yogataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. It is heard that the earth was formerly enjoyed by many kings. They are (called) Pārthiva on account of their connection with the earth; but on account of (its) connection with whom is the Pṛthvī (earth) so called?

## \|\| 8.2 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ ca kṛtā saṃjñā bhūmessā pāribhāṣikī \|*  
*gauritīyaṃ ca saṃjñā vā bhuvaḥ kasmādbravīhi me \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Why is the earth given that technical name? Tell me why it has the name Gau, or why it is (called) Bhū?

## \|\| 8.3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*purā kṛtayugasyāsīdaṃgo nāma prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*mṛtyostu duhitā tena pariṇītātidurmukhī \|\| 3 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

3\. Formerly Aṅga by name was the Prajāpati of the Kṛtayuga. He married Mṛtyu’s extremely ugly daughter named Sunīthā. Her son was Vena.

## \|\| 8.4-12 \|\|

*sunīthā nāma tasyāstu veno nāma sutaḥ purā \|*  
*adharmanirataḥ kāmī balavānvasudhādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*lokasyādharmakṛccāpi parabhāryāpahārakaḥ \|*  
*atha tasya prasidyarthaṃ jagadarthaṃ maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anunītopi na dadāvaśuddhātmā'bhayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*śāpena mārayitvainamarājakabhayārditāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*mamaṃthurbrāhmaṇāstasya balāddehamakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*tatkāyānmathyamānāttu janitā mlecchajātayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śarīre māturaṃśena kṛṣṇāṃjanasamaprabhāḥ \|*  
*pituraṃśasya saṃgena dhārmiko dharmakārakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*utpanno dakṣiṇāddhastātsadhanuḥ saśaro gadī \|*  
*divyatejomayaḥ putrassaratnakavacāṃgadaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pṛthurevābhavannāmnā sa ca viṣṇurajāyata \|*  
*sa viprairabhiṣiktaḥ saṃstapaḥ kṛtvā suduṣkaraṃ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viṣṇorvareṇa sarvasya prabhutvamagamatprabhuḥ \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ nirddharmaṃ vīkṣya bhūtalaṃ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*veddhumevodyataḥ kopācchareṇāmitavikramaḥ \|*  
*tato gorūpamāsthāya bhūḥ palāyitumudyatā \|\| 12 \|\|*

4-12. This king was attached to wickedness, and was lustful and powerful. He did unrighteous things to people, and took away others’ wives. Though entreated by the great sages for his success and for the (good of the) world, he, of an impure mind, did not grant them safety. The sinless brāhmaṇas distressed with the fear of anarchy, having killed him, with a curse, forcibly churned his body. From that body, being churned, the Mlecha \[Mleccha?\] tribes, dark like collyrium, due to the (presence of) the mother’s portion in the body were created. Due to the contact of the father’s portion, from the right hand of the body a pious son, full of divine lustre, doing righteous things, and with a bow, an arrow, a mace and gems, an armour and armlets, named Pṛthu, who was Viṣṇu himself, was born. Being consecrated by the brāhmaṇas, and having practised a very difficult penance, he, due to Viṣṇu’s boon, became the lord of all. Seeing the earth without sacred study, without oblation to deities, and void of righteous behaviour, he, of unlimited valour, was, through anger, quite ready to pierce it with his arrow. Then the earth, taking up the form of a cow, was about to flee.

## \|\| 8.13 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhe tvanvagamattasyāḥ pṛthuḥ seṣuśarāsanaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ sthitvaikadeśe tu kiṃ karomīti cābravīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Pṛthu, having a bow and arrows, pursued her. Then remaining in one place, she said: “What should I do?”

## \|\| 8.14 \|\|

*pṛthurapyavadadvākyamīpsitaṃ dehi suvrate \|*  
*sarvasya jagataḥ śīghraṃ sthāvarasya carasya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Pṛthu also uttered (these) words: “O you of righteous vow, give quickly what is desired by the world—immobile and mobile”.

## \|\| 8.15 \|\|

*tatheti cābravīdbhūmirdudoha sa narādhipaḥ \|*  
*svake pāṇau pṛthurvatsaṃ kṛtvā svāyaṃbhuvaṃ manuṃ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The earth said: “All right”. Then king Pṛthu, making Svāyambhuva Manu the calf, milked her (milk in the pot) in his hand.

## \|\| 8.16 \|\|

*tadannamabhavaddugdhaṃ prajā jīvaṃti yena tu \|*  
*tatastu ṛṣibhirdugdhā vatsaḥ somastadābhavat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. That milk turned into food on which the creatures subsist. Then the earth was milked by the sages, when Soma was the calf.

## \|\| 8.17-18 \|\|

*dogdhā vācaspatirabhūtpātraṃ vedastapo rasaḥ \|*  
*devaiśca vasudhā dugdhā maruddogdhā tadābhavat \|\| 17 \|\|*

*indro vatsaḥ samabhavatkṣīramūrjjasvalaṃ balaṃ \|*  
*devānāṃ kāṃcanaṃ pātraṃ pitṛṇāṃ rājataṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Vācaspati (then) milked her (lit. became the milkman); Veda was the pot, and penance the milk. Then the gods milked her when Marut was the milkman. Indra became the calf and mighty power was the milk. The pot of the gods was golden and that of the Pitṛs was silvery.

## \|\| 8.19-21 \|\|

*aṃtakaścābhavaddogdhā yamo vatsaḥ svadhā rasaḥ \|*  
*bilaṃ ca pātraṃ nāgānāṃ takṣako vatsakobhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viṣaṃ kṣīraṃ tato dogdhā dhṛtarāṣṭrobhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*asurairapi dugdheyaṃ āyase śatrupīḍanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pātre māyāmabhūdvatsaḥprālhādistuvirocanaḥ \|*  
*dogdhā trimūrddhā tatrāsīnmāyā yena pravartitā \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The god of death milked her when Yama was the calf and Svadhā the milk. The pot of the serpents was a hole and Takṣaka was the calf, and poison was the milk. And Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the demons too, milked her (taking the milk) in an iron pot, the milk being the trickery harassing the enemies. The calf was Virocana, the son of Prahlāda. The milkman then was Trimūrdhan, who promoted deceit.

## \|\| 8.22 \|\|

*yakṣaiśca vasudhā dugdhā purāṃtarddhānamīpsubhiḥ \|*  
*kṛtvā viśvāvasuṃ vatsaṃ maṇimaṃtaṃ mahīpate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. O king, the Yakṣas desiring to conceal themselves, also milked the earth in ancient days, making Vivasvān, having the gem, the calf.

## \|\| 8.23 \|\|

*pretarakṣogaṇairdugdhā vasā rudhiramulbaṇaṃ \|*  
*raupyanābhobhavaddogdhā sumālī vatsa eva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The groups of evil spirits and fiends milked the earth, marrow and clotted blood (being the milk). Raupyanābha was the milkman and Sumālin the calf.

## \|\| 8.24 \|\|

*gaṃdharvaiśca punardugdhā vasudhā sāpsarogaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vatsaṃ citrarathaṃ kṛtvā gaṃdhānpadmadale tathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The Gandharvas again, along with the groups of the celestial nymphs milked the earth, making Citraratha (Gandharva) the calf, and the fragrances in the lotus-petal (the milk).

## \|\| 8.25 \|\|

*dogdhāvasurucirnāmātharvavedasya pāragaḥ \|*  
*giribhirvasudhā dugdhā ratnāni vividhāni ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Vararuci, the expert in Atharva Veda milked the cow. The mountains also milked her with various jewels (as the milk).

## \|\| 8.26 \|\|

*auṣadhāni ca divyāni dogdhā merurmahīdharaḥ \|*  
*vatsobhūddhimavāṃstatra pātraṃ śailamayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Mountain Meru milked (her with) divine herbs (as the milk). The Himālaya was the calf and the pot was made of mountains.

## \|\| 8.27 \|\|

*vṛkṣaiśca vasudhā dugdhā kṣīraṃ chinnaprarohaṇaṃ \|*  
*pālāśapātre dogdhā tu sālaḥ puṣpavanākulaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The trees also milked the (milk of the) earth, into the pot made from the Palāsa tree; the cut-off sprouts were the milk and Sāla full of flowers and woods was the milkman.

## \|\| 8.28 \|\|

*plakṣobhavattato vatsaḥ sarvavṛkṣavanādhipaḥ \|*  
*evamanyaiśca vasudhā tathā dugdhā yathecchataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. And the fig-tree, the lord of all trees and woods, was the calf. Thus others also milked the earth according to their desire.

## \|\| 8.29 \|\|

*āyurddhanāni saukhyaṃ ca pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*na dāridryaṃ tathā rogī nādhanonacapāpakṛt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. While Pṛthu was ruling, there prevailed longevity, wealth, and happiness. There was no poverty, and also no sick person, no poor person and no sinner.

## \|\| 8.30 \|\|

*nopasargā na cāghātaḥ pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*nityaṃpramuditālokā duḥkhaśokavivarjitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When Pṛthu was ruling, there were no calamities; there was no misfortune; people not having sorrow or grief, were ever joyful.

## \|\| 8.31 \|\|

*dhanuḥ koṭyā ca śaileṃdrānutsārya sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhūmaṃḍalaṃ samaṃ cakre lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Having uprooted, with the end of his bow, the big mountains, he, with the desire to do good to the people, made the terrestrial globe (i.e. the earth) even.

## \|\| 8.32-33 \|\|

*na puragrāmadurgāṇi na cāyudhadharā narāḥ \|*  
*mriyaṃte yatra duḥkhaṃ ca nārthaśāstrasya cādaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dharmaikatānāḥ puruṣāḥ pṛthau rājyaṃ praśāsati \|*  
*kathitāni ca pātrāṇi yatkṣīraṃ ca yathā tava \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. There were no inaccessible cities or villages; men did not die with weapons in their hands; there was no sorrow, and science of politics was honoured; men were given to piety when Pṛthu was ruling. I have narrated to you, in the manner mentioned (above), (which were) the pots, which was the milk (etc.).

## \|\| 8.34-35 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ yena rucistatra tebhyo dattaṃ vijānatā \|*  
*yajñaśrīdeṣu sarveṣu mayā tubhyaṃ niveditaṃ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*duhitṛtvaṃ gatā yasmātpṛthoḥ pṛthvī mahāmate \|*  
*tasyānusārayogācca pṛthivī viśrutā budhaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. He, the wise one, gave those whatever they liked, when all were giving importance to sacrifice (or, when all were giving i.e. pouring wealth into sacrifice). I have (thus) told you, O highly intelligent one, that since the earth became the daughter of Pṛthu, she accordingly was known by the wise to be Pṛthivi.

## \|\| 8.36 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*ādityavaṃśamakhilaṃ vada brahmanyathākramaṃ \|*  
*somavaṃśaṃ ca tattvajña yathāvadvaktumarhasi \|\| 36 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

36\. O brāhmaṇa, tell me in due order, about the entire solar dynasty \[Ādityavaṃśa or Sūryavaṃśa\]; please also explain (to me) the lunar dynasty \[Somavaṃśa or Candravaṃśa\], O you who know the truth.

## \|\| 8.37 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*vivasvānkaśyapātpūrvamadityāmabhavatpurā \|*  
*tasya patnītrayaṃ tadvatsaṃjñā rājñī prabhā tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

37\. Formerly Vivasvān was born to Aditi from Kaśyapa. He had three daughters: Saṃjñā, Rājñi and Prabhā.

## \|\| 8.38 \|\|

*raivatasya sutā rājñī revataṃ suṣuve sutaṃ \|*  
*prabhā prabhātaṃ suṣuve tvāṣṭraṃ saṃjñā tathā manuṃ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Raivata’s daughter Rājñi gave birth to a son (called) Revata. Prabhā gave birth to Prabhāta and Saṃjñā to Manu.

## \|\| 8.39-40 \|\|

*yamaśca yamunā caiva yamalau ca babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*tatastejomayaṃ rūpamasahaṃtī vivasvataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*nārīmutpādayāmāsa svaśarīrādaniṃditāṃ \|*  
*tvāṣṭrī svarūparūpeṇa nāmnā chāyeti bhāminī \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. The twins Yama and Yamunā were also born (to Saṃjñā). Then unable to bear Vivasvān’s lustre, she, the beautiful daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, produced from her own body, a blameless lady, Chāyā by name.

## \|\| 8.41-42 \|\|

*kiṃkaromīti purataḥ saṃsthitāṃ tāmabhāṣata \|*  
*chāye tvaṃ bhaja bhartāraṃ madīyaṃ taṃ varānane \|\| 41 \|\|*

*apatyāni madīyāni mātṛsnehena pālaya \|*  
*tathetyuktvā ca sā devamagātkāmāya suvratā \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. To her, who stood before her saying; “what should I do?” she said: “O beautiful Chāyā, you serve my husband, nourish my children with motherly affection” Saying “All right” she of a righteous vow, went to god (Vivasvān) for sensual enjoyment.

## \|\| 8.43-45 \|\|

*kāmayāmāsa devopi saṃjñeyamiti cādarāt \|*  
*janayāmāsa sāvarṇiṃ manuṃ manusvarūpiṇam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*savarṇatvācca sāvarṇermanorvaivasvatasya tu \|*  
*tataḥ sutāṃ ca tapatīṃ tvāṣṭrīṃ caiva krameṇa tu \|\| 44 \|\|*

*chāyāyāṃ janayāmāsa saṃjñeyamiti bhāskaraḥ \|*  
*chāyā svaputre tvadhikaṃ snehaṃ cakre manau tadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

43-45. The god too, taking her to be Saṃjñā, longed for her with regard, (and) generated Sāvarṇi Manu resembling Manu (the son of Saṃjñā) in form due to his having complexion similar to that of Vaivasvata Manu. Then in due order he generated a daughter by name Tapatī, on Chāyā, the daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, taking her to be Saṃjñā. Chāyā loved her son Manu more.

## \|\| 8.46 \|\|

*na cakṣame manuḥ pūrvastadyamaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ \|*  
*saṃtarjayāmāsa tadā pādamutkṣipya dakṣiṇaṃ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The former Manu (i.e. the elder one) did not tolerate it. So Yama, violent with anger, and raising his right foot, threatened (her).

## \|\| 8.47 \|\|

*śaśāpa ca yamaṃ chāyā bhavatu krimisaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*pādoyameko bhavitā pūyaśoṇitavisravaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Chāyā too, cursed Yama: “This one foot will be full of worms and pus, and blood will ooze from it.”

## \|\| 8.48-49 \|\|

*nivedayāmāsa pituryamaḥ śāpena dharṣitaḥ \|*  
*niḥkāraṇamahaṃ śapto mātrā deva sakopayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bālabhāvānmayā kiṃcidudyataścaraṇaḥ sakṛt \|*  
*manunā vāryamāṇāpi mama śāpamadādvibho \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Insulted by this curse, Yama told his father: “O god, mother has angrily cursed me without any reason. Due to child-like nature, I raised my foot a little. O lord, even though warded off by Manu, she gave me a curse.

## \|\| 8.50-52 \|\|

*prāyo na mātā sāsmākamasamā snehato yataḥ \|*  
*devopyāha yamaṃ bhūyaḥ kiṃ karomi mahāmate \|\| 50 \|\|*

*saukhyātkasya na duḥkhaṃ syādathavā karmasaṃtatiḥ \|*  
*anivāryā bhavasyāpi kā kathānyeṣu jaṃtuṣu \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kṛkavākustava pade sa krimiṃ bhakṣayiṣyati \|*  
*khaṃjaṃ ca ruciraṃ caiva pādametadbhaviṣyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. Probably she is not our mother, since she is partial in her love.” God (Vivasvān) also said in return to Yama: “O highly intelligent one, what should I do? Who does not get misery after happiness? Or (rather), the flow of karma is difficult to be resisted even by Bhava, then what about other creatures? A cock will eat the worms on your leg. This leg of yours will be lame and charming.”

## \|\| 8.53-54 \|\|

*evamuktaḥ samāśvastastapastīvraṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*vairāgyātpuṣkare tīrthe phalaphenānilāśanaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pitāmahaṃ samārādhya yāvadvarṣāyutaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tapaḥprabhāvāddeveśaḥ saṃtuṣṭaḥ padmasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Thus addressed and consoled, he, through detachment, and subsisting on fruits, foam and wind, and propitiating Brahmā, practised, for myriads of years, a severe penance at Puṣkara Tīrtha. The lotus-born one was pleased by the power of his penance.

## \|\| 8.55 \|\|

*vavre sa lokapālatvaṃ pitṛlokaṃ tathākṣayaṃ \|*  
*dharmādharmātmakasyāsya jagatastu parīkṣaṇam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He asked for the lordship of the world and for the eternal world of Pitṛs, and putting to test this world full of piety and impiety.

## \|\| 8.56 \|\|

*evaṃ sa lokapālatvamagamatpadmasaṃbhavāt \|*  
*pitṝṇāmādhipatyaṃ ca dharmādharmasya cānagha \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O innocent one, he thus obtained the lordship of the world, the supremacy over the Pitṛs and over piety and impiety.

## \|\| 8.57 \|\|

*vivasvānatha tajjñātvā saṃjñāyāḥ karmaceṣṭitaṃ \|*  
*tvaṣṭuḥ samīpamagamadācacakṣe saroṣavān \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Vivasvān then having come to know that act of Saṃjñā, went to Tvaṣṭṛ and angrily reported it to him.

## \|\| 8.58-60 \|\|

*tamuvāca tatastvaṣṭā sāṃtvapūrvamidaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*tavāsahaṃtī bhagavaṃstejastīvraṃ tamonuda \|\| 58 \|\|*

*baḍavārūpamāsthāya matsakāśamihāgatā \|*  
*nivāritā mayā sā ca tvadbhayena divaspate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*yasmādavijñātamanā matsakāśamihāgatā \|*  
*tasmānmadīyaṃ bhavanaṃ praveṣṭuṃ na tavārhati \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Then Tvaṣṭṛ said these kind words to him: “O remover of darkness, not being able to bear your severe lustre, she came to me here, I, fearing you, kept her off, O lord of the sky. ‘Since you have come to me here without your intention being known (by your husband), please do not enter my house’.

## \|\| 8.61 \|\|

*evamuktā jagāmāśu marudeśamaniṃditā \|*  
*baḍavārūpamāsthāya bhūtale saṃpratiṣṭhitā \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Thus addresed, she the blameless one, quickly went to the Maru country and taking the form of a mare, lived on the earth.

## \|\| 8.62-66 \|\|

*tasmātprasādaṃ kuru me yadyanugrahabhāgaham \|*  
*apaneṣyāmi te tejaḥ kṛtvā yaṃtre divākaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*rūpaṃ tava kariṣyāmi lokānaṃdakaraṃ prabho \|*  
*tathetyuktaḥ sa raviṇā bhrame kṛtvā divākaraṃ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*pṛthakcakāra tejaśca cakraṃ viṣṇoḥ prakalpayat \|*  
*triśūlaṃ cāpi rudrasya vajramiṃdrasya cāparaṃ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*daityadānavasaṃhartṛ sahasrakiraṇātmakaṃ \|*  
*rūpaṃ cāpratimaṃ cakre tvaṣṭā padbhyāmṛte mahat \|\| 65 \|\|*

*na śaśāka ca taddraṣṭuṃ pādarūpaṃ raveḥ punaḥ \|*  
*adyāpi ca tataḥ pādau na kaścitkārayetkvacit \|\| 66 \|\|*

62-66. “Therefore, show favour to me if I deserve it. Putting you on a machine I shall take off your lustre and will make your appearance delightful to the eyes of the world, O lord.” When the Sun said to him, “All right”, he separated the Sun’s lustre from him, and fashioned from it Viṣṇu’s disk, and also Rudra’s trident and Indra’s bolt (all) capable of destroying the demons and the friends. Tvaṣṭṛ made the Sun’s form matchless and having a thousand rays, (but) without feet. He could not see the form of the feet of the Sun. Even now nobody should ever fashion the (Sun’s image with) feet.

## \|\| 8.67 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti sa pāpiṣṭho gatimāpnoti niṃditāṃ \|*  
*kuṣṭharogamavāpnoti lokesminduḥkhasaṃjñitaṃ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He, the most sinful one, who fashions it, reaches a censured condition, and contracts leprosy, known to be miserable in this world.

## \|\| 8.68 \|\|

*tasmānna dharmakāmārthī citreṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*na kvacitkārayetpādau devadevasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Therefore one, desiring religious merit and sensual enjoyments, should never fashion in pictures and temples the feet of the intelligent lord of lords.

## \|\| 8.69-70 \|\|

*tataḥ sa bhagavāngatvā bhūrlokamamarādhipaḥ \|*  
*kāmayāmāsa kāmārto mukha eva divākaraḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*aśvarūpeṇa mahatā tejasā ca samanvitaḥ \|*  
*saṃjñā ca manasā kṣobhamagamadbhayavihvalā \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Then the love-striken lord of gods going to the earth in the guise of a horse and endowed with great lustre, had oral coitus with her; and the mind of Saṃjñā, afflicted by fear, became agitated.

## \|\| 8.71 \|\|

*nāsāpuṭābhyāmutsṛṣṭaṃ paroyamiti śaṃkayā \|*  
*tasyātha retaso jātāvaśvināviti naḥ śrutam \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Suspecting him to be a stranger, she threw out (his semen) through her nostrils. We have heard that from that semen Aśvins were born.

## \|\| 8.72 \|\|

*dasrau śrutitvātsaṃjātau nāsatyau nāsikāgrataḥ \|*  
*jñātvā cirācca taṃ devaṃ saṃtoṣamagamatparaṃ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. They became known as Dasra (wonder-workers) and Nāsatya (truthful) (due to their being born) from the nostrils.

## \|\| 8.73 \|\|

*vimānenāgamatsvarge patnyā saha mudānvitaḥ \|*  
*sāvarṇyopi manurmerāvadyāpi tapate tapaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Full of joy, he went to the heaven with his wife in an aeroplane. Sāvarṇya Manu also is even now practising penance on Meru.

## \|\| 8.74 \|\|

*śanistapobalāccāpi grahāṇāṃ samatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*yamunā tapatī caiva punarnadyau babhūvatuḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Śani also, due to the power of his penance, attained equality with the planets, and Yamunā and Tapatī became rivers.

## \|\| 8.75 \|\|

*viṣṭhirghorātmikā tadvatkālatvena vyavasthitā \|*  
*manorvaivasvatasyāpi daśa putrā mahābalāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Similarly, Viṣṭhi too, of a terrible form, settled in the form of time. Vaivasvata Manu too had ten sons.

## \|\| 8.76-77 \|\|

*ilastu prathamasteṣāṃ putreṣṭyā samakalpi yaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākuḥ kuśanābhaśca ariṣṭo dhṛṣṭa eva ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*nariṣyaṃtaḥ karūṣaśca śaryātiśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣadhraścātha nābhāgaḥ sarve te divyamānuṣāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. Out of them Ila was the first who was born as a result of a sacrifice performed to obtain a male issue. (The ten sons were:) Ikṣvāku, Kuśanābha, Ariṣṭa and Dhṛṣṭa, Nariṣyanta, Karūṣa, and very powerful Śaryāti, Pṛṣadhra, and Nābhāga; all these were divine men.

## \|\| 8.78 \|\|

*abhiṣicya manuḥ pūrvamilaṃ putraṃ sa dhārmikam \|*  
*jagāma tapase bhūyaḥ puṣkaraṃ sa tapovanaṃ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Manu, having first consecrated his righteous son Ila, went to the Puṣkara penance-grove for (practising) penance.

## \|\| 8.79 \|\|

*athājagāma sidhyarthaṃ tasya brahmā varapradaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te mānaveya yathepsitaṃ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. For his success Brahmā, the giver of boons, came there, (and said to him:) “Well-being to you, O Mānaveya; ask for a boon”.

## \|\| 8.80-81 \|\|

*uvāca sa tadā devaṃ padmākṣaṃ padmajaṃ vibhuṃ \|*  
*vaṃśe me dharmasaṃyuktāḥ pṛthivyāṃ sarvapārthivāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*bhaveyurīśvarāḥ svāminprasādāttava kaṃjaja \|*  
*tathetyuktvā tu deveśastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Then he said to the lotus-born god, having lotuslike eyes: “O lotus-born, lord, let all the righteous kings, the lords on the earth, be under my control, through your favour”. Saying “Let it be so”, the lord of gods vanished there only.

## \|\| 8.82-85 \|\|

*tatoyodhyāṃ samāgatya samatiṣṭhadyathā purā \|*  
*athaikadā rathārūḍha ilo nija suto manoḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*nirjagāmārthasidhyarthaminaprāyāṃ mahīmimāṃ \|*  
*bhramandvīpāni sarvāṇi kṣmābhṛtaḥ saṃprasādhayan \|\| 83 \|\|*

*jagāmopavanaṃ śaṃbhorathākṛṣṭaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*kalpadrumalatākīrṇaṃ nāmnā śaravaṇaṃ mahat \|\| 84 \|\|*

*ramate yatra deveśaḥ somaḥ somārddhaśekharaḥ \|*  
*umayā samayastatra purā śaravaṇe kṛtaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

82-85. Then coming (back) to Ayodhyā, he lived as before. Then, once, Ila, Manu’s son, seated in a chariot, moved out on this earth, rich with kings, for the fulfilment of an object, and roaming overall regions and subduing kings; and he, the brave one, being attracted, went to Śaṅkara’s great grove called Śaravaṇa, full of desire-yielding creepers and trees, in which, Śiva, lord of gods, having the crescent moon on his head, sports with Umā. Formerly a convention was fixed about that Śaravaṇa:

## \|\| 8.86 \|\|

*puṃnāmasaṃjñaṃ yatkiṃcidāgamiṣyati no vanaṃ \|*  
*strītvameṣyati tatsarvaṃ daśayojanamaṃḍale \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. “Whatever called male enters our grove, all that, within a radius of ten yojanas, will turn into a female.”

## \|\| 8.87 \|\|

*ajñātasamayo rājā ilaḥ śaravaṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*strītvaṃ jagāma sahasā baḍavāśvo'bhavatkṣaṇāt \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Not knowing this convention, king Ila entered Śaravaṇa, (and) instantly became a woman, and the same moment (his) horse turned into a mare.

## \|\| 8.88-91 \|\|

*puruṣatve kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ strīkāye vismṛtaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*ileti sābhavannārī pīnonnataghanastanī \|\| 88 \|\|*

*unnataśroṇijaghanā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā \|*  
*pūrṇenduvadanā tanvī vilāsinyasitekṣaṇā \|\| 89 \|\|*
