*pīnonnatāyatabhujā nīlakuṃcitamūrddhajā \|*  
*tanulomā suvadanā mṛdugadgadabhāṣiṇī \|\| 90 \|\|*

*śyāmāgaureṇa varṇena tanutāmranakhāṃkurā \|*  
*kārmukabhrūyugopetā haṃsāvaraṇagāminī \|\| 91 \|\|*

88-91. And while in the female body, he forgot everything that he did as a man; he became a slender lady called llā, having plump, raised and compact breasts, raised hips and loins, having long and dark eyes like lotus-leaves, having a face like the full moon, having plump, raised and long arms, and dark, curly and fine hair, of a charming face and talking sweetly and indistinctly, of a slender shape, with a fair complexion, and having thin, reddish, sprout-like nails, having bow-like eyebrows, and with a gait concealing (i.e. superior to) that of a swan.

## \|\| 8.92-94 \|\|

*bhramamāṇā vane tasminciṃtayāmāsa bhāminī \|*  
*ko me pitā vā bhrātā vā ko me trātā bhavediha \|\| 92 \|\|*

*kasya bhartturahaṃ dattā kiyadvarṣāsmi bhūtale \|*  
*ciṃtayaṃtī ca dadṛśe somaputreṇa sāṅganā \|\| 93 \|\|*

*ilārūpa samākṣipta manasā varavarṇinī \|*  
*budhastadāptaye yatnamakarotkāmapīḍitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

92-94. The beautiful young woman, wandering in the forest, thought: ‘Who would be my father, or brother, or mother here? To which husband am I given? For how many years am I (living) on the earth?’ While thinking (thus), she, a lady of an excellent complexion, was seen by (Budha), the son of Soma, with his mind seized by the figure of Ilā. Budha, oppressed by love, tried to secure her.

## \|\| 8.95-96 \|\|

*viśiṣṭākāravānmuṃḍī sa kamaṃḍalupustakaḥ \|*  
*veṇudaṃḍakṛtāveśaḥ pavitraka khanitrakaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*dvijarūpaḥ śikhī brahma nigadankarṇakuṃḍalī \|*  
*vaṭubhiścārthibhiryuktaḥ samitpuṣpakuśodakaiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

95-96. He, of a distinguished form, bald-headed, entered the grove with a water-pot and a book, a bamboo-stick in his hand, having a ring of kuśa-grass and a shovel, with a brāhmaṇa’s form, having a tuft of hair, reciting Veda, wearing earrings, accompanied by young boys and having sacred fuel, flowers, kuśa grass and water.

## \|\| 8.97-100 \|\|

*kālenviṣyāṃ tatastasminnājuhāva sa tāmilām \|*  
*bahirvanasyāṃtaritaḥ kila pādapamaṃḍape \|\| 97 \|\|*

*sasaṃbhramamakasmācca sopālaṃbhamivābhavat \|*  
*tyaktvāgnihotraśuśrūṣāṃ kva gatā maṃdirānmama \|\| 98 \|\|*

*iyaṃ vihāravelā te atikrāmati sāṃpratam \|*  
*ehyehi pṛthusuśroṇi saṃbhrāṃtā kena hetunā \|\| 99 \|\|*

*iyaṃ sāyaṃtanī velā vihārasyeha varttate \|*  
*kṛtvopalepanaṃ puṣpairalaṃkuru gṛhaṃ mama \|\| 100 \|\|*

97-100. At that time, having looked into it, he hastily concealing himself in a bower outside the grove, called that Ilā, and it was, as it were, an unexpected taunt (for her). “Leaving the service of my sacred fire, where have you gone? Now the time for your sport is over, O you of large hips, come on; why are you confused? This evening time is here, the time for diversion. Having besmeared ground, adorn my house with flowers”.

## \|\| 8.101 \|\|

*sābravīdvismṛtāhaṃ ca sarvameva tapodhana \|*  
*ātmānaṃ tvāṃ ca bharttāraṃ kulaṃ ca vada menagha \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. She said: “O you having penance as your wealth, I have forgotten all th is. Tell me all about myself, about you—my husband, and my family, O sinless one.”

## \|\| 8.102 \|\|

*budhaḥ provāca tāṃ tanvīmilā tvaṃ varavarṇinī \|*  
*ahaṃ ca kāmuko nāma bahuvidyo budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Budha said to that slender lady: “O you ofexcellent complxion, you are Ilā, and I am known as passionate Budha, well-versed in many lores.

## \|\| 8.103-105 \|\|

*tejasvinaḥ kule jātaḥ pitā me brāhmaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*iti sā tasyavacanātpraviṣṭā budhamaṃdiram \|\| 103 \|\|*

*ratnastaṃbhasamākīrṇaṃ divyamāyāvinirmitam \|*  
*ilā kṛtārthamātmānaṃ mene tadbhavane sthitā \|\| 104 \|\|*

*aho vṛttamahorūpamaho dhanamahokulam \|*  
*mama cāsya ca bhartturvā aho lāvaṇyamuttamam \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. I am born in the family of the brilliant one (i.e. Soma); my father is the chief of the brāhmaṇas.” After these words uttered by him, she entered Buddha’s abode, full of jewelled pillars, fashioned with divine illusion. Ilā, having remained in that house regarded herself to be blessed. ‘Oh! wonderful are the vow, the figure, the wealth and the family of this my lord’.

## \|\| 8.106 \|\|

*reme ca sā tena samamatikālamilā vane \|*  
*sarvabhogamaye gehe yatheṃdrabhavane tathā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. And Ilā sported with him in the forest for a long time, in the house full of all enjoyments as in Indra’s residence.

## \|\| 8.107 \|\|

*athānviṣyaṃto rājānaṃ bhrātarastasya mānavāḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākupramukhā jagmustadā śaravaṇāṃtikam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Then the king’s brothers, the sons of Manu, Ikṣvāku and others, looking for him, came to that Śaravaṇa.

## \|\| 8.108 \|\|

*tataste dadṛśuḥ sarve vaḍavāmagrataḥ sthitām \|*  
*ratnaparyaṃtakiraṇadīpyamānāmanuttamām \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then they all saw an excellent mare, shining with rays shooting from the points of gems, standing in front of them.

## \|\| 8.109-110 \|\|

*saṃprāpya pratyabhijñānātsarve vismayamāgatāḥ \|*  
*ayaṃ caṃdraprabho nāma vājī tasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*agamadvaḍavārūpamuttamaṃ kena hetunā \|*  
*tatastu maitrāvaruṇiṃ papracchuḥ svapurohitam \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Recognising her, all of them were amazed. ‘This is the horse, Candraprabha by name, of that magnanimous one. Why has he turned into an excellent mare?’ Then they asked Maitrāvaruṇi (i.e. Vasiṣṭha), their priest (about it).

## \|\| 8.111 \|\|

*kimetadityabhūccitraṃ vada yogavidāṃ vara \|*  
*vasiṣṭhopyabravītsarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ dhyānacakṣuṣā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. “O you best among the contemplative sages, tell us, as to what this extraordinary appearance is”. Vasiṣṭha too, knowing all that bymeans of his divine intuition, said:

## \|\| 8.112-114 \|\|

*samayaḥ śaṃbhudayitā kṛtaḥ śaravaṇe purā \|*  
*yaḥ pumānpraviśeccātra sa nārītvamavāpsyati \|\| 112 \|\|*

*ayamaśvopi nārītvamagādrājñā sahaiva tu \|*  
*ilaḥ puruṣatāmeti yathāsau dhanadopamaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*tathaiva yatnaḥ karttavya ārādhya ca pinākinam \|*  
*tataste mānavā jagmuryatra devo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. “Formerly in the Śaravaṇa a stipulation was laid down by Śambhu’s wife: The man who would enter this grove will become a woman. This horse also, along with the king, turned into a female. Propitiating the trident-holder (i.e. Śiva), make such an effort that this Ilā will (again) turn into a man resembling Kubera.”

## \|\| 8.115 \|\|

*tuṣṭavurvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ pārvatīparameśvarau \|*  
*tāvūcaturalaṃ caiṣa samayaḥ kiṃ nu sāṃprataṃ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. With various eulogies they praised Pārvatī and the highest lord (Śiva). They (two) said: “Severe is the stipulation.

## \|\| 8.116 \|\|

*ikṣvākoraśvamedhena yatphalaṃ syāttadāvayoḥ \|*  
*datvā kiṃpuruṣo vīraḥ sa bhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. What indeed is proper? Having given us that fruit which will accrue through Īkṣvāku’s horse-sacrifice the brave one will undoubtedly be a low man (kiṃpuruṣa?).”

## \|\| 8.117 \|\|

*tathetyuktvā tu te sarve jagmurvaivasvatātmajāḥ \|*  
*iṣṭvāśvamedhena tata ilā kiṃpuruṣobhavat \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Saying “All right”, all those sons of Vaivasvata went (from that place). After the performance of the horse-sacrifice, Ilā became a low man.

## \|\| 8.118-119 \|\|

*māsamekaṃ pumānvīraḥ strītvaṃ māsamabhūtpunaḥ \|*  
*budhasya bhavane tiṣṭhannilo garbhadharobhavat \|\| 118 \|\|*

*ajījanatputramekamanekaguṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*budha utpādya taṃ pūruṃ sa svargamagamatpunaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

118-119. The brave one became a man for one month, and a woman for another. Remaining in the house of Budha, Ilā became pregnant, and gave birth to a son endowed with many good qualities. Budha, having generated that Pūru, again went to heaven.

## \|\| 8.120 \|\|

*ilasya nāmnā tadvarṣamilāvṛtamabhūttadā \|*  
*somārkavaṃśajo rājā ilobhūdvaṃśavarddhanaḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Then, after Ilā’s name that region became (i.e. came to be called) ‘Ilāvṛta’. King Ila born in the lunar and solar families, increased his family.

## \|\| 8.121 \|\|

*evaṃ purūravāḥ pūrorabhavadvaṃśavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākurarkavaṃśasya tathaivokto nareśvaraḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Similarly Purūravas, who increased the family was born from Pūru. And king Ikṣvāku was said to (belong to) the solar race.

## \|\| 8.122-126 \|\|

*ilaḥ kiṃpuruṣatve ca sudyumna iti cocyate \|*  
*punaḥ putratrayamabhūtsudyumnasyāparājitam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*utkalotha gayastadvaddharitāśvaśca vīryavān \|*  
*utkalasyotkalā nāma gayasya tu gayāpurī \|\| 123 \|\|*

*haritāśvasya digyāmyā saṃjñātā kurubhiḥ saha \|*  
*pratiṣṭhānebhiṣicyātha sa purūravasaṃ sutam \|\| 124 \|\|*

*jagāmelāvṛtaṃ bhoktuṃ divyaṃ varṣaṃ phalāśanaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākurjyeṣṭhadāyādo madhyadeśamavāptavān \|\| 125 \|\|*

*nariṣyaṃtasya putrobhūcchuko nāma mahābalaḥ \|*  
*nābhāgādaṃbarīṣastu dhṛṣṭasya tu sutatrayam \|\| 126 \|\|*

122-126. Ila is called Sudyumna in his low man’s condition. Again, three victorious sons were born to Sudyumna: Utkala, and Gaya, and powerful Haritāśva. The city of Utkala is Utkalā by name; that of Gaya is Gayā; (to its) south, along with the Kuru-country is said to be the region of Haritāśva. Having consecrated his son Purūravas, as the king, he went to Ilāvṛta to enjoy (there) for a divine year, subsisting on fruits. Ikṣvāku, the eldest son, got the Madhyadeśa (as his kingdom). Śuka of great strength was the son of Nariṣyanta. Ambarīṣa was born from Nābhāga.

## \|\| 8.127 \|\|

*dhṛṣṭaketuḥ svadharmātho raṇadhṛṣṭaśca vīryavān \|*  
*ānarto nāma śaryāteḥ sukanyā caiva dārikā \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Dhṛṣṭa had three sons: Dhṛṣṭaketu, Svadharman and the valorous Raṇadhṛṣṭa. Śaryāti’s son was Ānarta, and his daughter was Sukanyā.

## \|\| 8.128 \|\|

*ānartasyābhavatputro rocamānaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*ānarto nāma deśobhūnnagarī ca kuśasthalī \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Brave Rocamāna was the son of Ānarta; his country was Ānarta, and (capital) city was Kuśasthalī.

## \|\| 8.129 \|\|

*rocamānasya revobhūdrevādraivata eva ca \|*  
*kakudmī cāparaṃ nāma jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasya ca \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Rocamāna’s son was Reva, and from Reva was born Raivata; his other name was Kakudmin; he was the eldest among (Reva’s) sons.

## \|\| 8.130 \|\|

*revatī tasya sā kanyā bhāryā rāmasya viśrutā \|*  
*karūṣāccaiva kārūṣā bahavaḥ prathitā bhuvi \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Revatī was his daughter; she is known to be the wife of (Bala-) Rāma; and from Karūṣā, were born Kārūṣas, well-known on the earth.

## \|\| 8.131 \|\|

*pṛṣadhro govadhācchūdro guruśāpādajāyata \|*  
*ikṣvākuputrā nāmnātha vikukṣi nimidaṃḍakāḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Pṛṣadhra became a Śūdra as a result of a cow’s slaughter, due to his preceptor’s curse. Ikṣvāku’s sons named Vikukṣi, Nimi, Daṇḍaka were pre-eminant among his hundred sons.

## \|\| 8.132 \|\|

*śreṣṭhāḥ putraśatasyāsanpaṃcāśaccātha tatsutāḥ \|*  
*meroruttarataste tu jātāḥ pārthivasattamāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. His other fifty sons became best kings to the north of Meru.

## \|\| 8.133 \|\|

*catvāriṃśattathāṣṭānye śatamadhye ca yebhavan \|*  
*merordakṣiṇataścaiva rājānaste prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Forty-eight out of the hundred were known to be the kings to the south of Meru.

## \|\| 8.134 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhātkakutsthanāmābhūtsutastasya suyodhanaḥ \|*  
*tasya putraḥ pṛthṛrnāma viśvastasya pṛthoḥ sutaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. From the eldest son was born Kakutstha. His son was Suyodhana. His son was Pṛthu. Viśva was the son of that Pṛthu.

## \|\| 8.135 \|\|

*ārdrastasya ca putrobhūdyuvanāśvastatobhavat \|*  
*yuvanāśvasya putrobhūcchāvasto nāma vīryavān \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. His (Viśva’s) son was Ārdra; from him was born Yuvanāśva.

## \|\| 8.136 \|\|

*nirmitā yena śāvastī hyaṃgadeśe narādhipa \|*  
*śāvastādbṛhadaśvo bhūtkuvalāśvastatobhavat \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Yuvanāśva’s valourous son was Śāvasta, by whom was set up Śāvastī in the Aṅga country, O prince.

Bṛhadaśva was born of Śāvasta, and from Bṛhadaśva Kuvalāśva was born.

## \|\| 8.137-138 \|\|

*dhuṃdhumāratvamagamaddhuṃdhuṃ hatvā'suraṃ purā \|*  
*tasya putrāstrayo jātā dṛḍhāśvo ghṛṇireva ca \|\| 137 \|\|*

*kapilāśvaśca vikhyāto dhauṃdhumāriḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*dṛḍhāśvasya pramodastu haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

137-138. He became (i.e. came to be called) Dhundhumāra for having formerly killed the demon Dhundhu. He had three sons; Dṛḍhāśva and Ghṛṇi, and the brave Kapilāśva was also the famous son of Dhundhumāra. Dṛḍhāśva’s son was Pramoda, and his son was Haryaśva.

## \|\| 8.139 \|\|

*haryaśvasya nikuṃbhobhūtsaṃhatāśvastatobhavat \|*  
*akṛtāśvo raṇāśvaśca saṃhatāśva sutāvubhau \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Haryaśva’s son was Nikumbha, and from him was born Saṃhatāśva. Akṛtāśva and Raṇāśva were the two sons of Saṃhatāśva.

## \|\| 8.140-141 \|\|

*yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya māṃdhātā ca tatobhavat \|*  
*māṃdhātuḥ purukutsobhūddharmasetuśca pārthivaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

*mucukundaśca vikhyātaśśakramitraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*purukutsasya putrobhūddussaho narmadāpatiḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

140-141. Raṇāśva’s son was Yuvanāśva and from him was born Māndhātr. Purukutsa and king Dharmasetu, well known Mucukunda and the brave Śakramitra were born from Māndhātṛ. Dussaha, Narmadā’s husband, was the son of Purukutsa.

## \|\| 8.142 \|\|

*saṃbhūtistasya putrobhūttridhanvā ca tatobhavat \|*  
*tridhanvanaḥ suto jātastrayyāruṇa iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. His (Dussaha’s) son was Sambhūti; from him was born Tridhanvan; the son born to Tridhanvan is known as Trayyāruṇa.

## \|\| 8.143 \|\|

*tasya satyavrato nāma tasmātsatyarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro hariścandro hariścaṃdrācca rohitaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. His son was Satyavrata; his son was known to be Satyaratha; his son was Hariścandra; Rohita was born from Hariścandra.

## \|\| 8.144 \|\|

*rohatācca vṛko jāto vṛkādbāhurajāyata \|*  
*sagarastasya putrobhūdrājā paramadhārmikaḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Vṛka was born from Rohita, and Bāhu from Vṛka. Sagara who was a very religious king was his son.

## \|\| 8.145 \|\|

*dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā \|*  
*tābhyāmārādhitaḥ pūrvamaurvāgniḥ putrakāmyayā \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Sagara had two wives; Prabhā and Bhānumati. In olden days they propitiated Aurvāgni (the sub-marine fire).

## \|\| 8.146 \|\|

*aurvastuṣṭastayoḥ prādādyatheṣṭaṃ varamuttamam \|*  
*ekā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi sutamekaṃ tathāparā \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Aurva, pleased with them, granted them an excellent boon as desired by them.

## \|\| 8.147 \|\|

*agṛhṇādvaṃśakartāraṃ prabhā'gṛhṇādbahūnsutān \|*  
*ekaṃ bhānumatī putramagṛhṇādasamaṃjasaṃ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. One asked for sixty thousand sons; the other chose a son continuing the race. Prabhā chose many sons, Bhānumatī chose one son, viz. Asamañjasa.

## \|\| 8.148 \|\|

*tataḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi suṣuve yādavī prabhā \|*  
*khanaṃtaḥ pṛthivīṃ dagdhā viṣṇunā ye 'śvamārgaṇe \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. Prabhā, of the Yadu family, gave birth to sixty thousand sons, who pursuing the (Aśvamedha) horse dug the earth and were burnt in a group by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 8.149-150 \|\|

*asamaṃjastu tanayo hyaṃśumānnāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro dilīpastu dilīpāttu bhagīrathaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

*yena bhāgīrathī gaṅgā tapaḥ kṛtvāvatāritā \|*  
*bhagīrathasya tanayo nābhāga iti viśrutaḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. The well known son of Asamañjasa was Aṃśumān; his son was Dilīpa; from him Bhagīratha was born, who, by performing a penance brought down the Ganges (known) as Bhāgīrathī (after him) (to the earth). Bhagīratha’s son was the well-known Nābhāga.

## \|\| 8.151 \|\|

*nābhāgasyāṃbarīṣobhūtsiṃdhudvīpastatobhavat \|*  
*tasyāyutāyuḥ putrobhūdṛtuparṇastatobhavat \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Nābhāga’s son, was Ambarīṣa; from him Sindhudvīpa was born; his son was Ayutāyu, and from his Ṛtuparṇa was born.

## \|\| 8.152 \|\|

*tasya kalmāṣapādastu sarvakarmā tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyānaraṇyaḥ putrobhūnnighnastasya sutobhavat \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. His son was Kalmāṣapāda. Sarvakarman is known to have been born to him. His son was Anaraṇya; his son was Nighna.

## \|\| 8.153 \|\|

*nighnaputrāvubhau jātāvanamitra raghūttamau \|*  
*anamitro vanamagādarināśakṛte nṛpa \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Nighna had two sons: Anamitra and Raghūttama. Anamitra went to the forest after having destroyed his enemies.

## \|\| 8.154 \|\|

*raghorabhūddilīpastu dilīpāccāpyajastathā \|*  
*dīrghabāhurajājjātaḥ prajāpālastatobhavat \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. From Raghu was born Dilīpa and from Dilīpa Aja was born. Dīrghabāhu was born from Aja and from him (Dīrghabāhu) Prajāpāla was born.

## \|\| 8.155 \|\|

*tato daśaratho jātastasya putracatuṣṭayaṃ \|*  
*nārāyaṇātmakāḥ sarve rāmastasyāgrajobhavat \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. From him was born Daśaratha; he had four sons, of the nature of Nārāyaṇa, and Rāma was his eldest son.

## \|\| 8.156 \|\|

*rāvaṇāṃtakarastadvadraghūṇāṃ vaṃśavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*vālmīkiryasya caritaṃ cakre bhārgavasattamaḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. He destroyed Rāvaṇa and increased the race of Raghus. Vālmīki, the best of the Bhārgavas, composed his biography.

## \|\| 8.157 \|\|

*tasya putraḥ kuśo nāma ikṣvākukulavarddhanaḥ \|*  
*atithistu kuśājjāto niṣadhastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. His son was Kuśa by name, who increased the Ikṣvāku-race. Atithi was born from Kuśa and Niṣadha was his (Atithi’s) son.

## \|\| 8.158 \|\|

*nalastu niṣadhājjāto nabhāstasmādajāyata \|*  
*nabhasaḥ puṃḍarīkobhūtkṣemadhanvā tataḥ param \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. From Niṣadha was born Nala; from him was born Nabhas. From Nabhas Puṇḍarīka was born and from him Kṣemadhanvan was born.

## \|\| 8.159 \|\|

*tasyaputrobhavadvīro devānīkaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*ahīnagustasya sutaḥ sahasrāśvastataḥ paraḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. His son was the brave Devānīka; his son was Ahīnagu; Sahasrāśva was born from him.

## \|\| 8.160 \|\|

*tataścaṃdrāvalokastu tārāpīḍastatobhavat \|*  
*tasyātmajaścandragiriścaṃdrastasya sutobhavat \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. From him (Sahasrāśva) was born Candrāvaloka and from him Tārāpīḍa was born. His son was Candragiri, whose son was Candra.

## \|\| 8.161-162 \|\|

*śrutāyurabhavattasmādbhārate yo nipātitaḥ \|*  
*nalau dvāveva vikhyātau vaṃśe yasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*vīrasenasutastadvannaiṣadhaśca narādhipaḥ \|*  
*ete vivasvato vaṃśe rājāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

161-162. From him was born Śrutāyu, who was killed in the Bhārata war; in his family two Nalas only were particularly famous: the son of Vīrasena and the king Naiṣadha, i.e. the son of Niṣadha. These were the kings in Vivasvat’s race, who gave rich presents. (Thus) the important kings in the Ikṣvāku race have been described.

## Chapter 9 - General Rules of Śrāddha Performance

## \|\| 9.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanśrotumicchāmi pitṝṇāṃ vaṃśamuttamam \|*  
*raveśca śrāddhadevasya somasya ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. O revered one, I wish to learn about the best family of the manes (pitṛs), and also particularly of Ravi, of the deity of Śrāddha i.e. Soma.

## \|\| 9.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*haṃta te kathayiṣyāmi pitṝṇāṃ vaṃśamuttamam \|*  
*svarge pitṛgaṇāḥ sapta trayasteṣāmamūrtayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

2\. I shall narrate to you the best family of the manes. In the heaven there are seven groups of the manes. Out of them three are incorporeal.

## \|\| 9.3 \|\|

*mūrtimaṃtotha catvāraḥ sarveṣāmamitaujasāṃ \|*  
*amūrttayaḥ pitṛgaṇā vairājasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Of all (the manes) of unlimited lustre four are corporeal. The incorporeal groups of manes are said to belong to Vairāja Prajāpati.

## \|\| 9.4 \|\|

*yajanti yāndevagaṇā vairājā iti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*ye vai te yogavibhraṣṭāḥ prāpurlokānsanātanān \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They are (whom groups of gods worship) called Vairāja. They fallen from Yoga, attained eternal worlds.

## \|\| 9.5 \|\|

*punarbrahmadināṃte tu jāyaṃte brahmavādinaḥ \|*  
*saṃprāpya tāṃ smṛtiṃ bhūyo yogaṃ sāṃkhyamanuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Again at the end of Brahmā’s day, these teachers of Veda are born and would again get recollection and the excellent Sāṃkhya and Yoga.

## \|\| 9.6 \|\|

*siddhiṃ prayāṃti yogena punarāvṛttidurllabhām \|*  
*yogināmeva deyāni tasmācchāddhāni dātṛbhiḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Again by means of deep and abstract meditation they would attain the state of perfection, (reaching) which rebirth is not obtained. Therefore, givers of gifts should offer obsequial oblations to the Yogins only.

## \|\| 9.7 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā patnī himavato matā \|*  
*mainākastasya dāyādaḥ kraucastasya sutobhavat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The mind-born daughter of these is supposed to be the wife of Himālaya. Her son was Maināka, and his son was Krauñca.

## \|\| 9.8-10 \|\|

*krauṃcadvīpaḥ smṛto yena caturtho dhṛtasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*menā tu suṣave tisraḥ kanyā yogavatīstataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*umaikaparṇā parṇā ca tīvravrataparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*rudrasyaikā bhṛgoścaikā jaigīṣavyasya cāparā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dattā himavatā bālāḥ sarvalokatapodhikāḥ \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ lokasaṃgītaṃ kathayāmi śṛṇuṣva tat \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. He is remembered to have held together the fourth Dvīpa, viz. Krauñca. Menā gave birth to three daughters possessing deep and abstract meditation, viz. Umā, Ekaparṇā and Parṇā, engaged in severe vows. Himavat gave these daughters, superior due to their austerities, (marrying) one to Rudra, another to Bhṛgu and the third to Jaigiṣavya. I shall now tell you about the music in the world of manes; listen to it.

## \|\| 9.11 \|\|

*lokāḥ somapathā nāma yatra mārīcanaṃdanāḥ \|*  
*varttaṃte yena pitaro yāndevā bhāvayantyalam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. There are worlds named Somapatha, where live the sons of Mārīca; by (living there) they are manes, and gods honour them fully.

## \|\| 9.12 \|\|

*agniṣvāttā iti khyātā yajvāno yatra saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*acchodā nāma teṣāṃ tu kanyābhūdvaravarṇinī \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They lived where the sacrifices are called ‘Agniṣvātta’. Their daughter was Acchodā of excellent complexion.

## \|\| 9.13 \|\|

*acchodaṃ ca sarastatra pitṛbhirnirmitaṃ purā \|*  
*acchodātha tapaścakre divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Formerly the manes also fashioned there a lake named Acchodā. Acchodā practised penance for one thousand divine years.

## \|\| 9.14-15 \|\|

*ājagmuḥ pitarastuṣṭā dāsyantaḥ kila te varam \|*  
*divyarūpadharāḥ sarve divyamālyānulepanāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarve pradhānā balinaḥ kusumāyudhasannibhāḥ \|*  
*tanmadhyemāvasuṃ nāma pitaraṃ vīkṣya sāṃganā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The manes, having divine forms, having divine flowers and unguents, all pre-eminent, strong and resembling Cupid, came there and being pleased would indeed grant her a boon. That lady, having seen among them a mane named Amāvasu being oppressed by passion and desiring a groom, longed for him.

## \|\| 9.16-18 \|\|

*vavre varārthinī saṃgaṃ kusumāyudhapīḍitā \|*  
*yogādbhraṣṭā tu sā tena vyabhicāreṇa bhāminī \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dharānna spṛśate pūrvaṃ prayātātha bhuvastale \|*  
*tathaivāmāvasuryoyamicchāṃ cakre na tāṃ prati \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhairyeṇa tasya sā loke amāvāsyeti viśrutā \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ vallabhā yasmāddattasyākṣayakārikā \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Due to that violation that beautiful lady deviated from her concentration, went (down) to the earth, though she never touched the ground. And Amāvasu due to his steadiness did not long for her who had bowed to him. She came to be known in the world as Amāvāsyā. Since she was dear to the manes, she made the gift (given on Amāvāsyā) inexhaustible.

## \|\| 9.19 \|\|

*acchodādhomukhī dīnā lajjitā tapasaḥ kṣayāt \|*  
*sā pitṝnprārthayāmāsa punarātmasamṛddhaye \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Acchodā, helpless and with her face hung down due to the loss (of the merit) of her penance, again entreated the manes for her prosperity.

## \|\| 9.20 \|\|

*vilajjamānā pitṛbhiridamuktā tapasvinī \|*  
*bhaviṣyamatha cālokya devakāryaṃ ca te tadā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The bashful and miserable one was thus addressed by the manes taking into consideration her future and her worship of gods.

## \|\| 9.21 \|\|

*idamūcurmahābhāgāḥ prasāda śubhayāgirā \|*  
*divi divyaśarīreṇa yatkiṃcitkriyate budhaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The magnimous ones thus spoke to her with words auspicious due to their favour:

## \|\| 9.22 \|\|

*tenaiva tatkarmaphalaṃ bhujyate varavarṇinī \|*  
*sadyaḥ phalaṃti karmāṇi devatve pretyamānuṣe \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O you of excellent complexion, the fruit of whatever is done with a divine body in heaven is to be enjoyed with that (body) only. The deeds done in human life give their fruits instantly after death, in the divine life.

## \|\| 9.23 \|\|

*tasmāttvaṃ sukṛtaṃ kṛtvā prāpsyase pretya yatphalam \|*  
*aṣṭāviṃśe bhavitrī tvaṃ dvāpare matsyayonijā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Therefore perform good deeds whose fruits you will obtain after death. In the twenty-eighth Dvāpara-period you will be born in the fish species.

## \|\| 9.24 \|\|

*vyatikramātpitṝṇāṃ tu kaṣṭaṃ kulamavāpsyasi \|*  
*tasmādrājño vasoḥ kanyā tvamavaśyaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Due to your disregard for the manes you will obtain (birth in) an evil family. Thence you will certainly be the daughter of king Vasu.

## \|\| 9.25 \|\|

*kanyātve devalokāṃstānpunaḥ prāpsyasi durllabhān \|*  
*parāśarasya vīryeṇa putramekamavāpsyasi \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. As a maiden you will certainly obtain the divine worlds difficult to get.

## \|\| 9.26 \|\|

*dvīpe tu badarīprāye bādarāyaṇamapyuta \|*  
*sa vedamekaṃ bahudhā vibhajiṣyati te sutaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. From the semen of Parāśara you will get a son named Bādarāyaṇa in a grove full of the badari trees. That your son will divide one Veda into many.

## \|\| 9.27-28 \|\|

*pauravasyātmajau dvau tu samudrāṃśasya śaṃtanoḥ \|*  
*vicitravīryastanayastathā citrāṃgado nṛpaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*imāvutpādya tanayau kṣetrajau tasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*prauṣṭhapadyaṣṭakābhūyaḥ pitṛloke bhaviṣyasi \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Having begotten these two sons, viz. Vicitravīrya and Citrāṅgada, to that intelligent Paurava, viz. Śantanu, the secondary incarnation of Śiva, you will be again born as Prauṣṭhapadī and Aṣṭakā in the world of manes.

## \|\| 9.29-30 \|\|

*nāmnā satyavatī loke pitṛloke tathāṣṭakā \|*  
*āyurārogyadā nityaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyasi pare loke nadī tvaṃ ca gamiṣyasi \|*  
*puṇyatoyā saricchreṣṭhā lokeṣvacchodanāmikā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. In the (mortal) world you will be Satyavatī and Aṣṭakā in the world of manes. You will be giver of (long) life, health and wealth and will always fulfil all desires (while) in the other world; and you will become the river named Acchodā of holy water and the best river in the worlds.”

## \|\| 9.31 \|\|

*ityuktā sā gaṇaistaistu tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*sāpyāpacāritraphalaṃ mayā yaduditaṃ purā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Thus addressing her the groups (of manes) vanished there only; and she also obtained the fruit of her bad deed which I have already told.

## \|\| 9.32-34 \|\|

*vibhrājo nāma ye cānye divi saṃti suvarcasaḥ \|*  
*lokā barhiṣado yatra pitaraḥ saṃti suvratāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yatra barhiṣi yuktāni vimānāni sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*saṃkalpapādapā yatra tiṣṭhaṃti phaladāyinaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yadabhyudayaśālāsu modaṃte śrāddhadāyinaḥ \|*  
*ye dānavāsuragaṇā gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. In heaven there are other very lustrous worlds called Vibhrāj, where there are manes called Barhiṣad, of good vows, where (i.e. in these worlds) there are thousands of aeroplanes equipped with seats of Kuśa grass, where there are desire-yielding trees, in the halls for festive occasions in which those groups of demons, gods, Gandharvas, Apsarasas, also groups of Yakṣas, fiends, making obsequial offering are delighted and worship deities in heaven.

## \|\| 9.35 \|\|

*yakṣarakṣogaṇāste ca yajaṃti divi devatāḥ \|*  
*pulastyaputrāḥ śataśastapoyogabalānvitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. They (the Barhiṣads) are hundreds of sons of Pulastya; they are endowed with austerities and concentration of mind.

## \|\| 9.36 \|\|

*mahātmāno mahābhāgā bhaktānāmabhayaṃkarāḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ pīvarī kanyā mānasī divi viśrutā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. They are magnanimous ones and give security to their devotees.

## \|\| 9.37 \|\|

*yoginī yogamātā ca tapaścakre sudāruṇaṃ \|*  
*prasanno bhagavāṃstasyā varaṃ vavre tu sā tataḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Their mind-born daughter is known as Pīvarī. She, a contemplative saint and a divine mother, of abstract meditation, practised a very severe panance. The lord was pleased with her, and then she asked for a boon.

## \|\| 9.38 \|\|

*yogavaṃtaṃ surūpaṃ ca bhartāraṃ vijiteṃdriyam \|*  
*dehi deva prasannastvaṃ yadi te vadatāṃ vara \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. “O god, the foremost among the eloquent, if you are pleased, give me a husband possessed of abstract meditation, handsome and one who has controlled his organs of sense”.

## \|\| 9.39 \|\|

*uvāca devo bhavitā vyāsaputro yadā śukaḥ \|*  
*bhavitrī tasya bhāryā tvaṃ yogācāryasya suvratā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The lord said: “When Śuka, the master of Yoga (and), Vyāsa’s son, will be born, you, of a good vow, will be his wife.

## \|\| 9.40 \|\|

*bhaviṣyati ca te kanyā kṛttīnāmātha yoginī \|*  
*pāṃcālapataye deyā sātvatāya tu sā tadā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. You will have a saintly daughter Kṛtti by name; you should give her in marriage to Sāttvata, the lord of Pāñcāla.

## \|\| 9.41 \|\|

*jananī brahmadattasya yogasiddhāṃtagā smṛtā \|*  
*kṛṣṇa gauraśca śaṃbhuśca bhaviṣyaṃti ca te sutāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Then she will be the mother of Brahmadatta and will be known as having mastered the tenets of Yoga. You will have sons named Kṛṣṇagaura and Śambhu.

## \|\| 9.42 \|\|

*sarvakāmasamṛddheṣu vimāneṣvapi pāvanāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ punaḥ śrāddhadā viprā bhaktimaṃtaḥ kriyānvitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. They will be (regarded as) holy even among the specially respected ones who have all their desires fulfilled and are devoted; what to speak of the devoted brāhmaṇas who make obsequial offerings and perform (religious) rites?

## \|\| 9.43 \|\|

*gaurnāma kanyā yeṣāṃ tu mānasī divi rājate \|*  
*sukanyā dayitā patnī sādhyānāṃ kīrtivarddhinī \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. They have in heaven, a mind-born daughter named Gau. She is a good daughter, a loving wife and adds to the fame of the Sādhyas.

## \|\| 9.44 \|\|

*marīcigarbhanāmāno loke mārtaṃḍamaṃḍale \|*  
*pitaro yatra tiṣṭhaṃti haviṣmaṃtoṃgiraḥ sutāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. In the orb of the sun there are worlds named Marīci-garbha where the manes getting oblations and sons of Speech live.

## \|\| 9.45 \|\|

*tīrthaśrāddhapradā yāṃti yatra kṣatriyasattamāḥ \|*  
*rājñāṃ tu pitaraste vai svargabhogaphalapradāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. To these worlds go the best Kṣatriyas performing obsequial rites at sacred places; they are the ancestors of kings and are givers of fruits like enjoyments in heaven.

## \|\| 9.46 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā yaśodā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*patnī yāṃśumataḥ śreṣṭhā snuṣā paṃcajanasya ca \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The mind-born daughter is known to be Yaśodā, who is the wife of Aṃśumat and the eldest daughter-in-law of Pañcajana.

## \|\| 9.47 \|\|

*jananyatha dilīpasya bhagīrathapitāmahī \|*  
*lokāḥ kāmadughā nāma kāmabhogaphalapradāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. She is the mother of Dilīpa and grand-mother of Bhagīratha. There are worlds named Kāmadugha giving the fruits in the form of enjoyment of desires.

## \|\| 9.48-50 \|\|

*susvadhā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhanti te sutāḥ \|*  
*ājyapā nāma lokeṣu kardamasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pulahāgrajadāyādā vaiśyāstānbhāvayaṃti ha \|*  
*yatra śrāddhakṛtaḥ sarve paśyaṃti yugapadgatāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mātṛbhrātṛpitṛsvasṝḥ sakhisaṃbaṃdhibāṃdhavān \|*  
*apijanmāyutairdṛṣṭānanubhūtānsahasraśaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-50. There live sonless manes named Susvadhā. In the worlds named Ājyapā of Kardama Prajāpati, there are the elderly relatives of Pulaha and the Vaiśyas honour them; those who perform the obsequial rites go there and simultaneously meet their mothers, brothers, fathers, sisters, friends and relatives, thousands of whom, not known before, are seen there after myriads of existences.

## \|\| 9.51 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ mānasī kanyā virajā nāma viśrutā \|*  
*sā patnī nahuṣasyāsīdyayāterjananī tathā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The mind-born daughter of these is known as Virajā. She was the wife of Nahuṣa and the mother of Yayāti.

## \|\| 9.52 \|\|

*eṣāṣṭakābhavatpaścādbrahmalokagatā satī \|*  
*traya ete gaṇāḥ proktāścaturthaṃ tu vadāmyaham \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Later, she, having gone to the Brahmaloka, became Aṣṭakā. I have told you about these three groups. I shall (now) describe the fourth.

## \|\| 9.53 \|\|

*lokāḥ sumanaso nāma brahmalokoparisthitāḥ \|*  
*somapā nāma pitaro yatra tiṣṭhaṃti śāśvataṃ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There are worlds by name Sumanas which exist beyond the world of Brahmā. Here manes named Somapā live eternally.

## \|\| 9.54-57 \|\|

*dharmamūrtidharāḥ sarve parato brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*utpannāḥ pralayāṃte tu brahmatvaṃ prāpya yoginaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kṛtvā sṛṣṭyādikaṃ sarve mānase sāṃprataṃ sthitāḥ \|*  
*narmadā nāma teṣāṃ tu kanyā toyavahā sarit \|\| 55 \|\|*

*bhūtāni punatī yā tu paścimodadhigāminī \|*  
*tebhyaḥ sarvatra manujāḥ prajāsarge ca nirmitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

*jñātvā śrāddhāni kurvaṃti dharmabhāvena sarvadā \|*  
*sarvadā tebhya evāsya prasādādyogasaṃtatiḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. All they were further than Brahmā and were piety embodied. Born at the end of deluge, they, practising deep meditation having reached Brahman, and having fashioned the world etc. have now settled in Mānasa. Their daughter is the river Narmadā, who purifies beings and flows to the Western Ocean. Men, knowing that all beings and whatever is created at the time of creation are (created) from them, always devoutly offer obsequial offerings to them. From them only due to their favour a man gets devoted children.

## \|\| 9.58-59 \|\|

*pitṝṇāmādisarge tu śrāddhamevaṃ vinirmitam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ rājataṃ pātramathavā rājatānvitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*dattaṃ svadhāṃ purodhāya pitṝnprīṇāti sarvadā \|*  
*āgnīdhrasomapābhyāṃ tu kāryamāpyāyanaṃ budhaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Thus Śrāddha had been created at the first creation of the manes. Whatever is offered with the utterance of Svadhā to all these manes in a silver pot or a pot of imitation silver always pleases them. The wise should always satisfy the Āgnīdhra and the Somapā.

## \|\| 9.60 \|\|

*agnyabhāve tu viprasya pāṇau vātha jalepi vā \|*  
*ajākarṇeśvakarṇe vā goṣṭhe vātha śivāṃtike \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. In the absence of fire the offering (should be) made on the brāhmaṇa’s hand or under the Ajākarṇa or Aśvakarṇa tree or in a cowpen or near a god.

## \|\| 9.61 \|\|

*pitṝṇāmamalaṃ sthānaṃ dakṣiṇādikpraśasyate \|*  
*prācīnāvītamudakaṃ tilasaṃtyāgameva ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The proper place for the manes is said to be the southern direction. (While making offerings to them) the sacred thread should be worn over the right shoulder and passed under the left arm and offering of sesamum (should be made).

## \|\| 9.62-63 \|\|

*khaḍgiganāmāmiṣaṃ caivamannaṃ śyāmākaśālayaḥ \|*  
*yavanīvāramudgekṣu śuklapuṣpa phalāni ca \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vallabhāni praśastāni pitṝṇāmiha sarvadā \|*  
*darbhā māṣaṣṣaṣṭikānnaṃ gokṣīraṃ madhusarpiṣī \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. The flesh of rhinoceros, food, śyāmāka and śāli-grains, barley, nīvāra grains, kidney-beans, sugar-cane and white flowers and fruits are always dear to and commended for the manes, and also, Darbhas, beans, Ṣaṣṭikā-rice, sweetened milk, honey and ghee.

## \|\| 9.64-65 \|\|

*śastrāṇi ca pravakṣyāmi śrāddhe varjyāni yāni ca \|*  
*masūra śaṇa niṣpāvā rājamāṣāḥ kulutthakāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*padma bilvārkāduttūra pāribhadrāṭarūṣakāḥ \|*  
*na deyāḥ pitṛkāryeṣu payaścājāvikaṃ tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. I shall now tell you things to be avoided at the obsequial rite. Masūra-pulse. hemp (seeds), winnowed bean and Kuluttha grains, lotuses, bilva, flowers of sun-plant, of Duttūra, Nimba-leaves, Aṭarūṣa, and also goat-milk.

## \|\| 9.66 \|\|

*kodravodāravaraṭakapitthaṃ madhukātasī \|*  
*etānyapi na deyāni pitṝbhyaḥ śriyamicchatā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. One desiring wealth should not give Kodrava, Varāṭa, Kapittha, Aśoka-flowers and flax.

## \|\| 9.67 \|\|

*pitṛnprīṇāti yo bhaktyā te punaḥ prīṇayaṃti taṃ \|*  
*yacchaṃti pitaraḥ puṣṭiṃ svāṃgārogyaṃ prajāphalam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Him, who pleases the manes with devotion, the manes also please. The manes give him the fruit in the form of nourishment, health, and progeny.

## \|\| 9.68 \|\|

*devakāryādapi punaḥ pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*devatābhyaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tu pūrvamāpyāyanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Again the rite in honour of manes is superior to that in honour of gods. It is said that manes are to be satisfied before gods.

## \|\| 9.69 \|\|

*śīghraprasādāstvakrodhā nissaṃgāḥ sthira sauhṛdāḥ \|*  
*śāṃtātmānaḥ śaucaparāḥ satataṃ priyavādinaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They are pleased quickly; they are wrathless; are unattached and of a steady affection, of a tranquil mind, intent on purity, and always speak pleasing words.

## \|\| 9.70 \|\|

*bhaktānuraktāḥ sukhadāḥ pitaraḥ parvadevatāḥ \|*  
*haviṣmatāmādhipatye śrāddhadevaḥ smṛto raviḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. The manes, the deities of the Parvans always love their devotees, give them happiness; and the Sun, the god of the obsequial rite, is said to be the chief of those who receive oblations.

## \|\| 9.71 \|\|

*etaddhi sarvamākhyātaṃ pitṛvaṃśānukīrttanam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramārogyaṃ kīrttanīyaṃ nṛbhiḥ sadā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. I have narrated to you all this account of the family of manes. It is meritorious, holy and leading to health. It should always be recited by men.

## \|\| 9.72 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*śrutvaitadakhilaṃ bhūyaḥ parābhaktirupasthitā \|*  
*śrāddhakālaṃ vidhiṃ caiva śrāddhameva tathaiva ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

72\. Having heard all this, a great devotion has again arisen (in me). (Tell me about) the time of Śrāddha, its rite, and the Śrāddha itself.

## \|\| 9.73-74 \|\|

*śrāddheṣu bhojanīyā ye śrāddhavarjyā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*kasminvāsarabhāge tu pitṛbhyaḥ śrāddhamārabhet \|\| 73 \|\|*

*annaṃ dattaṃ kathaṃ yāti śrāddhe vai brahmavittama \|*  
*vidhinā kena karttavyaṃ kathaṃ prīṇāti tānpitṝn \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Which kinds of brāhmanas are to be fed at Śrāddhas and which ones are to be avoided; at what division (i.e. time) of the day should one begin the Śrāddha in honour of the manes? O best of brāhmaṇas, how does the food offered at a Śrāddha proceed? With which procedure should it be offered? How does it please the manes?

## \|\| 9.75 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*kuryādaharahaḥ śrāddhamannādyenodakena ca \|*  
*payomūlaphalairvāpi pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahan \|\| 75 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

75\. Having love for the manes one should everyday offer Śrāddha with food and water, or with milk, roots and fruits.

## \|\| 9.76-77 \|\|

*nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ trividhaṃ śrāddhamucyate \|*  
*nityaṃ tāvatpravakṣyāmi arghyāvāhanavarjitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*adaivataṃ vijānīyātpārvaṇaṃ parva susmṛtam \|*  
*pārvaṇaṃ trividhaṃ proktaṃ śṛṇu yatnānmahīpate \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. Śrāddha is said to be of three kinds: Nitya (regularly performed); Naimittika (occasionally performed); and Kāmya (performed for some particular desire). I shall explain to you the Nitya (Śrāddha). One should know it to be without a respectful offering and invocation and deity. The Śrāddha performed on the change of the moon is called Pārvaṇa. O King, the Pārvaṇa is said to be of three kinds. Please listen to them.

## \|\| 9.78-81 \|\|

*pārvaṇeya niyojyāstu tānśṛṇuṣva narādhipa \|*  
*paṃcāgniḥ snātakaścaiva trisauparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṃgavit \|\| 78 \|\|*

*śrotriyaḥ śrotriyasuto vidhivākyaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*sarvajño vedavānmaṃtrī jñānavaṃśakulānvitaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*triṇāciketastrimadhuḥ śruteṣvanyeṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*purāṇavettā brahmajñaḥ svādhyāyī japatatparaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*brahmabhaktaḥ pitṛparaḥ sūryabhaktotha vaiṣṇavaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇo yoganiṣṭhātmā vijitātmā suśīlavān \|\| 81 \|\|*

78-81. Listen O king, as to who are to be appointed at a Pārvaṇa: a Brāhmaṇa who keeps the fires; one who has returned from the preceptor’s house and become an initiated householder; one who has studied the Trisuparṇa; one who knows the six limbs of the Veda; one who is well-versed in the Vedas or his son; one who is proficient in the ritual; one who knows everything; one who possesses (the knowledge of) the Vedas; one who knows the incantations, endowed with knowledge and belonging to a good family, Triṇāciketa; Trimadhu; well-settled in other scriptures also; knower of the Purāṇas; knowing Brahma; studying Vedas; eagerly engaged in muttering prayers; a devotee of Brahma; obedient to his father; devoted to the Sun and Viṣṇu; having firm faith in abstract meditation; having control over his mind; and of a good character.

## \|\| 9.82 \|\|

*ete toṣyāḥ prayatnena varjanīyānimānśṛṇu \|*  
*patitastatsutaḥ klībaḥ piśuno vyaṃgarogitaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. These are to be satisfied with effort. Now listen to those who are to be avoided: a brāhmaṇa who is fallen, or his son, an impotent brāhmaṇa, a wicked one, and a deformed one.

## \|\| 9.83 \|\|

*sarve te śrāddhakāle tu tyājyā vai dharmadarśibhiḥ \|*  
*pūrvedyuraparedyurvā vinītāṃśca nimaṃtrayet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. All these are to be avoided by those who know what is right. Either on the previous or on the same day one should invite the learned brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 9.84 \|\|

*nimaṃtritāṃśca pitara upatiṣṭhaṃti tāndvijān \|*  
*vāyubhūtāni gacchaṃti tathāsīnānupāsate \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The manes turning themselves into air remain by those brāhmaṇas who are invited; they go to them and sit by them when they (i.e. the brāhmaṇas) sit.

## \|\| 9.85-88 \|\|

*dakṣiṇaṃ jānucālabhya vāmaṃ pātyanimaṃtrayet \|*  
*akrodhanaiḥ śaucaparaiḥ susnātairbrahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*bhavitavyaṃ bhavadbhistu mayā ca śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*pitṛyajñaṃ vinirvartya tarpaṇākhyaṃ tu yognimān \|\| 86 \|\|*

*piṃḍānvāhāryakaṃ kuryācchrāddhamiṃdukṣaye tathā \|*  
*gomayenānulipte tu dakṣiṇāplavanasthale \|\| 87 \|\|*

*śrāddhaṃ samārabhedbhaktyā goṣṭhe vā jalasannidhau \|*  
*agnimānnirvapetpitryaṃ caruṃ vā saktumuṣṭibhiḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

85-88. Kneeling with the left leg by touching the right knee of the brāhmaṇa he should invite him. (He should tell the brāhmaṇas) ‘You should be wrathless, intent on purity, well-bathed and reciting the Vedas. I should be also like that at the obsequial rite’. One who maintains the fire, should, having performed the sacrifice in honour of the manes called Tarpaṇa (satiating), and having done Piṇḍānvāhāryaka (i.e. having offered a meal in honour of the manes), perform a Śrāddha at the wane of the moon. Having besmeared with cow dung (a spot near the) bathing place in the south, he should devoutly begin the Śrāddha either in a cowpen or (at a place) near water. He, maintaining the fire, should offer the (rice or barley-flour cooked in) the saucepan in honour of the manes with handfuls of barley-flour.

## \|\| 9.89 \|\|

*pitṛbhyo nirvapāmīti sarvaṃ dakṣiṇato nyaset \|*  
*abhighārya tataḥ kuryānnirvāpatrayamagrataḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Saying, ‘I am offering this to the manes’, he should keep all that in the southern direction. Then having restrained himself, he should, in front of him, thrice make offerings in honour of the manes.

## \|\| 9.90 \|\|

*te vitastyāyatāḥ kāryāścaturaṅgulavistṛtāḥ \|*  
*darvītrayaṃ ca kurvīta khādiraṃ rajatānvitam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. The length of these (fires) should be of the measure of twelve aṅgulis and the breadth should be four aṅgulis. He should also make three laddies of Khadira wood, fixed with silver. Its length should be a cubit; it should be smooth, excellent and its end should have the shape of the hand.

## \|\| 9.91 \|\|

*ratnimātraṃ pariślakṣṇaṃ hastākārāgramuttamam \|*  
*udapātrāṇi kāṃsyasya mekṣaṇaṃ ca samitkuśam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He should make the vessels of water of bell-metal, and also a wooden stick (for stirring up the Caru) and sacred fuel and Kuśa.

## \|\| 9.92 \|\|

*tilapātrāṇi sadvāso gaṃdhadhūpānulepanam \|*  
*āharedapasavyaṃ ca sarvaṃ dakṣiṇataḥ śanaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Making the sacred thread hang down towards the left part of the body over the right shoulder he should slowly place all (these things, viz.) pots containing sesamum, a good piece of cloth, incense and unguent at his right hand.

## \|\| 9.93-94 \|\|

*evamāsādya tatsarvaṃ bhavanasyottareṃtare \|*  
*gomayenānuliptāyāṃ gomūtreṇa ca maṃḍalam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*sākṣatābhiḥ sapuṣpābhiradbhiḥ savyāpasavyavat \|*  
*viprāṇāṃ kṣālayetpādāvabhivaṃdya punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. Having procured all these, he should, at the northern part of the house, on the ground besmeared with cow-dung and encircled with cow-urine, wash with water (mixed) with whole rice grains and flowers, the feet of the brāhmaṇas when they are duly seated on Darbha-seats, saluting them again, placing his sacred thread once on the right and once on the left shoulder.

## \|\| 9.95 \|\|

*āsaneṣūpaviṣṭeṣu darbhavatsu vidhānataḥ \|*  
*upaspṛṣṭodakānviprānupaveśyānumaṃtrayet \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Having (thus) seated the brāhmaṇas, who have sipped water, he should invite them.

## \|\| 9.96 \|\|

*dvau daive pitṛkṛtye trīnekaikaṃ cobhayatra vā \|*  
*bhojayedīśvaropīha na kuryādvistaraṃ budhaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He should give food to two brāhmaṇas for a rite in honour of gods, to three for a rite in honour of the manes or one at each of these two rites, even though he is rich; a wise man should avoid multiplying (the number).

## \|\| 9.97 \|\|

*daivapūrvaṃ nivedyātha viprānarghādinā budhaiḥ \|*  
*agnau kuryādanujñāto viprairvipro yathāvidhi \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Having first performed the worship in honour of gods and having made to them respectful offering, permitted by the wise brāhmaṇa he should duly make offerings into fire.

## \|\| 9.98-99 \|\|

*svagṛhyoktena vidhinā kāle kṛtvā samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*agnīṣomamayābhyāṃ tu kuryādāpyāyanaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāgnau praṇītena sa evāgnirdvijottamaḥ \|*  
*yajñopavītānnirvartya tataḥ paryukṣaṇādikam \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. Performing all rites according to the rules in the Gṛhya-sūtras of his branch the wise brāhmaṇa should (offer worship) to satisfy Agnīṣoma and Yama, when the southern fire is kindled, that is not the same fire. Then the best brāhmaṇa changing the sacred thread from the left shoulder to the right should do the sprinkling round of water silently and without uttering any ritual formula etc.

## \|\| 9.100-101 \|\|

*prācīnāvītinā kāryametatsarvaṃ vijānatā \|*  
*labdhvā tasmādviśeṣeṇa piṃḍānkurvīta codakaṃ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*dadyādudakapātraistu salilaṃ savyapāṇinā \|*  
*dadyātsarvaṃ prayatnena damayukto vimatsaraḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. Then taking from it (some fire) discriminately he should prepare the Piṇḍas and offer water. He should offer water from the water-pots with his right hand. Being restrained and free from hatred he should offer all this.

## \|\| 9.102 \|\|

*vidhāya rekhāṃ yatnena nirvapedavanejanaṃ \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhimukhaḥ kuryāttato darbhānnidhāya vai \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. Carefully drawing a line he should, facing the south, offer oblations in honour of the manes and (after feeding the brāhmaṇas) (give them water for) washing (their hands etc.)

## \|\| 9.103 \|\|

*nidhāya piṃḍamekaikaṃ sarvaṃ darbhoparikramāt \|*  
*nirvapedatha darbheṣu nāmagotrānukīrtanaiḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Then placing the darbhas he should place serially one piṇḍa each on all the darbhas. Then he should offer libation on the darbhas by uttering his name and family.

## \|\| 9.104-105 \|\|

*teṣu darbheṣu taṃ hastaṃ vimṛjyāllepabhāgināṃ \|*  
*tathaiva ca japaṃ kuryātpunaḥ pratyavanejanam \|\| 104 \|\|*

*jalayuktaṃ namaskṛtya gaṃdhadhūpārcanādibhiḥ \|*  
*evamāvāhya tatsarvaṃ vedamaṃtrairyathoditaiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. Then he should touch the darbhas meant for the paternal ancestors of the 4th, 5th and 6th degrees; and also he should mutter prayers and having worshipped (the brāhmaṇas) reverentially with fragrance, incense etc. he should again wash (his hands etc.).

## \|\| 9.106 \|\|

*ekāgnarekaevādbhirnirvapeddarvikāṃ tathā \|*  
*tataḥ kṛtvā naro dadyātpitṛbhyastu kuśānbudhaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Having thus invoked all that he, maintaining a fire, should also offer the spoon with water, and with Vedic hymn as mentioned. Then the wise man, preparing Kuśas should offer them to the manes.

## \|\| 9.107-108 \|\|

*tataḥ piṃḍādikaṃ kuryādāvāhanavisarjanam \|*  
*tato gṛhītvā piṃḍebhyo mātrāḥ sarvāḥ krameṇa tu \|\| 107 \|\|*

*tāneva viprānprathamamāśayitvā ca mānavaḥ \|*  
*varṇayanbhojayedannamiṣṭaṃ pūrtaṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. Then preparing piṇḍas etc. he should invoke and allow (the deities) to go. Then taking portions from the piṇḍas serially and feeding these very brāhmaṇas first, the man should praise the food, desired (by the brāhmaṇa) and pure.

I 09. He should, remembering Nārāyaṇa Hari, avoid wrath. Knowing the brāhmaṇas to be pleased he should again distribute all kinds (of food).

## \|\| 9.110 \|\|

*vidhṛtya sodakaṃ tvannaṃ satilaṃ prakṣipedbhuvi \|*  
*ācāṃteṣu punardadyājjalaṃ puṣpākṣatodakam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Then picking up food, he should place it on the ground with water and sesamum. When they have rinsed their mouths, he should again offer water and flowers and whole rice grains.

## \|\| 9.111 \|\|

*svadhāvācanakaṃ sarvaṃ piṃḍopari samācaret \|*  
*devādyaṃtaṃ prakurvīta śrāddhanāśonyathā bhavet \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Then declaring the oblation of food to the manes he should worship the piṇḍas. He should complete (the Śrāddha) by honouring the gods, otherwise the Śrāddha perishes.

## \|\| 9.112-114 \|\|

*visṛjya viprānpraṇatasteṣāṃ kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃdiśamākāṃkṣanpitṝnuddiśya mānavaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*dātāro nobhivarddhaṃtāṃ vedāḥ santatireva ca \|*  
*śraddhā ca no mā vyagamadbahudeyaṃ ca nostviti \|\| 113 \|\|*

*annaṃ ca no bahubhavedatithīṃśca labhemahi \|*  
*yācitāraśca naḥ saṃtu mā ca yāciṣma kaṃcana \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. Having given leave to the brāhmaṇas and going round them keeping them to his right, and desiring the southern direction and mentioning the manes the man (should pray): “May our donors increase; may the Vedas flourish; may our progeny increase; may our faith not go away from us; may we be able to give much; have ample food; may we have guests; may sufficient be ours (i.e. come to us); may we not beg of anyone.”

## \|\| 9.115 \|\|

*etadagnimataḥ proktamanvāhāryaṃ tu pārvaṇaṃ \|*  
*yatheṃdusaṃkṣaye tadvadanyatrāpi nigadyate \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. This is called the Anvāhārya (i.e. the monthly Śrāddha performed in honour of the manes on the day of the new moon). As it is said on the new moon day it is also said to be performed on other days.

## \|\| 9.116 \|\|

*piṃḍāṃstu gojaviprebhyo dadyādagnau jalepi vā \|*  
*vaprāṃte vātha vikiredāpobhiratha vāpayet \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. The piṇḍas should be given to a cow, a goat or brāhmaṇas or may be cast into fire or water, or near the rampart.

## \|\| 9.117 \|\|

*patnīṃ tu madhyamaṃ piṃḍaṃ prāśayedvinayānvitām \|*  
*ādhatta pitaro garbhaṃ putrasaṃtānavarddhanaṃ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He should make his modest wife eat the middle piṇḍa. (If this is done) the manes deposit a foetus into her womb which would increase the sons and (other) progeny.

## \|\| 9.118 \|\|

*tāvannirvāpaṇaṃ tiṣṭhedyāvadviprā visarjitāḥ \|*  
*vaiśvadevaṃ tataḥ kuryānnivṛttaḥ pitṛkarmaṇaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Till the brāhmaṇas are dismissed the oblation should stand (should not be removed). Having performed the rite in honour of the manes, he should then make an offering to all gods.

## \|\| 9.119 \|\|

*iṣṭaiḥ saha tataḥ śāṃto bhuṃjīta pitṛsevitam \|*  
*punarbhojanamadhvānaṃ yānamāyāsamaithunam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. He should then calmly eat the food partaken of by the manes, along with his dear persons.

## \|\| 9.120 \|\|

*śrāddhakṛcchrāddhabhugyo vā sarvametadvivarjayet \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ kalahaṃ caiva divāsvapnaṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. One who performs a Śrāddha or eats at it should avoid eating again, should avoid journey, (or) going in a vehicle, exertion and coitus, study, quarrel and sleep by day.

## \|\| 9.121 \|\|

*anena vidhinā śrāddhaṃ trivargasyeha nirvapet \|*  
*kanyā kuṃbha vṛṣastherke kṛṣṇapakṣeṣu sarvadā \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Thus one should offer Śrāddha to anyone of the three castes, when the sun is in the zodiacal sign, viz. Kanyā, Kumbha or Vṛṣabha and always in the dark fortnights.

## \|\| 9.122 \|\|

*yatrayatra pradātavyaṃ sapiṃḍīkaraṇātmakam \|*  
*tatrānena vidhānena deyamagnimatā sadā \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Wherever Sapiṇḍa Śrāddha is to be offered it should always be offered according to this procedure by one who maintains a fire.

## \|\| 9.123 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi brahmaṇā yadudīritam \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nāma bhuktimuktiphalapradam \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Hereafter I shall explain (to you) the Sādhāraṇa Śrāddha as told by Brahmā and giving enjoyment and salvation.

## \|\| 9.124-126 \|\|

*ayane viṣuve caiva amāvasyārkasaṃkrame \|*  
*amāvasyāṣṭakā kṛṣṇapakṣa paṃcadaśīṣu ca \|\| 124 \|\|*

*ārdrā maghā rohiṇīṣu dravyabrāhmaṇasaṃgame \|*  
*gajacchāyāvyatīpāte viṣṭivaidhṛtivāsare \|\| 125 \|\|*

*vaiśākhasya tṛtīyāyāṃ navamīkārtikasya ca \|*  
*paṃcadaśī tu māghasya nabhasye ca trayodaśī \|\| 126 \|\|*

124-126. (Śrāddha should be offered) during the solstices and the sun’s equinoctial passage, on a new moon day, and during the sun’s passage from one zodiacal sign to another; on an aṣṭakā (i.e. a collection of three days, viz. 7th, 8th and 9th beginning from the seventh day after the full moon, new moon day, and the 15th day of the dark half, and on the days of Ārdrā, Maghā and Rohiṇī when the materials and brāhmaṇas are available; on Gajacchāyā day (when an elephant’s shadow falls in the east), on the Vyatīpāta (i.e. new-moon-day when it falls on Sunday and when the moon is in certain Nakṣatras), on a rainy day, on the day of Vaidhṛti (i.e. the day of the conjunction of the sun and the moon), the third of Vaiśākha, the ninth of Kārtika, the fifteenth of Māgha, the thirteenth of Bhādrapada.

## \|\| 9.127-131 \|\|

*yugādayaḥ smṛtā hyetāḥ pitṝpakṣopakārikāḥ \|*  
*tathā manvaṃtarādau ca deyaṃ śrāddhaṃ vijānatā \|\| 127 \|\|*

*aśvayuṅnavamī caiva dvādaśī kārtike tathā \|*  
*tṛtīyā caitramāsasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca \|\| 128 \|\|*

*phālgunasya tvamāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī tathā \|*  
*āṣāḍhasyāpi daśamī māghamāsasya saptamī \|\| 129 \|\|*

*śrāvaṇe cāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhī ca pūrṇimā \|*  
*kārtikī phālgunī caivā jyeṣṭhe paṃcadaśī sitā \|\| 130 \|\|*

*manvaṃtarādayastvetā dattasyākṣayakārikāḥ \|*  
*pānīyamapyatra tilairvimiśraṃ dadyātpitṛbhyaḥ prayato manuṣyaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

127-131. These are said to be the Yuga-tithis and favourable for the fortnight of the manes’. So also Śrāddha should be offered on the Manvantara tithis i.e. the ninth of the bright half of Āśvina, the twelfth of the bright half of Kārtika, the third of the bright half of Caitra, the third of the bright half of Bhādrapada, the new moon day of Phālguna, the eleventh of the bright half of Pauṣa, the tenth of the bright half of Āṣāḍha, the seventh of the bright half of Māgha, the eighth of the dark half of Śrāvaṇa, and the full moon days of Āṣāḍha, Kārtika, Phālguna and Jyeṣṭha. These are Manvantara tithis making the gifts inexhaustible. A restrained man should give on these days at least water mixed with sesamum.

## \|\| 9.132 \|\|

*śrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ tena samāssahasraṃ rahasyametatpitaro vadaṃti \|*  
*vaiśākhyāmupavāseṣu tathotsavamahālaye \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. The manes say that the secret is that such a man has performed Śrāddha for a thousand years.

## \|\| 9.133 \|\|

*tīrthāyatanagoṣṭheṣu dvīpodyānagṛheṣu ca \|*  
*vivikteṣūpalipteṣu śrāddhaṃ deyaṃ vijānatā \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. A wise man should offer Śrāddha on the full moon day of Vaiśākha and on fast days, during festivals and in sanctuaries, at sacred places and in cowpens, in islands, gardens and houses, in solitary places that are besmeared.

## \|\| 9.134 \|\|

*viprānpūrveparecāhni vinītātmāni maṃtrayet \|*  
*śīlavṛttaguṇopetānvayorūpasamanvitān \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. Politely he should invite the brāhmaṇas, endowed with character and (good) behaviour and virtues and age and form, either on the previous or the same day.

## \|\| 9.135 \|\|

*dvau daive pitṛkṛtye trīnekaikamubhayatra vā \|*  
*bhojayetsusamṛddhopi na prakurvīta vistaram \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Even though he is very rich he should feed two brāhmaṇas at the rite in honour of gods and three at the rite in honour of manes or one brāhmaṇa at (each of) the two; he should not indulge in multiplying (the number).

## \|\| 9.136 \|\|

*viśvedevānyavaiḥ puṣpairabhyarcyāsanapūrvakaṃ \|*  
*pūrayetpātrayugmaṃ tu sthāpyaṃ darbhapavitrake \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Having worshipped the Viśvedevas with barley (-flour) and flowers after offering them a seat, he should fill a couple of pots (with water) and place it on the darbha-blades.

## \|\| 9.137 \|\|

*śannodevītyapaḥ kuryādyavosīti yavānapi \|*  
*gaṃdhapuṣpaistu saṃpūjya viśvāndevānpratinyaset \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Reciting (the hymn) ‘Śan no devīḥ’ (may the deities be to our welfare) he should offer water; reciting ‘Yavaḥ asi’ (you are barley) he should offer barley grains. Having worshipped Viśvedevas with sandal and flowers he should place them.

## \|\| 9.138 \|\|

*viśvedevāsa ityābhyāmāvāhya vikiredyavān \|*  
*yavosi dhānyarājastvaṃ vāruṇo madhumiśritaḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Having invoked them with these two (incantations) ‘Viśvedevā saḥ’, he should scatter the barley-grains.

## \|\| 9.139 \|\|

*nirṇudaḥ sarvapāpānāṃ pavitra ṛṣisaṃstutaḥ \|*  
*gaṃdhapuṣpairalaṃkṛtya yā divyetyarghamutsṛjet \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Reciting ‘you are barley, the king of grains dedicated to Varuṇa, and mixed with honey, destroyer of all sins, holy and praised by the sages’, and adorning them with sandal and flowers he should scatter them.

## \|\| 9.140-141 \|\|

*abhyarcya gaṃdhādyutsṛjya pitṛyajñaṃ samārabhet \|*  
*darbhāsanādi kṛtvādau trīṇi pātrāṇi cārcayet \|\| 140 \|\|*

*sapavitrāṇi kṛtvādau śannodevītyapaḥ kṣipet \|*  
*tilosīti tilānkuryādgandhapuṣpādikaṃ punaḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

140-141. Having (thus) worshipped them and having cast away the sandal etc. he should commence the rite in honour of the manes. Making seats of darbha etc. he should first consecrate three pots; putting the darbha blades in them he should sprinkle water reciting the incantation ‘Śan no devīḥ’. Reciting ‘Tilosi’ (you are sesamum), he should again put sesamum, sandal etc.

## \|\| 9.142 \|\|

*pātraṃ vanaspatimayaṃ tathā parṇamayaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*rājataṃ vā prakurvīta tathā sāgarasaṃbhavam \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. He should make a pot made from a tree or of leaves or of silver or gold.

## \|\| 9.143 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ tāmraṃ pitṝṇāṃ pātramucyate \|*  
*rajatasya kathā vāpi darśanaṃ dānameva ca \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. A golden pot or a silver pot or a copper pot is said to be the pot of manes; or even the mention of silver, seeing it or its gift (delights them).

## \|\| 9.144 \|\|

*rājatairbhājanaireṣāṃ pitṝṇāṃ rajatānvitaiḥ \|*  
*vāryapi śraddhayā dattamakṣayāyopakalpate \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Even water given with faith to these manes in silver pots or pots (of metal mixed with) silver becomes inexhaustible.

## \|\| 9.145 \|\|

*adyāpi pitṛpātreṣu pitṝṇāṃ rājatānvitam \|*  
*śivanetrodbhavaṃ yasmāduttamaṃ pitṛvallabham \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Even now among the pots meant for (making offerings to) manes, one having silver in it, is excellent and dear to the manes, since it has originated from Śiva’s eye.

## \|\| 9.146 \|\|

*evaṃ pātrāṇi saṃkalpya yathālābhaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*yā divyeti piturnāma gotre darbhānkare nyaset \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Thus securing the pots as available, he, without ill-feeling, should place the darbhas in his hand reciting the incantation ‘yā divyā’; (mentioning) the name and family of the manes (he should say) ‘I shall invoke the manes’.

## \|\| 9.147 \|\|

*pitṝnāvāhayiṣyāmi tathetyuktaḥ sa taiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*uśaṃtastvā tathāyantu ṛgmyāmāvāhayetpitṝn \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. When they (brāhmaṇas) say ‘all right’ he should invoke the the manes with the two ṛcs ‘Uśantastvā’, ‘Āvantu (naḥ pitaraḥ)’.

## \|\| 9.148 \|\|

*yā divyetyarghyamutsṛjya dadyādgaṃdhādikaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vastrottaraṃ darbhapūrvaṃ datvā saṃśrayamāditaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. Having made a respectful offering with (the incantation) ‘Yā divyā’, he should offer sandal etc. First the darbhas, then a piece of cloth should be offered, and a resting place from the beginning.

## \|\| 9.149 \|\|

*pitṛpātre nidhāyātha nyubjamuttarato nyaset \|*  
*pitṛbhyaḥ sthānamasīti nidhāya pariveṣayet \|\| 149 \|\|*

149\. Keeping (these) in the pot meant for manes, then having bent he should keep it to the north. Saying, ‘You are the place for the manes' he should serve up meals (to the brāhmaṇas).

## \|\| 9.150 \|\|

*tatrāpi pūrvataḥ kuryādagnikāryaṃ vimatsaraḥ \|*  
*ubhābhyāmapi hastābhyāmāhṛtya pariveṣayet \|\| 150 \|\|*

150\. There also he should first, free from ill-feeling, perform the rite with reference to fire. Holding the pots of the food with both hands he should serve up (the brāhmaṇas).

## \|\| 9.151 \|\|

*uśantastveti taṃ darbhaṃ pāṇibhaktaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*guṇānvitaiśca śākādyairnānābhakṣyaistathaiva ca \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. With the (hymn) ‘Uśantastvā’ he should keep the food in his hand on the darbha, along with subordinate dishes, vegetables etc., and eatables of various kinds.

## \|\| 9.152 \|\|

*annaṃ ca sadadhikṣīraṃ goghṛtaṃ śarkarānvitaṃ \|*  
*māsaṃ prīṇāti vai sarvānpitṝnityāha padmajaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Brahmā said that food with curds, milk, ghee made from cow's milk, and with sugar pleases all the manes for one month.

## \|\| 9.153 \|\|

*dvau māsau matsyamāṃsena trīnmāsānhāriṇena tu \|*  
*aurabhreṇātha caturaḥ śākunenātha paṃca vai \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. They are pleased for two months with the flesh of fish, for three months with the flesh of deer, for four months with the flesh of ram and for five months with bird’s flesh.

## \|\| 9.154 \|\|

*vārāhasya tu māṃsena ṣaṇmāsaṃ tṛptiruttamā \|*  
*saptalohasya māṃsena tathāṣṭāvājakena tu \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. They get excellent satisfaction for six months by pig’s flesh, for seven months by red goat’s flesh, for eight months by a lamb’s flesh.

## \|\| 9.155 \|\|

*pṛṣatasya tu māṃsena tṛptirmāsānnavaiva tu \|*  
*daśamāsāṃśca tṛpyaṃte varāhamahiṣāmiṣaiḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. The flesh of a spotted antelope gives (them) satisfaction for nine months. They are satisfied for ten months with the flesh of boar and buffalo.

## \|\| 9.156 \|\|

*śaśakūrmayostu māṃsena māsānekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena vā \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. (They are satisfied) for eleven months with the flesh of hare and tortoise; for a year with cow’s milk or sweetened milk.

## \|\| 9.157 \|\|

*saukareṇa tu tṛpyaṃte māsānpaṃcadaśaiva tu \|*  
*vārdhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptirdvādaśavārṣikī \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. They are satisfied for fifteen months with hog’s flesh and satisfaction for twelve years is brought about by the flesh of rhinoceros. Eternal satisfaction comes by the potherb ocimum sanctum and also by the flesh of a rhinoceros.

## \|\| 9.158 \|\|

*kālaśākena cānaṃtyaṃ khaḍgamāṃsena caiva hi \|*  
*yatkiṃcinmadhunā miśraṃ gokṣīraṃ dadhipāyasam \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. The old deities—the manes—say, ‘Whatever cow’s milk, curds and sweetened milk, mixed with honey is offered becomes eternal’.

## \|\| 9.159 \|\|

*dattamakṣayamityāhuḥ pitaraḥ pūrvadevatāḥ \|*  
*svādhyāyaṃ śrāvayetpitryaṃ purāṇānyakhilāni ca \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. One should narrate the passages sacred to the manes and all the Purāṇas.

## \|\| 9.160 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇāṃ stavāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*iṃdreśasomasūktāni pāvamānīśca śaktitaḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. So also the various eulogies of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Arka and Rudra, of Indra, Īśa, Soma and Pavamāna, according to his ability.

## \|\| 9.161 \|\|

*bṛhadrathaṃtaraṃ tatra jyeṣṭhasāmātha rauravaṃ \|*  
*tathaiva śāṃtikādhyāyaṃ madhubrāhmaṇameva ca \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. So also Bṛhadrathantara, Jyeṣṭhasāman, Rorava, and propitiatory passages and Madhu brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 9.162 \|\|

*maṇḍalabrāhmaṇaṃ tadvatprītikāri ca yatpunaḥ \|*  
*viprāṇāmātmanaścāpi tatsarvaṃ samudīrayet \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. So also Maṇḍala brāhmaṇa which is agreeable. He should narrate all this to the brāhmaṇas and himself.

## \|\| 9.163 \|\|

*bhāratādhyayanaṃ kāryaṃ pitṝṇāṃ paramapriyaṃ \|*  
*bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu bhojyatoyādikaṃ nṛpa \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. He should listen to the chapters from Bharata very dear to the manes.

## \|\| 9.164 \|\|

*sārvavarṇikamannādyamānayetsāvadhāraṇaṃ \|*  
*samutsṛjedbhuktavatāmagrato vikirānbhuvi \|\| 164 \|\|*

164\. O Prince, when the brāhmaṇas have eaten, he should bring carefully food of all kinds and water etc. He should spread it on the ground before the brāhmaṇas who have eaten.

## \|\| 9.165 \|\|

*agnidagdhāśca ye jīvā yepyadagdhāḥ kule mama \|*  
*bhūmau dattena tṛpyaṃtu tṛptā yāṃtu parāṃ gatiṃ \|\| 165 \|\|*

165\. ‘Those who in my family were Agnidagdhas (i.e. a class of pitṛs, who, when on earth, maintained a sacred fire) and those who were not, may be pleased with (the food) given on the ground and may get the highest place as a result of satisfaction.

## \|\| 9.166 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ na mātā na pitā na baṃdhurna cāpi mitraṃ na tathānnamasti \|*  
*tattṝptayennaṃ bhuvi dattametatpayātu yogāya yato yataste \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. This food is offered on the ground for the satisfaction of those who do not have mother, father, brother, not a friend; since they may go in for abstract meditation from wherever they are.’

## \|\| 9.167-168 \|\|

*asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyāgināṃ kulabhāgināṃ \|*  
*uchiṣṭabhāgadheyānāṃ darbheṣu vikirāsanaṃ \|\| 167 \|\|*

*tṛptānjñātvodakaṃ dadyātsakṛdvikiraṇe tathā \|*  
*vipraliptamahīpṛṣṭe gośakṛnmūtravāriṇā \|\| 168 \|\|*

167-168. Giving a seat to them who died without any purificatory rite being performed over them, also to the relatives who have left the family, and partaking of the remaining; knowing them to be satisfied one should offer water on the scattered (food), when the surface of the earth is besmeared with cow-dung, cow-urine and water.

## \|\| 9.169 \|\|

*nidhāya darbhānvidhivaddakṣiṇāgrānprayatnataḥ \|*  
*sarvavarṇavidhānena piṃḍāṃśca pitṛyajñavat \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. Placing carefully the darbhas with their tips facing the south he should offer the piṇḍas of all the varieties as in the rite in honour of the manes.

## \|\| 9.170-171 \|\|

*avanejanapūrvaṃ tu nāmagotraṃ tu mānavaḥ \|*  
*uktvā puṣpādikaṃ datvā kṛtvā pratyavanejanaṃ \|\| 170 \|\|*

*jñātvāpasavyaṃ savyena pāṇinā triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ \|*  
*pitṛvanmātṛkaṃ kāryaṃ vidhivaddarbhapāṇinā \|\| 171 \|\|*

170-171. After washing (his hands etc.) the man uttering his name and family, offering flowers etc., doing the washing off again, with the thread on the left and then the right shoulder should go round thrice. One should perform with darbhas in one’s hands the rite in honour of one’s mother like that of one’s father.

## \|\| 9.172 \|\|

*dīpaprajvālanaṃ tadvatkuryātpuṣpārcanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*tathā cāṃteṣu cācamya dadyāccāpaḥ sakṛtsakṛt \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. In the same way the wise one should burn the lamp and should worship with flowers; then when they have sipped water he should, having sipped water, offer water once.

## \|\| 9.173 \|\|

*tathā puṣpākṣatānpaścādakṣayyodakameva ca \|*  
*satilaṃ nāmagotreṇa dadyācchaktyā ca dakṣiṇām \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. Then he should offer flowers and whole rice-grains and inexhaustible water along with sesamum and uttering the name and family and should give presents according to his capacity.

## \|\| 9.174 \|\|

*gobhūhiraṇyavāsāṃsi bhavyāni śayanāni ca \|*  
*dadyādyadiṣṭaṃ viprāṇāmātmanaḥ pitureva ca \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. He should give cows, land, gold, garments, large beds and whatever is dear to the brāhmaṇas, to himself and to the mane.

## \|\| 9.175 \|\|

*vittaśāṭhyena rahitaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāvahet \|*  
*tataḥ svadhāvācanakaṃ viśvedeveṣu codakaṃ \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. Void of perfidy due to wealth he should have love for the manes, then should do the recitation of ‘Svadhā’ and offering of water to Viśvedevas. Offering prayers to the brāhmaṇas the wise one should accept blessings from them.

## \|\| 9.176-177 \|\|

*datvāśīḥ pratigṛhṇīyāddvijebhyopi yathā budhaḥ \|*  
*aghorāḥ pitaraḥ saṃtu saṃtvityuktaḥ punardvijaiḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

*gotraṃ tathā varddhatāṃ tu tathetyuktaśca taiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*svastivācanakaṃ kuryātpiṃḍānuddhṛtya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

176-177. He should say, ‘May the manes be amiable’, when the brāhmaṇas in return say, ‘May they be so’; ‘May my family increase’, when they in return say, ‘Let it be so’. He should make the complimentary present after devoutly lifting up the piṇḍas.

## \|\| 9.178 \|\|

*uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tattiṣṭhedyāvadvipravisarjanam \|*  
*tato gṛhabaliṃ kuryāditi dharmo vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. The remainders should remain till the brāhmaṇas are dismissed. Then he should make the domestic oblation (i.e. offering of the remnants to all creatures and household deities). This is the settled practice.

## \|\| 9.179 \|\|

*uccheṣaṇaṃ bhūmigatamajihmasyāśaṭhasya ca \|*  
*dāsavargasya tatpiṃḍaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. The remnant on the ground, the portionof the piṇḍas, is said to belong to honest and diligent servants.

## \|\| 9.180 \|\|

*pitṛbhirnirmitaṃ pūrvametadāpyāyanaṃ sadā \|*  
*avratānāmaputrāṇāṃ strīṇāmapi narādhipa \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. This act of satisfying was formerly prescribed by the manes for those not practising any vow, and for the sonless and the wifeless, O King.

## \|\| 9.181 \|\|

*tataḥ sthānāgrataḥ sthitvā pratigṛhyāṃbupātrikāṃ \|*  
*vājevājeti ca japankuśāgreṇa visarjayet \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Then standing ahead of the seat and washing the water-pot, one should dismiss with the tip of a Kuśa muttering ‘Vāja, Vāja’.

## \|\| 9.182 \|\|

*bahiḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryātpadānyaṣṭāvanuvrajet \|*  
*baṃdhuvargeṇa sahitaḥ putrabhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. He should circumambulate and walk eight steps with his relatives, sons and wife.

## \|\| 9.183 \|\|

*nivṛtya praṇipatyātha prayujyāgniṃ sa maṃtravit \|*  
*vaiśvadevaṃ prakurvīta naityikaṃ balimeva ca \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Then returning and saluting, he, knowing the incantations, employing the fire, should offer the Vaiśvadeva (rite) and make the daily offering.

## \|\| 9.184 \|\|

*tatastu vaiśvadevāṃte sabhṛtyasutabāṃdhavaḥ \|*  
*bhuṃjītātithisaṃyuktaḥ sarvaṃ pitṛniṣevitaṃ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Then at the end of the Vaiśvadeva (rite) he should, along with his servants, sons, relatives and guests eat what was enjoyed by the manes.

## \|\| 9.185 \|\|

*etaccānupanītopi kuryātsarveṣu parvasu \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ sādhāraṇaṃ nāma sarvakāmaphalapradam \|*  
*bhāryāvirahitopyetatpravāsasthopi bhaktimān \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Even one who has not undergone the thread ceremony should offer this Śrāddha called Sādhāraṇa (general) fulfilling all desires on all parvans (the eighth and fourteenth day of each month and the days of the full moon and new moon).

## \|\| 9.186 \|\|

*śūdropyamaṃtrakaṃ kuryādanena vidhinā nṛpa \|*  
*tṛtīyamābhyudayikaṃ vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ vidhīyate \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. Even one without a wife or while journeying, or even a Śūdra should devoutly offer the Śrāddha according to this procedure, without the accompaniment of the sacred prayers. The third Śrāddha that is enjoined is Vṛddhiśrāddha leading to prosperity.

## \|\| 9.187-188 \|\|

*utsavānaṃdasaṃskāre yajñodvāhādimaṃgale \|*  
*mātaraḥ prathamaṃ pūjyāḥ pitarastadanaṃtaraṃ \|\| 187 \|\|*

*tato mātāmahā rājanviśvedavāstathaiva ca \|*  
*pradakṣiṇopacāreṇa dadhyakṣataphalodakaiḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

187-188. In a festival or a happy sacrament, at a sacrifice or an auspicious celebration like marriage one should first worship the divine mothers and then the manes, then one’s mother and then the Viśvedeva, by circumambulation and with curds, whole rice-grains, fruits and water.

## \|\| 9.189 \|\|

*prāṅmukho nirvapetpiṃṇḍānpūrvāṃścaiva purātanān \|*  
*saṃpannamityabhyudaye dadyādarghaṃ dvayordvayoḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. He, facing the east, should offer the earlier and the later piṇḍas. He should declare ‘It is accomplished’ and should make respectful offering to two brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 9.190 \|\|

*yugmā dvijātayaḥ pūjyā vastrākalpāṃbarādibhiḥ \|*  
*tilakāryaṃ yavaiḥ kāryaṃ tacca sarvānupūrvakaṃ \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. The brāhmaṇas should be honoured in pairs with pieces of cloth or clothe etc.

## \|\| 9.191 \|\|

*maṃgalyāni ca sarvāṇi vācayeddvijapuṃgavān \|*  
*evaṃ śūdropi sāmānyaṃ vṛddhiśrāddhaṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. He should speak auspicious things to the brāhmaṇas. In the same way a wise Śūdra should always perform the general Vṛddhi-śrāddha (an offering made to manes on prosperous occasions such as the birth of a son) and make presents with salutation and incantations.

## \|\| 9.192 \|\|

*namaskāreṇa maṃtreṇa kuryāddānāni vai budhaḥ \|*  
*dānaṃ pradhānaṃ śūdrasya ityāha bhagavānprabhuḥ \|*  
*dānena sarvakāmāptistasya saṃjāyate yataḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. The lord said: ‘For a Śūdra, giving gifts is the principal thing, since all his desires are fulfilled by giving in charity’.

## Chapter 10 - The Greatness of Pitṛs

## \|\| 10.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ekoddiṣṭaṃ tato vakṣye yaduktaṃ brahmaṇā purā \|*  
*mṛte putrairyathākāryamāśaucaṃ ca pituryadi \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. I shall now explain the Ekoddiṣṭa (a śrāddha performed for one definite deceased individual, not including other ancestors) described by Brahmā formerly as to how the sons should perform it till the purification from personal defilement caused by the death of the father.

## \|\| 10.2 \|\|

*daśāhaṃ śāvamāśaucaṃ brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate \|*  
*kṣatriyeṣu daśa dve ca pakṣaṃ vaiśyeṣu caiva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. For a brāhmaṇa the defilement caused by the death is said to be for ten days; for a kṣatriya it is for twelve days, for a Vaiśya it is for a fortnight and for a Śudra it is for one month on the death of a Sapiṇḍa.

## \|\| 10.3 \|\|

*śūdreṣu māsamāśaucaṃ sapiṃḍeṣu vidhīyate \|*  
*naiśamācūḍamāśaucaṃ trirātraṃ parataḥ smṛtam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the case of a child dying before the tonsure-ceremony is performed, the defilement (i.e. mourning period) is for a night only. Afterwards it is said to be three nights.

## \|\| 10.4 \|\|

*jananepyevameva syātsarvavarṇeṣu sarvadā \|*  
*asthisaṃcayanādūrdhvamaṅgasparśo vidhīyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It should always be like this also at the time of birth in all castes. After the collection of bones (i.e. the ashes after burning a corpse) touching (one another’s) body is laid down.

## \|\| 10.5 \|\|

*pretāya piṃḍadānaṃ tu dvādaśāhaṃ samācaret \|*  
*pātheyaṃ tasya tatproktaṃ yataḥ prītikaraṃ mahat \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. One should give piṇḍas to the dead person for twelve days, that is said to be his provender since it gives him great joy.

## \|\| 10.6 \|\|

*yasmātpretapuraṃ preto dvādaśāhena nīyate \|*  
*gṛhe putrakalatraṃ ca dvādaśāhaṃ prapaśyati \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Since the dead person is taken to the city of the dead at the end of twelve days, he sees (is able to see) his son and wife in the house for twelve days.

## \|\| 10.7 \|\|

*tasmānnidheyamākāśe daśarātraṃ payastathā \|*  
*sarvadāhopaśāṃtyarthamadhvaśramavināśanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Therefore, for ten nights (and days) water removing the fatigue of journey should be offered in the sky for the cessation of all tormentation.

## \|\| 10.8 \|\|

*tatastvekādaśāhepi dvijānekādaśaiva tu \|*  
*gotrādisūtakāṃte ca bhojayenmanujo dvijān \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Then on the eleventh day a man should feed eleven brāhmaṇas; so also at the end of the defilement due to the birth of a child in the family.

## \|\| 10.9 \|\|

*dvitīyehni punastadvadekoddiṣṭaṃ samācaret \|*  
*nāvāhanāgnaukaraṇaṃ daivahīnaṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. In the same way, on the next day he should perform the Ekoddiṣṭa. Invocation or preparation of fire is not done there according to the procedure and may be without worship offered to gods.

## \|\| 10.10 \|\|

*ekaṃ pavitramekorgha ekaḥ piṃḍo vidhīyate \|*  
*upatiṣṭhatāmiti vadeddeyaṃ paścāttilodakaṃ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. (For it) only one Kuśa-ring, one object and one piṇḍa are laid down. First he should say ‘(Please) be near’, and then should offer water with sesamum.

## \|\| 10.11 \|\|

*svāsti brūyādviprakare visarge cābhiramyatām \|*  
*śeṣaṃ pūrvavadatrāpi kāryaṃ vedavido viduḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should say, ‘May it be well with (us)’ and should take interest in scattering (the food) and offering it.

## \|\| 10.12-14 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvamanumāsaṃ samācaret \|*  
*sūtakāṃte dvitīyehni śayyāṃ dadyādvilakṣaṇām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kāṃcanaṃ puruṣaṃ tadvatphalavastrasamanvitam \|*  
*prapūjya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ nānābharaṇabhūṣitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*upaveśya tu śayyāyāṃ madhuparkaṃ tato dadet \|*  
*rajatasya tu pātreṇa dadhidugdhasamanvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. With this procedure he should do all this month after month. On the second day after the defilement due to birth is over, he should present an unusual bed, so also a golden image along with fruits and cloth. Having worshipped a brāhmaṇa couple adorned with various ornaments and seating them on the bed he should make a respectful offering of honey mixed with curds and milk to the couple from a silver pot.

## \|\| 10.15 \|\|

*asthilālāṭikaṃ gṛhya sūkṣmaṃ kṛtvā vimiśrayet \|*  
*pāyayedidvajadāṃpatyaṃ pitṛbhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Taking a bone of the forehead, pounding it and mixing it, and with devotion to the manes, he should make the couple drink it.

## \|\| 10.16 \|\|

*eṣa eva vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ pārvatīyairdvijotamaiḥ \|*  
*tena duṣṭā tu sā śayyā na grāhyā dvijasattamaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. This alone is the procedure as observed by the best brāhmaṇas living in the mountains. Due to it (i.e. the couple’s sitting upon it) the bed is defiled and so should not be accepted by best brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 10.17 \|\|

*gṛhītāyāṃ tu tasyāṃ hi punaḥ saṃskāramarhati \|*  
*vede caiva purāṇe ca śayyā sarvatra garhitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. If it is accepted it again requires sanctification—(such) a bed is condemned everywhere in the Veda and the Purāṇa.

## \|\| 10.18-20 \|\|

*grahītārastu jāyante sarve narakagāminaḥ \|*  
*grathitāṃ vasujālena śayyāṃ dāṃpatyasevitām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ye spṛśaṃti na jānaṃtaḥ sarve narakagāminaḥ \|*  
*navaśrāddhena bhoktavyaṃ bhuktvā cāṃdrāyaṇaṃ caret \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pitṛbhaktyā tu putrāṇāṃ kāryameva sadā bhavet \|*  
*vṛṣotsargaṃ ca kurvīta deyā ca kapilā śubhā \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Those who accept it all go to hell. Those who unknowingly touch (such) a bed woven with excellent texture and used by a couple go to hell. One should enjoy by means of a new Śrāddha, and after having enjoyed should practise the Cāndrāyaṇa vow. Sons should always perform it out of their devotion for the dead ancestors. One should present a bull (to a brāhmaṇa) or an auspicious tawny cow should be presented.

## \|\| 10.21-23 \|\|

*udakuṃbhaśca dātavyo bhakṣyabhojyaphalānvitaḥ \|*  
*yāvadabdaṃ naraśreṣṭha satilodakapūrvakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tataḥ saṃvatsare pūrṇe sapiṃḍīkaraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sapiṃḍīkaraṇādūrddhvaṃ pretaḥ pārvaṇabhugyataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vṛddhipūrveṣu kāryeṣu gṛhasthasya bhavettataḥ \|*  
*sapiṃḍīkaraṇaṃ śrāddhaṃ devapūrvaṃ niyojayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. O prince, till one year is over, he should give a jar of water along with eatables. Then when the year is complete there should be Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa preceded by water with sesamum.
