After the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, since the dead person becomes the enjoyer of the Śrāddhas offered on the parvan, a householder should have Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa in rites preceded by the Vṛddhi (Śrāddha). One should perform the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa Śrāddha after the rite in honour of gods.

## \|\| 10.24 \|\|

*pitṝnāvāhayettatra pṛthakpretaṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*gaṃdhodakatilairyuktaṃ kuryātpātracatuṣṭayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In it (i.e., this Śrāddha) he should invite the dead ancestors and should indicate the dead person separately. He should keep (ready) four pots with sandal, water and sesamum for respectful offering.

## \|\| 10.25-26 \|\|

*arghyārthaṃ pitṛpātreṣu pretapātraṃ prasecayet \|*  
*tadvatsaṃkalpya caturaḥ piṃḍānpitṛparastadā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ye samānā iti dvābhyāmannaṃ tu vibhajettridhā \|*  
*anena vidhinā cārghyaṃ pūrvameva pradāpayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. He should sprinkle the pot for the dead person kept among the pots meant for the manes. Similarly, being solely devoted to the manes and having prepared four piṇḍas for the dead, with the two incantations ‘Ye samānā' he should divide the piṇḍas into three parts. And with this procedure he should offer them preceded by the respectful offering (of water etc.).

## \|\| 10.27 \|\|

*tataḥ pitṛtvamāpannassa caturthastadā tvanu \|*  
*agniṣvāttādi madhye tu prāpnotyamṛtamuttamam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Then the fourth one that attained the status of manes obtains immortality among the Agniṣvāttas etc.

## \|\| 10.28 \|\|

*sapiṇḍīkaraṇādūrdhvaṃ pṛthaktasmai na dīyate \|*  
*pitṛṣveva ca dātavyaṃ tatpiṃḍaṃ yeṣu saṃsthitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. After the Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, a separate offering is not to be made to him. The piṇḍa should be offered to him who has (now) settled among the dead ancestors.

## \|\| 10.29 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti saṃkrāntāvuparāgādi parvasu \|*  
*tripiṃḍamācarecchrāddhamekoddiṣṭaṃ mṛtehani \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Since then on Saṃkrānti or on the days of solar and lunar eclipse, he should perform the Tripiṇḍa Śrāddha with the Ekoddiṣṭa.

## \|\| 10.30 \|\|

*ekoddiṣṭaṃ parityajya mṛtāhe yaḥ samācaret \|*  
*sa daivaṃ pitṛhā sa syāttathā bhrātṛvināśakaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On the day of the death anniversy \[anniversary?\] of a person one who moves without the Ekoddiṣṭa harms the gods and manes and also his brothers.

## \|\| 10.31 \|\|

*mṛtāhe pārvaṇaṃ kurvannadho yāti sa mānavaḥ \|*  
*saṃpṛkte svargatī bhāve pretamokṣo yato bhavet \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. If a man performs a pārvaṇa (a general ceremony of offering oblations to all the manes) on the day of the death of a person, he has a downward fall, from which the dead person may get release if he gets contact with the course to heaven.

## \|\| 10.32 \|\|

*āmaśrāddhaṃ tadā kuryādvidhijñaḥ śrāddhadastataḥ \|*  
*tenāgnaukaraṇaṃ kuryātpiṃḍāṃstenaiva nirvapet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then the knower of the procedure and giver of the Śrāddha should perform the Āma-śrāddha. With that he should make the offering and offer the piṇḍas into fire.

## \|\| 10.33 \|\|

*tribhiḥ sapiṃḍīkaraṇaṃ māsaikye tritaye tathā \|*  
*yadā prāpsyati kālena tadā mucyeta baṃdhanāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. When with three piṇḍas he performs sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, then after one month or three months, the person to whom the Śrāddha is offered becomes free from bondage.

## \|\| 10.34 \|\|

*muktopi lepabhāgitvaṃ prāpnoti kuśamārjanāt \|*  
*lepabhājaścaturthādyāstrayaḥ syuḥ piṃḍabhāginaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Even a free soul gets a share in the offerings by sprinkling with a Kuśa blade. The dead ancestors beginning from the fourth are lepa-bhāja, and the first three share the piṇḍas.

## \|\| 10.35 \|\|

*piṇḍadaḥ saptamasteṣāṃ sapiṃḍāḥ saptapūruṣāḥ \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ havyāni deyāni kavyāni ca janairiha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The offerer of the piṇḍa is the seventh among them and the seven are called sapiṇḍas.

## \|\| 10.36 \|\|

*gṛhṇaṃti pitṛloke vā prāyaḥ ke kairnigadyate \|*  
*yadi martye dvijo bhuṃkte hūyate yadi vānale \|\| 36 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

36\. In this world how should people make offerings to gods and deceased persons? Who generally accept these in the world of manes? With which (signs) arc they enumerated? If on the earth a brāhmaṇa is fed or if offering is made into fire how is it that the dead with good and bad minds enjoy that food?

## \|\| 10.37 \|\|

*śubhāśubhātmakāḥ pretāstadannaṃ bhuṃjate katham \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*vasusvarūpāḥ pitaro rudrāścaiva pitāmahāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

37\. The fathers are of the form of Vasu; and the grandfathers are Rudra. Similarly, the great-grandfathers are Āditya. So says Vedic text.

## \|\| 10.38 \|\|

*prapitāmahāstathādityā ityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ \|*  
*nāmagotraṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu prāpakaṃ havyakavyayoḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The (mention of) the name and family of the manes takes to them the offerings meant for divinities and manes.

## \|\| 10.39 \|\|

*śrāddhasya mantratastatvamupalabhyeta bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*agniṣvāttādayasteṣāmādhipatye vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. One should devoutly understand the truth about the Śrāddha offered with incantations. The Agniṣvāttas and others are kept as their chiefs.

## \|\| 10.40 \|\|

*nāmagotrāstadā deśā bhavaṃtyudbhavatāmapi \|*  
*prāṇinaḥ prīṇayatyetadarhaṇaṃ samupāgataṃ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The names and families also of those to be born are controlled by them. This worship when accomplished pleases beings.

## \|\| 10.41 \|\|

*divyo yadi pitā mātā guruḥ karmānuyogataḥ \|*  
*tasyānnamamṛtaṃ bhūtvā divyattvepyanugacchati \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. If the father or the mother or an elderly person is in the heaven due to good deeds, their food (i.e. food offered) becoming nectar goes to them even in their godhead.

## \|\| 10.42 \|\|

*daityatve bhogarūpeṇa paśutvepi tṛṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śrāddhānnaṃ vāyurūpeṇa nāgatvepyupatiṣṭhati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. It takes the form of a repast if they have became (i.e. are born as) demons, and turns into grass if they have become (i.e. are born as) beasts.

## \|\| 10.43 \|\|

*pānaṃ bhavati yakṣatve rākṣasatve tathāmiṣaṃ \|*  
*dānavatve tathā pānaṃ pretatve rudhirodakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The food offered at a Śrāddha stands by them by becoming air (even) if they have become (i.e. born as) serpents. It turns into a drink if they have become (i.e. born as) Yakṣas and becomes flesh if they have turned into fiends; similarly it becomes a drink if they are demons and becomes blood like water if they have become ghosts.

## \|\| 10.44-45 \|\|

*manuṣyatvennapānādi nānābhogavatāṃ bhavet \|*  
*ratiśaktistriyaḥ kānte'nyeṣāṃ bhojanaśaktitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*dānaśaktiḥ sa vibhavā rūpamārogyameva ca \|*  
*śrāddhapuṣpamidaṃ proktaṃ phalaṃ brahmasamāgamaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. If they are born as human beings it turns into food and drink; it is (thus enjoyed) in many ways by the enjoyers. The flower of Śrāddha is said to be sexual power in a lady and the husband’s ability to feed others. It is the power accompanied by prosperity; it is to give handsomeness, and health; and the fruit is union with Brahman.

## \|\| 10.46 \|\|

*āyuḥ putrāndhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargaṃ mokṣaṃ sukhāni ca \|*  
*prayacchanti tathā rājyaṃ prītāḥ pitṛgaṇā nṛpa \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O King, when the hosts of the manes are pleased they grant (long) life, sons, wealth, knowledge, heaven, final release and pleasures and kingdom also.

## \|\| 10.47 \|\|

*śrūyate ca purā mokṣaṃ prāptāḥ kauśikasūnavaḥ \|*  
*paṃcabhirjanmasaṃbaṃdhaiḥ prāptā brahmaparaṃ padam \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. It is heard that Kauśika’s sons after having five existences reached the highest place, viz. that of Brahman.

## \|\| 10.48 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ kauśikadāyādāḥ prāptā yogamanuttamam \|*  
*paṃcabhirjanmasaṃbandhaiḥ kathaṃ karmakṣayo bhavet \|\| 48 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

48\. How did the sons of Kauśika obtain the best union (with Brahman) after having five existences? How does the destruction of (the bondage due to one’s) deeds come about?

## \|\| 10.49 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*kauśiko nāma dharmātmā kurukṣetre mahānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*nāmataḥ karmatastasya putrāṇāṃ tannibodha me \|\| 49 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

49\. In Kurukṣetra there was a great high-souled sage Kauśika by name. Listen to the names and deeds of his sons from me (i.e. as I tell you):

## \|\| 10.50 \|\|

*svasṛpaḥ krodhano hiṃsraḥ piśunaḥ kavireva ca \|*  
*vāgduṣṭaḥ pitṛvartī ca gargaśiṣyāstadābhavan \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Svasṛpa, Krodhana, Hiṃsra, Piśuna, Kavi, Vāgduṣṭa, and Pitṛvartin. They were then the disciples of Garga

## \|\| 10.51 \|\|

*pitaryuparate teṣāmabhūddurbhikṣamulbaṇaṃ \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭiśca mahatī sarvalokabhayaṃkarī \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When their father died, they had to face a great famine; there was also drought causing great fear to all the world.

## \|\| 10.52 \|\|

*gargādeśādvane dogdhrīṃ rakṣaṃti ca tapodhanāḥ \|*  
*khādāmaḥ kapilāmetāṃ vayaṃ kṣutpīḍitā bhṛśaṃ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Those (Kauśika-sons), whose wealth was their penance, protected in the forest, (Garga’s) milch-cow by his order. ‘We are very much oppressed by hunger, (so) we shall eat up this tawny cow’.

## \|\| 10.53 \|\|

*iti ciṃtayatāṃ pāpaṃ laghuḥ prāha tadānujaḥ \|*  
*yadyavaśyamiyaṃ vadhyā śrāddharūpeṇa yojyatāṃ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When they were conceiving this sinful idea, the youngest brother said: “If she must be killed, then utilize her for a Śrāddha. When she will be utilized for a Śrāddha, our sin will certainly perish”.

## \|\| 10.54 \|\|

*śrāddhe niyojyamānāyāṃ pāpaṃ naśyati no dhruvaṃ \|*  
*evaṃ kurvityanujñātaḥ pitṛvartī tadānujaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. When Pitṛvartin was permitted by his brothers with the words ‘Do so’ he, being concentrated, performed the Śrāddha by utilising her.

## \|\| 10.55 \|\|

*cakre samāhitaḥ śrāddhamupayujyātha tāṃ punaḥ \|*  
*dvau daive bhrātaro kṛtvā pitrye trīṃścāparānkramāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He employed, in (due) order two brothers (to receive offerings made to) gods, three (to receive offerings made to) manes, employed one as the guest and himself became the performer of the Śrāddha.

## \|\| 10.56 \|\|

*tathaikamatithiṃ kṛtvā śrāddhadaḥ svayameva tu \|*  
*cakāra maṃtravacchrāddhaṃ smaranpitṛparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Being devoted to his dead ancestors, he performed the Śrāddha with (the recital of) the sacred texts.

## \|\| 10.57 \|\|

*tadā gatvā viśaṃkāste gurave ca nyavedayan \|*  
*vyāghreṇa nihatā dhenurvatsoyaṃ pratigṛhyatāṃ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Then they free from fear, went (to their teacher) and told him: “(Your) cow was killed by a tiger; (please) take back this calf”.

## \|\| 10.58 \|\|

*evaṃ sā bhakṣitā dhenuḥ saptabhistaistapodhanaiḥ \|*  
*vaidikaṃ balamāśritya krūre karmaṇi nirbhayāḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. In this way the seven ascetics fearless due to their depending upon Vedic power in (doing) the cruel deed, had consumed the cow.

## \|\| 10.59 \|\|

*tataḥ kāle praṇaṣṭāste vyādhā daśa purebhavan \|*  
*jātismaratvaṃ prāptāste pitṛbhāvena bhāvitāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Then after having died in (due course of) time, they were born in Daśapura. Transformed into the state of manes, they remembered their (former) existence.

## \|\| 10.60-61 \|\|

*tatra vijñāya vairāgyaṃ prāṇānutsṛjya dharmataḥ \|*  
*lokairavīkṣyamāṇāste tīrthāṃtenaśanena tu \|\| 60 \|\|*

*saṃjātā mṛgarūpāste sapta kālaṃjare girau \|*  
*prāptavijñānayogāste tatyajustāṃ nijāṃ tanum \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Then understanding the true character of asceticism and giving up life religiously not being seen by people, dying near a sacred place, they were born as deer on the Kālañjara mountain. Having secured, through knowledge, contemplation of the Supreme Spirit, they gave up those bodies also.

## \|\| 10.62 \|\|

*mamruḥ prapatanenātha jātavairāgyamānasāḥ \|*  
*mānase cakravrākāste saṃjātāḥ saptayoginaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. With indifference to world produced in their minds they died by falling (from the mountain). The seven ascetics were born as Cakravāka (birds) in the Mānasa lake.

## \|\| 10.63-64 \|\|

*nāmataḥ karmataḥ sarve sumanāḥ kusumovasuḥ \|*  
*cittadarśī sudarśī ca jñātā jñānasya pāragaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*jyeṣṭhānuraktāḥ śreṣṭhāste saptaite yogapāvanāḥ \|*  
*yogabhraṣṭāstrayasteṣāṃ babhūvuścalacetasaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. By name and by deeds they were: Sumanas, Kusuma, Vasu, Cittadarśī, Sudarśī, Jñātā and Jñānapāraga. They loved the eldest brother and (all) the seven were holy due to control of mind. Out of them three of unsteady minds had swerved from the path of yoga.

## \|\| 10.65-69 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā vibhrājamānaṃ tamaṇuhaṃ strībhiranvitam \|*  
*krīḍaṃtaṃ vividhairbhogairmahābalaparākramam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*pañcālānvayasaṃbhūtaṃ prabhūtabalavāhanam \|*  
*rājyakāmobhavattvekasteṣāṃ madhye jalaukasām \|\| 66 \|\|*

*pitṛvartī ca yo vipraḥ śrāddhakṛtpitṛvatsalaḥ \|*  
*aparau maṃtriṇau dṛṣṭvā prabhūtabalavāhanau \|\| 67 \|\|*

*maṃtritve cakratuścecchāmasminmartyau dvijottamau \|*  
*vibhrājaputrastvekobhūdbrahmadatta iti smṛtaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*maṃtriputrau tathā caiva puṃḍarīkasubālakau \|*  
*brahmadattobhiṣiktastu kāṃpilye nagarottame \|\| 69 \|\|*

65-69. Then one of the aquatic birds—brāhmaṇa Pitṛvartin, devoted to manes who performed the Śrāddha, seeing the bright, strong and brave king Aṇuha of the Pañcāla family accompanied by ladies, sporting with various enjoyments, having a large army and vehicles, desired the kingdom (i.e. to be the king). Seeing (Aṇuha’s) two ministers, the other two best brāhmaṇas desired to be his ministers. One of them became Aṇuha’s son (who came to be) known as Brahmadatta. The minister’s sons also came to be known as Puṇḍarīka and Subālaka. Brahmadatta was consecrated in the excellent city of Kāmpilya as the Pañcāla King.

## \|\| 10.70 \|\|

*paṃcālarājo vikrāṃtaḥ śrāddhakṛtpitṛvatsalaḥ \|*  
*yogavitsarvajaṃtūnāṃ cittavettābhavattadā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. He was devoted to his dead anecstors and performed Śrāddha, knew (the path of) Yoga (contemplation of the Supreme Spirit) and read the minds (of others).

## \|\| 10.71 \|\|

*tasya rājñobhavadbhāryā sudevasyātmajā tadā \|*  
*sannatirnāma vikhyātā kapilāyābhavatpurā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. His wife, the queen, was the daughter of Vāsudeva. She was well known as Sannati and was the same tawny cow (in the former existence).

## \|\| 10.72 \|\|

*pitṛkārye niyuktatvādabhavadbrahmavādinī \|*  
*tayā cakāra sahitaḥ sa rājyaṃ rājanaṃdanaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Being engaged in deeds relating to manes she became the expounder of the Vedas. The king ruled over the kingdom with her.

## \|\| 10.73 \|\|

*kadācidgataudyānaṃ tayā saha sa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*dadarśa kīṭamithunamanaṃgakalahānvitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Once he went to a garden with her, and (there) he saw a couple of insects (ants) engaged in love-quarrel.

## \|\| 10.74 \|\|

*pipīlikāmadhovaktrāṃ purataḥ kīṭakāmukaḥ \|*  
*paṃcabāṇābhitaptāṃgaḥ sagadgadamuvāca ha \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The he-ant with his body tormented with sex love said in a faltering tone to the she-ant in front of him and with her face hung down:

## \|\| 10.75-76 \|\|

*na tvayā sadṛśī loke kāminī vidyate kvacit \|*  
*madhye kṣīṇātijaghanā bṛhadvaktrātigāminī \|\| 75 \|\|*

*suvarṇavarṇasadṛśī sadvaktrā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*ālakṣyate ca vadanaṃ guḍaśarkaravatsalaṃ \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. “Nowhere in the world there is a loving female like

you, slender in the waist, of large hips, of expansive breasts, of an excellent gait, having a golden complexion, of a charming face and sweet smile; your face is sweet like jaggery and sugar.

## \|\| 10.77 \|\|

*bhokṣyase mayi bhukte tvaṃ snāsi snāte tathā mayi \|*  
*proṣite mayi dīnā tvaṃ kruddhe ca bhayacaṃcalā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. You eat after I do and bathe after I bathe. You are distressed when I go on a journey and you are uneasy with fear when I am angry.

## \|\| 10.78 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ vada kalyāṇi sadādhovadanāsthitā \|*  
*sā tamāha jvalatkopā kimālapasi re śaṭha \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Why is that, O auspicious one, you always remain with your face hung down?” She with blazing anger said: “What are you speaking?

## \|\| 10.79 \|\|

*tvayā modakacūrṇaṃ tu māṃ vihāyāpi bhakṣitam \|*  
*prādāstvaṃ tadatikramya māmanyasyai samanmathaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. You ate the powder of the modakas without me. Being passionate you gave it to someone else”.

## \|\| 10.80-81 \|\|

*pipīlaka uvāca \|*  
*tvatsādṛśyānmayā dattamanyasyai varavarṇini \|*  
*tadekamaparādhaṃ me kṣaṃtumarhasi bhāmini \|\| 80 \|\|*

*naivaṃ punaḥ kariṣyāmi tyaja kopaṃ ca sustani \|*  
*spṛśāmi pādau satyena praṇatasya prasīda me \|\| 81 \|\|*

The he-ant said:

80-81. O you of excellent complexion, due to similarity with you I gave it to other ant; O you beautiful lady, please forgive (this) one fault of mine; O you of charming breasts, I shall not do so again; give up your anger. Verily I touch your feet (i.e. I salute you), please be pleased with me.

## \|\| 10.82 \|\|

*ruṣṭāyāṃ tvayi suśroṇi mṛtyurme purato bhavet \|*  
*tuṣṭāyāṃ tvayi vāmoru pūrṇāḥ sarvamanorathāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. O you of beautiful hips, when you are angry, death would stand before me; O you of charming thighs, when you are pleased, all my desires are fulfilled.

## \|\| 10.83 \|\|

*pūrṇacaṃdropamaṃ vaktraṃ svādemṛtarasopamam \|*  
*nirbharaṃ piba suśroṇi kāmāsaktasya me sadā \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. O you of beautiful buttocks, drink (i.e. kiss) fully the face of me who am always passionate like the full moon and resembling nectar in taste.

## \|\| 10.84 \|\|

*etanmatvā śubhe kāryā sarvadā tu kṛpā mayi \|*  
*iti sā vacanaṃ śrutvā prasannā cābhavattataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Granting this, O you auspicious one, you should always show favour to me.

Hearing these words she then became pleased.

## \|\| 10.85 \|\|

*ātmānamarpayāmāsa mohanāya pipīlikā \|*  
*brahmadattopi tatsarvaṃ jñātvā sasmayamāhasat \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The she-ant offered herself to the fascinating one. Brahmadatta too, conversant with the sounds of all animals due to the efficacy of the deeds (in his) former (existence) knowing all that, smiled in amazement.

## \|\| 10.86 \|\|

*sarvasatvarutajñānī prabhāvātpūrvakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ sarvarutajñobhūdbrahmadatto narādhipaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

86\. How did king Brahmadatta know the (meaning of the) sounds of all (animals)?

## \|\| 10.87 \|\|

*taccāpi cābhavatkutra cakravākacatuṣṭayaṃ \|*  
*tanme kathaya sarvajña kule kasya ca suvratam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Where did the group of the four Cakravākas live? O omniscient one, tell me all that and (tell me) in which family that (group) of good vows was (born)?

## \|\| 10.88 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tasminneva pure jātāścakravākā atho nṛpa \|\| 88 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

88\. O king, the Cakravākas were born in the same city as the sons of an old brāhmaṇa and all they—the wise brāhmaṇas—remembered their (former) birth.

## \|\| 10.89 \|\|

*vṛddhadvijasya dāyādā viprā jātismarā budhāḥ \|*  
*dhṛtimāṃstattvadarśī ca vidyāvarṇastapodhikaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. They were the sons of a brāhmaṇa named Sudaridra,

## \|\| 10.90 \|\|

*nāmataḥ karmataścaiva sudaridrasya te sutāḥ \|*  
*tapase buddhirabhavatteṣāṃ vai dvijajanmanāṃ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Their names and deeds befitted them: Dhṛtimān, Tattvadarśī, Vidyāvarṇa and Tapodhika. The brāhmaṇas had a mind to practise penance.

## \|\| 10.91-93 \|\|

*yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ siddhimūcuste dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*tatteṣāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā sudaridro mahātapāḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*uvāca dīnayā vācā kimetaditi putrakāḥ \|*  
*adharma eṣa vaḥ putrā pitā tānityuvāca ha \|\| 92 \|\|*

*vṛddhaṃ pitaramutsṛjya daridraṃ vanavāsinam \|*  
*kva nu dharmotra bhavitā māṃ tyaktvā gatimeva ca \|\| 93 \|\|*

91-93. The best brāhmaṇas said: “We shall attain great superhuman power”. Hearing these words of them, Sudaridra, a great ascetic, said with piteous words: “What is this, O sons?” He said to them “O sons, this is a failure in your duty; forsaking your old father, living in a forest, what merit, what scope will you have by doing this?”

## \|\| 10.94-98 \|\|

*ūcuste kalpitā vṛttistava tāta vacaśśṛṇu \|*  
*vratametatpurā rājñaḥ sa te dāsyati puṣkalaṃ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ grāma sahasrāṇi prabhāte paṭhatastava \|*  
*kurukṣetre tu ye viprā vyādhā daśapure tu ye \|\| 95 \|\|*

*kālaṃjare mṛgā bhūtāścakravākāstu mānase \|*  
*ityuktvā pitaraṃ jagmuste vanaṃ tapase punaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*vṛddhopi sa dvijo rājanjagāma svārthasiddhaye \|*  
*aṇuho nāma vaibhrājaḥ pañcālādhipatiḥ purā \|\| 97 \|\|*

*putrārthī devadeveśaṃ padmayoniṃ pitāmaham \|*  
*ārādhayāmāsa vibhuṃ tīvravrataparāyaṇaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

94-98. They said: “O father, we have arranged for your subsistance; listen to our words. The King (here) maintains an old vow. He will give much wealth, a thousand villages to you who (should) tell him in the morning, ‘Those who were brāhmaṇas in Kurukṣetra, who were hunters in Daśapura, they became deer on the Kālañjara (mountain) and Crkravākas \[Cakravākas?\] in the Mānasa (lake)’. Speaking thus to the father they went to the forest for (practising) penance. O King, that old (brāhmaṇa) too, went to secure his object. Formerly, Vaibhrāja, named Aṇuha, the lord of Pañcāla, desiring a son, engaged in severe penance, propitiated eternal Brahmā, the lord of lords.

## \|\| 10.99 \|\|

*tataḥ kālena mahatā tuṣṭastasya pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te hṛdayebhīpsitaṃ nṛpa \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Then after a long time Brahmā was pleased with him (and said to him); “Well-being to you; choose a boon—the desire of your heart”.

## \|\| 10.100-102 \|\|

*aṇuha uvāca \|*  
*putraṃ me dehi deveśa mahābalaparākramam \|*  
*pāragaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ dhārmikaṃ yogināṃ varam \|\| 100 \|\|*

*sarvasatvarutajñaṃ me dehi yoginamātmajam \|*  
*evamastviti viśvātmā tamāha parameśvaraḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*tataḥ sa tasya putrobhūdbrahmadattaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 102 \|\|*

Aṇuha said:

100-102. O lord of gods, give me a son of great strength and valour, master of all lores, religious, and best among the devotees. Give me a son, a devotee and one who would know (the meaning of) the sounds of all beings.

The lord, the universal soul, said to him: “Let it be so,” and disappeared there only when all the beings were seeing (i.e. in the presence of all beings). Then he had that brave son, Brahmadatta.

## \|\| 10.103 \|\|

*sarvasatvānukaṃpī ca sarvasatvabalādhikaḥ \|*  
*sarvasatvarutajñaśca sarvasatveśvareśvaraḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. (He was) compassionate to all beings, and was more powerful than all of them; he knew (the meaning of) the sounds of all beings and was the lord of lords of all beings.

## \|\| 10.104 \|\|

*atha satvena yogātmā sa pipīlakamāgataḥ \|*  
*yatra tatkīṭamithunaṃ ramamāṇamavasthitam \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Due to his inherent power, he, naturally disposed to concentration of mind, came to the he-ant to that place where the couple of the sporting ants had remained.

## \|\| 10.105 \|\|

*tataḥ sā sannatirdṛṣṭvā prahasaṃtaṃ suvismitaṃ \|*  
*kimapyāśaṃkamānā sā tamapṛcchannareśvaram \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Then that Sannati, seeing him smiling and very much amazed, suspecting something, asked the king:

## \|\| 10.106 \|\|

*sannatiruvāca \|*  
*akasmādatihāsoyaṃ kimarthamabhavannṛpa \|*  
*hāsyahetuṃ na jānāmi yadakāle kṛtaṃ tvayā \|\| 106 \|\|*

Sannati said:

106\. O King, why this untimely smile? I do not know the reason for which you have smiled untimely.

## \|\| 10.107-108 \|\|

*avadadrājaputrosau taṃ pipīlikabhāṣitam \|*  
*rāgavadvirasotpannametaddhāsyaṃ varānane \|\| 107 \|\|*

*na cānyatkāraṇaṃ kiṃciddhāsyahetuḥ śucismite \|*  
*na sāmanyatataṃ devī prāhālīkamidaṃ tava \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. The prince told her the words of the ant. “O you of excellent face, this sympathetic smile has sprung up from great interest; O you of bright smile, there is no other reason for my smile”. The queen did not agree with him, She said: “You are telling a lie.

## \|\| 10.109 \|\|

*ahameveha hasitā na jīviṣye tvayādhunā \|*  
*kathaṃ pipīlikālāpaṃ martyo vetti surādṛte \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. You laughed at me only. Now I won’t live with you. How can a mortal, who is not a god, understand the talk of ants?

## \|\| 10.110 \|\|

*tasmāttvayāhamevādya hasitā kimataḥ param \|*  
*tato niruttaro rājā jijñāsustadvaco hareḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Therefore, today you laughed at me only. What else (can be said)?”

## \|\| 10.111 \|\|

*āsthāya niyamaṃ tasthau saptarātramakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*svapnānte prāha taṃ brahmā prabhāte paryaṭanpuram \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. The king, unable to answer, desiring to know (seek) Hara’s advice observed, remaining pure, his (Hara’s) vow for seven nights. Brahmā while wandering in the city in the morning, said to him at the end of his (King’s) dream:

## \|\| 10.112-113 \|\|

*vṛddhadvijottamādvākyaṃ sarvaṃ jñāsyati te priyā \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhe brahmā prabhāte ca nṛpaḥ purāt \|\| 112 \|\|*

*nirgacchanmantrisahitaḥ sabhāryo vṛddhamagrataḥ \|*  
*gadaṃtaṃ vipramāyāṃtaṃ vṛddhaṃ ca sa dadarśa ha \|\| 113 \|\|*

112-113. “Your beloved will learn every word from the best of brāhmaṇas.” Saying so, Brahmā disappeared. In the morning the king moving out of the city with his minisrers and wife saw the old brāhmaṇa, saying (something) and coming before (i.e. towards) him.

## \|\| 10.114 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*ye vipramukhyāḥ kurujāṃgaleṣu dāśāstathā dāśapure mṛgāśca \|*  
*kālaṃjare sapta ca cakravākā ye mānase tetra vasaṃti siddhāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. The brāhmaṇa said: “Those sages who were the chief brāhmaṇas in Kurujāṅgala, fishermen in Daśapura, and deer in Kālañjara mountain and the seven Cakravākas in the Mānasa lake, they are living here”.

## \|\| 10.115 \|\|

*ityākarṇya vacastasya sa papāta śucānvitaḥ \|*  
*jātismaratvamagamattau ca maṃtrivarātmajau \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Hearing these words of him, he fell down with grief and recollected his (past) birth; the minister's two sons also (remembered their past birth).

## \|\| 10.116 \|\|

*kāmaśāstrapraṇetā tu bābhravyaḥ sa tu bālakaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāla iti lokeṣu viśrutaḥ sarvaśāstravit \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. That boy Bābhravya who knew all sciences, came to be known as Pañcāla in the worlds and was the expounder of the science of love.

## \|\| 10.117 \|\|

*puṃḍarīkopi dharmātmā vedaśāstrapravartakaḥ \|*  
*bhūtvā jātismarau śokātpatitāvagratastathā \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Pious Puṇḍarīka too, the founder of the science of Veda, recollected his former birth and through grief fell before them in the same way.

## \|\| 10.118 \|\|

*hā vayaṃ karmavibhraṣṭāḥ kāmataḥ karmabaṃdhanāt \|*  
*evaṃ vilapya bahuśastrayaste yogapāragāḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. ‘Oh! Due to passion, we had, due to the bondage of our actions, fallen from our (proper) deeds’.

## \|\| 10.119 \|\|

*vismayācchrāddhamāhāmyamabhinaṃdya punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*sa tu tasmai dhanaṃ dattvā prabhūtagrāmasaṃyutam \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. The three, well-versed in Yoga, having thus lamented again and again, repeatedly praised with wonder the greatness of Śrāddha.

## \|\| 10.120 \|\|

*visṛjya brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ ca vṛddhaṃ dhanamadānvitam \|*  
*ātmīyaṃ nṛpatiḥ putraṃ nṛpalakṣaṇasaṃyutam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. The king, then having given (the old brāhmaṇa) wealth with many villages and having dismissed him, full of joy, due to (having received) wealth, consecrated on the throne his son, Viṣvaksena by name and endowed with kingly qualities.

## \|\| 10.121-123 \|\|

*viṣvaksenābhidhānaṃ ca rājārājyebhyaṣecayat \|*  
*mānase salile sarve tataste yogināṃ varāḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

*brahmadattādayastasminpitṛbhaktā vimatsarāḥ \|*  
*sannatiścābhavaddhṛṣṭā mayaiva tava darśitam \|\| 122 \|\|*

*rājanyogaphalaṃ sarvaṃ yadetadabhilakṣyate \|*  
*tatheti prāha rājāpi purastādabhinaṃdayan \|\| 123 \|\|*

121-123a. Then all the best ascetics, Brahmadatta and others, devoted to their parents and free from hatred, went to the water of the Mānasa lake. Sannati too, was glad saying “O King, I pointed out to you all this and the fruit of abstract meditation—that is seen”.

123b. Then (in the sequel) praising her the king said:

## \|\| 10.124 \|\|

*tvatprasādādidaṃ sarvaṃ mayaivaṃ prāpyate phalam \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. “It is so; through your favour I have obtained all this fruit.”

## \|\| 10.125 \|\|

*tataste yogamāsthāya sarva eva vanaukasaḥ \|*  
*brahmaraṃdhreṇa paramaṃ padamāpustapobalāt \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Then all these residents of forest, contemplating on the Supreme Spirit, obtained, by the strength of their penance, the highest place through the aperture in the crown of the head.

## \|\| 10.126 \|\|

*evamāyurdhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargamokṣasukhāni ca \|*  
*prayacchaṃti sutaṃ rājyaṃ nṛṇāṃ tuṣṭāḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. Thus the ancestors, when pleased, give men (long) life, wealth, knowledge, heaven, final release and pleasure, and also son and kingdom.

## \|\| 10.127 \|\|

*idaṃ ca pitṛmāhātmyaṃ brahmadattasya vai nṛpa \|*  
*dvijebhyaḥ śrāvayedvidvānśṛṇoti paṭhatepi vā \|*  
*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. O king, one who reads out to brāhmaṇas or listens to or reads this Pitṛ-māhātmya (greatness of the ancestors) of Brahmadatta, is honoured in heaven for a full hundred crores of Kalpas (Kalpa=432 million years of mortals).

## Chapter 11 - A list of sacred places (tīrtha)

## \|\| 11.2-3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tīrthaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ nāma yattu śreṣṭhatamaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ dvijamukhyānāṃ manorathamiva sthitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra dattaṃ hutaṃ japtamanantaṃ bhavati dhruvam \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ vallabhaṃ nityamṛṣīṇāṃ paramaṃ matam \|\| 3 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

I. During which portion of the day should the performer of a Śrāddha perform it? O brāhmaṇa, what are the sacred places in which Śrāddha performed gives abundant fruit?

Pulastya spoke:

2-3. The sacred place named Puṣkara, is said to be the greatest. Presents or offerings made there, or muttering done there certainly becomes endless. It is always dear to the manes and is regarded as great by the sages.

## \|\| 11.4 \|\|

*naṃdātha lalitā tadvattīrthaṃ māyāpurī śubhā \|*  
*tathā mitrapadaṃ rājaṃstataḥ kedāramuttamam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. So also, O king, Nandā, Lalitā, so also the sacred place, viz. the auspicious Māyāpurī, so also Mitrapada; Kedāra is still better.

## \|\| 11.5 \|\|

*gaṃgāsāgaramityāhuḥ sarvatīrthamayaṃ śubham \|*  
*tīrthaṃ brahmasarastadvacchatadrusalilaṃ śubham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Gaṅgāsāgara is also said to be an aupsicious sacred place composed of all sacred places; similarly Brahma-tīrtha is auspicious having the water of Śatadru.

## \|\| 11.6-7 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ tu naimiṣaṃ nāma sarvatīrthaphalapradam \|*  
*gaṃgodbhedastu gomatyāṃ yatrodbhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tathā yajñavarāhastu devadevaśca śūladhṛk \|*  
*yatra tatkāṃcanaṃ dānamaṣṭādaśabhujo haraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. There is a sacred place named Naimiṣa giving the fruit of all sacred places. On (the bank of) Gomatī there is a sacred place called Gaṅgodbheda, where Brahmā, Viṣṇu and (Śiva) the trident-holder came up; where golden gifts are offered, and Hara with eighteen arms (lives).

## \|\| 11.8 \|\|

*nemistu dharmacakrasya śīrṇā yatrābhavatpurā \|*  
*tadetannaimiśāraṇyaṃ sarvatīrthaniṣevitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. That is the Naimiṣa forest where formerly the rim of the wheel of Dharma wore out. It is waited upon by all (other) Tīrthas.

## \|\| 11.9 \|\|

*devadevasya tatrāpi varāhasya ca darśanam \|*  
*yaḥ prayāti sa pūtātmā nārāyaṇapuraṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There also one can have the sight of (Viṣṇu in his) Varāha (incarnation). One who goes there, goes, with his soul purified, to the city of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 11.10 \|\|

*kokāmukhaṃ paraṃ tīrthamindramārgopi lakṣyate \|*  
*athāpi pitṛtīrthaṃ tu brahmaṇovyaktajanmanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Another sacred place is Kokāmukha; Indramārga is also noted (as a Tīrtha). Another Tirtha is Pitṛ-tīrtha (sacred to) Brahmā, manifesting his existence.

## \|\| 11.11 \|\|

*puṣkarāraṇyasaṃsthosau yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*viriṃcidarśanaṃ śreṣṭhamapavargaphalapradam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. That lord Brahmā resides in Puṣkara forest. The sight of Brahmā is most prosperous and gives the fruit in the form of final release.

## \|\| 11.12 \|\|

*kṛtaṃ nāma mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapāpaniṣūdanam \|*  
*yatrādyo nārasiṃhastu svayameva janārdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Kṛta is (one more) sacred place of great religious merit and it destroys all sins; where Janārdana, the first Narasiṃha (resides).

## \|\| 11.13 \|\|

*tīrthamikṣumatīnāma pitṝṇāṃ ca śubhāvahā \|*  
*tuṣyanti pitaro nityaṃ gaṃgāyamunasaṃgame \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Īkṣumati is a sacred place auspicious to the manes; at the confluence of the Ganges and Jumna the manes are always pleased.

## \|\| 11.14 \|\|

*kurukṣetraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ yatra mārgopi lakṣyate \|*  
*adyāpi pitṛtīrthaṃ tu sarvakāmaphalapradam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Kurukṣetra has great religious merit; where the path (to heaven) is also noticed. Even now (this) tīrtha, sacred to the manes, fulfils all desires.

## \|\| 11.15-16 \|\|

*nīlakaṇṭhamiti khyātaṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*tathā bhadrasaraḥ puṇyaṃ saro mānasameva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*maṃdākinī tathā'cchodā vipāśā ca sarasvatī \|*  
*sarvamitrapadaṃ tadvadvaidyanāthaṃ mahāphalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. O King, (there is another sacred place) called Nīlakaṇṭha, sacred to the manes. Similarly other tīrthas are: Bhadrasaras, Puṇyasaras, and Mānasa. So also Mandākinī, Acchodā, Vipāsā, and Sarasvatī, Sarvamitrapada, Vaidyanātha giving great fruit.

## \|\| 11.17 \|\|

*kṣiprā nadī tathā puṇyā tathā kālañjaraṃ śubham \|*  
*tīrthodbhedaṃ harodbhedaṃ garbhabhedaṃ mahālayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. River Kṣiprā is similarly sacred; so also Kālañjara is auspicious; (other tīrthas are) Tīrthodbheda, Harodbheda, Garbhabheda, Mahālaya.

## \|\| 11.18 \|\|

*bhadreśvaraṃ viṣṇupadaṃ narmadā dvārameva ca \|*  
*gayāpiṃḍapradānena samānyāhurmaharṣayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Bhadreśvara, Viṣṇupada and Narmadādvāra, Gayā; the great sages say that they resemble (one another) (are equally meritorious) because of the offering of piṇḍas i.e. as far as offering of piṇḍas goes.

## \|\| 11.19 \|\|

*etāni pitṛtīrthāni sarvapāpaharāṇi ca \|*  
*smaraṇādapi lokānāṃ kimu śrāddhapradāyinām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. These places sacred to the manes remove all sins, even of those people who remember them; then what about those who offer Śrāddha (at these places)?

## \|\| 11.20-21 \|\|

*oṃkāraṃ pitṛtīrthaṃ tu kāverīkapilodakam \|*  
*saṃbhedaścaṇḍavegāyāṃ tathaivāmarakaṃṭakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kurukṣetrāccadviguṇaṃ tasminsnānādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śuklatīrthaṃ tu vikhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ someśvaraṃ param \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Oṃkāra is (another) place sacred to the manes; so also Kāverī and Kapilodaka; Sambheda on (the bank of) the Caṇḍavegā (river); so also Amarakaṇṭaka; bath etc. in it gives merit which is double that of Kurukṣetra. (Another) well-known sacred place is Śuklatīrtha; Someśvara is a great Tīrtha.

## \|\| 11.22 \|\|

*sarvavyādhiharaṃpuṇyaṃphalaṃkoṭiguṇādhikam \|*  
*śrāddhedānetathāhomesvādhyāyecāpisannidhau \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. It removes all ailments, is meritorious and gives a crore times greater fruit by (one’s) offering śrāddha, giving gifts, performing sacrifice or reciting sacred texts in its vicinity.

## \|\| 11.23 \|\|

*kāyāvārohaṇaṃ nāma devadevasya śūlinaḥ \|*  
*avatāraṃ rocamānaṃ brāhmaṇāvasathe śubhe \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Another sacred place is by name Kāyāvārohaṇa where, in the auspicious dwelling place of Brāhmaṇas, there is a lovely form of the trident-holder, lord of gods.

## \|\| 11.24 \|\|

*jātaṃ tatsumahāpuṇyaṃ tathā carmaṇvatī nadī \|*  
*śūlatāpī payoṣṇī ca payoṣṇīsaṃgamastathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. It has become extremely meritorious; similarly the river Carmaṇvatī (is a tīrtha); Śūlatāpī, Payoṣṇī and the confluence of Payoṣṇī (with Śūlatāpī).

## \|\| 11.25 \|\|

*mahauṣadhī cāraṇā ca nāgatīrthapravarttinī \|*  
*mahāveṇā nadī puṇyā mahāśālastathaiva ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Mahauṣadhī, Cāraṇā and the meritorious Mahāveṇā flowing to Nāgatīrtha; so also Mahāśāla.

## \|\| 11.26 \|\|

*gomatī varuṇā tadvattīrthaṃ hautāśanaṃ param \|*  
*bhairavaṃ bhṛgutuṃgaṃ ca gaurītīrthamanuttamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. So also Gomatī. Varuṇā is a great sacred place of Agni. Bhairava, Bhṛgutuṅga and Gaurītīrtha are incomparably the best.

## \|\| 11.27 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ vaināyakaṃ nāma vastreśvaramanuttamam \|*  
*tathā pāpaharaṃ nāma puṇyā vetravatī nadī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. (Then there is) a sacred place by name Vaināyaka; so also the best tīrtha Vastreśvara. Similarly (there is the tīrtha) named Pāpahara and there is the holy river Vetravatī.

## \|\| 11.28 \|\|

*mahārudraṃ mahāliṃgaṃ daśārṇā ca mahānadī \|*  
*śatarudrā śatāhvā ca tathā pitṛpadaṃ puram \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. (The tīrthas) Mahārudra and Mahāliṅga (are other sacred places) and the great river Daśārṇā. So also Śatarudrā, Śatāhvā and the city called Pitṛpada.

## \|\| 11.29 \|\|

*aṃgāravāhikā tadvannadau dvau śoṇaghargharau \|*  
*kālikā ca nadī puṇyā pitarā ca nadī śubhā \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. (River) Aṅgāravāhikā and the two big rivers Śoṇa and Gharghara, the holy river Kālikā and the auspicious river Pitarā.

## \|\| 11.30 \|\|

*etāni pitṛtīrthāni śasyaṃte snānadānayoḥ \|*  
*śrāddhameteṣu yaddattaṃ tadanaṃtaphalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. These are sacred places for manes which are recommended for bath and for making presents. śrāddha offered here is said to have an inexhaustible fruit.

## \|\| 11.31 \|\|

*śatāvaṭā nadī jvālā śaradvī ca nadī tathā \|*  
*dvārakā kṛṣṇatīrthaṃ ca tathā hyudaksarasvatī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The river Śatāvaṭā, so also Jvālā and Śaradvī. Dvārakā, Kṛṣṇatīrtha and the Northern Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 11.32 \|\|

*nadī mālavatī nāma tathā ca girikarṇikā \|*  
*dhūtapāpaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ samudre dakṣiṇe tathā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. River Mālavatī; so also Girikarṇikā; so also the Dhūtapāpatīrtha in the southern ocean.

## \|\| 11.33 \|\|

*gokarṇo gajakarṇaśca tathā cakranadī śubhā \|*  
*śrīśailaṃ śākatīrthaṃ ca nārasiṃhamataḥ param \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Gokarṇa and Gajakarṇa; similarly the auspicious river Cakra. Śrīśaila, Śākatīrtha and then Nārasiṃha.

## \|\| 11.34 \|\|

*maheṃdraṃ ca tathā puṇyā puṇyā cāpi mahānadī \|*  
*eteṣvapi sadā śrāddhamanaṃtaphaladaṃ smṛtam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. So also Mahendra, Puṇya and the holy Mahānadī. A śrāddha offered at these places also is said to give unending fruit.

## \|\| 11.35 \|\|

*darśanādapi puṇyāni sadyaḥ pāpaharāṇi vai \|*  
*tuṃgabhadrā nadī puṇyā tathā cakrarathīti ca \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Even their sight gives religious merit and they instantly remove sin. Tuṅgabhadrā is a holy river; so also is Cakrarathī.

## \|\| 11.36 \|\|

*bhīmeśvaraṃ kṛṣṇaveṇā kāverī cāṃjanā nadī \|*  
*nadī godāvarī puṇyā trisaṃdhyā pūrṇamuttamam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Bhīmeśvara, (and rivers) Kṛṣṇaveṇā, Kāverī and Añjanā. River Godāvarī is holy; Trisandhyāpūrṇa is the best.

## \|\| 11.37 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ traiyaṃbakaṃ nāma sarvatīrthanamaskṛtam \|*  
*yatrāste bhagavānbhīmaḥ svayameva trilocanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The tīrtha named Tryambaka is a complete and excellent tīrtha and is respected by (i.e. superior to) all other sacred places. Here the terrible three-eyed lord (i.e. Śiva) himself resides.

## \|\| 11.38 \|\|

*śrāddhameteṣu sarveṣu dattaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*smaraṇādapi pāpāni vrajaṃti śatadhā nṛpa \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Śrāddha offered at these places is a crore times meritgiving; O king, even by remembering these (places) sins go away in a hundred ways.

## \|\| 11.39 \|\|

*śrīparṇā ca nadī puṇyā vyāsatīrthamanuttamam \|*  
*tathā matsyanadī kārā śivadhārā tathaiva ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The river Śrīparṇā is holy, so also the Vyāsatīrtha is unparalleled. So, also Matsyanadī, Kārā and Śivadhārā.

## \|\| 11.40 \|\|

*bhavatīrthaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ puṇyatīrthaṃ ca śāśvatam \|*  
*puṇyaṃ rāmeśvaraṃ tadvadveṇāpuramalaṃpuram \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. There is the well-known Bhava-tīrtha and the eternal Puṇyatīrtha. Similarly there are the holy Rāmeśvara and Veṇāpura and Alaṃpura.

## \|\| 11.41 \|\|

*aṃgārakaṃ ca vikhyātamātmadarśamalaṃbuṣam \|*  
*vatsavrāteśvaraṃ tadvattathāgokāmukhaṃ param \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The famous Aṅgāraka, and Ātmadarśa and Alambuṣa; so also Vatsavrāteśvara and the great Gokāmukha.

## \|\| 11.42 \|\|

*govarddhanaṃ hariścaṃdraṃ puraścandraṃ pṛthūdakam \|*  
*sahasrākṣaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathā ca kadalīnadī \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Govardhana, Hariścandra, Puraścandra, Pṛthūdaka, Sahasrākṣa, Hiraṇyākṣa, so also the river Kadalī.

## \|\| 11.43 \|\|

*nāmadheyāni ca tathā tathā saumitrisaṃgatam \|*  
*iṃdranīlaṃ mahānādaṃ tathā ca priyamelakam \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The (other) names are: Lakṣmaṇa-tīrtha, Indranīla, Mahānāda; so also Priyamelaka.

## \|\| 11.44 \|\|

*etānyapi sadā śrāddhe praśastānyadhikāni ca \|*  
*eteṣu sarvadevānāṃ sāṃnidhyaṃ paṭhyate yataḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. These also are very much recommended for the performance of śrāddha, since it is said that in these holy places all gods are present.

## \|\| 11.45 \|\|

*dānameteṣu sarveṣu bhavetkoṭiśatādhikam \|*  
*bāhudā ca nadī puṇyā tathā siddhavaṭaṃ śubham \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Presents made at all these become a crore times more

fruitful. Similarly there is the river Bāhudā, so also the auspicious Siddhavaṭa.

## \|\| 11.46 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ pāśupataṃ caiva nadī paryaṭikā tathā \|*  
*śrāddhameteṣu sarveṣu dattaṃ koṭiśatottaram \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. And the holy place Pāśupata, similarly river Paryaṭikā. Presents made at all these places become a crore times greater.

## \|\| 11.47 \|\|

*tathaiva paṃcatīrthaṃ ca yatra godāvarī nadī \|*  
*yutā liṃgasahasreṇa savyetara jalāvahā \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. So also the Pañcatīrtha where the river Godāvarī, flowing towards left, comes in contact with Liṅga-sahasra.

## \|\| 11.48 \|\|

*jāmadagnyasya tattīrthaṃ modāyatanamuttamam \|*  
*pratīkasya bhayātsiddhā yatra godāvarī nadī \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The place sacred to Jāmadagnya is the best place for (getting) final release; where the river stands ready due to the fear of an adversary.

## \|\| 11.49 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ taddhavyakavyānāmapsarogaṇasaṃyutam \|*  
*śrāddhāgni dānakāryaṃ ca tatra koṭiśatādhikam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. That is the holy place for making offerings to gods and manes and has a host of the celestial nymphs.

## \|\| 11.50 \|\|

*tathā sahasraliṃgaṃ ca rāghaveśvaramuttamam \|*  
*sendrakālā nadī puṇyā tatra śakro gataḥ purā \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. So also Sahasraliṅga and excellent Rāghaveśvara with the sacred river Indrakālā; there Śakra had formerly gone.

## \|\| 11.51 \|\|

*nihatya namuciṃ mitraṃ tapasā svargamāptavān \|*  
*tatra dattaṃ naraiḥ śrāddhamanaṃtaphaladaṃ bhavet \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Having killed Namuci he reached heaven by (practising) penance. Śrāddha offered here by men gives inexhaustible fruit.

## \|\| 11.52 \|\|

*puṣkaraṃ nāma vai tīrthaṃ śālagrāmaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*śoṇapātaśca vikhyāto yatra vaiśvānarāśayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The sacred place Puṣkara, so also Śālagrāma; then the well-knwon Śoṇapāta where there is the abode of Supreme Being.

## \|\| 11.53 \|\|

*tīrthaṃ sārasvataṃ caiva svāmitīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*malaṃdarā nadī puṇyā kauśikī caṃdrakā tathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Then (there are) the Sārasvatatīrtha, and Svāmitīrtha also; then the holy river Malandarā, so also Kauśikī and Candrakā.

## \|\| 11.54 \|\|

*vidarbhā cātha vegā ca payoṣṇī prāṅmukhā parā \|*  
*kāverī cottarāṃgā ca tathā jālaṃdharo giriḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Then (the river) Vidarbhā, and Vegā and Payoṣṇī flowing towards the east. Kāverī flowing in the northern direction; similarly the mountain Jālandhara.

## \|\| 11.55 \|\|

*eteṣu śrāddhatīrtheṣu śrāddhamānaṃtyamaśnute \|*  
*lohadaṃḍaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ citrakūṭastathaiva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Śrāddha offered at these holy places meant for offering Śrāddha becomes endless. Similarly Lohadaṇḍa is a tīrtha, so also Citrakūṭa.

## \|\| 11.56 \|\|

*divyaṃ sarvatra gaṃgāyāstathā nadyāstaṭaṃ śubham \|*  
*kubjāmrakaṃ tathā tīrthamurvaśīpulinaṃ tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Similarly the bank of the river Ganges is everywhere divine and auspicious. Then (there are the tīrthas) Kubjā, Āmraka and Urvaśīpulina.

## \|\| 11.57 \|\|

*saṃsāramocanaṃ tīrthaṃ tathaiva ṛṇamocanam \|*  
*eteṣu pitṛtīrtheṣu śrāddhamānaṃtyamaśnute \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. (Then there are) the Saṃsāramocana-tīrtha, so also Ṛṇamocana. Śrāddha offered at these places meant for offering Śrāddha is inexhaustible.

## \|\| 11.58 \|\|

*aṭṭahāsaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ gautameśvarameva ca \|*  
*tathā vasiṣṭhatīrthaṃ ca bhārataṃ ca tataḥ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Similarly is the tīrtha Aṭṭahāsa; so also Gautameśvara; then is the Vasiṣṭha-tīrtha; next one is Bhārata (tīrtha).

## \|\| 11.59 \|\|

*brahmāvartaṃ kuśāvartaṃ haṃsatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*piṃḍārakaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ śaṃkhoddhāraṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Similarly Brahmāvarta, Kuśāvarta and Haṃsatīrtha (are other tīrthas), so also (are) the well-known Piṇḍāraka and Śaṃkhoddhāra.

## \|\| 11.60 \|\|

*bhāṃḍeśvaraṃ bilvakaṃ ca nīlaparvatameva ca \|*  
*tathā ca badarītīrthaṃ sarvatīrtheśvareśvaram \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. So also Bhāṇḍeśvara, Bilvaka and Nīlaparvata; Similarly (is) Badaritīrtha, the greatest of all holy places.

## \|\| 11.61 \|\|

*vasudhārāhvayaṃ tīrthaṃ rāmatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*jayaṃtī vijayā caiva śuklatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. And (there is) the holy place called Vasudhārā, so also Rāmeśvara; then Jayantī, Vijayā and Śukla.

## \|\| 11.62 \|\|

*eṣu śrāddhapradātāraḥ prayāṃti paramaṃ padam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ mātṛgṛhaṃ nāma karavīrapuraṃ tathā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Those who offer Śrāddha at these places go to the highest place; (then there is) a sacred place named Mātṛgṛha; also Karavīra.

## \|\| 11.63 \|\|

*saptagodāvarīnāma sarvatīrtheśvareśvaram \|*  
*tatra śrāddhaṃ pradātavyamanaṃtaphalamīpsubhiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. (The tīrtha) Sapta-godāvarī is the best among all the holy places; those desiring inexhaustible fruit should offer Śrāddha there.

## \|\| 11.64 \|\|

*kīkaṭeṣu gayā puṇyā puṇyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ vanam \|*  
*cyavanasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ nadī puṇyā punaḥpunā \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The holy Gayā is in the Kīkaṭa country; the Rājagṛha forest is holy; so also (is) Cyavanāśrama; the river Punaḥpunā is also holy.

## \|\| 11.65 \|\|

*viṣayārādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ nadī yā tu punaḥpunā \|*  
*yatra gāthā vicarati brahmaṇā parikīrtitā \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The holy place Viṣayārādhana and the sacred river Punaḥpunā, where the (following) verse composed by Brahmā is (still) floating.

## \|\| 11.66 \|\|

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyekopi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. ‘If someone desires many sons he should go to Gayā; one should either perform a horse-sacrifice or should let loose a bull at the Nīla (mountain)’.

## \|\| 11.67 \|\|

*eṣā gāthā vicarati tīrtheṣvāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*sarve manuṣyā rājeṃdra kīrttayaṃtaḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. This is the verse floating at the sacred (and other) places; all men, O best king, came saying:

## \|\| 11.68 \|\|

*kimasmākaṃ kule kaścidgayāṃ yāsyati yaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*prīṇayiṣyati tāngatvā saptapūrvāṃstathāparān \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Will any son from our family go to Gayā, who, will propitiate the seven earlier and later (members of the family)?

## \|\| 11.69-70 \|\|

*mātāmahānāmapyevaṃ śrutireṣā ciraṃtanī \|*  
*gaṃgāyāmasthinicayaṃ gatvā kṣepsyati yaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tilaiḥ saptāṣṭabhirvāpi dāsyate ca jalāṃjalim \|*  
*araṇyatritaye vāpi piṃḍadānaṃ kariṣyati \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Among the maternal grandfathers these words have become long-standing: (Will there be) a son, who, having gone (to the Ganges), will drop the collection (of the ashes) of the bones into the Ganges and offer water with even seven or eight sesamum seeds or offer piṇḍas in (one of) the three forests (viz. Puṣkara, Naimiṣa and Dharma)?

## \|\| 11.71 \|\|

*prathamaṃ puṣkarāraṇye naimiṣe tadanaṃtaraṃ \|*  
*dharmāraṇyaṃ punaḥ prāpya śrāddhaṃ bhaktyā pradāsyati \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. (Who) with devotion will offer a śrāddha, first in the Puṣkara-araṇya, then in the Naimiṣāraṇya and then in Dharmāraṇya?

## \|\| 11.72 \|\|

*gayāyāṃ dharmapṛṣṭhe vā sarasi brahmaṇastathā \|*  
*gayāśīrṣavaṭe caiva pitṝṇāṃ dattamakṣayam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Whatever is offered to the manes at Gayā or in Dharmāraṇya or at Brahmasaras and at Gayāśīrṣavaṭa becomes inexhaustible.

## \|\| 11.73 \|\|

*vrajankṛtvā nivāpaṃ yastvadhvānaṃ parisarpati \|*  
*narakasthānpitṝnsopi svargaṃ nayati satvaraṃ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. One who going to these places and having made a libation moves round, quickly takes to heaven the manes residing in hell.

## \|\| 11.74 \|\|

*kule tasya na rājeṃdra preto bhavati kaścana \|*  
*pretatvaṃ mokṣabhāvaṃ ca piṃḍadānācca gacchati \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. O best king, in his family no one becomes an evil spirit, (because) the evil spirit attains liberation due to the offering of piṇḍas.

## \|\| 11.75 \|\|

*eko munistāmrakarāgrahasto hyāmreṣu mūle salilaṃ dadāti \|*  
*āmrāśca siktāḥ pitaraśca tṛptā ekā kriyā dvyarthakarī prasiddhā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. A holy man with water in his right hand gives water at the root of mango (trees). (Thereby) the mango-trees are watered and the manes are propitiated; thus one action is known to serve two purposes.

## \|\| 11.76 \|\|

*gayāyāṃ piṇḍadānasya nānyaddānaṃ viśiṣyate \|*  
*ekena piṃḍadānena tṛptāste mokṣagāminaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. There is no other offering surpassing that made at Gayā; those (manes) moving towards liberation are pleased by one offering of piṇḍas.

## \|\| 11.77 \|\|

*dhānyapradānaṃ pravaraṃ vadaṃti vasupradānaṃ ca tathāmunīṃdrāḥ \|*  
*gayā sutīrtheṣu naraiḥ pradattaṃ taddharmahetuṃ pravaraṃ vadaṃti \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The best sages say that giving grains is (an) excellent (gift), so also giving wealth. They say that whatever is given by men at holy places like Gayā is a great source of religious merit.

## \|\| 11.78-79 \|\|

*sarvātmanā surucinā mahācala mahānadī \|*  
*ye tu paśyaṃti tāṃ gatvā mānase dakṣiṇottare \|\| 78 \|\|*

*praṇamya dvijamukhyebhyaḥ prāptaṃ tairjanmanaḥ phalaṃ \|*  
*yadyadicchati vai martyastattadāpnotyasaṃśayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. Those who go to the south and north of the Mānasa lake and with all their heart and with love see Mahācala and Mahānadī after having saluted chief brāhmaṇas, get the fruit of their life. Whatever a mortal desires, he undoubtedly obtains it.

## \|\| 11.80 \|\|

*eṣa tūddeśataḥ proktastīrthānāṃ sagraho mayā \|*  
*vāgīśopi na śaknoti vistarātkimu mānuṣaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. I have briefly stated this compendium of the holy places. Even the lord of speech cannot describe it in detail; then what about a human being?

## \|\| 11.81 \|\|

*satyaṃ tīrthaṃ dayā tīrthaṃ tīrthamindriyanigrahaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramāṇāṃ gehepi tīrthaṃ śama udāhṛtam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Truth is a holy place; compassion is a holy place; restraint of senses is a holy place; in the houses of those (who observe) the castes and the four stages of life, tranquility is said to be a sacred place.

## \|\| 11.82-83 \|\|

*yeṣu tīrtheṣu yacchrāddhaṃ tatkoṭiguṇamiṣyate \|*  
*gayāyāṃ yattu vai śrāddhaṃ tacchrāddhamapavargadam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*yasmāttasmātprayatnena tīrthe śrāddhaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*prātaḥkālo muhūrtāṃstrīnsaṃgavastāvadeva tu \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. Since whatever Śrāddha is recommended at the holy places is laid down to (have) a crore-fold (fruit), and since, the Śrāddha offered at Gayā is the giver of final release, therefore an effort should be made to offer a Śrāddha at a holy place. The morning time has three muhūrtas (a muhurta = 48 minutes), the saṅgava (period after morning time) has a similar duration; fore-noon has three muhūrtas; then afternoon follows.

## \|\| 11.84 \|\|

*madhyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syādaparāhṇastataḥ param \|*  
*sāyāhnastrimuhūrtaḥ syācchrāddhaṃ tatra na kārayet \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The evening time has three muhūrtas; a śrāddha should not be performed during that period.

## \|\| 11.85 \|\|

*rākṣasī nāma sā velā garhitā sarvakarmasu \|*  
*ahno muhūrtā vyākhyātā daśapaṃca ca sarvadā \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. That time is rākṣasī (demonish) and is condemned for all rites; the muhūrtas of the day are always said to be fifteen.

## \|\| 11.86 \|\|

*tatrāṣṭamo muhūrto yaḥ sa kālaḥ kutapaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*madhyāhnātsarvadā yasmānmaṃdī bhavati bhāskaraḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Among them the eighth period is said to be Kutapa; since after noon the sun always becomes mild.

## \|\| 11.87-91 \|\|

*tasmādanaṃtaphaladastatrāraṃbho viśiṣyate \|*  
*khaḍgapātraṃ ca kutapastathā naipālakaṃbalam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*rukmaṃ darbhāstilā gāvo dauhitraścāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pāpaṃ kutsitamityāhustasya tattāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*aṣṭāvete yatastasmātkutapā iti viśrutāḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ muhurttātkutapānmahūrttaṃ ca catuṣṭayam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*muhūrttapaṃcakaṃ caiva svadhāvācanamiṣyate \|*  
*viṣṇudehasamudbhūtāḥ kuśāḥ kṛṣṇatilāstathā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*śrāddhasya lakṣaṇaṃ kālamiti prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*tilodakāṃjalirdeyo jalāṃte tīrthavāsibhiḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

87-91. Therefore, the act during that period, is specified as the giver of eternal fruit. A sword, a vessel, the Kutapa (period), so also a blanket made in Nepal, gold, darbhas, sesamum seeds and cows (these are the seven necessary things for a Śrāddha); and a daughter’s son is said to be the eighth. Sin is said to be Kutsita (condemned); since these eight torment it, they are known as Kutapa. After the Kutapa-period there are four muhūrtas; so also is the fifth one (which) is laid down for the performance of a Śrāddha. Kuśas, so also black sesamum are said to have sprung up from Viṣṇu’s body. The wise say that black is the mark of a Śrāddha; the residents of a holy place should offer water with sesamum seed after water is offered (to the manes).

## \|\| 11.92 \|\|

*sadarbhahastenaikena gṛhe śrāddhaṃ gamiṣyati \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pavitramāyuṣyaṃ sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. With darbha inone hand one should offer in one’s house a Śrāddha (which is) meritorious and holy, gives (long) life, and destroys all sins.

## \|\| 11.93 \|\|

*brahmaṇā caiva kathitaṃ tīrthaśrāddhānukīrtanam \|*  
*śṛṇoti yaḥ paṭhedvāpi śrīmānsaṃjāyate naraḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. And this glory of śrāddha is narrated by Brahmā too; a man who listens to or recites it becomes rich.

## \|\| 11.94 \|\|

*śrāddhakāle ca vaktavyaṃ tathā tīrthanivāsibhiḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpopaśāṃntyarthamalakṣmīnāśanaṃ mataṃ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Similarly the residents of a holy place should, at the time of a Śrāddha, say it for the cessation of all sins (the following verse) which is regarded as the remover of poverty:

## \|\| 11.95 \|\|

*idaṃ pavitraṃ yaśaso nidhānamidaṃ mahāpātakanāśanaṃ ca \|*  
*brahmārkarudrairabhipūjitaṃ ca śrāddhasya māhātmyamuśaṃti tajjñāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. ‘This is pure, the treasure of fame; this is the destroyer of great sins; the greatness of Śrāddha is honoured by Brahmā, Arka and Rudra—(thus) declare the wise’.

## Chapter 12 - The dynasty of Yadu

## \|\| 12.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*somavaṃśaḥ kathaṃ jātaḥ kathayātra viśārada \|*  
*tadvaṃśe keturājāno babhūvuḥ kīrtivarddhanāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. O learned one, tell me now how the Soma dynasty came up and which kings were born in that family that increased its fame.

## \|\| 12.2-3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ādiṣṭo brahmaṇā pūrvamatriḥ sargavidhau purā \|*  
*anaṃtaraṃ nāma tapaḥ sṛṣṭyarthaṃ taptavānvibhuḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadānaṃdakaraṃ brahma bhagavankleśanāśanaṃ \|*  
*brahmarudrendrasūryāṇāmabhyaṃtaramatīṃdriyaṃ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

2-3. Formerly Atri was ordered by Brahmā to create. Then the lord practised penance for creation. (It was) delightful, removing the trouble of Brahmā, nearest to Brahmā, Rudra, Indra and Sūrya and supra-sensual.

## \|\| 12.4-5 \|\|

*śāntiṃ kṛtvātmamanasā tadatriḥ saṃyame sthitaḥ \|*  
*māhātmyaṃ tapaso vāpi paramānaṃdakārakaṃ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yasmādvaṃśapatiḥ sārddhaṃ samaye tadadhiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvācaṣṭa somena tasmātsomobhavadvibhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Having made his mind tranquil Atri then remained restrained. Even the greatness of penance causes great delight. Since the chief of the dynasty then stood out it increased by half and since Soma having seen him reported it he became mighty.

## \|\| 12.6 \|\|

*atha susrāva netrābhyāṃ jalaṃ tatrātrisaṃbhavam \|*  
*dyotayadviśvamakhilaṃ jyotsnayā sacarācaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then from Atri’s eyes water of tears, illuminating all the mobile and immobile things with its moonlight, flowed.

## \|\| 12.7 \|\|

*taddiśo jagṛhustatra strīrūpeṇāsahṛcchayāḥ \|*  
*garbho bhūtvodare tāsāṃ sthitaḥ sopyatrisaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The quarters in the form of ladies drank it up; it turned into an embryo generated by Atri and remained in their uterus.

## \|\| 12.8-9 \|\|

*āśāśca mumucurgarbhamaśaktā dhāraṇe tataḥ \|*  
*samādāyātha taṃ garbhamekīkṛtya caturmukhaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yuvānamakarodbrahmā sarvāyudhadharaṃ naram \|*  
*syaṃdanetha sahastena vedaśaktimaye prabhuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then the quarters unable to hold it dropped it. Brahma then took the embryo and put it together and (thus) fashioned a youth skilled in using all weapons.

## \|\| 12.10 \|\|

*āropya lokamanayadātmīyaṃ sa pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tato brahmarṣibhiḥ proktaṃ hyasmatsvāmībhavatvayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Having put him with his own hands in a chariot, full of the power of Vedas, he took him to the world. Then the brāhmaṇic sages said: Let him be our lord.

## \|\| 12.11 \|\|

*ṛṣibhirdevagaṃdharvairapsarobhistathaiva ca \|*  
*stūyamānasya tasyābhūdadhikaṃ mahadaṃtaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then the interior of that (Soma) who was being praised by sages, Gandharvas and celestial nymphs became very great.

## \|\| 12.12 \|\|

*tejovitānādabhavadbhuvi divyauṣadhīgaṇaḥ \|*  
*taddīptiradhikā tasmādrātrau bhavati sarvadā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. From that expanding lustre the host of herbs sprang on the earth; his lustre is great; so he always is (i.e. shines) during the night.

## \|\| 12.13-15 \|\|

*tenauṣadhīśaḥ somobhūddvijeṣvapi hi gaṇyate \|*  
*vedadhāmā rasaścāyaṃ yadidaṃ maṃḍalaṃ śubham \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṣīyate varddhate caiva śukle kṛṣṇe ca sarvadā \|*  
*viṃśatiṃ ca tathā sapta dakṣaḥ prācetaso dadau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*rūpalāvaṇyasaṃyuktāstasmai kanyāḥ suvarcasaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śaktisahasrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Therefore Soma became the lord ofherbs; he is also counted among the brāhmaṇas; as he is the Vedic lustre and the fluid. The auspicious disc in the dark and bright (fortnights) wanes and waxes. Prācetasa Dakṣa gave him (his) twenty-seven brilliant daughters endowed with form and beauty and then ten thousand of thousand (-fold) powers.

## \|\| 12.16-17 \|\|

*tapaścakāra śītāṃśurviṣṇudhyānaikatatparaḥ \|*  
*tatastuṣṭaśca bhagavāṃstasmai nārāyaṇo hariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva covāca paramātmā janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tato vavre varaṃ somaḥ śakraloke yajāmyaham \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Soma intent on meditating upon Viṣṇu practised penance. Then the lord, Nārāyaṇa-Hari, thesupremejanārdana was pleased with him and said to him, “Ask for a boon.” Then Soma asked for a boon: “I shall perform a sacrifice in the world of Indra.

## \|\| 12.18-19 \|\|

*pratyakṣameva bhoktāro bhavaṃtu mama maṃdire \|*  
*rājasūye suragaṇā brahmādyā ye caturvidhāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rakṣapālaḥ surosmākamāstāṃ śūladharo haraḥ \|*  
*tathetyuktaḥ samājahre rājasūyaṃ tu viṣṇunā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-1 9. The groups of gods with the four led by Brahmā should in person enjoy (the offerings) in my house, at the Rājasūya. The trident-holder god, Hara, should be our protector.” When Viṣṇu said, “Let it be so” he performed the Rājasūya.

## \|\| 12.20 \|\|

*hotātrirbhṛguradhvaryurudgātā ca caturmukhaḥ \|*  
*brahmatvamagamattasya upadraṣṭā hariḥ svayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Atri was the Hotṛ (the priest reciting the prayers of the Ṛgveda). Bhṛgu was the Adhvaryu (an officiating priest). Brahmā became the Udgātā (one who chants the hymns of Sāmaveda), and Hari himself was the superintendent.

## \|\| 12.21 \|\|

*sadasyāḥ sarvadevāstu rājasūyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*vasavodhvaryavastadvadviśvedevāstathaiva ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. All the (other) gods were assisting priests; the rite was laid down (said) to be Rājasūya. The Vasus and also the Viśvedevas were the officiating priests.

## \|\| 12.22 \|\|

*trailokyaṃ dakṣiṇā tena ṛtvigbhyaḥ pratipāditā \|*  
*somaḥ prāpyāthaduṣprāpyamaiśvaryaṃ sṛṣṭisatkṛtaṃ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. He gave the three worlds as the sacrificial fee to the priests. Having obtained splendour which was difficult to obtain, and which was honoured by the world, Soma, by means of his penance, got the sovereignty of the seven worlds.

## \|\| 12.23-24 \|\|

*saptalokaikanāthatvaṃ prāptassvatapasā tadā \|*  
*kadācidudyānagatāmapaśyadanekapuṣpābharaṇopaśobhām \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bṛhannitaṃbastanabhārakhedāṃ puṣpāvabhaṃgepyatidurbalāṃgīṃ \|*  
*bhāryāṃ ca tāṃ devaguroranaṃgabāṇābhirāmāyata cārunetrāṃ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Once he saw in a garden Bṛhaspati’s wife, Tārā, adorned with many flowers and ornaments, of large hips, oppressed with the burden of breasts, so feeble (i.e. delicate) (that she would not) even (tolerate) the plucking of flowers, charming like Cupid’s arrows and having broad and beautiful eyes.

## \|\| 12.25 \|\|

*tārāṃ sa tārādhipatiḥ smarārtaḥ keśeṣu jagrāha viviktabhūmau \|*  
*sāpi smarārtā sahate na reme tadrūpakāṃtyāhṛtamānasaiva \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In that secluded region, the lord of stars, being smit with love, seized her with her hair. She too, (equally) love-sick with her mind attracted by his form and handsomeness, enjoyed with him.

## \|\| 12.26 \|\|

*ciraṃ vihṛtyātha jagāma tārāṃ vidhurgṛhītvā svagṛhaṃ tatopi \|*  
*na tṛptirāsītsvagṛhepi tasya tārānuraktasya sukhāgameṣu \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Having sported for a long time Soma took Tārā to his house; then even in his own house he, attached to Tārā, was not satisfied with the (sexual) pleasures.

## \|\| 12.27-28 \|\|

*bṛhaspatistadvirahāgnidagdhastaddhyānaniṣṭhaikamanā babhūva \|*  
*śaśāka śāpaṃ na ca dātumasmai na maṃtraśastrāgniviṣairanekaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tasyāpakartuṃ vividhairupāyairnaivābhicārairapi vāgadhīśaḥ \|*  
*sa yācayāmāsa tatastu devaṃ somaṃ svabhāryārthamanaṃgataptaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Bṛhaspati, scorched by the fire of the separation had his mind contemplating on her only. He was unable to curse him (i.e. Soma), nor was (the lord of speech) able to harm him by means of many chants, missiles, fire or poisons; or by various stratagems or by magical spells. Being tormented with love, he besought god Soma to (return) his wife.

## \|\| 12.29 \|\|

*sa yācyamānopi dadau na bhāryāṃ bṛhaspateḥ kāmavaśena mohitaḥ \|*  
*maheśvareṇātha caturmukhena sādhyairmarudbhiḥ saha lokapālaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Being infatuated with love, he, though besought by Śiva or Brahmā, by the Sādhyas, and Maruts along with the regents of the quarters, did not give (back) Bṛhaspati’s wife.

## \|\| 12.30 \|\|

*dadau yadā tāṃ na kathaṃcidiṃdustadā śivaḥ krodhaparo babhūva \|*  
*yo vāmadevaprathitaḥ pṛthivyāmanekarudrārcitapādapadmaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When he did not give her (back) Śiva, who (also called Vāmadeva) was well known on the earth and whose lotus like feet were worshipped by many Rudras, became angry.

## \|\| 12.31 \|\|

*tataḥ saśiṣyo giriśaḥ pinākī bṛhaspateḥ snehavaśānubaddhaḥ \|*  
*dhanurgṛhītvājagavaṃ purārirjagāma bhūteśvarasiddhajuṣṭaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then, Śiva the trident-holder, along with his disciples, bound by love for Bṛhaspati, resorted to by the lords of spirits, and Siddhas, taking his bow called Jagava, went (forth) to fight with Soma.

## \|\| 12.32-34 \|\|

*yuddhāya somena viśeṣadīptastṛtīyanetrānalabhīmavaktraḥ \|*  
*sahaiva jagmuśca gaṇeśvarāṇāṃ viṃśādhikā ṣaṣṭirathogramūrtiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*yakṣeśvarāṇāṃ sagaṇairanekairyutonvagātsyaṃdanasaṃsthitānāṃ \|*  
*vetālayakṣoragakinnarāṇāṃ padmena caikena tathārbudānām \|\| 33 \|\|*

*lakṣaistribhirdvā daśabhī rathānāṃ somopyagāttatra vivṛddhamanyuḥ \|*  
*śanaiścarāṃgārakavṛddhatejā nakṣatradaityāsurasainyayuktaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. He, especially brilliant, of a terrible form and terrible and cruel due to the fire in his third eye, and the eighty lords of his attendants and with the lords of Yakṣas seated in a war-chariot, and Soma too, with his anger, and with a thousand billions of Vetālas, Yakṣas, Snakes and Kinnaras, so also of serpents, so also with thirty-six thousand chariots, with his lustre increased by Śani and Aṅgāraka came there, accompanied by the army of the Nakṣatras, demons and fiends.

## \|\| 12.35 \|\|

*jagmurbhayaṃ sapta tathaiva lokā dharāvanadvīpasamudragarbhāḥ \|*  
*sasomamevābhyagamatpinākī gṛhītadīptāstraviśālavahniḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The seven worlds, earth, forests, islands and the interiors of the oceans got frightened. The trident-holder, who had taken the blazing missile and great fire went forth to (fight) Soma.

## \|\| 12.36 \|\|

*athābhavadbhīṣaṇa bhīma soma sainyadvayasyātha mahāhavosau \|*  
*aśeṣasatvakṣayakṛtpravṛddhastīkṣṇapradhāno jvalanaikarūpaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Then took place a great war between the terrible armies of Rudra and Soma. Capable of destroying all animals, it (i.e. the war) of the form of intensive and pre-eminent fire, escalated.

## \|\| 12.37 \|\|

*śastrairathānyonyamaśeṣasainyaṃ dvayorjagāmakṣayamugratīkṣṇaiḥ \|*  
*pataṃti śastrāṇi tathojvalāni svarbhūmipātālamalaṃ dahaṃti \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The full armies of both with sharp and poignant missiles met destruction. Bright missiles, capable of burning heaven, earth and the nether region were discharged.

## \|\| 12.38 \|\|

*rudraḥ krodhādbrahmaśiro mumoca somopi somāstramamoghavīryaṃ \|*  
*tayornipātena samudrabhūmyorathāṃtarikṣasya ca bhītirāsīt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Through anger, Rudra released the missile Brahmasiras; Soma too released the missile ‘Soma’ of infallible power. By the fall of the two (missiles) fear spread in the ocean, on the earth, in the atmosphere.

## \|\| 12.39 \|\|

*tadā suyuddhaṃ jagatāṃ kṣayāya pravṛddhamālokya pitāmahopi \|*  
*tataḥ praviśyātha kathaṃcideva nivārayāmāsa suraiḥ sahaiva \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then seeing that war escalating and capable of destroying the worlds, Brahmā along with gods, entering there, somehow averted it.

## \|\| 12.40-41 \|\|

*akāraṇaṃ kiṃ kṣayakṛjjanānāṃ soma tvayāpīdamakāryakāryaṃ \|*  
*yasmātparastrīharaṇāya soma tvayā kṛtaṃ yuddhamatīva bhīmam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pāpagrahastvaṃ bhavitā janeṣu pāposyalaṃ vahnimukhāśināṃ tvaṃ \|*  
*bhāryāmimāmarpaya vākpatestvaṃ pramāṇayanneva madīya vācam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. “O Soma, why are you, without any cause, doing this ignoble deed, leading to the destruction of people? Since you waged this terrible war for taking away the wife of someone else you will be (taken to be) an evil planet among people; you are a sinner; you will be equal to the eaters of brāhmaṇas. Honouring my word, restore this Bṛhaspati’s wife to him.”

## \|\| 12.42 \|\|

*tatheti covāca himāṃśumālī yuddhādapākrāmadataḥ praśāṃtaḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspatistāmatha gṛhya tārāṃ hṛṣṭo jagāma svagṛhaṃ ca rudraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Saying ‘let it be so’, Soma, being tranquilled, kept away from fighting; Bṛhaspati taking Tārā and being delighted, went home; so also Rudra.

## \|\| 12.43-45 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte dvādaśādityasannibhaḥ \|*  
*divyapītāmbaradharo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tārodaraviniṣkrāntaḥ kumārassūryasannibhaḥ \|*  
*sarvārthaśāstravidvidvānhastiśāstrapravarttakaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nāmayadrājaputroyaṃ viśruto rājavaidyakaḥ \|*  
*rājñaḥ somasya putratvādrājaputro budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

43-45. Then at the end of a year, a boy resembling twelve suns, wearing a divine yellow garment, adorned with divine ornaments, and like the sun, was born to Tārā. He knew all the sciences, and was the propounder of the science of elephants. Named Rājaputra he was a well-known royal physician. He was known as Budha, being the son of king Soma.

## \|\| 12.46 \|\|

*janānāṃ tu sa tejāṃsi sarvāṇyevākṣipadbalī \|*  
*brahmādyāstatra cājagmurdevā devarṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He, the powerful one, snatched all the lustre of all people. Brahma and others came there; so also gods with the divine sages came to the house of Bṛhaspati at the time of the ceremony performed at the birth of the child.

## \|\| 12.47 \|\|

*bṛhaspatigṛhe sarve jātakarmotsave tadā \|*  
*papracchuste surāstārāṃ kena jātaḥ kumārakaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The gods asked Tārā by whom was the boy begotten (i.e. who was his father—Soma or Bṛhaspati)?

## \|\| 12.48-49 \|\|

*tataḥ sā lajjitā teṣāṃ na kiṃcidavadattadā \|*  
*punaḥ punastadā pṛṣṭā lajjayaṃtī varāṃganā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*somasyeti cirādāha tato gṛhṇādvidhuḥ sutaṃ \|*  
*budha ityakaronnāma prādādrājyaṃ ca bhūtale \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. She, ashamed of them, did not say anything, at that time. The excellent lady, being again asked, replied shamefully after a long time that the son was Soma’s. Then Soma took the son, named him ‘Budha’ and gave him a kingdom on the earth.

## \|\| 12.50-51 \|\|

*abhiṣekaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā pradānamakarodvibhuḥ \|*  
*grahamadhyaṃ pradāyātha brahmā brahmarṣibhiryutaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|*  
*ilodare ca dharmiṣṭhaṃ budhaḥ putramajījanat \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Then having consecrated him, the supreme lord Brahmā offered him a seat in the planets; having given it he, along with the brāhmaṇic sages, disappeared there only even as all beings were watching. Buddha produced the most religious son in (i.e. from) the womb of Ilā.

## \|\| 12.52 \|\|

*aśvamedhaśataṃsāgramakarodyassvatejasā \|*  
*purūravā iti khyātaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He (i.e. the son) fully performed a hundred horse-sacrifices, and due to his lustre was known as Purūravas and was honoured by all people.

## \|\| 12.53 \|\|

*himavacchikhare ramye samārādhya pitāmahaṃ \|*  
*lokaiśvaryamagādrājansaptadvīpapatistadā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Having propitiated Brahmā on the peak of the Himālayas, he, the lord of the seven islands, obtained the lordship of the world.

## \|\| 12.54 \|\|

*keśiprabhṛtayo daityāstadbhṛtyatvaṃ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*urvaśī yasya patnītvamagamadrūpamohitā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The demons Keśin and others became his servants; Urvaśī, enamoured of his handsomeness, became his wife.

## \|\| 12.55 \|\|

*saptadvīpāvasumatī saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*dharmeṇa pālitā tena sarvalokahitaiṣiṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Desiring the good of all the people, he justly protected the earth having seven islands, with mountains, forests and groves.

## \|\| 12.56 \|\|

*cāmaragrahaṇākīrtiḥ svayaṃ caivāṃgavāhikā \|*  
*brahmaprasādāddeveṃdro dadāvarddhāsanaṃ tadā \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Due to the favour of Brahmā (he obtained) fame that became his carrier and waiting girl holding the chowrie. The lord of gods offered him half (of his) seat.

## \|\| 12.57 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmāndharmeṇa samavetobhyapālayat \|*  
*dharmārthakāmāstaṃ draṣṭumājagmuḥ kautukānvitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He protected Dharma, Artha and Kāma equally and justly.

## \|\| 12.58 \|\|

*jijñāsavastaccaritaṃ kathaṃ paśyati naḥ samam \|*  
*bhaktyā cakre tatasteṣāmarghyapādyādikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Dharma, Artha and Kāma came to see him with curiosity, desiring to know how he maintained them equally. With devotion he then offered them offerings, water for washing feet etc.

## \|\| 12.59 \|\|

*āsanatrayamānīya divyaṃ kanakabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*niveśyāthākarotpūjāmīṣaddharmedhikāṃ punaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Having brought three seats adorned with gold, and seating them on the seats, he offered them worship, (offering) slightly superior worship to Dharma.

## \|\| 12.60 \|\|

*jagmatustau ca kāmārthāvatikopaṃ nṛpaṃ prati \|*  
*arthaḥ śāpamadāttasmai lobhāttvaṃ nāśameṣyasi \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Kāma and Artha then became very angry with the king; Artha cursed him: “You will perish due to greed.”

## \|\| 12.61 \|\|

*kāmopyāha tavonmādo bhavitā gaṃdhamādane \|*  
*kumāravanamāśritya viyogāccorvaśībhavāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Kāma also said: “You will become insane in the Gandhamādana, after having gone to the grove (sacred to) Kumāra due to the separation from Urvaśī”.

## \|\| 12.62-64 \|\|

*dharmopyāha cirāyustvaṃ dhārmikaśca bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*saṃtatistava rājeṃdra yāvadācaṃdratārakam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*śataśo vṛddhimāyāti na nāśaṃ bhuvi yāsyati \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣāṇi conmāda ūrvaśīkāmasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*acirādeva bhāryāpi vaśameṣyati cāpsarāḥ \|*  
*ityuktvāṃtardadhuḥ sarve rājā rājyaṃ tadānvabhūt \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. Dharma too said: “You will have a long life and will be religious; O lord of kings, your progeny will increase hundred times as long as the sun and the moon stay (in the sky) and will not perish on the earth. The madness caused by (the longing for) Urvaśī will last for sixty years; and that celestial nymph, your wife, will soon be won over by you”. Saying so all of them disappeared.

## \|\| 12.65-66 \|\|

*ahanyahani deveṃdraṃ draṣṭuṃ yāti purūravāḥ \|*  
*kadācidāruhya rathaṃ dakṣiṇāṃbaracāriṇā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*sārdhaṃ śakreṇa so'paśyannīyamānāmathāṃbare \|*  
*keśinā dānaveṃdreṇa citralekhāmathorvaśīm \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Purūravas everyday went to see Urvaśī. Once while moving in the sky in the southern direction seated in the chariot with Indra he saw Urvaśī and Citralekhā being taken (away) in the atmosphere by the lord of demons, Keśin.

## \|\| 12.67-68 \|\|

*taṃ vinirjitya samare vividhāyudhapātanaiḥ \|*  
*purā śakropi samare yena vajrī vinirjitaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*mitratvamagamattena prādādiṃdrāya corvaśīṃ \|*  
*tataḥprabhṛti mitratvamagamatpākaśāsanaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Having in a battle vanquished him (i.e. Keśin) who had formerly vanquished in battle even Indra by throwing various missiles (at him), he (i.e. Purūravas) became friendly with Indra and gave Urvaśī to him. Since then Indra became his friend.

## \|\| 12.69 \|\|

*sarvaloketiśayitaṃ purūravasameva tam \|*  
*prāha vajrī tu saṃtuṣṭo nīyatāmiyameva ca \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Indra being pleased, with Purūravas, excelling (everyone) in the world, said to him: “You take her”.

## \|\| 12.70 \|\|

*sā purūravasaḥ prītyai cāgāyaccaritaṃ mahat \|*  
*lakṣmīsvayaṃvaraṃnāma bharatena pravartitam \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Due to love she sang to Purūravas a great story enacted by Bharata and named Lakṣmī-svayaṃvara.

## \|\| 12.71 \|\|

*menakāṃ corvaśīṃ raṃbhāṃ nṛtyadhvamiti cādiśat \|*  
*nanarta salayaṃ tatra lakṣmīrūpeṇa corvaśī \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. He (i.e. Bharata) ordered Menakā, Urvaśī and Rambhā to dance. There Urvaśī, in the role of Lakṣmī, danced with proper pauses (in music).

## \|\| 12.72 \|\|

*sā purūravasaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛtyaṃtī kāmapīḍitā \|*  
*vismṛtābhinayaṃ sarvaṃ yatpurātanacoditam \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. She, while dancing, seeing Purūravas, became oppressed by love and forgot all acting that was directed before.

## \|\| 12.73-74 \|\|

*śaśāpa bharataḥ krodhādviyogāttasya bhūtale \|*  
*paṃcapaṃcāśadabdāni latābhūtā bhaviṣyasi \|\| 73 \|\|*

*tatastamurvaśī gatvā bharttāramakarocciraṃ \|*  
*śāpānubhavanāṃte ca urvaśī budhasūnunā \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. Bharata angrily cursed her that separated from him (i.e. Purūravas) she would turn into a creeper, live on the earth for fifty-five years. Then Urvaśī having gone to him, made him her husband for a long time. After experiencing the curse, Urvaśī gave birth to eight sons by (Purūravas), the son of Budha.

## \|\| 12.75-77 \|\|

*ajījanatsutānaṣṭau nāmatastānnibodha me \|*  
*āyurdṛḍhāyurvaśyāyurbalāyurdhṛtimānvasuḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*divyajāyuḥ śatāyuśca sarve divyabalaujasaḥ \|*  
*āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ putro vṛddhaśarmā tathaiva ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

*rajirdaṃḍo viśākhaśca vīrāḥ paṃcamahārathāḥ \|*  
*rajeḥ putraśataṃ jajñe rājeyā iti viśrutaṃ \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. Listen to their names from me (as I tell them). Āyu, Dṛdhāyu, Vaśyāyu, Balāyu, Dhṛtimān, Vasu, Divyajāyu, and Śatāyu—a ll were having divine strength and vigour. Nahuṣa was the son of Āyu, so also was Vṛddhasarmā; and Raji, Daṇḍa and Viśākha; these five were brave warriors. A hundred sons were born to Raji; they were known as Rājeya.

## \|\| 12.78 \|\|

*rajirārādhayāmāsa nārāyaṇamakalmaṣaṃ \|*  
*tapasā toṣito viṣṇurvaraṃ prādānmahīpateḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Raji propitiated pure Nārāyaṇa; Viṣṇu who was (thus) propitiated by penance, gave a boon to the king.

## \|\| 12.79 \|\|

*devāsuramanuṣyāṇāmabhūtsa vijayī tadā \|*  
*atha devāsuraṃ yuddhamabhūdvarṣaśatatrayam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. He then became the conqueror of gods, demons and men. Then the war between gods and demons continued for three hundred years.

## \|\| 12.80 \|\|

*prahlādaśakrayorbhīmaṃ na kaścidvijayī tayoḥ \|*  
*tato devāsuraiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ pṛthagdevaścaturmukhaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A terrible battle took place between Prahlāda and Śakra, and none of them came out victorious. Then gods and demons separately asked Brahmā:

## \|\| 12.81 \|\|

*anayorvijayī kaḥ syādrajiryatreti sobravīt \|*  
*jayāya prārthito rājā sahāyastvaṃ bhavasva naḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. “Who will be victorious out ofthe two?” He said: “He, where (i.e. on whose side) Raji is (will be victorious).”

## \|\| 12.82 \|\|

*daityaiḥ prāha yadi svāmī vo bhavāmi tatastvalam \|*  
*nāsuraiḥ pratipannaṃ tatpratipannaṃ suraistadā \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. The demons requested the king, “Help us to victory”. He said: “If I shall be your lord (I shall help you); otherwise enough of it (i.e. I shall not help you)”. The demons did not accept it; but the gods did.

## \|\| 12.83 \|\|

*svāmī bhava tvamasmākaṃ balanāśaya vidviṣaḥ \|*  
*tato vināśitāḥ sarve ye vadhyā vajrapāṇinaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. “Be our lord and destroy the enemy’s army.” Then he destroyed all that were to be killed by Indra.

## \|\| 12.84 \|\|

*putratvamagamattuṣṭastasyeṃdraḥ karmaṇā tataḥ \|*  
*dattveṃdrāya purā rājyaṃ jagāma tapase rajiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. By that deed of his, Indra then became his son. Then giving the kingdom to Indra, Raji went (to perform) penance.

## \|\| 12.85 \|\|

*rajiputraistadāchinnaṃ balādiṃdrasya vaiyadā \|*  
*yajñabhāgaśca rājyaṃ ca tapobalaguṇānvitaiḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Then, Raji’s sons endowed with the merit of penance and power, forcibly snatched the kingdom from Indra and his portion in the sacrifice.

## \|\| 12.86-87 \|\|

*rājyabhraṣṭastataḥ śakro rajiputranipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*prāha vācaspatiṃ dīnaḥ pīḍito'smi rajeḥ sutaiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*na yajñabhāgo rājyaṃ me pīḍitasya bṛhaspate \|*  
*rājyalābhāya me yatnaṃ vidhatsva dhiṣaṇādhipa \|\| 87 \|\|*

86-87. He, deprived of the kingdom and oppressed by Raji’s sons, being helpless, said to Bṛhaspati: “O Bṛhaspati, lam harassed by Raji’s sons; I who am oppressed, am not having the kingdom nor the portion in the sacrifice; master of intellect, strive to get the kingdom for me.”

## \|\| 12.88 \|\|

*tato bṛhaspatiḥ śakramakarodbaladarpitam \|*  
*grahaśāṃtividhānena pauṣṭikena ca karmaṇā \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Then Bṛhaspati, by means of the rite to pacify the planets and to promote welfare, made Indra haughty with power.

## \|\| 12.89-91 \|\|

*gatvātha mohayāmāsa rajiputrānbṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*jinadharmaṃ samāsthāya vedabāhyaṃ sa dharmavit \|\| 89 \|\|*

*vedatrayīparibhraṣṭāṃścakāra dhiṣaṇādhipaḥ \|*  
*vedabāhyānparijñāya hetuvādasamanvitān \|\| 90 \|\|*

*jaghāna śakro vajreṇa sarvāndharmabahiṣkṛtān \|*  
*nahuṣasya pravakṣyāmi putrānsaptaiva dhārmikān \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-91. Bṛhaspati, having gone to Raji’s sons, stupefied them. The lord of intellect (i.e. Bṛhaspati) who knew religion, resorting to the religion of the Jainas, which was out of the Vedic fold, made them fallen from the three Vedas. Knowing them to be out of the Vedic fold and endowed with disputation, Indra with his bolt killed them all—who were excommunicated from the (Vedic) religion. I shall tell you about the seven pious sons of Nahuṣa:

## \|\| 12.92 \|\|
