*yatiryayātiśśaryātiruttaraḥ para eva ca \|*  
*ayatirviyatiścaiva saptaite vaṃśavarddhanāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Yati, Yayāti, Śaryāti, Uttara and Para; so also Ayati and Viyati; these seven propagated the race.

## \|\| 12.93 \|\|

*yatiḥ kumārabhāvepi yogī vaikhānasobhavat \|*  
*yayātirakarodrājyaṃ dharmaikaśaraṇaḥ sadā \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Yati became an anchorite even in his boyhood. Yayāti, always given to piety, ruled his kingdom.

## \|\| 12.94 \|\|

*śarmiṣṭhā tasya bhāryābhūdduhitā vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavasyātmajā caiva devayānī ca suvratā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, was his wife; so also Bhārgava’s daughter Devayānī of a good vow (was his wife).

## \|\| 12.95 \|\|

*yayāteḥ paṃcadāyādāstānpravakṣyāmi nāmataḥ \|*  
*devayānī yaduṃ putraṃ turvasuṃ cāpyajījanat \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Yayāti had five sons; I shall mention them by names. Devayānī gave birth to a son (named) Yadu and also (another son) Vasu.

## \|\| 12.96 \|\|

*tathā druhyamaṇaṃ pūruṃ śarmiṣṭhājanayatsutān \|*  
*yaduḥ pūrūśca bharataste vai vaṃśavivarddhanāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Śarmiṣṭhā gave birth to (three) sons: Druhyu, Aṇu and Pūru. Yadu, Pūru and Bharata continued the race.

## \|\| 12.97-98 \|\|

*pūrorvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi yatra jātosi pārthiva \|*  
*yadostu yādavā jātā yatra tau balakeśavau \|\| 97 \|\|*

*bhārāvatāraṇārthāya pāṃḍavānāṃ hitāya ca \|*  
*yadoḥ putrā babhūvuśca paṃca devasutopamāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. O King, (now) I shall describe the Pūru-race, in which you are born. From Yadu the Yādavas were born, among whom were (born) Bala (-rāma) and Kṛṣṇa for taking down the burden of Pāṇḍavas and for their welfare. Yadu’s five sons were like god’s sons.

## \|\| 12.99 \|\|

*sahasrajittathā jyeṣṭhaḥ kroṣṭā nīloñjiko raghuḥ \|*  
*sahasrajito dāyādaḥ śatajinnāma pārthivaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The eldest was Sahasrajit, then Kroṣṭṛ, Nīla, Añjika and Raghu. King named Śatajit was Sahasrajit’s son.

## \|\| 12.100 \|\|

*śatajitaśca dāyādāstrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ \|*  
*haihayaśca hayaścaiva tathā tālahayaśca yaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Śatajit had three extremely religious sons: Haihaya, Haya and Tālahaya also.

## \|\| 12.101 \|\|

*haihayasya tu dāyādo dharmanetraḥ pratiśrutaḥ \|*  
*dharmanetrasya kuṃtistu saṃhatastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Dharmanetra was the well-known son of Haihaya; Dharmanetra’s son was Kunti and his (Kunti’s) son was Saṃhata.

## \|\| 12.102-104 \|\|

*saṃhatasya tu dāyādo mahiṣmānnāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*āsīnmahiṣmataḥ putro bhadrasenaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 102 \|\|*

*vārāṇasyāmabhūdrājā kathitaḥ pūrvameva hi \|*  
*bhadrasenasya putrastu durdamo nāma dhārmikaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*durdamasya suto bhīmo dhanako nāma vīryavān \|*  
*dhanakasya sutā hyāsancatvāro lokaviśrutāḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

102-104. The king named Mahiṣmān was Saṃhata’s son. Brave Bhadrasena was the son of Mahiṣmān. He was a king in Vārāṇasī, who has already been mentioned. The religious son of Bhadrasena was Durdama by name. The terrible son of Durdama was named Dhanaka. Dhanaka had four sons well-known in the world.

## \|\| 12.105 \|\|

*kṛtāgniḥ kṛtavīryaśca kṛtadharmā tathaiva ca \|*  
*kṛtaujāśca caturthobhūtkṛtavīryācca sorjunaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Kṛtāgni, Kṛtavīrya, so also Kṛtadharma; the fourth son was Kṛtaujas; that (well known) Arjuna was (the son) of Kṛtavīrya.

## \|\| 12.106 \|\|

*jāto bāhusahasreṇa saptadvīpeśvaro nṛpaḥ \|*  
*varṣāyutaṃ tapastepe duścaraṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. By means of his thousand arms the king became the lord of seven islands. Then the lord of the earth practised penance for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 12.107 \|\|

*dattamārādhayāmāsa kārttavīryotrisaṃbhavam \|*  
*tasmai datto varānprādāccaturaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Kārtavīrya propitiated Datta born of Atri. Datta, the best among men granted him four boons.

## \|\| 12.108 \|\|

*pūrvaṃ bāhusahasraṃ tu sa vavre rājasattamaḥ \|*  
*adharmaṃ dhyāyamānasya bhītiścāpi nivāraṇam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. The best king, first chose a thousand arms. (By the second boon he chose that) one thinking impiously would incur fear and be warded off.

## \|\| 12.109 \|\|

*yuddhena pṛthivīṃ jitvā dharmeṇāvāpya vai balam \|*  
*saṃgrāme vartamānasya vadhaścaivādhikādbhavet \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. (By the third boon) he would conquer the earth by fighting and would get strength by means of religious acts; and by the additional (i.e. the fourth boon) he would kill anyone that would stand before him in a battle.

## \|\| 12.110 \|\|

*eteneyaṃ vasumatī saptadvīpā sapattanā \|*  
*saptodadhi parikṣiptā kṣātreṇa vidhinā jitā \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. He conquered this earth by his heroism with its seven islands and cities and surrounded by seven seas.

## \|\| 12.111 \|\|

*jajñe bāhusahasraṃ ca icchatastasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*sarve yajñā mahābāhostasyāsanbhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Of him, the intelligent one, a thousand arms were produced as desired by him; he performed all sacrifices in which large fees were paid.

## \|\| 12.112 \|\|

*sarve kāṃcanayūpāste sarve kāṃcanavedikāḥ \|*  
*sarve devaiśca saṃprāptā vimānasthairalaṃkṛtaiḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. All of them had golden sacrificial posts and golden altars; all were attended by gods seated in aerial cars and adorned.

## \|\| 12.113-116 \|\|

*gaṃdharvairapsarobhiśca nityamevāpi sevitāḥ \|*  
*yasya yajñe jagau gāthā gaṃdhaṃrvo nāradastathā \|\| 113 \|\|*

*kārttavīryasya rājarṣermahimānaṃ nirīkṣya saḥ \|*  
*na nūnaṃ kārttavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyaṃti pārthivāḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*yajñairdānaistapobhiśca vikrameṇa śrutena ca \|*  
*saptadvīpānanucaranvegena pavanopamaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

*paṃcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ ca narādhipaḥ \|*  
*saptadvīpapṛthivyāśca cakravartī babhūva ha \|\| 116 \|\|*

113-116. They were always attended by the Gandharvas and the celestial nymphs also. In his sacrifice Gandharva and Nārada sang a verse, after having seen the greatness of the royal sage Kārtavīrya. Kings would never attain to the position of Kārtavīrya by means of sacrifices, gifts, austerities, valour or learning. Moving swiftly on the seven islands the king, comparable to wind, became the sovereign emperor of the earth with seven islands, for eighty-five thousand years.

## \|\| 12.117 \|\|

*sa eva paśupālobhūtkṣetrapālaḥ sa eva hi \|*  
*sa eva vṛṣṭyā parjanyo yogitvādarjunobhavat \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He became the protector of beasts; he alone was the protector of fields; he alone became cloud by means ofshowers and became Arjuna by means ofhis diligence (assiduity),

## \|\| 12.118 \|\|

*yosau bāhusahasreṇa jyāghātakaṭhinatvacā \|*  
*bhāti raśmisahasreṇa śāradeneva bhāskaraḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. By means ofhis thousand arms, and with skin rugged on account of the strokes of the bowstring he shone like the autumnal sun with thousand rays.

## \|\| 12.119 \|\|

*eṣa nāma manuṣyeṣu māhiṣmatyāṃ mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*eṣa vegaṃ samudrasya prāvṛṭkāle bhajeta vai \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. In Māhiṣmatī he was (a man) of great brilliance among men; in the rainy season he would meet the agitation of the ocean.

## \|\| 12.120 \|\|

*krīḍate svasukhā ye vipratisroto mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*lalanāḥ krīḍatā tena pratibaddhormimālinī \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. He sports (i.e. sported) against the current, for his own pleasure; sporting with the lashes he tied down the sea.

## \|\| 12.121-123 \|\|

*ūrmibhrukuṭimālā sā śaṃkitābhyeti narmadā \|*  
*eṣa eva manorvaṃśe tvavagāhenmahārṇavam \|\| 121 \|\|*

*kareṇoddhṛtya vegaṃ tu kāminīprīṇanena tu \|*  
*tasya bāhusahasreṇa kṣobhyamāṇe mahodadhau \|\| 122 \|\|*

*bhavaṃti līnā niśceṣṭāḥ pātālasthā mahāsurāḥ \|*  
*tadūrukṣobhacakitā amṛtotpādaśaṃkitāḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

121-123. Narmadā, frightened and having a series of knittings of her eye-brows in the form of her ripples flowed to him. He alone, from Manu’s family, would, plunge into the sea, by drawing out, with one hand the ocean and plunging into it by pleasing the beautiful ladies. When by his thousand arms the great ocean would be agitated, the great demons of the nether region would hide themselves and remain motionless.

## \|\| 12.124-128 \|\|

*natā niścalamūrddhāno bhavaṃti ca mahoragāḥ \|*  
*eṣa dhanvī ca cikṣepa rāvaṇaṃ prati sāyakān \|\| 124 \|\|*

*eṣa dhanvī dhanurgṛhya utsiktaṃ paṃcabhiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*laṃkeśaṃ mohayitvā tu sabalaṃ rāvaṇaṃ balāt \|\| 125 \|\|*

*nirjitya baddhvā tvānīya māhiṣmatyāmbabaṃdha tam \|*  
*tato gatohaṃ tasyāgre arjunaṃ saṃprasādayan \|\| 126 \|\|*

*mumoca rājanpautraṃ me sakhyaṃ kṛtvā ca pārthivaḥ \|*  
*tasya bāhusahasrasya babhūva jyātalasvanaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

*yugāṃtāgneḥ pravṛttasya yathā jyātalaniḥsvanaḥ \|*  
*aho balaṃ vidhervīryaṃ bhārgavaḥ sa yadācchinat \|\| 128 \|\|*

124-128. The great serpents stunned by the agitation of his thighs, and suspecting that nectar was being churned out, bent down keeping their heads motionless. This archer discharged arrows against Rāvaṇa. This archer taking a bow, having (with force) stupefied and vanquished the haughty lord of Laṅkā—Rāvaṇa, with five arrows and having arrested and brought him to Māhiṣmatī imprisoned him there. Then to propitiate that Arjuna, I went to him; having made friendship with my grandson (i.e. Rāvaṇa) he released him. The sound of the bow-string of him having a thousand arms was like that of the fire, that would spread on the earth at the end of a Yuga (the age of the world).

## \|\| 12.129 \|\|

*mṛdhe sahasraṃ bāhūnāṃ hematālavanaṃ yathā \|*  
*yaṃ vasiṣṭhastu saṃkruddho hyarjunaṃ śaptavānvibhuḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. (Paraśurāma) cut off in battle the thousand arms like the grove of golden Tāla-trees. The powerful Vasiṣṭha getting angry cursed that Arjuna:

## \|\| 12.130 \|\|

*yasmādvanaṃ pradagdhaṃ te viśrutaṃ mama haihaya \|*  
*tasmātte duṣkṛtaṃ karma kṛtamanyo haniṣyati \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. “Since, O Haihaya, you burnt my well known grove, so someone else will destroy your wicked deeds.

## \|\| 12.131 \|\|

*chitvā bāhusahasraṃ te pramathya tarasā balī \|*  
*tapasvī brāhmaṇastvāṃ vai vadhiṣyati sa bhārgavaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. That powerful ascetic brāhmaṇa Bhārgava, having powerfully cut off your thousand arms (and thus) having harassed you, will kill you.”

## \|\| 12.132-134 \|\|

*tasya rāmotha haṃtāsīnmuniśāpena dhīmataḥ \|*  
*tasya putraśataṃ tvāsītpaṃca tatra mahārathāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

*kṛtāstrā balinaḥ śūrā dharmātmāno mahābala \|*  
*śūrasenaśca śūraśca dhṛṣṭo vai kṛṣṇa eva ca \|\| 133 \|\|*

*jayaddhvajaḥ sa vai kartā avantiśca rasāpatiḥ \|*  
*jayadhvajasya putrastu tālajaṃgho mahābalaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

132-134. Paraśurāma was thus the killer of that intelligent (Kārtavīrya). O very powerful (Bhīṣma), he had a hundred sons; out of them (the following) five were great warriors, trained in the science of missiles, mighty, brave and religious: Śūrasena, Śūra, Dhṛṣṭa, Kṛṣṇa and Jayadhvaja; he was the builder of Avantī and the lord of the earth. Tālajaṅgha of great might was Jayadhvaja’s son.

## \|\| 12.135 \|\|

*tasya putrāśśatānyeva tālajaṃghā iti smṛtāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ paṃcakulānyāsanhaihayānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. His hundred sons were known as Tālajaṅghas. Of these Haihayas there were five families.

## \|\| 12.136 \|\|

*vītihotrāśca saṃjātā bhojāścāvaṃtayastathā \|*  
*tuṃḍakerāśca vikrāṃtāstālajaṃghāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. The Vītihotras were born (in this family), so also Bhojas and Avantis, and Tuṇḍakera; (all these) were called Tālajaṅghas.

## \|\| 12.137 \|\|

*vītihotrasutaścāpi anaṃto nāma vīryavān \|*  
*durjayastasya putrastu babhūvāmitrakarṣaṇaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The powerful son of Vītihotra was Ananta. His son was Durjaya who tormented his enemies.

## \|\| 12.138-140 \|\|

*sadbhāvena mahārājaḥ prajādharmeṇa pālayan \|*  
*kārtavīryārjuno nāma rājā bāhusahasradhṛt \|\| 138 \|\|*

*yena sāgaraparyaṃtā dhanuṣā nirjitā mahī \|*  
*yastasyakīrtayennāma kalyamutthāya mānavaḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*na tasya vittanāśaḥ syānnaṣṭaṃ ca labhate punaḥ \|*  
*kārtavīryasya yo janma kathayediha dhīmataḥ \|*  
*yathā yaṣṭā yathā dātā svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 140 \|\|*

138-140. The great king Kārtavīrya by name having a thousand arms protected the subjects sincerely, who with his bow vanquished the earth bounded by the oceans; and a man who getting up at daybreak utters his name, never loses his wealth; he regains what is lost. One who narrates the life of the intelligent Kārtavīrya, becomes honoured in heaven like a donor or a sacrificer.

## Chapter 13 - The Deeds of the Avatāra (Incarnation)

## \|\| 13.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*kroṣṭoḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ rājeṃdra vaṃśamuttamapūruṣam \|*  
*yasyānvavāye saṃbhūto viṣṇurvṛṣṇikulodvahaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. O king of kings, listen to (the account) of Kroṣṭṛ’s family (in which) excellent men (were born). In his family was born Viṣṇu, the perpetuator of the Vṛṣṇi family.

## \|\| 13.2 \|\|

*kroṣṭorevābhavatputro vṛjinīvānmahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*tasya putrobhavatsvātiḥ kuśaṃkustatsutobhavat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. From Kroṣṭṛ was born Vṛjinīvān, of great fame. His son was Svāti, and Kuśaṅku was his (i.e. Svāti’s) son.

## \|\| 13.3 \|\|

*kuśaṃkorabhavatputro nāmnā citrarathosya tu \|*  
*śaśabiṃduriti khyātaścakravartī babhūva ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Kuśaṅku had a son Citraratha by name; his son named Śaśabindu became a sovereign emperor.

## \|\| 13.4-5 \|\|

*atrānuvaṃśaślokoyaṃ gītastasya purābhavat \|*  
*śaśabiṃdostu putrāṇāṃ śatānāmabhavacchatam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dhīmatāṃ cārurūpāṇāṃ bhūridraviṇatejasām \|*  
*teṣāṃ śatapradhānānāṃ pṛthusāhvā mahābalāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. About him this verse containing the genealogical table was formerly sung. The hundred sons of Śatabindu had a hundred sons. From those hundred intelligent, handsome and important sons resplendent with great wealth were born the very mighty kings having the appellation Pṛthu.

## \|\| 13.6 \|\|

*pṛthuśravāḥ pṛthuyaśāḥ pṛthutejāḥ pṛthūdbhavaḥ \|*  
*pṛthukīrtiḥ pṛthumato rājānaḥ śaśabiṃdavaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Pṛthuśravas, Pṛthuyaśas, Pṛthutejas, Pṛthūdbhava, Pṛthukīrti, Pṛthumata were the kings (in the family) of Śaśabindu.

## \|\| 13.7-8 \|\|

*śaṃsaṃti ca purāṇajñāḥ pṛthuśravasamuttamam \|*  
*tataścāsyābhavanputrāḥ uśanā śatrutāpanaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*putraścośanasastasya śineyurnāmasattamaḥ \|*  
*āsītśineyoḥ putro yaḥ sa rukmakavaco mataḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Those well-versed in the Purāṇas praise Pṛthuśravas to be the best. He had sons. (Out of them) Uśanas tormented the enemies. Uśanas’s son was Śineyu by name and was most virtuous. Śineyu’s son was known as Rukmakavaca.

## \|\| 13.9-10 \|\|

*nihatya rukmakavaco yuddhe yuddhaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*dhanvino vividhairbāṇairavāpya pṛthivīmimām \|\| 9 \|\|*

*aśvamedhe 'dadādrājā brāhmaṇebhyaśca dakṣiṇāṃ \|*  
*jajñe tu rukmakavacātparāvṛtparavīrahā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Rukmakavaca, skilled in fighting, having killed the archers with various arrows and having obtained this earth, gave gifts to brāhmaṇas in the horse-sacrifice. Parāvṛt, the killer of the rival heroes was born from Rukmakavaca.

## \|\| 13.11 \|\|

*tatputrā jajñire paṃca mahāvīryaparākramāḥ \|*  
*rukmeṣuḥ pṛthurukmaśca jyāmaghaḥ parigho hariḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Five sons were born to him who were very powerful and valourous: Rukmeṣu, Pṛthurukma, Jyāmagha, Parigha and Hari.

## \|\| 13.12 \|\|

*parighaṃ ca hariṃ caiva videhe sthāpayatpitā \|*  
*rukmeṣurabhavadrājā pṛthurukmastathāśrayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The father put Parigha and Hari in Videha. Rukmeṣu became a king and Pṛthurukma lived with him.

## \|\| 13.13-14 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ pravrājito rājyājjyāmaghovasadāśrame \|*  
*praśāṃtaścāśramasthastu brāhmaṇena vibodhitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*jagāma dhanurādāya deśamanyaṃ dhvajī rathī \|*  
*narmadātaṭa ekākī kevalaṃ vṛttikarśitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Jyāmagha, exiled by these two, lived in a hermitage. He, living peacefully in the hermitage and being roused by a brāhmaṇa took his bow and carrying a flag and seated in a chariout went to another country. Being all alone and distressed for want of subsistence he went to the mountain Ṛkṣavān on the bank of Narmadā, deserted by others, and sat there.

## \|\| 13.15 \|\|

*ṛkṣavaṃtaṃ giriṃ gatvā muktamanyairupāviśat \|*  
*jyāmaghasyābhavadbhāryā śaibyā pariṇatā satī \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Śaibyā was Jyāmagha’s chaste wife old (in age).

## \|\| 13.16-17 \|\|

*aputropyabhavadrājā bhāryāmanyāmaciṃtayan \|*  
*tasyāsīdvijayo yuddhe tatra kanyāmavāpya saḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*bhāryāmuvāca saṃtrāsātsnuṣeyaṃ te śucismite \|*  
*evamuktvābravīdenaṃ kasya keyaṃ snuṣeti vai \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The king too, being sonless, thought of taking another wife. He got victory in a war and securing a maiden in the war he through fear said to his wife, “O you of bright smile, this is your daughter-in-law.” When he said this, she said to him: “Who is she? Whose daughter-in-law is she?”

## \|\| 13.18-19 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*yaste janiṣyate putrastasya bhāryā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasyāḥ sā tapasogreṇa kanyāyāḥ saṃprasūyata \|\| 18 \|\|*

*putraṃ vidarbhaṃ subhagaṃ śaibyā pariṇatā satī \|*  
*rājaputryāṃ tu vidvāṃsau snuṣāyāṃ krathakauśikau \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The king replied, “She will be the wife of the son that will be born to you.” Due to the severe penance of that maiden that old Śaibyā gave birth to the son (named) Vidarbha.

## \|\| 13.20 \|\|

*lomapādaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu putraṃ paramadhārmikam \|*  
*paścādvidarbho janayacchūraṃ raṇaviśāradam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Vidarbha generated on the princess, (Jyāmagha’s) daughter-in-law, two sons, Kratha and Kauśika and later the third son Lomapāda by name, who was extremely pious, brave, and skilled in fighting.

## \|\| 13.21 \|\|

*lomapādātmajo babhrurdhṛtistasya tu cātmajaḥ \|*  
*kauśikasyātmajaścedistasmāccaidyanṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Babhru was Lomapāda’s son; Babhru’s son was Dhṛti; Kauśika’s son was Cedi and the kings who are known as Caidya were (born) from him.

## \|\| 13.22 \|\|

*kratho vidarbhaputro yaḥ kuṃtistasyātmajobhavat \|*  
*kuṃterdhṛṣṭastato jajñe dhṛṣṭātsṛṣṭaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Kunti was the son of Kratha who was the son of Vidarbha. Dhṛṣṭa was Kunti’s son; from that Dhṛṣṭa brave Sṛṣṭa was born.

## \|\| 13.23 \|\|

*sṛṣṭasya putro dharmātmā nivṛttiḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*nivṛttiputro dāśārho nāmnā sa tu vidūrathaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Sṛṣṭa’s son was pious Nivṛtti, the killer of rival heroes. Nivṛtti’s son named Daśārha was the same as Vidūratha.

## \|\| 13.24-25 \|\|

*dāśārhaputro bhīmastu bhīmājjīmūta ucyate \|*  
*jīmūtaputro vikṛtistasyabhīmarathaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*atha bhīmarathasyāpi putro navarathaḥ kila \|*  
*tasya cāsīddaśarathaḥ śakunistasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Daśārha’s son was Bhīma; Bhīma’s son is said to be Jīmūta; Jimūta’s son was Vikṛti; Bhīmaratha was his son; and Bhīmaratha’s son was said to be Navaratha. His son was Daśaratha; his son was Śakuni.

## \|\| 13.26 \|\|

*tasmātkaraṃbhastasmācca devarāto babhūva ha \|*  
*devakṣatrobhavadrājā devarātānmahāyaśāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. From him was born Karambha, and from him Devarāta; from Devarāta was born the very renowned Devakṣatra.

## \|\| 13.27 \|\|

*devagarbhasamo jajñe devakṣatrasya naṃdanaḥ \|*  
*madhurnāmamahātejā madhoḥ kuruvaśaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A god-like and very bright son by name Madhu was born of Devakṣatra. Kuruvaśa is said to be born from Madhu.

## \|\| 13.28 \|\|

*āsītkuruvaśātputraḥ puruhotraḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*aṃśurjajñetha vaidarbhyāṃ dravaṃtyāṃ puruhotrataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. A brave son Puruhotra was born from Kuruvaśa. From Puruhotra Aṃśa was born on the sporting Vaidarbhī.

## \|\| 13.29-30 \|\|

*vetrakī tvabhavadbhāryā aṃśostasyāṃ vyajāyata \|*  
*sātvataḥ satvasaṃpannaḥ sātvatānkīrtivarddhanaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*imāṃ visṛṣṭiṃ vijñāya jyāmaghasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*prajāvāneti sāyujyaṃ rājñaḥ somasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Vetrakī was Aṃśu’s wife; on her Sātvata (i.e. Aṃśu) endowed with energy and of growing fames generated Sātvatas. One having children and knowing this progeny of the magnanimous Jyāmagha, becomes united with the intelligent Soma.

## \|\| 13.31-32 \|\|

*sātvatānsatvasaṃpannā kausalyā suṣuve sutān \|*  
*teṣāṃ sargāśca catvāro vistareṇaiva tānśṛṇu \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhajamānasya sṛṃjayyāṃ bhājanāmā sutobhavat \|*  
*sṛṃjayasya sutāyāṃ tu bhājakāstu tatobhavan \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Kausalyā gave birth to the sons called Sātvata, endowed with energy. Their creations (i.e. lines) are four; listen to them (as I tell you) in detail: On Sṛñjayī, Bhajamāna got a son named Bhāja. Then Bhājakas were born on the daughter of Sṛñjaya.

## \|\| 13.33 \|\|

*tasya bhājasya bhārye dve suṣuvāte sutānbahūn \|*  
*nemiṃ cakṛkaṇaṃ caiva vṛṣṇiṃ parapuraṃjayaṃ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The two wives of that Bhāja gave birth to many sons: Nemica, Kṛkaṇa and Vṛṣṇi, the conqueror of the enemies’ cities.

## \|\| 13.34 \|\|

*te bhājakāḥ smṛtā yasmādbhajamānādvi jajñire \|*  
*devāvṛdhaḥ pṛthurnāma madhūnāṃ mitravarddhanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Since they were born from Bhajamāna they came to be called Bhājaks. There was Devāvṛdha Pṛthu and he increased friendship with the Madhus.

## \|\| 13.35-36 \|\|

*aputrastvabhavadrājā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*putraḥ sarvaguṇopeto mama bhūyāditi spṛhan \|\| 35 \|\|*

*saṃyojya kṛṣṇamevātha parṇāśāyā jalaṃ spṛśan \|*  
*sā toyasparśanāttasya sāṃnidhyaṃ nimnagā hyagāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. This king was sonless, so desiring ‘I should have a son endowed with all virtues’ and concentrating upon Kṛṣṇa only and touching the water of the Parṇāśā (river), he practised a great penance. Due to his touching the water the river came near him.

## \|\| 13.37-38 \|\|

*kalyāṇaṃ caratastasya śuśoca nimnagātataḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayātha parītātmā jagāmātha viniścayam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*bhūtvā gacchāmyahaṃ nārī yasyāmevaṃ vidhaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*jāyeta tasmādadyāhaṃ bhavāmyasya sutapradā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then the river worried about the well-being of him who was practising penance. With her mind full of anxiety she resolved: ‘Turning myself into a woman I shall go (to him), from whom a son like this (i.e. endowed with all qualities) would be born. Therefore today I shall (be his wife who would) give him a son’.

## \|\| 13.39 \|\|

*atha bhūtvā kumārī sā bibhratī paramaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*jñāpayāmāsa rājānaṃ tāmiyeṣa nṛpastataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Then becoming a maiden and taking up an excellent body she informed the king (about herself); the king then longed for her.

## \|\| 13.40 \|\|

*athasānavamemāsisuṣuvesaritāṃvarā \|*  
*putraṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ babhruṃ devāvṛdhātparam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then from Devāvṛdha, that best river, in the ninth month, gave birth to a great son viz. Babhru endowed with all virtues.

## \|\| 13.41 \|\|

*atra vaṃśe purāṇajñā bruvaṃtīti pariśrutam \|*  
*guṇāndevāvṛdhasyātha kīrttayaṃto mahātmanaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. We have heard that those who know the Purāṇas, narrating the virtues of the magnanimuos Devāvṛdha, say that:

## \|\| 13.42 \|\|

*babhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devairdevāvṛdhaḥ samaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiḥ śataṃ ca putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi ca saptatiḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Babhru was the greatest among men; Devāvṛdha resembled gods; from Babhru and Devāvṛdha seventy thousand and six hundred sons were born and they became immortal.

## \|\| 13.43-46 \|\|

*etemṛtatvaṃ saṃprāptā babhrordevāvṛdhādapi \|*  
*yajñadānatapodhīmānbrahmaṇyassudṛḍhavrataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*rūpavāṃśca mahātejā bhojotomṛtakāvatīm \|*  
*śarakāntasya duhitā suṣuve caturaḥ sutān \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kukuraṃ bhajamānaṃ ca śyāmaṃ kaṃbalabarhiṣam \|*  
*kukurasyātmajo vṛṣṭirvṛṣṭestu tanayo dhṛtiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*kapotaromā tasyāpi tittiristasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*tasyāsīdbahuputrastu vidvānputro nariḥ kila \|\| 46 \|\|*

43-46. Bhoja (given to performing) sacrifice, (giving) gifts, (practising) penance, intelligent, pious and of a very strong vow, handsome and very bright (married) Mṛtakāvatī. (This) daughter of Śarakānta gave birth to four sons: Kukura, Bhajamāna, Śyāma and Kambalabarhiṣa. Kukura’s son was Vṛṣṭi and Vṛṣṭi’s son was Dhṛti. His son was Kapotaroman; and his son was Tittiri; his son was Bahuputra. It is said that (his) learned son was Nari; his other name is said to be Candanodakadundubhi.

## \|\| 13.47 \|\|

*khyāyate tasya nāmānyaccaṃdanodakaduṃdubhiḥ \|*  
*asyāsīdabhijitputrastato jātaḥ punarvasuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. His son was Abhijit; from him Punarvasu was born.

## \|\| 13.48 \|\|

*aputrohyabhijitpūrvamṛṣibhiḥ prerito mudā \|*  
*aśvamedhaṃtuputrārthamājuhāvanarottamaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Abhijit was first sonless; but this (king), best among men, encouraged by sages gladly performed the horse-sacrifice to obtain a son.

## \|\| 13.49 \|\|

*tasya madhye vicarataḥ sabhāmadhyātsamutthitaḥ \|*  
*andhastu vidvāndharmajño yajñadātā punarvasuḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When he was moving in the gathering (at the sacrifice) from it arose blind Punarvasu learned, well-versed in religion and giver at sacrifices.

## \|\| 13.50 \|\|

*tasyāsītputramithunaṃ vasoścārijitaḥ kila \|*  
*āhukaścāhukī caiva khyātā matimatāṃ vara \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. It is said that Vasu had a couple of sons. O best among the intelligent, they were known as Āhuka and Āhukī.

## \|\| 13.51-52 \|\|

*imāṃścodāharaṃtyatra ślokāṃścātirasātmakān \|*  
*sopāsaṃgānukarṣāṇāṃ tanutrāṇāṃ varūthinām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*rathānāṃ meghaghoṣāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi daśaiva tu \|*  
*nāsatyavādino bhojā nāyajñā nāsahasradāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. In this matter they quote very interesting verses. They had ten thousand armoured and mailed chariots, thundering like cloud and having their bottoms with attachments. The Bhojas never told a lie; they never remained without performing sacrifices; and never gave less than a thousand.

## \|\| 13.53 \|\|

*nāśucirnāpyavidvāṃso na bhojādadhikobhavat \|*  
*āhukāṃ tamanuprāpta ityeṣonvaya ucyate \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. There was never a purer or a more learned person than a Bhoja. This family is said to have come down upto Āhuka.

## \|\| 13.54-55 \|\|

*āhukaścāpyavaṃtīṣu svasāraṃ cāhukīṃ dadau \|*  
*āhukasyaiva duhitā putrau dvau samasūyata \|\| 54 \|\|*

*devakaṃ cograsenaṃ ca devagarbhasamāvubhau \|*  
*devakasya sutāścaiva jajñire tridaśopamāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. And Āhuka gave his sister (to the Avanti-king) in Avanti. And the daughter of Āhuka gave birth to two sons; Devaka and Ugrasena who were like divine children; and the sons that were born to Devaka were like gods.

## \|\| 13.56 \|\|

*devavānupadevaśca sudevo devarakṣitaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptaiva vasudevāya tā dadau \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. (They were) Devavān, Upadeva, Sudeva and Devarakṣita; they had seven sisters whom he (Ugrasana) gave to Vāmadeva:

## \|\| 13.57 \|\|

*devakī śrutadevā ca yaśodā ca śrutiśravā \|*  
*śrīdevā copadevā ca surūpā ceti saptamī \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Devakī, Śrutadevā, Yaśodā, Śrutiśravā, Śrīdevā, Upadevā and Surūpā was the seventh.

## \|\| 13.58-60 \|\|

*navograsenasya sutāḥ kaṃsasteṣāṃ ca pūrvajaḥ \|*  
*nyagrodhastu sunāmā ca kaṃkaḥ śaṃkuḥ subhūśca yaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*anyastu rāṣṭrapālaśca baddhamuṣṭiḥ samuṣṭikaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ svasāraḥ paṃcāsankaṃsā kaṃsavatī tathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*surabhī rāṣṭrapālī ca kaṃkā ceti varāṃganāḥ \|*  
*ugrasenaḥ sahāpatyo vyākhyātaḥ kukurodbhavaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

58-60. Ugrasena had nine sons and Kaṃsa was the eldest among them: Nyagrodha, Sunāman, Kaṅka, Śaṅku, and (he) who (was called) Subhū. The other one was Rāṣṭrapāla; so also (were) Baddhamuṣṭi and Samuṣṭika. They had five sisters: Kaṃsā, Kaṃsavatī, Surabhī, Rāṣṭrapālī and Kaṅkā; they were beautiful ladies. Ugrasena along with his children belonged to the Kukura (i.e. Daśārha) country.

## \|\| 13.61 \|\|

*bhajamānasya putrobhūdrathimukhyo vidūrathaḥ \|*  
*rājādhidevaḥ śūraśca vidūrathasutobhavat \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Vidūratha, best among the warriors, was Bhajamāna’s son. The brave Rājādhideva was Vidūratha’s son.

## \|\| 13.62 \|\|

*rājādhidevasya sutau jajñāte vīrasaṃmatau \|*  
*kṣatravratetiniratau śoṇāśvaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. The two sons born to Rajādhideva were Śoṇāśva and Śvetavāhana. They were liked by brave men, very much given to the Kṣatriya-vow.

## \|\| 13.63 \|\|

*śoṇāśvasya sutāḥ paṃca śūrā raṇaviśāradāḥ \|*  
*śamī ca rājaśarmā ca nimūrttaḥ śatrujicchuciḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Śoṇāśva had five brave sons skilled in fighting: Śamī, Rājaśarmā, Nimūrtta, Śatrujit and Śuci.

## \|\| 13.64 \|\|

*śamīputraḥ pratikṣatraḥ pratikṣatrasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*pratikṣatrasuto bhojo hṛdīkastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*hṛdīkasyābhavanputrā daśa bhīmaparākramāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Pratikṣatra was the son of Śamī and the son of Pratikṣatra was Bhoja and his son was Hṛdīka. Hṛdīka had ten sons of fearful valour.

## \|\| 13.65-66 \|\|

*kṛtavarmāgrajasteṣāṃ śatadhanvā ca sattamaḥ \|*  
*devārhaśca subhānuśca bhīṣaṇaśca mahābalaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ajātaśca vijātaśca karakaśca karaṃdhamaḥ \|*  
*devārhasya suto vidvānjajñe kaṃbalabarhiṣaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Among them Kṛtavarman was the eldest, and best was Śatadhanvan. (Others were) Devārha, Subhānu, Bhīṣaṇa and Mahābala, and Ajāta, Vijāta, Kakara and Karandhama. A son, Kambalabarhiṣa was born to Devārha; (he was) learned.

## \|\| 13.67 \|\|

*asamaujāstatastasya samaujāśca sutāvubhau \|*  
*ajātaputrasya sutau prajāyete samaujasau \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He had two sons: Asamauja and Samauja. Two valourous sons were born to the son of Ajāta.

## \|\| 13.68 \|\|

*samaujaḥ putrā vikhyātāstrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ \|*  
*sudaṃśaśca suvaṃśaśca kṛṣṇa ityanunāmataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Samauja had three well-known and very religious sons. Their names in order were: Sudaṃśa, Suvaṃśa and Kṛṣṇa.

## \|\| 13.69 \|\|

*aṃdhakānāmimaṃ vaṃśaṃ yaḥ kīrtayati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*ātmano vipulaṃ vaṃśaṃ prajāmāpnotyayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. One who everyday glorified this family of the Andhakas, consequently had a large family and progeny.

## \|\| 13.70-71 \|\|

*gāṃdhārī caiva mādrī ca kroṣṭorbhārye babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*gāṃdhārī janayāmāsa sunitraṃ mitravatsalam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*mādrī yudhājitaṃ putraṃ tato vai devamīḍhuṣaṃ \|*  
*anamitraṃ śiniṃ caiva paṃcātra kṛtalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. Kroṣṭṛ had two wives: Gāndhārī and Mādrī. Gāndhārī gave birth to Sunitra affectionate to his friends; Mādrī gave birth to a son Yudhājit (by name), then to Devamīḍhuṣa, (then to) Anamitra and Śini. These five possessed lucky marks (on their bodies).

## \|\| 13.72 \|\|

*anamitrasuto nighno nighnasyāpi ca dvau sutau \|*  
*prasenaśca mahāvīryaḥ śaktisenaśca tāvubhau \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Nighna was Anamitra’s son; Nighna had two sons: the two were Prasena and the very brave Śaktisena.

## \|\| 13.73 \|\|

*syamaṃtakaṃ prasenasya maṇiratnamanuttamaṃ \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ maṇiratnānāṃ rājeti samudāhṛtam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Prasena had the best and unparalleled gem by name ‘Syamantaka’. It was described as the ‘King of best gems in the world’.

## \|\| 13.74 \|\|

*hṛdi kṛtvā subahuśo maṇiṃ taṃ sa vyarājata \|*  
*maṇiratnaṃ yayācetha rājārthaṃ śauriruttamam \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Wearing that gem on his chest very many times he shone brightly. Śauri asked for that excellent gem for his king.

## \|\| 13.75 \|\|

*goviṃdaśca na taṃ lebhe śaktopi na jahāra saḥ \|*  
*kadācinmṛgayāṃ yātaḥ prasenastena bhūṣitaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Govinda too did not obtain it; though capable, he did not snatch it. Some time Prasena, adorned with it went ahunting.

## \|\| 13.76-77 \|\|

*bile śabdaṃ sa śuśrāva kṛtaṃ sattvena kenacit \|*  
*tataḥ praviśya sa bilaṃ praseno hyṛkṣamāsadat \|\| 76 \|\|*

*ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ ca tathā ṛkṣaṃ cāpi prasenajit \|*  
*āsādya yuyudhāte tau parasparajayecchayā \|\| 77 \|\|*

76-77. He heard a sound made by a certain being in a cave. Then entering the cave Prasena encountered a bear (viz. Jāmbavān). The bear attacked Prasena and Prasenjit also attacked the bear and (thus) they, desirous of vanquishing each other, fought.

## \|\| 13.78-79 \|\|

*hatvā ṛkṣaḥ prasenaṃ ca tatastaṃ maṇimādadāt \|*  
*prasenaṃ tu hataṃ śrutvā goviṃdaḥ pariśaṃkitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*satrājitrā tu tadbhrātrā yādavaiśca tathāparaiḥ \|*  
*goviṃdena hato nūnaṃ praseno maṇikāraṇāt \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. The bear, having killed Prasena took that gem. Hearing that Prasena was killed Govinda was suspected by his (i.e. Prasena’s) brother, so also by others that Prasena was killed by Govinda to get the gem.

## \|\| 13.80-81 \|\|

*prasenastu gatoraṇyaṃ maṇiratnena bhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā nijaghānātha na tyajantaṃ syamaṃtakam \|\| 80 \|\|*

*jaghānaivāpradānena śatrubhūtaṃ ca keśavaḥ \|*  
*iti pravādassarvatra khyātassatrājitā kṛtaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Prasena, adorned with that best gem, had gone to the forest; seeing him who was not willing to part with Syamantaka, Kaśava had killed him (Prasena) as he, by not giving the gem, had turned into his enemy. This rumour started by Satrājit spread everywhere.

## \|\| 13.82 \|\|

*atha dīrgheṇa kālena mṛgayāṃ nirgataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*yadṛcchayā ca goviṃdo bilābhyāśamathāgamat \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Then after a long time, Govinda who had again set out for hunting, by chance came near the cave.

## \|\| 13.83-84 \|\|

*tataśśabdaṃ yathāpūrvaṃ sa cakre ṛkṣarāḍbalī \|*  
*śabdaṃ śrutvā tu goviṃdaḥ khaṅgapāṇiḥ praviśya ca \|\| 83 \|\|*

*apaśyajjāṃbavaṃtaṃ ca ṛkṣarājaṃ mahābalaṃ \|*  
*tatastūrṇaṃ hṛṣīkeśastamṛkṣamatiraṃhasā \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. Then that mighty lord of bears (viz. Jāmbavān) made a sound as before. Govinda having heard the sound and entering the cave with a sword in his hand, saw the very mighty king of the bears, viz. Jāmbavān. Then Hṛṣīkeśa, with his eyes reddened with rage, at once seized Jāmbavān very violently.

## \|\| 13.85-86 \|\|

*jāṃbavaṃtaṃ sa jagrāha krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā cainaṃ tathā viṣṇuṃ karmabhirvaiṣṇavīṃ tanuṃ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāva ṛkṣarājopi viṣṇusūktena satvaraṃ \|*  
*tatastu bhagavāṃstuṣṭo vareṇa samarocayat \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. Then seeing him as Viṣṇu in Viṣṇu’s body due to his (past) deeds the lord of the bears too quickly praised him with Viṣṇusūkta (a eulogy in honour of Viṣṇu). Then the lord being pleased, favoured him with a boon.

## \|\| 13.87 \|\|

*jāmbavānuvāca \|*  
*iṣṭaṃ cakraprahāreṇa tvatto me maraṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*kanyā ceyaṃ mama sutā bharttāraṃ tvāmavāpnuyāt \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Jāmbavān said: “It is desirable and auspicious to meet death at your hands with the stroke of your disc. This virgin daughter of mine should have you as her husband.

## \|\| 13.88 \|\|

*yoyaṃ maṇiḥ prasenāttu hatvā caivāptavānaham \|*  
*sa tvayā gṛhyatāṃ nātha maṇireṣo'tra varttate \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O lord, you should take the gem which I obtained from Prasena by killing him. The gem is here”.

## \|\| 13.89 \|\|

*ityukto jāṃbavaṃtaṃ vai hatvā cakreṇa keśavaḥ \|*  
*kṛtakāryo mahābāhuḥ kanyāṃ caivādadau tadā \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Keśava having killed Jāmbavān who had spoken thus with his disc, he of mighty arms, having achieved his purpose, took that daughter.

## \|\| 13.90-92 \|\|

*tataḥ satrājite caitanmaṇiratnaṃ sa vai dadau \|*  
*yallabdhamṛkṣarājācca sarvayādavasannidhau \|\| 90 \|\|*

*tena mithyāpravādena saṃtaptoyaṃ janārdanaḥ \|*  
*tataste yādavāḥ sarve vāsudevamathābruvan \|\| 91 \|\|*

*asmākaṃ manasi hyāsītprasenastu tvayā hataḥ \|*  
*ekaikasyāstu suṃdaryo daśa satrājitaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

90-92. Then in the presence of all Yādavas, Janārdana, who was angry due to the false rumour, gave to Satrājit that best gem which he had received from the bear-king. Then all the Yādavas said to Vāsudeva: “We had thought that you had killed Prasena”. Satrājit had ten sons from each one of his ten wives.

## \|\| 13.93 \|\|

*satyotpannāssutāstasya śatamekaṃ ca viśrutāḥ \|*  
*vikhyātāśca mahāvīryā bhaṃgakāraśca pūrvajaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He had hundred and one sons born of Satyā. They were well-known and very brave, and Bhaṅgakāra was the eldest.

## \|\| 13.94 \|\|

*satyā vratavatī svapnā bhaṃgakārasya pūrvajā \|*  
*suṣuvustāḥ kumārāṃśca śinīvālaḥ pratāpavān \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Satyā, Vratavati and Svapnā, elder to Bhaṅgakāra, gave birth to those boys. Śinīvāla was brave.

## \|\| 13.95 \|\|

*abhaṃgo yuyudhānaśca śinistasyātmajobhavat \|*  
*tasmādyugaṃdharaḥ putrāśśataṃ tasya prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. There was (born) the warrior Abhaṅga; Śini was his son; from him Yugandhara (was born); he is said to have had a hundred sons.

## \|\| 13.96 \|\|

*anamitrāhvayo yo vai vikhyāto vṛṣṇivaṃśajaḥ \|*  
*anamitrātśinirjajñe kaniṣṭho vṛṣṇinaṃdanaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. He was called Anamitra; was well known as a descendant of the Vṛṣṇi family. From Anamitra was born Śini, the youngest member of the Vṛṣṇi family.

## \|\| 13.97 \|\|

*anamitrācca saṃjajñe vṛṣṇivīro yudhājitaḥ \|*  
*anyau ca tanayau vīrā vṛṣabhaścitra eva ca \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. From Anamitra again was born Yudhājit, a warrior of the Vṛṣṇi family. Two other sons also (were born from Anamitra): Ṛṣabha and Citra.

## \|\| 13.98 \|\|

*ṛṣabhaḥ kāśirājasya sutāṃ bhāryāmaniṃditāṃ \|*  
*jayaṃtaśca jayaṃtīṃ ca śubhāṃ bhāryāmaviṃdata \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Ṛṣabha got as his wife the praiseworthy daughter of Kāśirāja, and Jayanta obtained auspicious Jayantī as his wife.

## \|\| 13.99 \|\|

*jayaṃtasya jayaṃtyāṃ vai putraḥ samabhavattataḥ \|*  
*sadā yajvātidhīraśca śrutavānatithipriyaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Then Jayanta’s son was born of Jayantī. He always performed sacrifices, was very courageous, learned and was dear to the guests (or he) liked guests.

## \|\| 13.100 \|\|

*akrūraḥ suṣuve tasmātsudakṣo bhūridakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*ratnakanyā ca śaibyā ca akrūrastāmavāptavān \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. From him Akrūra, very diligent and giver of large presents was born. Śaibyā was the gem among virgins; Akrūra obtained her (as his wife).

## \|\| 13.101-102 \|\|

*putrānutpādayāmāsa ekādaśamahābalān \|*  
*upalaṃbhaṃ sadālaṃbhamutkalaṃ cāryyaśaiśavaṃ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*sudhīraṃ ca sadāyakṣaṃ śatrughnaṃ vārimejayaṃ \|*  
*dharmadṛṣṭiṃ ca dharmaṃ ca sṛṣṭimauliṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. On her he generated eleven very mighty sons: Upalambha, Sadālambha, Utkala, Āryaśaiśava, Sudhīra, Sadāyakṣa, Śatrughna, Vārimejaya, Dharmadṛṣṭi, Dharma and Sṛṣṭimauli.

## \|\| 13.103-107 \|\|

*sarve ca pratihartāro ratnānāṃ jajñire ca te \|*  
*akrūrācchūrasenāyāṃ sutau dvau kulanaṃdanau \|\| 103 \|\|*

*devavānupadevaśca jajñāte devasaṃmatau \|*  
*aśvinyāṃ tricatuḥ putrāḥ pṛthurvipṛthureva ca \|\| 104 \|\|*

*aśvagrīvo śvabāhuśca supārśvaka gaveṣaṇau \|*  
*riṣṭanemiḥ suvarcā ca sudharmā mṛdureva ca \|\| 105 \|\|*

*abhūmirbahubhūmiśca śraviṣṭhā śravaṇe striyau \|*  
*imāṃ mithyābhiśaptiṃ yo veda kṛṣṇasya buddhimān \|\| 106 \|\|*

*na sa mithyābhiśāpena abhigamyaśca kenacit \|*  
*ekṣvākī suṣuve putraṃ śūramadbhutamīḍhuṣam \|\| 107 \|\|*

103-106a. And all of them were born (so brave) that they took away gems. Two sons, resembling gods, and delighting the family were born on Śūrasenā from Akrūra: Devavān and Upadeva. From Akrūra twelve sons were born to Aśvinī: Pṛthu Vipṛthu, Aśvagrīva, Aśvabāhu, Supārśva, Gaveṣaṇa, Riṣṭanemi Suvarcas, Sudharman, Mṛdu, Abhūmi and Bahubhūmi; and two daughters: Śraviṣṭhā and Śravaṇā.

106b-107a. An intelligent preson, who knows about this false accusation of Kṛṣṇa can never be assailed by anyone with a false curse.

107b. Aikṣvākī gave birth to a brave son—the wonderful Mīḍhuṣa.

## \|\| 13.108-111 \|\|

*mīḍhuṣā jajñire śūrā bhojāyāṃ puruṣā daśa \|*  
*vasudevo mahābāhuḥ pūrvamānakaduṃdubhiḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

*devabhāgastathā jajñe tathā devaśravāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭiṃ kuniścaiva naṃdiścaiva sakṛdyaśāḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*śyāmaḥ śamīkaḥ saptākhyaḥ paṃca cāsya varāṃganāḥ \|*  
*śrutakīrtiḥ pṛthā caiva śrutadevī śrutaśravāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*rājādhidevī ca tathā paṃcaitā vīramātaraḥ \|*  
*vṛddhasya śrutadevī tu kārūṣaṃ suṣuve nṛpam \|\| 111 \|\|*

108-111. Ten brave sons were generated on Bhojā by Mīḍhuṣa: Vasudeva (was born) first, (then)Ānakadundubhi; so also Devabhāga was generated (by Mīḍhuṣa); and Devaśravas, Anāvṛṣṭi, Kunti, and Nandi and Sakṛdyaśa, Śyama, Śamīka (also) known as Sapta. He had five beautiful wives: Śrutakīrti, Pṛthā, and Śrutadevī and Śrutaśravā and also Rājādhidevī. These five were the mothers of heroes. Vṛddha’s wife Śrutadevī gave birth to king Kāruṣa.

## \|\| 13.112 \|\|

*kaikeyācchrutakīrtestu jajñe saṃtardano nṛpaḥ \|*  
*śrutaśravasi caidyasya sunīthaḥ samapadyata \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. From Kaikaya Śrutakīrti gave birth to king Santardana. Sunītha was born on Śrutaśravas from Caidya.

## \|\| 13.113 \|\|

*rājādhidevyāḥ saṃbhūto dharmādbhayavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*śūraḥ sakhyena baddhosau kuṃtibhoje pṛthāṃ dadau \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. From Dharma Bhayavivarjita was born on Rājādhidevī. Śūra, bound by friendship, gave (in adoption) Pṛthā to Kuntibhoja.

## \|\| 13.114 \|\|

*evaṃ kuṃtī samākhyā ca vasudevasvasā pṛthā \|*  
*kuṃtibhojodadāttāṃ tu pāṃḍorbhāryāmaniṃditām \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Thus, Pṛthā, Vasudeva’s sister was also called Kuntī. Kuntibhoja gave that praiseworthy Pṛthā to Pāṇḍu as his wife.

## \|\| 13.115 \|\|

*pāṇḍvarthesūta devī sā devaputrānmahārathān \|*  
*dharmādyudhiṣṭhiro jajñe vātājjajñe vṛkodaraḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. That queen gave birth to five brave sons for Pāṇḍu: Yudhiṣṭhira was born from Dharma; Vṛkodara (i.e. Bhīma) was born from Vāyu.

## \|\| 13.116 \|\|

*iṃdrāddhanaṃjayaścaiva śakratulyaparākramaḥ \|*  
*yo'sau tripuruṣājjātastribhiraṃśairmahārathaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Dhanañjaya (i.e. Arjuna) comparable to Indra in valour was born from Indra; he the brave one, was born with the three portions from three gods.

## \|\| 13.117 \|\|

*devakāryakaraścaiva sarvadānavasūdanaḥ \|*  
*avadhyāścāpi śakrasya dānavā yena ghātitāḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. He worked for gods, and killed all demons; he killed those demons whom even Indra was unable to kill.

## \|\| 13.118 \|\|

*sthāpitassa tu śakreṇa labdhavarcāstriviṣṭape \|*  
*mādravatyāṃ tu janitāvaśvināviti naḥ śrutam \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. He who had obtained vigour was placed in heaven by Indra. We have heard that two sons were generated on Mādravatī (by the Aśvins).

## \|\| 13.119 \|\|

*nakulaḥ sahadevaśca rūpasatvaguṇānvitau \|*  
*rohiṇī pauravī nāma bhāryā cānakaduṃdubheḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. (They were) Nakula and Sahadeva and were endowed with handsome form and goodness. Ānakadundubhi had a wife named Rohiṇī of the Pūru family.

## \|\| 13.120-121 \|\|

*lebhe ceṣṭaṃ sutaṃ rāmaṃ sāraṇaṃ ca raṇapriyam \|*  
*durdharaṃ damanaṃ caiva piṃḍārakamahāhanuṃ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*atha māyātvamāvāsyā devakī yā bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tasyāṃ jajñe mahābāhuḥ pūrvaṃ tu sa prajāpatiḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. He had (from her) a son Rāma dear to him; so also Sāraṇa, Caraṇapriya, Durdhara, Damana, Piṇḍāraka and Mahāhanu. That who was Māyā Amāvāsyā would be Devakī. First that mighty Prajāpati was born from her.

## \|\| 13.122 \|\|

*anujātābhavatkṛṣṇā subhadrā bhadrabhāṣiṇī \|*  
*vijayo rocamānastu vardhamānaśca devalaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Then from her the darkish Subhadrā, gracious in speech, was born; so also (were born) Vijaya, Rocamāna, Vardhamāna and Devala.

## \|\| 13.123-126 \|\|

*ete sarve mahātmāna upadevyāṃ prajajñire \|*  
*agāvahaṃ mahātmānaṃ bṛhaddevī vyajāyata \|\| 123 \|\|*

*bṛhaddevyāṃ svayaṃ jajñe mandako nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*saptamaṃ devakī putraṃ remaṃtaṃ saṣuve sutam \|\| 124 \|\|*

*gaveṣaṇaṃ mahābhāgaṃ saṃgrāmeṣvaparājitam \|*  
*śrutadevyā vihāre tu vane vicaratā purā \|\| 125 \|\|*

*vaiśyāyāṃ samadhācchauriḥ putraṃ kauśikamagrajam \|*  
*śrutaṃdharā tu rājñī tu sauragaṃdhaparigrahaḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

123-126. All these were born on the subordinate queen. Bṛhaddevī gave birth to the magnanimous Agāvaha. He himself was born by name Mandaka on Bṛhaddevī. Devakī gave birth to her seventh son Romanta, and Gaveṣaṇa unvanquished in battles. While formerly wandering in the forest, Śauri produced in Śrutadevī’s pleasure-house, the eldest son viz. Kusika on a Vaiśya lady. Śrutandharā was one of the queens (of Vasudeva).

## \|\| 13.127 \|\|

*putraṃ ca kapilaṃ caiva vasudevātmajo balī \|*  
*janānāṃ ca viṣādobhūtprathamaḥ sa dhanurddharaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Vasudeva’s mighty son Kapila, having divine fragrance, the first archer, caused grief to the people.

## \|\| 13.128-129 \|\|

*saubhadraścābhavaścaiva mahāsatvau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*devabhāgasutaścāpi prastāvaḥ sa budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*paṇḍitaṃ prathamaṃ bāhu devaśravasamuttamam \|*  
*ikṣvākukulato yasya manasvinyā yaśasvinī \|\| 129 \|\|*

128a. These two, viz. Saubhadra and Bhava were very energetic.

128b-129. (Obscure) Devabhāga’s son (named) Prastāva together with Budha is remembered. The first and best Devaśravas is said (Bāhu or Prāhuḥ?) to be a scholars. His daughter Yaśasvinī was born from Manasvin of Ikṣvāku family. (Her son was) Śatrughna.

## \|\| 13.130-133 \|\|

*nivṛttaśatruḥ śatrughnaḥ śraddhā tasmādajāyata \|*  
*gaṃḍūṣāyāmapatyāni kṛṣṇastuṣṭaḥ śataṃ dadau \|\| 130 \|\|*

*sa caṃdraṃ tu mahābhāgaṃ vīryavaṃtaṃ mahābalam \|*  
*raṃtipālaśca raṃtiśca naṃdanasya sutāvubhau \|\| 131 \|\|*

*śamīkaputrāścatvāro vikrāṃtāḥ sumahābalāḥ \|*  
*virajaśca dhanuścaiva vyomastasya sa sṛṃjayaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

*anapatyobhavadvyomaḥ sṛṃjayasya dhanaṃjayaḥ \|*  
*yo jāyamāno bhojatvaṃ rājarṣitvamavāptavān \|\| 133 \|\|*

130-13la. (Obscure) His enemies had retreated from him; he was the killer of enemies; Śraddhā was born from him. Kṛṣṇa being pleased gave a hundred children to Gaṇḍūṣā, with the moon, magnanimous, powerful and strong(?)

131b-133. Nandana’s two sons were Rantipāla and Ranti-Śamīka’s four brave and very mighty sons were: Viraja, Dhanu and Vyoma and Sṛñjaya. Vyoma was childless; Dhanañjaya was Sṛñjaya’s (son); he who was born as Bhoja became a royal sage.

## \|\| 13.134 \|\|

*kṛṣṇasya janmābhyudayaṃ yaḥ kīrtayati nityaśaḥ \|*  
*śṛṇoti vā naro nityaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. The man who always narrates or listens to Kṛṣṇa’s birth and rise is freed from all sins.

## \|\| 13.135 \|\|

*atha devo mahādevaḥ pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*vihārārthaṃ sa devosau mānuṣeṣvapyajāyata \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Kṛṣṇa, the great god, formerly the creator, was born even among men.

## \|\| 13.136 \|\|

*devakyāṃ vasudevena tapasā puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*caturbāhustu saṃjāto divyarūpo janāśrayaḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. By means of penance Vasudeva produced on Devakī the lotus-eyed (Kṛṣṇa), having four arms, of a divine form and the refuge for people.

## \|\| 13.137 \|\|

*śrīvatsalakṣaṇaṃ devaṃ dṛṣṭvā devaiḥ salakṣaṇam \|*  
*uvāca vasudevastaṃ rūpaṃ saṃhara vai prabho \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Having seen him with the sign of Śrivatsa and resembling gods, Vasudeva said to him “O Lord, withdraw your form.

## \|\| 13.138 \|\|

*bhītohaṃ deva kaṃsasya tatastvetadbravīmi te \|*  
*mama putrā hatāstena śreṣṭhāḥ ṣaḍbhīmavikramāḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. O god, I am afraid of Kaṃsa, therefore I am saying this to you. He killed my six pre-eminent sons of terrible valour.”

## \|\| 13.139 \|\|

*vasudevavacaḥ śrutvā rūpaṃ saṃharadacyutaḥ \|*  
*anujñāpya tu taṃ śaurirnandagopagṛhenayat \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Having heard Vasudeva’s words Acyuta withdrew his form.

## \|\| 13.140 \|\|

*datvā taṃ naṃdagopāya rakṣyatāmiti cābravīt \|*  
*atastusarvakalyāṇaṃ yādavānāṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. After he agreed to it, Śauri took him to the house of the cowherd Nanda. Having handed him over to Nanda, he said to him, “Protect him; then only all the Yādavas will be happy.

## \|\| 13.141 \|\|

*ayaṃ tu garbho devakyā yāvatkaṃsaṃ haniṣyati \|*  
*tāvatpṛthivyāṃ bhavitā kṣemo bhārāvahaḥ param \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. As soon as this embryo (i.e. son) of Devakī will kill Kaṃsa, there will be happiness in the world, which would greatly remove the burden (of the earth).

## \|\| 13.142 \|\|

*ye vai duṣṭāstu rājānastāṃstu sarvānhaniṣyati \|*  
*kauravāṇāṃ raṇe bhūte sarvakṣatrasamāgame \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. Who (i.e. he) will kill all those kings who are wicked, when there will be a war among the Kauravas where all the Kṣatriyas will assemble.

## \|\| 13.143 \|\|

*sārathyamarjunasyāyaṃ svayaṃ devaḥ kariṣyati \|*  
*niḥkṣatriyāṃ dharāṃ kṛtvā bhokṣyate śeṣatāṃ gatām \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. This god himself will be the charioteer of Arjuna; having rid the earth of the Kṣatriyas he will enjoy the rest (i.e. void of the Kṣatriyas) and will take the entire Yadu-race to the divine world.”

## \|\| 13.144 \|\|

*sarvaṃ yadukulaṃ caiva devalokaṃ nayiṣyati \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*ka eṣa vasudevastu devakī kā yaśasvinī \|\| 144 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

144\. Who is this Vasudeva? Who is this glorious Devakī?

## \|\| 13.145 \|\|

*naṃdagopaśca kaścaiva yaśodā kā mahāvratā \|*  
*yā viṣṇuṃ poṣitavatī yāṃ sa mātetyabhāṣata \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Who is the cowherd Nanda? Who is Yaśodā rigidly observing vows, who nourished Viṣṇu and whom he called his mother?

## \|\| 13.146 \|\|

*yā garbhaṃ janayāmāsa yā cainaṃ samavarddhayat \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*puruṣaḥ kaśyapaścāsāvaditistatpriyā smṛtā \|\| 146 \|\|*

146a. Who gave birth to (a son) an embryo and brought him up?

Pulastya said:

146b. Kaśyapa was the Supreme Being and Aditi is said to be his beloved.

## \|\| 13.147 \|\|

*kaśyapo brahmaṇoṃśastu pṛthivyā aditistathā \|*  
*naṃdo droṇassamākhyāto yaśodātha dharābhavat \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Kaśyapa was a portion of Brahman and Aditi that of the earth. Nanda was said to be a cloud and Yaśodā was the earth.

## \|\| 13.148 \|\|

*athakāmānmahābāhurdevakyāḥ samapūrayat \|*  
*ye tayā kāṃkṣitāḥ pūrvamajāttasmānmahātmanaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. He satisfied many desires of Devakī, which she had formerly entertained from the great unborn one.

## \|\| 13.149-150 \|\|

*aciraṃ sa mahādevaḥ praviṣṭo mānuṣīṃ tanuṃ \|*  
*mohayansarvabhūtāni yogādyogī samāyayau \|\| 149 \|\|*

*naṣṭe dharme tathā yajñe viṣṇurvṛṣṇikule vibhuḥ \|*  
*kartuṃ dharmavyavasthānamasurāṇāṃ praṇāśanam \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. Soon that great god entered a human body. He (lord Viṣṇu) possessed of magical powers, stupefying all beings with his superhuman faculties came (down) in the family to establish righteousness and destroy the demons, when righteousness and sacrifice had perished.

## \|\| 13.151-152 \|\|

*rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca satyā nāgnijitī tathā \|*  
*sumitrā ca tathā śaibyā gāṃdhārī lakṣmaṇā tathā \|\| 151 \|\|*

*subhīmā ca tathā mādrī kauśalyā vijayā tathā \|*  
*evamādīni devīnāṃ sahasrāṇi ca ṣoḍaśa \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Satyā, so also Nāgnijitī and Sumitrā, Śaibyā, Gāndhāri and Lakṣmaṇā. So also Subhīmā, Mādrī, Kausalyā and Vijayā. These and others were his sixteen thousand wives.

## \|\| 13.153 \|\|

*rukmiṇī janayāmāsa putrānśṛṇu viśāradān \|*  
*cārudeṣṇaṃ raṇeśūraṃ pradyumnañca mahābalam \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Listen to the (names of) sons born of Rukmiṇī: Cārudeṣṇa who was brave in battles, and very mighty Pradyumna.

## \|\| 13.154 \|\|

*sucāruṃ cārubhadrañca sadaśvaṃ hrasvameva ca \|*  
*saptamañcāruguptañca cārubhadrañca cārukaṃ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. Sucāru and Cārubhadra and Sadaśva and also Hrasva.

## \|\| 13.155-156 \|\|

*cāruhāsaṃ kaniṣṭhañca kanyāñcārumatīṃ tathā \|*  
*jajñire satyabhāmāyā bhānurbhīmarathaḥ kṣaṇaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

*rohito dīptimāṃścaiva tāmrabaṃdho jalaṃdhamaḥ \|*  
*catasro jajñire teṣāṃ svasāraśca yavīyasīḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

155-156. The youngest was Cāruhāsa, and a daughter (named) Cārumatī. On Rohiṇī were born Bhānu, Bhīmaratha, Kṣaṇa, Rohita and Dīptimān, Tāmrabandhu, Jalandhama. Among them, four daughters were born and they were younger.

## \|\| 13.157 \|\|

*jāṃbavatyāḥ suto jajñe sāṃbaścaivātiśobhanaḥ \|*  
*sauraśāstrasya karttā vai pratimā maṃdirasya ca \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. From Jāmbavatī was born the extremely charming Sāmba. He was the author of solar science, and an image in the house.

## \|\| 13.158 \|\|

*mūlasthāne niveśaśca kṛtastena mahātmanā \|*  
*tuṣṭena devadevena kuṣṭharogo vināśitaḥ \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. The magnanimous one entered the very base (supreme spirit); (then) the god of gods being pleased destroyed his leprosy.

## \|\| 13.159 \|\|

*sumitraṃ cārumitraṃ ca mitraviṃdā vyajāyata \|*  
*mitrabāhuḥ sunīthaśca nāgnajityāṃ babhūvatuḥ \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. Mitravindā gave birth to Sumitra and Cārumitra. From Nāgnajitī were born Mitrabāhu and Sunītha.

## \|\| 13.160 \|\|

*evamādīni putrāṇāṃsahasrāṇi niśāmaya \|*  
*aśītiśca sahasrāṇāṃ vāsudevasutāstathā \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. Know these and others to be thousands of (Kṛṣṇa’s) sons; the sons of Vāsudeva are eighty thousand.

## \|\| 13.161 \|\|

*pradyumnasya ca dāyādo vaidarbhyāṃ buddhisattamaḥ \|*  
*aniruddho raṇe yoddhā jajñesya mṛgaketanaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Pradyumna’s most intelligent son, viz. Aniruddha, a warrior in battle and Mṛgaketana (having the deer on his banner) was born of Vaidarbhī.

## \|\| 13.162 \|\|

*kāmyā supārśvatanayā sāṃbāllebhe tarasvinam \|*  
*sattvaprakṛtayo devāḥ parāḥ paṃca prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. Kāmyā, the daughter of Supārśva obtained Tarasvin from Sāmba. The other five were declared to be good-natured gods.

## \|\| 13.163 \|\|

*tisraḥ koṭyaḥ pravīrāṇāṃ yādavānāṃ mahātmanāṃ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi vīryavaṃto mahābalāḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. There were three crores of the great Yādavas. Sixty thousand were brave and very mighty.

## \|\| 13.164-165 \|\|

*devāṃśāḥ sarva eveha utpannāste mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*daivāsure hatā ye vā asurāstu mahābalāḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*ihotpannā manuṣyeṣu bādhaṃte sarvamānavān \|*  
*teṣāmuddharaṇārthāya utpannā yādave kule \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. Portions of gods were born in the form of all of these of great prowess. Or mighty demons killed in the war between gods and demons were born here among men and harassed all men. For their emancipation they were born in the Yādava-family.

## \|\| 13.166 \|\|

*kulānāṃ śatamekaṃ ca yādavānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*viṣṇusteṣāṃ praṇetā ca prabhutve ca vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. There were a hundred families of the magnanimous Yādavas. Viṣṇu was their promoter and was placed as their lord.

## \|\| 13.167 \|\|

*nideśasthāyinastasya ṛddhyaṃte sarvayādavāḥ \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*saptarṣayaḥ kuberaśca yakṣo maṇidharastathā \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. All those Yādavas remaining obedient to him prospered.

## \|\| 13.168-169 \|\|

*sātyakirnāradaścaiva śivo dhanvaṃtaristathā \|*  
*ādidevastathāviṣṇurebhistu saha daivataiḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ sahasaṃbhūtāḥ surasambhūtayaḥ kṣitau \|*  
*bhaviṣyāḥ kati vā cāsya prādurbhāvā mahātmanaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

168-169. The seven sages, Kubera, Maṇidhara, Yakṣa, Sātyaki, Nārada, Śiva and Dhanvantari, Viṣṇu the first god along with (other) deities—why were all these hosts of gods born together on the earth?

## \|\| 13.170 \|\|

*sarvakṣetreṣu sarveṣu kimarthamiha jāyate \|*  
*yadarthamiha saṃbhūto viṣṇurvṛṣṇyaṃdhake kule \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. How many manifestations of this great one will be there? For which purpose is he born in all fields? For what purpose is Viṣṇu born in the Vṛṣṇyandhaka family? Please tell me who am asking you.

## \|\| 13.171 \|\|

*punaḥpunarmanuṣyeṣu tanme tvaṃ brūhi pṛcchataḥ \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu bhūpa pravakṣyāmi rahasyātirahasyakam \|*  
*yathā divyatanurviṣṇurmānuṣeṣviha jāyate \|\| 171 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

171\. O prince, listen, I shall tell you a very great secret as to why Viṣṇu of a divine body is born among men.

## \|\| 13.172 \|\|

*yugāṃte tu parāvṛtte kāle praśithile prabhuḥ \|*  
*devāsuramanuṣyeṣu jāyate harirīśvaraḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. When the Yuga comes to an end, and time becomes lax, Hari, the lord, is born among gods, demons or men,

## \|\| 13.173-174 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityastrailokyasya praśāsitā \|*  
*balinādhiṣṭhite caiva punarlokatraye kramāt \|\| 173 \|\|*

*sakhyamāsītparamakaṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha \|*  
*yugākhyā daśa saṃpūrṇā āsīdavyākulaṃ jagat \|\| 174 \|\|*

173-174. The demon Hiraṇyakaśipu was the ruler of the three worlds; again subsequently when Bali was the ruler of the three worlds there was great friendship of the gods with the demons. Ten complete yugas passed; the world was unperturbed.

## \|\| 13.175 \|\|

*nideśasthāyinaścāpi tayordevāsurā svayaṃ \|*  
*baddho balirvimardoyaṃ susaṃvṛttaḥ sudāruṇaḥ \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. The gods and demons were obedient to those two. Bali was bound (by Vāmana). His destruction was extremely fearful, (which) brought a great loss both to gods and demons.

## \|\| 13.176-177 \|\|

*devānāmasurāṇāṃ ca ghoraḥ kṣayakaro mahān \|*  
*kartuṃ dharmavyavasthāṃ ca jāyate mānuṣeṣviha \|\| 176 \|\|*

*bhṛgoḥ śāpanimittaṃ tu devāsurakṛte tadā \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ devāsurakṛte harirdehamavāptavān \|\| 177 \|\|*

176-177. Here (in this world) he is then born among men due to Bhṛgu’s curse to establish religious order for gods and men.

## \|\| 13.178 \|\|

*daivāsuraṃ yathāvṛttaṃ tanme kathaya suvrata \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*teṣāṃ jayanimittaṃ vai saṃgrāmā syuḥ sudāruṇāḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

178\. Why did Hari take up a body for gods and demons? O you of good vow, tell me the (full account of the war) between gods and demons as it took place.

Pulastya spoke:

Terrible battles were fought between them for victory.

## \|\| 13.179 \|\|

*avatārā daśadvau ca śuddhā manvaṃtare smṛtāḥ \|*  
*nāmadheyaṃ samāsena śṛṇu teṣāṃ vivakṣitam \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Ten and two pure incarnations are said (to have been taken) in the period of Manu. Listen to their names as desired to be told by me.

## \|\| 13.180 \|\|

*prathamo nārasiṃhastu dvitīyaścāpi vāmanaḥ \|*  
*tṛtīyastu varāhaśca caturtho'mṛtamaṃthanaḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. First (incarnation) is Narasiṃha; and the second one is Vāmana; the third is Varāha and the fourth is (Kūrma at the time of) churning out nectar.

## \|\| 13.181 \|\|

*saṃgrāmaḥ paṃcamaścaiva sughorastārakāmayaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭho hyāḍībakākhyaśca saptamastraipurastathā \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. Fifth one is the very terrible war Tārakāmaya involving Tāraka. The sixth one is called Āḍīvaka; similarly the seventh is Traipura.

## \|\| 13.182 \|\|

*aṣṭamaścāṃdhakavadho navamo vṛtraghātanaḥ \|*  
*dhvajaśca daśamasteṣāṃ hālāhalastataḥ paraṃ \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. Eighth is that of the murder of Andhaka, the ninth is that of the murder of Vṛtra. Tenth of them is that of Dhvaja, and Hālāhala is next to that.

## \|\| 13.183 \|\|

*prathito dvādaśasteṣāṃ ghoraḥ kolāhalastathā \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo narasiṃhena sūditaḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. The twelfth is known as the terrible Kolāhala. The demon Hiraṇyakaśipu was killed by Narasiṃha.

## \|\| 13.184 \|\|

*vāmanena balirbaddhastrailokyākramaṇe purā \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣo hato dvaṃdve prativāde tu daivataiḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Formerly Bali was bound by Vāmana at the time of overpowering the three worlds.

## \|\| 13.185 \|\|

*daṃṣṭrayā tu varāheṇa samudrastho dvidhā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*prahlādo nirjito yuddhe iṃdreṇāmṛtamaṃthane \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. The deities killed Hiraṇyākṣa in an encounter. The Boar (incarnation) made him into two when he dwelt in the ocean.

## \|\| 13.186 \|\|

*virocanastu prāhlādirnityamindravadhodyataḥ \|*  
*iṃdreṇaiva ca vikramya nihatastārakāmaye \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. At the time of churning nectar (out of the ocean i.e. during the incarnation as Tortoise) Indra vanquished Prahlāda. Virocana, the son of Prahlāda, was always intent on killing Indra; but Indra having overpowered him killed him in the Tārakāmaya battle.

## \|\| 13.187-188 \|\|

*aśaknuvatsu deveṣu tripuraṃ soḍhumāsuram \|*  
*mohayitvā'mṛte pīte gorūpeṇāsurāriṇā \|\| 187 \|\|*

*nāsanjīvayituṃ śakyā bhūyo bhūyomṛtāsurāḥ \|*  
*nihatā dānavāḥ sarve trailokye tryaṃbakeṇa tu \|\| 188 \|\|*

187-188. When the gods were unable to conquer Tripura, the enemy of gods, they having deluded the demons drank the nectar and came to life again and again. All the demons in the three worlds were killed by Śiva.

## \|\| 13.189 \|\|

*asurāśca piśācāśca dānavāścāṃdhake vadhe \|*  
*hatā devamanuṣyaiste pitṛbhiścaiva sarvaśaḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. At the murder of Andhaka gods, men and manes killed demons, goblins and fiends everywhere.

## \|\| 13.190 \|\|

*saṃpṛkto dānavairvṛtro ghore kolāhale hataḥ \|*  
*tadā viṣṇusahāyena maheṃdreṇa nipātitaḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. In the terrible tumult Vṛtra who was (formerly) sprinkled (with nectar) by the demons was struck and destroyed by Indra with the help of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 13.191 \|\|

*hatastato maheṃdreṇa māyāchannastu yogavit \|*  
*vajreṇa kṣaṇamāviśya vipracittiḥ sahānugaḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. Having approached Vipracitti with his followers Mahendra with his bolt killed him who knew magical art and had concealed himself wickedly.

## \|\| 13.192 \|\|

*daityāśca dānavāścaiva saṃyutāḥ kṛtsnaśastu te \|*  
*ete daivā'surāvṛttāḥ saṃgrāmādvā daśaiva tu \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. The demons and gods who had fully gathered had fought twelve battles causing destruction of gods and demons and leading to the well-being of the beings.

## \|\| 13.193-194 \|\|

*devāsurakṣayakarāḥ prajānāṃ ca hitāya vai \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipū rājā varṣāṇāmarbudaṃ babhau \|\| 193 \|\|*

*dvisaptatiṃ tathānyāni niyutānyadhikāni tu \|*  
*aśīti ca sahasrāṇi trailokyaiśvaryavānabhūt \|\| 194 \|\|*

193-194. Hiraṇyakaśipu ruled as a king and enjoyed sovereignty in the three worlds for a hundred and seventy-two million and eighty thousand years.

## \|\| 13.195 \|\|

*paryāyeṇa tu rājābhūdbalirvarṣārbudaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhiṃ caiva sahasrāṇi niyutāni ca viṃśatiṃ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Bali, in turn, became a king (and ruled) for a hundred and twenty million and sixty thousand years.

## \|\| 13.196 \|\|

*balirājyādhikāre tu yāvatkālaśca kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tāvatkālaṃ tu prahlādo nirvṛto hyasuraiḥ saha \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. Prahlāda enjoyed with the demons for the same period as Bali was said to have ruled.

## \|\| 13.197-198 \|\|

*jayārthamete vijñeyā asurāṇāṃ mahaujasaḥ \|*  
*trailokyamidamavyagraṃ maheṃdreṇānupālyate \|\| 197 \|\|*

*asampannamidaṃ sarvaṃ yāvadvarṣāyutaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*paryāyeṇaiva samprāpte trailokyaṃ pākaśāsane \|\| 198 \|\|*

197-198. These (wars) of the mighty Indra should be known (to have been fought) for conquering the demons. This entire group of the three worlds is then protected by Indra, when for ten thousand years it was not prosperous. When after a lapse of time Indra obtained the (kingdom) of the three worlds, Yajña left the demons and went to the gods.

## \|\| 13.199 \|\|

*tato'surānparityajya yajño devānagacchata \|*  
*yajñe devānatha gate ditijāḥ kāvyamabruvan \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. When Yajña went to gods, the sons of Diti said to Śukra:

## \|\| 13.200 \|\|

*daityā ūcuḥ \|*  
*hṛtaṃ maghavatā rājyaṃ tyaktvā yajñaḥ surāngataḥ \|*  
*sthātuṃ na śuknumo hyatra praviśāmo rasātalam \|\| 200 \|\|*

200\. “Indra has snatched our kingdom; Yajña, deserting us, has gone to gods. We can’t remain here; we shall enter the lower world.”

## \|\| 13.201 \|\|

*evamuktobravīdetānviṣaṇṇānsāṃtvayangirā \|*  
*mā bhaiṣṭa dhārayiṣyāmi tejasā svena vo'surāḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

201\. Thus addressed, Śukra said to the dejected demons, consoling them with(these) words: “Do not be afraid, O demons, I shall support you with my might.

## \|\| 13.202 \|\|

*maṃtrāścauṣadhayaścaiva dharāyāṃ yattu vartate \|*  
*mayi tiṣṭhati tatsarvaṃ pādamātraṃ sureṣu vai \|\| 202 \|\|*

202\. Whatever chants and herbs are there on the earth all that is with me; only a portion of it is with gods.

## \|\| 13.203 \|\|

*tatsarvaṃ ca pradāsyāmi yuṣmadarthe dhṛtaṃ mayā \|*  
*tato devāstutāndṛṣṭvā dhṛtānkāvyena dhīmatā \|\| 203 \|\|*

203\. I shall give you all that is kept for you by me”. Then gods seeing them supported by Śukra and being dejected held consultation with a desire to kill them:

## \|\| 13.204 \|\|

*amaṃtrayaṃta devā vai saṃvignāstajjighṛkṣayā \|*  
*kāvyo hyeṣa idaṃ sarvaṃ vyāvartayati no balāt \|\| 204 \|\|*

204\. “This Śukra will with his might, withdraw all this from us. We shall well go (ahead) before he deprives us (of the kingdom).

## \|\| 13.205 \|\|

*sādhu gacchāmahe tūrṇaṃ yāvanna cyāvayeta vai \|*  
*prasahya jitvā śiṣṭāṃstu pātālaṃ prāpayāmahe \|\| 205 \|\|*

205\. Having forcibly conquered the remaining (demons) we shall send them to the nether world.”

## \|\| 13.206 \|\|

*tato devāstu saṃrabdhā dānavānupasṛtya ha \|*  
*tataste vadhyamānāstaiḥ kāvyamevābhidudruvuḥ \|\| 206 \|\|*

206\. Then the enraged gods approached the demons and the demons being killed by them rushed to Śukra himself.

## \|\| 13.207 \|\|

*tataḥ kāvyastu tāndṛṣṭvā tūrṇaṃ devairabhidrutān \|*  
*rakṣākāryeṇa saṃhṛtya devebhyastānsurārditān \|\| 207 \|\|*

207\. Then Kāvya (i.e. Śukra) seeing them being attacked by gods, brought them together for protecting them who were harassed by gods.

## \|\| 13.208-210 \|\|

*kāvyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ devā nirviśaṃkāstu te jahuḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kāvyonuciṃtyātha brahmaṇo vacanaṃ hitam \|\| 208 \|\|*

*tānuvāca tataḥ kāvyaḥ pūrvavṛttamanusmaran \|*  
*trailokyaṃ vo hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ vāmanena tribhiḥ kramaiḥ \|\| 209 \|\|*

*balirbaddho hato jaṃbho nihataśca virocanaḥ \|*  
*mahāsurā dvādaśasu saṃgrāmeṣu surairhatāḥ \|\| 210 \|\|*

208a. They stopped after seeing Kāvya, and the gods killed them without any fear.

208b-210. Then Kāvya pondering over the beneficial words of Brahman(?) and remembering the former account said to them: “Vāmana snatched the three worlds in three strides; Bali was bound; Jambha was killed; Virocana also was killed. The gods killed the great demons in the twelve battles.

## \|\| 13.211 \|\|

*taistairupāyairbhūyiṣṭhā nihatāstu pradhānataḥ \|*  
*kecicchiṣṭāśca yūyaṃ vai yuddhaṃ nāstīti me matam \|\| 211 \|\|*

211\. With various expedients many prominent demons among them were killed. A few of you have survived; I think this is no war.

## \|\| 13.212 \|\|

*nītayo vo vidhātavyā upāse kālaparyayāt \|*  
*yāsyāmyahaṃ mahādevaṃ maṃtrārthaṃ vijayāvaham \|\| 212 \|\|*

212\. Political wisdom must be employed by you. I shall stand by you till the times change. I shall go to Mahādeva for (obtaining) a chant that would bring victory to you.

## \|\| 13.213 \|\|

*apratīpāṃstato devānmaṃtrānprāpya maheśvarāt \|*  
*yotsyāmahe punardevaistataḥ prāpsyatha vai jayam \|\| 213 \|\|*

213\. Getting from god Maheśvara chants favourable to us we shall again fight with gods; then we shall get victory.”

## \|\| 13.214 \|\|

*tataste kṛtasaṃvādā devānūcustadāsurāḥ \|*  
*nyastaśastrā vayaṃ sarve niḥssannāhā rathairvinā \|\| 214 \|\|*

214\. Having agreed (having conversed among themselves) the demons said to gods: “All of us have put down our weapons; we are without armours and chariots.

## \|\| 13.215 \|\|

*vayaṃ tapaścariṣyāmaḥ saṃvṛtā valkalaistathā \|*  
*devāsteṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā satyābhivyāhṛtaṃ tataḥ \|\| 215 \|\|*

215\. Covered with bark-garments, we shall practise penance.”

## \|\| 13.216 \|\|

*tatonyavartayansarve vijvarā muditāśca te \|*  
*nyastaśastreṣu daityeṣu vinivṛttāstadā surāḥ \|\| 216 \|\|*

216\. Gods having heard their words spoken truthfully, being free from heat and being delighted retired from there. When the demons had laid down their weapons, then the demons also retired.

## \|\| 13.217-218 \|\|

*tatastānabravītkāvya upādhvaṃ tapasi sthitāḥ \|*  
*nirutsiktāstapoyuktāḥ kālaṃ kāryārthasādhakam \|\| 217 \|\|*

*piturāśramasaṃsthā vai māṃ pratīkṣatha dānavāḥ \|*  
*tānuddiśyāsurānkāvyo mahādevaṃ prapadyata \|\| 218 \|\|*

217-218. Then Kāvya said to them: “Being free from pride and endowed with moral virtue pass the time taking care of your bodies. Remaining in the hermitage of Brahmā, wait for me, O demons.” Kāvya approached Brahma for those demons.

## \|\| 13.219 \|\|

*śukra uvāca \|*  
*maṃtrānicchāmyahaṃ deva yena santi bṛhaspatau \|*  
*parābhavāya devānāmasurāṇāṃ jayāya ca \|\| 219 \|\|*

219\. Śukra said: “For the defeat of gods and victory of demons, O god, I want those chants which Bṛhaspati does not have.”

## \|\| 13.220 \|\|

*evamuktobravīddevo vrataṃ tvaṃ cara bhārgava \|*  
*pūrṇaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu kaṇadhūmamadhaḥ śirāḥ \|\| 220 \|\|*

220\. Thus addressed the god said: “O Bhārgava, with your head bent down, you practise the Kaṇadhūma vow for a full thousand years; if you practise it, God bless you, you will obtain the chants.”

## \|\| 13.221-222 \|\|

*yadi pāsyasi bhadraṃ te tato maṃtrānavāpsyasi \|*  
*tatheti samanujñāpya śukrastu bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ \|\| 221 \|\|*

*pādau saṃspṛśya devasya bāḍhamityabravīdvacaḥ \|*  
*vrataṃ carāmyahaṃ deva tvayādiṣṭodya vai prabho \|\| 222 \|\|*

221-222. Saying “all right” Śukra, son of Bhṛgu, being permitted by Brahmā and touching the feet of the lord said, “Yes sir, I shall, as ordered by you, practise the vow.”

## \|\| 13.223 \|\|

*ādiṣṭo devadevena kṛtavānbhārgavo muniḥ \|*  
*tadā tasmingate śukre asurāṇāṃ hitāya vai \|\| 223 \|\|*

223.-225. As ordered by the god of gods, sage Bhārgava did (as he was told). Then when that Śukra went for the good of the demons he observed celibacy to get the chants from Maheśvara. Then knowing that joy of them due to political wisdom, at this vulnerable point gods furnished with armours and weapons and led by Bṛhaspati, vehemently attacked them.

## \|\| 13.226 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā suragaṇā devānpragṛhītāyudhānpunaḥ \|*  
*utpetussahasā sarve saṃtrastāstānvacobruvat \|\| 226 \|\|*

226\. Seeing the groups of gods holding weapons all demons getting frightened, emerged into view and said to them (these) words:

## \|\| 13.227 \|\|

*daityā ūcuḥ \|*  
*nyastaśastrā vayaṃ devā ācārye vratamāsthite \|*  
*datvā bhavaṃtastvabhayaṃ saṃprāptā no jighāṃsayā \|\| 227 \|\|*

227\. “O gods, while our preceptor is practising a vow we have laid down our weapons. Having promised us security you have now approached us with a desire to kill us.

## \|\| 13.228 \|\|

*anamarṣā vayaṃ sarve tyaktaśastrāśca saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*cīrakṛṣṇājinadharā niṣkriyā niṣparigrahāḥ \|\| 228 \|\|*

228\. We all are free from jealousy and have remained (here) with our arms laid down. Clothed in rags and deer-skins we have remained inactive and possessionless.

## \|\| 13.229 \|\|

*raṇe vijetuṃ devāṃśca na śakṣyāmaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*ayuddhena prapatsyāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ kāvyamātaram \|\| 229 \|\|*

229\. In no way we are able to conquer gods in a battle.” (To one another they said:) “We shall surrender to Kāvya’s mother without (waging) war.

## \|\| 13.230 \|\|

*jñāpayāmaḥ kṛcchramidaṃ yāvannābhyeti no guruḥ \|*  
*nivṛtte ca tathā śukre yotsyāmo daṃśitāyudhāḥ \|\| 230 \|\|*

230\. (And) we shall acquaint her with this misery until our preceptor returns. When Śukra returns we, furnished with armours and arms, shall fight (with gods).”

## \|\| 13.231 \|\|

*evamuktvā ca tenyonyaṃ śaraṇaṃ kāvyamātaram \|*  
*prāpadyaṃta tato bhītāstebhyo'dādabhayaṃ tu sā \|\| 231 \|\|*

231\. Speaking thus to one another, they who were frightened, took the shelter of Kāvya’s mother. She too granted them security.

## \|\| 13.232 \|\|

*na bhetavyaṃ na bhetavyaṃ bhayaṃ tyajata dānavāḥ \|*  
*matsannidhau varttatāṃ vo na bhīrbhaviturmahati \|\| 232 \|\|*

232\. “Do not be afraid; give up your fear, O demons. Remain with me; (then) you will have no fear.”

## \|\| 13.233 \|\|

*tayābhirakṣitāṃstāṃśca dṛṣṭvā devāstadā'surān \|*  
*abhijagmuḥ prasahyaitānavicārya balābalam \|\| 233 \|\|*

233\. Gods then seeing the demons protected by her, and without judging their strength or weakness forcibly assailed them.

## \|\| 13.234 \|\|

*tatastānbadhyamānāṃstu devairdṛṣṭvāsurāṃstadā \|*  
*devī kruddhābravīddevānnidrayā mohayāmyaham \|\| 234 \|\|*

234\. Then that goddess (i.e. Kāvya’s mother) feeing the demons being murdered by gods, got angry and said to the gods: “I shall stupefy you with sleep.”

## \|\| 13.235 \|\|

*saṃbhṛtya sarvasaṃbhārānnidrāṃ sā vyasṛjattadā \|*  
*tastaṃbha devī ca balādyogayuktā tapodhanā \|\| 235 \|\|*

235\. Collecting all materials she then brought about sleep (to the gods); she rich in penance and endowed with meditation stupefied (them) with her power.

## \|\| 13.236 \|\|

*tatastaṃ stabhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā indraṃ devāśca mūḍhavat \|*  
*prādravaṃta tato bhītā indraṃ dṛṣṭvā vaśīkṛtam \|\| 236 \|\|*

236\. Then seeing Indra paralysed (by Kāvya’s mother) the army of gods fled. The gods, seeing Indra subdued, ran through fear.

## \|\| 13.237 \|\|

*gateṣu surasaṃgheṣu viṣṇuriṃdramabhāṣata \|*  
*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*māṃ tvaṃ praviśa bhadraṃ te rakṣiṣye tvāṃ surottama \|\| 237 \|\|*

237\. When the hosts of gods had fled, Viṣṇu said to Indra, “Enter me, God bless you, O best of gods, I shall protect you.”

## \|\| 13.238 \|\|

*evamuktastato viṣṇuṃ praviveśa puraṃdaraḥ \|*  
*viṣṇusaṃrakṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā devī kruddhā vaco'bravīt \|\| 238 \|\|*

238\. Indra, thus ad dressed, entered Viṣṇu. Seeing him protected by Viṣṇu the enraged goddess said (these) words:

## \|\| 13.239 \|\|

*eṣa tvāṃ viṣṇunā sārdhaṃ dahāmi maghavanbalāt \|*  
*miṣatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dṛśyatāṃ me tapobalam \|\| 239 \|\|*

239\. “O Indra, I shall now with force burn you along with Viṣṇu, when all the beings are looking on; see the might of my penance!”

## \|\| 13.240 \|\|

*tayābhibhūtau tau devāviṃdraviṣṇū babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ mucyeya sahito viṣṇuriṃdramabhāṣata \|\| 240 \|\|*

240\. The two gods, Indra and Viṣṇu, were overpowered by her. Viṣṇu said to Indra: “How should I get free with you?”

## \|\| 13.241 \|\|

*iṃdrobravījjahi hyenāṃ yāvannau na dahetprabho \|*  
*viśeṣeṇābhibhūtosmi jahīmāṃ jahi mā ciram \|\| 241 \|\|*

241\. Indra said: “Kill her as long as she does not burn us, O lord; I am especially subdued by her; kill her; do not delay.”

## \|\| 13.242 \|\|

*tataḥ samīkṣya viṣṇustāṃstrīvadhe kṛcchramāsthitaḥ \|*  
*abhidhyāya tataḥ śakramāpannaṃ satvaraṃ prabhuḥ \|\| 242 \|\|*

242\. Then observing her, Viṣṇu determined to do the evil deed of killing a woman (?) and the lord quickly approached the distressed Indra.

## \|\| 13.243-244 \|\|

*tataḥ sa tvarayāyuktaḥ śīghrakārī bhayānvitaḥ \|*  
*jñātvā viṣṇustatastasyāḥ krūraṃ devyāścikīrṣitam \|\| 243 \|\|*

*kruddhaśca cakramādāya śiraściccheda vai bhayāt \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā strīvadhaṃ ghoraṃ cukrodha bhṛgurīśvaraḥ \|\| 244 \|\|*

243-244. Then Viṣṇu, struck with fear and moving with speed, and knowing the cruel act desired to be done by the goddess got angry, took his disc and through dread cut off her head. Seeing that dreadful murder of the woman Lord Bhṛgu got angry.

## \|\| 13.245-246 \|\|

*tato hi śapto bhṛguṇā viṣṇurbhāryāvadhe kṛte \|*  
*bhṛguruvāca \|*  
*yattvayā jānatā dharmamavadhyā strī niṣūditā \|\| 245 \|\|*

*tasmāttvaṃ saptakṛtvo hi mānuṣeṣūpayāsyasi \|*  
*tatastenābhiśāpena naṣṭe dharme punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 246 \|\|*

245-246. Then Viṣṇu was cursed by Bhṛgu for his wife's murder.

## \|\| 13.247 \|\|

*lokasya ca hitārthāya jāyate mānuṣeṣviha \|*  
*atha vyāhṛtya viṣṇuṃ sa tadādāya śiraḥ svayam \|\| 247 \|\|*

Bhṛgu said:

Since you, knowing Dharma, have killed a lady who should not have been killed, therefore you will be born among human beings seven times.

247\. Then due to that curse he is repeatedly born among human beings for the well-being of the world, when Dharma disappears from it. Then, after having spoken to Viṣṇu, himself bringing the head, and bringing her body and holding (the head and the body) in his hand he said:

## \|\| 13.248 \|\|

*samānīya tataḥ kāyaṃ pāṇau gṛhyedamabravīt \|*  
*bhṛguruvāca \|*  
*eṣā tvaṃ viṣṇunā devi hatā saṃjīvayāmyahaṃ \|\| 248 \|\|*

248\. “O goddess, I am reviving you, who were killed by Viṣṇu. If I know the entire sacred law or have practised it, and if I am telling the truth, (forsooth) come back to life.”

## \|\| 13.249 \|\|

*yadi kṛtsno mayā dharmo jñāyate caritopi vā \|*  
*tena satyena jīvasva yadi satyaṃ bravīmyaham \|\| 249 \|\|*

249\. Then having sprinkled her with cold water, he said: “Come back to life, come back to life.”

## \|\| 13.250 \|\|

*tatastāṃ prokṣya śītādbhirjīvajīveti sobravīt \|*  
*tatobhivyāhṛte tasmindevī saṃjīvitā tadā \|\| 250 \|\|*

250\. When he spoke (thus) the goddess came back to life.

## \|\| 13.251 \|\|

*tatastāṃ sarvabhūtāni dṛṣṭvā suptotthitāmiva \|*  
*sādhusādhviti dṛṣṭvaiva vacastāṃ sarvatobruvan \|\| 251 \|\|*

251\. Then all the beings having seen her as if awakened from sleep, uttered the words ‘good! good!’ from all sides.

## \|\| 13.252 \|\|

*evaṃ pratyāhṛtā tena devī sā bhṛguṇā tadā \|*  
*miṣatāṃ daivatānāṃ hi tadadbhutamivābhavat \|\| 252 \|\|*

252\. Thus that Bhṛgu then brought back to life that respectable lady. While the gods were watching that wonderful thing took place.

## \|\| 13.253 \|\|

*asaṃbhrāṃtena bhṛguṇā patnī saṃjīvitā punaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ceṃdro nālabhata śarma kāvyabhayātpunaḥ \|\| 253 \|\|*

253\. Unperplexed Bhṛgu again brought back to life his wife; but seeing it, Indra, through fear of Kāvya, did not get happiness.

## \|\| 13.254 \|\|

*prajāgare tataśceṃdro jayaṃtīmidamabravīt \|*  
*saṃdhikāmobhyadhādvākyaṃ svāṃ kanyāṃ pākaśāsanaḥ \|\| 254 \|\|*

254\. Then after lying awake at night (i.e. sleepless) Indra, desiring peace said (these) words to his daughter, Jayanti:

## \|\| 13.255 \|\|

*indra uvāca \|*  
*eṣa kāvyo hyaniṃdrāya vrataṃ carati dāruṇam \|*  
*tenāhaṃ vyākulaḥ putri kṛto matimatā dṛḍham \|\| 255 \|\|*

255\. “This Kāvya is observing a terrible vow to destroy Indra (i.e. me). O daughter, he, the intelligent one, has very much frightened me.

## \|\| 13.256 \|\|

*taistairmanonukūlaiśca upacārairataṃdritā \|*  
*ārādhaya tathā putri yathā tuṣyeta sa dvijaḥ \|\| 256 \|\|*

256\. O daughter, propitiate him with service pleasing to his mind in such a way that the brāhmaṇa would be pleased.

## \|\| 13.257-259 \|\|

*gaccha tvaṃ tasya dattāsi prayatnaṃ kuru matkṛte \|*  
*evamuktā jayaṃtī sā vacaḥ saṃgṛhya vai pituḥ \|\| 257 \|\|*

*agacchadyatra ghoraṃ sa tapo hyārabhya tiṣṭhati \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca pibaṃtaṃ sā kaṇadhūmamadhomukham \|\| 258 \|\|*

*yakṣeṇa pātyamānaṃ ca kuṃḍadhāreṇa pāvanam \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā taṃ yatamānaṃ tu devī kāvyamavasthitam \|\| 259 \|\|*

257-259. Go to him; I have given you to him; make an effort for me.”

Comprehending well the words of her father, Jayantī went to that place where he remained after having undertaken the terrible vow. Seeing him with his face bent down, drinking the particles of smoke, dropped by a Yakṣa from a dripping bowl, seeing Kāvya who remained (there) trying and striving for the destruction of his enemies, reduced to a weak condition, she acted with Kāvya as she was told by her father.

## \|\| 13.260-263 \|\|

*śatrūpaghāte śrāmyaṃntaṃ durbalasthitimāsthitam \|*  
*pitrā yathoktaṃ vākyaṃ sā kāvye kṛtavatī tadā \|\| 260 \|\|*

*gīrbhiścaivānukūlābhiḥ stuvaṃtī valgubhāṣiṇī \|*  
*gātrasaṃvāhanaiḥ kāle sevamānā tvacaḥ sukhaiḥ \|\| 261 \|\|*

*vratacaryānukūlābhirupāsya bahulāḥ samāḥ \|*  
*pūrṇe dhūmavrate tasminghore varṣasahasrake \|\| 262 \|\|*

*vareṇa chaṃdayāmāsa śivaḥ prītobhavattadā \|*  
*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*etadvrataṃ tvayaikena cīrṇaṃ nānyena kenacit \|\| 263 \|\|*

260-263. The sweet-speaking girl praised him with agreeable eulogies. At the (proper) time she gently rubbed his limbs which soothed the skin and in keeping with the practice of the vow served him for many years. When that terrible vow (called Kaṇa-) Dhūma was over after a thousand years, Śiva being pleased granted him a boon. Maheśvara said: “You alone have observed this vow; none else has observed it.

## \|\| 13.264 \|\|

*tasmādvai tapasā buddhyā śrutena ca balena ca \|*  
*tejasā ca surānsarvāṃstvamekobhibhaviṣyasi \|\| 264 \|\|*

264\. Therefore, by your penance, intellect, knowledge and might and brilliance you (all) alone will overcome all gods.

## \|\| 13.265 \|\|

*yacca kiṃcinmayi brahmanvidyate bhṛgunaṃdana \|*  
*pratidāsyāmi tatsarvaṃ tvayā vācyaṃ na kasyacit \|\| 265 \|\|*

265\. O son of Bhṛgu, I shall give you all that I have; do not disclose it to anyone. What is the use of talking much? You will be immune to death.”

## \|\| 13.266 \|\|

*kiṃ bhāṣitena bahunā avadhyastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi \|*  
*tāndatvā tu varāṃstasmai bhārgavāya punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 266 \|\|*
