266\. Having granted those boons to Bhārgava, he also granted him the lordship of beings, ofwealth and immunity from death.

## \|\| 13.267 \|\|

*prajeśatvaṃ dhaneśatvamavadhyatvaṃ ca vai dadau \|*  
*etānlabdhvā varānkāvyaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ \|\| 267 \|\|*

267\. Kāvya, receiving these boons was happy with his hair standing on end.

## \|\| 13.268 \|\|

*evamābhāṣya deveśamīśvaraṃ nīlalohitam \|*  
*prajñānvitastatastasmai prāñjali praṇato 'bhavat \|\| 268 \|\|*

268\. Speaking thus to lord Śiva, the god of gods, Śukra, endowed with intelligence, joining his palms bent down before him.

## \|\| 13.269 \|\|

*tataḥ soṃ'tarhite deve jayaṃtīmidamabravīt \|*  
*kasya tvaṃ subhage kā vā duḥkhite mayi duḥkhitā \|\| 269 \|\|*

269\. Then, when god (Śiva) vanished, he said this (i.e. these words) to Jayantī: “O auspicious one, whom do you belong to? Who are you that you are afflicted when I am distressed?

## \|\| 13.270 \|\|

*mahatā tapasā yuktā kimarthaṃ māṃ jigīṣasi \|*  
*anayā saṃsthitā bhaktyā praśrayeṇa damena ca \|\| 270 \|\|*

270\. Why do you, endowed with great penance, want to win me over? You have remained (here) with this (i.e. such) devotion, respect and restraint and affection; O you, charming lady of attractive hips, I am pleased with you.

## \|\| 13.271-272 \|\|

*snehena caiva suśroṇi prītosmi varavarṇini \|*  
*kimicchasi varārohe kaste kāmaḥ samudyataḥ \|\| 271 \|\|*

*taṃ te saṃpādayāmyadya yadyapi syātsuduṣkaram \|*  
*evamuktābravīdenaṃ tapasā jñātumarhasi \|\| 272 \|\|*

271-272. O you beautiful lady, what do you desire? What wish was arisen (in your mind)? I shall fulfil it even though it is difficult to accomplish.”

Thus addressed, she said to him: “By means of your penance you can know, O brāhmaṇa, what I desire you to do for me. (Now) tell me precisely (what you would do).”

## \|\| 13.273 \|\|

*cikīrṣitaṃ hi me brahmaṃstvaṃ vai vada yathātatham \|*  
*evamuktobravīdenaṃ dṛṣṭvā divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 273 \|\|*

273\. Thus addressed, he, looking at her with a divine eye, said to her:

## \|\| 13.274 \|\|

*mayā saha tvaṃ suśroṇi śatavarṣāṇi bhāmini \|*  
*sarvabhūtairadṛśyāṃtaḥ saṃprayogamihecchasi \|\| 274 \|\|*

274\. “O beautiful young lady, unseen by all beings you desire a union with me for a thousand years.

## \|\| 13.275 \|\|

*devi iṃdīvaraśyāme varārhe vāmalocane \|*  
*evaṃ vṛṇoṣi kāmāṃstvaṃ dade vai valgubhāṣite \|\| 275 \|\|*

275\. O respectable young divine lady, charming like the blue lotus, having beautiful eyes, and sweet-speaking thus you choose enjoyments.

## \|\| 13.276-277 \|\|

*evaṃ bhavatu gacchāva gṛhaṃ me mattakāśini \|*  
*tataḥ sa gṛhamāgamya jayaṃtyā saha cośanā \|\| 276 \|\|*

*tayā sahāvasaddevyā śatavarṣāṇi bhārgavaḥ \|*  
*adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ māyayā saṃśitavrataḥ \|\| 277 \|\|*

276-277. Let it be so; O you very beautiful and fascinating lady; we shall go to (my) house.”

Then having come to his house with Jayantī, Uśanas the son of Bhṛgu who had fulfilled his vow, lived for a hundred years unseen by all beings with that respectable lady.

## \|\| 13.278 \|\|

*kṛtārthamāgataṃ jñātvā śukraṃ sarve ditessutāḥ \|*  
*abhijagmurgṛhaṃ tasya muditāste didṛkṣavaḥ \|\| 278 \|\|*

278\. All the sons of Diti, having come to know that Śukra had returned after having gained his object, being delighted went to his house to see him.

## \|\| 13.279 \|\|

*gatā yadā na paśyaṃti māyayā saṃvṛtaṃ gurum \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃ tasya cābuddhvā nādyāgacchati no guruḥ \|\| 279 \|\|*

279\. When, after having gone there they did not see their preceptor who had concealed himself by his magical power, and not seeing any sign of his (having returned), they (concluded), ‘Our preceptor has not yet come’.

## \|\| 13.280 \|\|

*evaṃ te svāni dhiṣṇyāni gatāḥ sarve yathāgatāḥ \|*  
*tato devagaṇāssarve gatvāṃgirasamabruvan \|\| 280 \|\|*

280\. And so they went to their abodes as they had come. Then all the hosts of gods having gone to Aṅgiras, said to him:

## \|\| 13.281 \|\|

*dānavālaye tu bhagavāngatvā tatra ca tāṃ camūm \|*  
*mohayitvātmavaśagāṃ kṣiprameva tathā kuru \|\| 281 \|\|*

281\. “You, the revered one, go to the residence of the demons, and after stupefying their army, quickly bring it under your control.”

## \|\| 13.282 \|\|

*dhiṣaṇastānsurānāha evameva vrajāmyaham \|*  
*tena gatvā dānaveṃdraḥ prahlādo vai vaśīkṛtaḥ \|\| 282 \|\|*

282\. Bṛhaspati said to those gods: “Just so, (just now) I go.” Having gone (there) he subjugated Prahrāda, the lord of demons.

## \|\| 13.283 \|\|

*śukro bhūtvā sthitastatra paurohityaṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*sthito varṣaśataṃ sāgramuśanā tāvadāgataḥ \|\| 283 \|\|*

283\. Transforming himself into Śukra, he worked there as (their) priest. He stayed there for a full hundred years, when Uśanas came back.

## \|\| 13.284-285 \|\|

*danuputraistato dṛṣṭaḥ sabhāyāṃ tu bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*uśanā eka evātra dvitīyaḥ kimihāgataḥ \|\| 284 \|\|*

*sumahatkautukaṃ cātra bhavitā vigraho dṛḍham \|*  
*kiṃ vadiṣyati lokoyaṃ dvāri yoyaṃ vyavasthitaḥ \|\| 285 \|\|*

284-285. The demons saw Bṛhaspati in the assembly. “Here there is (already) one Uśanas. Why has the other one come here? It is a great wonder; a great quarrel will ensue (now); what will people say (about) this one who is seated at the door?

## \|\| 13.286 \|\|

*sabhāyāmāsthito yoyaṃ guruḥ kiṃ no vadiṣyati \|*  
*evaṃ prajalpatāṃ teṣāṃ danūnāṃ kavirāgataḥ \|\| 286 \|\|*

286\. (And) what will our preceptor, seated in the assembly say to us?” When the demons were speaking like this, Kavi came (there).

## \|\| 13.287 \|\|

*svarūpadhāriṇaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvāsīnaṃ bṛhaspatim \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ kruddhaḥ kimarthaṃ tvamihāgataḥ \|\| 287 \|\|*

287\. Seeing there Bṛhaspati who had taken his form and who was seated there, he, being angry said (these) words: “Why have you come here?

## \|\| 13.288-289 \|\|

*śiṣyānmohayase me tvaṃ yuktaṃ suragurostava \|*  
*mūḍhāste tvāṃ na jānaṃti tvanmāyāmohitā dhruvam \|\| 288 \|\|*

*tanna yuktaṃ tava brahmanparaśiṣyapradharṣaṇam \|*  
*vraja tvaṃ devalokaṃ svaṃ tiṣṭha dharmamavāpsyasi \|\| 289 \|\|*

288-289. You are confusing my disciples. Is it proper for you (who are) the preceptor of gods? Being certainly stupefied by your trickery, the ignorant ones do not recognise you. So, O brāhmaṇa, it is not proper for you thus to ill-treat another’s disciples.

Go to the abode of gods (and) stay (there). Thus (i.e. by doing so) you will obtain religious merit.

## \|\| 13.290 \|\|

*śiṣyo hi me kacaḥ pūrvaṃ hato dānavapuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*vidyārthī tanayo brahmaṃstavāyogyā gatistviha \|\| 290 \|\|*

290\. O brāhmaṇa, formerly the best of the demons had

killed your son and pupil Kaca who had come here as a student. (So) your entrance here is improper.”

## \|\| 13.291-293 \|\|

*śrutvā tu tasya tadvākyaṃ smitaṃ kṛtvāvadadguruḥ \|*  
*saṃti corāḥ pṛthivyāṃ yeparadravyāpahāriṇaḥ \|\| 291 \|\|*

*evaṃ vidhānadṛṣṭāśca rūpadehāpahāriṇaḥ \|*  
*vṛtraghātena ceṃdrasya brahmahahatyā purābhavat \|\| 292 \|\|*

*lokāyatika śāstreṇa bhavatā sā tiraskṛtā \|*  
*jānāmi tvāmāṃgirasaṃ devācāryaṃ bṛhaspatim \|\| 293 \|\|*

291-293. Hearing those words of him, and smiling, Bṛhaspati said: “There are thieves on the earth, who snatch away others’ wealth; (but) such thieves (like you as) takeaway another’s appearance and body, were not seen. Formerly, Indra by killing Vṛtra committed a brāhmaṇa’s murder. You have surpassed it by (i.e. by teaching) the science of the materialists (like Cārvāka). I know you to be Āṅgirasa Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of gods.

## \|\| 13.294 \|\|

*madrūpadhāriṇaṃ prāptaṃ sarve paśyata dānavāḥ \|*  
*eṣa vo mohanāyālaṃ prāpto viṣṇuviceṣṭitaiḥ \|\| 294 \|\|*

294\. O demons, all you observe (him) who has come (here after) taking my form. Through the efforts of Viṣṇu he, capable of infatuating you, has come here.

## \|\| 13.295 \|\|

*tadenaṃ śṛṃkhalairbaddhvā kṣipeta lavaṇārṇave \|*  
*punarevābravīcchukraḥ purodhāyaṃ divaukasām \|\| 295 \|\|*

295\. So binding him with chains you should throw him into the salt ocean.”

## \|\| 13.296 \|\|

*mohitānūnametena kṣayaṃ yāsyatha dānavāḥ \|*  
*bho ahaṃ dānaveṃdreha vaṃcito'smi durātmanā \|\| 296 \|\|*

296\. And again Śukra said: “He is the priest of gods. Stupefied by him, you will perish, O demons. O lord of demons, this wicked one has deceived me.

## \|\| 13.297 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ bhavatā tyaktaḥ kṛtaścānyaḥ purohitaḥ \|*  
*devācāryaoṃgiraḥputraeṣaevabṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 297 \|\|*

297\. Why did you leave me and take up another priest? This is Bṛhaspati only, the preceptor of gods and the son of Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 13.298 \|\|

*vaṃcitosi na saṃdeho hitārthaṃ tu divaukasām \|*  
*tyajasvainaṃ mahābhāga śatrupakṣajayāvaham \|\| 298 \|\|*

298\. You have been deceived in the interest of gods. There is no doubt (about) it. O magnanimous one, forsake him who would bring victory to the enemies.

## \|\| 13.299 \|\|

*anuśiṣyabhayādyātaḥ pūrvamevamahaṃ prabho \|*  
*jalamadhyesthitaḥ pīto mahādevena śaṃbhunā \|\| 299 \|\|*

299\. O lord, through anxiety about my disciples formerly only I went from here and remained in water. I was drunk by the great god Śambhu.

## \|\| 13.300-301 \|\|

*udarasthasya me jātaṃ sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ kila \|*  
*udarācchukrarūpeṇa śiśnenāhaṃ visarjitaḥ \|\| 300 \|\|*

*varadaḥ prāha māṃ devaśśukreṣṭaṃ tvaṃ varaṃ vṛṇu \|*  
*mayāvṛto varaṃ rājandevadevaḥ pinākadhṛt \|\| 301 \|\|*

300-301. I indeed passed a complete hundred years in his belly. I was discharged by him in the form of (his) semen through his generative organ. The god, granter of boons said to me; ‘Śukra, choose a boon liked by you.’ O king, I chose a boon from the god of gods, the trident-holder.

## \|\| 13.302 \|\|

*manasā ciṃtitā hyarthā mānase ye sthitā varāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃtu mayi te sarve prasādāttava śaṃkara \|\| 302 \|\|*

302\. ‘O Śaṅkara, let all the objects entertained by my mind and desires residing in my mind be (fulfilled) through your favour.’

## \|\| 13.303-305 \|\|

*evamastviti devena preṣito'smi tavāṃtikam \|*  
*tāvadatrābhavaccāyaṃ purodhāste bṛhaspatiḥ \|\| 303 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭaḥ satyaṃ dānaveṃdra mayoktaṃ tvaṃ niśāmaya \|*  
*bṛhaspatistadā vākyaṃ prahlādaṃ pratyabhāṣata \|\| 304 \|\|*

*nāhametaṃ prajānāmi devaṃ vā dānavaṃ naram \|*  
*madrūpadhāriṇaṃ rājanvaṃcanārthaṃ tavāgatam \|\| 305 \|\|*

303-305. Saying ‘Let it be so’ the god sent me to you; (but) thus by the time (I returned) I actually saw this Bṛhaspati to have become your priest. O lord of demons, listen to my words.” Bṛhaspati again said these words to Prahrāda: “I do not recognise him as to whether he is a god or a demon or a human being; he has, after assuming my form, come here to deceive you, O king.”

## \|\| 13.306 \|\|

*tataste dānavāḥ sarve sādhusādhviti vādinaḥ \|*  
*purodhāḥ paurviko nostu yo vā ko vā bhavatviti \|\| 306 \|\|*

306\. Then all the demons said: “Well-said; we would have the former priest; whosoever he may be; we have nothing to do with this (later); let him go as he has come!”

## \|\| 13.307-308 \|\|

*nānena kāryamasmākaṃ yā tu hyeṣa yathāgataḥ \|*  
*sakrodhamaśapatkāvyo dānaveṃdrānsamāgatān \|\| 307 \|\|*

*tyakto yathāhaṃ yuṣmābhistathā sarvāṃścirādiva \|*  
*gataśrīkāngataprāṇānpaśyeyaṃ duḥkhajīvikān \|\| 308 \|\|*

307-308. Kāvya angrily cursed all the lords of demons that had gathered there: “Since you have abandoned me, I shall see all of you void of wealth, dead (or) leading a miserable life for a long time.

## \|\| 13.309 \|\|

*sughorāmāpadaṃ prāptānacirādeva sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā gataḥ kāvyo yadṛcchātastapovanam \|\| 309 \|\|*

309\. And by all means an extremely terrible calamity will very soon befall you.”

Speaking thus Kāvya at his will went to a penance-grove.

## \|\| 13.310 \|\|

*tasmingate tataḥ śukre sthitastatra bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*pālayandānavāṃstatra kiṃcitkālamatiṣṭhata \|\| 310 \|\|*

310\. When that Śukra had (thus) left, Bṛhaspati remained there for some time, looking after the demons.

## \|\| 13.311-312 \|\|

*tato bahutithe kāle atikrāṃte nareśvara \|*  
*saṃbhūya dānavāḥ sarve paryapṛchaṃstadā gurum \|\| 311 \|\|*

*saṃsāresminnasāre tu kiṃcijjñānaṃ prayaccha naḥ \|*  
*yena mokṣaṃ vrajāmaśca prasādāttava suvrata \|\| 312 \|\|*

311-312. O King, then when a long time elapsed, all the demons collecting together asked Bṛhaspati: “Give us some knowledge (useful) in this worthless worldly life, by which we shall obtain release through your favour, O you of good vow.”

## \|\| 13.313-314 \|\|

*tataḥ suraguruḥ prāha kāvyarūpī tadā guruḥ \|*  
*mamāpyeṣā matiḥ pūrvaṃ yā yuṣmābhirudāhṛtā \|\| 313 \|\|*

*kṣaṇaṃ kurvaṃtu sahitāśśucībhūya samāhitāḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ vakṣyāmi vo daityā ahaṃ vai mokṣadāyi yat \|\| 314 \|\|*

313-314. Then Guru, the preceptor of gods, who had then assumed the form of Kāvya said: “I had already the same idea as expressed by you (now); so together you, being composed and pure, find leisure (so that), O demons, I shall tell you that knowledge which will give you release.

## \|\| 13.315 \|\|

*eṣā śrutirvaidikī yā ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitā \|*  
*vaiśvānaraprasādāttu duḥkhadā prāṇināmiha \|\| 315 \|\|*

315\. That knowledge called Ṛg(veda), Yajur(veda) and Sāma(veda) is Vaidika (knowledge); and is due to the favour of Vaiśvānara (the Supreme Being) but it causes grief to the beings in this world.

## \|\| 13.316-318 \|\|

*yajñaśrāddhaṃ kṛtaṃ kṣudrairaihikasvārthatatparaiḥ \|*  
*ye tvamī vaiṣṇavā dharmā ye ca rudrakṛtāstathā \|\| 316 \|\|*

*kudharmā dārasahitairhiṃsāprāyāḥ kṛtāhitaiḥ \|*  
*arddhanārīśvaro rudra kathaṃ mokṣaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 317 \|\|*

*vṛto bhūtagaṇairbhūribhūṣitaścāsthibhistathā \|*  
*na svargo naiva mokṣotra lokāḥ kliśyaṃti vai tathā \|\| 318 \|\|*

316-318. The mean, intent upon material self-aggrandisement, perform sacrifices and Śrāddhas. These unkind ones along with their wives follow the bad practices—practices laid down by Viṣṇu and by Rudra. How will Rudra, whose form is half male and half female, who is surrounded by hosts of goblins and is adorned with bones give release (to a person)? There is neither heaven nor release; people are afficted here.

## \|\| 13.319 \|\|

*hiṃsāyāmāsthito viṣṇuḥ kathaṃ mokṣaṃ gamiṣyati \|*  
*rajoguṇātmako brahmā svāṃ sṛṣṭimupajīvati \|\| 319 \|\|*

319\. How will Viṣṇu, practising violence, lead one to release? Brahma of the nature of Rajas subsists on his own progeny.

## \|\| 13.320-321 \|\|

*devarṣayotha ye cānye vaidikaṃ pakṣamāśritāḥ \|*  
*hiṃsāprāyāḥ sadā krūrā māṃsādāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 320 \|\|*

*surāstu madyapānena māṃsādā brāhmaṇāstvamī \|*  
*dharmeṇānena kaḥ svargaṃ kathaṃ mokṣaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 321 \|\|*

320-321. The others i.e. the divine sages, who have resorted to the Vedic fold are full of violence, always cruel and eat flesh; the gods also are sinners by virtue of their drinking wine. These brāhmaṇas are flesh-eaters. Who will and how will he, by (practising) such observances go to heaven or (get) release?

## \|\| 13.322 \|\|

*yacca yajñādikaṃ karma smārtaṃ śrāddhādikaṃ tathā \|*  
*tatra naivāpavargosti yatraiṣā śrūyate śrutiḥ \|\| 322 \|\|*

322\. Those religious rites like sacrifice etc. and like Śrāddha recorded in the Smṛtis etc. which the scriptures enjoin to be leading to heaven or release do not do so.

## \|\| 13.323 \|\|

*yajñaṃ kṛtvā paśuṃ hatvā kṛtvā rudhirakardamam \|*  
*yadyevaṃ gamyate svargo narakaḥ kena gamyate \|\| 323 \|\|*

323\. If a person is taken to heaven by performing a sacrifice and causing mire of blood by killing a beast, then what (is it) by which a person is taken to hell?

## \|\| 13.324 \|\|

*yadi bhuktamihānyena tṛptiranyasya jāyate \|*  
*dadyātpravasataḥ śrāddhaṃ na sa bhojanamāharet \|\| 324 \|\|*

324\. If by one’s eating (food), someone else is satisfied then Śrāddha should be offered to one who has gone on a journey; he should not (then) take food (with him).

## \|\| 13.325 \|\|

*ākāśagāmino viprāḥ patitā māṃsabhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*teṣāṃ na vidyate svargo mokṣo naiveha dānavāḥ \|\| 325 \|\|*

325\. O demons, (even) brāhmaṇas moving in the sky, fall by eating flesh; for them there is neither heaven nor release here (i.e. in this system of the Vaidikas).

## \|\| 13.326 \|\|

*jātasya jīvitaṃ jaṃtoriṣṭaṃ sarvasya jāyate \|*  
*ātmamāṃsopamaṃ māṃsaṃ kathaṃ khādeta paṃḍitaḥ \|\| 326 \|\|*

326\. For every being that is born his life becomes dear (to him); how would a wise man eat flesh which is like his own flesh?

## \|\| 13.327 \|\|

*yonijāstu kathaṃ yoniṃ sevaṃte jaṃtavastvamī \|*  
*maithunena kathaṃ svargaṃ yāsyaṃte dānaveśvara \|*  
*mṛdbhasmanā yatraśuddhistatra śuddhistu kā bhavet \|\| 327 \|\|*

327\. How do these (followers of the Vaidika practices) enjoy the female organ (i.e. have copulation) from which they are born? O lord of demons, by copulation how can they go to heaven? What kind of purity is that which is had by means of clay and ashes?

## \|\| 13.328-330 \|\|

*viparītatamaṃ lokaṃ paśya dānava yādṛśam \|*  
*viṇmūtrasya kṛtotsarge śiśnāpāne tu śodhanam \|\| 328 \|\|*

*bhukte vā bhojane rājankathaṃ nāpānaśiśnayoḥ \|\| 329 \|\|*

*kriyate śodhanaṃ tadvadviparītā sthitistviyam \|*  
*yatra prakṣālanaṃ proktaṃ tatra tenaiva kurvate \|\| 330 \|\|*

328-330. O demons, see how very perverse this world (of the Vaidikas) is! After passing urine or after excretion the organ of generation or the anus are cleansed with clay and water, but the same provision is not made in the case of the mouth after eating. Then O king, why are the organ of generation and anus not cleaned in the same way? This state (of things) is perverse (for) they do not do cleansing where (actually) it is enjoined.

## \|\| 13.331 \|\|

*tārāṃ bṛṃhaspaterbhāryāṃ hṛtvā somaḥ purā gataḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ jāto budhaḥ putro gururjagrāha tāṃ punaḥ \|\| 331 \|\|*

331\. Formerly Soma went away after snatching Tārā, Bṛhaspati’s wife. A son Budha was born on her (from Soma); and Guru again accepted her.

## \|\| 13.332 \|\|

*gautamasya muneḥ patnīmahalyāṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*agṛhṇāttāṃ svayaṃ śakraḥ paśya dharmo yathāvidhaḥ \|\| 332 \|\|*

332\. Śakra himself took away Gautama’s wife named Ahalyā; see what kind of religious practice this is!

## \|\| 13.333 \|\|

*etadanyacca jagati dṛśyate pāpadāyakam \|*  
*evaṃvidho yatra dharmaḥ paramārtho matastu kaḥ \|\| 333 \|\|*

333\. This and other things causing sin are seen in this world. When such kind of religious practices exists then tell me, which is said to be the highest good.

## \|\| 13.334 \|\|

*vadasva tvaṃ dānaveṃdra vada bhūyo vadāmi te \|*  
*gurostu gaditaṃ śrutvā paramārthānvitaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 334 \|\|*

334\. O lord of demons, ask me and I shall tell you again.”

## \|\| 13.335-336 \|\|

*jātakautūhalāstatra viviktāstu bhavārṇavāt \|*  
*dānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*dīkṣayasva guro sarvānprapannānbhaktitaḥ sthitān \|\| 335 \|\|*

*yena vai na punarmohaṃ vrajāmastava śāsanāt \|*  
*suviraktāḥ sma saṃsāre śokamohapradāyini \|\| 336 \|\|*

Hearing Bṛhaspati’s words full of truth, the demons with curiosity risen in them and being detached from the worldly existence, said:

335-336. “O preceptor, initiate all of us, who have approached you and are firm in our devotion, so that with your instruction we shall not again be infatuated; we shall remain very much detached in this worldly existence causing grief and infatuation.

## \|\| 13.337 \|\|

*uddharasva guro sarvānkeśākarṣeṇa kūpataḥ \|*  
*kasya devasya śaraṇaṃ gacchāmo brāhmaṇottama \|\| 337 \|\|*

337\. O preceptor, draw us out from the well (of mundane existence) by pulling our hair; O best of brāhmaṇas, which god should we take shelter of?

## \|\| 13.338-339 \|\|

*daivataṃ ca prapannānāṃ prakāśaya mahāmate \|*  
*smaraṇenopavāsena dhyānadhāraṇayā tathā \|\| 338 \|\|*

*pūjopahāre ca kṛte apavargastu labhyate \|*  
*viraktāssma kuṭuṃbe tu bhūyo nātra yatāmahe \|\| 339 \|\|*

338-339. O highly intelligent one, show us who have

approached you, a deity by remembering, serving or meditating on, so also by having worshipped which, release will be obtained (by us). We are displeased with the family, and we won’t strive again here (i.e. to have a family).”

## \|\| 13.340 \|\|

*evaṃ caiva guruśchannastairukto danupuṃgavaiḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa tatkāryaṃ kathametatkaromyaham \|\| 340 \|\|*

340\. When Guru, who was disguised, was thus addressed by the best of the demons, he thought about that undertaking: ‘How shall I bring about this?

## \|\| 13.341 \|\|

*kathamete mayā pāpāḥ kartavyā narakaukasaḥ \|*  
*viḍaṃbanācchruterbāhyāstrailokye hāsyakāriṇaḥ \|\| 341 \|\|*

341\. How can I make them sinners (and consequently) denizens of hell, outcast from the Vedic fold due to their ridiculing it and (therefore) being laughed at in the three worlds?’

## \|\| 13.342-344 \|\|

*ityuktvā dhiṣaṇo rājaṃścintayāmāsa keśavam \|*  
*tasya tacciṃtitaṃ jñātvā māyāmohaṃ janārdanaḥ \|\| 342 \|\|*

*samutpādya dadau tasya prāha cedaṃ bṛhaspatim \|*  
*māyāmohoyamakhilāṃstāndaityānmohayiṣyati \|\| 343 \|\|*

*bhavatā sahitaḥ sarvānvedamārgabahiṣkṛtān \|*  
*evamādiśya bhagavānaṃtarddhānaṃ jagāma ha \|\| 344 \|\|*

342-344. Saying thus (to himself) Bṛhaspati meditated on Keśava (i.e. Viṣṇu). Knowing that meditation of his Janardana created Māyāmoha (i.e. a being who would delude the demons with his tricks) and presented him to Bṛhaspati and said to him: “This Māyāmoha associated with you will infatuate all demons, outcast from the Vedic path.” Having instructed thus the lord disappeared.

## \|\| 13.345 \|\|

*tapasyabhiratānsotha māyāmoho gato'surān \|*  
*teṣāṃ samīpamāgatya bṛhaspatiruvāca ha \|\| 345 \|\|*

345\. That Māyāmoha went to the demons who were engaged in penance. Bṛhaspati approached them and said:

## \|\| 13.346 \|\|

*anugrahārthaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhaktyā prītastvihāgataḥ \|*  
*yogī digambaro muṇḍo barhipatradharo hyayam \|\| 346 \|\|*

346\. “This naked, clean-shaven ascetic holding a peacock’s feather, being pleased with your devotion has come to favour you.”

## \|\| 13.347-349 \|\|

*ityukte guruṇā paścānmāyāmohobravīdvacaḥ \|*  
*bho bho daityādhipatayaḥ prabrūta tapasi sthitāḥ \|\| 347 \|\|*

*ehikārthaṃ tu pārakyaṃ tapasaḥ phalamicchatha \|*  
*dānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*pārakyadharmalābhāya tapaścaryā hi no matā \|\| 348 \|\|*

*asmābhiriyamārabdhā kiṃ vā tatra vivakṣitam \|*  
*digaṃbara uvāca \|*  
*kurudhvaṃ mama vākyāni yadi muktimabhīpsatha \|\| 349 \|\|*

347-349. After Guru had spoken thus Māyāmoha said (these) words: “O demons, you who are engaged in penance, tell (me) whether you desire as the fruit of your penance something worldly or otherworldly?” The demons replied: “In our opinion performance of penance is for the acquisition of religious merit in the other world; (so) we have started it; what have you to say in this matter?” The naked one (i.e. Māyāmoha) said: “You act according to my words if you desire release.

## \|\| 13.350 \|\|

*ārhataṃ sarvametacca muktidvāramasaṃvṛtam \|*  
*dharmādvimukterarhoyaṃ naitasmādaparaḥ paraḥ \|\| 350 \|\|*

350\. The entire door to release as advised by the Arhat is open. This Ārhata (way) is for release from the (Vedic) path; there is none greater than he.

## \|\| 13.351 \|\|

*atraivāvasthitāḥ svargaṃ muktiṃ cāpi gamiṣyatha \|*  
*evaṃprakārairbahubhirmuktidarśanavarjitaiḥ \|\| 351 \|\|*

351\. Remaining here (i.e. in his fold) only you will reach heaven and release.”

## \|\| 13.352 \|\|

*māyāmohena te daityāḥ vedamārgabahiṣkṛtāḥ \|*  
*dharmāyaitadadharmāya sadetadasadityapi \|\| 352 \|\|*

352\. The demons were taken out of the Vedic path by Māyāmoha (saying) “This leads to merit, this to sin; this is good and this is bad.

## \|\| 13.353 \|\|

*vimuktaye tvidaṃ naitadvimuktiṃ saṃprayacchati \|*  
*paramārthoyamatyarthaṃ paramārtho na cāpyayam \|\| 353 \|\|*

353\. This leads to release, this would not give release; this is the highest truth.

## \|\| 13.354 \|\|

*kāryametadakāryaṃ hi naitadetatsphuṭaṃ tvidam \|*  
*digvāsasāmayaṃ dharmo dharmoyaṃ bahuvāsasām \|\| 354 \|\|*

354\. This ought to be done; this ought not to be done; this is not this (i.e. as it is said to be so); this is clear; this is the practice of the naked, this is that of those who put on many garments.”

## \|\| 13.355 \|\|

*ityanekārthavādāṃstu māyāmohena te yataḥ \|*  
*uktāstato'khilā daityāḥ svadharmāṃstyājitā nṛpa \|\| 355 \|\|*

355\. Thus Māyāmoha told the demons the words of the Arhats, and made them give up their own (old) practices.

## \|\| 13.356 \|\|

*arhadhvaṃ māmakaṃ dharmaṃ māyāmohena te yataḥ \|*  
*uktāstamāśritā dharmamārhatāstena tebhavan \|\| 356 \|\|*

356\. When Māyāmoha told them the words of Arhat, viz. ‘Honour my way of life’, they resorted to him and therefore they became the followers of the Arhats.

## \|\| 13.357-358 \|\|

*trayīmārgaṃ samutsṛjya māyāmohena tesurāḥ \|*  
*kāritāstanmayā hyāsaṃstathānye tatprabodhitāḥ \|\| 357 \|\|*

*tairapyanye pare taiśca tairanyonyaistathāpare \|*  
*namo'rhate ceti sarve saṃgame sthiravādinaḥ \|\| 358 \|\|*

357-358. After they had given up (the path of the) three Vedas Māyāmoha made them wholly absorbed in the Arhat way; others also were instructed by him; they instructed others; these instructed still others; these also still others. ‘Salutation to Arhats’ thus they spoke firmly in their congregation.

## \|\| 13.359 \|\|

*alpairahobhiḥ saṃtyaktā tairdaityaiḥ prāyaśastrayī \|*  
*punaśca raktāṃbaradhṛnmāyāmoho jitekṣaṇaḥ \|\| 359 \|\|*

359\. Within a few days the demons almost gave up (the path of the three) Vedas. Māyāmoha with his senses conquered again became the wearer of red garments.

## \|\| 13.360-361 \|\|

*sonyānapyasurāngatvā ūcenyanmadhurākṣaram \|*  
*svargārthaṃ yadi vo vāñchā nirvāṇārthāya vā punaḥ \|\| 360 \|\|*

*tadalaṃ paśughātādi duṣṭadharmairnibodhata \|*  
*vijñānamayametadvai tvaśeṣamadhigacchata \|\| 361 \|\|*

360-361. He too, going to other demons, spoke sweet words: ‘If you have a desire for (going to) heaven or for release, then enough of the wicked practices like killing the beasts. (Please) understand (it). Know this all to be of the nature of worldly knowledge.

## \|\| 13.362 \|\|

*budhyadhvaṃ me vacaḥ samyagbudhairevamihoditam \|*  
*jagadetadanādhāraṃ bhrāṃtijñānānutatparam \|\| 362 \|\|*

362\. Understand my words properly; they are said by the wise. This world is propless and erroneous knowledge is preeminent in it.

## \|\| 13.363 \|\|

*rāgādiduṣṭamatyarthaṃ bhrāmyate bhavasaṃkaṭe \|*  
*nānāprakāraṃ vacanaṃ sa teṣāṃ muktiyojitam \|\| 363 \|\|*

363\. It is very much defiled by passions like attachment and gets one involved in the peril of rebirth.”

## \|\| 13.364 \|\|

*tathā tathāvadaddharmaṃ tatyajuste yathāyathā \|*  
*kecidviniṃdāṃ vedānāṃ devānāmapare nṛpa \|\| 364 \|\|*

364\. He said manifold words intended for their release in such a manner that they abandoned their (former) practices. O king, some condemned the Vedas, while others condemned gods.

## \|\| 13.365 \|\|

*yajñakarmakalāpasya tathā cānye dvijanmanām \|*  
*naitadyuktisahaṃ vākyaṃ hiṃsā dharmāya jāyate \|\| 365 \|\|*

365\. Others condemned the group of religious practices and others brāhmaṇas. These logical arguments do not lead to the practices involving killing (i.e. are against killing):

## \|\| 13.366-367 \|\|

*havīṃṣyanaladagdhāni phalānyarhaṃti kovidāḥ \|*  
*nihatasya paśoryajñe svargaprāptiryadīṣyate \|\| 366 \|\|*

*svapitā yajamānena kiṃ vā tatra na hanyate \|*  
*tṛptaye jāyate puṃso bhuktamanyena cedyadi \|\| 367 \|\|*

366-367. “O wise ones, if the oblations burnt in fire be come fruitful, or if it is laid down that a beast killed in a sacrifice obtains heaven, then why does the sacrificer not kill his own father there (i.e. in the sacrifice)? If something eaten by one leads to the satisfaction of someone else, then Śrāddha should be offered to those who are travelling and they should not take (provender etc.) with them.

## \|\| 13.368-369 \|\|

*dadyācchrāddhaṃ pravasato na vaheyuḥ pravāsinaḥ \|*  
*yajñairanekairdevatvamavāpyeṃdreṇa bhujyate \|\| 368 \|\|*

*śamyādi yadi cetkāṣṭhaṃ tadvaraṃ patrabhukpaśuḥ \|*  
*janā śraddheyamityetadavagamya tu tadvacaḥ \|\| 369 \|\|*

368-369. After having obtained godhead by performing many sacrifices if wood of Śamī etc. is eaten by Indra then a beast eating leaves is certainly better. Knowing that his words are not to be relied on by men, ignore them, and be pleased (to take) the words uttered by me to be leading to final beatitude.

## \|\| 13.370 \|\|

*upekṣya śreyase vākyaṃ rocatāṃ yanmayeritam \|*  
*na hyāptavādā nabhaso nipataṃti mahāsurāḥ \|\| 370 \|\|*

370\. O great demons, those whose words are authoritative do not fall from the sky.

## \|\| 13.371 \|\|

*yuktimadvacanaṃ grāhyaṃ mayānyaiśca bhavadvidhaiḥ \|*  
*dānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tatvavāde vayaṃ sarve prapannāstava bhaktitaḥ \|\| 371 \|\|*

371\. Words having propriety should be accepted by me and others like you.”

## \|\| 13.372-374 \|\|

*kuruṣvānugrahaṃ cādya prasannosi yadi prabho \|*  
*saṃbhārānāharāmodya dīkṣāyogyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 372 \|\|*

*prasādāttava yenāśu mokṣo hastagato bhavet \|*  
*tatastānabravītsarvānmāyāmohosurāṃstadā \|\| 373 \|\|*

*prapannaḥ śāsanaṃ hyeṣa madīyo gururagryadhīḥ \|*  
*dīkṣāṃ dāsyati yuṣmākaṃ nideśānmama sattamaḥ \|\| 374 \|\|*

The demons said:

372-374. We all are resorting with devotion to this statement of facts made by you. If you are pleased, O lord, favour us today. We shall bring all the material necessary for initiation, by doing which, through your favour release would quickly be obtained by us.

Then Māyāmoha said to all these demons: “This my preceptor of best intellect, has betaken himself to this discipline. The best one will initiate you at my direction: ‘O brāhmaṇa, initiate these sons at my instruction’”.

## \|\| 13.375 \|\|

*etāndīkṣaya bho brahmanvacanānmama putrakān \|*  
*gate mohe dānavāste bhārgavaṃ vākyamabruvan \|\| 375 \|\|*

375\. The demons, when infatuated, said (these) words to Bhārgava:

## \|\| 13.376 \|\|

*dehi dīkṣāṃ mahābhāga sarvasaṃsāramocanīm \|*  
*tathetyāhośanā daityāngacchāmo narmadāmanu \|\| 376 \|\|*

376\. “O magnanimous one, give us initiation, that will free (us) from the entire worldly existence.” Uśanas said to the demons: “All right, let us go to (the river) Narmadā.

## \|\| 13.377 \|\|

*bhobhostyajata vāsāṃsi dīkṣāṃ kārayitāsmi vaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ te dānavā bhīṣma bhṛgurūpeṇa dhīmatā \|\| 377 \|\|*

377\. O you, strip off your garments, I shall initiate you.”

Thus, O Bhīṣma, the intelligent son of Aṅgiras in the form of Bhṛgu made the demons naked.

## \|\| 13.378-379 \|\|

*āṃgirasena te tatra kṛtā digvāsasosurāḥ \|*  
*barhipicchadhvajaṃ teṣāṃ guṃjikā cārumālikāṃ \|\| 378 \|\|*

*datvā cakāra teṣāṃ tu śiraso luṃcanaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*keśasyotpāṭanaṃ caiva paramaṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 379 \|\|*

378-379. And giving them peacock’s feathers, flags, berries of gunja plant, charming garlands, he got their hair plucked, (for) plucking out hair is a great means of (acquiring) religious merit.

## \|\| 13.380 \|\|

*dhanānāmīśvaro devo dhanadaḥ keśaluṃcanāt \|*  
*siddhiṃ paramikāṃ prāptāḥ sadā veṣasya dhāraṇāt \|\| 380 \|\|*

380\. God Kubera became the lord of wealth due to having plucked out his hair. By always remaining dress-less (devotees) obtained great superhuman power.

## \|\| 13.381 \|\|

*nityatvaṃ labhyate hyevaṃ purā prāhārhataḥ svayam \|*  
*vālotpāṭena devatvaṃ mānuṣairlabhyate tviha \|\| 381 \|\|*

381\. Arhat himself has formerly said that in this way (i.e. by following the Arhat-practices) eternity is obtained. Godhead is obtained here (only) by men by plucking out their hair.

## \|\| 13.382-383 \|\|

*kiṃ na kurvīta tattasmānmahāpuṇyapradaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*manoratho hi devānāṃ loke vai mānuṣe kadā \|\| 382 \|\|*

*asminsyādbhārate varṣe janmanaḥ śrāvake kule \|*  
*tapasā yuñjmahesmānvai keśotpāṭanapūrvakam \|\| 383 \|\|*

382-383. Why then not do it since it gives great religious merit? It was a great desire of gods: ‘When would we be born in the family of a layman in Bhārata country and would be endowed with penance after plucking out our hair.’

## \|\| 13.384-385 \|\|

*tīrthaṃkarāścaturviṃśattathā taistu puraskṛtāḥ \|*  
*chāyākṛtaṃ phaṇīṃdreṇa dhyānamārgapradarśakam \|\| 384 \|\|*

*stuvantaṃ maṃtravādena svargo hastagatorhataṃ \|*  
*mokṣo vā bhavitā nūnaṃ vicāraḥ kotra kathyate \|\| 385 \|\|*

384-385. They had adored the twentyfour Tīrthaṅkaras. (For them) Praising with the muttering of incantations the Arhat covered over with the lord of cobras and showing the path of meditation, heaven was (quite) at hand or release would come. Which thought is expressed by them?

## \|\| 13.386-387 \|\|

*kadā syāmarṣayo bhūtvā sūryāgnisamatejasaḥ \|*  
*japtvā virāgiṇaścaivamanupaṃcāṃgakaṃ tathā \|\| 386 \|\|*

*tathā tapasyatāṃ mṛtyuṃ gatānāṃ kālaparyayāt \|*  
*pāṣāṇena śirobhagnaṃ bhavate puṇyakarmaṇām \|\| 387 \|\|*

386-387. (The thought) is: Being similar to the sun and fire in lustre when shall we be sages? When shall we be passionless by (means of) muttering (incantations) and the five modes (of devotion)? For the heads of those religious people practising penance in that way and having met with death are broken with a stone.

## \|\| 13.388 \|\|

*araṇye nirjane vāsaḥkadā vai bhavitā hi naḥ \|*  
*karṇajapyaṃ śrāvakāśca kariṣyaṃti samāhitāḥ \|\| 388 \|\|*

388\. When shall we reside in a solitary forest? (When) will the calm layman mutter secretly into our ears:

## \|\| 13.389-391 \|\|

*bhobho ṛṣe na gaṃtavyaṃ mokṣamārgī yato bhavān \|*  
*labdhāni yāni sthānāni bhūyovṛttikarāṇi ca \|\| 389 \|\|*

*tyājyāni tena caitāni satyameva vaco hi naḥ \|*  
*asmadīyena tapasā niyamairvividhaistathā \|\| 390 \|\|*

*vrajadhvaṃ cottamaṃ sthānaṃ mokṣamārgaṃ ca yaṃ budhāḥ \|*  
*viṃdaṃti bhaktibhāvena tapoyuktāstapasvinaḥ \|\| 391 \|\|*

389-391. ‘O sage, do not go, since you are a traveller on the path to release. Whatever places you have secured cause further activity (and) so they are to be forsaken—these words of ours are true. By means of our penance and various restraints go to the best place and along that path of release which the wise ones, being endowed with penance obtain by means of devotion’.

## \|\| 13.392 \|\|

*akṣeṣu nigraho yatra dayābhūteṣu sarvadā \|*  
*tattapodharmamityuktaṃ sarvā cānyā viḍaṃbanā \|\| 392 \|\|*

392\. That is said to be the practice of penance where there is the restraint of senses and compassion for all beings; everything else is mockery’.

## \|\| 13.393 \|\|

*jñātvaitadbhavatā sādhyaṃ gaṃtavyaṃ paramaṃ padam \|*  
*yāṃ vai tīrthaṃkarā yātā yāṃ gatiṃ yogino gatāḥ \|\| 393 \|\|*

393\. Knowing this you should obtain the highest position worth going to and (should obtain) the same condition which the Tīrthaṅkaras and ascetics have obtained.

## \|\| 13.394 \|\|

*evaṃ vai devatāḥ pūrvaṃ vidyādharamahoragāḥ \|*  
*manorathābhilāṣāṃste ciṃtayaṃto divāniśam \|\| 394 \|\|*

394\. Thus (only) the deities, the Vidyādharas and the great serpents formerly entertaining desires day and night (obtained that state).

## \|\| 13.395 \|\|

*yadyeṣaṇā vai yuṣmākaṃ saṃsāraviratau kṛtā \|*  
*parityajadhvaṃ dārāṇi svargamārgārgalāni ca \|\| 395 \|\|*

395\. If you have entertained a desire to end the course of worldly life then leave (your) wives that are impediments in the path to heaven.

## \|\| 13.396 \|\|

*yasyāṃ yonau pitā yātastāṃ yoniṃ sevase katham \|*  
*ātmamāṃsopamaṃ māṃsaṃ kathaṃ khādaṃti jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 396 \|\|*

396\. How do you enjoy that female organ of generation into which your father entered (i.e. had coitus)? How is it that beings eat flesh which is similar to their own?

## \|\| 13.397 \|\|

*tataste dānavā bhīṣmā ūcuḥ sarve guruṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*dīkṣasva no mahābhāga bhrūṇakānagrataḥ sthitān \|\| 397 \|\|*

397\. Then all those terrible demons said (these) words to Guru: “O magnanimous one, initiate us (your) children who are before you!”

## \|\| 13.398 \|\|

*tathā kṛtvā sa tānāha samayena purohitaḥ \|*  
*praṇāmo nānyadeveṣu kartavyo vaḥ kadācana \|\| 398 \|\|*

398\. Having done so the priest at that time said: “You should never salute any other deity (than the Arhat).

## \|\| 13.399 \|\|

*ekasthāne yadā bhaktaṃ bhoktavyaṃ karasaṃpuṭe \|*  
*tatrasthāne sthitaṃ toyaṃ keśakīṭavivarjitam \|\| 399 \|\|*

399\. When you are required to eat at a place you have to eat by putting the food in the cavity of your hands and should look equally upon the water likeable or otherwise (which is) without hair and worms and not contaminated by other’s glance.

## \|\| 13.400 \|\|

*tulyaṃ priyāpriyaṃ kāryaṃ nānyadṛṣṭihataṃ kvacit \|*  
*bhoktavyametena vibho ācāreṇa tathā kuru \|\| 400 \|\|*

400\. O lord, one should eat according to this practice. Do like that. Those fit for release and you should remain together.”

## \|\| 13.401-402 \|\|

*bhavadhvaṃ sahitā yūyaṃ te tathā mokṣabhāginaḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā sa niyamānkṛtvā tāndanupuṃgavān \|\| 401 \|\|*

*jagāma dhiṣaṇo rājandevalokaṃ divaukasām \|*  
*ācacakṣe sa tatsarvaṃ dānavānāṃ ca kāritam \|\| 402 \|\|*

401-402. O prince, telling thus the restraints to those best demons, Guru went to heaven, the abode of gods and told them all that he had made the demons to do.

## \|\| 13.403-406 \|\|

*tataste tvasurā jagmurnarmadāmabhito vasan \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tāndānavāṃstatra prahlādena vinā kṛtān \|\| 403 \|\|*

*devarājastato hṛṣṭo namuciṃ prāha vai vacaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyākṣaṃ yajñahanaṃ dharmaghnaṃ vedaniṃdakam \|\| 404 \|\|*

*rākṣasaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ praghasaṃ vighasaṃ tathā \|*  
*muciṃ caiva tathā bāṇaṃ virocanamathāpi vā \|\| 405 \|\|*

*mahiṣākṣaṃ bāṣkalaṃ ca pracaṃḍaṃ caṃḍakaṃ tathā \|*  
*rocamānaṃ tathātyugraṃ suṣeṇaṃ dānavottamam \|\| 406 \|\|*

403-406. Then the demons went to Narmada and lived by it. Seeing there those demons except Prahrāda, the lord of gods, being pleased said (these) words ro Namuci: Seeing these—Hiraṇyākṣa, the destroyer of sacrifices and of religious practices and the censurer of the Vedas, so also Praghasa the demon of wicked deeds, and Vighasa, and Muci, and Bāṇa and Virocana, Mahiṣākṣa, Bāṣkala, Pracaṇḍa, Caṇḍaka, so also the shining and very cruel Suṣeṇa, the best among the demons—and others he said to the lords of demons:

## \|\| 13.407-408 \|\|

*etāndṛṣṭvā tathā cānyāndānaveṃdrānathābravīt \|*  
*indra uvāca \|*  
*dānaveṃdrāḥ purā jātāḥ kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ triviṣṭape \|\| 407 \|\|*

*idānīṃ kathamevedaṃ vrataṃ vedavilopakam \|*  
*bhavadbhiḥ kartumārabdhaṃ nagnamuṃḍikamaṃḍalu \|\| 408 \|\|*

Indra said:

407-408. O lords of demons, you were born in olden days; and you ruled over heaven; how is it that now you have started practising this vow destroying the Vedas, (being) naked, cleanshaven (and with) a pitcher and holding the peacock and have remained here?

## \|\| 13.409 \|\|

*mayūradhvajadhāritvaṃ kathaṃ caiveha tiṣṭhatha \|*  
*dānavā ūcuḥ \|*  
*tyaktaḥ sarvāsurabhāva ṛṣidharme vayaṃ sthitāḥ \|\| 409 \|\|*

The demons said:

409\. Having given up all our demonhood we have remained in these practices of the sages.

## \|\| 13.410 \|\|

*dharmavṛddhikaraṃ karma carāmaḥ sarvajaṃtuṣu \|*  
*trailokyarājyamakhilaṃ bhuṃkṣva śakra vrajasva ca \|\| 410 \|\|*

410\. We are doing deeds leading to the enhancement of religious practices in all the beings. O Indra, enjoy the kingdom of the three worlds and (now) depart (from here).

## \|\| 13.411 \|\|

*tatheti coktvā maghavā punaryātastriviṣṭapam \|*  
*evaṃ te mohitāḥ sarve bhīṣma devapurodhasā \|\| 411 \|\|*

411\. Saying ‘All right’ Indra again went to heaven. O Bhīṣma, all those (demons) were thus stupefied by (Bṛhaspati) the priest of gods.

## \|\| 13.412 \|\|

*narmadā saritaṃ prāpya sthitā dānavasattamāḥ \|*  
*jñātvā śukreṇa te sarve vṛttāṃtamanubodhitāḥ \|\| 412 \|\|*

412\. Going to the river Narmadā the best demons stayed (there). Knowing all that account Śukra again advised them.

## \|\| 13.413 \|\|

*tadā trailokyaharaṇe cakruḥ krūrāṃ punarmatim \|\| 413 \|\|*

413\. Then they again entertained the wicked idea of conquering the three worlds.

## Chapter 14 - Chopping-off of Brahmā’s head by Rudra

## \|\| 14.1-2 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ tripuruṣājjāto hyarjunaḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*kathaṃ karṇastu kānīnaḥ sūtajaḥ parikīrtyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*varaṃ tayoḥ kathaṃ bhūtaṃ nisargādeva tadvada \|*  
*bṛhatkautūhalaṃ mahyaṃ tadbhavānvaktumarhati \|\| 2 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1-2. Tell me how Arjuna, the killer of the brave enemies, was born from Tripuruṣa; how again, Karṇa, the son of an unmarried woman is known as born from a charioteer; how enmity sprang up between the two. I have a great curiosity; so please tell me that.

## \|\| 14.3-4 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*chinne vaktre purā brahmā krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*lalāṭe svedamutpannaṃ gṛhītvā tāḍayadbhuvi \|\| 3 \|\|*

*svedataḥ kuṃḍalī jajñe sadhanuṣko maheṣudhiḥ \|*  
*sahasrakavacī vīraḥ kiṃkaromītyuvāca ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

3-4. Formerly when his face was rent, Brahma, overpowered by great anger, took up the perspiration produced on his forehead and struck it on the ground; from that perspiration a brave hero having rings, arrows and a great bow and having a thousand armours was born and he said: “What shall I do?”

## \|\| 14.5 \|\|

*tamuvāca viriṃcastu darśayanrudramojasā \|*  
*hanyatāmeṣa durbuddhirjāyate na yathā punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Pointing, with vigour, to Rudra, Brahmā said to him: “Kill this wicked-minded one so that he will not be born again.”

## \|\| 14.6 \|\|

*brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā dhanurudyamya pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*saṃpratasthe maheśasya bāṇahastotiraudradṛk \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Hearing the words of Brahmā and raising the bow from behind Maheśa, he with arrows in his hand and having very angry eyes started (to kill him).

## \|\| 14.7-8 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā puruṣamatyugraṃ bhītastasya trilocanaḥ \|*  
*apakrāṃtastato vegādviṣṇorāśramamabhyagāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

*trāhitrāhīti māṃ viṣṇo narādasmācca śatruhan \|*  
*brahmaṇā nirmitaḥ pāpo mleccharūpo bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Seeing that very terrible man, Rudra being frightened speedily went away from there and reached Viṣṇu’s hermitage. “O Viṣṇu, killer of enemies, save me from this man; this terrible sinner of the form of a Mleccha is created by Brahma. O lord of the world, act in such a manner that he, an angry man, would not kill me.”

## \|\| 14.9-11 \|\|

*yathā hanyānna māṃ kruddhastathā kuru jagatpate \|*  
*huṃkāradhvaninā viṣṇurmohayitvā tu taṃ naram \|\| 9 \|\|*

*adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yogātmā viśvadṛkprabhuḥ \|*  
*tatra prāptaṃ virūpākṣaṃ sāṃtvayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tatassa praṇato bhūmau dṛṣṭo devena viṣṇunā \|*  
*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*pautro hi me bhavānrudra kaṃ te kāmaṃ karomyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Lord Viṣṇu, invisible to all beings (yet himself) seeing everything and possessed of magical powers having deluded that man, concealed Virūpākṣa (i.e. Rudra) who had come there. God Viṣṇu saw him who had bent himself (before Viṣṇu) on the ground.

Viṣṇu said to him:

O Rudra, you are my grandson, tell me which desire of you I should fulfil?

## \|\| 14.12 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ bhikṣāṃ dehītyuvāca ha \|*  
*kapālaṃ darśayitvāgre prajvalaṃstejasotkaṭam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Seeing god Viṣṇu and blazing exceedingly with lustre and pointing to his (begging) skull, he said, “Give me alms”.

## \|\| 14.13 \|\|

*kapālapāṇiṃ saṃprekṣya rudraṃ viṣṇuracintayat \|*  
*konyo yogyo bhavedbhikṣurbhikṣādānasya sāṃpratam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Seeing Rudra with the skull in his hand Viṣṇu thought: ‘Now who else (but you) would be proper for giving alms to?’

## \|\| 14.14 \|\|

*yogyo'yamiti saṃkalpya dakṣiṇaṃ bhujamarpayat \|*  
*tadbibhedātitīkṣṇena śūlena śaśiśekharaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thinking ‘this one is proper’ he offered him his right arm. Śiva cut it with his sharp trident.

## \|\| 14.15 \|\|

*prāvartata tato dhārā śoṇitasya vibhorbhujāt \|*  
*jāṃbūnadarasākārā vahnijvāleva nirmitā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then from the lord’s arm a stream of blood like liquified gold produced from a flame of fire started (to flow).

## \|\| 14.16 \|\|

*nipapāta kapālāṃtaśśambhunā sā prabhikṣitā \|*  
*ṛjvī vegavatī tīvrā spṛśaṃtī tvāṃbaraṃ javāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It fell out of the skull, and Śambhu begged it; it was straight, strong and touched the sky with speed.

## \|\| 14.17 \|\|

*paṃcāśadyojanā dairghyādvistārāddaśayojanā \|*  
*divyavarṣasahasraṃ sā samuvāha harerbhujāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. From Viṣṇu’s arm it flowed for a thousand years and was fifty-five Yojanas long and its expanse was ten Yojanas.

## \|\| 14.18 \|\|

*iyaṃtaṃ kālamīśosau bhikṣāṃ jagrāha bhikṣukaḥ \|*  
*dattā nārāyaṇenātha kāpāle pātra uttame \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The lord, the beggar, received the alms for such (a long) period. It was given (i.e. put) by Nārāyaṇa into an excellent (begging) skull.

## \|\| 14.19 \|\|

*tato nārāyaṇaḥ prāha śaṃbhuṃ paramidaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*saṃpūrṇaṃ vā na vā pātraṃ tato vai paramīśvaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then Nārāyaṇa said these words to that great Śambhu (i.e. Rudra):

## \|\| 14.20-21 \|\|

*satoyāṃbudanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā vākyaṃ harerharaḥ \|*  
*śaśisūryāgninayanaḥ śaśiśekharaśobhitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kapāle dṛṣṭimāveśya tribhirnetrairjanārdanam \|*  
*aṃgulyā ghaṭayanprāha kapālaṃ paripūritam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. “Is the pot filled or not?” Then the great lord, hearing Viṣṇu’s words resembling the thundering of clouds, having eyes like the moon and the sun and adorned with the (crescent) moon on his head, fixing (all his) three eyes on the skull, and reaching it said to Janārdana: “The skull is full.”

## \|\| 14.22-24 \|\|

*śrutvā śivasya tāṃ vāṇīṃ viṣṇurdhārāṃ samāharat \|*  
*paśto'tha harerīśaḥ svāṃgulyā rudhiraṃ tadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*divyavarṣasahasraṃ ca dṛṣṭipātairmamaṃtha saḥ \|*  
*mathyamāne tato rakte kalilaṃ budbudaṃ kramāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

*babhūva ca tataḥ paścātkirīṭī saśarāsanaḥ \|*  
*baddhatūṇīrayugalo vṛṣaskaṃdhoṅgulitravān \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Hearing those words of Śiva, Viṣṇu withdrew the stream. When Hari was observing, the lord (i. e. Rudra) churned (stirred) that blood with his finger and his glances for a thousand divine years. When the blood was (thus) churned (stirred), it gradually became first a mass, then a bubble and after that a man with a crown (on his head), with a bow, having bull-like (i.e. strong) shoulders, with two quivers tied to his back, with a finger-protector, appearing like fire, in the skull.

## \|\| 14.25 \|\|

*puruṣo vahnisaṃkāśaḥ kapāle saṃpradṛśyate \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānviṣṇuḥ prāha rudramidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Seeing him lord Viṣṇu said these words to Rudra:

## \|\| 14.26-27 \|\|

*kapāle bhava ko vā'yaṃ prādurbhūto'bhavannaraḥ \|*  
*vacaḥ śrutvā harerīśastamuvāca vibho śṛṇu \|\| 26 \|\|*

*naro nāmaiṣa puruṣaḥ paramāstravidāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*bhavatokto nara iti narastasmādbhaviṣyati \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. “O Bhava, who is this man (Nara) that has sprung

up in the skull?” Hearing (these) words of Viṣṇu, Śiva said to him: “O Lord, listen; this is the man named Nara, best among those who know (the use of) great missiles. You called him Nara, so he will be (called) Nara.

## \|\| 14.28-30 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇau cobhau yuge khyātau bhaviṣyataḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāme devakāryeṣu lokānāṃ paripālane \|\| 28 \|\|*

*eṣa nārāyaṇasakho narastasmādbhaviṣyati \|*  
*athāsuravadhe sāhyaṃ tava kartā mahādyutiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*munirjñānaparīkṣāyāṃ jetā loke bhaviṣyati \|*  
*tejodhikamidaṃ divyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paṃcamaṃ śiraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. Both Nara and Nārāyaṇa will be famous in the Yuga and in battles, in deeds helping gods and in the protection of people. This Nara, therefore, will be the friend of Nārāyaṇa. This one of great lustre will help you in killing the demons; he will be a sage in testing knowledge and a conquerer in the world. This is the fifth head of Brahmā, with a superior lustre.

## \|\| 14.31-33 \|\|

*tejaso brahmaṇo dīptādbhujasya tava śoṇitāt \|*  
*mama dṛṣṭi nipātācca trīṇi tejāṃsi yāni tu \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tatsaṃyogasamutpannaḥ śatruṃ yuddhe vijeṣyati \|*  
*avadhyā ye bhaviṣyaṃti durjayā api cāpare \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śakrasya cāmarāṇāṃ ca teṣāmeṣa bhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*evamuktvā sthitaḥ śaṃbhurvismitaśca haristadā \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Born from the combination of the three lustres that rose from the blazing lustre of Brahmā and the glance that I cast, he will conquer the enemy in battle. He will be terrible to those who cannot be killed by Indra and (other) gods and also to the others who will be invincible to Indra and (other) gods.”

Saying so, Śambhu then stood still and Hari too stood wondering.

## \|\| 14.34-37 \|\|

*kapālasthaḥ sa tatraiva tuṣṭāva harakeśavau \|*  
*śirasyaṃjalimādhāya tadā vīra udāradhīḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kiṃkaromīti tau prāha ityuktvā praṇataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*tamuvāca haraḥ śrīmānbrahmaṇā svena tejasā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sṛṣṭo naro dhanuṣpāṇistvamenaṃ tu niṣūdaya \|*  
*itthamuktvāṃjalidharaṃ stuvaṃtaṃ śaṃkaro naram \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tathaivāṃjalisaṃbaddhaṃ gṛhītvā ca karadvayam \|*  
*uddhṛtyātha kapālāttaṃ punarvacanamabravīt \|\| 37 \|\|*

34-37. The (man) remaining in the skull praised Śiva and Viṣṇu. The hero, of generous mind, joining his palms together and raising them to his head said to them: “What should I do?” Saying so he remained bent (i.e. humble) before them. The glorious Hara said to him: “With his own lustre Brahmā has created a man with a bow in his hand. You kill him”. Śaṅkara, speaking thus, holding the man’s both hands which were joined like that in satisfaction, and lifting up the man, who was praising him, from the skull said these words again:

## \|\| 14.38-39 \|\|

*sa eṣa puruṣo raudro yo mayā veditastava \|*  
*viṣṇuhuṃkāraracitamohanidrāṃ praveśitaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vibodhayainaṃ tvaritamityuktvāntardadhe haraḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇasya pratyakṣaṃ nareṇānena vai tadā \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. “This is the terrible man about whom I told you, he has been put to sleep. Awaken him quickly.” Saying so Hara disappeared. Then in the presence of Nārāyaṇa, the mighty one struck by the left foot by Nara, got up.

## \|\| 14.40-41 \|\|

*vāmapādahataḥ sopi samuttasthau mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tato yuddhaṃ samabhavatsvedaraktajayormahat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*visphāritadhanuḥ śabdaṃ nāditāśeṣabhūtalam \|*  
*kavacaṃ svedajasyaikaṃ raktajena tvapākṛtam \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Then between the two born of (Brahmā’s) perspiration and (Viṣṇu’s) blood, took place a great battle in which the sound of the extended bow spread (everywhere) and the entire earth resounded with the sound (of the battle).

The one born of (Viṣṇu’s) blood (i.e. Nara) took off the armour of the one born of perspiration.

## \|\| 14.42-43 \|\|

*evaṃ sametayoryuddhe divyaṃ varṣadvayaṃ tayoḥ \|*  
*yudhyatoḥ samatītaṃ ca svedaraktajayornṛpa \|\| 42 \|\|*

*raktajaṃ dvibhujaṃ dṛṣṭvā svedajaṃ caiva saṃgatau \|*  
*vicintya vāsudevogādbrahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ param \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. O king, a couple of divine years passed when the two thus met in battle and fought. Seeing the two-handed one born of (Viṣṇu’s) blood and the one born of (Brahmā’s) perspiration thus encountering (each other) Viṣṇu after having thought, went to the great abode of Brahmā.

## \|\| 14.44-46 \|\|

*sasaṃbhramamuvācedaṃ brahmāṇaṃ madhusūdanaḥ \|*  
*raktajenādya bho brahmansvedajoyaṃ nipātitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*śrutvaitadākulo brahmā babhāṣe madhusūdanam \|*  
*hare dyajanmani naro madīyo jīvatādayam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tathā tuṣṭo'bravīttaṃ ca viṣṇurevaṃ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*gatvā tayo raṇamapi nivāryā''ha ca tāvubhau \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. Madhusūdana (i.e. Viṣṇu) spoke, in alarm, these words to Brahma: “O Brahman, the one born of (your) perspiration was today hurled down by the one born of (my) blood.”

On hearing this Brahmā who (became) distressed said to Madhusūdana:

“O Hari, let this my man live (again) in this existence.”

## \|\| 14.47 \|\|

*anyajanmani bhavitā kalidvāparayormithaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhau mahāraṇe jāte tatrāhaṃ yojayāmi vāṃ \|\| 47 \|\|*

Viṣṇu being pleased said: “It shall be so.”

47\. Going to their battlefield and warding them off he said to both of them: “In the intervening period between the Kali and Dvāpara yugas, in your next birth there will be (a war); when the great war will take place I shall bring both of you together (to fight).”

## \|\| 14.48 \|\|

*viṣṇunā tu samāhūya graheśvarasureśvarau \|*  
*uktāvimau narau bhadrau pālanīyau mamājñayā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Viṣṇu having called the lord of planets and the lord of gods told them: “By my command these two good men are to be protected by you.

## \|\| 14.49 \|\|

*sahasrāṃśo svedajoyaṃ svakīyoṃ'śo dharātale \|*  
*dvāparāṃtevatāryoyaṃ devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. O sun (having a thousand rays), this one born of the perspiration (of Brahmā) is to be descended on the earth as your portion at the end of the Dvāpara (yuga) for the success of gods.

## \|\| 14.50 \|\|

*yadūnāṃ tu kule bhāvī śūronāma mahābalaḥ \|*  
*tasya kanyā pṛthā nāma rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. In the family of the Yadus there will be born very mighty Śūra.

## \|\| 14.51 \|\|

*utpatsyati mahābhāgā devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye \|*  
*durvāsāstu varaṃ tasyai maṃtragrāmaṃ pradāsyati \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. His glorious daughter Pṛthā, incomparable in beauty on the earth will be born for the success of gods; and Durvāsas will grant her a boon and a group of spells:

## \|\| 14.52 \|\|

*maṃtreṇānena yaṃ devaṃ bhaktyā āvāhayiṣyati \|*  
*devi tasya prasādāttu tava putro bhaviṣyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. ‘Whatever god she (i.e. you) would invoke with that spell by the favour of that god, O venerable lady, you will obtain a son’.

## \|\| 14.53 \|\|

*sā ca tvāmudaye dṛṣṭvā sābhilāṣā rajasvalā \|*  
*ciṃtābhipannā tiṣṭhaṃtī bhajitavyā vibhāvaso \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O Sun, she during her menses seeing you rising will long for you; when she is (thus) afflicted with anxiety you should enjoy her.

## \|\| 14.54 \|\|

*tasyā garbhe tvayaṃ bhāvī kānīnaḥ kuṃtinaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyati suto devadevakāryārthasiddhaye \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. In her i.e. Kuntī’s womb he will be (conceived and) born as the son ofan unmarried woman for the success of gods, O lord.”

## \|\| 14.55 \|\|

*tatheti coktvā provāca tejorāśirdivākaraḥ \|*  
*putramutpādayiṣyāmi kānīnaṃ balagarvitam \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The Sun, the heap of lustre Saying “All right” spoke (further): “On the maiden I shall generate a son who will be proud ofhis power.

## \|\| 14.56 \|\|

*yasya karṇeti vai nāma lokaḥ sarvo vadiṣyati \|*  
*matprasādādasya viṣṇo viprāṇāṃ bhāvitātmanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. And all people will address him by the name Karṇa. O Viṣṇu, due to my favour in the world there will be nothing with him, of a pure soul, that will not be given to brāhmaṇas, O Keśava.

## \|\| 14.57 \|\|

*adeyaṃ nāsti vai loke vastu kiṃcicca keśava \|*  
*evaṃ prabhāvaṃ caivainaṃ janaye vacanāttava \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. By your direction I shall generate him of such a prowess.”

## \|\| 14.58 \|\|

*evamuktvā sahasrāṃśurdevaṃ dānavaghātinam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ mahātmānaṃ tatraivāṃtardadhe raviḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Having thus addressed the magnanimous god Nārāyaṇa, the destroyer of demons, the Sun disappeared there only.

## \|\| 14.59 \|\|

*adarśanaṃ gate deve bhāskare vāritaskare \|*  
*vṛddhaśravasamapyevamuvāca prītamānasaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. When the Sun-god, the robber of clouds, diappeared (Viṣṇu) with his mind pleased said to Indra also:

## \|\| 14.60 \|\|

*sahasranetraraktottho naro'yaṃ madanugrahāt \|*  
*svāṃśabhūto dvāparāṃte yoktavyo bhūtale tvayā \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. “O Indra, this Nara sprung up from (my) blood due to my favour and who is a portion of me should be placed by you on the earth at the end of Dvāpara.

## \|\| 14.61 \|\|

*yadā pāṃḍurmahābhāgaḥ pṛthāṃ bhāryāmavāpsyati \|*  
*mādrīṃ cāpi mahābhāga tadāraṇyaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. O magnanimous one, when the illustrious Pāṇḍu will obtain Pṛthā as his wife and so also Mādrī he will go to a forest.

## \|\| 14.62 \|\|

*tasyāpyaraṇyasaṃsthasya mṛgaḥ śāpaṃ pradāsyati \|*  
*tena cotpannavairāgyaḥ śataśṛgaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. A deer will give him a curse when he will be in the forest; with aversion produced by that he will go to Śataśṛṅga.

## \|\| 14.63 \|\|

*putrānabhīpsankṣetrotthānbhāryāṃ sa pravadiṣyati \|*  
*anīpsaṃtī tadā kuṃtī bharttāraṃ sā vadiṣyati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Desiring sons to be born on his wife (by another) he will say (so) to her. Then Kuntī unwilling (to do so) will say to her husband (i.e. Pāṇḍu):

## \|\| 14.64 \|\|

*nāhaṃ martyasya vai rājanputrānicche kathaṃcana \|*  
*daivatebhyaḥ prasādācca putrānicche narādhipa \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. ‘O King, I do not at all desire sons (begotten) by a mortal. O King, I desire sons from the deities by their favour.’

## \|\| 14.65 \|\|

*prārthayaṃtyai tvayā śakra kuṃtyai deyo narastataḥ \|*  
*vacasā ca madīyena evaṃ kuru śacīpate \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. O Śakra then you should present Nara to Kuntī who would beseech you. O Lord of Śacī, do so by my direction.”

## \|\| 14.66-72 \|\|

*athābravīttadā viṣṇuṃ deveśo duḥkhito vacaḥ \|*  
*asminmanvaṃtare'tīte caturviṃśatike yuge \|\| 66 \|\|*

*avatīrya raghukule gṛhe daśarathasya ca \|*  
*rāvaṇasya vadhārthāya śāṃtyarthaṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 67 \|\|*

*rāmarūpeṇa bhavatā sītārthamaṭatā vane \|*  
*matputro hiṃsito deva sūryaputrahitārthinā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*vālināma plavaṃgeṃdraḥ sugrīvārthe tvayā yataḥ \|*  
*duḥkhenānena taptohaṃ gṛhṇāmi na sutaṃ naram \|\| 69 \|\|*

*agṛhṇamānaṃ deveṃdraṃ kāraṇāṃtaravādinam \|*  
*hariḥ proce śunāsīraṃ bhuvo bhārāvatāraṇe \|\| 70 \|\|*

*avatāraṃ kariṣyāmi martyaloke tvahaṃ prabho \|*  
*sūryaputrasya nāśārthaṃ jayārthamātmajasya te \|\| 71 \|\|*

*sārathyaṃ ca kariṣyāmi nāśaṃ kurukulasya ca \|*  
*tato hṛṣṭobhavacchakro viṣṇuvākyena tena ha \|\| 72 \|\|*

66-72. Then the unhappy lord of gods said (these) words to Viṣṇu: “When this period of Manu passes, then in the twenty-fourth Yuga you, descending (i.e. being born) as Rāma in Raghu’s family, in Daśaratha’s house for killing Rāvaṇa and for causing peace to the gods, (while) wandering in the forest for Sītā, desiring the good of Sun’s son, (will have) killed my son, named Vālin, the chief of the monkeys. Being, tormented by this grief, I shall not accept that son viz. Nara.” To Indra, the lord of gods, who did not accept Nara and telling some other reason, Viṣṇu spoke for taking down the burden of the earth: “O Lord, I shall take an incarnation in the mortal world for destroying Sun’s son and for your son’s success. I shall also act as (Arjuna’s) charioteer and bring about the destruction of the Kuru-family.”

## \|\| 14.73 \|\|

*pratigṛhya naraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ satyaṃ cāstu vacastava \|*  
*evamuktvā varaṃ devaḥ preṣayitvā'cyutaḥ svayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Then with these words of Viṣṇu, Śakra accepting Nara, was pleased. Being delighted he (said): “May your words come true.” God Viṣṇu himself, granting the boon thus and sending (Indra) and having gone to Brahmā, the lotus-eyed one (i.e. Viṣṇu) again said to him:

## \|\| 14.74-85 \|\|

*gatvā tu puṃḍarīkākṣo brahmāṇaṃ prāha vai punaḥ \|*  
*tvayā sṛṣṭamidaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 74 \|\|*

*āvāṃ kāryasya karaṇe sahāyau ca tava prabho \|*  
*svayaṃ kṛtvā punarnāśaṃ kartuṃ deva na budhyase \|\| 75 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ jugupsitaṃ karma śaṃbhumetaṃ jighāṃsatā \|*  
*tvayā ca devadevasya sṛṣṭaḥ kopena vai pumān \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śuddhyarthamasya pāpasya prāyaścittaṃ paraṃ kuru \|*  
*gṛhṇanvahnitrayaṃ deva agnihotramupāhara \|\| 77 \|\|*

*puṇyatīrthe tathā deśe vane vāpi pitāmaha \|*  
*svapatnyā sahito yajñaṃ kuruṣvāsmatparigrahāt \|\| 78 \|\|*

*sarve devāstathādityā rudrāścāpi jagatpate \|*  
*ādeśaṃ te kariṣyaṃti yatosmākaṃ bhavānprabhuḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*ekohi gārhapatyognirdakṣiṇāgnirdvitīyakaḥ \|*  
*āhavanīyastṛtīyastu trikuṃḍeṣu prakalpaya \|\| 80 \|\|*

*vartule tvarcayātmānammāmatho dhanurākṛtau \|*  
*catuḥkoṇe haraṃ devaṃ ṛgyajuḥsāmanāmabhiḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*agnīnutpādya tapasā parāmṛddhimavāpya ca \|*  
*divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu hutvāgnīnśamayiṣyasi \|\| 82 \|\|*

*agnihotrātparaṃ nānyatpavitramiha paṭhyate \|*  
*sukṛtenāgnihotreṇa praśuddhyaṃti bhuvi dvijāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*paṃthāno devalokasya brāhmaṇairdaśitāstvamī \|*  
*ekogniḥ sarvadā dhāryo gṛhasthena dvijanmanā \|\| 84 \|\|*

*vināgninā dvijeneha gārhasthyanna tu labhyate \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*yo'sau kapālādutpanno naro nāma dhanurddharaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

74-85. “You have created the three worlds (consisting of) the movable and immovable. O lord, we two shall help you in the execution of (your) job. O lord, you do not realize that you are destroying (the world) after having yourself created it. Desiring to kill this Śambhu, you have done the censurable deed. Due to your anger for god (Śiva) you created the man. To absolve you of this sin undertake great expiation. O god, accepting the three fires offer an oblation to Agni, either at a sacred place or in a sacred region or forest. O Pitāmaha, perform, with your wife, a sacrifice under our protection. O lord of the worlds, all gods, so also Ādityas and Rudras will obey your command as you are our lord. One is the Gārhapatya fire, second is the Dakṣiṇāgni and the third is the Āhavanīya. Prepare these in three fire-vessels. Worship yourself in a circle, me in a bow-like figure and god Hara in a quadrangle by means of (the recitation of) the Ṛks, Yajus and Sāmans. Having generated fires by means of penance and obtaining great affluence, you will put out the fires after having offered oblations into them for one thousand divine years. Nothing is said to be more sacred than offering oblations to fire in this world. Brāhmaṇas are purified on the earth by well-offered oblation to fire.

These are indicated by the brāhmaṇas to be the paths leading to the world of gods. A brāhmaṇa householder should always maintain a fire. The status of a householder can never be obtained by a brāhmaṇa without (maintaining) a fire.”

## \|\| 14.86 \|\|

*kimeṣa mādhavājjāta utāho svena karmaṇā \|*  
*uta rudreṇa janito hyathavā buddhipūrvakam \|\| 86 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

86\. Was that archer, named Nara, who sprang up from the skull, born from Mādhava or due to his own deeds? Or was he deliberately created by Rudra?

## \|\| 14.87 \|\|

*brahmanhiraṇyagarbho'yamaṃḍajātaścaturmukhaḥ \|*  
*adbhutaṃ pañcamaṃ tasya vaktraṃ tatkathamutthitam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. O brāhmaṇa, Brahmā, the Hiraṇyagarbha, sprang up from an egg. How is it that that fifth face came up?

## \|\| 14.88 \|\|

*satve rajo na dṛśyeta na satvaṃ rajasi kvacit \|*  
*satvastho bhagavānbrahmā kathamudrekamādadhāt \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Rajas (a cosmic quality—the cause of activity) is never seen in Sattva (quality of goodness), nor Sattva in Rajas. How did Brahmā (always) remaining in Sattva have excess (of Rajas) by which he with his mind deluded, sent the man to kill Hara?

## \|\| 14.89 \|\|

*mūḍhātmanā naro yena haṃtuṃ hi prahito haraṃ \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*maheśvaraharī caito dvāveva satpathi sthitau \|\| 89 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

89\. Maheśvara (i.e. Śiva) and Hari both these remained on the good path.

## \|\| 14.90 \|\|

*tayoraviditaṃ nāsti siddhāsiddhaṃ mahātmanoḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ paṃcamaṃ vaktramūrddhvamāsīnmahātmanaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. For the two magnanimous ones, nothing that is either unaccomplished or accomplished, is unknown. The fifth face of the great Brahmā had come up.

## \|\| 14.91 \|\|

*tato brahmābhavanmūḍho rajasā copabṛṃhitaḥ \|*  
*tato'yaṃ tejasā sṛṣṭimamanyata mayā kṛtā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. So, growing with Rajas Brahmā became deluded. He thought that he had fashioned the creation (i.e. the world) with his lustre.

## \|\| 14.92 \|\|

*matto'nyo nāsti vai devo yena sṛṣṭiḥ pravartitā \|*  
*saha devāḥ sagaṃdharvāḥ paśupakṣimṛgākulāḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. ‘There is no other god than I, who set forth the creation including gods, Gandharvas, beasts, birds and deer.’

## \|\| 14.93 \|\|

*evaṃ mūḍhaḥ sa paṃcāsyo viriṃcirabhavatpunaḥ \|*  
*prāgvaktraṃ mukhametasya ṛgvedasya pravartakam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. And the five-faced Brahmā was thus deluded. His face facing the east was the originator of Ṛgveda.

## \|\| 14.94 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ vadanaṃ tasya yajurvedapravartakam \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ sāmavedasya atharvārthaṃ caturthakam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. His second face set forth Yajurveda. The third one was the originator of Sāmaveda and fourth of Atharvaveda.

## \|\| 14.95 \|\|

*sāṃgopāṃgetihāsāṃśca sarahasyānsasaṃgrahān \|*  
*vedānadhīte vaktreṇa paṃcamenorddhvacakṣuṣā \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. With the fifth face looking upwards he studies the Vedas with limbs (i.e. the Vedāṅgas) and sub-limbs (i.e. the supplementary works to the Vedāṅgas), history, secret sciences and compilations (of laws).

## \|\| 14.96 \|\|

*tasyā'surasurāḥ sarve vaktrasyādbhutavarcasaḥ \|*  
*tejasā na prakāśaṃte dīpāḥ sūryodaye yathā \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. By the lustre of that face of wonderful brilliance all demons and gods lost their brilliance like lamps at sunrise.

## \|\| 14.97 \|\|

*svapureṣvapi sodvegā hyavartaṃta vicetasaḥ \|*  
*na kaṃcidgaṇayeccānyaṃ tejasā kṣipate parān \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. The perplexed ones being disgusted remained in their own cities. One neither cared for another nor offended others with his might.

## \|\| 14.98 \|\|

*nābhigaṃtu na ca draṣṭuṃ purastānnopasarpitum \|*  
*śekustrastāḥ surāssarve padmayoniṃ mahāprabhum \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. All the frightened gods were unable to approach or to see or to go near that great lord Brahmā.

## \|\| 14.99 \|\|

*abhibhūtamivātmānaṃ manyamānā hatatviṣaḥ \|*  
*sarve te maṃtrayāmāsurdaivatā hitamātmanaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Dimmed in lustre they regarded themselves as overpowered. All they pondered over their own good—the good of gods.

## \|\| 14.100 \|\|

*gacchāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ śaṃbhuṃ nistejaso'sya tejasā \|*  
*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namastesarvasatveśa maheśvara namonamaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100a. ‘We, who have lost our lustre by his brilliance will resort to Śiva.’

Gods said:

100b. Salutation to you, O lord of all beings, great god, we repeatedly salute you.

## \|\| 14.101 \|\|

*jagadyone paraṃbrahma bhūtānāṃ tvaṃ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*pratiṣṭhā sarvajagatāṃ tvaṃ heturviṣṇunā saha \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. O you source of the world, O you highest Brahman, you are eternal. You are, along with Viṣṇu, the support and the cause of all the worlds.

## \|\| 14.102 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃstūyamānosau devarṣipitṛdānavaiḥ \|*  
*aṃtarhita uvācedaṃ devāḥ prārthayatepsitam \|\| 102 \|\|*

102\. He, being thus praised by gods, sages, forefathers and demons, remaining hidden, said: “O gods, ask for your desired object.”

## \|\| 14.103 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣadarśanaṃ datvā dehi deva yathepsitam \|*  
*kṛtvā kāruṇyamasmākaṃ varaścāpi pradīyatām \|\| 103 \|\|*

Gods said:

103\. O god, appearing in person, give us as much as is desired by us. Have pity on us and give us a boon also.

## \|\| 14.104 \|\|

*yadasmākaṃ mahadvīryaṃ teja ojaḥ parākramaḥ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ brahmaṇā grastaṃ paṃcamāsyasya tejasā \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Whatever great valour, lustre, power we had—all that has been eclipsed by Brahma with his fifth face.

## \|\| 14.105 \|\|

*vineśuḥ sarvatejāṃsi tvatprasādātpunaḥ prabho \|*  
*jāyate tu yathāpūrvaṃ tathā kuru maheśvara \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. All lustres have perished. O great lord, act in such a way that everything becomes as before.

## \|\| 14.106 \|\|

*tataḥ prasannavadano devaiścāpi namaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*jagāma yatra brahmā'sau rajohaṃkāramūḍhadhīḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Then Śiva, with his face pleased and saluted even by gods, went there where Brahma was with his mind deluded by the pride of his Rajas quality.

## \|\| 14.107 \|\|

*stuvaṃto devadeveśaṃ parivārya samāviśan \|*  
*brahmā tamāgataṃ rudraṃ na jajñe rajasāvṛtaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. (Gods) praising the lord of gods and surrounding him approached him. Brahma enveloped in (i.e. overpowered by) the Rajas quality did not recognise Rudra who had come to him.

## \|\| 14.108 \|\|

*sūryakoṭisahasrāṇāṃ tejasā raṃjayanjagat \|*  
*tadādṛśyata viśvātmā viśvasṛgviśvabhāvanaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. At that time the soul of all, the creator of the universe and the illuminator of everything was seen to please the world with his lustre (like that) of crores of suns.

## \|\| 14.109 \|\|

*sapitāmahamāsīnaṃ sakalaṃ devamaṃḍalam \|*  
*abhigamya tato rudro brahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. Then Rudra, approaching Brahmā, the Almighty, seated (there) with the entire group of gods (said):

## \|\| 14.110 \|\|

*ahotitejasā vaktramadhikaṃ deva rājate \|*  
*evamuktvāṭṭahāsaṃ tu mumoca śaśiśekharaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. “O god, with great lustre your face shines more!” Saying so Śiva laughed loudly.

## \|\| 14.111 \|\|

*vāmāṃguṣṭhanakhāgreṇa brahmaṇaḥ paṃcamaṃ śiraḥ \|*  
*cakarta kadalīgarbhaṃ naraḥ kararuhairiva \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. As a man cuts off the interior of a plantain tree with his nails, Śiva cut off Brahmā’s fifth head with the nail of the left thumb.

## \|\| 14.112 \|\|

*vicchinnaṃ tu śiraḥ paścādbhavahaste sthitaṃ tadā \|*  
*grahamaṃḍalamadhyastho dvitīya iva caṃdramāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. That head that was cut off then remained in the hand of Śiva, like another moon remaining in the midst of planets.

## \|\| 14.113 \|\|

*karotkṣiptakapālena nanarta ca maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*śikharasthena sūryeṇa kailāsa iva parvataḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Maheśvara danced with the head held up in his hand like the Kailāsa mountain with the sun on its peak.

## \|\| 14.114 \|\|

*chinne vaktre tato devā hṛṣṭāstaṃ vṛṣabhadhvajam \|*  
*tuṣṭuvurvividhaistotrairdevadevaṃ kapardinam \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. When the head was chopped off, the gods being pleased, praised Vṛṣabhadhvaja Kapardin (i.e. Śiva), the god of gods, with various hymns of praise.

## \|\| 14.115 \|\|

*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*namaḥ kapāline nityaṃ mahākālasya kāline \|*  
*aiśvaryajñānayuktāya sarvabhāgapradāyine \|\| 115 \|\|*

Gods said:

115\. Salutation forever to the holder of the skull, to the destroyer of great death, to him who is endowed with splendour and knowledge and is the giver of all portions (of enjoyment).

## \|\| 14.116 \|\|

*namo harṣavilāsāya sarvadevamayāya ca \|*  
*kalau saṃhārakartā tvaṃ mahākālaḥ smṛto hyasi \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. Salutation to him who is the flash of joy, and who is full of all gods. You are the destroyer in the Kali (age), hence you are known to be Mahākāla.

## \|\| 14.117 \|\|

*bhaktānāmārtināśastvaṃ duḥkhāṃtastena cocyase \|*  
*śaṃkaroṣyāśubhaktānāṃ tena tvaṃ śaṃkaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. You destroy the afflictions of (your) devotees; you are called Duḥkhānta (i.e. one who puts an end to all miseries). As you quickly bring about the welfare of (your) devotees you are called Śaṅkara.

## \|\| 14.118 \|\|

*chinnaṃ brahmaśiro yasmāttvaṃ kapālaṃ bibharṣi ca \|*  
*tena deva kapālī tvaṃ stuto hyadya prasīda naḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. O god, since you hold (Brahmā’s) head that is cut off and the skull, you are therefore Kapālin. Favour us as you are praised by us.

## \|\| 14.119 \|\|

*evaṃ stutaḥ prasannātmā devānprasthāpya śaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*svāni dhiṣṇyāni bhagavāṃstatraivāsīnmudānvitaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Thus praised, Śaṅkara with his mind pleased, sent the gods to their respective abodes and remained there full of joy.

## \|\| 14.120-121 \|\|

*vijñāya brahmaṇo bhāvaṃ tato vīrasya janma ca \|*  
*śiro nīrasya vākyāttu lokānāṃ kopaśāṃtaye \|\| 120 \|\|*

*śirasyaṃjalimādhāya tuṣṭāvātha praṇamya tam \|*  
*tejonidhi paraṃ brahma jñātumitthaṃ prajāpatim \|\| 121 \|\|*

120-121. Knowing the mind of Brahmā and the birth of Vīra, Śiva, throwing off the head at the words (i.e. request) of the people, having put his joined palms on his head and having saluted Brahmā praised him for appeasing his anger and to know the Brahman, the greatest storehouse of lustre with expressions, hymns, secret (chants) and texts from Ṛg(veda), Yajur (veda) and Sāma (veda) thus:

## \|\| 14.122-123 \|\|

*niruktasūktarahasyairṛgyajuḥ sāmabhāṣitaiḥ \|*  
*rudra uvāca \|*  
*aprameya namastestu paramasya parātmane \|\| 122 \|\|*

*adbhutānāṃ prasūtistvaṃ tejasāṃ nidhirakṣayaḥ \|*  
*vijayādviśvabhāvastvaṃ sṛṣṭikartā mahādyute \|\| 123 \|\|*

Rudra said:

122-123. Salutation to you, O infinite one, and the supreme spirit of the highest one; you are the origin of wonderful things; you are an inexhaustible treasure of lustres. Due to your success you are the soul of all. You are the author of the creation, O you of great lustre.

## \|\| 14.124 \|\|

*ūrddhvavaktra namastestu satvātmakadharātmaka \|*  
*jalaśāyinjalotpanna jalālaya namostu te \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Salutation to you, O you having one face turned upwards, of the nature of goodness, of the form of the earth, O you lying in water, born of water and having your abode in water.

## \|\| 14.125 \|\|

*jalajotphullapatrākṣa jaya deva pitāmaha \|*  
*tvayā hyutpāditaḥ pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭyarthamahamīśvara \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. O you born of water, having eyes like blooming leaves; victory to you O grandsire, O god, O lord; you formerly created me for the creation.

## \|\| 14.126 \|\|

*yajñāhutisadāhāra yajñāṃgeśa namo'stu te \|*  
*svarṇagarbha padmagarbha devagarbha prajāpate \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. O you who always took oblations made into the sacrifice, O you the lord of the constituents of sacrifice, salutation to you, O you the interior of gold, of lotus, of gods, O you lord of beings.

## \|\| 14.127 \|\|

*tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkāraḥ svadhā tvaṃ padmasaṃbhava \|*  
*vacanena tu devānāṃ śiraśchinnaṃ mayā prabho \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. O you born of lotus, you are the sacrifice, the Vaṣaṭkāra (the exclamation Vaṣaṭ used on making an oblation to a deity) and the Svadhā (oblation offered to the pitṛs). O lord, I cut off the head at the direction of gods.

## \|\| 14.128 \|\|

*brahmahatyābhibhūtosmi māṃ tvaṃ pāhi jagatpate \|*  
*ityukto devadevena brahmā vacanamabravīt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. I am humiliated with the murder of a brāhmaṇa; O lord of the world, protect me.

Thus addressed by the god of gods, Brahmā said (these) words:

## \|\| 14.129 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*sakhā nārāṇo devaḥ sa tvāṃ pūtaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*kīrtanīyastvayā dhanyaḥ sa me pūjyaḥ svayaṃ vibhuḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

Brahma said:

129\. God Nārāyaṇa, (our) friend, will purify you. You should praise that virtuous one; the self-mighty one is venerable to me.

## \|\| 14.130 \|\|

*anudhyāto'si vai nūnaṃ tena devena viṣṇunā \|*  
*yena te bhaktirutpannā stotuṃ māṃ matirutthitā \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Indeed you were thought of by that god Viṣṇu, so as devotion in you was produced, and a desire to praise me sprang up in you.

## \|\| 14.131 \|\|

*śiraśchedātkapālī tvaṃ somasiddhāṃtakārakaḥ \|*  
*koṭīḥ śataṃ ca viprāṇāmuddhartāsi mahādyute \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. You are Kapāli for having cut off the head. You are the author of the Soma doctrine. O you of great lustre, you have emancipated a hundred crores of brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 14.132 \|\|

*brahmahatyāvrataṃ kuryā nānyatkiṃcana vidyate \|*  
*abhāṣyāḥ pāpinaḥ krūrā brahmaghnāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. You should perform the vow (of expiation) for killing a brāhmaṇa; there is no other course. The sinful, cruel murderers ofbrāhmaṇas who are sinners, should not be talked to.

## \|\| 14.133 \|\|

*vaitānikā vikarmasthā na te bhāṣyāḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*taistu dṛṣṭaistathā kāryaṃ bhāskarasyāvalokanam \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Sacrificers, doing wrong acts, should never be talked to. If they see one, one should look at the sun (to be free from the sin).

## \|\| 14.134 \|\|

*aṃgasparśe kṛte rudra sacailo jalamāviśet \|*  
*evaṃ śuddhimavāpnoti pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭāṃ manīṣibhiḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. O Rudra, if they touch one’s body, one should, with one’s garments on, enter water. Thus one obtained purity as formerly observed by the wise.

## \|\| 14.135 \|\|

*sa bhavānbrahmahantāsi śuddhyarthaṃ vratamācara \|*  
*cīrṇe vrate punarbhūyaḥ prāpsyasi tvaṃ varānbahūn \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Such as you are, you are the murderer of a brāhmaṇa; observe a vow for (getting) purity. On your having observed a vow you will obtain many boons.

## \|\| 14.136 \|\|

*evamuktvā gato brahmā rudrastannābhijajñivān \|*  
*aciṃtayattadāviṣṇuṃ dhyānagatyā tataḥ svayaṃ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Having spoken thus Brahma went away. Rudra did not understand that. He then meditated on Viṣṇu himself.

## \|\| 14.137 \|\|

*lakṣmīsahāyaṃ varadaṃ devadevaṃ sanātanam \|*  
*aṣṭāṃgapraṇipātena devadevastrilocanaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Trilocana (i.e. Rudra), the god of gods, bowing, saluting, with the eight parts of the body, touching the ground, praised (Viṣṇu), the eternal god, giver of boons, accompanied by Lakṣmī and the holder of the conch, disc and mace.

## \|\| 14.138-139 \|\|

*tuṣṭāva praṇato bhūtvā śaṃkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*rudra uvāca \|*  
*paraṃ parāṇāmamṛtaṃ purāṇaṃ parātparaṃ viṣṇumanaṃtavīryaṃ \|\| 138 \|\|*

*smarāmi nityaṃ puruṣaṃ vareṇyaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ niṣpratimaṃ purāṇam \|*  
*parātparaṃ pūrvajamugravegaṃ gaṃbhīragaṃbhīradhiyāṃ pradhānam \|\| 139 \|\|*

Rudra said:

138-139. I mentally recall Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa who is immortal through continuous series, who is old, who has infinite power, who is eternal, is the most distinguished person, is matchless, is greater than the greatest, the first-born and very powerful and is the chief among those whose intellect is inscrutable and profound.

## \|\| 14.140 \|\|

*natosmi devaṃ harimīśitāraṃ parātparaṃ dhāmaparaṃ ca dhāma \|*  
*parāparaṃ tatparamaṃ ca dhāma parāpareśaṃ puruṣaṃ viśālam \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. I salute god Hari, the controller, the greatest abode, the supreme place, that highest and distinguished resort, the highest lord and the huge being.

## \|\| 14.141 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ staumi viśuddhabhāvaṃ parāparaṃ sūkṣmamidaṃ sasarja \|*  
*sadāsthitatvātpuruṣapradhānaṃ śāṃtaṃ pradhānaṃ śaraṇaṃ mamāstu \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. I (shall) praise Nārāyaṇa, of a pure nature, (who) created this high and low and the subtle. (I praise him who) being always present (everywhere) is the highest person, calm and prominent. Let him be my refuge.

## \|\| 14.142-143 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ vītamalaṃ purāṇaṃ parātparaṃ viṣṇumapārapāram \|*  
*purātanaṃ nītimatāṃ pradhānaṃ dhṛtikṣamāśāṃtiparaṃ kṣitīśam \|\| 142 \|\|*

*śubhaṃ sadā staumi mahānubhāvaṃ sahasramūrddhānamanekapādam \|*  
*anaṃtabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetraṃ kṣarākṣaraṃ kṣīrasamudranidram \|\| 143 \|\|*

142-143. I (shall) always praise Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa, free from impurity, old, greater than the greatest, having no end, ancient, chief among the prudent, given to courage, forgiveness and peace, the lord of the earth, auspicious, of great prowess, having a thousand heads and many feet and innumerable hands, having the moon and the sun as his eyes, of the nature of the mobile and the immobile, lying in the ocean.

## \|\| 14.144 \|\|

*nārāyaṇaṃ staumi paraṃ pareśaṃ parātparaṃ yattridaśairagamyam \|*  
*trisargasaṃsthaṃ trihutāśanetraṃ tritatvalakṣyaṃ trilayaṃ trinetram \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. I (shall) praise Nārāyaṇa, the supreme one, the highest lord, greater than the greatest, who cannot be approached (even) by gods, living in the three creations, having three principles, absorbed in three and having three eyes.

## \|\| 14.145-146 \|\|

*namāmi nārāyaṇamaprameyaṃ kṛte sitaṃ dvāparataśca raktam \|*  
*kalau ca kṛṣṇaṃ tamatho namāmi sasarja yo vaktrata eva viprān \|\| 145 \|\|*

*bhujāṃtarātkṣatramathoruyugmādviśaḥ padāgrācca tathaiva śūdrān \|*  
*namāmi taṃ viśvatanuṃ purāṇaṃ parātparaṃ pāragamaprameyam \|\| 146 \|\|*

145-146. I salute the immeasurable Nārāyaṇa white in the Kṛta (yuga), red in the Dvāpara (yuga) and black in the Kali (yuga); I salute him who from his very mouth, created the Brāhmaṇas. (I salute him who created) the Kṣatriyas from his arms, (created) the Vaiśyas from his two thighs and the Śūdras from the tips of his feet. I salute him having the universe as his body, profoundly learned and infinite.

## \|\| 14.147 \|\|

*sūkṣmamūrttiṃ mahāmūrttiṃ vidyāmūrttimamūrtikam \|*  
*kavacaṃ sarvadevānāṃ namasye vārijekṣaṇam \|\| 147 \|\|*
