(Saying) ‘Salutation to Ardhanārīśvara’, he should worship (Śiva, and should worship) the nose (of the image of Gaurī, saying) ‘Salutation to you, O you of white complexion.’ He should worship Lokeśa (the lord of the worlds saying) ‘Salutation to Ugra’, and should worship the eye-brows (of Gaurī’s image saying) ‘Salutation to you, O Lalitā’.

## \|\| 29.28 \|\|

*śarvāya puraharttāraṃ vāsudevyai tathālakam \|*  
*namaḥ śrīkaṃṭhanāthāya śivakeśāṃstathārcayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. He should worship Purāhartā (saying) ‘Salutation to Śarva’, and should worship the (image’s hair saying:) ‘Salutation to Vasudevī’. (Saying) ‘Salutation to Śrīkaṇṭhanātha’, he should worship Śiva’s hair.

## \|\| 29.29-34 \|\|

*bhīmograbhīmarūpiṇyai śiraḥ sarvātmane namaḥ \|*  
*haramabhyarcya vidhivatsaubhāgyāṣṭakamagrataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*sthāpayetsnigdhaniṣpāvānkusuṃbhakṣīrajīrakam \|*  
*tarurājekṣulavaṇaṃ kustuṃburumathāṣṭamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*dadyātsaubhāgyakṛdyasmātsaubhāgyāṣṭakamityuta \|*  
*evaṃnivedya tatsarvamagrataḥ śivayoḥ punaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*caitre śṛṃgāṭakānprāśya svapedbhūmāvariṃdama \|*  
*punaḥ prabhāte ca tathā kṛtasnānajapaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*saṃpūjya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ mālyavastraṃ vibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*saubhāgyāṣṭakasaṃyukta sauvarṇaṃ pratimādvayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*prīyatāṃ metra lalitā brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvattṛtīyāyāṃ sadā nṛpa \|\| 34 \|\|*

29-32a. Saying ‘Salutation to Bhīmarūpiṇī, of a terrible and fierce form, and to Sarvātman’, having duly worshipped Hara and the group of eight objects causing good fortune he should place them before him. (They are:) greasy beans, saffron, milk, cuminseeds, tāla, sugarcane, salt and gourd as the eighth. He should offer this group of eight ‘saubhāgya’ (to a brāhmaṇa), as it causes good fortune. Having thus presented all that in front of Śiva and Pārvatī, he should eat Śṛṅgāṭakas in Caitra, and should sleep on the (bare) ground, O you tamer of enemies.

32b-34a. Then again in the morning, having bathed and muttered sacred texts (and thus having become) pure, and having honoured a brāhmaṇa couple with flowers, clothes and ornaments, he should give a couple of golden images (of Śiva and Pārvatī) along with the eight auspicious things to a brāhmaṇa, (saying) ‘May Lalitā be pleased here (i.e. as a result of this vow) with me’.{GL\_NOTE::}

34b. O king, he should always do like this on the third (day of every month) for a year.

## \|\| 29.35 \|\|

*prāśane dānamaṃtre ca viśeṣoyaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*gośṛṃgāṃbu madhau proktaṃ vaiśākhe gomayaṃ punaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Listen to the speciality (that lies) in eating (Śṛṅgāṭakas etc.) and in the sacred text used at the time of making an offering. In Caitra water (flowing from) a cow’s horns is recommended while in Vaiśākha cowdung is recommended.

## \|\| 29.36 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe maṃdārakusumaṃ bilvapatraṃ śucau smṛtam \|*  
*śrāvaṇe dadhisaṃprāśyaṃ nabhasye tu kuśodakam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Mandāra-flower is recommended in Jyeṣṭha, and bilva-leaf in Āṣāḍha. In Śrāvaṇa curds should be eaten and water flowing from darbhas should be drunk.

## \|\| 29.37 \|\|

*kṣīraṃ cāśvayuje māsi kārttike pṛṣadājyakam \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣe tu gomūtraṃ pauṣe saṃprāśayedghṛtam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In the month of Āśvina milk should be drunk, and ghee mixed with coagulated milk should be eaten in Kārtika. He should drink cow-urine in Mārgaśīrṣa, and ghee in Pauṣa.

## \|\| 29.38-39 \|\|

*māghe kṛṣṇatilāṃstadvatpaṃcagavyaṃ ca phālgune \|*  
*lalitā vijayā bhadrā bhavānī kumudā śivā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vāsudevī tathā gaurī maṃgalā kamalā satī \|*  
*umā ca dānakāle tu prīyatāmiti kīrttayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. He should eat black sesamum in Māgha and the five products of cow in Phālguna; and at the time of making an offering he should say: ‘May Lalitā, Vijayā, Bhadrā, Bhavānī, Kumudā, Śivā, Vāsudevī and also Gaurī, Maṅgalā, Kamalā, Satī and Umā be pleased’.

## \|\| 29.40 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu dvādaśe māsi dvādaśyāṃ kṛṣṇamarcayet \|*  
*tathā lakṣmīṃ ca tatraiva bhartrā sārdhamathārcayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Then in the twelfth month he should worship Kṛṣṇa on the twelfth day; similary he should worship Lakṣmī along with her husband there only (i.e. on the same day).

## \|\| 29.41 \|\|

*paurṇamāsyāmatastadvatsapatnīkaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*upāsanīyo viduṣā paratrā bhītimicchatā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. A wise man desiring his well-being in the next world should similarly worship Brahmā with his wife on the full-moon day.

## \|\| 29.42-43 \|\|

*saubhāgyāṣṭakaṃ tadvacca dātavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|*  
*mallikāśokakamalaṃ kadaṃbotpalacaṃpakam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kubjakaṃ karavīraṃ ca bāṇamamlānapaṃkajam \|*  
*siṃduvāraṃ ca sarveṣu māseṣu kusumaṃ smṛtam \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Similarly desiring his well-being he should give the Saubhāgyāṣṭaka (i.e. the group of eight things leading to good fortune). (He should also offer) the flowers of mallikā (i.e. jasmine) and of aśoka, lotuses, kadamba flowers, blue lotuses, campaka flowers, flowers of kubjaka, karavira, bāṇa, and fresh lotuses. Sinduvāra flowers and (other) flowers are recommended in all the months.

## \|\| 29.44 \|\|

*japākusuṃbhakusumaṃ mālatī śatapatrikā \|*  
*yathālābhaṃ praśastāni karavīraṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The flowers of japā (i.e. the china roses), safflowers, flowers of mālatī, śatapatra and karavīra flowers when available are always recommended.

## \|\| 29.45-48 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ yāvadupoṣya vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*strī ca naktaṃ kumārī ca śivamabhyarcya bhaktitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vratāṃte śayanaṃ dadyātsarvopaskarasaṃyutam \|*  
*umāmaheśvarau haimau vṛṣabhaṃ ca gavā saha \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sthāpayitvā ca śayanaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ vatsaraṃ tvekaṃ mahālakṣmyā ca keśavam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*brahmāṇaṃ saha sāvitryā pūjayitvā narastviha \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti manasā samabhīpsitān \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-46a. Thus, for one year, a man or a woman or a maiden, having duly observed a fast at night and having devoutly worshipped Śiva for a year, should give a fully furnished bed at the end of the vow.

46b-47a. Having placed on the bed golden images of Umā and Maheśvara, and also (the image of) a bull with a cow he should offer it to a brāhmaṇa.

47b-48. A man, who, for one year on the twelfth day (of every month) worships Keśava with Mahālakṣmī, and Brahmā with Sāvitrī fulfils all desires that he thinks of.

## \|\| 29.49-51 \|\|

*anyānyapi yathāśakti mithunānyaṃbarādibhiḥ \|*  
*dhānyālaṅkāragodānairanyaiśca dhanasañcayaiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*vittaśāṭhayena rahitaḥ pūjayedgatavismayaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ karoti yaḥ samyaksaubhāgyaśayanavratam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti padaṃ vā nityamaśnute \|*  
*phalasyaikasya ca tyāgametatkurvansamācaret \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-50a. He, free from vanity of wealth and free from pride, should worship other couples (i.e. couples of images of other deities), according to his capacity, with garments, grains, ornaments and gifts of cows and other large quantities of valuables.

50b-51. He, who properly observes the vow of Saubhāgyaśayana, obtains all desired things and an eternal position. He should, while observing this vow, abandon eating one fruit each month.

## \|\| 29.52-58 \|\|

*yaśaḥ kīrtimavāpnoti pratimāsaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*saubhāgyārogyarūpaiśca vastrālaṃkārabhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*na viyukto bhavedrājansaubhāgyaśayanapradaḥ \|*  
*yastu dvādaśavarṣāṇi saubhāgyaśayanavratam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*karoti sapta cāṣṭau vā brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*pūjyamāno vasetsamyakyāvatkalpāyutaṃ naraḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*viṣṇorlokamathāsādya śivalokagatastathā \|*  
*nārī vā kurute yā tu kumārī vā nareśvara \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sāpi tatphalamāpnoti devyanugrahalālitā \|*  
*śṛṇuyādapi yaścaiva pradadyādathavā matim \|\| 56 \|\|*

*sopi vidyādharo bhūtvā svargaloke ciraṃ vaset \|*  
*idamiha madanena pūrvasṛṣṭaṃ śatadhanuṣā ca kṛtaṃ nareṇa tadvat \|\| 57 \|\|*

*kṛtamatha pavanena naṃdinā ca kimu jananāthamahādbhutaṃ na vā syāt \|\| 58 \|\|*

52-53a. O king, he (then) gets success and fame. O king, he who makes gifts at the vow of Saubhāgya-śayana, is not separated from good fortune, good health, handsome form, garments, ornaments and decorations.

53b-55a. He, who observes the vow of Saubhāgya-śayana for twelve years, or for seven or eight years, is honoured in in Brahmā’s world. Then having reached the world of Viṣṇu and that of Śiva, and being honoured there he duly lives there for a couple of Kalpas.

55b-56a. O lord of men, a lady or a maiden who observes that vow, also, being graced by the favour of Lalitā, gets the same fruit.

56b-58. He too, who listens to (the account of the vow) or intends to observe it, becomes a Vidyādhara, and lives for a long time in heaven. This vow was formerly created (i.e. introduced) by Madana. It was observed by Śatadhanu and Nara, also by Pavana and Nandī. How then, O lord of people, is it not wonderful?’

## Chapter 30 - Origin of Viṣṇu’s steps

## \|\| 30.1-5 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*yajñapavartamāsādya viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|*  
*padāni ceha dattāni kimarthaṃ padapaddhatiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kṛtā vai devadevena tanme vada mahāmate \|*  
*katamo dānavastena viṣṇunā damitotra vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kṛtvā vai padavinyāsaṃ tanme śaṃsa mahāmune \|*  
*svarloke vasatirviṣṇorvaikuṃṭhe'sya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sa kathaṃ mānuṣe loke padanyāsaṃ cakāra ha \|*  
*devalokeṣu vai deva devāḥ seṃdrapurogamāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tapasā mahatā brahmanbhaktā ye satataṃ prabhum \|*  
*śrīvarāhasya vasatirmaharlloke prakīrtitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1-4a. Having reached the sacrificial mountain. the powerful Viṣṇu planted his foot (-steps) there. What is the purpose of this line of the foot (-steps) which the lord of lords planted? O highly intelligent one, tell me (about) that. O great sage, tell me which demon he subdued after having planted his foot (-steps) there. The residence of Viṣṇu is in heaven, the great-souled one lives in Vaikuṇṭha. How is it that he planted his foot (-step) in the human world?

4b-5. O brahman, lords of gods (i.e. great gods) with Indra as their leader, and also devotees who continuously (please) the lord by means of great penance (live in the world of gods). It is said that the residence of Śrīvarāha is in the Mahar-world.

## \|\| 30.6-8 \|\|

*nṛsiṃhasya tathā proktā janaloke mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*trivikramasya vasatistapoloke prakīrtitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*lokānetānparityajya kathaṃ bhūmau padadvayam \|*  
*kṣetre paitāmahe cāsminpuṣkare yajñaparvate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*padāni kṛtavānbrahmanvistarānmama kīrtaya \|*  
*śrutena sarvapāpasya nāśo vai bhavitā dhruvam \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Similarly the residence of Nṛsiṃha, the great-souled one, is said to be in the Jana-world. The residence of Trivikrama is said to be in the Tapas-world. Tell me in detail, O brahman, how (is it that the lord), leaving these worlds, planted his two foot-steps on the earth and (how is it that he) planted his footsteps on the sacrificial mountain in this place, viz. Puṣkara, which is sacred to Brahmā. By hearing (this account) all sins will certainly perish.

## \|\| 30.9 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*samyakpṛcchasi bhostvaṃ yatsaṃśṛṇu tvaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*yathāpūrvaṃ padanyāsaḥ kṛto devena viṣṇunā \|\| 9 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

9\. That you have asked properly, listen attentively to (the account as to how) in olden days, lord Viṣṇu having come to the sacrificial mountain, planted his foot (-step) on the embankment of it.

## \|\| 30.10-20 \|\|

*yajñaparvatamāsādya śilāparvatarodhasi \|*  
*purā kṛtayuge bhīṣma devakāryārthasiddhaye \|\| 10 \|\|*

*viṣṇunā ca kṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ pṛthivyarthe paraṃtapa \|*  
*tridivaṃ sarvamānītaṃ dānavairbalavattaraiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*trailokyaṃ vaśamānīya jitvā devānsavāsavān \|*  
*dānavā yajñabhoktārastatrāsanbalavattarāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kṛtā bāṣkalinā sarve dānavena balīyasā \|*  
*evaṃbhūte tadā loke trailokye sacarācare \|\| 13 \|\|*

*paramārtiṃ yayau śakro nirāśo jīvite kṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa bāṣkalirdānaveṃdro'vadhyoyaṃ mama saṃyuge \|\| 14 \|\|*

*brahmaṇo varadānena sarveṣāṃ tu divaukasām \|*  
*tadahaṃ brahmaṇo loke vṛtaḥ sarvairdivaukasaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ devaṃ gatiranyā na vidyate \|*  
*evaṃ viciṃtya deveṃdro vṛtaḥ sarvairdivaukasaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*jagāma tvarito bhīṣma yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ sa padaṃ prāpya vṛtastaiśca divaukasaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*abravījjagataḥ kāryaṃ prāptāmāpadamuttamām \|*  
*kiṃ na jānāsi vai deva yato no bhayamāgatam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*daityairyadāhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ varadānācca te prabho \|*  
*kathitaṃ vai mayā sarvaṃ bāṣkaleśca durātmanaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kriyatāṃ cāvilaṃbena pitā tvaṃ naḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*tattvaṃ ciṃtaya deveśa śāṃtyarthaṃ jagatastviha \|\| 20 \|\|*

10-12a. O Bhīṣma, formerly in the Kṛtayuga Viṣṇu performed a (mighty) deed for the attainment of gods’ purpose and for the (good of the) earth. The stronger demons, having conquered gods along with Indra, had brought under their control the entire heaven, after subduing the three worlds.

12b-14a. The very mighty demon Bāṣkali had made the stronger demons the enjoyers (of portions) at sacrifices. When the three worlds with the mobile and the immobile were reduced to this condition, Indra, being disappointed with life, became very much distresed.

14b-16a. (He thought:) ‘Due to the grant of boon to him by Brahma, that Bāṣkali, the lord of demons, cannot be killed in a battle by all the residents of heaven. So surrounded (accompanied) by all gods in the world of Brahmā, I shall seek refuge with the lord (i.e. Brahmā). There is no other course.’

16b-18a. O Bhīṣma, thinking thus, the lord of gods, sur

rounded by all residents of heaven, quickly went to Brahmā’s place. Surrounded by those residents of heaven he reached (i.e. touched) the feet of Brahmā and told (i.e. acquainted) him (with) what should be done about the world and also about the worst calamity that had befallen the world.

18b-20. “O god, do you not know wherefrom fear has come to us? O lord, I have told you what the demons have snatched, and also everything of (i.e. done by) that wicked Bāṣkali; you are our grandsire; (so) do (something) without delay (to save us). O lord of gods, think now about some measures for world-peace.

## \|\| 30.21 \|\|

*teṣāṃ ca paśyatāṃ kiṃcicchrautasmārtādikāḥ kriyāḥ \|*  
*na prāvartanta hānistu tairasmākaṃ dinedine \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When they (i.e. the demons) have been watching, the rites laid down in the śrutis and smṛtis have not proceeded. Everyday they are causing harm to us.

## \|\| 30.22 \|\|

*yathā hi prākṛtaḥ kaścitsvārthamuddiśya bhāṣate \|*  
*vijñāpyase tathāsmābhirnirastopakṛtaiḥ sadā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. As an insignificant person speaks about (i.e. gives importance to) his own interest, in the same way, we who have thrown into the background your obligations, have always spoken to (i.e. requested) you.

## \|\| 30.23-24 \|\|

*yadyenopakṛtaṃ yasya sahasraguṇitaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*yo na tasyopakārāya tatkaroti vṛthā matiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tasyopakāradagdhasya nistrapasyāsataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*narakeṣvapi saṃvāsastasya duṣkṛtakāriṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. If a man with a false mind does not do (i.e. return the favour) thousandfold to him who has obliged him, then for that bad and shameless man of wicked action and scorched by obligation there is residence in hell alone.

## \|\| 30.25 \|\|

*naitāvataiva sādhutvaṃ kṛte yātu pratikriyā \|*  
*svārthaikaniṣṭhabuddhīnāmetannāpi pravartate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Goodness does not lie in this much (i.e. in merely) returning an obligation; but those whose minds are bent on selfishness do not do even this (i.e. do not even return a good turn).

## \|\| 30.26 \|\|

*yadyasya nābhavatsthānaṃ jagato hyatra duḥkhadaṃ \|*  
*śatadhā hṛdayaṃ dīrṇaṃ tanna tṛptimupāgatam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. (I wish) if only the stability of the world should not have become a cause of worry; my heart is rent into a hundred (pieces); it is not satisfied (i.e. happy).

## \|\| 30.27 \|\|

*tatra vā yatra gaṃtāsmi nimagnānuddharasva naḥ \|*  
*upāyakathanenāsya yena tejaḥ pravartate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I am going (i.e. wandering) here and there (for help). (Please) drag us up who are drowned (in grief), by telling us a means by which our lustre will again shoot up.

## \|\| 30.28 \|\|

*yathākhyātaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ jagattatsthamavekṣya tām \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkāraṃ nivṛttotsavamaṃgalam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I have told you as I have seen the world. You (can) see it as it is. It is bereft of Vedic studies and the exclamation of Vaṣat. Festivals (and other) auspicious (rites) have ceased.

## \|\| 30.29 \|\|

*tyaktādhyayanasaṃyogaṃ muktavārtā parigraham \|*  
*daṃḍanītyā parityaktaṃ śvāsamātrāvaśeṣitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Contact with study i.e Vedic study has been abandoned (by the brāhmaṇas); agriculture\[1\] is given up; it (i.e. the world) is left by administration of justice; it remains merely in breath (i.e. it is barely alive).

## \|\| 30.30 \|\|

*jagadārtimapi prāptaṃ punaḥ kaṣṭatarāṃ daśāṃ \|*  
*etāvatā hi kālena vayaṃ glānimupāgatāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The world has met with distress; and by (the passing of) this much time we are exhausted.”

## \|\| 30.31 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jānāmi bāṣkaliṃ taṃ tu varadānācca garvitam \|*  
*ajeyaṃ bhavatāṃ manye viṣṇusādhyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 31 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

31\. I know that Bāṣkali has become arrogant as a result of (my) having granted him a boon; I think he cannot be conquered by you; (but) he will be conquerable by Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 30.32-33 \|\|

*nirudhya saṃsthito brahmā bhāvaṃ tatvamayaṃ tadā \|*  
*samādhisthasya tasyaiva dhyānamātrāccaturbhujaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*stokenaiva hi kālena ciṃtyamānaḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*ājagāma muhūrtena sarveṣāmeva paśyatām \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Having restrained (his senses) Brahmā then remained in his original nature (i.e. resumed his usual silence). When the self-born Brahmā was thinking about him, the four-armed one (i.e. Viṣṇu) came there after a while merely as the result of Brahmā’s meditating on him, when all (the gods) were looking on.

## \|\| 30.34 \|\|

*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*bho bho brahmannivarttasva dhyānādasmānnivāritaḥ \|*  
*yadarthamiṣyate dhyānaṃ sohaṃ tvāṃ samupāgataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

Viṣṇu said:

34\. Warded off (by) me, O Brahman, stop this meditation. I, for whom this meditation was intended, have approached you.

## \|\| 30.35 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*mahāprasāda eṣo'tra svāmino hi pradarśanam \|*  
*kasyānyasya bhaveccaiṣā cintā yā jagataḥ prabho \|\| 35 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

35\. It is indeed a great favour that the lord has manifested himself here. Who else would have so much anxiety for the world as the lord has?

## \|\| 30.36 \|\|

*mamaiva tāvadutpattirjagadarthe vinirmitā \|*  
*jagadetattvadarthīyaṃ tattvato nāsti vismayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. For the (good of) the world I brought about its creation. Virtually the world depends upon you. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 30.37-38 \|\|

*bhavatā pālanaṃ kāryaṃ saṃharedrudra eva tu \|*  
*evaṃbhūte jagatyasminśakrasyāsya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ bāṣkalinā trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*bhṛtyasya kriyatāṃ sāhyaṃ maṃtradānena keśava \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. You should protect the world, and Rudra should destory it. When such was the case with the world, Bāṣkali snatched off the kingdom consisting of the three worlds and of the mobile and immobile, of (i.e. from) this great-souled Indra. O Keśava, help your servant by offering him counsel.

## \|\| 30.39 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*bhavato varadānena avadhyaḥ sa tu sāṃpratam \|*  
*buddhisādhyaḥ sa vai kāryo baṃdhanādiha dānavaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

Vāsudeva (i.e. Viṣṇu) said:

39\. That demon (viz. Bāṣkali) has been now immune to being killed due to your having granted him a boon. By captivating him he must be conquered by intelligent handling.

## \|\| 30.40 \|\|

*vāmanohaṃ bhaviṣyāmi dānavānāṃ vināśakaḥ \|*  
*mayā saha vrajatveṣa bāṣkalestu niveśanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I shall be a dwarf, the destroyer of the demons. This one (i.e. Indra) should go with me to Bāṣkali’s residence.

## \|\| 30.41 \|\|

*tatra gatvā varaṃ tveṣa madarthe yācatāmimam \|*  
*vāmanasyāsya viprasya bhūme rājanpadatrayam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Having gone there he should ask him for this boon for me:

## \|\| 30.42 \|\|

*prayacchasva mahābhāga yācñaiṣā tu mayā kṛtā \|*  
*śakreṇokto dānaveṃdro dadyātsvamapi jīvitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. ‘O king, O magnanimous one, give (a piece of) land (measuring) three steps to this short brāhmaṇa. This is the request I make to you’. Asked by Indra the lord of the demons might offer even his own life.

## \|\| 30.43-44 \|\|

*gṛhya pratigrahaṃ tasya dānavasya pitāmaha \|*  
*taṃ badhvā ca tato yatnātkṛtvā pātālavāsinam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*saukaraṃ rūpamāsthāya vadhārthaṃ ca durātmanaḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyāmi na saṃdeho vraja śakra tvarānvitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. O grandsire, having accepted the gift from that demon, having bound him carefully and made him the resident of the nether world, I shall be (born), taking the form of a boar, to kill that wicked one. There is no uncertainty about this. O Indra, move on quickly.

## \|\| 30.45-48 \|\|

*virarāma tamuktvaivamaṃtarddhānaṃ gataśca vai \|*  
*atha kālāṃtare viṣṇāvaditergarbhatāṃ gate \|\| 45 \|\|*

*nimittānyatighorāṇi prādurbhūtānyanekaśaḥ \|*  
*samastajagadādhāre viṣṇau garbhatvamāgate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*śobhanaṃ hi tadā jātaṃ nimittaṃ caivamūrjitam \|*  
*mālatīkusumānāṃ tu sugaṃdhaḥ surabhirvavau \|\| 47 \|\|*

*atha vihitavidhānaṃ kālamāsādya devastridaśagaṇahitārthaṃ sarvabhūtānukaṃpī \|*  
*vimala virala keśaścaṃdraśaṃkhodayaśrīradititanayabhāvaṃ devadevaścakāra \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-46a. Having thus told (Brahmā) he ceased (speaking) and disappeared. Then after some time, when Viṣṇu was conceived by Aditi, many fearful ill omens appeared.

46b-47a. When Viṣṇu, the prop of the entire world, was conceived (by Aditi), an excellent auspicious omen also appeared.

47b-48. Breezes carrying the fragrance of Mālati flowers blew. Then, having reached (i.e. at) the time as ordained, the god, the lord of gods (i.e. Viṣṇu), kind to all beings, of pure and scanty hair, having the beauty of the moon, the conch and the (sun-) rise, became (i.e. was born as) Aditi’s son.

## \|\| 30.49 \|\|

*avatarati ca viṣṇau siddhadevāsurāṇāmanimiṣanayanānāṃ viprasedurmukhāni \|*  
*ativiratarajobhirvāyubhiḥ saṃvahadbhirdinamapi ca tadāsījjanma viṣṇoḥ sugarbhe \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. When Viṣṇu thus descended (on the earth), the faces of Siddhas, gods and demons with the winkings of their eyes stopped, were pleased; and that day, too, on which Viṣṇu got into that excellent womb, was having breezes, of scanty pollen, blowing (gently).

## \|\| 30.50 \|\|

*aditirajanagarbhā sāpi devī prayāṃtī natajaghanabharārttā maṃdasaṃcāraramyā \|*  
*alasavadanakhedaṃ pāṃḍubhāvaṃ vahaṃtī gurutaramavagāḍhaṃ garbhamevodvahaṃtī \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. That respectable Aditi also, having the unborn one (i.e. Viṣṇu) in her womb, walked charmingly, distressed by her heavy hips. Her face was dull, gloomy and pale. Thus she carried the embryo that was heavier and was (lying) low (in her womb).

## \|\| 30.51 \|\|

*tataḥ praviṣṭe khalu garbhavāsaṃ nārāyaṇe bhūtabhaviṣyayogāt \|*  
*vināpadaṃ prāptamanorathāni bhūtāni sarvāṇi tadā babhūvuḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. When, Nārāyaṇa thus entered the womb (of Aditi) as a result of the past and future (deeds), all beings got their desires fulfilled without any difficulty.

## \|\| 30.52-53 \|\|

*samīraṇo vāti ca maṃdamaṃdaṃ patatsu varṣeṣu nagodbhaveṣu \|*  
*viviktamārgeṣu digaṃtareṣu janeṣu vai satyamupāgateṣu \|\| 52 \|\|*

*vimucyamāne gagane rajobhiḥ śanaiśśanairnaśyati cāṃdhakāre \|*  
*udarāṃtargate viṣṇau drohabuddhistadābhavat \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. (When) the wind was blowing very gently; and (when) indeed people had gone to other regions by isolated paths; when the sky was being deserted by dust-particles and when darkness was gradually disappearing; (and) when Viṣṇu was in (Aditi’s) womb, that mother of gods entertained a malicious design.

## \|\| 30.54-55 \|\|

*tāṃ niśāmaya rājeṃdra devamāturyathākramam \|*  
*kimanukramaṇenaiva laṃghayāmi triviṣṭapam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bāṣkaliṃ dānaveṃdraṃ taṃ kuryāṃ pātālavāsinam \|*  
*śakrasya tu mayā dattaṃ dhanaṃ lāvaṇyameva ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Listen to it, O lord of kings, in succession: “What is the use of proceeding in order? I shall spring over the heaven; and I shall make that Bāṣkali, the lord of demons, the resident of the nether world. I have (already) given wealth and handsomeness to Indra.

## \|\| 30.56 \|\|

*dānavānāṃ vināśāya ekaiva prabhavāmyaham \|*  
*kṣipāmi śarajālāni cakrayānānyanekaśaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. I alone shall be able to destroy the demons. I shall throw (at them) volleys of arrows and trains of discs in many ways.

## \|\| 30.57-58 \|\|

*gadāvrātāṃśca vividhāndānavānāṃ vināśane \|*  
*vibudhāndevalokasthānadhobhūmestu dānavān \|\| 57 \|\|*

*karomi kālayogena tattu kāryaṃ vratena me \|*  
*nissṛtā sahasā vāṇī vaktramevābhisaṃsthitā \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58a. (I shall also discharge) multitudes ofmaces for the destruction of the demons; and as fate would have it, I shall make gods the residents of heaven and the demons the residents of the nether region”.

58b. (Thus) the words that were (lingering) in her mouth at once came out.

## \|\| 30.59 \|\|

*yenedaṃ cintyate pūrvaṃ yanna dṛṣṭaṃ na ca śrutam \|*  
*baṃdhaṃ vai danumukhyasya kṛtaṃ kopena paśya me \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. “See (now), I shall, through anger, bind the chief of the demons in such a way as was not thought of before, nor seen before nor (also) heard of before.

## \|\| 30.60 \|\|

*kaśyapāya purā dattaṃ dhanaṃ lāvaṇyameva ca \|*  
*kimayaṃ vigatotsāho vāyavotha samākulāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Formerly I have given wealth and handsomeness to Kaśyapa. Why has he lost his energy and (why is) the wind gusty?

## \|\| 30.61 \|\|

*bhramatīva hi me dṛṣṭirmaitadrūpaṃ praciṃtitam \|*  
*āviṣṭā kimahaṃ vacmi kenāpyasadṛśaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. My eyes are as it were reeling; let me not have conceived this form. By what am I possessed that I am uttering these improper words?”

## \|\| 30.62 \|\|

*vikalpavaśamāpannā'bhīkṣṇaṃ hṛdimamarśa sā \|*  
*dadhāra divyaṃ varṣāṇāṃ sahasraṃ divyamīśvaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Got into (i.e. caught between) alternatives she repeatedly reflected in her heart. She carried (in her womb) the divine lord for a thousand divine years.

## \|\| 30.63 \|\|

*tataḥ samabhavattasyāṃ vāmano bhūtavāmanaḥ \|*  
*jātena yena cakṣūṃṣi dānavānāṃ hṛtāni vai \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Then Vāmana (i.e. Viṣṇu), the cause of the beings, was born of her—(Vāmana) who, when born, attracted the eyes of the demons.

## \|\| 30.64 \|\|

*jātamātre tatastasmindevadeve janārdane \|*  
*nadyaḥ svacchāṃbuvāhinyo vavau gaṃdhavaho'nilaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. As soon as that Janārdana, the god of gods, was born, rivers flowed with clear water, and fragrant breezes blew.

## \|\| 30.65-66 \|\|

*kaśyapopi sukhaṃ lebhe tena putreṇa bhāsvatā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ mānasotsāhastrailokyāṃtaravāsinām \|\| 65 \|\|*

*saṃjātamātre tu tato janādhipajanārdane \|*  
*svargaloke duṃdubhayo vinedustaiśca tāḍitāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Kaśyapa too obtained pleasure due to that bright son. O lord of men, no sooner was Janārdana born, than the minds of all the residents of the three worlds were full of enthusiasm, and kettle-drums that were beaten in heaven gave out sounds.

## \|\| 30.67-68 \|\|

*atipraharṣāttu jagattrayasya mohaśca duḥkhāni ca nāśamīyuḥ \|*  
*jago ca gandharvagaṇotimātraṃ bhāvasvarairbhartṛvimiśritāśca \|\| 67 \|\|*

*surāṅganāścāpi ca bhāvayuktā nṛtyaṃti tatrāpsarasāṃ samūhāḥ \|*  
*tathaiva vidyādharasiddhasaṃghā vimānayānairmuditā bhramaṃti \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Due to extreme joy the delusion and miseries of the three worlds came to an end. The group of Gandharvas sang with notes full of emotion; and the groups of heavenly damsels, mingling with their lords, and full of emotions, danced there (i.e. in the heaven). In the same way, groups of Vidyādharas and Siddhas wandered in (i.e. being seated in) aeroplanes.

## \|\| 30.69-71 \|\|

*vadaṃti satyānṛtakāryanirṇayaṃ tathābhiraṃgaṃ pratidarśayaṃti \|*  
*gāyaṃti geyaṃ vinivṛttarāgā muhurmuhurduḥkhasukhaprabhūtāḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nṛtyaṃti vai svargagatāśca te tu dharmārjitaṃ svargamito vrajaṃti \|*  
*iti vigataviṣāde nirmale jīvaloke timiranikaramuktā nirvṛtiṃ prāptukāmāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tatrocuḥ kecidurvyāṃ jayajaya bhagavansaṃprahṛṣṭāśca kecit \|*  
*tvevaṃ proktapraṇādairavirala manasaścānuvādaistathānyaiḥ \|*  
*dhyāyaṃtenye nigūḍhaṃ jananabhaya jarāmṛtyuvicchedaheto \|*  
*rityevaṃ kṛtsnamāsījjagadidamakhilaṃ sarvataḥ saṃpṛhṛṣṭam \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. They discussed the verdict about good and bad deeds and exhibited acting and singing. Free from passions and full of pain and pleasure they sang songs, and being in the heaven they danced and (i.e. since they) have gone to the heaven from here after having obtained it by dint of their religious merit. Then some, being very much delighted, uttered (the words:) ‘Victory (to you), O lord’. Others, with a steady mind, repeated these words loudly. Others secretly meditated upon him through fear of (re-) birth and for the destruction of old age and death. Thus the entire world was fully delighted.

## \|\| 30.72-73 \|\|

*paramāsādya yaṃ viṣṇuṃ brahmāha jagataḥ kṛte \|*  
*jātoyaṃ bhavatāmarthe vāmano yadapīśvaraḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*eṣa brahmā ca viṣṇuśca eṣa eva maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*eṣa vedāśca yajñāśca svargaścaiṣa na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. (It was said:) ‘Though a dwarf, this is the lord, who has been born for you, and after having approached whom, Brahmā had told (i.e. requested) about the (well-being of the) world. This one (i.e. he) is Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara (i.e. Śiva) himself; also be is the sacrifices; he is the heaven. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 30.74 \|\|

*viṣṇuvyāptamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam \|*  
*ekaḥ sa tu pṛthktvena svayaṃbhūriti viśrutaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. This entire world—immobile and mobile—is pervaded by Viṣṇu. He, the self-born one, though one only, is known to be many.

## \|\| 30.75 \|\|

*yathārthavarṇake sthāne vicitraḥ sphāṭiko maṇiḥ \|*  
*tato guṇavaśāttasya svayaṃbhoranuvarttanam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The crystal-gem is (i.e. appears) variegated at a place where there are colours (which get reflected in the gem). The self-born one behaves in the same way (i.e. appears to be many) due to (his contact with) the constituents (like sattva, rajas and tamas).

## \|\| 30.76 \|\|

*yathā hi gārhapatyogniranyasaṃjñāṃ punarvrajet \|*  
*labheta saṃjñāṃ bhagavānbrāhmādiṣu tathā hyasau \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. As the Gārhapatya fire gets another name, similarly this lord gets appellations like Brahmā etc.

## \|\| 30.77-80 \|\|

*sarvathā vāmano devo devakāryaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*evaṃ ciṃtayatāṃ teṣāṃ bhāvitānāṃ divaukasām \|\| 77 \|\|*

*jagāma śakrasahito bāṣkaleśca niveśanam \|*  
*dūrādeva ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā purīṃ tasya samāvṛtām \|\| 78 \|\|*

*pāṃḍuraiḥ khagamāgamyaiḥ sarvaratnopaśobhitaiḥ \|*  
*śobhitāṃ bhavanairmukhyaissuvibhaktamahāpathaiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*nityaprabhinnairmātaṃgairaṃjanācalasannibhaiḥ \|*  
*devanāgakulotpannaiḥ śatasaṃkhyairvirājitām \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-78a. By all means god Vāmana will accomplish this feat (of subduing Bāṣkali).’ When the residents of heaven were thus thinking and reflecting, (Viṣṇu), with Indra, went to Bāṣkali’s residence.

78b-80. Having seen (i.e. he saw) the city adorned with prominent white buildings approachable by Gandharvas, and decorated with all (kinds of) jewels, and well-separated (from one another) by big roads; (it was) adorned with hundreds of elephants always in rut, resembling the mountain of collyrium, and born in the family of divine elephants.

## \|\| 30.81 \|\|

*nirmāṃsagātraisturagairalpakarṇairmanojavaiḥ \|*  
*dīrghagrīvākṣikūṭaiśca manojñairupaśobhitām \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. (It was also) adorned with horses with bodies having (almost) no flesh (i.e. having slim bodies), having small ears, having the speed of the mind, having long necks and long prominent parts of the foreheads above the eyes.

## \|\| 30.82 \|\|

*padmagarbhasuvarṇābhāḥ pūrṇacaṃdranibhānanāḥ \|*  
*saṃllāpollāpakuśalāstatra veśyāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. There were thousands of courtesans having excellent complexion like the interiors of lotuses, having faces resembling the full moon, and skilled in conversation and caressing.

## \|\| 30.83 \|\|

*na tatpuṇyaṃ na sā vidyā na tacchilpaṃ na sā kalā \|*  
*bāṣkalerna pure'syātha nivāsaṃ pratigacchati \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. There was no religious merit, no lore, no architecture, no art that did not exist (i.e. that was not found) in the city of this Bāṣkali.

## \|\| 30.84-86 \|\|

*udyānaśatasaṃbādhaṃ samājotsavamālini \|*  
*anvite danumukhyaiśca sarvairaṃtakavarjitaiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*vīṇāveṇumṛdaṃgānāṃ śabdaiḥ sarvatra nādite \|*  
*sadā prahṛṣṭā danujā bahuratnopaśobhitāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*krīḍamānāḥ pradṛśyaṃte merāviva yathāmarāḥ \|*  
*brahmaghoṣo mahāṃstatra danuvṛddhairudīritaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. It was crowded with hundreds of gardens. In it having a series of social festivals, endowed with all chief demons except Yama, resounding everywhere with sounds of lutes, flutes and tabors, sons of Danu, always joyful, decorated with many jewels, were seen sporting likegods on the Meru mountain. There was a great sound of (the recitation of) the Vedas made by the venerable demons.

## \|\| 30.87-88 \|\|

*sājyadhūmena cāgnīnāṃ vāyunā naṣṭakilbiṣe \|*  
*sugaṃdhadhūpavikṣepa surabhīkṛtamārute \|\| 87 \|\|*

*sugaṃdhidanujākīrṇe pure tasmiṃstu bāṣkali \|*  
*trailokyaṃ tu vaśe kṛtvā sukhenāste sa dānavaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. That demon Bāṣkali having subdued the three worlds lived happily in that city, the sins in which were destroyed by the smoke of the ghee of (i.e. put into) fires, and by wind, in which the breezes were made fragrant by the moving about of the fragrant incense, and which was crowded with virtuous demons.

## \|\| 30.89-90 \|\|

*tatrasthaḥ pālayannāste trailokyaṃ sacarācaraṃ \|*  
*dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca satyavādī jiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*sudarśaḥ pūrvadevānāṃ nayānayavicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇyaśca śaraṇyaśca dīnānāmanukaṃpakaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Living there he protected the three worlds along with the mobile and the immobile. He was conversant with righteousness, was grateful, truth-speaking, and had his senses controlled, was handsome, and knew the good and bad ways of life of the ancient gods. He was well-versed in the Vedas, was a protector and was kind to the distressed.

## \|\| 30.91-92 \|\|

*vedamaṃtraprabhūtsāha sarvaśaktisamanvitaḥ \|*  
*ṣāḍguṇyaviṣayotsāhaḥ smitapūrvābhibhāṣitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*vedavedāṃgatatvajño yajñayājī taporataḥ \|*  
*na ca duḥśīlanirataḥ sa sarvatrāvihiṃsakaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. He was endowed with all the (regal) powers\[5\] like the Vedic, that of good counsel, personal preeminence and energy. He was interested in the six measures to be practised by a king, and talked with a smile. He knew the essence of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, performed sacrifices and was engaged in (practising) penance. He was not ill-mannered and always abstained from causing harm to others.

## \|\| 30.93 \|\|

*mānyamānayitā śuddhaḥ sumukhaḥ pūjyapūjakaḥ \|*  
*sarvārthavidanādhṛṣyaḥ subhagaḥ priyadarśanaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. He honoured those who deserved honour, was pure, pleasing, and worshipped the venerable. He knew all objects; he was invincible, agreeable and of a pleasing appearance.

## \|\| 30.94 \|\|

*bahudhānyo bahudhano bahuyānaśca dānavaḥ \|*  
*trivargasādhako nityaṃ trailokye varapūruṣaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The demon had ample grains, wealth, and vehicles. He always accomplished the three objects (of worldly existence). He was the best person in the three worlds.

## \|\| 30.95-102 \|\|

*svapurīnilayo nityaṃ devadānavadarpahā \|*  
*sa caivaṃ pālayāmāsa trailokye sakalāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*nādhamaḥ kaścidapyāste tasminrājani dānave \|*  
*dīno vā vyadhito vāpi alpāyurvātha duḥkhitaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*mūrkho vā maṃdarūpo vā durbhago vā nirākṛtaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ yutaṃ taṃ vimalairguṇaughairdṛṣṭvā ca matvā ca niviṣṭabuddhiṃ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*prasādayandaityavaraṃ mahātmā puraṃdarastaṃ tu danupradhānaṃ \|*  
*tejoyuktaṃ dānavaṃ taṃ tapaṃtamiva bhāskaraṃ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*trailokyadhāraṇe śaktaṃ vismitaḥ so'bhavattadā \|*  
*iṃdraṃ purāgataṃ dṛṣṭvā dānaveṃdrāya pārthiva \|\| 99 \|\|*

*idamūcustadāgatvā dānavā yuddhadurmadāḥ \|*  
*āścaryamiti vai kṛtvā iṃdrobhyeti purīṃ tava \|\| 100 \|\|*

*ekākī dvijamukhyena vāmanena saha prabho \|*  
*asmābhiryadanuṣṭheyaṃ sāṃprataṃ no vadasva rāṭ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*dānavānabravītsarvānpure tiṣṭhata saṃkulaṃ \|*  
*praveśyatāṃ devarājaḥ pūjyaḥ sa tu mamādya vai \|\| 102 \|\|*

95-97a. He always lived in his own city and always removed the pride of gods and demons. In this way he protected all the beings in the three worlds. When he was the king (i.e. in his kingdom) there was no mean person, no poor person, no sick person, no short-lived person, no unhappy person, no foolish person, no person of a dull form, no unfortunate person, nor a person that was expelled.

97b-99a. Seeing that excellent chief of the demons, who was endowed with multitudes of pure qualities and who was bright like the sun, and taking him to be a person of a controlled mind, and capable of sustaining the three worlds, Indra was amazed.

99b-100a. O king, seeing Indra to have entered the city the demons maddened for fight, said this to the lord of demons:

100b-101a. “It is something strange that Indra is doing when he, all alone, except being accompanied by a short preeminent brāhmaṇa, is coming.

101b-102. O king, tell us what we should do now.” He said to all the demons: “Assembled together you remain in the city. Let the lord of gods enter the city. Today he is to be honoured by me.”

## \|\| 30.103 \|\|

*etasminneva kāle tu vāmanaḥ sa ca vāsavaḥ \|*  
*āgatau danunāthena premṇā caivāvalokitau \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. In the meantime that short (brāhmaṇa) and Indra arrived there; they were looked at affectionately by the lord of demons.

## \|\| 30.104 \|\|

*kṛtārthaṃ manyatātmānaṃ praṇipātapuraḥsaram \|*  
*uvāca vacanaṃ rājā dānavānāṃ dhuraṃdharaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. He regarded himself as blessed and the king, the leader of the demons said (to them) after saluting them:

## \|\| 30.105-106 \|\|

*adya vai triṣu lokeṣu nāsti dhanyataro mayā \|*  
*yohaṃ śriyāvṛtaḥ śakraṃ paśyāmi gṛhamāgatam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*arthitvakāmyayā yastu māmayaṃ yācayiṣyati \|*  
*gṛhāgatasya tasyāhaṃ dāsye prāṇānapi dhruvam \|\| 106 \|\|*

105-106. “Today, in the three worlds, there is no person who is luckier than I, who, chosen by Glory, am seeing Indra coming (to me). With a desire to receive something from me he will beseech me. I shall certainly give (up) even my life for him who has come to my house.

## \|\| 30.107-108 \|\|

*dārānputrāṃstathāgāraṃ trailokye kā kathā mama \|*  
*āgatya saṃmukhaṃ tasya aṃkamānīya sādaram \|\| 107 \|\|*

*pariṣvajyābhinandyainaṃ gṛhaṃ prāveśayatsvakam \|*  
*tasya svāgatamarghyādyaiḥ kṛtvā pūjāṃ prayatnataḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

107a. (I shall even give up) my wife, sons, and also my residence. What then should I say (even) about the three worlds?”

107b-108. Going to meet him, and bringing him near himself with respect, and embracing and greeting him, and carefully offering him welcome and worship with materials of worship etc. he brought him (i.e. Indra) into his house.

## \|\| 30.109 \|\|

*adya me saphalaṃ janma pūrṇāḥ sarve manorathāḥ \|*  
*yastvāṃ paśyāmi śakrādya svayameva gṛhāgatam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. (He said:) “Today my birth is fruitful, all my desires are fulfilled, that, O Indra, I am seeing you who have visited my house.

## \|\| 30.110 \|\|

*khyāpyohaṃ danumukhyānāṃ devarāja tvayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*āgacchatā mama gṛhaṃ puṇyatā tu parā hi me \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. O lord of gods, I have (today indeed) been proclaimed to be the king of demons by you who have come to my house. It is my great religious merit.

## \|\| 30.111 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādibhiryajñaissamyagiṣṭaistu yatphalam \|*  
*tatphalaṃ samavāpyeta tvayi dṛṣṭe puraṃdara \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. O Purandara, one would get that fruit, which is obtained by sacrifices like the Agniṣṭoma, on seeing you.

## \|\| 30.112 \|\|

*yatphalaṃ bhūmidānena gavāṃ dānena ṛtvije \|*  
*mamādya tatphalaṃ bhūtamathavā rājasūyakam \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. I have today obtained that fruit which is obtained by the grant of land, or of cows to a priest, or (the fruit that is obtained by the performance) of the Rājasūya sacrifice.

## \|\| 30.113 \|\|

*nālpena tapasā labhyaṃ darśanaṃ tava vāsava \|*  
*evaṃ gehe mayā yatte priyaṃ kāryaṃ taducyatām \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. O Vāsava, you are not to be seen by little penance. Tell me what I can do, that is dear to you, in my house.

## \|\| 30.114 \|\|

*vikalpo'nyo na bhavatā hṛdi kāryaḥ kathaṃcana \|*  
*kṛtaṃ ca tadvijānīyā yadyadi syātsuduṣkaraṃ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Do not entertain any other doubt in your heart. Know that it shall be done even if it is very difficult.

## \|\| 30.115 \|\|

*puṇyohaṃ puṇyatāṃ prāpto darśanāttava śatruhan \|*  
*yatte deva varairvaṃdyau vaṃditau caraṇau mayā \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. O you, killer of enemies, I am lucky, I have obtained religious merit on having seen you, since I have saluted your feet adored by excellent gods.

## \|\| 30.116 \|\|

*kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ te vada sarvaṃ mayi prabho \|*  
*atyāścaryamidaṃ manye tavāgamana kāraṇaṃ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. O lord, tell (me) all that has made you come (to me). I take the intention of your arrival to be a great surprise (your arrival has caused surprise).”

## \|\| 30.117 \|\|

*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*jānehaṃ danumukhyānāṃ pradhānaṃ tvāṃ tu bāṣkale \|*  
*nātyāścaryamidaṃ bhāti tvayi dṛṣṭe'surottama \|\| 117 \|\|*

Indra said:

117\. O Bāṣkali, I know you to be the chief among the pre-eminent demons. It is not a great surprise to have seen you, O best of the demons.

## \|\| 30.118 \|\|

*vimukhā nārthino yāṃti bhavato gṛhamāgatāḥ \|*  
*arthināṃ kalpavṛkṣosi dātā cānyo na vidyate \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Suppliants who have visited your house never go (back) being averse (i.e. disappointed). You are the desire-yielding tree to the suppliants. There is no other donor (like you).

## \|\| 30.119 \|\|

*prabhāyāṃ sūryatulyosi gāṃbhīrye sāgaropamaḥ \|*  
*sahiṣṇutve dharā caiva śriyā nārāyaṇopamaḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. In lustre you (i.e. as far as lustre is concerned) arc comparable to the sun; in (i.e. as far as) depth (i.e. seriousness is concerned), you are the earth and in (i.e. as far as) wealth (is concerned) you are like Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 30.120 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaḥ kaśyapakule jātoyaṃ vāmanaḥ śubhe \|*  
*prārthitohamanenaivaṃ bhūmerdehi padatrayaṃ \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. This short brāhmaṇa is born in the auspicious family of Kaśyapa.

## \|\| 30.121 \|\|

*mamāgniśaraṇārthāya yatra kuryāṃ makhaṃ tvahaṃ \|*  
*tadasya kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā arthitaiṣā mama prabho \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. I was requested by him: “Give here (a piece of) land measuring the distance covered by three steps, to me who want a fire-sanctuary where I would perform a sacrifice.” I have, therefore, O lord, asked you on his behalf.

## \|\| 30.122-123 \|\|

*lokatrayaṃ me'pahṛtaṃ tvayā vikramya bāṣkale \|*  
*nirvṛttiko nirdhanosmi yadditse na tadasti me \|\| 122 \|\|*

*bhavaṃtaṃ yācayiṣyāmi parārthenāpi cātmanā \|*  
*arthittvena mamāpyasya yadyogyaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. O Bāṣkali, having overpowered (me) you have taken away the three worlds belonging to me. I have nothing to subsist upon; I am poor; I do not want for myself what you desire to give. For someone else I am going to beseech you as a suppliant (does). For this (brāhmaṇa) I have turned a suppliant. Do what is proper.

## \|\| 30.124 \|\|

*jātosi kāśyape ca tvaṃ vaṃśe vaṃśavivarddhanaḥ \|*  
*dityāstvaṃ garbhasaṃbhūtaḥ pitā trailokapūjitaḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. You, who have exalted the family, are born in the family of Kaśyapa. You are born from the womb of Diti and your father is revered in the three worlds.

## \|\| 30.125-126 \|\|

*evaṃbhūtamahaṃ jñātvā tena tvāṃ yācayāmyaham \|*  
*asyāgniśaraṇārthāya dīyatāṃ bhū padatrayam \|\| 125 \|\|*

*atīva hrasvagātrasya vāmanasyāsya dānava \|*  
*bhūmibhāge ca pārakye dātuṃ na tvahamutsahe \|\| 126 \|\|*

125-126. Knowing that you are like this I am requesting you. O demon, give a piece of land measuring three footsteps to this one (i.e. this brāhmaṇa)—this dwarf, with short limbs, who desires to have a fire-sanctuary.

## \|\| 30.127 \|\|

*etadeva mayā dattaṃ yadbhavānarthitosi me \|*  
*guravo yadi manyaṃte maṃtriṇo vā padatrayam \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. I do not dare to give the portion of land belonging to someone else. This is what is given (i.e. what is said) by me since you asked me to ask for something. You may give the piece of land measuring three steps if yourpreceptors and ministers agree.

## \|\| 30.128 \|\|

*arthitvena madīyena svakule bāṃdhavepi ca \|*  
*gṛhāyāte mayi tathā yadyogyaṃ tatsamācara \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. When I, your kinsman of the same family have come to your house as a suppliant, do what is proper.

## \|\| 30.129 \|\|

*yadi te rucitaṃ vīra dānaveṃdra mahādyute \|*  
*tadasmai dīyatāṃ śīghraṃ vāmanāya mahātmane \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. O you hero, O you lord of demons, O you of great lustre, if you like then quickly give (a piece of land) to this short, great-souled (brāhmaṇa).

## \|\| 30.130 \|\|

*bāṣkaliruvāca \|*  
*deveṃdra svāgataṃ te'stu svasti prāpnuhi mā ciram \|*  
*tvaṃ samīkṣasvadhātmānaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca parāyaṇam \|\| 130 \|\|*

Bāṣkali said:

130\. O lord of gods, welcome and well-being to you. With pleasure look upon yourself as the highest object of all.

## \|\| 30.131 \|\|

*tvayi bhāraṃ samāveśya sukhamāste pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*dhyānadhāraṇayāyuktaściṃtayānaḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. The grandsire, having placed the burden (i.e. the responsibility of looking after the three worlds), given to meditation and reflecting upon the highest position, lives happily.

## \|\| 30.132 \|\|

*saṃgrāmairbahubhiḥ khinno jagacciṃtāmapāsya tu \|*  
*kṣīrābdhidvīpamāśritya sukhaṃ svapiti keśavaḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Keśava(i.e. Viṣṇu), exhausted due to (having fought) many battles, after having given up anxiety about the world, and after having gone to the milky ocean, sleeps (there) happily.

## \|\| 30.133 \|\|

*anye ca dānavāḥ sarve balinaḥ sāyudhāstvayā \|*  
*asahāyenaiva śakra sarvepi vinipātitāḥ \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. O Śakra, even all other powerful demons having weapons were destroyed by you without (the help of) anybody else.

## \|\| 30.134-137 \|\|

*ādityā dvādaśaiveha rudrāstvekādaśāpi vā \|*  
*aśvinau vasavaścaiva dharmaścaiva sanātanaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

*tvadbāhubalamāśritya tridive makhabhāginaḥ \|*  
*tvayā kratuśatairiṣṭaṃ samāptavaradakṣiṇaiḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

*tvayā ca ghātito vṛtro namuciḥ pākaśāsana \|*  
*tvadājñākāriṇā pūrvaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 136 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśiporbhrātā hiraṇyākṣopi ghātitaḥ \|*  
*hiraṇyakaśipuryotra jaṅghe cāropya ghātitaḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

134-135a. The twelve Ādityas, the eleven Rudras, the two Aśvins, the Vasus and eternal Dharma are enjoying the portions of sacrifice in the heaven (only because they have) resorted to the power of your arms.

135b-136a. You have performed a hundred sacrifices endowed with excellent sacrificial fees; and O Pākaśāsana, you killed Vṛtra Namuci.

136b-137. Powerful Viṣṇu, who obeyed your order, formerly also killed Hiraṇyākṣa, the brother of Hiraṇyakaśipu. He also killed Hiyaṇyakaśipu by striking on his shank.

## \|\| 30.138 \|\|

*vajrapāṇinamāyāṃtamairāvaṇaśirogatam \|*  
*saṃgrāmabhūmau dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ sarve naśyaṃti dānavāḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. All demons seeing you, when you, with the thunderbolt in your hand and seated on the head of Airāvata, come to the battle-field, flee away.

## \|\| 30.139 \|\|

*ye tvayā vijitāḥ pūrvaṃ dānavā balavattarāḥ \|*  
*sahasrāṃśena tattulyo na bhavāmi kathaṃcana \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. In no way shall I be even equal to one-thousandth part of you who formerly defeated the very powerful demons.

## \|\| 30.140 \|\|

*evaṃvidho'si deveṃdra mama kā gaṇanā bhavet \|*  
*māṃ samuddhartukāmena tvayaivāgamanaṃ kṛtam \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. O lord of gods, you are like this. What need I say about you? You have arrived here with a desire to emancipate me.

## \|\| 30.141 \|\|

*kariṣyāmi na saṃdeho dāsye prāṇānapi dhruvam \|*  
*kimarthaṃ devarājoktā bhūmireṣā tvayā hi me \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. I shall do (what you tell me). There is no doubt that I shall even give up life. For what purpose, O lord of gods, you have asked me to give this land?

## \|\| 30.142 \|\|

*ime dārāḥ sutā gāvo yaccānyadvidyate vasu \|*  
*trailokyarājyamakhilaṃ viprasyāsya pradīyatām \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. Let all these—mywife, sons, cows, and whatever other wealth I have, and also this entire kingdom of the three worlds be given to this brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 30.143 \|\|

*apakīrtirbhavenmahyaṃ pūrveṣāṃ ca na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*gṛhāyātasya śakrasya dattaṃ bāṣkalinā na tu \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. There is no doubt that infamy will accrue to me and my ancestors, viz. ‘Bāṣkali did not give to Śakra (what he asked for and) who had come to his house.’

## \|\| 30.144 \|\|

*anyopi yorthī me prāptaḥ same priyataraḥ sadā \|*  
*bhavānatra viśeṣeṇa vicāraṃ mā kṛthāḥ kvacit \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Even if some other suppliant had come here, he would be dearer to me. You are especially so. Do not hesitate at all.

## \|\| 30.145 \|\|

*bṛhattrapā me deveṃdra yadbhūmestu padatrayam \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa prārthitaṃ tu tvayā vibho \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. O lord, O god of gods, it causes me great shame that you have asked only for a piece of land measuring three steps and that too for the sake of a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 30.146-147 \|\|

*dāsye grāmavarānasya bhavatastu triviṣṭapam \|*  
*aśvāngajānbhūmidhanaṃ striyaścodbhinnacūcukāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

*yāsāṃ darśanamātreṇa vṛddhopi taruṇāyate \|*  
*tāḥ striyo vasudhāṃ caitāṃ vāmanasya pratigraham \|\| 147 \|\|*

146-147. I shall give this brāhmaṇa excellent villages and will give you heaven; (I shall give him) horses, elephants, land. wealth and ladies with sprout-like breast-nipples, seeing whom even an old man becomes young. The brāhmaṇa will receive those ladies and this earth.

## \|\| 30.148-149 \|\|

*pratidāsyāmi devendra prasādaḥ kriyatāṃ hi me \|*  
*etāvadukte vacane tadā bāṣkalinā nṛpa \|\| 148 \|\|*

*purodhāstūśanā prāha dānaveṃdraṃ tadā vacaḥ \|*  
*bhavānrājā dānaveṃdra aiśvaryeṣṭavidhe sthitaḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

148-149a. I shall give (these things), O lord of gods. (Please) favour me (by accepting them).

When, O king, Bāṣkali had said these words, his family priest Uśanas (i.e. Śukra) said these words to the lord of demons:

149b. “O lord of demons, you are a king remaining in (i.e. having) eightfold prosperity.

## \|\| 30.150-151 \|\|

*yuktāyuktaṃ na jānāsi deyaṃ kasya mayā kvacit \|*  
*maṃtribhiḥ susamālocya yuktāyuktaṃ parīkṣya ca \|\| 150 \|\|*

*prāptaṃ trailokyarājyatvaṃ jitvā devānsavāsavān \|*  
*vākyasyāsyāvasāneva bhavānprāpsyati baṃdhanaṃ \|\| 151 \|\|*

150-151. (But) you do not realize what is proper and what is improper. (You also do not understand): ‘I should give something to someone after having consultations with my ministers and after having assessed what is proper and what is improper’. Having conquered the gods along with Indra you have obtained the kingdom of the three worlds. (Just) as the sentence (I am speaking) is over you will be made a captive.

## \|\| 30.152-153 \|\|

*ya eṣa vāmano rājanviṣṇureva sanātanaḥ \|*  
*nāsya vai bhavatā deyaṃ pitā te ghātitaḥ svayaṃ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*ayaṃ te pitṛhā prāpto mātṛhā baṃdhughātakaḥ \|*  
*vaṃśocchedakarastubhyaṃ bhūtaścaiva bhaviṣyati \|\| 153 \|\|*

152-153. This dwarf is that eternal Viṣṇu only. Do notgive (anything) to him. This is the one who is the killer of your father, mother, and relatives. He has formerly cut off (i.e. destroyed) your family and will do the same in future.

## \|\| 30.154 \|\|

*na caiṣa dharmaṃ jānāti śakrādīnāṃ hite rataḥ \|*  
*māyāvinā dānavā ye māyayā yena nirjitāḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. Interested in the well-being of Śakra and others he does not know (i.e. does not care for) moral merit. He is the deceitful one who vanquished the demons with trickery.

## \|\| 30.155 \|\|

*māyayā brāhmaṇaṃ rūpaṃ vāmanaṃ ca pradarśitam \|*  
*atra kiṃ bahunoktena nāsya deyaṃ tu kiṃcana \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. He has manifested this form of a dwarfish brāhmaṇa through trickery (only). What is the use of prolixity in this matter? Nothing should be given to him.

## \|\| 30.156 \|\|

*makṣikāpādamātraṃ tu bhūmirasya pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*vināśameṣyasi kṣipraṃ satyaṃsatyaṃ mayā śrutam \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. You will perish even if you give a (particle of) land measuring just the foot of a bee. This is the truth, the only truth I have heard about.”

## \|\| 30.157 \|\|

*guruṇāpyevamuktastu bhūyo vākyamathābravīt \|*  
*dharmārthinā mayā sarvaṃ pratijñātaṃ guro tvidam \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Even though he was thus addressed by his preceptor he again spoke (these) words: “O preceptor, desiring religious merit I have made this promise.

## \|\| 30.158 \|\|

*pratijñāpālanaṃ kāryaṃ satāṃ dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*yadyeṣa bhagavānviṣṇurnāsti dhanyataro mayā \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. It is the eternal duty of the good to keep their promise. If this is revered Viṣṇu then there is none else luckier than I (am).

## \|\| 30.159 \|\|

*gṛhya pratigrahaṃ matto yadi devānbubhūṣati \|*  
*bhūyopi dhanyatāṃ nīto devenānena vai guro \|\| 159 \|\|*

159\. (Even) after receiving a gift from me he (still) desires to become (i.e. to be called) a god, (then) I O preceptor, again made blessed by this god.

## \|\| 30.160 \|\|

*yaṃ yogino dhyānayuktā dhyāyamānā hi darśanam \|*  
*na labhaṃte tathā viprāssoyaṃ dṛṣṭo mayādya vai \|\| 160 \|\|*

160\. I have seen him, whom the devotees meditating on him with concentration and the brāhmaṇa also, do not see.

## \|\| 30.161-163 \|\|

*dānāni ye prayacchaṃti sakuśodakapāṇinā \|*  
*prīyatāṃ bhagavānviṣṇuḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*evamukte tu vacane apavargasya bhāginaḥ \|*  
*yadatra kāryakaraṇe vikalpo me babhūva ha \|\| 162 \|\|*

*upadiṣṭosmi bhavatā bālatve cāvadhāritam \|*  
*śatrāvapi gṛhāyāte māstvadeyaṃ tu kiṃcana \|\| 163 \|\|*

161-163. They, who give gifts with darbhas and water in their hands and utter the sacred text, ‘May the revered Viṣṇu, the highest soul and the eternal one, be pleased,’ share (i.e. obtain) salvation. If there was any doubt doing this act (of giving, it was because) I was advised and was determined to be a fool by you. There is nothing that should not be given even to an enemy when he comes to one’s house.

## \|\| 30.164-172 \|\|

*etadeva viciṃtyāhaṃ prāṇānapi svakānguro \|*  
*vāmanasya pradāsyāmi śakrasyāpi triviṣṭapam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*apīḍākāri yaddānaṃ taddānamiha dīyate \|*  
*pīḍākāri ca yaddānaṃ taddānaṃ samalaṃ smṛtam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*etacchrutvā gurustatra trapayādhomukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*bāṣkaliruvāca \|*  
*arthitā bhavato deva deyā sarvā dharā mayā \|\| 166 \|\|*

*trapākaraṃ bhavenmahyaṃ yadasya bhūpadatrayam \|*  
*iṃdra uvāca \|*  
*satyametaddānavendra yaduktaṃ bhavatā hi me \|\| 167 \|\|*

*bhūmeḥ padatrayārthitvaṃ dvijenānena me kṛtam \|*  
*etāvatā tvayaṃ cārthī mayāpyasya kṛte bhavān \|\| 168 \|\|*

*danuputro yācitosi varametatpradīyatām \|*  
*bāṣkaliruvāca \|*  
*padatrayaṃ vāmanāya devarāja pratīccha me \|\| 169 \|\|*

*tatra tvaṃ suciraṃ kālaṃ sukhī surapate vasa \|*  
*evamuktvā bāṣkalinā vāmanāya padatrayam \|\| 170 \|\|*

*toyapūrvaṃ tadā dattaṃ prīyatāṃ me hariḥ svayam \|*  
*datte tu dānaveṃdreṇa tyaktvā rūpaṃ ca vāmanam \|\| 171 \|\|*

*harirācakrame lokāndevānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*yajñaparvatamāsādya gatvā caiva udaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 172 \|\|*

164-166a. O preceptor, having given thought to this, I shall give even my life to this dwarf and heaven to Indra. In this world that gift which causes suffering is said to be impure.” Having heard this, the preceptor remained there with his face hung down in shame.

Bāṣkali said:

166b-167a. O god, when you have asked for (a gift of land) I should give you the entire earth. It would be shameful to me to give him (the piece of) land measuring three (foot-) steps.

Indra said:

167b-169a. O lord of demons, these words which you have said to me are true; (but) this brāhmaṇa has asked me for a piece of land measuring three (foot-) steps (only). He has asked me for this much land; and I have (therefore) asked you to give that much (only). You, the son of Danu, have thus been implored by me. Grant me this boon.

Bāṣkali said:

169b-1 70a. O King of gods, accept from me (the piece of land measuring) three (foot-) steps for (this) dwarf; (and) O lord of gods, live there (i.e. in the heaven) happily for a very long time.

170b-17la. Saying so, Bāṣkali then gave (the piece of land measured by) three (foot-) steps to the dwarf, after (pouring) water (on his hand), saying, ‘Let Hari himself be pleased with me.’

171 b-172. Desiring the well-being of gods, Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu), when he was given the gift by the lord of demons, gave up the dwarf-form and with his face turned towards the north, he having reached the sacrificial mountain, took possession of the worlds.

## \|\| 30.173 \|\|

*devasya vāmacaraṇe niviṣṭo dānavālayaḥ \|*  
*tatra kramaṃ sa prathamaṃ dadau sūrye jagatpatiḥ \|\| 173 \|\|*

1 73. The residence of the demons came to be put under the god’s left foot. Then the lord of the world first put his step on the Sun.

## \|\| 30.174 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ ca dhruve devastṛtīyena ca pārthiva \|*  
*brahmāṃḍastāḍitastena devenādbhutakarmaṇā \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. He placed the second step on Dhruva, and with the third, the god of wondrous deeds, struck the universe.

## \|\| 30.175-176 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhāgreṇa bhinneṃḍe jalaṃ bhūri viniḥsṛtam \|*  
*plāvayitvā brahmalokānsarvānlokānanukramāt \|\| 175 \|\|*

*dhruvasthānaṃ sūryalokaṃ plāvya taṃ yajñaparvatam \|*  
*praviṣṭā puṣkaraṃ dhārā dhautvā viṣṇupadāni sā \|\| 176 \|\|*

175-176. When the universe was pierced with the tip ofhis toe profuse water flowed out. That stream, having inundated all Brahmā-worlds one by one, and also the place of Dhruva, the world of the Sun, and the sacrificial mountain, entered, having washed Viṣṇu’s feet, the Puṣkara (Tīrtha).

## \|\| 30.177-178 \|\|

*padāni yāni jātāni vaiṣṇavāni dharātale \|*  
*tatrāśrame tu yo gatvā snānaṃ vāpyāṃ samācaret \|\| 177 \|\|*

*aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya darśanādeva jāyate \|*  
*ekaviṃśagaṇopeto vaikuṃṭhe vāsamāpnuyāt \|\| 178 \|\|*

177-178. He, who, having gone to (the spot) where the footprints were produced on the earth, bathes in the well in the hermitage (there), gets the fruit of the Aśvamedha (sacrifice) merely by seeing (the spot). With the group of the twenty-one attendants he obtains (i.e. reaches) Vaikuṇṭha.

## \|\| 30.179 \|\|

*bhuktvā tu vipulānbhogānkalpānāṃ tu śatatrayam \|*  
*tadaṃte jāyate rājā sārvabhaumaḥ kṣitāviha \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Then having enjoyed many pleasures (there) for three hundred Kalpas, he, at the end of it (i.e. that period), becomes a sovereign emperor on this earth.

## \|\| 30.180 \|\|

*toyadhārā tu sā bhīṣma aṃguṣṭhāgrādviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*nadī sā vaiṣṇavī proktā viṣṇupādasamudbhavā \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. O Bhīṣma, the stream of water that flowed out from the tip of (Viṣṇu’s) toe, is called the river Viṣṇupadī (since) it sprang up from Viṣṇu’s foot.

## \|\| 30.181 \|\|

*anena kāraṇenābhūdgaṃgā viṣṇupadī nṛpa \|*  
*yayā sarvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. For this reason (i.e. this is the reason why), O king Gaṅgā became (i.e. came to be known as) Viṣṇupadī, which has pervaded all this universe along with the mobile and the immobile.

## \|\| 30.182 \|\|

*aṃguṣṭhāgrakṣatādaṃḍādyatpraviṣṭaṃ jalaṃ śubham \|*  
*prāptaṃ devanadītvaṃ tu yātu viṣṇupadī nadī \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. That auspicious water, which entered (Puṣkara after flowing out) from the wound (i.e. the hole made into) the universe caused by the tip of (Viṣṇu’s) toe, obtained the status of a divine river. It is that river called Viṣṇupadī.

## \|\| 30.183 \|\|

*devanadyā tayā vyāptaṃ brahmāṃḍaṃ sacarācaram \|*  
*vibhūtibhirmahābhāga sarvānugrahakāmyayā \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. O you illustrious one, that divine river, with a desire to favour all, has occupied the universe with the mobile and immobile, by means of its splendours.

## \|\| 30.184 \|\|

*sa bāṣkalirvāmanena uktaḥ pūraya me kramān \|*  
*adhomukhastadā jāta uttaraṃ nāsya viṃdati \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Vāmana said to that Bāṣakali: “(Now) fill out (i.e. give space for) my steps”. He hung down his face (as) he did not find an answer (i.e. a solution).

## \|\| 30.185-187 \|\|

*maunībhūtaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā purodhā vākyamabravīt \|*  
*svābhāvikī dānaśaktirna tu sraṣṭuṃ vayaṃ kṣamāḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

*yāvatīyaṃ dharā deva sā dattānena te prabho \|*  
*ukto bāṣkalinā viṣṇuryāvanmātrā vasuṃdharā \|\| 186 \|\|*

*yā sṛṣṭā bhavatā pūrvaṃ sā mayā na ca gopitā \|*  
*alpābhūmirbhavāndīrgho na tu sṛṣṭerahaṃ kṣamaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

185-186a. Seeing him silent the family-priest (i.e. Śukra) said (these) words: “The power of giving is natural (i.e. it cannot be increased and so) we are not able to create (another earth where Vāmana could put his steps). O lord, he has given you whatever land exists.”

186b-187. Bāṣkali said to Viṣṇu: “That much earth (i.e. of that extent) which you formerly created (has beengiven to you); I have not held it back. The earth is small (and) you are great; (and) I am not capable of creation.

## \|\| 30.188 \|\|

*icchāśaktiḥ prabhavati prabhoste deva sarvadā \|*  
*niruttarastadā viṣṇurmatvā taṃ satyavādinam \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. O lord, your will power always prevails.” Viṣṇu, finding no reply, and taking him to be truth-speaking, (said to him):

## \|\| 30.189-190 \|\|

*brūhi dānavamukhya tvaṃ kaṃ te kāmaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*mama hastagataṃ toyaṃ tvayā dattaṃ tu dānava \|\| 189 \|\|*

*tena tvaṃ varayogyosi varāṇāṃ bhājanaṃ śubhaṃ \|*  
*dāsyehaṃ bhavataḥ kāmamarthīyena vṛṇuṣva ha \|\| 190 \|\|*

189-190. “O chief of the demons, tell me, which desire (entertained) by you I should satisfy. Since I have in my hand the water offered by you, you, deserve a boon. You are an auspicious receptacle of boons. I shall give what you desire. Ask for the object of your desire.”

## \|\| 30.191-193 \|\|

*vijñapto hi tadā tena devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*bhaktiṃ vṛṇomi deveśa tvaddhastānmaraṇaṃ hi me \|\| 191 \|\|*

*vrajāmi śvetadvīpaṃ te durlabhaṃ tu tapasvinām \|*  
*āhaivamukte viṣṇustaṃ tiṣṭhasvaiva yugāṃtaram \|\| 192 \|\|*

*vārāharūpī yadāhaṃ pravekṣyāmi dharātalam \|*  
*tadā haniṣyehaṃ tvāṃ tu madagre ca yadaiṣyasi \|\| 193 \|\|*

191-193. He (i.e. Bāṣkali) then requested Janādana, the lord of gods: “O, lord of gods, I seek devotion to you and death at your hands. I shall enter Śvetadvīpa, which is inaccessible to the ascetics.” When he spoke thus, Viṣṇu, said to him: “Do remain (there) till the end of the age of the world. When I, taking the boar-form, shall enter (i.e. come to) the earth, I shall kill you when you will come before me.”

## \|\| 30.194 \|\|

*uktotha dānavastena apāsarppattadagrataḥ \|*  
*vāmanena samākrāṃtāḥ sarve lokāstadā nṛpa \|\| 194 \|\|*

194\. The demon, thus addressed by him, went away from him. Then, O king, Vāmana occupied all worlds.

## \|\| 30.195 \|\|

*asuraistaistadā tyaktaṃ devānāṃ satyabhāṣaṇam \|*  
*devo hṛtvā tu trailokyaṃ jagāmādarśanaṃ vibhuḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

195\. Those demons then gave up speaking truthfully with gods. The powerful lord, having snatched the three worlds, disappeared.

## \|\| 30.196 \|\|

*pātālanilayaścāpi sukhamāste sa bāṣkali \|*  
*śakropi pālayāmāsa vipaścidbhuvanatrayam \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. Bāṣkali lived happily in the nether world where he took residence. The wise Indra also protected the three worlds.

## \|\| 30.197 \|\|

*ayaṃ traivikramo nāma prādurbhāvo jagadguroḥ \|*  
*gaṃgāsaṃbhavasaṃyuktassarvakalmaṣanāśanaḥ \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. This manifestation of the lord of the world is called Traivikrama. It is connected with the rise of the Ganges and is the destroyer of all sins.

## \|\| 30.198 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ padānāmeṣā te utpattiḥ kathitā nṛpa \|*  
*yāṃ śrutvā tu naro loke sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 198 \|\|*

198\. O king, I have told you this origin of the steps of Viṣṇu hearing which a man becomes free from all sins.

## \|\| 30.199 \|\|

*duḥsvapnaṃ durviciṃtyaṃ ca duḥṣkaraṃ duḥṣkṛtāni ca \|*  
*kṣipraṃ hi nāśamāyāṃti dṛṣṭe viṣṇupadatraye \|\| 199 \|\|*

199\. At the sight of the three steps of Viṣṇu, (the effects of) an evil dream, an evil thought, a difficult or bad deed perish quickly.

## \|\| 30.200-202 \|\|

*yugānukramaśo dṛṣṭvā pāpino jaṃtavastathā \|*  
*sūkṣmatā darśitā bhīṣma viṣṇunā padadarśane \|\| 200 \|\|*

*yastvārohati tasmiṃstu maunavānmānavo bhuvi \|*  
*kṛtvā tripuṣkarī yātrāmaśvamedhaphalaṃ vrajet \|\| 201 \|\|*

*mucyate sarvapāpaiśca mṛto viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet \|\| 202 \|\|*

200-202. Sinful beings (have emancipated themselves) age after age after having seen (the steps of Viṣṇu). O Bḥīṣma, Viṣṇu has shown ingenuity in manifesting the steps. A man, who, observing silence, climbs up (the mountain) and takes up the pilgrimage of Puṣkara gets the fruit of Aśvamedha (sacrifice). He is free from all sins and would goto Viṣṇu’s city.

## Chapter 31 - The account of Śivadūtī

## \|\| 31.1-2 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*bhagavanmahadāścaryaṃ bāṣkalerbaṃdhanaṃ hi yat \|*  
*kṛtaṃ trivikramaṃ rūpaṃ yadā saṃyamito bali \|\| 1 \|\|*

*etanmayā śrutaṃ pūrvaṃ kathyamānaṃ dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*pātāle vasatedyāpi vairocanasuto bali \|\| 2 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1-2. O revered one, the killing of Bāṣkali is a great wonder I have heard (the account) being narrated by best brāhmaṇas (that Viṣṇu) had taken the form of Trivikrama (i.e. Vāmana) when he had formerly subdued Bali, the son of Vairocana who even now stays in Pātāla.

## \|\| 31.3 \|\|

*nāgatīrthaṃ yathābhūtaṃ piśācānāṃ tu saṃbhavam \|*  
*śivadūtī kathaṃ cātra keneyaṃ maṃgalīkṛtā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. (Tell me now as to) how Nāgatīrtha came into being, and also (tell me about) the origin of goblins, and how Śivadūti came there and who made her auspicious.

## \|\| 31.4 \|\|

*aṃtarikṣe puṣkaraṃ tu kena nītaṃ mahāmune \|*  
*etadācakṣva me sarvaṃ yathā bāṣkalibaṃdhanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. O great sage (tell me) who took Puṣkara into the intermediate space. Tell me all this as (you told me) about the killing of Bāṣkali.

## \|\| 31.5 \|\|

*bhūmiprakramaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ devena viṣṇunā \|*  
*dvitīye kāraṇaṃ kiṃ ca yena devaścakāra ha \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Formerly (i.e. when he subdued Bali) god Viṣṇu had trodden upon the earth. What is the reason for the second treading for which he (again) did it?

## \|\| 31.6 \|\|

*tattvatastvaṃ hi tatsarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ tathā vada \|*  
*pāpakṣayakaraṃ hyetacchrotavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Tell me all that accurately and as it took place, for it destroys sins, and should be heard by him who desires his well-being.

## \|\| 31.7 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*praśnabhārastvayā rājankautukādeva kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*kathayāmi hi tatsarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nṛpottama \|\| 7 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

7\. O king, you have put on me this load (i.e. volley) of questions through curiosity only. O best king, I shall tell you all as it happened.

## \|\| 31.8 \|\|

*viṣṇoḥ padānuṣaṃgeṇa baṃdhanaṃ bāṣkaleriha \|*  
*śrutaṃ tadbhavatā sarvaṃ mayā te parikīrtitaṃ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The subduing of Bāṣkali (took place) in connection with the steps of Viṣṇu. You have heard all that. I have narrated all that to you.

## \|\| 31.9-10 \|\|

*bhūyopi viṣṇunā bhīṣma prāpte vaivasvateṃtare \|*  
*trailokyaṃ balinākrāṃtaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*gatvā tvekākinā yajñe tathā saṃyamito bali \|*  
*bhūyopi devadevena bhūmeḥ prakramaṇaṃ kṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. When the age of Vaivasvata (Manu) set in, Viṣṇu again did it. The three worlds were occupied by Bali. Powerful Viṣṇu, having gone all alone, subdued Bali like that in a sacrifice. The lord of gods again trod upon the earth.

## \|\| 31.11 \|\|

*prādurbhāvo vāmanasya tathābhūto narādhipa \|*  
*punastrivikramo bhūtvā vāmano bhūdavāmanaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O king, Vāmana appeared like that. Vāmana having become Trivikrama, again became Avāmana (non-Vāmana).

## \|\| 31.12 \|\|

*utpattireṣā te sarvā kathitā kurunaṃdana \|*  
*nāgānāṃ tu yathā tīrthaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva mahāvrata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. O you descendant of the Kuru (-family), I have told you all (about) this becoming visible (of Viṣṇu). O you of a great vow, listen as to how the place sacred to the Nāgas (came about).

## \|\| 31.13-15 \|\|

*anaṃto vāsukiścaiva takṣakaśca mahābalaḥ \|*  
*karkoṭakaśca nāgeṃdraḥ padmaścānyaḥ sarīsṛpaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mahāpadmastathā śaṃkhaḥ kulikaścāparājitaḥ \|*  
*ete kaśyapadāyādā etairāpūritaṃ jagat \|\| 14 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ tu prasūtyā tu idamāpūritaṃ jagat \|*  
*kuṭilābhīmakarmāṇastīkṣṇāsyāśca viṣolbaṇāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Ananta, Vāsuki and the very powerful Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka—the chief of Nāgas, and also another Nāga (named) Padma, Mahāpadma, as well as Śaṅkha, and Kulika, the undefeated one: these were the heirs of Kaśyapa and had occupied the world. Their issues also ocoupied this world. These (issues) were crooked, performed fearful acts, had sharp mouths, and were strong with poison.

## \|\| 31.16 \|\|

*daṣṭvā maṃdāṃścamanujānkuryurbhasmakṣaṇāttu te \|*  
*taddarśanādbhavennāśo manuṣyāṇāṃ narādhipa \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Seeing dull persons, they reduced them to ashes in a moment. O king (merely) by seeing them people perished (i.e. died).

## \|\| 31.17-27 \|\|

*ahanyahani jāyeta kṣayaḥ paramadāruṇaḥ \|*  
*ātmanastu kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvā prajāssarvāssamaṃtataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jagmuḥ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ brahmāṇaṃ parameśvaraṃ \|*  
*imamevārthamuddiśya prajāḥ sarvā mahīpate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ūcuḥ kamalajaṃ dṛṣṭvā purāṇaṃ brahmasaṃjñakam \|*  
*prajā ūcuḥ \|*  
*devadeveśa lokānāṃ prasūte parameśvara \|\| 19 \|\|*

*trāhi nastīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāṇāṃ bhujagānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*dinedine bhayaṃ deva paśyāmaḥ kṛpaṇā bhṛśam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*manuṣyapaśupakṣyādi tatsarvaṃ bhasmasādbhavet \|*  
*tvayā sṛṣṭiḥ kṛtā deva kṣīyate tu bhujaṃgamaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*etajjñātvā yaducitaṃ tatkuruṣva pitāmaha \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ rakṣāṃ vidhāsyāmi bhavatīnāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vrajadhvaṃ svaniketāni nīrujo gatasādhvasāḥ \|*  
*evamukte prajāḥ sarvā brahmaṇā'vyaktamūrtinā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*ājagmuḥ paramaprītāḥ stutvā caiva svayaṃbhuvam \|*  
*prayātāsu prajāsvevaṃ tānāhūya bhujaṃgamān \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śaśāpa paramakruddho vāsukipramukhāṃstadā \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*ahanyahani bhūtāni bhakṣyaṃte vai durātmabhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*naśyaṃti tūragairdaṣṭā manuṣyāḥ paśavastathā \|*  
*yasmānmatprabhavānnityaṃ kṣayaṃ nayatha mānuṣān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*atonyasminbhave bhūyānmamakopātsudāruṇāt \|*  
*bhavatāṃ hi kṣayo ghoro bhāvi vaivasvateṃtare \|\| 27 \|\|*

17-18a. Day by day very terrible destruction took place. All the beings seeing their destruction sought refuge with the great god Brahma.

18b-19a. O king, with this object in mind all the beings saw the ancient (god) born from a lotus and named Brahmā and said to him:

19b-22a. The beings said: “O lord of gods, the origin of the worlds, O highest god, protect us from the great-souled serpents of sharp fangs. We, the extremely distressed ones, day by day are seeing (i.e. anticipating) fear. All men, beasts and birds will be reduced to ashes. O god, you fashioned the creation of the world; but that is being destroyed by the serpents. O grandsire, considering this, do what is proper.”

Brahmā said:

22b-23a. I shall undoubtedly protect you. Go to your (respective) residences without anguish and fear.

23b-24a. Thus addressed by Brahmā, who had manifested his form, all the beings, being very much pleased, returned (home) after having praised the self-born one.

24b-25a. When the beings had left, Brahmā who was very angry, called the serpents led by Vāsuki and cursed them.

Brahmā said:

25b-27. The wicked ones are day by day eating the beings. Men and beasts, bitten by serpents, are perishing. (He said to them:) Since you are always destroying the men born of (i.e. created by) me, therefore due to my terrible wrath, you you will meet with a terrible destruction in the future Vaivasvata Manu-ages.

## \|\| 31.28-29 \|\|

*tathānyaḥ somavaṃśīyo rājā vai janamejayaḥ \|*  
*dhakṣyate sarpasatreṇa pradīpte havyavāhane \|\| 28 \|\|*

*mātṛṣvasuśca tanayāṃstārkṣyo vo bhakṣayiṣyati \|*  
*evaṃ vo bhavitā nāśaḥ sarveṣāṃ duṣṭacetasām \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Similarly king Janamejaya, of the Lunar dynasty will burn you in blazing fire by (performing) serpent sacrifice; and the son of your mother’s sister (viz. Garuḍa) will (also) swallow you. Thus all of you of wicked hearts will perish.

## \|\| 31.30-32 \|\|

*śaptvā kulasahasraṃ tu yāvadekaṃ kulaṃ sthitam \|*  
*evamukte tu vepaṃto brahmaṇā bhujagottamāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nipatya pādayostasya idamūcurvacastadā \|*  
*bhagavankuṭilā jātirasmākaṃ bhūtabhāvana \|\| 31 \|\|*

*viṣolbaṇatvaṃ krūratvaṃ daṃdaśūkatvameva ca \|*  
*saṃpāditaṃ tvayā deva idānīṃ śapase kathaṃ \|\| 32 \|\|*

30a. I curse the thousand families (i.e. the effect of my curse will last) till only one family (of the serpents) survives.

30b-3la. When Brahmā spoke like this, the excellent serpents, trembling, fell at the feet of Brahmā and said these words to him):

31b-32. “O revered sir, O you cause of the beings, our species is crooked. O god, you have effected in us profuseness of poison, cruelty and biting. Then how do you curse us now?”

## \|\| 31.33 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yadi nāma mayā sṛṣṭā bhavaṃtaḥ kuṭilāśayāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kiṃ bahunā nityaṃ bhakṣayadhvaṃ gatavyathāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Brahmā said: “Granted that I have made you of crooked hearts. Then, why say much? You (should) always eat without anxiety.";

## \|\| 31.34 \|\|

*nāgā ūcuḥ \|*  
*maryādāṃ kuru deveśa sthānaṃ caiva pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*manuṣyāṇāṃ tathāsmākaṃ samayaṃ deva kāraya \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The serpents said: “O lord of gods, fix a rule and allot separate places (to men and us) and bring about an agreement between men and us.

## \|\| 31.35 \|\|

*śāpo yo bhavatā datto manuṣyo janamejayaḥ \|*  
*nāśaṃ naḥ sarpasatreṇa ulbaṇaṃ ca kariṣyati \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. You have given us this curse that a man (called) Janamejaya will bring about a great destruction of the serpents in a serpent-sacrifice.”

## \|\| 31.36 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*jaratkāruriti khyāto bhavitā brahmavittamaḥ \|*  
*jaratkanyā tasya deyā tasyāmutpatsyate sutaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

36\. There will be a man, best among the knowers of the Veda, by name Jaratkāru. Jaratkanyā will be given to him (in marriage). A son will be born to her.

## \|\| 31.37 \|\|

*rakṣāṃ kartā sa vo vipro bhavatāṃ kulapāvanaḥ \|*  
*tathā karomi nāgānāṃ samayaṃ manujaiḥ saha \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. That brāhmaṇa will be your protector and the purifier of your family. I shall also bring about an agreement between the serpents and men.

## \|\| 31.38-41 \|\|

*tadekamanasaḥ sarve śṛṇudhvaṃ mama śāsanam \|*  
*sutalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva tṛtīyaṃ ca talātalam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*dattaṃ ca triprakāraṃ vo gṛhaṃ tatra gamiṣyatha \|*  
*tatra bhogānbahuvidhānbhuṃjānā mama śāsanāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhadhvaṃ saptamaṃ yāvatkālaṃ taṃ tu punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*tato vaivasvatasyādau kāśyapeyo bhaviṣyati \|\| 40 \|\|*

*dāyādaḥ sarvadevānāṃ suparṇassarpabhakṣakaḥ \|*  
*tadā prasūtiḥ sarpāṇāṃ dagdhā vai citrabhānunā \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-39a. So listen with concentration to my order. I have given you three places of residence, viz. Sutala, Vitala and the third called Talātala. You will go there.

39b-41. By my order, enjoy there pleasures of various kinds. Remain there till the seventh Kala i.e. the kalpa period. Then at the beginning of the Vaivasvata the son of Kaśyapa, Suparṇa the relative of all gods, the devourer of all serpents, will be born.

## \|\| 31.42 \|\|

*bhavatāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*ye ye krūrā bhogino durvinītāsteṣāmaṃto bhāvitā nānyathaitat \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Then the progeny of the serpents will be burnt by fire. There is no doubt that your progeny will be (burnt by fire). Those serpents who are cruel and wicked will perish. This (statement) will not be falsified.

## \|\| 31.43-46 \|\|

*kālavyāptaṃ bhakṣayadhvaṃ ca satvaṃ tathāpakāre cakṛte manuṣyam \|*  
*maṃtrauṣadhairgāruḍaiścaiva taṃtrairbaṃdhairjuṣṭā mānavā ye bhavaṃti \|\| 43 \|\|*

*tebhyo bhītairvartitavyaṃ na cānyaccitte kāryaṃ cānyathā vo vināśaḥ \|*  
*itīrite brahmaṇā vai bhujaṃgā jagmuḥ sthānaṃ sutalākhyaṃ hi sarve \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tasthurbhogānbhuṃjamānāśca sarve rasātale līlayā saṃsthitāste \|*  
*evaṃ śāpaṃ tute labdhvāprasādaṃ ca caturmukhāt \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasthuḥ pātālanilaye muditenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*tataḥ kālāṃta rebhūte punarevaṃ vyaciṃtayan \|\| 46 \|\|*

43a. You should eat that being which is possessed by death and also (you should eat) a man when (he) has done harm to you.

43b-44a. Of those men, who are endowed with charms against snake-poison or spells or snares, you should be afraid. Do not entertain any other idea in your mind. Otherwise you will perish.

44b-45a. When Brahmā finished speaking thus all the serpents went to the place named Sutala. All (the serpents) lived in the lower world enjoying pleasures. They lived there comfortably.

45b-46. Thus having received a curse and a favour from Brahmā, they lived in (the lower world viz.) Pātāla with their hearts pleased. Again when (some) time passed, they thought like this:

## \|\| 31.47 \|\|

*bhavitā bharato rājā pāṃḍaveyo mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ tu kṣayakaro daivayogena kenacit \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. ‘There will be born a king of the Bharata race, and a descendant of Pāṇḍu who, through some (stroke of ill) luck, will destroy us.

## \|\| 31.48 \|\|

*kathaṃ tribhuvane nāthaḥ sarveṣāṃ ca pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭikartā jagadvaṃdyaḥ śāpamasmāsu dattavān \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. How is it that the grandsire, the lord in (i.e. of) the three worlds, the creator, and the one respected by the world cursed us?

## \|\| 31.49 \|\|

*devaṃ viraṃcinaṃ tyaktvā gatiranyā na vidyate \|*  
*vairāje bhavanaśreṣṭhe tatra devaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. We have no other recourse than god Brahmā. That god stays in Vairāja, the best residence.

## \|\| 31.50 \|\|

*sa devaḥ puṣkarastho vai yajñaṃ yajati sāṃpratam \|*  
*gatvā prasādayāmastaṃ varaṃ tuṣṭaḥ pradāsyati \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Now, that god, living in Puṣkara, is performing a sacrifice. Going (there) we shall propitiate him. Being pleased he will grant (us) a boon’.

## \|\| 31.51 \|\|

*evaṃ viciṃtya te sarve nāgā gatvā ca puṣkaram \|*  
*yajñaparvatamāsādya śailabhittimupāśritāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thinking thus, all the serpents, having reached the sacrificial mountain, resorted to its slope.

## \|\| 31.52 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā nāgāṃstathā śrāntānvāridhārāśca śītalāḥ \|*  
*udaṅmukhā vai niṣkrāṃtāssarveṣāṃ tu sukhapradāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Seeing the serpents fatigued like that cool streams of water, turned towards the north, came out and delighted all.

## \|\| 31.53 \|\|

*nāgatīrthaṃ tato jātaṃ pṛthivyāṃ bharatarṣabha \|*  
*nāgakuṃḍaṃ ca vai kecitsaritaṃ cāpare'bruvan \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. O best among the Bharatas, as a result of those (streams) Nāgatīrtha was formed. Some call it Nāgakuṇḍa; others call it a river.

## \|\| 31.54-56 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ tatsarvatīrthānāṃ sarpāṇāṃ viṣanāśanam \|*  
*majjanti tatra ye martyā adhiśrāvaṇa paṃcami \|\| 54 \|\|*

*na teṣāṃ tu kule sarpāḥ pīḍāṃ kurvanti karhicit \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ ye tatra kariṣyaṃti narā bhuvi \|\| 55 \|\|*
