*brahmā teṣāṃ paraṃ sthānaṃ dāsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nāgānāṃ tu bhayaṃ jñātvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-55a. The sacred place is the holiest of all and destroys (i.e. removes the effect of the) poison of serpents. Serpents do not cause any harm to any member of the family of those mortals who bathe there on the fifth day of Śrāvaṇa.

55b-56a. There is no doubt that Brahmā gives an excellent place to those men who offer Śrāddha to their dead ancestors in that region.

## \|\| 31.56-66 \|\|

*brahmā teṣāṃ paraṃ sthānaṃ dāsyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*nāgānāṃ tu bhayaṃ jñātvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*pūrvoktaṃ tu punarvākyaṃ nāgānaśrāvayattadā \|*  
*paṃcamī sā tithirdhanyā sarvapāpaharā śubhā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yato'syāmeva sutithau nāgānāṃ kāryamuddhṛtam \|*  
*etasyāṃ sarvato yastu kaṭvamlaṃ parivarjayet \|\| 58 \|\|*

*kṣīreṇa snāpayennāgāṃstasya te yāṃti mitratām \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*śivadūtī yathā jātā yena caiva niveśitā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tanme sarvaṃ yathātattvaṃ bhavānśaṃsiturmahati \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*śivā nīlagiriṃ prāptā tapase dhṛtamānasā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*raudrī jaṭodbhavā śaktistasyāḥ śṛṇu nṛpa vratam \|*  
*tapaḥ kṛtvā ciraṃ kālaṃ grasiṣyāmyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 61 \|\|*

*evamuddiśya paṃcāgniṃ sādhayāmāsa bhāminī \|*  
*tasyāḥ kālāṃtare devyāstapaṃtyāstapa uttamam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*rururnāmamahātejā brahmadattavaro'suraḥ \|*  
*samudramadhye ratnākhyaṃ puramasti mahādhanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tatrātiṣṭhatsa daityeṃdrassarvadevabhayaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*aneka śatasāhasra koṭikoṭiśatottamaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*asurairarcitaḥ śrīmāndvitīyo namuciryathā \|*  
*kālena mahatā so'tha lokapālapuraṃ yayau \|\| 65 \|\|*

*jigīṣuḥ sainyasaṃvīto devairvairamarocayat \|*  
*uttiṣṭhatastasya mahāsurasya samudratoyaṃ vavṛdheti vegāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

56b-59a. Realising the fear of the serpents, Brahmā again said the words which he had uttered before: “That fifth day (of Śrāvaṇa) is blessed, removes all sins and is auspicious, since the work of the emancipation of the serpents was done on that day. They befriend him who completely avoids pungent and sour (things) on this day and bathes (an image of) a cow with milk.”

Bhīṣma said:

59b-60a. You (please) tell me how Śivadūtī was born and how she was installed.

Pulastya said:

60b-61a. O king, a power called Śivā, sprung up from the matted hair of Rudra, and determined to (practise) penance went to Nīlagiri. Listen to (the account of) the vow in her (honour).

61b-62a. ‘Practising penance, I shall devour the entire world.’ With this intention, the beautiful young woman accomplished (the vow of) the five fires.

62b-65a. When that goddess was practising excellent penance, there lived in the wealthy city called Ratnākhya in the middle of the ocean, a demon by name Ruru, who was very lustrous and to whom a boon was given by Brahma. That lord of demons, fearful to all gods, wealthy and respected by many hundred thousands of excellent demons, was like another Namuci.

65b-66. After a long time he went to the city of the regent of the quarter. He, desirous of conquering, and adorned with an army liked enmity with gods. When that great demon rose up, the water of the ocean increased with a great speed.

## \|\| 31.67-69 \|\|

*aneka nāga graha mīnajuṣṭamāplāvayatparvatasānudeśān \|*  
*aṃtaḥsthitānekasurārisaṃghaṃ vicitravarmāyudhacitraśobham \|\| 67 \|\|*

*bhīmaṃ balaṃ calitaṃ cāruyodhaṃ viniryayau siṃdhujalādviśālam \|*  
*tatra dvipā daityabhaṭhābhyupetāḥ sayānaghaṃṭāśca samṛddhiyuktāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*viniryayuḥ svākṛtibhirjhaṣāṇāṃ samatvamuccaiḥ khalu darśayaṃtaḥ \|*  
*aśvāstathā kāṃcanasūtranaddhā rohītamatsyā iva te jalāṃte \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69 Possessed of many sharks, crocodiles and fish it inundated the peaks of mountains. A huge, fearful army, having in it many groups of the enemies of gods, having a variegated beauty due to various armours and weapons, consisting of excellent warriors, set out of the water of the ocean. Elephants, with demon-warriors (on their backs), with moving bells, and endowed with supremacy, and very much demonstrating their similarity with large fish by means of their own figures, moved out.

## \|\| 31.70 \|\|

*vyavasthitāstaiḥ samameva tūrṇaṃ viniryayurlakṣaśaḥ koṭiśaśca \|*  
*tathā ravisyaṃdanatulyavegāḥ sacakradaṃḍākṣataveṇuyuktāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Lakhs and crores of horses, tied with golden strings, resembling rohita fish, arranged in order in the water also quickly moved out with them (i.e. elephants).

## \|\| 31.71-78 \|\|

*rathāśca yaṃtroparipīḍitāṃgāścalatpatākāḥ svanitaṃ vicakruḥ \|*  
*tathaiva yodhāḥ sthagitāstarībhistitīrṣavaste pravarāstrapāṇayaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*raṇeraṇe labdhajayāḥ prahāriṇo virejuruccairasurānugā bhṛśaṃ \|*  
*deveṣu vai raṇe teṣu vidruteṣu viśeṣataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*asurāssarvadevānāmanvadhāvaṃstatastataḥ \|*  
*tato devagaṇāḥ sarve dravaṃto bhayavihvalāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*nīlaṃ girivaraṃ jagmuryatra devī svayaṃ sthitā \|*  
*raudrī taponvitā dhanyā śāṃbhavī śaktiruttamā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*saṃhārakāriṇī devī kālarātrīti yāṃ viduḥ \|*  
*sā tu dṛṣṭvā tadā devānbhayatrastānvicetasaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*papraccha vismayāddevī protphullāṃbujalocanā \|*  
*pṛṣṭhato vo na paśyāmi bhayaṃ kiṃcidupāgatam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*kathaṃ tu vidrutā devāḥ sarve śakrapuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*devā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ayamāyāti daityeṃdro rururbhīmaparākramaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*caturaṃgeṇa sainyena mahatā parivāritaḥ \|*  
*tasmāddīnā vayaṃ devīṃ bhavatīṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

71-72a. Similarly, chariots, having the speed of the Sun’s chariot, with wheels and sticks and with unrent bamboos, with banners moving (on their tops), made a noise. In the same way warriors, with excellent missiles in their hands, hidden in boats and desiring to cross (the ocean in the boats), victorious in every battle and the followers of the demon shone very brightly.

72b-73a. When in the fights the gods fled, the demons particularly pursued all of them.

73b-74a. Then all groups of gods, distressed with fear and fleeing went to that excellent Nīlagiri, where the goddess herself had remained.

74b-76a. That goddess, Raudrī (i.e. sprung up from Rudra), endowed with penance, blessed one, and the excellent power of Śambhu, causing destruction, and known as the night of the destruction of the world, and having eyes like blooming lotuses, seeing the gods distressed with fear and confounded, asked them through amazement:

76b-77a. “I am not seeing any (cause of) fear for you. How is it that all gods, led by Indra, have fled away?”.

The gods said:

77b-78. This Ruru, the lord of demons, of a fearful valour and surrounded by great complete army is coming. Therefore, we being distressed, have sought the resort of you, the goddess.

## \|\| 31.79 \|\|

*devānāmiti vai śrutvā vākyamuccairjahāsa sā \|*  
*tasyāṃ hasaṃtyāṃ niścerurvarāṃgyo vadanāttataḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Hearing these words of gods she laughed loudly. From the mouth of her who was laughing, excellent ladies came out.

## \|\| 31.80-81 \|\|

*pāśāṃkuśadharāḥ sarvāḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ \|*  
*sarvāśśūladharā bhīmāḥ sarvā daṃṣṭrāṅkuśānanāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*ābaddhamakuṭāḥ sarvāḥ saṃdaṣṭadaśanacchadāḥ \|*  
*phūtkārarāvairaśivaistrāsayaṃtyaścarācaram \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. They all held nooses and goads; their breasts were stout and raised; all held tridents, all were fearful; their mouths had goads in the form of large teeth; they had put on crowns; they bit their lower lips; they frightened the mobile and the immobile with the sounds of their hissing.

## \|\| 31.82 \|\|

*kāścicchuklāmbaradharāḥ kāściccitrāmbarāstathā \|*  
*sunīlavasanāḥ kāścidraktapānātilālasāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Some had put on white garments; some had put on variegated garments. The garments of some were dark-blue; some had a strong desire to drink blood.

## \|\| 31.83 \|\|

*nānārūpairmukhaistāstu nānāveṣavapurdharāḥ \|*  
*tābhirevaṃ vṛtā devī devānāmabhayaṃkarī \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Their faces had various forms; their dresses were of various kinds, so also their bodies. That goddess, causing absence of fear among the gods, was thus surrounded by them.

## \|\| 31.84-90 \|\|

*mā bhaiṣṭa devā bhadraṃ vo yāvadvadati dānavaḥ \|*  
*caturaṃgabalopeto rurustāvatsamāgataḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*taṃ nīlaparvatavaraṃ devānāṃ mārgamārgaṇaḥ \|*  
*devānāmagrataḥ sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvā devī samākulam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhatiṣṭheti jalpaṃto daityāste samupāgatāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tāsāṃ teṣāṃ mahābhayam \|\| 86 \|\|*

*nārācairbhinnadehānāṃ daityānāṃ bhuvi sarpatāṃ \|*  
*roṣāddaṃḍaprabhagnānāṃ sarpāṇāmiva sarpatām \|\| 87 \|\|*

*śaktinirbhinnahṛdayā gadāsaṃcūrṇitorasaḥ \|*  
*kuṭhārairbhinnaśiraso musalairbhinnamastakāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*viddhodarāstriśūlāgraiśchinnagrīvā varāsibhiḥ \|*  
*kṣatāśvarathamātaṃgapādātāḥ peturāhave \|\| 89 \|\|*

*raṇabhūmiṃ samāsādya daityāḥ sarve ruruṃ vinā \|*  
*tato balaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rururmāyāṃ tadādade \|\| 90 \|\|*

84-85a. No sooner did she say to the gods, ‘O gods, do not be frightened; well-being to you’, than the demon Ruru came with his complete army, to that excellent Nīla-parvata, in search of gods.

85b-86a. Seeing in front of them the army of gods with the goddess, the demons came there saying, ‘Wait, wait’.

86b-90a. Then a great war was waged between them, when all the demons who had come to the battlefield, whose bodies were pierced with arrows, who were moving on the ground, whose staffs were broken in anger, and who were creeping (i.e. moving) like serpents, with the wounded horses, the broken chariots, the injured elephants and the foot-soldiers, with their chests pounded by the mace that came out from the heart of that Śakti (i.e. that goddess), with their heads cut off with axes and broken with pestles, with their bellies pierced with the tips of tridents, and with their necks cut off with excellent swords, fell (on the ground) in the war, except Ruru.

90b. Then seeing his army destroyed Ruru created (malignant) illusion.

## \|\| 31.91 \|\|

*tayā saṃmohitā devyo devāścāpi raṇājire \|*  
*tāmasyā māyayā devyā sarvamandhaṃtamobhavat \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. Gods and goddesses were deluded by that (illusion) on the battlefield. Everywhere pitch-darkness prevailed due to the malignant illusion.

## \|\| 31.92 \|\|

*tato devī mahāśakyā taṃ daityaṃ samatāḍayat \|*  
*tayā tu tāḍitasyājau daityasya pragataṃ tamaḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. Then the goddess (i.e. Śivadūtī) struck the demon with great power. When the demon was struck by her, the darkness (caused) by the demon passed away.

## \|\| 31.93-94 \|\|

*māyāyāmatha naṣṭāyāṃ tāmasyāṃ dānavo ruruḥ \|*  
*pātālamāviśattūrṇaṃ tatrāpi parameśvarī \|\| 93 \|\|*

*devībhiḥ sahitā kruddhā puratobhimukhī sthitā \|*  
*rurostu dānaveṃdrasya bhītasyāgre gatasya ca \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. When the illusion came to an end, the demon Ruru quickly entered Pātāla. There too the angry goddess, along with (other) goddesses stood before Ruru, the lord of demons, who had gone there before.

## \|\| 31.95-98 \|\|

*nakhāgreṇa śiraśchitvā carma cādāya vegitā \|*  
*niṣpapātātha pātālātpuṣkaraṃ ca punargirim \|\| 95 \|\|*

*kanyā sainyena mahatā bahurūpeṇa bhāsvatā \|*  
*devaistuvismitairdṛṣṭā carmamuṃḍadharā ruroḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*svakīye tapasaḥ sthāne niviṣṭā parameśvarī \|*  
*tato devyo mahābhāgāḥ parivārya vyavasthitāḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*yācayāmāsuravyagrāstāṃ tu devīṃ bubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*bubhukṣitā vayaṃ devi dehi no bhojanaṃ varam \|\| 98 \|\|*

95-96a. Cutting off Ruru’s head with the tips of her nails, and taking off his skin, she speedily went out of Pātāla, and again came to the Puṣkara (Tīrtha) and to the mountain (called Nīlagiri), along with the bright and multi-formed army of the maidens (created by her).

96b-98a. The gods saw with amazement the goddess holding Ruru’s head and skin and remaining at the place of her penance. Then the magnanimous, hungry and bewildered goddesses (created by Śivadūtī) stood surrounding her and implored her:

98b. “O goddess, we are hungry; give us excellent food.”

## \|\| 31.99 \|\|

*evamuktvā tato devī dadhyau tāsāṃ tu bhojanam \|*  
*nādhyagacchattadā tāsāṃ bhojanaṃ cintitammahat \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Thus addressed, she pondered over the food to be given to them. But she did not get the food though she very much thought about it.

## \|\| 31.100 \|\|

*tadā dadhyau mahādevaṃ rudraṃ paśupatiṃ vibhum \|*  
*sopi dhyānātsamuttasthau paramātmā trilocanaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Then she meditated upon the mighty Mahādeva, the lord of beings. He, the three-eyed highest soul, stood up (before her) as a result of her meditation.

## \|\| 31.101 \|\|

*uvāca rudrastāṃ devīṃ kiṃ te kāryaṃ vivakṣitam \|*  
*brūhi devi mahāmāye yatte manasi vartate \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Rudra said to that goddess: “What is the mission that you desire to tell me? O you goddess, the great creator of illusion, tell me what is in your mind.”

## \|\| 31.102 \|\|

*śivadūtyuvāca \|*  
*chāgamadhye tu vai deva chāgarūpeṇa vartase \|*  
*etāstvāṃ bhakṣayiṣyanti bhakṣyamīpsitamādarāt \|\| 102 \|\|*

Śivadūtī said:

102\. O you god, in a goat you remain in the form of a goat. These will eat you with great respect as their desired food.

## \|\| 31.103 \|\|

*bhakṣārthamāsāṃ deveśa kiṃciddātumihārhasi \|*  
*śūlīkurvaṃti māmetā bhakṣārthinyo mahābalāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. O lord of gods, please give them something as their food. Otherwise the mighty ones, desiring food will put me (and roast me) on an iron-spit.

## \|\| 31.104 \|\|

*anyathā māmapi balādbhakṣayeyurbubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ māṃ tu samālakṣya bhakṣyaṃ kalpaya satvaram \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. The hungry ones may even forcibly devour me. Taking me to be like this (please) prepare (i.e. bring about) food quickly.

## \|\| 31.105 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*śivadūti bravīmyekaṃ pravṛttaṃ yadyugāṃtare \|*  
*gaṃgādvāre dakṣayajño gaṇairvidhvaṃsito mama \|\| 105 \|\|*

Rudra said:

105\. O Śivadūtī, I am telling you one (incident) that took place in another (i.e. previous) yuga. My attendants destroyed Dakṣa’s sacrifice (being performed) at Gaṅgādvāra.

## \|\| 31.106 \|\|

*tatra yajño mṛgo bhūtvā pradudrāva suvegavān \|*  
*mayā bāṇena nirviddho rudhireṇa prasecitaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. There (i.e. at that time) sacrifice, being (i.e. turning himself into) a deer ran fast. He was pierced by me with an arrow and (as a result) he was sprinkled with blood (i.e. started bleeding.

## \|\| 31.107-108 \|\|

*ajagaṃdhastadā bhūto nāma devaistu me kṛtam \|*  
*ajagaṃdhastvameveti dāsye cānyattu bhojanam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*etāsāṃ śṛṇu me devi bhakṣyamekaṃ mayocitam \|*  
*kathyamānaṃ varārohe kālarātri mahāprabhe \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. Then Ajagandha sprang up. Gods gave me the (same) name (saying:) ‘You yourself are Ajagandha’. I shall give (these goddesses) other food also. O you Kālarātri of great lustre and beautiful one, listen to (the name of) the food suited to these (goddesses, now) being told by me.

## \|\| 31.109-111 \|\|

*yā strī sagarbhā deveśi anyastrīparidhānakam \|*  
*paridhatte spṛśedvāpi puruṣasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*sabhāgostu varārohe kāsāṃcitpṛthivītale \|*  
*apyekavarṣaṃ bālaṃ tu gṛhītvā tatra vai balāt \|\| 110 \|\|*

*bhuktvā tiṣṭhaṃtu suprītā api varṣaśatānbahūn \|*  
*anyāḥ sūtigṛhe cchidraṃ gṛhṇīyustu hyapūjitāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

109-110a. Let that woman, who, while pregnant, puts on or touches the garment of another woman and especially of a man be the food of some of these (goddesses) on the earth, O you chief goddess.

110b-111. Also let them forcibly seize the child of such a lady till that child becomes a year old, and then let them remain well-pleased for many hundreds of years. Let others, who will not be worshipped, find a flaw in the lying-in chamber.

## \|\| 31.112 \|\|

*nivasiṣyaṃti deveśi tathā vai jātahārikāḥ \|*  
*gṛhe kṣetre taṭāke ca vāpyudyāneṣu caiva hi \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Also, (some goddesses) seizing new-born infants will live in houses, fields, lakes and also in gardens.

## \|\| 31.113 \|\|

*atyeṣu ca rudaṃtyo yā striyastiṣṭhaṃti nityaśaḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ śarīragāścānyāḥ kāścittṛptimavāpnuyuḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Those and others possessing the bodies of those women who always weep, will satisfy themselves (by eating) such women.

## \|\| 31.114-115 \|\|

*śivadūtya uvāca \|*  
*kutsitaṃ bhavatā dattaṃ prajānāṃ paripīḍanam \|*  
*na ca tvaṃ budhyase dātuṃ śaṃkararasya viśeṣataḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*trapākaraṃ yadbhavati prajānāṃ paripīḍakam \|*  
*na tu tadyujyate dātuṃ tāsāṃ bhakṣyaṃ tu śaṃkara \|\| 115 \|\|*

Śivadūtī said:

114-115. O Śaṅkara, you have given them (food) which is despised and which would inflict pain on them. You do not realize that you should give them some special food. O Śaṅkara, please do not give them food which would cause shame to them, and which would cause pain to the beings.

## \|\| 31.116-117 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*avaṃtyāṃ tu yadā skaṃdo mayā pūrvaṃ tu bhadritaḥ \|*  
*cūḍākarmaṇi vṛtte tu kumārasya tadā śubhe \|\| 116 \|\|*

*āgatya mātaro bhakṣyamapūrvaṃ tu pracakrire \|*  
*devalokāddevagaṇā mātṝṇāṃ bhoktumāgatāḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

Rudra said:

116-117a. When, formerly, in Avanti, I (got) Skanda shaved, (that is) when the auspicious tonsure-ceremony of Kumāra (i.e. Skanda) took place, the mothers, having come there, prepared unprecedented food.

117b. Groups of gods came from the world of gods to enjoy the food of (i.e. prepared by) the mothers.

## \|\| 31.118-121 \|\|

*tāsāṃ gṛhe yadā pūrvaṃ brahmādyāssurasattamāḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharvāpsarasaścaiva yakṣāssarve ca guhyakāḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*mervādayaḥ śikhariṇo gaṃgādyāḥ saritastathā \|*  
*sarve nāgā gajāssiddhāḥ pakṣiṇo'surasūdanāḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

*ḍākinyaḥ saha vetālairvṛtāḥ sarvairgrahaistadā \|*  
*kimuktenāmunā devi yatsṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā tviha \|\| 120 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ bhojanaṃ dattaṃ svecchānnaṃ ca nabhogataṃ \|*  
*śivadūtyuvāca \|*  
*āsāṃ kṛtaṃ dehi bhojyaṃ durlabhaṃ yattriviṣṭape \|\| 121 \|\|*

118-121. At that olden time in their house best gods like Brahmā and Gandharvas, celestial nymphs, Yakṣas and Guhyakas, mountains like Meru and rivers like Gaṅgā, as well as all serpents, elephants, Siddhas, birds and killers of the demons, female goblins with vampires and surrounded by all planets had gathered. What should I say, O goddess? All that was created here by Brahmā was given.

## \|\| 31.122 \|\|

*snehāktaṃ saguḍaṃ hṛdyaṃ supakvaṃ parikalpitam \|*  
*kvacinnānyena yadbhuktamapūrvaṃ parameśvara \|\| 122 \|\|*

Śivadūtī said:

122\. For these goddesses give me food which is inaccessible in heaven, which is oily, mixed with jaggery, tasty and well-cooked and which is intended for them, and which is not enjoyed by anyone else before, O great god.

## \|\| 31.123 \|\|

*evamuktastadā sopi devadevo maheśvaraḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyārthaṃ tāstadā prāha pārvatyāścaiva sannidhau \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Thus addressed Maheśvara, the god of gods, told them in the vicinity of Pārvatī about their food:

## \|\| 31.124 \|\|

*mayā vai sādhitaṃ cānnaṃ prakārairbahubhiḥ kṛtaṃ \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ ca vyayaṃ yātaṃ na cānyadiha dṛśyate \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. “I have accomplished the food prepared in many ways. All that is exhausted. And no other (kind of food) is seen here.

## \|\| 31.125 \|\|

*bhavatīṣvāgatāsvadya kiṃ mayā deyamucyatām \|*  
*apūrvaṃ bhavatīnāṃ yanmayā deyaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Tell me what I should today give to you who have come (to me). I have especially to give something quite new.

## \|\| 31.126-127 \|\|

*asvāditaṃ na cānyena bhakṣyārthe ca dadāmyaham \|*  
*adhobhāge ca me nābhervartulau phalasannibhau \|\| 126 \|\|*

*bhakṣayadhvaṃ hi sahitā laṃbau me vṛṣaṇāvimau \|*  
*anena cāpi bhojyena parā tṛptirbhaviṣyati \|\| 127 \|\|*

126-127. I shall give you as food which has never been tasted before by anyone. Below my navel are these two circular long and fruit-like testicles. Even with this food you will have great satisfaction.”{GL\_NOTE::}

## \|\| 31.128 \|\|

*mahāprasādaṃ tā labdhvā devyassarvāstadā śivam \|*  
*praṇipatya sthitāśśarva idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Receiving that great favour all the goddesses saluted Śiva. Śarva said these words to them:

## \|\| 31.129-130 \|\|

*kariṣyaṃti śubhācārānvinā hāsyena ye narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dhanaṃ paśuḥ putrā dārāścaiva gṛhādikam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati mayā dattaṃ yaccānyanmanasi sthitam \|*  
*hāsyena dīrghadaśanā daridrāśca bhavaṃti te \|\| 130 \|\|*

129-130. “The wealth, beasts, sons, wives and houses etc. of those who perform auspicious deeds without laughing, will be given to you by me; and also whatever else is in your mind. Those who by laughing have long teeth (i.e. show their teeth) (will) become poor.

## \|\| 31.131 \|\|

*tasmānna niṃdā hāsyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ hi vijānatā \|*  
*bhavatyo mātaraḥ khyātā hyasminloke bhaviṣyatha \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Therefore, one who is wise, should not indulge in censuring or laughing (at others). In this world you will be known as mothers.

## \|\| 31.132-134 \|\|

*upahāre narā ye tu kariṣyaṃti ca kaumudīm \|*  
*caṇakānpūrikāścaiva vṛṣaṇaiḥ saha pūpakān \|\| 132 \|\|*

*baṃdhubhiḥ svajanaiścaiva teṣāṃ vaṃśo na chidyate \|*  
*aputro labhate putraṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*rūpavānsubhago bhogī sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ \|*  
*haṃsayuktena yānena brahma loke mahīyate \|\| 134 \|\|*

132-133a. The lineage of those men, who, along with their relatives and kinsmen, prepare (articles from) a lotus, grams, and also cakes and sorts of bread with (i.e. having the shape of) testicles, as an offering, is not cut off.

133b-134. A man who has no son, gets a son; he, who desires wealth, obtains it; he, being handsome, lucky, enjoyer, well-versed in all sciences, is honoured in Brahmā’s world with (i.e. being taken in) a vehicle to which swans are yoked.

## \|\| 31.135 \|\|

*śivadūti mayāpyevaṃ tāsāṃ dattaṃ ca bhakṣaṇam \|*  
*trapākaraṃ kiṃ bhavatyā uktohaṃ tanniśāmaya \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. O Śivadūtī, thus I have given them food. Does it bring shame to you? Please listen to what I said:

## \|\| 31.136-142 \|\|

*jayasva devi cāmuṃḍe jaya bhūtāpahāriṇi \|*  
*jaya sarvagate devi kālarātri namostu te \|\| 136 \|\|*

*viśvamūrtiyute śuddhe virūpākṣi trilocane \|*  
*bhīmarūpe śive vidye mahāmāye mahodare \|\| 137 \|\|*

*manojaye manodurge bhīmākṣi kṣubhitakṣaye \|*  
*mahāmāri vicitrāṃgi gītanṛtyapriye śubhe \|\| 138 \|\|*

*vikarāli mahākāli kālike pāpahāriṇi \|*  
*pāśahaste daṃḍahaste bhīmahaste bhayānake \|\| 139 \|\|*

*cāmuṃḍe jvalamānāsye tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭre mahābale \|*  
*śivayānapriye devi pretāsanagate śive \|\| 140 \|\|*

*bhīmākṣi bhīṣaṇe devi sarvabhūtabhayaṃkari \|*  
*karāli vikarāle ca mahākāli karālini \|\| 141 \|\|*

*kālikarālavikrāṃte kālarātri namostu te \|*  
*sarvaśastrabhṛte devi namo devanamaskṛte \|\| 142 \|\|*

136-142. Be victorious, O goddess, Cāmuṇḍā; victory to you who snatch away beings. Victory to you who are omnipresent; O goddess Kālarātri, salutation to you. O you (goddess) endowed with the universal form, O you Virūpākṣī (of deformed eyes), O you Trilocanā, O you Bhīmarūpā (i.e. of a terrible form), O Śivā, Vidyā, Mahāmāyā, Mahodarā, Manojayā, Manodurgā, Bhhīmākṣī, Kṣubhitakṣayā, Mahāmārī, Vicitrāṅgī, O you to whom singing and dancing are dear, O you auspicious one, O Vikarālī, Mahākālī, Kālikā, Pāpahāriṇī, Pāśahastā, Daṇḍahastā, Bhīmahastā, Bhayānakā, Cāmuṇḍā, Jvalamānāsyā, Tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrā, Mahābalā, Śivayānapriyā, Devi, Pretāsanagatā, Śivā, Bhīmākṣī, Bhīṣaṇā, O you goddess, Sarvabhūtabhayaṅkarī, Karālī, Vikarālī, Mahākālī, Karālinī, Kālī, Karālavikrāntā, Kālarātri, salutation to you. O you goddes, salutation to you who hold all weapons and who are saluted by all gods.

## \|\| 31.143 \|\|

*evaṃ stutā śivadūtī rudreṇa parameṣṭhinā \|*  
*tutoṣa paramā devī vākyaṃ caivamuvāca ha \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. Śivadūtī, who was thus praised by Parameṣṭhin Rudra, the great goddess was pleased and said these words:

## \|\| 31.144 \|\|

*varaṃ vṛṇīṣva deveśa yatte manasi vartate \|*  
*rudra uvāca \|*  
*stotreṇānena ye devi stoṣyaṃti ttvāṃ varānane \|\| 144 \|\|*

144a. “O lord of gods, ask for a boon which you have in your mind.”

Rudra said:

144b. O goddess of a beautiful face, being present every where grant boons to those men who praise you with this eulogy.

## \|\| 31.145-148 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tvaṃ varadā devi bhava sarvagatā satī \|*  
*imaṃ parvatamāruhya yaḥ pūjayati bhaktitaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

*sa putrapautrapaśumānsamṛddhimupagacchatu \|*  
*yaścaivaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā stavaṃ devi samudbhavaṃ \|\| 146 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamṛcchatu \|*  
*bhraṣṭarājyo yadā rājā navamyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

*aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ sopavāso narottama \|*  
*saṃvatsareṇa labhatāṃ rājyaṃ niṣkaṃṭakaṃ punaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

145-146a. May he, who climbing up this mountain, worships you with devotion, have sons, grandsons and prosperity.

146b-147a. He, who hears this eulogy rising from (i.e. about) the goddess, becomes free from all sins, may obtain (i.e. obtains) the highest bliss.

147b-148. If a king, who has lost his kingdom, being controlled and pure, (praises) while observing a fast, (the goddess) on the ninth, or eighth or fourteenth (day of a month), he regains his kingdom, free from enemies, after a year.

## \|\| 31.149-154 \|\|

*eṣā jñānānvitā śaktiḥ śivadūtīti cocyate \|*  
*ya evaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ bhaktyā paramayā nṛpa \|\| 149 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ paraṃ nirvāṇamāpnuyāt \|*  
*yaścainaṃ paṭhate bhaktyā snātvā vai puṣkare jale \|\| 150 \|\|*

*sarvametatphalaṃ prāpya brahmaloke mahīyate \|*  
*yatraitallikhitaṃ gehe sadā tiṣṭhati pārthiva \|\| 151 \|\|*

*na tatrāgnibhayaṃ ghoraṃ sarvacorādisaṃbhavaṃ \|*  
*yaścedaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā pustakepi sthitaṃ budhāḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*tena ceṣṭaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaraṃ \|*  
*jāyaṃte bahavaḥ putrā dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ varastriyaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

*ratnānyaśvā gajā bhṛtyāsteṣāmāśu bhavaṃti ca \|*  
*yatredaṃ likhyate gehe tatrāpyevaṃ dhruvaṃ bhavet \|\| 154 \|\|*

149-151a. This power endowed with knowledge is called Śivadūtī. O king, he, who listens to this (eulogy) with great devotion, being free from all sins, would obtain the highest salvation. He, who, after having bathed in the water of the Puṣkara (Tīrtha), recites this (eulogy), gets all this fruit, and is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

151b-152a. That house, in which a written (copy) of this (eulogy) is kept, has no fear of terrible fire or fear due to thieves etc.

152b-154. A wise man, who devoutly worships this remaining in a book-form, has everything desired by him—(even) the three worlds with the mobile and the immobile. Many sons are born (i.e. he gets many sons, and also he gets) wealth, grains, and excellent ladies; and also quickly gets gems, horses, elephants and servants. All this will certainly take place in the house in which this is kept in a manuscript-form.

## Chapter 32 - Descent of a Holy Place

## \|\| 32.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kena karmavipākena pretatvaṃ jāyate punaḥ \|*  
*kena vātra pramucyeta tanme brūhi mahāmate \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. O you highly intelligent one, tell me, as a result of which deeds the condition of an evil spirit is produced (i.e. as a result of which one turns into an evil spirit after death); and also (tell me) by (doing which) deeds one is freed from here (i.e. this condition of evil spirit).

## \|\| 32.2 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi sarvametadaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yacchrutvā na punarmohaṃ yāsyate nṛpasattama \|\| 2 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

2\. O best king, I shall entirely tell you all this, hearing which you will not be deluded.

## \|\| 32.3 \|\|

*yena jāyeta pretatvaṃ yena cāsmātpramucyate \|*  
*prāpnoti narakaṃ ghoraṃ dustaraṃ tridaśairapi \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I shall tell you by which (deeds) one is reduced to the condition of a spirit, and by (doing which deeds) one is freed from it; (I shall also tell you how) one reaches a terrible hell which is insuperable even to gods.

## \|\| 32.4 \|\|

*satāṃ saṃbhāṣaṇe caiva puṇyatīrthānukīrttane \|*  
*mānavāstu pramucyaṃta āpannāḥ pretayoniṣu \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Men who have been reduced to the state of an evil spirit are emancipated by conversation with the good, and by (listening to) accounts of holy places.

## \|\| 32.5-6 \|\|

*śrūyate hi purā bhīṣma brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ \|*  
*pṛthussarvatra vikhyātaḥ saṃtoṣe ca sadā sthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*svādhyāyayukto geheṣu nityayogaśca yogavit \|*  
*japayajñavidhānena yuktaṃ kālaṃ kṣipecca saḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. O Bhīṣma, it is learnt that in olden times there was a brāhmaṇa, named Pṛthu, who had fulfilled his vow, who was well-known everywhere, who was always content, who was devoted to the study of sacred texts in his house, who always engaged in the practice of yoga (deep and abstract meditation) and who was a knower of yoga. He passed his time in muttering prayers and performing sacrifices.

## \|\| 32.7 \|\|

*yuktaḥ kṣamādayābhyāṃ ca kṣāṃtyāyuktaśca tattvavit \|*  
*ahiṃsāhitacittaśca mārddave ca tathāsthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He was endowed with forgiveness and kindness and with forbearance, and was a knower of truth. He had put his mind in (i.e. practised) harmlessness, and also he was steady in gentleness (i.e. he was gentle).

## \|\| 32.8 \|\|

*brahmacaryasamāyuktastapoyogasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*yuktaḥ sa pitṛkāryeṣu yukto vaidikakarmasu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He was devoted to self-restraint and penance and meditation; he was engaged in (performing) rites (in honour) of the dead ancestors and in rites enjoined by the Vedas.

## \|\| 32.9 \|\|

*paralokabhayeyukto yuktassatyavacaḥ prati \|*  
*yukto madhuravākyeṣu yuktaścātithipūjane \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He entertained fear of the other world; he was given to truthful speech; he was devoted to (speaking) sweet words and to honouring guests.

I 0. He was engaged in performing sacrifices and doing acts of charity; he avoided the pairs (of pleasure, pain etc.); he performed his duties; and busied himself in the study of sacred texts.

## \|\| 32.11 \|\|

*evaṃ karmāṇi kurvaṃtassaṃsāravijigīṣayā \|*  
*bahūnyabdānyatītāni brāhmaṇasya gṛhe sataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus many years passed when the brāhmaṇa, residing in his house, performed acts like these with a desire to conquer (i.e. to go beyond) the worldly existence.

## \|\| 32.12 \|\|

*tasya buddhiriyaṃ jātā tīrthābhigamanaṃ prati \|*  
*puṇyaistīrthajalairetatklinnaṃ kuryāṃ kalevaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He made up his mind to visit holy places: ‘I shall make my body wet with the auspicious water of the sacred places.’

## \|\| 32.13 \|\|

*prayataḥ puṣkare snātvā bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati \|*  
*kṛtajapyanamaskāropyaddhvānaṃ pratyapadyata \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the time of sun-rise, he, having bathed in the Puṣkara (Tīrtha) and become pure, and muttered prayers and having saluted (the deities), resorted to the path (i.e. walked ahead).

## \|\| 32.14 \|\|

*agrataḥ paṃcapuruṣānapaśyatsoti bhīṣaṇān \|*  
*vane kaṃṭakavṛkṣāḍhye nirjane pakṣivarjite \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. In a lonely forest, full of thorny trees and void of birds, he saw in front of him five very fearful men.

## \|\| 32.15 \|\|

*tāndṛṣṭvā vikṛtākārānsughorānpāpadarśanān \|*  
*īṣatsaṃtrastahṛdayo vyatiṣṭhanniścalākṛtiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Seeing the deformed, very terrible men of a wicked appearance he, with his heart slightly frightened, remained still.

## \|\| 32.16 \|\|

*avalaṃbya tato dhairyyaṃ bhayamutsṛjya dūrataḥ \|*  
*papraccha madhurābhāṣī ke yūyaṃ vikṛtāḥ kutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He, of a sweet tongue, then mustered courage and casting off his fear asked them (in sweet words): “Who are you and what makes you deformed?

## \|\| 32.17 \|\|

*kiṃ vā caiva kṛtaṃ karma ye naprāptāśca vaikṛtam \|*  
*kathamevaṃvidhāḥ sarve prasthitāḥ kutra cādhvani \|\| 17 \|\|*

1 7. Or which deed did you perform by (i.e. as a result of) which you got this deformity? How are you like this? Which way are all of you setting on (i.e. where are you going)?”

## \|\| 32.18 \|\|

*pretā ūcuḥ \|*  
*kṣutpipāsānvitā nityaṃ mahāduḥkhasamāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*hṛtaprajñā vayaṃ sarve naṣṭasañjñāvicetasaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

The evil spirits said:

18\. We are always hungry and thirsty, and are enveloped by great grief. We all have lost our understanding, our intellect and have become confounded.

## \|\| 32.19 \|\|

*na jānīmo diśaṃ cāpi pradiśaṃ cāpi kāṃ ca na \|*  
*nāṃtarikṣaṃ mahīṃ cāpi na jānīmo divaṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. We are unable to recognize a direction or an intermediate direction, nor are we able to recognize the sky, or the earth or heaven.

## \|\| 32.20 \|\|

*yadetadduḥkhamākhyātametadeva sukhaṃ bhavet \|*  
*prabhātamidamābhāti bhāskarodayadarśanāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. But it would be (i.e. it is) a pleasure that we have told all (this) grief (of ours to you). Now it seems to be the morning that the sun is seen rising.

## \|\| 32.21 \|\|

*ahaṃ paryuṣito nāma sūcīmukhastathā'paraḥ \|*  
*śīghrago rohakaścaiva paṃcamo lekhakastathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I am Paryuṣita by name. (This) other one is Sūcīmukha. (This is) Śīghraga. (This is) Rohaka and this fifth one is Lekhaka.

## \|\| 32.22 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*pretānāṃ karmajātānāṃ nāmnā vai saṃbhavaḥ kutaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tatkāraṇamuddiśya yato yūyaṃ sanāmakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

The brāhmaṇa said:

22\. How is it possible that those, who have turned into evil spirits as a result of their deeds have names? For what reason did you have (these) names?

## \|\| 32.23 \|\|

*pretā ūcuḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ svādu sadā bhuṃje dadyāṃ paryuṣitaṃ dvije \|*  
*etatkāraṇamāsādya nāma paryuṣito mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

The evil spirits said:

23\. I always eat (i.e. ate) dainty food; and would give stale food to a brāhmaṇa. For this reason my name is Paryuṣita.

## \|\| 32.24 \|\|

*sūcitā bahavo'nena viprāścānnādyakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*etatkāraṇamuddiśya sūcīmukhābhidho mataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. This one pierced many brāhmaṇas desiring food etc.; for that reason he is regarded as having the name (i.e. he is named as) Sūcīmukha.

## \|\| 32.25 \|\|

*śīghraṃ gato'smi vipreṇa yācitaḥ kṣudhitena ca \|*  
*etatkāraṇamuddiśya śīghrago dvijasattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O best brāhmaṇa, I am (called) Śīghraga for the reason that when solicited by a hungry brāhmaṇa I moved (away) quickly.

## \|\| 32.26 \|\|

*gṛhopari sadā svādu bhuṃkte dvijabhayena hi \|*  
*udvignamānasastatra tenāsau rohakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. This one, through fear of (being requested by) a brāhmaṇa (to give him food), always ate delicious food on the top of the house (to avoid the brāhmaṇa) of whom he was afraid. So he is called Rohaka.

## \|\| 32.27 \|\|

*maune cāpi sthito nityaṃ yācito vilikhanmahīm \|*  
*asmākamapi pāpiṣṭho lekhako nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. This one is called Lekhaka, the most sinful amongst us, who always remained silent, scratching on the ground, when solicited (by someone for something).

## \|\| 32.28 \|\|

*kṛcchreṇa lekhako yāti rohakastu avākśirāḥ \|*  
*śīghragaḥ paṃgutāṃ prāptaḥ sūcī sūcīmukho'bhavat \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Lekhaka walks with (great) difficulty. Rohaka has his head hung down. Śīgharga has become lame. Sūcīmukha has become (like) a needle.

## \|\| 32.29 \|\|

*paryuṣito lambagrīvo laṃbodara udāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*bṛhadvṛṣaṇalaṃboṣṭhaḥ pāpādasmādajāyata \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Paryuṣita’s neck is long and he is called pot-bellied. As a result of this sin his scrotum and his lips are protruding.

## \|\| 32.30 \|\|

*etatte sarvamākhyātamātmavṛttaṃ sahetukam \|*  
*pṛcchasva yadi te śraddhā pṛṣṭāśca kathayāmahe \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus I have told you everything about our mode of life and its cause. If you have a strong desire, then ask (further questions). When (thus) asked we shall state (further).

## \|\| 32.31 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*ye jīvā bhuvi tiṣṭhaṃti sarvepyāhāramūlakāḥ \|*  
*yuṣmākamapi cāhāraṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

The brāhmaṇa said:

31\. All the beings that live on the earth, depend upon food. I desire to hear the truth about your food.

## \|\| 32.32 \|\|

*pretā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāhāramasmākaṃ sarvasatvavigarhitam \|*  
*yacchrutvā niṃdase vipra bhūyobhūyaśca nityaśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

The evil spirits said:

32\. O brāhmaṇa, listen to (the description) of our food condemned by all beings, hearing which you will again and again censure us.

## \|\| 32.33 \|\|

*śleṣmamūtrapurīṣeṇa yoṣidaṅgamalena ca \|*  
*gṛhāṇi tyaktaśaucāni pretā bhuṃjaṃti tatra vai \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The evil spirits enjoy in those houses where purity is ignored (i.e. which are impure) due to phlegm, urine, feces and the dirt of the bodies of women.

## \|\| 32.34 \|\|

*strībhirdagdhāni kīrṇāni prakīrṇocchiṣṭakāni ca \|*  
*malenāpi jugupsyāni pretā bhuṃjaṃti tatra vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The evil spirits enjoy there (i.e. in those places) where the remnants of food are burnt or scattered or thrown out by ladies or which are censured due to fith.

## \|\| 32.35 \|\|

*cittalajjāvihīnāni homahīnāni yāni ca \|*  
*vrataiścaiva vihīnāni pretā bhuṃjaṃti tatra vai \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The evil spirits enjoy there (i.e. in those houses) where there is no sense of shame in the hearts (of the residents), in which no sacrifices are performed, and which are void of vows.

## \|\| 32.36 \|\|

*guravo naiva pūjyaṃte strījitāni gṛhāṇi ca \|*  
*krodhalobhagṛhītāni pretā bhuṃjaṃti tatra vai \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The evil spirits enjoy in those houses where the elders are not respected, and which are dominated by ladies, and (the inmates of) which are overpowered by anger and greed.

## \|\| 32.37 \|\|

*trapā me jāyate tāta kathyamāne svabhojane \|*  
*asmātparataraṃ cānyanna vaktumapi śakyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O dear, I am ashamed of telling you about my food. It is not possible even to tell you still further.

## \|\| 32.38 \|\|

*nivṛttiṃ pretabhāvasya pṛcchāmastvāṃ dṛḍhavrata \|*  
*yathā na bhavati pretastanme vada tapodhana \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O you of a firm vow, I am asking you about (i.e. as to how to bring about) the cessation of this condition of an evil spirit. O you whose wealth is penance, tell me how (a man) does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.39 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*ekarātra dvirātrādi kṛcchracāṃdrāyaṇadibhiḥ \|*  
*vratairanyaiḥ kṛtairnityaṃ na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

The brāhmaṇa said:

39\. A man does not become an evil spirit if he always performs vows lasting for a day or two days or Kṛcchra Cāndrāyaṇa and other vows.

## \|\| 32.40 \|\|

*trīnagnīnpañca caikaṃ vā yo'hanyahani sevate \|*  
*sa vai bhūtadayāpanno na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. One who, full of compassion for beings, serves (i.e. worships) three, five or one fire everyday does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.41 \|\|

*tulyo māne'pamāne ca tulyaḥ kāṃcanaloṣṭayoḥ \|*  
*tulyaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. One who looks equally upon honour and dishonour, upon gold and a clod of earth, and upon friend and foe, does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.42 \|\|

*devatā'tithipūjāsu gurupūjāsu nityaśaḥ \|*  
*rato vai pitṛpūjāsu na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. One who is always engaged in worshipping deities, guests and preceptors and also in worshipping his dead ancestors, does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.43 \|\|

*śuklāṃgārakasaṃyuktā caturthī jāyate yadā \|*  
*śraddhayā śrāddhakṛttasyāṃ na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. One who, with faith, offers a śrāddha on the fourth day of a month which falls on a Tuesday in the bright half of a month, does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.44 \|\|

*jitakrodhavimarśoyastṛṣṇāsaṃgavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*kṣamāvāndānaśīlaśca na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. One who has conquered his anger and doubt and is free from desire and attachment, is given to forgiveness and charity, does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.45 \|\|

*gobrāhmaṇāṃśca tīrthāni parvatāṃśca nadīstathā \|*  
*devāṃścaiva tu yo vandyānna preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. One, who salutes cows, brāhmaṇas, sacred places, mountains and rivers, and also gods, does not become an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.46 \|\|

*pretā ūcuḥ \|*  
*śrutāśca vividhā dharmāḥ pṛcchāmo duḥkhitā mune \|*  
*yena vai jāyate pretastanno vada mahāmate \|\| 46 \|\|*

The evil spirits said:

46\. O highly intelligent sage, we have heard about various duties. Being distressed we are asking you. Tell us (about that) by (doing) which a man becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.47 \|\|

*brāhmaṇa uvāca \|*  
*śūdrānnena tu bhuktena brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*mriyate hyudarasthena sa vai preto bhavennaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

The brāhmaṇa said:

47\. If a man, especially a brāhmaṇa, dies having eaten Śūdra’s food, (with the food) lying in his belly, he becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.48 \|\|

*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ bhrātṝnbhaginīṃ sutameva ca \|*  
*adṛṣṭadoṣāṃstyajati sa preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He, who abandons his mother, father or brothers, or his sister or his son in whom no fault is seen, becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.49 \|\|

*ayājyayājanāccaiva yājyasya ca vivarjanāt \|*  
*rato vai śūdrasevāsu sa preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. A man who performs sacrifices for those for whom no sacrifice should be performed, or who does not perform sacrifices for those for whom they should be performed, or who is engaged in serving the Śūdras, becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.50 \|\|

*nyāsāpahartā mitradhrukśūdrapākarataḥ sadā \|*  
*visraṃbhaghātī kūṭasthaḥ sa preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. A man who takes away a deposit (kept with him), or harms his friends, or is always engaged in cooking for a Śūdra, or is a betrayer of trust (i.e. deceives a person who trusts him), becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.51 \|\|

*brahmahā goghnakaḥ stenaḥ surāpo gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*bhūmikanyāpaharttā ca sa preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. A man who kills a brāhmaṇa or a cow, who is a thief, or who drinks liquor, or who violates his teacher's bed (i.e. his teacher’s wife), who abducts a virgin or misappropriates a land, becomes an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.52 \|\|

*sāmānyāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ labdhvā eka eva nigūhati \|*  
*nāstikībhāvanirataḥ sa vai pretobhijāyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. He who, having received a gift in common, conceals it (for himself), or he who is attached to atheism, is born as an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.53 \|\|

*evaṃ bruvāṇe viprendra ākāśe duṃdubhisvanaḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ papātorvyāṃ devairmuktā sahasraśaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. When the best brāhmaṇa was speaking like this, there was (produced) a sound of kettle-drums in the sky and a shower of thousands of flowers discharged by gods fell on the earth.

## \|\| 32.54 \|\|

*pretānāṃ tu vimānāni āgatāni samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*asya viprasya saṃbhāṣātpuṇyasaṃkīrtanena ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. Due to the talk of the brāhmaṇa and his telling about virtue many aeroplanes of the evil spirits came (there) from all sides.

## \|\| 32.55 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena satāṃ saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ kuru \|*  
*yadi te śreyasā kāryaṃ gaṃgāsuta ataṃdritaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Therefore, O Gaṅgāsuta (i.e. son of Gaṅgā), if you want bliss, then being vigilant, make every effort to convene with the good.

## \|\| 32.56 \|\|

*tilakaṃ sarvadharmasya pañcapretakathāmimām \|*  
*paṭhellakṣaṃ yo'sya kule na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. In the family of him who recites for a lakh of times this account of the five evil spirits—which is the ornament of all virtue—no one is born as an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.57 \|\|

*śṛṇoti vāpyabhīkṣṇaṃ vā śraddhayā parayānvitaḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā samanvito vāpi na preto jāyate naraḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. He, who, endowed with devotion, repeatedly listens to it with great faith, is not born as an evil spirit.

## \|\| 32.58 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*aṃtarikṣe kimarthaṃ tu puṣkaraṃ parikīrtyate \|*  
*munibhirdharmaśīlaiśca labhyate tatkathaṃ tviha \|\| 58 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

58\. Why is Puṣkara (Tīrtha) said to be (situated) in the sky? How is it that the sages, given to virtue, have it here (i.e. on the earth)?

## \|\| 32.59 \|\|

*yena tallabhyate labdhaṃ labdhaṃ caiva phalapradam \|*  
*tanme sarvaṃ samācakṣva kautukādeva pṛcchataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Tell me, who am asking through curiosity, all that as to who secures it and (tell me) howit gives fruit when secured?

## \|\| 32.60 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ṛṣikoṭissamāyātā dakṣiṇāpathavāsinī \|*  
*snānārthaṃ puṣkare rājanpuṣkaraṃ ca viyadgatam \|\| 60 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

60\. O king, a crore of sages, living in the southern part came to Puṣkara to bathe; but Puṣkara went up to the sky.

## \|\| 32.61 \|\|

*matvāte munayaḥ sarve prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ \|*  
*dhyāyamānāḥ paraṃ brahma sthitā dvādaśavatsarān \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. All the sages, knowing this, absorbed in suspending the breath, remained there for twelve years, meditating upon the highest Brahman.

## \|\| 32.62 \|\|

*brahmā maharṣayastatra devāssendrāssamāgatāḥ \|*  
*ṛṣayoṃtarhitāḥ procurniyamāṃste suduṣkarān \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Brahmā, great sages, gods with Indra came there. The (great) sages, concealing themselves, told the very difficult restraints:

## \|\| 32.63 \|\|

*ākāraṇaṃ puṣkarasya maṃtreṇa kriyatāṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*āpohiṣṭheti tisṛbhirṛgbhiḥ sāṃnidhyameṣyati \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. “O brāhmaṇas, invoke Puṣkara with a prayer. It will come near you by your reciting (i.e. if you recite) the three ṛks (beginning with) Āpohiṣṭha.

## \|\| 32.64 \|\|

*aghamarṣaṇajapyena bhavedvai phaladāyakam \|*  
*viprairvākyāvasāne tu sarvaistaistu tathā kṛtam \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. It will give you fruit by your muttering the expiatory prayer”. At the end of the words (uttered by the sages) all brāhmaṇas did like that (i.e. as they were told).

## \|\| 32.65-66 \|\|

*kṛtena puṇyatāṃ prāptā ye nideśācca te dvijāḥ \|*  
*garhitā dharmaśāstreṣu te viprā dakṣiṇottarāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ye cānye pārvatīyāśca śrāddhenārhaṃti ketanam \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇādrājanviyatyevaṃ samāsthitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. The brāhmaṇas, who did like that according to the instruction, obtained religious virtue. The brāhmaṇas living in the south and north censured in the codes of laws and other brāhmaṇas dwelling in mountains do not deserve an invitation to a śrāddha. O king, for this reason, it (i.e. Puṣkara) remained in the sky only.

## \|\| 32.67 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ puṣkaraṃ snānātpūtatāmabhiyacchati \|*  
*brahmaṇā sahitaṃ rājansarveṣāṃ puṇyadāyakam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. O king, Puṣkara gives purity (to a person) by bathing (in it) on the full moon day of Kārtika. It gives religious merit to all including even Brahmā.

## \|\| 32.68 \|\|

*tatrāgatāstu ye varṇāḥ sarve te puṇyabhājanāḥ \|*  
*dvijaistulyā na saṃdeho vinā maṃtreṇa te nṛpa \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. O king, (persons of) all castes who come there to obtain religious merit become equal to brāhmaṇas (even) without (the recitation of) a prayer.

## \|\| 32.69 \|\|

*āgneyaṃ tu yadā ṛkṣaṃ kārtikyāṃ bhavati kvacit \|*  
*mahatī sā tithirjñeyā snāne dāne tathottamā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The day on which the Moon is in the lunar mansion viz. Kṛttikā on the full moon day of Kārtika, should be regarded as important, and is good for (taking) a bath and (giving in) charity.

## \|\| 32.70 \|\|

*yadā yāmyaṃ tu bhavati ṛkṣaṃ tasyāṃ tithau kvacit \|*  
*tithiḥ sāpi mahāpuṇyā yatibhiḥ parikīrtitā \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. When on this day the Moon is in the lunar mansion called Bharaṇī that (day) also is declared to be very auspicious by the ascetics.

## \|\| 32.71 \|\|

*prājāpatyaṃ yadā ṛkṣaṃ tithau tasyāṃ narādhipa \|*  
*sā mahākārtikī proktā devānāmapi durlabhā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. That full moon day of Kārtika on which the Moon enters the mansion called Rohiṇi, that day, O king, is said to be Mahākārtikī; it is difficult to be had even by gods.

## \|\| 32.72 \|\|

*yadā cārke gurau some vāreṣveteṣu vai triṣu \|*  
*trīṇyetāni ca ṛkṣāṇi svayaṃ proktāni brahmaṇā \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Brahmā himself has declared these three lunar mansions (to be auspicious) when they fall on Sundays or Thursdays or Mondays.

## \|\| 32.73 \|\|

*atrāśvamedhikaṃ puṇyaṃ snātasya bhavati dhruvam \|*  
*dānamakṣayatāṃ yāti pitṝṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. He, who takes a bath (on one of these days in Puṣkara), obtains greater religious merit than (by performing) an Aśvamedha sacrifice. Gifts (given on one of these days) and also offering oflibations to the manes (made on one of these days) become inexhaustible.

## \|\| 32.74 \|\|

*viśākhāsu yadā bhānuḥ kṛttikāsu ca caṃdramāḥ \|*  
*sa yogaḥ puṣkaro nāma puṣkareṣvatidurlabhaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. That combination when the Sun is in the Viśākhā and the Moon in the Kṛttikā is called Puṣkara and very difficult to be had at the Puṣaras.

## \|\| 32.75 \|\|

*aṃtarikṣāvatīrṇe tu tīrthe paitāmahe śubhe \|*  
*snānaṃ ye'tra kariṣyaṃti teṣāṃ lokā mahodayāḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Those, who take bath at Puṣkara, which has come down (to the earth) from the sky, which is auspicious and which is sacred to the grandsire (i.e. Brahmā), obtain worlds of prosperity.

## \|\| 32.76 \|\|

*na spṛhāṃtenyapuṇyasya kṛtasyāpyakṛtasya ca \|*  
*kariṣyaṃti mahārāja satyametadudāhṛtam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. O great king, I have told you the truth that these people will not long for any other religious merit done or undone.

## \|\| 32.77 \|\|

*tīrthānāṃ pravaraṃ tīrthaṃ pṛthivyāmiha paṭhyate \|*  
*nāsmātparaṃ puṇyatīrthaṃ lokeṣu nṛpa paṭhyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. It is said to be (the best) holy place of all holy places here on the earth. O king, no holy place is said to be superior to this.

## \|\| 32.78 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa puṇyā pāpaharā śubhā \|*  
*uduṃbaravanāttasmādāgatā ca sarasvatī \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Especially on the full moon day of Kārtika that auspicious Sarasvatī that removes sins has arrived (here) from that Udumbara forest.

## \|\| 32.79-81 \|\|

*tayā tatpūritaṃ tīrthaṃ puṣkaraṃ munisevitam \|*  
*dakṣiṇe śikharaṃ bhāti parvatasyāvidūrataḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*nīlāṃjanacayaprakhyaṃ varṇato nīlaśādvalam \|*  
*tayā tacchikharaṃ tasya khasthitaṃ puṣkaraṃ yathā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*prāvṛṭkāle viyatpūrṇaṃ ghanavṛṃdamivocchritam \|*  
*kadaṃbapuṣpagaṃdhāḍhyaṃ kuṭajārjunabhūṣitam \|\| 81 \|\|*

79-80a. She has filled up (with her water) the holy place resorted to by sages. Not far from it shines the mountain-peak called Nīlāñjanacaya and dark-blue in colour like a grass-plot.

80b-81. Due to her the peak appears to be the Puṣkara high up in the sky full of lofty multitude of clouds in the rainy season. It was full of the fragrance of Kadamba flowers and decorated with Kuṭaja and Arjuna flowers.

## \|\| 32.82-83 \|\|

*rathamārgamivāroḍhuṃ ravestacchikharaṃ sthitam \|*  
*vṛttaissapulakaissnigdhaiḥ strīṇāmiva payodharaiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*śrīphalaiḥ śikharaṃ bhāti samantātsumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*guṃjadbhiḥ ṣaṭpadakulaiḥ samaṃtādupaśobhitam \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. It remained there as it were to go up to the path of the Sun. The peak shines (i.e. s hone) with beautiful coconuts on all sides. The coconuts were round like the glossy round breasts of ladies full of horripilation. It was adorned all round with the humming swarms of bees.

## \|\| 32.84-85 \|\|

*kokilārāvaruciraṃ śikhi kekā ravākulam \|*  
*śṛṃge manohare tasminnudgatāsu manoramā \|\| 84 \|\|*

*puṇyāpuṇyajalopetā nadīyaṃ brahmaṇassutā \|*  
*vaṃśastaṃbātsuvipulā pravṛttā cottarāmukhī \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. It was charming with the notes of cuckoos and full of the notes of peacocks. This auspicious river, having auspicious water, the daughter of Brahmā and very beautiful has risen on that charming peak; and from that cluster of bamboos that very great river has flowed towards the north.

## \|\| 32.86-89 \|\|

*gatvā tato nātidūrātpunaryāti parāṅmukhī \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti sā devī prasannā prakaṭāsthitā \|\| 86 \|\|*

*antardhānaṃ parityajya prāṇināmanukampayā \|*  
*kanakā suprabhā caiva nandā prācī sarasvatī \|\| 87 \|\|*

*paṃcasrotāḥ puṣkareṣu brahmaṇā paribhāṣitā \|*  
*tasyāstīre suramyāṇi tīrthānyāyatanāni ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

*saṃsevitāni munibhiḥ siddhaiścāpi samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*teṣu sarveṣu bhavitā dharmahetuḥ sarasvatī \|\| 89 \|\|*

86-87a. Not flowing far away from that place she again flows towards the west. Thereafter that goddess, who was pleased, having given up her concealment, stays manifest due to her compassion for beings.

87b-88a. At Puṣkara Brahma has given her, having five streams (five names viz.) Kanakā, Suprabhā, Nandā, Prācī and Sarasvatī.

88b-89. On her bank there are very charming holy places and temples, which have been resorted to by sages and Siddhas from every side. In all these (sacred places etc.) the cause of religious merit is Sarasvatī.

## \|\| 32.90 \|\|

*hāṭakakṣitigaurīṇāṃ tattīrtheṣu mahodayam \|*  
*dānaṃ dattaṃ naraiḥ snātairjanayatyakṣayaṃ phalam \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Gift of gold, dwelling or land made at these holy places by men who have bathed (i.e. after having bathed) causes great prosperity and generates inexhaustible fruit.

## \|\| 32.91 \|\|

*dhānyapradānaṃ pravaraṃ vadaṃti tilapradānaṃ ca tathā munīṃdrāḥ \|*  
*yaisteṣu tīrtheṣu naraiḥ pradattaṃ taddharmahetu pravaraṃ pradiṣṭam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The best sages declare that the gift of grains is excellent, and also the gift of oil. That which is given by men at the holy places is said to be superior.

## \|\| 32.92 \|\|

*prāyopaveśaṃ prayataḥ prayatnādyasteṣu kuryātpramadā pumānvā \|*  
*tīrthepi saṃyojya manopi cetthaṃ bhuṃkte phalaṃ brahmagṛhe yatheṣṭam \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. A woman or a man, who, being restrained and having fixed her or his mind on the holy places would fast unto death with perseverance, enjoys fruit at Brahmā’s residence as much as he desires.

## \|\| 32.93 \|\|

*tasyopakaṃṭhe mriyate hi yaistu karmakṣayātsthāvarajaṃgamaiśca \|*  
*te cāpi sarve sakalaṃ prasahya labhaṃti yajñasya phalaṃ durāpam \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. All those—the immobile and the mobile—who die in her vicinity as a result of the exhaustion of their deeds, get the excellent fruit of a sacrifice which is difficult to obtain.

## \|\| 32.94 \|\|

*tatastu sā dharmaphalāraṇī ca janmādiduḥkhārditacetasāṃ tu \|*  
*sarvātmanā cāruphalā sarasvatī sevyā prayatnātpuruṣairmahānadī \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. Therefore, men with all their heart should, with great effort, resort to the great river Sarasvatī that gives a charming fruit, gives the reward of religious merit to those whose minds are afflicted with the grief of birth etc.

## \|\| 32.95 \|\|

*tatra ye salilaṃ pūtaṃ pibaṃti satataṃ narāḥ \|*  
*na te manuṣyā devāste jagatyāmiha saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Those who always drink that sacred water there, are not men but gods dwelling here on the earth.

## \|\| 32.96 \|\|

*yajñairdānaistapobhiśca yatphalaṃ prāpyate dvijaiḥ \|*  
*tadatra snānamātreṇa śūdrairapi svabhāvajaiḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. That fruit which the brāhmaṇas get by (performing) sacrifices, (making) gifts, is obtained even by śūdras born according to their innate nature by taking a bath here.

## \|\| 32.97 \|\|

*darśanātpuṣkarasyāpi mahāpātakinopi ye \|*  
*tepi tatpāpanirmuktāḥ svargaṃ yāṃti tanukṣaye \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Even great sinners, by the sight of Puṣkara, being free from sins, go to heaven after they cast their body.

## \|\| 32.98 \|\|

*tatropavāsī yajñasya puṃḍarīkasya yatphalam \|*  
*tatprāpnoti naraḥ kṣipramalpāyāsena puṣkare \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. By observing a fast at Puṣkara a man quickly and with little effort obtains that fruit which is the fruit of a fire-sacrifice.

## \|\| 32.99 \|\|

*māghamāse tilānyastu prayacchati ca sa ddvije \|*  
*yathāśakti ca bhaktyā ca sa viṣṇubhavane vaset \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. He, who, in the month of Māgha, offers, with devotion and according to his capacity, sesamum to a virtuous brāhmaṇa, would live in the house of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 32.100 \|\|

*tatropavāsaṃ snānaṃ ca paṃcagavyāśanaṃ tathā \|*  
*yaḥ karoti naraḥ sopi dehāṃte svargamāpnuyāt \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. That man also, who observes a fast there, bathes and eats the five products of a cow, would obtain (i.e. go to) heaven after death.

## \|\| 32.101 \|\|

*vasaṃti tatsamīpasthā yepi taskarajātayaḥ \|*  
*tepi tasyānubhāvena svaryāṃti ca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Even the thieves who live in its vicinity go to heaven due to its power. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 32.102-103 \|\|

*ye punaḥ śūdravṛttisthāstrirātropoṣitā narāḥ \|*  
*prayacchaṃti dvijeṣvarthaṃ brahmaśaktisamanvitāḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*te mṛtā yānamārūḍhāḥ padmāsanacaturbhujāḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā saha sāyujyaṃ prāpnuvaṃtyapunarbhavam \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. Also men following the occupation of śūdras, who, by fasting for three nights, give money to brāhmaṇas, being endowed with the power due to pious utterances, and being immortal and having four arms, get into a vehicle having a lotus-seat and obtain union with Brahman and are not reborn.

## \|\| 32.104 \|\|

*gaṃgodbhedaṃ yatra gaṃgā saṃprāptā saritāṃ varām \|*  
*sarasvatīṃ draṣṭukāmā sāṃtvārthe prodgatāṃ'barāt \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. Gaṅgodbheda is the place where Gaṅgā came to see and appease Sarasvatī, the best river, rising from the sky.

## \|\| 32.105-115 \|\|

*tatra gatvā payaḥpūtaṃ surasiddhaniṣevitam \|*  
*sārasvataṃ ca vimalaṃ vidyādharagaṇārcitam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*pītamekāṃjalimitaṃ yenāptaṃ tena tatparaṃ \|*  
*avalokya diśaṃ pūrvāmāha gaṃge sakhi tvayā \|\| 106 \|\|*

*ekākinī viyuktāsmi kva yāsyehamabāṃdhavā \|*  
*tāṃ vijñāya tato gaṃgā rudaṃtīṃ śokakarśitām \|\| 107 \|\|*

*pūrvadeśātsamāyātā draṣṭuṃ tāṃ dīnamānasām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ mahābhāgāṃ pariṣvajya tu pīḍitām \|\| 108 \|\|*

*netre pramṛjya caitasyāḥ prāha gaṃgā vacastadā \|*  
*mā rodīstvaṃ mahābhāge duḥṣkaraṃ te kṛtaṃ sakhi \|\| 109 \|\|*

*devakāryaṃ yadanyena kartuṃ śakyeta naiva hi \|*  
*etasmātte mahābhāge draṣṭuṃ devāḥ samāgatāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*eṣāṃ ca kriyatāṃ pūjā vāṅmanaḥ kāya karmaṇā \|*  
*sarasvatī sureṃdrāṇāṃ kṛttvā pūjā vidhikramam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*krameṇa brahmajā paścātsaṃgatā tu sakhījanam \|*  
*jyeṣṭhamadhyamayormadhye saṃgamo lokaviśrutaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*paścānmukhī brahmasutā jāhnavī tu udaṅmukhī \|*  
*tataste vibudhāḥ sarve puṣkaraṃ ye samāgatāḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*viditvā duṣkaraṃ karma tasyā stutimakārayan \|*  
*tvaṃ buddhistvaṃ matirlakṣmīstvaṃ vidyā tvaṃ gatiḥ parā \|\| 114 \|\|*

*tvaṃ śraddhā ttvaṃ parā niṣṭhā buddhirmedhā ratiḥ kṣamā \|*  
*tvaṃ siddhistvaṃ svadhā svāhā tvaṃ pavitraṃ mataṃ mahat \|\| 115 \|\|*

105-106a. He, who, having gone there, has drunk a cavityful pure water (of Gaṅgā) resorted to by gods and Siddhas and also the pure water of Sarasvatī, worshipped by groups of Vidyādharas, attains to that highest (Brahman).

106b-107a. Looking in the east, Sarasvatī said: “O friend Gaṅgā, you have left me alone. Where are you going? I am friendless.”

1 07b-108a. Gaṅgā, finding her to be weeping and distressed with grief, came there from the eastern region to see her of afflicted mind.

108b-111a. Seeing the highly virtuous one and having embraced the distressed one, and having wiped her eyes Gaṅgā said these words at that time: “O you glorious one, do not weep. O friend, you have done, for the gods, a difficult task, which none else can do. For this reason, O you highly virtuous one, gods have come to see you. Worship them with words and with mental and physical acts.”

111b-112a. Sarasvatī, Brahma’s daughter, having duly worshipped the best gods, got united with (i.e. mixed with) her friend.

112b-114a. The confluence of the two between the Jyeṣṭha and the Madhyama Puṣkara is well-known in the world. Brahmā’s daughter (i.e. Sarasvatī then flowed) towards the west and Gaṅgā towards the north. Then all the gods who had come to Puṣkara, realising the difficult task (she had done) praised her:

114b-115. “You are intellect; you are thought; you are Lakṣmī (i.e. prosperity): you are knowledge; you are faith; you are highest devotion; you are intellect; you are retentive faculty; you are love; you are forbearance; you are success; you are libation offered to dead ancestors; you are oblation offered to gods; you are pure thought.

## \|\| 32.116 \|\|

*saṃdhyā rātriḥ prabhā bhūtirmedhā śraddhā sarasvatī \|*  
*yajña vidyā mahāvidyā guhyavidyā ca śobhanā \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. You are twilight, night, lustre, prosperity, retentive faculty, and faith. You are sacrificial lore, great knowledge, secret knowledge and bright.

## \|\| 32.117 \|\|

*ānvīkṣikī tu yā vārtā daṃḍanītiśca kathyate \|*  
*namostu te puṇyajale namaḥ sāgaragāmini \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. You are said to be metaphysics, agriculture, and judicature. O you of auspicious water, salutation to you who go to the ocean.

## \|\| 32.118-119 \|\|

*namaste pāpanirmoke namo devi jagatpriye \|*  
*evaṃ stutā hi sā devī divyā svārthaparāyaṇaiḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*evaṃ sā prāṅmukhī tatra sthitā devī sarasvatī \|*  
*sarvatīrthamayī devī sarvāmarasamanvitā \|\| 119 \|\|*

118a. Salutation to you who liberate (persons) from sins; salutation to you, O goddess dear to the world”.

118b-119. Thus the divine goddess was praised by (the gods) intent upon securing their own interest. Thus that goddess Sarasvatī, full of all holy places, remained there with all gods, facing the east.

## \|\| 32.120 \|\|

*prācī seti budhairjñeyā brahmaṇo vacanaṃ tathā \|*  
*tatra śuddhāvaṭaṃnāma tīrthaṃ paitāmahaṃ smṛtam \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. She is to be known as Prācī—these are the words of Brahmā. There is a place named Śuddhavaṭa, said to (be sac,. red) to the grandsire (i.e. Brahmā).

## \|\| 32.121 \|\|

*darśanenāpi vai tasya mahāpātakinopi ye \|*  
*bhogibhogānsamaśnaṃti viśuddhā brahmaṇoṃtike \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Even those, who are great sinners, becoming pure merely by seeing it, obtain the pleasures of the happy persons, in the vicinity of Brahma.

## \|\| 32.122 \|\|

*prāyopaveśaṃ ye tatra prakurvaṃti narottamāḥ \|*  
*te mṛtā brahmayānena divaṃ yāṃtyakutobhayāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. Those who observe there a fast unto death, being immortal and having no fear from anywhere, go to heaven in Brahmā’s vehicle.

## \|\| 32.123 \|\|

*tatrālpamapi yairdānaṃ dattaṃ brahmavidātmanām \|*  
*janmāṃtaraśataṃ teṣāṃ tairdattaṃ bhāvitātmanām \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Those who have even given very little to the knowers of Brahman—to those whose thoughts are fixed on the supreme spirit—have given a hundred existences (are not to be born for at least a hundred existences).

## \|\| 32.124 \|\|

*khaṇḍasphuṭitasaṃskāraṃ tatra kurvanti ye narāḥ \|*  
*te brahmalokamāsādya modante sukhinassadā \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. Those men who perform there the purificatory rite called Khaṇḍasphuṭita, reach the world of Brahmā and are always happy there.

## \|\| 32.125 \|\|

*yo'tra pūjājapohomaḥ kṛto bhavati dehinām \|*  
*anantaṃ tatphalaṃ sarvaṃ brahmabhaktiratātmanām \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. The fruit of the worship offered, or prayers muttered or sacrifice performed here, which is obtained by men whose minds are engrossed in devotion to Brahman, is infinite.

## \|\| 32.126 \|\|

*tatra dīpapradānena jñānacakṣuratīṃdriyaḥ \|*  
*prāpnoti dhūpadānena sthānaṃ brahmaniṣevitam \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. A person offering a lamp there, gets intellectual vision and becomes one with the supreme soul. A person, by offering incense (there) obtains the place resorted to by Brahma.

## \|\| 32.127 \|\|

*atha kiṃ bahunoktena saṃgame yatpradīyate \|*  
*tadanaṃtaphalaṃ proktaṃ jīvato vā mṛtasya ca \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Or what is the use of talking much? Whatever is offered at the confluence (of Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī) is said to give infinite fruit to a person alive or dead.

## \|\| 32.128-131 \|\|

*snānājjapāttathā homādanaṃtaphalasādhakam \|*  
*rāmeṇāgatya vai tatra piṃḍaṃ daśarathasya ca \|\| 128 \|\|*

*dattaṃ śrāddhaṃ tatra tena mārkaṃḍeyena darśite \|*  
*tatra vāpī catuḥkoṇā tatra piṃḍapradā narāḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

*haṃsayuktena yānena sarve yāṃti triviṣṭapam \|*  
*tasyāṃ vāpyāṃ tu vai brahmā pitṛmedhaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 130 \|\|*

*yajñaṃ yajñavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ samāptavaradakṣiṇam \|*  
*vasavaḥ pitaro jñeyā rudrāścaiva pitāmahāḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

128-129a. An unending fruit accrues by taking a bath or muttering prayers or performing a sacrifice there. Having come to that place Rāma offered a piṇḍa and a śrāddha to Daśaratha as directed by that (sage) Mārkaṇḍeya.

129b-130a. There is a well with four corners. All men who offer there go to heaven (borne) in a car to which swans are yoked.

130b-131. Brahma, the best among those well-versed in (performing) sacrifices, performed at that well a sacrifice in honour of manes in which excellent gifts were given. Vasus should be known as the manes and Rudras as the grandsires.

## \|\| 32.132 \|\|

*ādityāśca tatasteṣāṃ vihitāḥ prapitāmahāḥ \|*  
*trividhā api āhūya punaruktā viriṃcinā \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. Similarly Ādityas are mentioned as their great grandsires. (All these) of the three categories were called and addressed by Brahma:

## \|\| 32.133-134 \|\|

*bhavadbhiḥ piṃḍadānādyaṃ grāhyamatra sthitaissadā \|*  
*yatkṛtaṃ pitṛkāryaṃ ca tadanaṃtaphalaṃ bhavet \|\| 133 \|\|*

*vṛtyarthaṃ pitarasteṣāṃ tuṣṭāścaiva pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*labhaṃte tarpaṇāttṛptiṃ piṃḍadānāttriviṣṭapam \|\| 134 \|\|*

133a. “Always remaining here you should accept the offering of piṇḍas etc.”

133b-134. Since what is done for (i.e. offered to) manes for their maintenance would give unending fruit, the manes and the grandsires also are pleased with them. By the libation they are satisfied and by the offering of piṇḍas they obtain (i.e. go to) heaven.

## \|\| 32.135 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaṃ parityajya prācīne piṃḍado bhavet \|*  
*datvā putraḥ prayatnena pitṝnsarvāṃśca tarpayet \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. Therefore leaving everything (else) (a man) should offer piṇḍas at Prācīna. A son by offering (piṇḍas) should please all his manes.

## \|\| 32.136 \|\|

*prācīneśvaradevasya purobhūtaṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*āditīrthaṃ tadityuktaṃ darśanādapi muktidam \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. It is preferred and valued by Pracīneśvara, is called the Āditīrtha (i.e. the best sacred place) and brings about salvation even by (merely) being seen.

## \|\| 32.137 \|\|

*spṛṣṭvā tu salilaṃ tatra mucyate janmabaṃdhanāt \|*  
*avagāhanādbrahmaṇo'sau bhavatyanucaraḥ sadā \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. A person merely by touching the water there becomes free from the bondage of birth (and death); by bathing in it he ever becomes the follower of Brahman.

## \|\| 32.138 \|\|

*āditīrthe naraḥ snātvā yaḥ pradadyātsamādhinā \|*  
*annamalpamapi prāyaḥ prāyaśassvargamāpnuyāt \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. A man who having bathed at Āditīrtha, gives even little food, would generally obtain (i.e. go to) heaven.

## \|\| 32.139 \|\|

*yastatra brahmabhaktānāṃ naraḥ snātvā dadeddhanam \|*  
*kṛseraṇāpi hemnā ca sa svarge modate sukhī \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. A man, who, after having bathed there, would offer money with a dish consisting of sesamum and rice and with gold, being happy, enjoys in heaven.

## \|\| 32.140 \|\|

*prācīsarasvatī tatra naraiḥ kiṃ mṛgyate param \|*  
*tasyāṃ snānātphalaṃ tṛptyai tapoyajñādilakṣaṇam \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Prācī Sarasvatī resides there; what else do men seek? The fruit of a bath in her (water) leads to satisfaction, and is of the nature of (the fruit of) penance, sacrifice etc.

## \|\| 32.141 \|\|

*ye pibaṃti narāḥ puṇyāṃ prācīṃ devīṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*na te narāḥ surā jñeyā mārkaṃḍeyarṣirabravīt \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. Those men who drink the auspicious (water of) goddess Prācī Sarasvatī are not men. They should be known as gods. So said sage Mārkaṇḍeya.

## \|\| 32.142 \|\|

*sarasvatī nadīṃ prāpya na snāne niyamaḥ kvacit \|*  
*bhukte vā na ca vā bhukte divā vā yadi vā niśi \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. After having reached river Sarasvatī, there is no (strict) rule about bath. (A person can have it) after having eaten food or without having eaten food, or by day or at night.

## \|\| 32.143 \|\|

*tattīrthaṃ sarvattīrthānāṃ prācīnaṃ pravaraṃ smṛtat \|*  
*pāpaghnaṃ puṇyajananaṃ prāṇināṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. That sacred place, viz. Prācīna is said to be best of all. It is said to destroy the sins of beings, and to be give religious virtue.

## \|\| 32.144 \|\|

*ye punarbhāvitātmānastatra snātvā janārdanam \|*  
*pūjayanti yathāśakti te prayāṃti triviṣṭapam \|\| 144 \|\|*

144\. Again, those devout persons, who having bathed there, worship Janārdana according to their capacity, go to heaven.

## \|\| 32.145 \|\|

*devānāṃ pravaro viṣṇustena yatra sarasvatī \|*  
*sevitā tatparaṃ tīrthaṃ kṣitau brahmasuto'bravīt \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Viṣṇu is the best among gods. So that place where he resorted to Sarasvatī is a great holy place—so said the son of Brahmā.

## \|\| 32.146 \|\|

*tatastasmānmahātīrthaṃ manyamānā mahodayam \|*  
*maṃdākinīmudīkṣaṃtī sthitā tatra sarasvatī \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. Therefore (i.e. because Viṣṇu resorted to that place), Sarasvatī, looking upon it as a great and very glorious sacred place, remained there waiting for Mandākinī (i.e. Gaṅgā).

## \|\| 32.147-149 \|\|

*tattīrthaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ paraṃ svāyaṃbhuvo'bravīt \|*  
*maṃdākinyāsamaṃ yatra prāpya puṇyasamāgamam \|\| 147 \|\|*

*tatrasthāne sthitā devaiḥ stutā devī sarasvatī \|*  
*matvā caikākinīṃ tāṃ tu dīnāsyāṃ dīnamānasāṃ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*sakhīṃ tadā'sṛjadbrahmā rūpiṇīṃ vimalekṣaṇām \|*  
*hariṇīṃ harirapyāśu jajñe kamalalocanām \|\| 149 \|\|*

147-148a. The son of Brahmā said, that sacred place is the best of all sacred places; gods praised Sarasvatī that remained there, where they obtained religious merit equal to (that obtained by resorting to) Gaṅgā.

148b-149. Knowing her to be of a melancholy face and of a distressed mind, Brahmā created her beautiful friend of spotless eyes.

l50-15la. Viṣṇu also created Lakṣmī of eyes like lotuses. Śiva (called) Nīlakaṇṭha, Vṛṣadhvaja, Vajrapāṇi, who was the lord of lords, created Sarasvatī’s friend, viz. Vajriṇī, having the lustre of an excellent doe.

## \|\| 32.151-154 \|\|

*sakhīṃ saṃjanayāmāsa sarasvatyāstrilocanaḥ \|*  
*vilokyamānā sā rājansakhībhiḥ surasuṃdarī \|\| 151 \|\|*

*prahṛṣṭā yātumārabdhā devādeśānmahānadī \|*  
*tataḥ sakhībhiḥ sārddhaṃ sā prācīnāgaṃtumudyatā \|\| 152 \|\|*

*sarasvatī samastānāṃ tāsāṃ śreṣṭhatamā smṛtā \|*  
*prācīsarasvatītoyaṃ ye pibaṃti mṛgā bhuvi \|\| 153 \|\|*

*tepi svargaṃ gamiṣyaṃti yajñairdvijavarā yathā \|*  
*ciṃtāmaṇirivātraiṣā prācī jñeyā sarasvatī \|\| 154 \|\|*

151b-153a. That great river, that divine beauty, being seen by her friends and being very much delighted started to proceed by the command of gods. Then that Sarasvatī, regarded as the best of all those (friends), turning towards the east, was eager to proceed.

153b-154. Even those beasts who drink the water of Prācī Sarasvatī go to heaven as the best brāhmaṇas (go to heaven) by (performing) sacrifices. Prācī Sarasvatī at this place should be looked upon as the desire-yielding gem.

## \|\| 32.155-156 \|\|

*tathā kāmaphalasyeyaṃ hetubhūtā mahānadī \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṃ diśamālokya punaḥ paścānmukhī gatā \|\| 155 \|\|*

*uktā tayā tathā gaṃgā diśaṃ prācīṃ vrajasva ha \|*  
*vismartavyā na cāhaṃ te vraja devi yathāgatam \|\| 156 \|\|*

155-156. Like it this great river has become the fulfiller of desires. Having seen (i.e. flowed towards) the southern direction she has gone to the west. She said to Gaṅgā: “Go to the eastern region; forget me not; O goddess, go as you had come.”

## Chapter 33 - Rāma’s Visit to Mārkaṇḍeya’s Hermitage

## \|\| 33.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*mārkaṃḍeyena vai rāmaḥ kathamatra prabodhitaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ samāgamo bhūtaḥ kasminkāle kadā mune \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said;

1\. O sage, how was Rāma enlightened here by Mārkaṇ-ḍeya? How did they meet? When did they meet?

## \|\| 33.2 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeyaḥ kasya sutaḥ kathaṃ jāto mahātapāḥ \|*  
*nāmno'sya nigamaṃ brūhi yathābhūtaṃ mahāmune \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Whose son was Mārkaṇḍeya? How was the one of great penance born? O great sage, tell me the exact explanation of his name.

Pulastya said;

## \|\| 33.3 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi mārkaṃḍeyodbhavaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*purākalpe muniḥ pūrvaṃ mṛkaṃḍurnāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I shall tell you about the birth of Mārkaṇḍeya. In the old Kalpa there was a well-known sage by name Mṛkaṇḍu.

## \|\| 33.4 \|\|

*bhṛgoḥ putro mahābhāgaḥ sabhāryastaptavāṃstapaḥ \|*  
*tasya putrastadā jāto vasatastu vanāṃtare \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The illustrious (sage), the son of Bhṛgu, practised penance with his wife. When he was living in a forest, a son was born to him.

## \|\| 33.5 \|\|

*sapaṃcavārṣiko bhūto bāla eva guṇādhikaḥ \|*  
*jñāninā sa tadā dṛṣṭo bhramanbālastadāṃgaṇe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. That boy, superior in virtues, became five years old. At that time a sage saw the boy roaming about in the courtyard.

## \|\| 33.6 \|\|

*sthitvā sa suciraṃ kālaṃ bhāvyarthaṃ pratyabudhyata \|*  
*tasya pitrā sa vai pṛṣṭaḥ kiyadāyuḥ sutasya me \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Remaining there for a pretty long time, he knew the future (events in the life of the boy). He was asked by the boy’s father: “What is the span of the life of my son?

## \|\| 33.7 \|\|

*saṃkhyāyācakṣva varṣāṇi tasyālpānyadhikāni vā \|*  
*mṛkaṃḍunaivamuktastu sa jñānī vākyamabravīt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Calculate and tell me (the number of) years (of the span of his life—whether they are) few or many.” Thus addressed by Mṛkaṇḍu, the wise sage spoke:

## \|\| 33.8 \|\|

*ṣaṇmāsamāyuḥ putrasya dhātrā sṛṣṭaṃ munīśvara \|*  
*naiva śokastvayā kāryaḥ satyametadudāhṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “‘O best sage, the Creator has determined (the span of) your son’s life to be six months. Do not grieve. I have told you the truth.”

## \|\| 33.9 \|\|

*sa tacchrutvā vaco bhīṣma jñāninā yadudāhṛtam \|*  
*athopanayanaṃ cakre bālakasya pitā tadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The father, having heard what the sage had said, then performed the thread-ceremony of the boy.

## \|\| 33.10 \|\|

*āha cainaṃ pitāputramṛṣīṃstvamabhivādaya \|*  
*evamuktaḥ sa vai pitrā prahṛṣṭaścābhivādane \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. And the father said (to the son): “O son, salute the sages.” Thus told by the father, he took delight in saluting people.

## \|\| 33.11 \|\|

*na varṇā varṇatāṃ vetti sarvavarṇābhivādanaḥ \|*  
*paṃcamāsāstvatikrāṃtā divasāḥ paṃcaviṃśatiḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He did not care for the (high) caste or the absence of it (in the case of persons whom he saluted since) he saluted (persons belonging to) all castes. (In this way) five years and twenty-five days rolled by.

## \|\| 33.12 \|\|

*mārgeṇātha samāyātā ṛṣayastatra sapta vai \|*  
*bālena tena te dṛṣṭāḥ sarve cāpyabhivāditāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. There were going seven sages along the path. The boy saw them, and he saluted them all.

## \|\| 33.13 \|\|

*āyuṣmānbhava tairuktaḥ sa bālo daṃḍamekhalī \|*  
*uktvaivaṃ te punarbālamapaśyankṣīṇajīvitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The boy having a staff and wearing a muñjā-girdle was addressed by them: “Live long”. Having spoken thus, they observed (that) the boy (would) be short-lived.

## \|\| 33.14 \|\|

*dināni paṃca tasyāyurjñātvā bhītāśca te nṛpa \|*  
*taṃ gṛhītvā bālakaṃ ca gatāste brahmaṇoṃtikam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. O king, knowing that his life would be just five days (more), they were frightened. Taking the boy, they went near Brahmā.

## \|\| 33.15 \|\|

*pratimucya ca taṃ rājanpraṇipetuḥ pitāmaham \|*  
*ayamāveditastaistu tena brahmābhivāditaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. And, O king, leaving (i.e. placing) him there, they saluted the grandsire. They gave Brahmā information about (i.e. told Brahmā the account of) the boy. Then he saluted Brahmā.

## \|\| 33.16 \|\|

*cirāyurbrahmaṇā bālaḥ proktaḥ sa ṛṣisannidhau \|*  
*tataste munayaḥ prītāḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ pitāmahāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In the presence of the sages, Brahmā said to the boy: “Live long”. Then all the sages, having heard those words from the grandsire, were pleased.

## \|\| 33.17 \|\|

*pitāmaha ṛṣīndṛṣṭvā provāca vismayānvitaḥ \|*  
*kāryeṇa yena cāyātaḥ koyaṃ bālo nivedyatām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The grandsire, seeing the sages, was amazed and said (to them): “Tell me for what purpose this boy has come to me and also tell me who is.”

## \|\| 33.18 \|\|

*tatasta ṛṣayo rājansarvaṃ tasmai nyavedayan \|*  
*putro mṛkaṃḍoḥ kṣīṇāyuḥ sāyuṣaṃ kuru bālakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Then, O king, the sages told him everything. “This is the son of Mṛkaṇḍu. His life is short. Make him long-lived.

## \|\| 33.19 \|\|

*alpāyuṣastvasya munirbadhvemāṃ cāpi mekhalām \|*  
*yajñopavītaṃ daṃḍaṃ ca datvā cainamabodhayat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The sage (Mṛkaṇḍu) tied a (muñjā-) girdle (round) his (waist), gave him whose life was short a sacred thread and a staff (i.e. the sage Mṛkaṇḍu performed his thread-ceremony) and advised him:

## \|\| 33.20 \|\|

*yaṃ kaṃcitpaśyase bāla bhramaṃtaṃ bhūtale janam \|*  
*tasyābhivādaḥ kartavya evamāha pitā vacaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. ‘O boy, salute every person whom you see going about on the earth’. The father said these words to him.

## \|\| 33.21 \|\|

*abhivādanaśīloyaṃ kṣitau dṛṣṭaḥ paribhraman \|*  
*tīrthayātrāprasaṃgena daivayogātpitāmaha \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. O grandsire, we, who were going on a pilgrimage, saw, by chance, this boy disposed to saluting (everyone he saw).

## \|\| 33.22 \|\|

*cirāyurbhava putreti proktosau tatra bālakaḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ vaco bhavetsatyamasmākaṃ bhavatā saha \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. We said to him: O son, live long. How will our words along with (words uttered by) you come true?”

## \|\| 33.23 \|\|

*evamuktastadā taistu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*ṛtavākyādiyaṃ bhūmiḥ saṃsthitā sarvatobhayā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus addressed by them, Brahmā, the grandsire of the worlds (said): “This land stands fearless due to true words (being spoken on it)”.

## \|\| 33.24 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*matsamaścāyuṣā bālo mārkaṃḍeyo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*kalpasyādau tathācāṃte mato me munisattamaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

24\. This boy, Mārkaṇḍeya, will have the (span of) life as I (shall have). (This) best sage is commended by me (to be present) at the beginning as well as at the end of a Kalpa.

## \|\| 33.25-26 \|\|

*evaṃ te munayo bālaṃ brahmaloke pitāmahāt \|*  
*saṃsādhya preṣayāmāsurbhūyopyenaṃ dharātalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*tīrthayātrāṃ gatā viprā mārkaṃḍeyo nijaṃ gṛham \|*  
*jagāma teṣu yāteṣu pitaraṃ svamathābravīt \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Thus the sages having got the boy made safe by the grandsire, sent him to the earth, and proceeded with their pilgrimage. Mārkaṇḍeya went home. When they had left, he said to his father:

## \|\| 33.27 \|\|

*brahmalokamahaṃ nīto munibhirbrahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuśca kṛtaścāsmi varāndatvā visarjitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. “Sages, teachers of the Vedas, had taken me to Brahmā’s world. Having made me a long-lived person (i.e. granting me a long life) and having given me boons, they sent me (home).

## \|\| 33.28-29 \|\|

*etadanyacca me dattaṃ gataṃ ciṃtākaraṃ tava \|*  
*kalpasyādau tathā cāṃte bhaviṣye samanaṃtare \|\| 28 \|\|*

*lokakarturbrahmaṇohaṃ prasādāttasya vai pitaḥ \|*  
*puṣkaraṃ vai gamiṣyāmi tapastaptuṃ samudyataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. (They gave me) this and other things. The cause of your anxiety has (now) gone. I shall be present continuously at the beginning and also at the end of a Kalpa, as a result of the favour of Brahmā, the creator of the worlds and the father (of all). Being eager I shall (now) go to Puṣkara to practise penance.

## \|\| 33.30-31 \|\|

*tatrāhaṃ devadeveśamupāsiṣye pitāmaham \|*  
*sarvakāmāvāptikaraṃ sarvārātinibarhaṇam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sarvasaukhyapradaṃ devamindrādīnāṃ parāyaṇam \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ toṣayiṣyāmi sarvalokapitāmaham \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. There I shall wait upon the grandsire, the lord of gods. I shall please Brahmā, who fulfils all desires, who destroys all enemies, who gives all pleasures, who is the highest object of Indra and others and who is the grandsire of all the worlds.”

## \|\| 33.32-34 \|\|

*mārkaṃḍeyavacaḥ śrutvā mṛkaṃḍurmunisattamaḥ \|*  
*jagāma paramaṃ harṣaṃ kṣaṇamekaṃ samucchvasan \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dhairyaṃ sumanasā sthāya idaṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*adya me saphalaṃ janma jīvitaṃ ca sujīvitam \|\| 33 \|\|*
