*saptadvīpāssamudrāśca sapta vai kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*anayā saṃkhyayā kṛtvā nipuṇaiḥ śilpibhistataḥ \|\| 395 \|\|*

*pādapādīni bhūtāni rājatānyeva kārayet \|*  
*āraṇyāni ca sattvāni sauvarṇāni ca kārayet \|\| 396 \|\|*

395-396. In accordance with this number he should get fashioned by skilled artisans seven islands, seven seas and seven principal mountains. He should get fashioned the trees and beings with silver; and he should get fashioned the forests and beasts with gold.

## \|\| 34.397 \|\|

*vṛkṣānvanaspatīngulmatṛṇaparṇāni vīrudhaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ prakalpya vidhivattīrthe deyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 397 \|\|*

397\. The wise ones should duly get fashioned trees, plants, thickets, grass, leaves and creepers and should present them at a holy place.

## \|\| 34.398-400 \|\|

*kurukṣ̣etre gayāyāṃ ca prayāge'marakaṃṭake*  
*dvāravatyāṃ prabhāse ca gaṃgādvāre ca puṣ̣kare \|\| 398 \|\|*

*tīrtheṣveteṣu vai deyaṃ grahaṇe śaśisūryayoḥ \|*  
*dinacchidreṣu sarveṣu ayane dakṣiṇottare \|\| 399 \|\|*

*vyatīpāte bahuguṇaṃ viṣuve ca viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*dātavyametadrājeṃdra vicāraṃ naiva kārayet \|\| 400 \|\|*

398-399a. At the time of the lunar or the solar eclipse he should present these things at these sacred places: Kurukṣetra, Gayā, Prayāga, Amarakaṇṭaka, Dvāravatī, Prabhāsa, Gaṅgādvāra and Puṣkara.

399b-400. O lord of kings, all this should be given on all the openings of days, during the summer and the winter solstice. It is very meritorious on days of portents and especially on equinoctial points. He should entertain no doubt about this.

## \|\| 34.401-404 \|\|

*śālāgnihotriṇaṃ kṛtvā surūpaṃ ca guṇānvitam \|*  
*sapatnīkaṃ ca saṃpūjya bhūṣayitvā ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 401 \|\|*

*purohitaṃ mukhyatamaṃ kṛtvā'nye ca tathā dvijāḥ \|*  
*caturviṃśadguṇopetāḥ sapatnīkā nimaṃtritāḥ \|\| 402 \|\|*

*aṃgulīyāni ca tathā karṇaveṣṭaṃ ca dāpayet \|*  
*evaṃvidhāṃstu tānpūjya teṣāmagre susaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 403 \|\|*

*aṣṭāṃgapraṇipātena praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*purohitāya purataḥ kṛtvā vai karasaṃpuṭam \|\| 404 \|\|*

401-403a. Appointing a brāhmaṇa who is handsome and endowed with five qualities as the chief of the fire-chamber, and having honoured him with his wife, and making him the chief priest, and in the same way, having invited other brāhmaṇas with twenty-four qualities, along with their wives, he should give them rings and ear-rings.

403b-404. Having honoured them thus and having placed himself before them, and having again and again saluted with the eight parts of his body touching the ground, he, with the palms of his hands joined in obeisance, (should praise the brāhmaṇas) with the family-priest in the fore (i.e. headed by the family-priest with these words:)

## \|\| 34.405-407 \|\|

*yūyaṃ vai brāhmaṇāḥ prītā maitratvenānugṛhṇata \|*  
*saumukhyena dvijaśreṣṭhā bhūyaḥ pūtatarastvahaḥ \|\| 405 \|\|*

*bhavatāṃ prītiyogena svayaṃ prītaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*brahmāṃḍena tu dattena toṣaṃ yātu janārdanaḥ \|\| 406 \|\|*

*pinākapāṇirbhagavānśakraśca tridaśeśvaraḥ \|*  
*ete toṣaṃ samāyāṃtu anudhyānāddvijottamāḥ \|\| 407 \|\|*

405-407. ‘O brāhmaṇas, being pleased you should favour (me) with a friendly attitude, and a kind disposition. I have again been more purified. Due to your devotion the grandsire himself is pleased. May Janārdana be pleased with (this) gift of Brahmāṇḍa. And also, O best brāhmaṇas, may the Pināka-holding god and Śakra, the lord of gods, be pleased by (my) meditation on them.’

## \|\| 34.408-409 \|\|

*evaṃ stutvā tato rājā brāhmaṇānvedapāragān \|*  
*brahmāṇḍaṃ tu guroḥ prādātsavidhānaṃ punaḥ kṣaṇāt \|\| 408 \|\|*

*sarvakāmaistatastṛpto yayau svargaṃ narādhipaḥ \|*  
*tenaiva guruṇā tacca vibhaktaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 409 \|\|*

408-409. Having thus praised the brāhmaṇas, who had mastered the Vedas, the king in a moment, duly presented the Brahmāṇḍa to his preceptor. Then with all his desires satisfied the king went to heaven.

## \|\| 34.410 \|\|

*dattaṃ tenāpi cānyebhyo brahmāṃḍaṃ ca narādhipa \|*  
*brahmāṃḍe bhūmidāne ca grāhī caiko na vai bhavet \|\| 410 \|\|*

410\. That priest shared that (Brahmāṇḍa) with (the other) brāhmaṇas (i.e.) he too gave (portions of) it to other brāhmaṇas, O king. There should not be only one recipient of Brahmāṇḍa or the gift of land.

## \|\| 34.411-412 \|\|

*gṛhṇandoṣamavāpnoti brahmahatyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ caiva pratyakṣaṃ dātavyaṃ parikīrtya vai \|\| 411 \|\|*

*dīyamānaṃ ca paśyaṃti tepi pūtā bhavaṃti hi \|*  
*darśanādeva te muktā bhavaṃntyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 412 \|\|*

411-412. If only one man receives it he commits a sin—brāhmaṇacide—there is no doubt about it. This is witnessed by all. One should proclaim and give. Those also who see (the gift) being given are purified. Merely by seeing it, they are liberated. There is no doubt about this.

## \|\| 34.413-414 \|\|

*yā bhīmadvādaśī proktā svarṇaṃ toyaṃ mṛgājinaṃ \|*  
*etāni kṛtvā paśyantu dṛṣṭairetaiḥ kriyāphalaṃ \|\| 413 \|\|*

*ayatnādeva labhyeta kartuścaiva salokatā \|*  
*sadā gāvaḥ praṇamyāśca maṃtreṇānena pārthiva \|\| 414 \|\|*

413-414. (On the day) which is called Bhīmadvādaśī, he should make (offerings of) gold, water and deer-hide. Let them (i.e. people) see these. When seen by them they easily get the fruit of the rite, and get (i.e. go to) the same world as the performer (of the rite). O king, cows should always be saluted with this sacred prayer:

## \|\| 34.415 \|\|

*namo gobhyaḥ śrīmatībhyaḥ saurabheyībhya eva ca \|*  
*namo brahmasutābhyaśca pavitrābhyo namonamaḥ \|\| 415 \|\|*

415\. ‘(My) repeated salutation to the prosperous cows that have descended from Surabhi. (My) repeated salutation to the pure daughters of Brahman.’

## \|\| 34.416-418 \|\|

*maṃtrasya cāsya smaraṇādgodānaphalamāpnuyāt \|*  
*tasmāttvamapi rājeṃdra puṣkare tīrtha uttame \|\| 416 \|\|*

*kārtikyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa godānaphalamāpsyasi \|*  
*yatkiṃcidvidyate pāpaṃ striyo vā puruṣasya vā \|\| 417 \|\|*

*puṣkare snānamātreṇa tadaśeṣaṃ praṇaśyati \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni āsamudrāttu bhārata \|\| 418 \|\|*

416-41 7a. One would obtain the fruit of the gift of cows (merely) by remembering this sacred prayer. Therefore, O king, you too will obtain the fruit of the gift of cows, especially on the full-moon day of Kārtika, at the excellent holy place, viz. Puṣkara.

417b-418. Whatever sin is of (i.e. committed by) a woman or a man, all that (sin) completely perishes by merely having a bath at Puṣkara. O descendant of Bharata, whichever sacred places there are on the earth right from the sea, they go to (i.e. merge into) Puṣkara, especially on the full-moon day of Kārtika.

## Chapter 35 - The Killing of a Śūdra Ascetic

## \|\| 35.1 \|\|

*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*uktaṃ bhagavatā sarvaṃ purāṇāśrayasaṃyutaṃ \|*  
*tathā śvetena brahmāṃḍaṃ gurave pratipāditaṃ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Bhīṣma said:

1\. The revered one has told (me) everything based on the Purāṇa; and also (has narrated to me) how (king) Śveta presented Brahmāṇḍa to his preceptor.

## \|\| 35.2 \|\|

*śrutvaitatkautukaṃ jātaṃ yathā tenāsthilehanaṃ \|*  
*kṛtaṃ kṣudhāpanodārthe annadānādvinā dvija \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Hearing this curiosity has arisen (in me) as to how, O brāhmaṇa, he licked (his own) bones in the absence of (i.e. as a result of his non-gifting of) food.

## \|\| 35.3 \|\|

*tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi pṛthivyāṃ ye ca pārthivāḥ \|*  
*annadānāddivaṃ prāptāḥ kratavaścānnamūlakāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I desire to hear that; I also desire to hear about other kings on the earth who reached heaven due to (i.e. as a result of) giving food; for sacrifices are based on food.

## \|\| 35.4 \|\|

*kathaṃ tasya matirnaṣṭā śvetasya ca mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*na dattaṃ tenānnadānamṛṣibhirvā na darśitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. How is it that the great-souled Śveta lost his good sense with the result that he neither gave food to the sages nor showed it to them.

## \|\| 35.5 \|\|

*aho māhātmyamannasya iha dattasya yatphalam \|*  
*paratra bhujyate puṃbhiḥ svargaścākṣayatāṃ vrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Ah, just see the greatness of food. The fruit of the food that is given here is enjoyed by men in heaven; and (due to it) one would have unending (residence in) heaven.

## \|\| 35.6 \|\|

*annadānaṃ paraṃ viprāḥ kīrtayaṃti sadotthitāḥ \|*  
*annadānātsuredreṇa trailokyamiha bhujyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The prominent brāhmaṇas have declared the gift of food as great. Due to the gift of food the lord of gods enjoys the three worlds.

## \|\| 35.7 \|\|

*śatakraturiti proktaḥ sarvaireva dvijottamaiḥ \|*  
*tenāvasthāṃ tatsadṛśīṃ prāptavāṃstridaśeśvaraḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. All best brāhmaṇas call him Śatakratu. Due to that (i.e. the gift of food) the lord of the gods has attained that position.

## \|\| 35.8-17 \|\|

*dānadevagataḥ svargaṃ tvattaḥ sarvaṃ śrutaṃ mayā \|*  
*aparaṃ ca purāvṛttaṃ nivṛttaṃ yadi karhicit \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhūyopi śrotumicchāmi tanme vada mahāmate \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*etadākhyānakaṃ pūrvamagastyena mahātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*rāmāya kathitaṃ rājaṃstatte vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam \|*  
*bhīṣma uvāca \|*  
*kasminvaṃśe samutpanno rāmo'sau nṛpasattamaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yasyāgastyena kathitaścetihāsaḥ purātanaḥ \|*  
*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*raghuvaṃśe samutpanno rāmo nāma mahābalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*devakāryaṃ kṛtaṃ tena laṃkāyāṃ rāvaṇo hataḥ \|*  
*pṛthivīṃ rājyasaṃsthasya ṛṣayo'bhyāgatā gṛhe \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prāptāste tu mahātmāno rāghavasya niveśanam \|*  
*pratīhārastato rāmamagastyavacanāddrutam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*āvedayāmāsa ṛṣīnprāptāstāṃśca tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ dvārapālaḥ pūrṇacaṃdramivoditam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kausalyāsuta bhadraṃ te suprabhātādya śarvarī \|*  
*draṣṭumabhyudayaṃ tedya samprāpto raghunaṃdana \|\| 15 \|\|*

*agastyo munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ dvāri tiṣṭhati te nṛpa \|*  
*śrutvā prāptānmunīnrāmastānbhāskarasamadyutīn \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prāha vākyaṃ tadā dvāsthaṃ praveśaya tvarānvitaḥ \|*  
*kimarthaṃ tu tvayā dvāri niruddhā munisattamāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

8-9a. He went to heaven because of having given food. All (this) I have heard from you. If something else has formerly taken place I desire to hear that too again; so, O highly intelligent one, now tell me about it.

Pulastya said:

9b-10a. O king, formerly this old episode was narrated to Rāma by the great-souled Agastya. I shall now tell it to you.

Bhīṣma said:

10b-11a. In which family was Rāama, the best king, to whom Agastya narrated the old episode, born?

Pulastya said:

11b-12a. The very mighty (hero) named Rāma was born in the family of Raghu. He did the mission of gods: he killed Rāvaṇa in Laṅkā.

12b-13a. (Once) sages came to the house of him who had settled (himself) as (the king) of the kingdom of the world. The great-souled (sages) arrived at Rāghava’s residence.

13b-14a. The doorkeeper, at the bidding of Agastya, immediately informed Rāma that the sages had come (to see him).

14b-16a. Seeing Rama, like the full moon that had risen (he said:) “O son of Kausalyā, well-being to you. The night (has ended and) an auspicious dawn has broken. O king, O descendant of Raghu, to see your prosperity Agastya has today come with sages. He is waiting at the door.”

16b-17. Hearing that the sages, resembling the sun in lustre, had arrived, Rāma said (these) words to the doorkeeper: “Quickly bring them in. Why have you detained the best sages at the door?”

## \|\| 35.18 \|\|

*rāmavākyānmunīṃstāṃstu prāveśayadyathāsukham \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā tu tānmunīṃnprāptānpratyuvāca kṛtāṃjali \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. At these words of Rāma the doorkeeper gladly ushered them in. Seeing the sages who had arrived, Rāma, with his hands joined in obeisance, spoke (words of greeting to them).

## \|\| 35.19-20 \|\|

*rāmo'bhivādya praṇata āsaneṣu nyaveśayat \|*  
*te tu kāṃcanacitreṣu svāstīrṇeṣu sukheṣu ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kuśottareṣu cāsīnāḥ samaṃtānmunipuṃgavāḥ \|*  
*pādyamācamanīyaṃ ca dadau cārghyaṃ purohitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Rama, having humbly saluted them made them sit on (i.e. offered them) seats. The best sages sat all around on golden, variegated, well-spread, comfortable seats, covered with Kuśa-grass. The family-priest offered them water for washing their feet, for rinsing their mouths and a respectful offering.

## \|\| 35.21 \|\|

*rāmeṇa kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭā ṛṣayaḥ sarva eva te \|*  
*maharṣayo vedavida idaṃ vacanamabruvan \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Rāma enquired after the health and welfare of all the sages. The great sages, well-versed in the Vedas said these words:

## \|\| 35.22 \|\|

*kuśalaṃ te mahābāho sarvatra raghunaṃdana \|*  
*tvāṃ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṃ paśyāmo hatavidviṣam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. “O you Raghu’s descendant of mighty arms, welfare to you everywhere. Luckily we are seeing you happy with your enemies killed.

## \|\| 35.23 \|\|

*hṛtā sītātipāpena rāvaṇena durātmanā \|*  
*patnī te raghuśārdūla tasyā evaujasā hataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. O best of Raghus, the extremely vicious Rāvaṇa, the villain, kidnapped Sītā, your wife. He was killed by her vigour only.

## \|\| 35.24 \|\|

*asahāyena caikena tvayā rāma raṇe hataḥ \|*  
*yādṛśaṃ te kṛtaṃ karma tasya kartā na vidyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. O Rāma, you all alone killed him in a battle. No other person is (seen) who would do the deed that you did

## \|\| 35.25 \|\|

*iha saṃbhāṣituṃ prāptā dṛṣṭvā pūtāḥ sma sāṃpratam \|*  
*darśanāttava rājeṃdra sarve jātāstapasvinaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. We had come here to talk to you; and now, on seeing you, we all the ascetics, are purified, O lord of kings.

## \|\| 35.26 \|\|

*rāvaṇasya vadhāttedya kṛtamaśrupramārjanam \|*  
*datvā puṇyāmimāṃ vīra jagatyabhayadakṣiṇām \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. You have today wiped the tears (of the world) by killing Rāvaṇa (i.e.) by giving this auspicious gift of fearlessness to the world, O hero.

## \|\| 35.27 \|\|

*diṣṭyā vardhasi kākutstha jayenāmitavikrama \|*  
*dṛṣṭassaṃbhāṣitaścāsi yāsyāmaścāśramānsvakān \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O Rāghava, we are glad due to this victory of yours, O you of unlimited valour. Now that we have seen and talked to you, we shall go to our respective hermitages.

## \|\| 35.28 \|\|

*araṇyaṃ te praviṣṭasya mayā ceṃdraśarāsanam \|*  
*arpitaṃ cākṣayau tūṇau kavacaṃ ca paraṃtapa \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. O you tormentor of the enemies, I had given Indra’s bow and two inexhaustible quivers and an armour to you when you had (formerly) entered the forest.

## \|\| 35.29 \|\|

*bhūyopyāgamanaṃ kāryamāśrame me raghūdvaha \|*  
*evamuktvā tu te sarve munayoṃtarhitā'bhavan \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O you descendant of Raghu, (please) visit my hermitage again.” Saying so all the sages disappeared.

## \|\| 35.30 \|\|

*gateṣu munimukhyeṣu rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayāmāsa tatkāryaṃ kiṃ syānme muninoditam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. When the chief sages had left, Rāma, the best among the supporters of righteousness, thought about the work (the sages wanted to assign to him. He said to himself:)

## \|\| 35.31 \|\|

*bhūyopyāgamanaṃ kāryamāśrame raghunaṃdana \|*  
*avaśyameva gaṃtavyaṃ mayā'gastyasya sannidhau \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. “What could be the mission (for which) the sage said to me: ‘O you descendant of Raghu, please come to my hermitage-again?’ I must certainly go to Agastya.

## \|\| 35.32-33 \|\|

*śrotavyaṃ devaguhyaṃ tu kāryamanyacca yadvadet \|*  
*evaṃ ciṃtayatastasya rāmasyāmitatejasaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*kariṣye niyataṃ dharmaṃ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ \|*  
*sutavarṣasahasrāṇi daśa rājyamakārayat \|\| 33 \|\|*

32a. I must hear (what the) secret (intention) of the gods is, and the mission that he would tell (me to do).”

32b-33. Rāma, of unlimited lustre, thought like this: “I shall surely perform my duty; for duty is the highest recourse.” He ruled for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 35.34 \|\|

*dadato juhvataścaiva jagmustānyekavarṣavat \|*  
*prajāḥ pālayatastasya rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. That great-souled Rāma, who gave gifts, performed sacrifices and protected his people, passed (this period just) like a year.

## \|\| 35.35 \|\|

*etasminneva divase vṛddho jānapado dvijaḥ \|*  
*mṛtaṃ putramupādāya rāmadvāramupāgataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. On this very day an old brāhmaṇa villager bringing with him his dead son, came to the door of (the residence of) Rāma.

## \|\| 35.36-37 \|\|

*uvāca vividhaṃ vākyaṃ snehākṣarasamanvitam \|*  
*duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃtu me putra pūrvadehāṃtare kṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tvāmekaputraṃ yadahaṃ paśyāmi nidhanaṃ gatam \|*  
*aprāptayauvanaṃ bālaṃ paṃcavarṣaṃ gatāyuṣam \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. He uttered many sentences with words full of affection: “O son, what wicked deed had I done in my previous existence, that I am seeing you, my only son, a child, who has not even attained youth and has just lived for five years, dead?

## \|\| 35.38 \|\|

*akāle kālamāpannaṃ duḥkhāya mama putraka \|*  
*akṛtvā pitṛkāryāṇi gato vaivasvatakṣayam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O son, you have died prematurely (only) to cause me grief. Without doing the obsequial rites you have gone to Yama’s residence.

## \|\| 35.39-40 \|\|

*rāmasya duṣkṛtaṃ vyaktaṃ yena te mṛtyurāgataḥ \|*  
*bālavadhyā brahmavadhyā strīvadhyā caiva rāghavam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pravekṣyati na sandehaḥ sabhārye tu mṛte mayi \|*  
*śuśrāva rāghavaḥ sarvaṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. (Indeed) Rama’s wicked deed is evident that death has come to you. When I die with my wife the sin of killing a child, a brāhmaṇa, and a woman will accrue to Rāma; there is no doubt about it.” Rāghava listened to all that accompanied by (i.e. causing) grief.

## \|\| 35.41 \|\|

*nivārya taṃ dvijaṃ rāmo vasiṣṭhaṃ vākyamabravīt \|*  
*kiṃ mayādya ca kartavyaṃ kāryamevaṃ vidhe sthite \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Rāma said (these) words to Vasiṣṭha who was sending the brāhmaṇa back: “When this is the state (of things) what should I do today?

## \|\| 35.42 \|\|

*prāṇānahaṃ juhomyagnau parvatādvā patehyaham \|*  
*kathaṃ śuddhimahaṃ yāmi śrutvā brāhmaṇabhāṣitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. I shall sacrifice my life or fall from a mountain. How shall I get purity (i.e. feel innocent) after I have heard the brāhmaṇa’s words?”

## \|\| 35.43 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhasyāgrataḥ sthitvā rājño dīnasya nāradaḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca śrutaṃ vākyamṛṣīṇāṃ sannidhau tadā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Nārada who was there in Vasiṣṭha’s proximity, told the dejected Rāma the words he had heard in the vicinity of (i.e. from) the sages:

## \|\| 35.44-45 \|\|

*śṛṇu rāma yathākālaṃ prāpto vai bālasaṃkṣayaḥ \|*  
*purā kṛtayuge rāma sarvatra brāhmaṇottaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

*abrāhmaṇo na vai kaścittapastapati rāghava \|*  
*amṛtyavastadā sarve jāyaṃte cirajīvinaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. “O Rāma, listen (how) at the right time the child’s death has taken place. O Rāma, formerly in Kṛtayuga, everywhere there was the superiority of brāhmaṇas. No non-brāhmaṇa, O Rāghava, even practised penance. All (men) then were immortal and long-lived.

## \|\| 35.46 \|\|

*tretāyuge punaḥ prāpte brahmakṣatramanuttamam \|*  
*adharmo dvāpare teṣāṃ vaiśyānśūdrāṃstathāviśat \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Again in Tretāyuga brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas became superior. In Dvāparayuga their sin entered vaiśyas and śūdras.

## \|\| 35.47 \|\|

*evaṃ niraṃtaraṃ juṣṭamudbhūtamanṛtaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*adharmasya trayaḥ pādā eko dharmasya cāgataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Thus falsehood that was continuously resorted to, again came up (i.e. became effective). Three feet (i.e. three quarters) of unrighteousness and (only) one foot (i.e. quarter) of righteousness appeared there.

## \|\| 35.48 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrve bhṛśaṃ trastā varṇā brāhmaṇapūrvakāḥ \|*  
*bhūyaḥ pādastu dharmasya dvitīyaḥ samapadyata \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Then there were many casteless persons led by brāhmaṇas. Then again the second foot (i.e. quarter) of righteousness came (up).

## \|\| 35.49 \|\|

*tasmindvāparasaṃjñe tu tapo vaiśyaṃ samāviśat \|*  
*yugatrayasya vaidharmyaṃ dharmasya pratitiṣṭhati \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In that (yuga) called Dvāpara, penance entered (i.e. went to) vaiśyas. The unrighteousness of the three yugas stood \[...?\]

## \|\| 35.50 \|\|

*kalisaṃjñe tataḥ prāpte vartamāne yugeṃtime \|*  
*adharmaścānṛtaṃ caiva vavṛdhāte nararṣabha \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. O best man, then when the last yuga called Kali came, (both) unrighteousness and falsehood increased.

## \|\| 35.51-53 \|\|

*bhavitā śūdrayonyāṃ tu tapaścaryā kalau yuge \|*  
*sa te viṣayaparyaṃte rājannugrataraṃ tapaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śūdrastapati durbuddhistena bālavadhaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*yasyādharmamakāryaṃ vā viṣaye pārthivasya hi \|\| 52 \|\|*

*pure vā rājaśārdūla kurute durmatirnaraḥ \|*  
*kṣipraṃ sa narakaṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-52a. In (this) Kaliyuga practice of penance will be (found) in the persons born as śūdras. O king, a śūdra, the tormentor of his enemies, and of a wicked mind, is practising a very severe penance at the border of your country. He killed the child.

52b-53. O best of kings, a king, in whose kingdom or (capital-)city, a wicked person does an unrighteous thing unfit to be done, instantly goes to hell (and stays there) till deluge.

## \|\| 35.54-65 \|\|

*caturthaṃ tasya pāpasya bhāgamaśnāti pārthivaḥ \|*  
*sattvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla gacchasva viṣayaṃ svakam \|\| 54 \|\|*

*duṣkṛtaṃ yatra paśyethāstatra yatnaṃ samācara \|*  
*evaṃ te dharmavṛddhiśca balasya vardhanaṃ tathā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*pure vā rājaśārdūla kurute durmatirnaraḥ \|*  
*kṣipraṃ sa narakaṃ yāti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyati naraśreṣṭha bālasyāsya ca jīvanam \|*  
*nāradenaivamuktastu sāścaryo raghunaṃdanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe lakṣmaṇaṃ cedamabravīt \|*  
*gaccha saumya dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ samāśvāsaya lakṣmaṇa \|\| 57 \|\|*

*bālasya ca śarīraṃ tvaṃ tailadroṇyāṃ nidhāpaya \|*  
*gaṃdhaiśca paramodāraistailaiścaiva sugaṃdhibhiḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*yathā na śīryate bālastathā saumya vidhīyatām \|*  
*yathā śarīraṃ guptaṃ syādbālasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*vipattiḥ paribhedo vā na bhavettattathā kuru \|*  
*tathā saṃdiśya saumitraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*manasā puṣpakaṃ dadhyāvāgaccheti mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*iṃgitaṃ tattu vijñāya kāmagaṃ hemabhūṣitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*ājagāma muhūrtāttu samīpaṃ rāghavasya hi \|*  
*sobravītprāñjalirvākyamahamasmi narādhipa \|\| 62 \|\|*

*agre tava mahābāho kiṃkaraḥ samupasthitaḥ \|*  
*bhāṣitaṃ suciraṃ śrutvā puṣpakasya narādhipa \|\| 63 \|\|*

*abhivādya maharṣīṃstānvimānaṃ sodhyarohata \|*  
*dhanurgṛhītvā tūṇau ca khaḍgaṃ cāpi mahāprabham \|\| 64 \|\|*

*nikṣipya nagare vīrau saumitri bharatāvubhau \|*  
*prāyātpratīcīṃ tvarito vicinvansusamāhitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

54-55a. The king takes the fourth portion of his sin. So, O best among men, you go to that (part of) your country where you will see a wicked deed (being committed). Make an effort (to stop it).

53b-56a. O best of men, by (doing) this your religious merit and might will increase, and also (the span of) this child’s life.”

56b-57a. Thus addressed by Nārada, the descendant of Raghu, who was astonished, obtained incomparable joy, and said these (words) to Lakṣmaṇa:

57b-59a. “O dear Lakṣmaṇa, go to the best brāhmaṇa and console him. Get the boy’s body placed in a trough containing oil. O dear one, using abundant perfumes and fragrant oils do that by which (the body of) the boy does not decay.

59b-60a. Do that by which the body of the boy, who has not done any deed of distress, would be preserved, and by which there would be no mishap or decomposition.”

60b-6la. Having thus ordered Sumitrā’s son Lakṣmaṇa of good marks he, of great fame, mentally thought of the Puṣpaka aeroplane and ordered it, “Come (here)”.

61b-63a. Knowing the internal thought (of Rāma) that aeroplane, decorated with gold and moving according to (the occupant’s) desire came near Rāma in a short time. He (i.e. the presidi ng deity of the aeroplane) joined the palms of his hands as a mark of humility and said: “O king, (here) I am. This servant, O you of mighty arms, stands before you.”

63b-64a. Having heard, for a long time, the words (of the presiding deity) of the plane, the king saluted those great sages, and got into it.

64b-65. He, the well-composed one, leaving the two heroes Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata in the city, and taking his bow and two quivers as well as his very powerful sword, looking for (the culprit) quickly went towards the west.

## \|\| 35.66-67 \|\|

*uttarāmagamatpaścāddiśaṃ himavadāśritām \|*  
*pūrvāmapi diśāṃ gatvā tathā'paśyannarādhipaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*sarvāṃ śuddhasamācārāmādarśamiva nirmalām \|*  
*tato diśaṃ samākrāmaddakṣiṇāṃ raghunaṃdanaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Then he went to the north which was resorted to by the Himālaya (mountain). Then the king went in all parts of the eastern direction (where people followed) good practices and which was spotless like a mirror. Then the descendant of Raghu traversed the south.

## \|\| 35.68-71 \|\|

*śailasya uttare pārśve dadarśa sumahatsaraḥ \|*  
*tasminsarasi tapyaṃtaṃ tāpasaṃ sumahattapaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*dadarśa rāghavo bhīmaṃ laṃbamānamadhomukhaṃ \|*  
*tamupāgamya kākutsthastapyamānaṃ tu tāpasam \|\| 69 \|\|*

*uvāca rāghavo vākyaṃ dhanyastvamamaraprabha \|*  
*kasyāṃ yonau tapovṛddhirvartate dṛḍhaniścaya \|\| 70 \|\|*

*ahaṃ dāśarathī rāmaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ kutūhalāt \|*  
*kortho vyavasitastubhyaṃ svargalokotha vetaraḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

68-69a. On the northern side of a mountain he saw a very big lake. In it Rāghava saw a terrible sage hanging upside down, practising very great (i.e. severe) penance.

69b-70a. Rāghava, the descendant of Kakutstha, approached the ascetic practising penance, and said (these) words:“O you having lustre like a god, you are lucky.

70b-71. O you of a firm resolve, in which caste does this penance prosper (i.e. to which caste do you, performing this severe penance, belong)? I am Rama, Daśaratha’s son, (who am) asking you through curiosity. Which object do you have in mind: heaven or some other world?

## \|\| 35.72-74 \|\|

*kimarthaṃ tapyase vā tvaṃ śrotumicchāmi tāpasa \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vāsi bhadraṃ te kṣatriyo vātha durjayaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*vaiśyastṛtīyavarṇo vā śūdro vā satyamucyatām \|*  
*tapaḥ satyātmakaṃ nityaṃ svargalokaparigrahe \|\| 73 \|\|*

*sātvikaṃ rājasaṃ caiva tacca satyātmakaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*jagadupakāraheturhi sṛṣṭaṃ tadvai viriṃcinā \|\| 74 \|\|*

72-73a. O ascetic, I desire to hear (i.e. to know) why you are practising penance. Are you a brāhmaṇa? Well-being to you. Or are you an invincible kṣatriya? Or are you a vaiśya i.e. belonging to the third caste? Or are you a śūdra? Tell (me) the truth.

73b-74. Penance is full of truth (and) is always (useful) in obtaining heaven. Penance is Sāttvika and Rājasa and it (i.e. Sāttvika) is of the nature of truth. It is the cause of (i.e. leads to) helping the world, and is created by Viriñci.

## \|\| 35.75 \|\|

*raudraṃ kṣatriyatejojaṃ tattu rājasamucyate \|*  
*parasyotsādanārthāya taccāsuramudāhṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. The Raudra (i.e. terrible) penance springs from kṣatriya’s lustre, and is called Rājasa. That which is (used) for the destruction of others is called Āsura.

## \|\| 35.76 \|\|

*aṃgāni nihnute yo vā asṛgdigdhāni bhāgaśaḥ \|*  
*paṃcāgniṃsādhayedvāpi siddhiṃ vā mṛtyumeva vā \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. He who conceals one by one the parts of his body smeared with blood, or he who practises penance to conquer the five fires or (tries to) accomplish perfection or conquer death (belongs to the Āsura category).

## \|\| 35.77 \|\|

*āsuro hyeṣa te bhāvo na ca me tvaṃ dvijo mataḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ te vadataḥ siddhiranṛte nāsti jīvitam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. This your disposition is Āsura; and I do not think you are a brāhmaṇa. If you speak the truth you will accomplish perfection; if yon tell a lie you will not live.”

## \|\| 35.78 \|\|

*tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*avākśirāstathā bhūto vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. Having heard those words of Rāma, who ha\[?\] never done any harmful deed, the ascetic remained hung upside down like that (i.e. before) and said:

## \|\| 35.79 \|\|

*svāgataṃ te nṛpaśreṣṭha cirāddṛṣṭosi rāghava \|*  
*putrabhūtosmi te cāhaṃ pitṛbhūtosi menagha \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. “O best king, welcome to you. O Rāghava, you are seen after a long time. O innocent one, I am your son, and you are my father.

## \|\| 35.80-82 \|\|

*athavā naitadevaṃ hi sarveṣāṃ nṛpatiḥ pitā \|*  
*satvamarcyo'si bho rājanvayaṃ te viṣaye tapaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*carāmastatrabhāgosti pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭaḥ svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*na dhanyāḥ smo vayaṃ rāma dhanyastvamasi pārthiva \|\| 81 \|\|*

*yasya te viṣaye hyevaṃ siddhimicchaṃti tāpasāḥ \|*  
*tapasā tvaṃ madīyena siddhimāpnuhi rāghava \|\| 82 \|\|*

80-82. Or this is not so; for the king is the father of all (his subjects). O king, such as you are, you deserve to be honoured. We are practising penance in your country. In it (you have) a share which is formerly produced (i.e. fixed) by the self-born. O Rāma, we are not lucky. You are lucky, O king, in whose country the ascetics desire perfection like this. O Rāghava, obtain prosperity with (i.e. as the the fruit of) my penance.

## \|\| 35.83-84 \|\|

*yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ yonau kasyāṃ tu te tapaḥ \|*  
*śūdrayoniprasūtohaṃ tapa ugraṃ samāsthitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*devatvaṃ prārthaye rāma svaśarīreṇa suvrata \|*  
*na mithyāhaṃ vade bhūpa devalokajigīṣayā \|\| 84 \|\|*

83-84. As to what you said (as to the question that you asked, viz.) ‘in which caste (are you born and) are practising your penance’ (I would say:) I am born in a śūdra family; and have resorted to a severe penance. O Rāma, of a good vow, I desire to have godhood with my body (i.e. I want to be a god, without casting off this body). O king, I am not telling a lie with a desire to conquer (i.e. go to) the world of gods.

## \|\| 35.85-88 \|\|

*śūdraṃ māṃ viddhi kākutstha śaṃbūkaṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*bhāṣatastasya kākutsthaḥ khaḍgaṃ tu ruciraprabhaṃ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*niṣkṛṣya kośādvimalaṃ śiraściccheda rāghavaḥ \|*  
*tasminśūdre hate devāḥ sendrāścāgnipurogamāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*sādhusādhviti kākutsthaṃ praśaśaṃsurmuhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*puṣpavṛṣṭiśca mahatī devānāṃ susugaṃdhinī \|\| 87 \|\|*

*ākāśādvipramuktā tu rāghavaṃ sarvatokirat \|*  
*suprītāścābruvandevā rāmaṃ vākyavidāṃvaram \|\| 88 \|\|*

85-86a. O descendant of Kakutstha, know me to be a śūdra, Śambūka, by name.” When he was thus talking, Rāma, the descendant of Kakutstha, took out from the sheath, a spotless sword, and cut off his head.

86b-88a. When the Śūdra was killed, gods with Indra, led by Agni, repeatedly praised Rāma (saying), ‘Well (done, well done)’; and a very fragrant shower of flowers discharged by the gods from the sky, scattered all around Rāghava.

88b. The gods, very much pleased, said these words to Rama, the best among those who knew (the meaning of) sentence.

## \|\| 35.89-92 \|\|

*surakāryamidaṃ saumya kṛtaṃ te raghunaṃdana \|*  
*gṛhāṇa ca varaṃ rāma yamicchasi mahāvrata \|\| 89 \|\|*

*tvatkṛtena hi śūdro'yaṃ saśarīro'bhyagāddivaṃ \|*  
*devānāṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā rāghavaḥ susamāhitaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

*uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ puraṃdaram \|*  
*yadi devāḥ prasannā me varārho yadi vāpyaham \|\| 91 \|\|*

*karmaṇā yadi me prītā dvijaputraḥ sa jīvatu \|*  
*varametaddhi bhavatāṃ kāṃkṣitaṃ paramaṃ hi me \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-90a. “O you descendant of Raghu, O you good one, you have done this mission of the gods. O Rāma of a great vow, take (i.e. choose) whichever boon you like. By your deed this śūdra has physically gone to heaven.”

90b-9la. Hearing (these) words of the gods, Rāghava who was well-composed, and who had joined his palms in obeisance, said these words to Indra, the thousand-eyed (god):

91b-92. “If gods are pleased with me, if I deserve a (grant of) boon, if they are happy with my deed, then let this brāhmaṇa-boy come to life (again). This is the best boon desired by me from you.

## \|\| 35.93-94 \|\|

*mamāparādhādbālo'sau brāhmaṇasyaikaputrakaḥ \|*  
*aprāptakālaḥ kālena nīto vaivasvata kṣayam \|\| 93 \|\|*

*taṃ jīvayata bhadraṃ vo nānṛtī syāmahaṃ guroḥ \|*  
*dvijasya saṃśruto hyartho jīvayiṣyāmi te sutam \|\| 94 \|\|*

93-94. Due to my fault this boy, the son of a brāhmaṇa, has met with an untimely death. He has been taken by Death to Yama’s abode. Revive him, well-being to you, I should not prove to be a liar to my preceptor. I have given a promise to the brāhmaṇa: I shall bring back your son to life.

## \|\| 35.95 \|\|

*madīyenāyuṣā bālaṃ pādenārddhena vā surāḥ \|*  
*jīvedayaṃ varo mahyaṃ varakoṭyadhiko vṛtaḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. O gods, let this boy live by having the full span of my life, or half a portion or a quarter portion of (the span of) my life”.

## \|\| 35.96 \|\|

*rāghavasya tu tadvākyaṃ śrutvā vibudhasattamāḥ \|*  
*pratyūcuste mahātmānaṃ prītāḥ prītisamanvitāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Hearing those words of Rāghava, the best gods who were pleased and were full of affection, said to the great-souled one:

## \|\| 35.97-98 \|\|

*nirvṛto bhava kākutstha brāhmaṇasyaikaputrakaḥ \|*  
*jīvitaṃ prāptavānbhūyaḥ sametaścāpi baṃdhubhiḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*yasminmuhūrte kākutstha śūdroyaṃ vinipātitaḥ \|*  
*tasminmuhūrte sahasā jīvena samayujyata \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. “O descendant of Kakutstha, give up your anxiety; the only son of the brāhmaṇa has regained his life and is united with his relatives. O descendant of Kakutstha, the boy suddenly became united with (i.e. regained his) life, (just) at the moment when this śūdra was destroyed by you.

## \|\| 35.99-100 \|\|

*svasti prāpnuhi bhadraṃ te sādhayāmaḥ paraṃtapaḥ \|*  
*agastyasyāśramapade draṣṭāraḥ sma mahāmunim \|\| 99 \|\|*

*sa tatheti pratijñāya devānāṃ raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*āruroha vimānaṃ taṃ puṣpakaṃ hemabhūṣitam \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. Obtain welfare; well-being to you; O you tormentor of your enemies, we (now) go (back). We shall see the great sage (viz. Agastya) in Agastya’s hermitage”. Having promised the gods with the words ‘All right’, the descendant of Raghu got into the Puṣpaka aeroplane decorated with gold.

## Chapter 36 - Conversation between Rāma and Agastya

## \|\| 36.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tato devāḥ prayātāste vimānairbahubhistadā \|*  
*rāmopyanujagāmāśu kuṃbhayonestapovanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. Then the gods went by many aeroplanes. Rāma too quickly went to the penance-grove of Agastya.

## \|\| 36.2 \|\|

*uktaṃ bhagavatā tena bhūyopyāgamanaṃ kriyāḥ \|*  
*pūrvameva sabhāyāṃ ca yo māṃ draṣṭuṃ samāgataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. (He thought:) ‘The revered one, who had formerly come to see me in my assembly, had told me to go to him again.

## \|\| 36.3 \|\|

*tadahaṃ devatādeśāttatkāryārthe mahāmuniṃ \|*  
*paśyāmi taṃ muniṃ gatvā devadānavapūjitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. So by the order of gods and for their work I shall go and see that great sage, honoured by gods and demons.

## \|\| 36.4 \|\|

*upadeśaṃ ca me tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ dāsyati sattamaḥ \|*  
*duḥkhī yena punarmartye na bhavāmi kadācana \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. And the best one will advise me so that I shall never again be unhappy in this mortal world.

## \|\| 36.5 \|\|

*pitā daśaratho mahyaṃ kausalyā jananī tathā \|*  
*sūryavaṃśe samutpannastathāpyevaṃ suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. My father is Daśaratha and Kausalyā is my mother. I am born in the solar family. Still I am so much unhappy!

## \|\| 36.6 \|\|

*rājyakāle vane vāso bhāryayā cānujena ca \|*  
*haraṇaṃ cāpi bhāryāyā rāvaṇena kṛtaṃ mama \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I had to stay in the forest with my wife and younger brother at the time (when I should have enjoyed) the kingdom. My wife also was abducted by Rāvaṇa.

## \|\| 36.7-9 \|\|

*asahāyena tu mayā tīrtvā sāgaramuttamam \|*  
*ruddhvā tu tāṃ purīṃ sarvāṃ kṛtvā tasya kulakṣayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭā sītā mayā tyaktā devānāṃ tu purastadā \|*  
*śuddhāṃ tāṃ māṃ tathocuste mayā sītā tathā gṛham \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samānītā prītimatā lokavākyādvisarjitā \|*  
*vane vasati sā devī pure cāhaṃ vasāmi vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-8a. I met Sītā after having crossed the excellent ocean without anybody’s help and having besieged that city (of Lanka) and having destroyed his (i.e. Rāvaṇa’s) family. I abandoned her in front of the gods.

8b-9. They (then) told me that she was pure, so I, full of love, brought her home; but (again) forsook her on account of (an adverse) public opinion. That respectable lady is living in a forest, (while) I am living in the city.

## \|\| 36.10 \|\|

*jātohamuttame vaṃśe uttamohaṃ dhanuṣmatām \|*  
*uttamaṃ duḥkhamāpanno hṛdayaṃ naiva bhidyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. I am born in the best family; I am best among the archers; I am suffering from the worst misery; (yet) my heart is not rent.

## \|\| 36.11 \|\|

*vajrasārasya sāreṇa dhātrāhaṃ nirmito dhruvam \|*  
*idānīṃ brāhmaṇādeśādbhramāmi dharaṇītale \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Surely the creator has created me with an adamantine essence. Now following the instruction of a brāhmaṇa, I wander over the surface of the earth.

## \|\| 36.12 \|\|

*tapaḥ sthitastu śūdrosau mayā pāpo nipātitaḥ \|*  
*devavākyāttu me bhūyaḥ prāṇo me hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Obeying the words of gods, I have destroyed this sinful śūdra who was practising penance. Again my life has stood still in my heart (i.e. I am very uneasy).

## \|\| 36.13 \|\|

*paśyāmi taṃ muniṃ vaṃdyaṃ jagatosya hite ratam \|*  
*dṛṣṭena me tathā duḥkhaṃ nāśameṣyati satvaram \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. I (shall now) see the adorable sage, engaged in the wellbeing of this world, so that by seeing him my grief will soon come to an end.

## \|\| 36.14 \|\|

*udayena sahasrāṃśorhimaṃ yadvadvilīyate \|*  
*tadvanme duḥkhasaṃprāptiḥ sarvathā nāśameṣyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As at the rise of the sun snow melts, in the same way (by seeing him) all the grief that has come to me will completely come to an end.’

## \|\| 36.15 \|\|

*dṛṣṭvā ca devānsaṃprāptānagastyo bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|*  
*arghyamādāya suprītaḥ sarvāṃstānabhyapūjayat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The revered sage Agastya too, seeing the gods who had come there, and being very well pleased offered them a respectful offering and worshipped them.

## \|\| 36.16 \|\|

*te tu gṛhya tataḥ pūjāṃ saṃbhāṣya ca mahāmuniṃ \|*  
*jagmustena tadā hṛṣṭā nākapṛṣṭhaṃ sahānugāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. They too, having talked to the great sage, and being delighted went to heaven with their followers.

## \|\| 36.17 \|\|

*gateṣu teṣu kākutsthaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya ca \|*  
*abhivādayituṃ prāptaḥ sogastyamṛṣimuttamam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When they had left, the descendant of Kakutstha (i.e. Rāma) got down from Puṣpaka and went to salute the best sage Agastya.

## \|\| 36.18 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*suto daśarathasyāhaṃ bhavaṃtamabhivāditum \|*  
*āgato vai muniśreṣṭha saumyenekṣasva cakṣuṣā \|\| 18 \|\|*

The king (i.e. Rāma) said:

18\. O best sage, I am Daśaratha’s son. I have come to salute you. (Please) look at me with a pleasing eye (i.e. favour me).

## \|\| 36.19 \|\|

*nirdhūtapāpastvāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavāmīha na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*etāvaduktvā sa munimabhivādya punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. By seeing you my sins will be shaken off. There is no doubt (about it).

## \|\| 36.20 \|\|

*kuśalaṃ bhṛtyavargasya mṛgāṇāṃ tanayasya ca \|*  
*bhagavaddarśanākāṃkṣī śūdraṃ hatvā tvihāgataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Saying this much and saluting the sage again and again, he (enquired after) the welfare of the servants, the beasts and his son (and said:) “After having killed the śūdra (viz. Śambūka) I have come here to see (you) the revered one.”

## \|\| 36.21-22 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*svāgataṃ te raghuśreṣṭha jagadvaṃdya sanātana \|*  
*darśanāttava kākutstha pūtohaṃ munibhiḥ saha \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvatkṛte raghuśārdūla gṛhāṇārghaṃ mahādyute \|*  
*svāgataṃ naraśārdūla diṣṭyā prāptosi śatruhan \|\| 22 \|\|*

Agastya said:

21-22. O you best among the Raghus, O you highly lust rous one, (please) accept the respectful offering meant for you. O best among the Raghus, O you who are adorable to the world, O you eternal one, welcome to you. O descendant of Kakutstha, your visit has purified me along with the sages. O you killer of enemies, due to my good luck, you have come here.

## \|\| 36.23 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi nityaṃ bahumato guṇairbahubhiruttamaiḥ \|*  
*atastvaṃ pūjanīyo vai mama nityaṃ hṛdisthitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. You are always very much respected due to your many excellent qualities. Therefore you deserve to be honoured. You have always remained in my heart.

## \|\| 36.24 \|\|

*surā hi kathayaṃti tvāṃ śūdraghātinamāgataṃ \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya ca dharmeṇa tvayā vai jīvitaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The gods also proclaim that you, the killer of the śūdra, have come. You have righteously brought the brāhmaṇa’s son back to life.

## \|\| 36.25 \|\|

*uṣyatāṃ ceha bhagavaḥ sakāśe mama rāghava \|*  
*prabhāte puṣpakeṇāsi gaṃtāyodhyāṃ mahāmate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. O Rāghava, (please) live with me. O you highly intelligent one, you will go to Ayodhyā in the Puṣpaka (next) morning.

## \|\| 36.26 \|\|

*idaṃ cābharaṇaṃ saumya sukṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|*  
*divyaṃ divyenavapuṣā dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Rāghava, O gentle one, O king of kings, (please) accept this divine ornament well fashioned by Viśvakarman of a divine body and shining with its own lustre.

## \|\| 36.27 \|\|

*pratigṛhṇīṣva rājendra matpriyaṃ kuru rāghava \|*  
*labdhasya hi punarddāne sumahatphalamucyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Do what is agreeable to me. It is said that great fruit accrues (to a person) when what is obtained is again given (by him).

## \|\| 36.28 \|\|

*tvaṃ hi śaktaḥ paritrātuṃ seṃdrānapi surottamān \|*  
*tasmātpradāsye vidhivatpratīcchasva nararṣabha \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. You are capable of protecting the best gods including Indra. Therefore I shall duly offer (this to you). O best of men, (please) accept it.

## \|\| 36.29 \|\|

*athovāca mahābāhurikṣvākūṇāṃ mahārathaḥ \|*  
*kṛtāṃjalirmuniśreṣṭhaṃ svaṃ ca dharmamanusmaran \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Then the great warrior of mighty arms (i.e. very powerful) among the Ikṣvākus, remembering his duty, with the palms of his hands joined in obeisance, said:

## \|\| 36.30 \|\|

*pratigraho vai bhagavaṃstava me'tra vigarhitaḥ \|*  
*kṣatriyeṇa kathaṃ vipra pratigrāhyaṃ vijānatā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “O revered sir, accepting a gift from you is censurable on my part. O brāhmaṇa, how can a wise kṣatriya accept a gift given by a brāhmaṇa? Please tell (i.e. explain) it to me.

## \|\| 36.31 \|\|

*brāhmaṇena tu yaddattaṃ tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|*  
*saputro gṛhavānasmi samarthosmi mahāmune \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. I have sons, I am a householder and I am capable (of securing such gifts), O great sage.

## \|\| 36.32 \|\|

*āpadā cana cākrāṃtaḥ kathaṃ grāhyaḥ pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*bhāryā me suciraṃ naṣṭā na cānyā mama vidyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. I am not overcome with a calamity. (Then) how can I accept this gift? My wife has deceased long back: and I have not (taken to) another wife.

## \|\| 36.33-35 \|\|

*kevalaṃ doṣabhāgī ca bhavāmīha na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kaṣṭāṃ caiva daśāṃ prāpya kṣatriyopi pratigrahī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*kurvanna doṣamāpnoti manurevātra kāraṇam \|*  
*vṛddhau ca mātāpitarau sādhvī bhāryā śiśuḥ sutaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*apyakāryaśataṃ kṛtvā bhartavyā manurabravīt \|*  
*nāhaṃ pratīcche viprarṣe tvayā dattaṃ pratigrahaṃ \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-34a. Here (i.e. if I accept the gift), I shall merely commit an offence. There is no doubt about it. If a kṣatriya accepts a gift when he is reduced to a miserable condition, he does not incur sin. Manu is the authority in this matter.

34b-35. Manu has said that old parents, a virtuous wife, a young son should be taken care of (by a man) even by doing a hundred evil deeds. (So) O brāhmaṇa sage, I shall not accept the gift offered by you.

## \|\| 36.36 \|\|

*na ca me bhavatā kopaḥ kāryo vai surapūjita \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. O you honoured by gods, (please) do not be angry with me.”

## \|\| 36.37 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*na ca pratigrahe doṣo gṛhīte pārthivairnṛpa \|*  
*bhavānvai tāraṇe śaktastrailokyasyāpi rāghava \|\| 37 \|\|*

Agastya said:

37\. O king, there is nothing wrong if kings accept a gift offered to them. O Rāghava, you are able to protect even the three worlds.

## \|\| 36.38 \|\|

*tāraya brāhmaṇaṃ rāma viśeṣeṇa tapasvinaṃ \|*  
*tasmātpradāsye vidhivatpratīcchasva narāghipa \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. O Rāma, then protect this brāhmaṇa especially when he is also an ascetic. Therefore I shall duly give (the gift). (Please) accept it, O king.

## \|\| 36.39 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*kṣatriyeṇa kathaṃ vipra pratigrāhyaṃ vijānatā \|*  
*brāhmaṇena tu yaddattaṃ tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi \|\| 39 \|\|*

Rāma said:

39\. O brāhmaṇa, please tell me how should a wise kṣat-riya accept what is offered by a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 36.40 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*āsītkṛtayuge rāma brahmapūte purātane \|*  
*apārthivāḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ surāṇāṃ ca śatakratuḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

Agastya said:

40\. O Rāma, in the old Kṛtayuga, that had become one with Brahman, all the beings were without a king: (only) Indra was (the king) of gods.

## \|\| 36.41-42 \|\|

*tāḥ prajā devadeveśaṃ rājārthaṃ samupāgaman \|*  
*surāṇāṃ vidyate rājā devadevaḥ śatakratuḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*śreyasesmāsu lokeśa pārthivaṃ kuru sāṃprataṃ \|*  
*yasminpūjāṃ prayuṃjānāḥ puruṣā bhuṃjate mahīm \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Those beings went to the great lord of gods for (securing) a king. (They said to him:) “Gods have a king viz. Śatakratu (i.e. Indra), the gods of gods. O lord of the worlds, for our well-being make (someone) our king, offering worship to whom men enjoy the earth.”

## \|\| 36.43 \|\|

*tato brahmā suraśreṣṭho lokapālānsavāsavān \|*  
*samāhūyābravītsarvāṃstejobhāgo'tra yujyatām \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then Brahmā, the greatest among gods, called the regents of the quarters with Indra, and said to all of them: “Bestow here a part of your lustre.”

## \|\| 36.44 \|\|

*tato dadurlokapālāścaturbhāgaṃ svatejasā \|*  
*akṣayaśca tato brahmā yato jāto'kṣayo nṛpaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Then the regents of the quarters (each) gave a quarter of their lustre. Due to that Brahmā became inexhaustible (in lustre), and from (i.e. due to) him the king also became inexhaustible (in lustre).

## \|\| 36.45 \|\|

*taṃ brahmā lokapālānāmaṃśaṃ puṃsāmayojayat \|*  
*tato nṛpastadā tāsāṃ prajānāṃ kṣemapaṃḍitaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Then Brahmā bestowed the portion(s) of the lustre of the regents of the quarters upon men. Due to that a king is skilled in (looking after) the welfare of these beings.

## \|\| 36.46 \|\|

*tatraiṃdreṇa tu bhāgena sarvānājñāpayennṛpaḥ \|*  
*vāruṇena ca bhāgena sarvānpuṣṇāti dehinaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Due to the portion (received) from Indra, the king should order all; and on account of Varuṇa’s portion (that he has in him) he nourishes all men.

## \|\| 36.47 \|\|

*kaubereṇa tathāṃśena tvarthāndiśati pārthivaḥ \|*  
*yaśca yāmyo nṛpe bhāgastena śāsti ca vai prajāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The king directs (i.e. gives) wealth by means of the portion of Kubera (that he has in him); and the king governs his subjects with the portion of Yama that (he has) in him.

## \|\| 36.48 \|\|

*tatra caiṃdreṇa bhāgena narendrosi raghūttama \|*  
*pratigṛhṇīṣvābharaṇaṃ tāraṇārthe mama prabho \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. O best of Raghus, when such is the case, you are the lord of men due to Indra’s portion (that you have in you) O lord, (please) accept the ornament to protect me.

## \|\| 36.49 \|\|

*tato rāmaḥ prajagrāha munerhastānmahātmanaḥ \|*  
*divyamābharaṇaṃ citraṃ pradīptamiva bhāskaraṃ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then Rāma accepted from the hand of the great-souled sage, the divine, bright ornament blazing like the sun.

## \|\| 36.50-54 \|\|

*pratigṛhya tatogastyādrāghavaḥ paravīrahā \|*  
*nirīkṣya suciraṃ kālaṃ vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mauktikāni vicitrāṇi dhātrīphalasamāni ca \|*  
*jāṃbūnadanibaddhāni vajravidrumanīlakaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*padmarāgaiḥ sagomedhairvaiḍūryaiḥ puṣparāgakaiḥ \|*  
*sunibaddhaṃ suvibhaktaṃ sukṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā prītisamāyukto bhūyaścedaṃ vyaciṃtayat \|*  
*nedṛśāni ca ratnāni mayā dṛṣṭāni kānicit \|\| 53 \|\|*

*upaśobhāni baddhāni pṛthvīmūlyasamāni ca \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇasya laṃkāyāṃ na dṛṣṭāni mayā purā \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-53 a. Rāghava, the killer of the heroes of enemies for a long time examined the ornament and thought again and again, and seeing that it had many bright pearls (big) like the āmalaka-fruits, and it was inlaid with gold, and was well-knit, well-divided and well-fashioned with diamonds, corals, sapphires, rubies, gomedhas, Lapis Lazuli and topaz, by Viśvakarman, he was pleased and again thought thus:

53b-54. ‘I have never (before) seen such gems inlaid for beauty and worth the price of the earth. I have not seen them even in Bibhīṣaṇa’s Laṅkā.’

## \|\| 36.55 \|\|

*iti saṃcitya manasā rāghavastamṛṣiṃ punaḥ \|*  
*āgamaṃ tasya divyasya praṣṭuṃ samupacakrame \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thinking like this mentally (i.e. in his mind), Rāghava again began to ask the sage about the acquisition of the divine (ornament):

## \|\| 36.56 \|\|

*atyadbhutamidaṃ brahmanna prāpyaṃ ca mahīkṣitām \|*  
*kathaṃ bhagavatā prāptaṃ kuto vā kena nirmitam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. “O brāhmaṇa, it is very wonderful, and not obtainable (even) to kings; how did the revered one obtain it? Wherefrom did you obtain it? Who has fashioned it?

## \|\| 36.57-59 \|\|

*kutūhalavaśāccaiva pṛcchāmi tvāṃ mahāmate \|*  
*karatalesthite ratne karamadhyaṃ prakāśate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*adhamaṃ tadvijānīyātsarvaśāstreṣu garhitam \|*  
*diśaḥ prakāśayedyattanmadhyamaṃ munisattama \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ūrdhvagaṃ triśikhaṃ yatsyāduttamaṃ tadudāhṛtam \|*  
*etānyuttamajātīni ṛṣibhiḥ kīrtitāni tu \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-58a. O you highly intelligent one, I ask you only through

curiosity. If the middle portion of the palm of the hand is illuminated when the gem is put on the palm, then one should know it to be of the lowest (quality), and it is condemned in all treatises.

58b-59. O best of sages, that which illumines the directions, is mediocre. That is said to be the best having three rays shooting up. These are said to be of the best kind by the sages.

## \|\| 36.60 \|\|

*āścaryāṇāṃ bahūnāṃ hi divyānāṃ bhagavānnidhiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ vadati kākutsthe munirvākyamathābravīt \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The revered one is a treasure of many divine marvels.” When the descendant of Kakutstha was speaking like this, the sage said (these) words:

## \|\| 36.61 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rāma purāvṛttaṃ purā tretāyuge mahat \|*  
*dvāpare samanuprāpte vane yaddṛṣṭavānaham \|\| 61 \|\|*

Agastya said:

61\. O Rāma, listen to the great ancient account of what formerly took place in Tretayuga, when Dvapara was about to set in, and what I saw in a forest.

## \|\| 36.62-68 \|\|

*āścaryaṃ sumahābāho nibodha raghunaṃdana \|*  
*purā tretāyuge hyāsīdaraṇyaṃ bahuvistaram \|\| 62 \|\|*

*samaṃtādyojanaśataṃ mṛgavyāghravivarjitam \|*  
*tasminniṣpuruṣe'raṇye cikīrṣustapa uttamam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*ahamākramituṃ saumya tadaraṇyamupāgataḥ \|*  
*tasyāraṇyasya madhyaṃ tu yuktaṃ mūlaphalaiḥ sadā \|\| 64 \|\|*

*śākairbahuvidhākārairnānārūpaiḥ sukānanaiḥ \|*  
*tasyāraṇyasya madhye tu paṃcayojanamāyatam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*haṃsakāraṃḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam \|*  
*tatrāścaryaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ saraḥ paramaśobhitam \|\| 66 \|\|*

*visārikacchapākīrṇaṃ bakapaṃktigaṇairyutam \|*  
*samīpe tasya sarasastapastaptuṃ gataḥ purā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*deśaṃ puṇyamupetyaivaṃ sarvahiṃsāvivarjitam \|*  
*tatrāhamavasaṃ rātriṃ naidāghīṃ puruṣarṣabha \|\| 68 \|\|*

62-63a. O descendant of Raghu, O you of mighty arms,

know (i.e. listen to) the great wonder. Formerly in Tretāyuga there was a very extensive forest, measuring a hundred yojanas on all sides, and without beasts and tigers.

63b-64a. With a desire to practise excellent penance in that manless forest I went to the forest to enter it, O gentle one.

64b-65a. The centre of the forest was always full of roots and fruits, vegetables of various shapes, and good groves of many forms.

65b-67a. In the middle of the forest I saw a wonder, viz. a very beautiful lake five yojanas in length, abounding in swans, ducks and adorned with ruddy geese, crowded with large tortoises and full of the rows of cranes.

67b-68. Formerly I had gone near the lake to practise penance. O best of men, having gone near the auspicious region free from all kinds of violence, I stayed there for one summer night.

## \|\| 36.69-74 \|\|

*prabhāte purutthāya sarastadupacakrame \|*  
*athāpaśyaṃ śavamahamaspṛṣṭajarasaṃ kvacit \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ parayā lakṣmyā saraso nātidūrataḥ \|*  
*tadarthaṃ ciṃtayānohaṃ muhūrtamiva rāghava \|\| 70 \|\|*

*asya tīre na vai prāṇī ko vāpyeṣa surarṣabhaḥ \|*  
*munirvā pārthivo vāpi kva muniḥ pārthivopi vā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*athavā pārthivasutastasyaivaṃ saṃbhavaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*atītehani rātrau vā prātarvāpi mṛto yadi \|\| 72 \|\|*

*avaśyaṃ tu mayā jñeyā sarasosya viniṣkriyā \|*  
*yāvadevaṃ sthitaścāhaṃ ciṃtayāno raghūttama \|\| 73 \|\|*

*athāpaśyaṃ mūhūrtāttu divyamadbhutadarśanam \|*  
*vimānaṃ paramodāraṃ haṃsayuktaṃ manojavam \|\| 74 \|\|*

69-70a. Having again got up in the morning, I went to that lake; and not far from the lake I saw a dead body not at all touched by decrepitude and lying with great loveliness.

70b-73a. O Rāghava, (I stood) for a while thinking about it: ‘There is no being on the bank of this lake; or who is (i.e. can be) this excellent god? Or can this be (the body of) a sage or a king? But where can there be such a sage or a king (near about)? Or how can there be the possibility (of the dead body being that) of a prince here? If the person died the previous day or night or in the morning, I must certainly know the vital part played by the lake (in bringing about the death).’

73b-74. O best of the Raghus, while I thus stood thinking, in a short while I saw before me a very big divine aeroplane looking wonderful, to which swans were yoked and which had the speed of mind.

## \|\| 36.75 \|\|

*purastatra sahasraṃ tu vimānepsarasāṃ nṛpa \|*  
*gaṃdharvāścaiva tatsaṃkhyā ramayaṃti varaṃ naram \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. In the aeroplane a thousand celestial nymphs and an equal number of Gandharvas were amusing an excellent man.

## \|\| 36.76-79 \|\|

*gāyaṃti divyageyāni vādayaṃti tathā pare \|*  
*athāpaśyaṃ naraṃ tasmādvimānādavarohitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*śavamāṃsaṃ bhakṣayantaṃ ca snātvā raghukulodvaha \|*  
*tato bhuktvā yathākāmaṃ sa māṃsaṃ bahupīvaram \|\| 77 \|\|*

*avatīrya saraḥ śīghramāruroha divaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tamahaṃ devasaṃkāśaṃ śriyā paramayānvitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*bho bho svarginmahābhāga pṛcchāmi tvāṃ kathaṃ tvidam \|*  
*jugupsitastavāhāro gatiśceyaṃ tavottamā \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-77a. (Some) were singing divine songs, others were playing on the musical instruments. O you perpetuator of Raghu’s family, I saw a man getting down from the aeroplane and eating, after having bathed, the flesh of (that) dead body.

77b-78a. Then having eaten a very large (quantity) of the flesh to the satisfaction of his desire, he quickly got down into the lake and then again went up to heaven.

78b-79. (I said to) him who resembled a god, and who was endowed with great loveliness: “O you resident of heaven, O you magnanimous one, I (would like to) ask you: “How is it that your food is (so) condemnable while your position is (so) excellent?

## \|\| 36.80 \|\|

*yadi guhyaṃ na caitatte kathaya tvadya me bhavān \|*  
*kāmataḥ śrotumicchāmi kimetatparamaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If it is not a secret, you may (please) tell it to me today. I have a desire to hear what important words they are (i.e. what important things you have to say).

## \|\| 36.81 \|\|

*ko bhavānvada saṃdehamāhāraśca vigarhitaḥ \|*  
*tvayedaṃ bhujyate saumya kimarthaṃ kva ca vartase \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Who are you? (Please) speak (and remove) my doubt. O gentle one, why do you eat this censured food? Where do you stay?

## \|\| 36.82 \|\|

*kasyāyamaiśvarobhāvaḥ śavatvena vinirmitaḥ \|*  
*āhāraṃ ca kathaṃ niṃdyaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Whose lordly condition is created as (i.e. transformed into) a dead body (i.e. who was the mighty person that is transformed into a dead body)? How is it that (you are enjoying) condemned food? I desire to hear the truth.”

## \|\| 36.83 \|\|

*śrutvā ca bhāṣitaṃ tatra mama rāma satāṃ vara \|*  
*prāṃjaliḥ pratyuvācedaṃ sa svargī raghunaṃdana \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Hearing (these) words of (i.e. uttered by) me, O Rāma, best among the good, the resident of heaven, replied with the palms of his hands joined in obeisance, O descendant of Raghu:

## \|\| 36.84 \|\|

*śṛṇuṣvādya yathāvṛttaṃ mamedaṃ sukhaduḥkhajam \|*  
*kāmo hi duritakramyaḥ śṛṇu yatpṛcchase dvija \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. “Today hear, how this, caused by pleasure and pain, happened in my case. O brāhmaṇa, desire is difficult to be resisted; hear (the reply to) what you ask.

## \|\| 36.85 \|\|

*purā vaidarbhako rājā pitā me hi mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*vāsudeva iti khyātastriṣu lokeṣu dhārmikaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Formerly there was a king of the Vidarbha country. He, of great fame, was my father known in the three worlds as Vāsudeva and was religious.

## \|\| 36.86 \|\|

*tasya putradvayaṃ brahmandvābhyāṃ strībhyāmajāyata \|*  
*ahaṃ śveta iti khyāto yavīyānsuratho'bhavat \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. O brāhmaṇa, he had sons born from two wives. I (the elder one) was known as Sveta, and the younger one was Suratha.

## \|\| 36.87 \|\|

*pitaryuparate tasminpaurā māmabhyaṣecayan \|*  
*tatrāhaṃkārayanrājyaṃ dharme cāsaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. When the father expired, the citizens consecrated me (as the king). There I ruled and was well-settled in righteousness.

## \|\| 36.88 \|\|

*evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi bahūni samupāvrajan \|*  
*mama rājyaṃ kārayataḥ paripālayataḥ prajāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. As I was ruling over the kingdom and protecting my subjects in this way, many thousand years passed.

## \|\| 36.89 \|\|

*sohaṃ nimitte kasmiṃścidvairāgyeṇa dvijottama \|*  
*maraṇaṃ hṛdaye kṛtvā tapovanamupāgamam \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. O best of brāhmaṇas, that I (i.e. I who lived like that), due to indifference to the world, as a result of some cause, thought of dying and went to the penance-grove.

## \|\| 36.90 \|\|

*sohaṃ vanamidaṃ ramyaṃ bhṛśaṃ pakṣivivarjitam \|*  
*praviṣṭastapa āsthātumasyaiva sarasoṃtike \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. That I (i.e. who thought...etc.) entered this very charming forest, free from birds, (and came) near this lake only.

## \|\| 36.91-92 \|\|

*rājye'bhiṣicya surathaṃ bhrātaraṃ taṃ narādhipam \|*  
*idaṃ saraḥ samāsādya tapastaptaṃ sudāruṇam \|\| 91 \|\|*

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi tapastaptvā mahāvane \|*  
*śubhaṃ tu bhavanaṃ prāpto brahmalokamanāmayam \|\| 92 \|\|*

91-92. Having placed Suratha on the throne as the king, I having come to this lake, practised a very severe penance. Having practised penance for ten thousand years in the great forest, I reached an auspicious residence, viz. the healthy world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 36.93 \|\|

*svargasthamapi māṃ brahmankṣutpipāse dvijottama \|*  
*abādhetāṃ bhṛśaṃ cāhamabhavaṃ vyathiteṃdriyaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. O best of brāhmaṇas, hunger and thirst tormented me even when I was in heaven; and my organs of sense were very much afflicted.

## \|\| 36.94-95 \|\|

*tatastribhuvanaśreṣṭhamavocaṃ vai pitāmaham \|*  
*bhagavansvargaloko'yaṃ kṣutpipāsā vivarjitaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*kasyeyaṃ karmaṇaḥ paktiḥ kṣutpipāse yato hi me \|*  
*āhāraḥ kaśca me deva brūhi tvaṃ śrīpitāmaha \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Then I said to the grandsire, the greatest in the three worlds: ‘O revered sir, this heaven is free from hunger and thirst. Of what deed (of mine) is this the result that I am having (i.e. am oppressed by) hunger and thirst? O respectable grandsire, tell me what food I should eat.’

## \|\| 36.96 \|\|

*tataḥ pitāmahaḥ samyakciraṃ dhyātvā mahāmune \|*  
*māmuvāca tato vākyaṃ nāsti bhojyaṃ svadehajam \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. Then, O great sage, the grandsire having thought for a long time said (these) words to me: ‘You have no other food than that produced from your own body.

## \|\| 36.97 \|\|

*ṝte te svāni māṃsāni bhakṣaya tvaṃ tu hi nityaśaḥ \|*  
*svaśarīraṃ tvayā puṣṭaṃ kurvatā tapa uttamam \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. You always eat your own flesh. While you were practising excellent penance you have nourished your body.

## \|\| 36.98-99 \|\|

*nādattaṃ jāyate tāta śveta paśya mahītale \|*  
*āgrahādbhikṣamāṇāya bhikṣāpi prāṇine purā \|\| 98 \|\|*

*na hi dattā gṛhe bhrāṃtyā mohādatithaye tadā \|*  
*tena svargagatasyāpi kṣutpipāse tavādhunā \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. O Śveta, note that nothing that is not given springs up (i.e. the fruit of what is given only is obtained by human beings) on the earth. Formerly you never even gave anything as alms to a (human) being pressing (you i.e. entreating you) for it; in your house also you never gave anything to a guest (even) through a mistake (or) ignorance. Therefore hunger and thirst are oppressing you now even though you are staying in heaven.

## \|\| 36.100 \|\|

*sa tvaṃ prapuṣṭamāhāraiḥ svaśarīramanuttamam \|*  
*bhakṣayasva ca rājeṃdra sā te tṛptirbhaviṣyati \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. O best king, you eat your own body well-nourished with (different kinds of) food. That would give you satisfaction.’

## \|\| 36.101-102 \|\|

*evamuktastato devaṃ brahmāṇamahamuktavān \|*  
*bhakṣite ca svake dehe punaranyanna me vibho \|\| 101 \|\|*

*kṣudhānivāraṇaṃ naiva dehasyāsya vinaudanaṃ \|*  
*khādāmi hyakṣayaṃ deva priyaṃ me na hi jāyate \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. Thus addressed (by Brahmā), I said to god Brahmā: ‘O lord, when I would have eaten my body, I would not have any food, except boiled rice, that would satiate my hunger. I shall eat my body till it is exhausted. Nothing agreeable comes to me.’

## \|\| 36.103 \|\|

*tatobravītpunarbrahmā tava deho'kṣayaḥ kṛtaḥ \|*  
*dinedine te puṣṭātmā śavaḥ śveta bhaviṣyati \|\| 103 \|\|*

103\. Then Brahma again said to me: ‘I have made your body inexhaustible. O Śveta, day by day your dead body (of the previous existence) will be (more and more) fat.

## \|\| 36.104-105 \|\|

*yāvadvarṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ svamāṃsaṃ khāda bho nṛpa \|*  
*yadāgacchati cāgastyaḥ śvetāraṇyaṃ mahātapāḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*bhagavānatidurdharṣastadā kṛcchrādvimokṣyase \|*  
*sa hi tārayituṃ śaktaḥ seṃdrānapi surāsurān \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. O king, till hundred years are over, eat your own flesh. When the revered Agastya, of great penance and very inaccessible comes to the Svetāraṇya, you will be free from the calamity; for he is able to protect (i.e. free) gods and demons including even Indra.

## \|\| 36.106 \|\|

*āhāraṃ kutsitaṃ cemaṃ rājarṣe kiṃ punastava \|*  
*surakāryaṃ mahattena sukṛtaṃ tu mahātmanā \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. Then what about this censurable food of you (i.e. he will easily make you get rid of this censurable food)? That great-souled one (i.e. Agastya) has well accomplished a great mission of the gods.

## \|\| 36.107 \|\|

*udadhiṃ nirjalaṃ kṛtvā dānavāśca nipātitāḥ \|*  
*viṃdhyaścādityavidveṣādvardhamāno nivāritaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. Having rendered the ocean waterless (i.e. having emptied the ocean) he destroyed the demons. He also stopped Vindhya who was growing due to his hatred for the Sun.

## \|\| 36.108 \|\|

*laṃbamānā mahī caiṣā gurutvenādhivāsitā \|*  
*dakṣiṇā digdivaṃ yātā trailākyaṃ viṣamasthitam \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. And he also made this dangling earth settled (i.e. steady) with heaviness. The southern direction had gone to the heaven, and the three worlds were in distress.

## \|\| 36.109-110 \|\|

*mayā gatvā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ preṣito dakṣiṇāṃ diśam \|*  
*samāṃ kuru mahābhāga gurutvena jagatsamam \|\| 109 \|\|*

*evaṃ ca tena muninā sthitvā sarvā dharā samā \|*  
*kṛtā rājeṃdra muninā evamadyāpi dṛśyate \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. Having gone to him with the gods I sent him to the southern direction. O magnanimous one, I said, make the earth well-poised with heaviness (i.e. by making it heavy). O lord of kings, the sage remaining (there) made the entire earth even. It is seen like that even now.’

## \|\| 36.111 \|\|

*sohaṃ bhagavata śrutvā devadevasya bhāṣitam \|*  
*bhuṃje ca kutsitāhāraṃ svaśarīramanuttamam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. That I (i.e. I who was told like that) having heard the words of the revered lord of gods, am eating this condensable food, this excellent body of mine.

## \|\| 36.112 \|\|

*pūrṇaṃ varṣaśataṃ cādya bhojanaṃ kutsitaṃ ca me \|*  
*kṣayaṃ nābhyeti tadvipra tṛptiścāpi mamottamā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Today a hundred years have completed (since) I (have been eating) this censurable food. O brāhmaṇa, it is not getting exhausted, and I ^ fully satisfied.

## \|\| 36.113 \|\|

*taṃ muniṃ kṛcchrasantaptaściṃtayāmi divāniśam \|*  
*kadā vai darśanaṃ mahyaṃ sa munirdāsyate vane \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. I, who am tormented by this calamity, am thinking about the sage day and night. ‘When will that sage appear before me in (this) forest?’

## \|\| 36.114-116 \|\|

*evaṃ me ciṃtayānasya gataṃ varṣaśatantviha \|*  
*sogastyo hi gatirbrahmanmunirme bhavitā dhruvaṃ \|\| 114 \|\|*

*na gatirbhavitā mahyaṃ kuṃbhayonimṛte dvijam \|*  
*śrutvetthaṃ bhāṣitaṃ rāma dṛṣṭvāhāraṃ ca kutsitam \|\| 115 \|\|*

*kṛpayā parayā yuktastaṃ nṛpaṃ svargagāminam \|*  
*karomyahaṃ sudhābhojyaṃ nāśayāmi ca kutsitam \|\| 116 \|\|*

114-115a. Thinking thus I have passed a hundred years. O brāhmaṇa, that Agastya (alone) will certainly be my refuge. No other brāhmaṇa than the pitcher-born (Agastya) will be my refuge.”

115b-116. O Rāma, hearing these words (of Śveta), and seeing censurable food, I, who was full of great compassion, thought: ‘I shall make that king, going to heaven, an enjoyer of nectar and shall put an end to his abominable food’.

## \|\| 36.117 \|\|

*cintayannityavocaṃ tamagastyaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*ahametatkutsitaṃ te nāśayāmi mahāmate \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. And I said to him: “What will Agastya do? I shall destroy this censurable food of yours, O you highly intelligent one.

## \|\| 36.118-119 \|\|

*īpsitaṃ prārthayasvāsmānmanaḥ prītikaraṃ param \|*  
*sa svargī māṃ tataḥ prāha kathaṃ brahmavaconyathā \|\| 118 \|\|*

*kartuṃ mune mayā śakyaṃ na cānyastārayiṣyati \|*  
*ṝte vai kuṃbhayoniṃ taṃ maitrāvaruṇasaṃbhavam \|\| 119 \|\|*

118-119. Ask your mind for the desired object; (for) the mind is highly agreeable.” Then that resident of heaven said to me: “O sage, how can I falsify the the words of Brahmā. None else but the pitcher-born son of Maitrā-Varuṇa will save me.

## \|\| 36.120-124 \|\|

*apṛṣṭopi mayā brahmannevamūce pitāmahaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ śvetamuktavānahamasmi saḥ \|\| 120 \|\|*

*āgatastava bhāgyena dṛṣṭohaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ svargī sa māṃ jñātvā daṃḍavatpatito bhuvi \|\| 121 \|\|*

*tamutthāpya tato rāmābravaṃ kiṃ te karomyaham \|*  
*rājovāca \|*  
*āhārātkutsitādbrahmaṃstārayasvādya duṣkṛtāt \|\| 122 \|\|*

*yena loko'kṣayaḥ svargo bhavitā tvatkṛtena me \|*  
*tataḥ pratigraho datto jagadvaṃdya nṛpeṇa hi \|\| 123 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 124 \|\|*

120-121a. O brāhmaṇa, even without being asked by me Brahma has told me thus.” I said to that Śveta, who was speaking thus: “Through your good luck, you have seen me, who have come here. There is no doubt about it (i.e. about your good luck).”

121b-122a. Then that resident of heaven, having recognised me, fell (i.e. prostrated himself) on the earth like a staff. Raising him I then said to him: “What can I do for you?”

The king said:

122b-123a. O brāhmaṇa, today protect me from this wicked deed of eating this abominable food, so that by what you will do I shall have inexhaustible heaven (i.e. live in heaven eternally).

123b-124. Then the king, adorable to the world, gave me (this) gift. “You may (please) favour me. (Please) accept this gift. O best and gentle brāhmaṇa, this ornament (I am giving you) for my protection.

## \|\| 36.125-131 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 125 \|\|no sanskrit verse \|\| 126 \|\|*

*bhavānmāmanugṛhṇātu pratīcchasva pratigraham \|\| 127 \|\|*

*kṛtā matistāraṇāya na lobhādraghunaṃdana \|*  
*gṛhīte bhūṣaṇe rāma mama hastagate tadā \|\| 128 \|\|*

*mānuṣaḥ paurviko dehastadā naṣṭosya bhūpate \|*  
*praṇaṣṭe tu śarīre ca rājarṣiḥ parayā mudā \|\| 129 \|\|*

*mayoktosau vimānena jagāma tridivaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tena me śakratulyena dattamābharaṇaṃ śubhaṃ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*tasminnimitte kākutstha dattamadbhutakarmaṇā \|*  
*śveto vaidarbhako rājā tadābhūdgatakalmaṣaḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

125-127a. O brāhmaṇa-sage, accept it. Please favour me. O brāhmaṇa, I offer you these cows, this gold, wealth with garments, articles of food and this ornament satisfying all desires and also (giving) all pleasures. O brāhmaṇa sage, please favour and protect me.”

Agastya said:

127b-128a. O descendant of Raghu, having heard the words of the resident of heaven full of pain and pleasure, I made up my mind to save him and not through greed.

128b-130a. When I accepted the ornament, and when it was in my hand, the former human body of the king was no more. When the body was destroyed, the royal sage, instructed by me, went in the aeroplane to heaven with great joy.

130b-131. He, comparable to Śakra, gave this auspicious ornament to me. For that reason, O Kākutstha, he, of wonderful deeds, gave me the ornament. Then Śveta, the king of Vidarbha became free from sins.

## Chapter 37 - Rāma’s Abstaining from the Performance of Rājasūya

## \|\| 37.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*tadadbhutatamaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā ca raghunaṃdanaḥ \|*  
*gauravādvismayāccāpi bhūyaḥ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. The descendant of Raghu, having heard those most wonderful words, asked Agastya again, prompted by the importance of the ornament and through amazement.

## \|\| 37.2 \|\|

*rāma uvāca \|*  
*bhagavaṃstadvanaṃ ghoraṃ yatrāsau taptavāṃstapaḥ \|*  
*śveto vaidarbhako rājā tadadbhutamabhūtkathaṃ \|\| 2 \|\|*

Rāma said:

2\. (Tell me) O revered sir, (about) the fearful forest where the Vidarbha-king Śveta practised penance. Tell me how the wonderful thing took place there.

## \|\| 37.3 \|\|

*viṣamaṃ tadvanaṃ rājā śūnyaṃ mṛgavivarjitaṃ \|*  
*praviṣṭastapa āsthātuṃ kathaṃ vada mahāmune \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Tell me how, (when) the fearful forest was desolate and void of beasts the king entered it to practise penance, O great sage.

## \|\| 37.4 \|\|

*samaṃtādyojanaśataṃ nirmanuṣyamabhūtkathaṃ \|*  
*bhavānkathaṃ praviṣṭastadyena kāryeṇa tadvada \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Tell me how it was manless for a hundred yojanas around and how and on what business you entered it.

## \|\| 37.5 \|\|

*agastya uvāca \|*  
*purā kṛtayuge rājā manurdaṃḍadharaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*tasya putrotha nāmnāsīdikṣvākuramitadyutiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

Agastya said:

5\. Formerly in Kṛtayuga there lived Manu, the king who wielded the rod (as a symbol of judicial authority and punishment). His son was Ikṣvāku by name, whose lustre was unlimited.

## \|\| 37.6 \|\|

*taṃ putraṃ pūrvajaṃ rājye nikṣipya bhuvisaṃmatam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśānāṃ bhava rājetyuvāca ha \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. (Manu) installed him, the elder son, on the throne on (i.e. of) the earth with the consent (of all) and said to him: “Be the king of royal families on the earth.”

## \|\| 37.7 \|\|

*tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ pituḥ putreṇa rāghava \|*  
*tataḥparamasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ punastaṃ pratyabhāṣata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. O Rāghava, the son promised to the father to do so. Then being highly pleased, he again said to him:

## \|\| 37.8 \|\|

*prītosmi paramodāra karmaṇā te na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*daṃḍena ca prajā rakṣa na ca daṃḍamakāraṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “I am pleased with your very generous deeds. There is no doubt about it. Protect the subjects with the rod. The rod (should not be used) without (proper) reason.

## \|\| 37.9 \|\|

*aparādhiṣu yo daṃḍaḥ pātyate mānavairiha \|*  
*sa daṃḍo vidhivanmuktaḥ svargaṃ nayati pārthivam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. That rod (i.e. punishment), which is inflicted upon the culprits by men here (i.e. in this world), being duly freed (from any blemish) takes the king to heaven.

## \|\| 37.10 \|\|

*tasmāddaṇḍe mahābāho yatnavānbhava putraka \|*  
*dharmaste paramo loke kṛta evaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Therefore, O (my) son, O you of mighty arms, be scrupulous (about using) the rod. If you do so, then you will have great religious merit in this world.”

## \|\| 37.11 \|\|

*iti taṃ bahusaṃdiśya manuḥ putraṃ samādhinā \|*  
*jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭo brahmalokamanuttamam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus having very much advised his son with perfect concentration and being happy, Manu went to the world of Brahmā.

## \|\| 37.12 \|\|

*janayiṣye kathaṃ putrāniti ciṃtāparo'bhavat \|*  
*karmabhirbahubhistaistaissasutaissaṃyuto'bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He (i.e. Ikṣvāku) became anxious (with the thought): ‘How shall I generate sons?’ As a result of various deeds he became united with (i.e. he had) many sons.

## \|\| 37.13 \|\|

*toṣayāmāsa putraissa pitṝndevasutopamaiḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāmuttamasteṣāṃ kanīyānraghunaṃdana \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He gratified his dead ancestors with (i.e. by giving birth to) (his) sons resembling sons of gods. Best among them was the youngest.

## \|\| 37.14-18 \|\|

*śūraśca kṛtavidyaśca guruśca janapūjayā \|*  
*nāma tasyātha daṃḍeti pitā cakre sa buddhimān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyaddaṇḍapatanaṃ śarīre tasya vīkṣya ca \|*  
*saṃpaśyamānastaṃ doṣaṃ ghoraṃ putrasya rāghava \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sa viṃdhyanīlayormadhye rājyamasya dadau prabhuḥ \|*  
*sa daṃḍastatra rājābhūdramye parvatamūrddhani \|\| 16 \|\|*

*puraṃ cāpratimaṃ tena niveśāya tathā kṛtam \|*  
*nāma tasya purasyātha madhumattamiti svayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tathādeśena saṃpannaḥ śūro vāsamathākarot \|*  
*evaṃ rājā sa tadrājyaṃ cakāra sapurohitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18a. He was brave, had mastered the lores and was important as he was honoured by people. Foreseeing that (for committing a grave sin) the rod in future will fall on his person (i.e. on him), the intelligent father named him Daṇḍa.

15b-16. Seeing that terrible blemish of the son, O Rāghava, the lord gave him kingdom between Vindhya and Nīla (mountains). That Daṇḍa became the king there on the beautiful top of the mountain.

## \|\| 37.17 \|\|

*puraṃ cāpratimaṃ tena niveśāya tathā kṛtam \|*  
*nāma tasya purasyātha madhumattamiti svayam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Similarly he fashioned a matchless city for his residence; and he himself named the city Madhumatta.

## \|\| 37.18-23 \|\|

*tathādeśena saṃpannaḥ śūro vāsamathākarot \|*  
*evaṃ rājā sa tadrājyaṃ cakāra sapurohitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prahṛṣṭa suprajākīrṇaṃ devarājo yathā divi \|*  
*tataḥ sa daṃḍaḥ kākutstha bahuvarṣagaṇāyutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*akārayattu dharmātmā rājyaṃ nihatakaṃṭakaṃ \|*  
*atha kāle tu kasmiṃścidrājā bhārgavamāśramam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ramaṇīyamupākrāmaccaitramāse manorame \|*  
*tatra bhārgavakanyāṃ tu rūpeṇāpratimāṃ bhuvi \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vicaraṃtīṃ vanoddeśe daṃḍo'paśyadanuttamām \|*  
*uttuṃgapīvarīṃ śyāmāṃ caṃdrābhavadanāṃ śubhām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sunāsāṃ cārusarvāṃgīṃ pīnonnatapayodharām \|*  
*madhye kṣāmāṃ ca vistīrṇāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ kurute mudam \|\| 23 \|\|*

18-19a. Thus endowed with (i.e. possessing) that region the brave (Daṇḍa) lived there. Thus the king with (the help of) his priests governed that kingdom, full of subjects that were very much pleased, as the king of gods (i.e. Indra) ruled in heaven.

19b-20a. O descendant of Kakutstha, the righteous-minded Daṇḍa governed the kingdom, free from any source of vexation for many groups of myriads of years.

20b-21a. Some time during the charming month of Caitra, the king approached the beautiful hermitage of Śukra.

21b-23. There he saw Śukra’s daughter of matchless beauty on the earth, who was wandering in the forest. Seeing her tall and stout, being in (the prime of) youth, with moon-like face, beautiful, of a fine nose, charming in all limbs, with stout and raised breasts, slim in the waist and big (in size), he was pleased.

## \|\| 37.24 \|\|

*ekavastrāṃ vane caikāṃ prathame yauvane sthitām \|*  
*sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvātvadharmeṇa anaṃgaśarapīḍitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Seeing her who had put on (only) one garment, who was (all) alone, and who was in her first (i.e. prime) youth, he naturally became tormented by love.

## \|\| 37.25-26 \|\|

*abhigamya suviśrāṃtāṃ kanyāṃ vacanamabravīt \|*  
*kutastvamasi suśroṇi kasya cāsi suśobhane \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pīḍatohamanaṃgena pṛcchāmi tvāṃ suśobhane \|*  
*tvayā me'pahṛtaṃ cittaṃ darśanādeva suṃdari \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Approaching the well-reposed unmarried girl he said (these) words to her: “O you lady of beautiful buttocks (i.e. O you beautiful lady), wherefrom do you come? Whose daughter are you, O beautiful lady? I am tormented by love, therefore I am asking (you), O you beautiful lady. O charming lady, merely on seeing you, my heart is snatched by you.

## \|\| 37.27 \|\|

*idaṃ te vadanaṃ ramyaṃ munīnāṃ cittahārakam \|*  
*yadyahaṃ na labhe bhoktuṃ mṛtaṃ māmavadhāraya \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Know me to be dead I do not get to enjoy this your beautiful face which attracts the hearts of sages.

## \|\| 37.28 \|\|

*tvayā hṛtā mama prāṇā māṃ jīvaya sulocane \|*  
*dāsosmi te varārohe bhaktaṃ māṃ bhaja śobhane \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. My life is taken away by you; O beautiful lady, revive me. O you charming lady, I am your servant. Accept me who am your devotee.”

## \|\| 37.29 \|\|

*tasyaivaṃ tu bruvāṇasya madonmattasya kāminaḥ \|*  
*bhārgavī pratyuvācedaṃ vacaḥ savinayaṃ nṛpam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the king, intoxicated by the passion of love, was thus talking, the daughter of Śukra politely spoke to him:

## \|\| 37.30 \|\|

*bhārgavasya sutāṃ viddhi śukrasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ \|*  
*arajāṃ nāma rājeṃdra jyeṣṭhāmāśramavāsinaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. “Know me to be the daughter of Bhārgava, i.e. Śukra of pious deeds. (I am) Arajā by name and the eldest daughter of (Śukra) living in the hermitage.

## \|\| 37.31 \|\|

*śukraḥ pitā me rājeṃdra tvaṃ ca śiṣyo mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*dharmato bhaginī cāhaṃ bhavāmi nṛpanaṃdana \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. O best king, my father is Śukra, and you are the disciple of that great-souled one. So, O king’s son, I am your spiritual sister.

## \|\| 37.32 \|\|

*evaṃvidhaṃ vaco vaktuṃ na tvamarhasi pārthiva \|*  
*anyebhyopi suduṣṭebhyo rakṣyā cāhaṃ sadā tvayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. O king, please do not utter such words. You should (in fact) protect me from other very wicked men.

## \|\| 37.33-34 \|\|

*krodhano me pitā raudro bhasmatvaṃ tvāṃ samānayet \|*  
*athavā rājadharmeṇāsaṃbaṃdhaṃ kuruṣe balāt \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pitaraṃ yācayasva tvaṃ dharmadṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|*  
*varayasva nṛpaśreṣṭha pitaraṃ me mahādyutim \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. My father is irascible and (when) angered will reduce you to ashes. Or (if) in view of the customary laws laid down for a king you (desire) to have union with me per force, ask my father through a prescribed course of conduct. O best king, request my father of a great lustre.

## \|\| 37.35 \|\|

*anyathā vipulaṃ duḥkhaṃ tava ghoraṃ bhaveddhruvam \|*  
*kruddho hi me pitā sarvaṃ trailokyamabhinirdahet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Otherwise you will certainly meet with a great terrible grief. When my father is angry he would burn (even) the three worlds.”

## \|\| 37.36 \|\|

*tato'śubhaṃ mahāghoraṃ śrutvā daṃḍaḥ sudāruṇam \|*  
*pratyuvāca madonmattaḥ śirasābhinataḥ punaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Hearing these inauspicious and very fearful and terrible words from (i.e. of) her, Daṇḍa, who was intoxicated by passion, said again with his head hung down:

## \|\| 37.37-38 \|\|

*prasādaṃ kuru suśroṇi kāmonmattasya kāmini \|*  
*tvayā ruddhā mama prāṇā viśīryaṃti śubhānane \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tvāṃ prāpya vairaṃ me'trāstu vadho vāpi mahattaraḥ \|*  
*bhaktaṃ bhajasva māṃ bhīru tvayi bhaktirhi me parā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. “O you beautiful lady, favour me who am mad with lust. O you beautiful lady, you have arrested my life; it will (now) perish. Let there be hostility or let me be even killed very (mercilessly) after I obtain you. O you timid one, resort to me—your devotee. I have great attachment for you.”

## \|\| 37.39-40 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ balātsaṃgṛhya bāhunā \|*  
*anyena rājñā hastena vivastrā sā tathā kṛtā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aṃgamaṃge samāśleṣya mukhe caiva mukhaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*visphuraṃtīṃ yathākāmaṃ maithunāyopacakrame \|\| 40 \|\|*
