110b-111a. Those who desire (to perform) sacrifices, get their desires (fulfilled), and have various (kinds of) penance. Whatever desire one entertains would have it fulfilled from (i.e. by) the lord of the world.

111b-113a. O you best among men, no evil would come to him, who, giving-up everything (else) would recite this account of Hari’s manifestation of Puṣkara. This manifestation of the great-souled one called Pauṣkaraka, is described in Vyāsa’s sacred text.

113b-114. Listen, from me (i.e. as I shall describe it) to Viṣṇu’s being Viṣṇu and Hari in the Kṛtayuga; and his being Vaikuṇṭha (i.e. Viṣṇu) among gods and his being Kṛṣṇa among the human beings. The course of the actions of that god is hard to be understood.

## \|\| 40.115-116 \|\|

*sāṃprataṃ bhūtabhavyaṃ ca śṛṇu rājanyathātathaṃ \|*  
*avyakto vyaktaliṃgastho ya eṣa bhagavānprabhuḥ \|\| 140115 \|\|*

*nārāyaṇo hyanaṃtātmā prabhavāpyaya eva ca \|*  
*eṣa nārāyaṇo bhūtvā harirāsītsanātanaḥ \|\| 140116 \|\|*

115-116. O king, now listen to the accurate (account of) past and future. This revered, unmanifest lord, with his characteristics being manifest, is Nārāyaṇa, of an unending soul and is devoid of origin and destruction. This one being Nārāyaṇa was the ancient Hari.

## \|\| 40.117 \|\|

*brahmā vāyuśca somaśca dharmaḥ śakro bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*aditerapi putratvametyajaḥ kurunaṃdana \|\| 140117 \|\|*

117\. He (was) Brahmā, Vāyu, Soma, Dharma, Śakra, Bṛhaspati. O you descendant of Kuru, the unborn one also becomes the son of Aditi.

## \|\| 40.118 \|\|

*eṣa viṣṇuriti khyāta indrasyāvarajo vibhuḥ \|*  
*prasādanaṃ tasyavibhoradityāḥ putrakāraṇam \|\| 140118 \|\|*

118\. This eternal one, the younger brother of Indra, is known as Viṣṇu. Pleasing to him was the cause of Aditi’s getting a son.

## \|\| 40.119 \|\|

*vadhārthaṃ suraśatrūṇāṃ daityadānavarakṣasām \|*  
*sasarjātha surānkalpe brahmāṇaṃ ca prajāpatīn \|\| 140119 \|\|*

119\. In the Kalpa (i.e. Brahmā’s day) he created gods, Brahmā, and Prajāpatis (i.e. the mind-born sons) for killing gods’ enemies, viz. Daityas, Dānavas and demons.

## \|\| 40.120 \|\|

*asṛjanmānasāṃstatra brahmavaṃśānanuttamān \|*  
*tebhyobhavanmahātmabhyaḥ paraṃbrahma sanātanam \|\| 140120 \|\|*

120\. He also created excellent mental families of Brahmā. From these magnanimous ones the eternal and supreme Brahman came up.

## \|\| 40.121 \|\|

*etadāścaryabhūtasya viṣṇoḥ karmānukīrtitaṃ \|*  
*kīrttanīyasya lokeṣu kīrtyamānaṃ nibodha me \|\| 140121 \|\|*

121\. I have told you this deed of Viṣṇu who (himself) is a wonder. Know from me the deed being narrated (since) it deserves to be told in the worlds.

## \|\| 40.122-123 \|\|

*vṛtte vṛtravadhe bhīṣma vartamāne kṛteyuge \|*  
*āsīttrailokyavikhyātaḥ saṃgrāmastārakāmayaḥ \|\| 140122 \|\|*

*yatra te dānavā ghorāḥ sarve saṃgrāmadurjayāḥ \|*  
*ghnaṃti devāsurānsarvānsayakṣoragarākṣasān \|\| 140123 \|\|*

122-123. O Bhiṣma, in the present Kṛtayuga, after Vṛtra was killed, there took place the well-known war called Tārakā- maya, in which the terrible Dānavas, all difficult to be conquered in a battle, killed all gods and Asuras and Yakṣas, Uragas and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 40.124 \|\|

*te vadhyamānā vimukhāśchinnapraharaṇā raṇe \|*  
*trātāraṃ manasā jagmurdevaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 140124 \|\|*

124\. They being killed, and with their weapons cut off in the battle, turned back and mentally approached their protector, the god, lord Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 40.125-126 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare meghā nirvāṇāṃgāravarcasaḥ \|*  
*sārkacaṃdragrahagaṇaṃ cchādayaṃto nabhastalam \|\| 140125 \|\|*

*caṃḍavidyudgaṇopetā ghoranirhrādakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*anyonyavegābhihatāḥ pravavuḥ saptamārutāḥ \|\| 140126 \|\|*

125-126. In the meanwhile, the clouds with brilliance (i.e. like) extinguished charcoal, covered the sky (as) with the solar and lunar eclipses. They were accompanied by multitudes of fierce (flashes of) lightning. They were making terrible sounds. They were obstructed by the speed of one another. The seven (kinds of) winds blew.

## \|\| 40.127 \|\|

*dīptatoyāḥ sanirghātaiḥ saha vajrānalānilaiḥ \|*  
*ravaissughorairutpātairdahyamānamivāmbaram \|\| 140127 \|\|*

127\. The clouds had the water heated due to their thunder strokes along with thunderbolt and winds. The sky was as it were being burnt by portents with terrible sounds.

## \|\| 40.128 \|\|

*peturulkāsahasrāṇi nipetuḥ khacarāṇyapi \|*  
*daivāni ca vimānāni prapataṃtyutpataṃti ca \|\| 140128 \|\|*

128\. Thousands of meteors fell; also those moving in the sky fell down. Heavenly cars fell down and jumped up.

## \|\| 40.129 \|\|

*caturyugāṃtasamaye lokānāṃ yadbhayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*arūpavati rūpāṇi tasminnutpātalakṣaṇe \|\| 140129 \|\|*

129\. That fear which would be there at the time of the end of the four yugas (spread everywhere). Forms became invisible due to the portents.

## \|\| 40.130 \|\|

*tasmādduṣprathitaṃ sarvaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃcana \|*  
*timiraughaparikṣiptā na rejuśca diśo daśa \|\| 140130 \|\|*

130\. As a result (of this) everything became screened, and nothing was recognised. Even the ten quarters surrounded by the flood of darkness, did not shine.

## \|\| 40.131 \|\|

*viveśa rūpiṇī kālī kālameghāvaguṃṭhitā \|*  
*dyaurnabhātyabhibhūtārkā ghoreṇa tamasā vṛtā \|\| 140131 \|\|*

131\. (Goddess) Kāli, covered with black clouds entered (i.e. appeared there) in an embodied form. The sky did not shine (as usual) with the sun being predominant (but) was covered with fearful darkness.

## \|\| 40.132 \|\|

*tāṃ ghanaughāṃ satimirāṃ dorbhyāmāchidya sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*vapuḥ svaṃ darśayāmāsa divyaṃ kṛṣṇavapurhariḥ \|\| 140132 \|\|*

132\. (Then) that lord Hari of a dark body, having rent, with his arms, that stream of clouds with darkness, manifested his divine body.

## \|\| 40.133 \|\|

*balāhakāṃjananibhaṃ balāhakatanūruham \|*  
*tejasā vapuṣā caiva kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇamivācalam \|\| 140133 \|\|*

133\. He resembled a cloud and collyrium, the hair on which was like a cloud, which was like a black mountain in respect of lustre and form.

## \|\| 40.134 \|\|

*dīptapītāṃbaradharaṃ taptakāṃcanabhūṣaṇam \|*  
*dhūmrāṃdhakāravapuṣaṃ yugāṃtāgnimivotthitam \|\| 140134 \|\|*

134\. He had on a bright yellow garment. The ornaments were of gold purified in fire. He was like a column of smoke and darkness, (and) like the fire rising at the time of the destruction of the world.

## \|\| 40.135 \|\|

*vṛttadviguṇapīnāṃ saṃkirīṭācchannamūrdhajam \|*  
*babhau cāmīkaraprakhyairāyudhairupaśobhitam \|\| 140135 \|\|*

135\. The shoulders were round and doubly plump, the hair on the head was covered with a crown. He shone more due to the weapons resembling gold.

## \|\| 40.136 \|\|

*caṃdrārkakiraṇodyotaṃ girikūṭamivocchritam \|*  
*naṃdakānaṃditakaraṃ kaustubhodbhāsitorasam \|\| 140136 \|\|*

136\. He was bright like the rays of the moon and the sun, lofty like a mountain-peak, with one hand blissful due to (holding) the Nandaka sword. His chest shone with the Kaustubha gem.

## \|\| 40.137 \|\|

*śakticitraphalodagraṃ śaṃkhacakragadādharam \|*  
*viṣṇuśailaṃ kṣamāśīlaṃ śrīvatsaṃ śārṅgapāṇinam \|\| 140137 \|\|*

137\. He was exalted on account of the power causing various results. He held a conch, discus and mace. He resembled an extensive mountain. He was of a forgiving nature. He had a curl ofhair on the chest and the Śārṅga bow in the hand.

## \|\| 40.138 \|\|

*tridaśodāraphaladaṃ svargastrīcāruvallabham \|*  
*sarvalokamanaḥkāṃtaṃ sarvasatvamanoharam \|\| 140138 \|\|*

138\. He gave generous fruits to gods, was charming and dear to the divine women, pleased the minds of all people, and attracted the minds of all beings.

## \|\| 40.139 \|\|

*māyāviśālaviṭapaṃ toyadaughasamaprabham \|*  
*vidyāhaṃkāramānāḍhya mahābhūtaprarohaṇam \|\| 140139 \|\|*

139\. He had a large branch in the form of divine power, was rich in knowledge, ego and pride and was the germination of the gross elements.

## \|\| 40.140 \|\|

*viśeṣapatrairnicitaṃ grahanakṣatrapuṣpitam \|*  
*daityalokamahāskaṃdhaṃ martyalokaprakāśitam \|\| 140140 \|\|*

140\. He was overcast with copious leaves, and had flowers of planets and stars; was the great stem of the world of Daityas, and was manifested in the mortal world.

## \|\| 40.141 \|\|

*sāgarākāranirhrādaṃ rasātalagalāśrayam \|*  
*nāgeṃdrapāśairvitataṃ pakṣijaṃtusamanvitam \|\| 140141 \|\|*

141\. He had the (huge) shape and sound of an ocean; he had resorted to the earth; he was covered with bonds of the lords of serpents, and was full of birds and creatures.

## \|\| 40.142 \|\|

*śīlānāhāryagaṃdhāḍhyaṃ sarvalokamahādrumam \|*  
*avyaktānaṃdasalilaṃ vyaktāhaṃkāraphenilam \|\| 140142 \|\|*

142\. He was endowed with natural fragrance of virtue; was a great tree for all the worlds; had the water of the joy of the unmanifest and had the foam of the manifest ego.

## \|\| 40.143 \|\|

*mahābhūtakaraughaughaṃ grahanakṣatrabudbudam \|*  
*vimānavāhanairvyāptaṃ toyadāḍambarākulam \|\| 140143 \|\|*

143\. He had the great stream of the rays in the form of the gross elements, had the bubbles in the form of planets and stars; was pervaded by the aeroplanes; was full of the roaring of clouds.

## \|\| 40.144 \|\|

*jaṃtumatsyagaṇākīrṇaṃ śailaśaṃkhakulairyutam \|*  
*traiguṇyaviṣayāvartaṃ sarvalokatimiṃgilam \|\| 140144 \|\|*

144\. He was crowded with groups of creatures and fish; was united with groups of mountains, and conches; had the eddy of the sensual objects based on the three properties (viz. Sattva, Rajas and Tamas); was swallowing the (big fish called) timi in the form of the worlds.

## \|\| 40.145 \|\|

*vīravṛkṣalatāgulmaṃ bhujagotsṛṣṭaśaivalam \|*  
*dvādaśārkamahādvīpaṃ rudraikādaśapattanam \|\| 140145 \|\|*

145\. He had the thickets in the form of heroes; had the moss emitted by the serpents, was the great shelter of the twelve Suns; was the city of the eleven Rudras.

## \|\| 40.146 \|\|

*vasvaṣṭaparvatopetaṃ trailokyāṃbho mahodadhim \|*  
*saṃdhyāsaṃdhyormisalilamāpūrṇānilaśobhitam \|\| 140146 \|\|*

146\. He was endowed with the mountains in the form of the eight Vasus; was a great ocean having the three worlds as its water; had the water having tawny ripples of the twilight; was adorned with wind that had filled it.

## \|\| 40.147 \|\|

*daityayakṣagaṇagrāmaṃ rakṣogaṇajhaṣākulam \|*  
*pitāmahamahāvīryaṃ svargastrīratnasaṃkulam \|\| 140147 \|\|*

147\. He had hosts of Daityas and Yakṣas; was full of the (fish called) jhaṣa in the form of the groups of demons; had the mighty power of the grandsire; was thronged with the gems of celestial women.

## \|\| 40.148 \|\|

*śrī kīrti kāṃtilakṣmībhirnadībhiśca samākulam \|*  
*kālayogamahāvarṣapralayotpattivegitam \|\| 140148 \|\|*

148\. He was full of the rivers in the form of wealth, fame, charm and Lakṣmī; was violent due to the dissolution having great showers caused by destiny.

## \|\| 40.149 \|\|

*satsaṃyogamahāpāraṃ nārāyaṇamahārṇavam \|*  
*devātidevaṃ varadaṃ bhaktānāṃ bhaktavatsalam \|\| 140149 \|\|*

149\. They saw the great ocean in the form of Nārāyaṇa having company of the good as its great extremity—Nārāyaṇa, who was the god of gods, who was a granter of boons, who was affectionate to his devotees.

## \|\| 40.150-153 \|\|

*anugrahakaraṃ devaṃ praśāṃtikaraṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*haryaśvarathasaṃyukta suparṇadhvajaśobhite \|\| 140150 \|\|*

*caṃdrārkacakraracita udārākṣavṛtāṃtare \|*  
*anaṃtaraśmisaṃyukte durdarśe merukūbare \|\| 140151 \|\|*

*tārakācitrakusume grahanakṣatrabaṃdhure \|*  
*bhayeṣvabhayade vyomni devadaityāparājite \|\| 140152 \|\|*

*haryaśvarathasaṃyuktamuktāśobhāsamanvitam \|*  
*dadṛśuste sthitaṃ devaṃ divyalokamaye rathe \|\| 140153 \|\|*

150-153. (They saw him as one) who showed favour; who brought about tranquility and who was auspicious; who shone with pearls attached to the chariot to which bay horses were yoked; seated in a chariot in the form of the divine world, (a chariot) to which bay horses were attached and which was adorned with the banner of Garuḍa, to which were fixed the wheels of the moon and the sun, had boundless reins, which was difficult to be seen (i.e. of an unbearable sight), which had Meru as its pole, which had the variegated flowers of stars (attached to it), which was pleasing due to planets and stars, which granted fearlessness in (times of) fear, which (remained) in the sky, which was invincible to gods and demons.

## \|\| 40.154 \|\|

*te kṛtāṃjalayaḥ sarve devā iṃdrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*jayaśabdaṃ puraskṛtya śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 140154 \|\|*

154\. All those gods led by Indra and with palms joined in obeisance, and (uttering) cries of victory sought the refuge of him who was a protector.

## \|\| 40.155 \|\|

*eteṣāṃ ca giraḥ śrutvā sa viṣṇurdevadaivataḥ \|*  
*manaścakre vināśāya dānavānāṃ mahāmṛdhe \|\| 140155 \|\|*

155\. That Viṣṇu, the god of gods, having heard their words, decided to destroy the demons in a great war.

## \|\| 40.156 \|\|

*ākāśe tu sthito viṣṇuruttamaṃ vapurāśritaḥ \|*  
*uvāca devatāḥ sarvāḥ sapratijñamidaṃ vacaḥ \|\| 140156 \|\|*

156\. Viṣṇu having resorted to (i.e. taken up) an excellent body and standing in the sky, said these words, containing a promise, to all the gods:

## \|\| 40.157 \|\|

*śāṃtiṃ vrajata bhadraṃ vo mā bhaiṣṭa marutāṃgaṇāḥ \|*  
*jitā me dānavāḥ sarve trailokyaṃ parigṛhyatām \|\| 140157 \|\|*

157\. “Be calm, well-being to you; do not be afraid, O host of gods. All the demons are conquered by me; accept the three worlds.”

## \|\| 40.158 \|\|

*tatosya satyasaṃdhasya viṣṇorvākyena toṣitāḥ \|*  
*devāḥ prītiṃ parājagmuḥ prāśyāmṛtamivottamam \|\| 140158 \|\|*

158\. Then the gods, pleased with the words of Viṣṇu, faithful to his promise, became very much delighted as if after having drunk excellent nectar.

## \|\| 40.159 \|\|

*tatastamaśca saṃhṛtya vineśuśca balāhakāḥ \|*  
*pravavuśca śivā vātāḥ prasannāśca diśo daśa \|\| 140159 \|\|*

159\. Then withdrawing darkness, the clouds disappeared. Auspicious breezes blew. The ten quarters became bright.

## \|\| 40.160 \|\|

*śuddhaprāyāṇi jyotīṃṣi somaṃ cakruḥ pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*na vigrahaṃ grahāścakruḥ prasannāścāpi siṃdhavaḥ \|\| 140160 \|\|*

160\. The luminaries, almost pure, went round the moon. The planets did not fight. The rivers also were (having) clear (water).

## \|\| 40.161 \|\|

*virajā abhavanmārgā lokāḥ svargādayastrayaḥ \|*  
*yathārthamūhussaritaścukṣubhe na tathārṇavaḥ \|\| 140161 \|\|*

161\. The paths, and the three worlds, heaven and others, were free from dust. The rivers flew properly. In the same way the ocean did not agitate.

## \|\| 40.162 \|\|

*āsanchubhānīndriyāṇi narāṇāmaṃtarātmasu \|*  
*maharṣayo vītaśokā vedānuccairadhīyata \|\| 140162 \|\|*

162\. The internal organs of men were auspicious (i.e. functioned well). The great sages, free from grief, recited the Vedas loudly.

## \|\| 40.163-171 \|\|

*yajñeṣu ca haviḥ pākaṃ śivamāpa ca pāvakaḥ \|*  
*pravṛttadharmasaṃvṛttā lokā muditamānasāḥ \|\| 140163 \|\|*

*viṣṇoḥ satyapratijñasya śrutvārinidhanā giraḥ \|*  
*tato bhayaṃ viṣṇumukhācchrutvā daiteyadānavāḥ \|\| 140164 \|\|*

*udyogaṃ vipulaṃ cakruryuddhāya vijayāya ca \|*  
*mayastu kāṃcanamayaṃ trinalvāṃtaramavyayam \|\| 140165 \|\|*

*catuścakraṃ suvipulaṃ sukalpitamahāyudham \|*  
*kiṃkiṇījālanirghoṣaṃ dvīpicarmapariṣkṛtam \|\| 140166 \|\|*

*ruciraṃ raśmijālaiśca haimajālaiśca śobhitam \|*  
*īhāmṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ pakṣisaṃghavirājitam \|\| 140167 \|\|*

*divyāstraśastraruciraṃ payodharanināditam \|*  
*svakṣaṃ rathavarodāraṃ sūpasthaṃ gaganopamam \|\| 140168 \|\|*

*gadāparighasaṃpūrṇaṃ mūrtimaṃtamivārṇavam \|*  
*hemakeyūravalayaṃ caṃdramaṃḍalakūbaram \|\| 140169 \|\|*

*sapatākadhvajopetaṃ sādityamiva maṃdaram \|*  
*gajeṃdrābhogavapuṣaṃ kvacitkesaravarcasam \|\| 140170 \|\|*

*yuktamṛkṣasahasreṇa sudhārāṃbudanāditam \|*  
*dīptamākāśagaṃ divyaṃ rathaṃ pararathārujam \|\| 140171 \|\|*

163-164a. Auspicious oblation was made in sacrifices. Fire roasted (the oblation) fully. People, set upon practising piety, were pleased at heart after having heard the words about killing the enemies—of Viṣṇu faithful to his promise.

164b-165a. Then the Daityas and Dānavas having learnt about the (imminent) fear from the mouth of Viṣṇu, exerted hard for the fight and victory (in it).

165b-171. Maya, desirous of fighting, mounted like the Sun on the Meru mountain, upon his imperishable, golden, divine chariot, which had its interior of the length of three nalvas1 (i.e. twelve hundred cubits), which had four wheels, which was very big, in which great weapons were well-arranged, which made the sound of the multitudes of bells, which was adorned with the hide of a tiger, which was charming with a mass of reins, which was adorned with golden lattices, which was crowded with groups of wolves, which was decorated with flocks of birds, which was bright with divine weapons and missiles, which was resounding like (thundering) clouds, which had a good (i.e. a strong) axle, which was the best among excellent chariots, the middle part of which was good (i.e. strong), which resembled the sky, which was full (i.e. well-equipped) with maces and iron-bars, which was as it were the ocean embodied, which had on it golden armlets, which was beautiful like the orb of the moon, which had banners and flag like the Mandara mountain with the Sun, the body of which was like the expanse of an elephant, which, at places, was bright like filaments of flowers, which had a thousand stars (studded to it), which was resounding like clouds with big showers, which was bright, and harmed the enemies’ chariots.

## \|\| 40.172-188 \|\|

*adhyatiṣṭhadraṇākāṃkṣī meruṃ dīptamivāṃśumān \|*  
*tārastu krośavistāramāyāme ca tathāvidham \|\| 140172 \|\|*

*śailakūbarasaṃkāśaṃ nīlāṃjanacayopamam \|*  
*kālalohasya ratnānāṃ samūhābaddhakūbaram \|\| 140173 \|\|*

*timirodgārakiraṇaṃ garjaṃtamiva toyadam \|*  
*lohajālena mahatā sagavākṣeṇa daṃśitam \|\| 140174 \|\|*

*āyasaiḥ parighaiḥ pūrṇaṃ kṣepaṇīyaiśca mudgaraiḥ \|*  
*prāsaiḥ pāśaiśca vitatairasaṃyuktaiśca kaṇṭakaiḥ \|\| 140175 \|\|*

*śobhitaṃ trāsanīyaiśca tomaraiḥ saparaśvadhaiḥ \|*  
*udyataṃ dviṣatāṃ hetordvitīyamiva maṃdaram \|\| 140176 \|\|*

*yuktaṃ kharasahasreṇa so'dhyārohadrathottamam \|*  
*virocanastu saṃkruddho gadāpāṇiravasthitaḥ \|\| 140177 \|\|*

*pramukhe tasya sainyasya dīptaśṛṃga ivācalaḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ hayasahasreṇa hayagrīvastu dānavaḥ \|\| 140178 \|\|*

*vyūhitaṃ dānavavyūhaṃ paricakrāma vīryavān \|*  
*vipracittisutaḥ śvetaḥ śvetakuṃḍalabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 140179 \|\|*

*syaṃdanaṃ vāhayāmāsa parānīkasya mardanaḥ \|*  
*vyāyataṃ kiṣkusāhasraṃ dhanurvisphārayanmahat \|\| 140180 \|\|*

*sa cāhavamukhe tasthau sapraroha ivācalaḥ \|*  
*kharastu viṣkirinkrodhānnetrābhyāṃ ropajaṃ jalam \|\| 140181 \|\|*

*sphuraddaṃtauṣṭhanayanaḥ saṃgrāmaṃ sobhyakāṃkṣata \|*  
*tvaṣṭā tvaṣṭādaśahayaṃ yānamāsthāya dānavaḥ \|\| 140182 \|\|*

*divyavyūhapratīkāśā yuddhāyābhimukhaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*ariṣṭo baliputraśca variṣṭho durdharāyudhaḥ \|\| 140183 \|\|*

*yuddhāyābhimukhastasthau dharādharavikaṃpanaḥ \|*  
*kiśorastvatisaṃharṣātkiśora iva coditaḥ \|\| 140184 \|\|*

*abhavaddaityamadhye sa grahamadhye yathā raviḥ \|*  
*laṃbastu navameghābhaḥ pralaṃbāṃbarabhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 140185 \|\|*

*daityavyūhagato bhāti sanīhāra ivāṃśumān \|*  
*vasuṃdharābhastadanu daśanauṣṭhekṣaṇāyudhaḥ \|\| 140186 \|\|*

*hasaṃstiṣṭhati daityānāmmadhye krūra mahāgrahaḥ \|*  
*anye hayagatāstatra mattebheṃdragatāḥ pare \|\| 140187 \|\|*

*siṃhavyāghragatāścānye varāharkṣeṣu cāpare \|*  
*kecitkharoṣṭrayātāraḥ kecittoyadavāhanāḥ \|\| 140188 \|\|*

172-177a. Tara also mounted upon an excellent chariot, the breadth of which was two miles, and which was like that (i.e. two miles) in length also, which resembled a rocky pole, which was like a heap of dark collyrium, to the pole of which a heap of black iron and gems was tied, which was full of (i.e. equipped with) iron bars, as well as with mallets that could be thrown, and with large darts and fetters, and with portions (i.e. pieces) of bamboos, which was decorated with fearful iron clubs with hatchets attached below, which was raised (i.e. lofty) like the Mandara for the sake of (the destuction of) enemies and to which a thousand asses were yoked.

177b-178a. And Virocana, who was angry and who had a mace in his hand, remained at the head of the army like a mountain with a radiant peak.

178b-179a. The powerful demon Hayagrīva went round the arrayed army, having a thousand horses, of the demons.

179b-18la. Vipracitti’s son Śveta, having white bracelets as his ornaments, the destroyer of the enemy’s army, stretching far his bow of the length of a thousand cubits, drove his chariot; and he stood at the head of the army like a mountain with a sprout.

181b-182a. Khara scattering (i.e. shedding) from his eyes water (i.e. tears)due to anger, with his teeth, lips and eyes throbbing, desired to fight.

182b-183a. Demon Tvaṣṭṛ having occupied a chariot to which eighteen horses were yoked, stood ready for battle facing the divine army.

183b-184a. Bali’s most distinguished son, Ariṣṭa, having invincible weapons, and causing the mountains to tremble, stood ready for the battle.

184b-185a. Kiśora, prompted by great joy like a young boy, remained in the midst of the demons as the Sun remains in the midst of planets.

185b-186a. Lamba, resembling a fresh cloud, and decorated with a long garment, remaining in the demons’ army, appeared like the Sun with fog.

186b-187a. After him Vasundharābha, laughing, and having missiles in the form of teeth, lips and eyes, stood among the demons like a cruel great planet.

187b-188. Others were seated upon horses; still others on intoxicated lordly elephants; others were seated on lions and tigers; others on bulls and bears, some were seated upon asses and camels and some were using clouds as their vehicles.

## \|\| 40.189 \|\|

*pattayaścāpare daityā bhīṣaṇā vikṛtānanāḥ \|*  
*ekapādāstvapādāśca nanṛturyuddhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|\| 140189 \|\|*

189\. Other demons, fearful and of deformed faces, were foot-soldiers. Desiring to fight, the one-legged ones and those with small legs, danced.

## \|\| 40.190 \|\|

*āsphoṭayaṃto bahavaḥ svanaṃtaśca tathāpare \|*  
*dṛptaśārdūlanirghoṣā nedurdānavapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 140190 \|\|*

190\. Many snapped their fingers, and others made a noise. Roaring like arrogant tigers the best demons thundered.

## \|\| 40.191 \|\|

*te gadāparighairghoraiḥ śilāmudgarapāṇayaḥ \|*  
*bāhubhiḥ parighākāraistarjayaṃti sma devatāḥ \|\| 140191 \|\|*

191\. They, having rocks and hammers in their hands threatened the gods with their fore-arms like iron-beams and with maces and fearful iron beams.

## \|\| 40.192-193 \|\|

*prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiśca pāśaiśca tomarāṃkuśapaṭṭiśaiḥ \|*  
*cikrīḍuste śataghnībhiḥ śatadhāraiśca mudgaraiḥ \|\| 140192 \|\|*

*khaḍgaśailaiśca śailaiśca parighaiścodyatāyudhaiḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ balāhakagaṇaiḥ sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaṃ nabhaḥ \|\| 140193 \|\|*

192-193a. They sported with the weapons used as missiles, with mallets having a hundred edges, with rock-like swords, with iron beams and raised weapons.

193b. The sky was covered everywhere with multitudes of clouds.

## \|\| 40.194 \|\|

*evaṃ taddānavaṃ sainyaṃ sarvasatvamadotkaṭam \|*  
*devatābhimukhaṃ tasthau meghānīkamivoditam \|\| 140194 \|\|*

194\. Thus the army of the demons, furious with spirit and madness, stood before the gods like a host of clouds that had come up (in the sky).

## \|\| 40.195 \|\|

*reje ca taddaityasahasragāḍhaṃ vāyvagniśailāṃbudatoyakalpam \|*  
*balaṃ balaughākulamabhyudīrṇaṃ yuyutsayonmattamivā babhāse \|\| 140195 \|\|*

195\. And that army shone with thousands of demons pressed closely to one another, resembling wind, fire, mountain, clouds and water. That army elated because of being full with multitudes of troops, appeared to be mad with the desire to fight.

## \|\| 40.196 \|\|

*śrutaste daityasainyasya vistāraḥ kurunaṃdana \|*  
*surāṇāmapi sainyasya vistaraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 140196 \|\|*

196\. O you descendant of Kuru, you have listened to the expanse of the army of the demons. Now listen to the expanse of the army of the gods led by Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 41 - The Rise of the Lotus and the War between Gods &amp; Demons

## \|\| 41.1 \|\|

*pulastya uvāca \|*  
*ādityā vasavo rudrā aśvinau ca mahābalau \|*  
*sabalāḥ sānugāścaiva saṃnahyanta yathākramam \|\| 1 \|\|*

Pulastya said:

1\. The Ādityas, the Vasus, the two mighty Aśvins got ready for battle with their troops and followers in due order.

## \|\| 41.2 \|\|

*puruhūtaśca purato lokapālaḥ sahasradṛk \|*  
*grāmaṇīḥ sarvadevānāmāruroha varadvipam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The thousand-eyed Indra, the guardian of the worlds and the leader of gods mounted on an excellent elephant.

## \|\| 41.3-7 \|\|

*savye cāsya rathaḥ pārśve pakṣipravaraketanaḥ \|*  
*surārucakracaraṇo haimacchatrapariṣkṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*devagaṃdharvayakṣaughairanuyātaḥ sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*dīptimadbhiśca svargasthairbrahmarṣibhirabhiṣṭutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vajravisphāritodbhūtairvidyudiṃdrāyudhaprabhaiḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ balāhakagaṇaiḥ parvatairiva kāmagaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yamārūḍhaḥ sa bhagavānparyeti sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*havirdāneṣu gāyaṃti viprā makhamukhesthitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*svargasaṃgrāmayāteṣu devatūryaninādiṣu \|*  
*seṃdraṃ tamupanṛtyaṃti śataśo hyapsarogaṇāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-6a. To his right stood the chariot, which had the best bird (i.e. Garuḍa) as its banner; which moved on very fine wheels; which was adorned with a golden umbrella; which was followed by the multitudes of gods, Gandharvas and Yakṣas in thousands; which was eulogised by brahmanic brilliant sages living in heaven; having mounted upon which chariot, furnished with multitudes of clouds having the lustre of lightning and rain-bow risen due to the vibration of the thunderbolt, and resembling mountains moving according to their will, the lord moves in the entire world.

6b-7. The brāhmaṇas remaining at the front of a sacrifice sing at the (time of the) presentation of oblations. Hundreds of groups of celestial nymphs dance by him accompanied by Indra when the sounds of the trumpets of gods were (heard) at the heavenly battle.

## \|\| 41.8-9 \|\|

*ketunā nāgarājena rājamāno yathā raviḥ \|*  
*yukto hayasahasreṇa manomārutaraṃhasā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samyagrathavaro bhāti yukto mātalinā tadā \|*  
*kṛtsnaḥ parivṛto merurbhāskarasyeva tejasā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The best chariot which was at that time occupied by Mātalin, to which a thousand horses, having the speed of the mind and the wind, were yoked, shone, like the Sun, with the banner of the lord of serpents; (it shone) like the Meru mountain which is fully covered with the Sun’s lustre.

## \|\| 41.10 \|\|

*yamastu daṃḍamudyamya kālayuktaṃ ca mudgaraṃ \|*  
*tasthau suragaṇānīke daityānāṃ caiva darśayan \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. And Yama, raising his staff and his fatal mallet and displaying them to the demons, stood in the army of gods.

## \|\| 41.11-14 \|\|

*caturbhiḥ sāgarairyukto lelihānaiśca pannagaiḥ \|*  
*śaṃkhamuktāṃgadadharo bibhrattoyamayaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kālapāśānsamāvidhya hayaiḥ śaśikaropamaiḥ \|*  
*vāyvīritajalākāraiḥ kurvanlīlāḥ sahasraśaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pāṃḍuroddhūtavasanaḥ pravālarucirāṃgadaḥ \|*  
*maṇiśyāmottamavapurhārakeṇārcitodaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*varuṇaḥ pāśadhṛṅmadhye devānīkasya tasthivān \|*  
*yuddhavelāmabhilaṣanbhinnavela ivārṇavaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Varuṇa, who held the nooses, who was accompanied by four oceans and the repeatedly licking snakes, who had put on ornaments of conches and pearls, who possessed a watery body, who had held together his fatal nooses, who wore excellent white garments and coral ornaments, who had an excellent body brown with gems, who indulged in thousands of sports with his horses of a watery appearance and resembling the moon and being impelled by the wind, remained in the gods’ army, desiring (i.e. waiting for) the time to fight, (looking) like the ocean that had broken the coast.

## \|\| 41.15-16 \|\|

*yakṣarākṣasasainyena guhyakānāṃ gaṇairapi \|*  
*yuktaśca śaṃkhapadmābhyāṃ nidhīnāmadhipaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rājarājeśvaraḥśrīmāngadāpāṇiradṛśyata \|*  
*vimānayodhī dhanado vimāne puṣpake sthitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Dhanada (i.e. Kubera), accompanied by the army of Yakṣas and demons, and by the hosts of Guhyakas, endowed with a conch and a lotus, who was the lord of treasures, and king of kings, possessed of prosperity and holding a mace in his hand, and fighting by remaining in an aeroplane, was seen there seated in the Puṣpaka.

## \|\| 41.17-20 \|\|

*sa rājarājaḥ śuśubhe yakṣeśo naravāhanaḥ \|*  
*pūrvapakṣe sahasrākṣaḥ pitṛrājaśca dakṣiṇe \|\| 17 \|\|*

*varuṇaḥ paścime pakṣa uttare naravāhanaḥ \|*  
*catuḥpakṣāśca cattvāro lokapālā mahābalāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ātmadikṣucaraṃtaścatasyadevabalasyate \|*  
*sūryaḥ saptāśvayuktena rathenānilagāminā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śriyā jājvalyamānena dīpyamānaiśca raśmibhiḥ \|*  
*udayāstamayau cakre meruparyantagāminā \|\| 20 \|\|*

17a. He i.e. Kubera, the king of kings, the lord of Yakṣas, shone (there).

17b-18a. Indra remained in the eastern wing, Yama in the southern, Varuṇa in the western and Kubera in the northern wing (of the army).

18b-19a. The very mighty four regents of quarters remaining in the four wings moved in their respective regions of that army of gods.

19b-20. The Sun, moving in a chariot to which seven horses were yoked, which was moving like the wind, which was resplendent with beauty, and which was shining with rays, and which went to the skirt of Meru, rose and set (i.e. went up and down).

## \|\| 41.21-35 \|\|

*tridiva dvāracakreṇa tapasā lokamavyayam \|*  
*sahasraraśmiyuktena bhrājamānena tejasā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*cacāra madhye devānāṃ dvādaśātmā divākaraḥ \|*  
*somaḥ śvetahayo bhāti syaṃdane śītaraśmimān \|\| 22 \|\|*

*himatoyaprapūrṇābhirbhābhirāhlādayañjagat \|*  
*tamṛkṣayogānugataṃ śiśirāṃśuṃ dvijeśvaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śaśacchāyāṃkitatanuṃ naiśasya tamasaḥ kṣayam \|*  
*jyotiṣāmīśvaraṃ vyomni rasadaṃ prabhumavyayam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*oṣadhīnāṃ pavitrāṇāṃ nidhānamamṛtasya ca \|*  
*jagataḥ paramaṃ bhāgaṃ saumyaṃ sarvamayaṃ rasam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dadṛśurdānavāḥ somaṃ himapraharaṇaṃ sthitam \|*  
*yaḥ prāṇaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ paṃcadhā bhidyate nṛṣu \|\| 26 \|\|*

*saptaskaṃdhagato lokāṃstrīndadhāra cakāra ca \|*  
*yamāhuragnikarttāraṃ sarvaprabhavamīśvaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saptasvaragatā yasya yonirgīrbhirudīryate \|*  
*yaṃ vadaṃti calaṃ bhūtaṃ yaṃ vadaṃtyaśarīriṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yamāhurākāśagamaṃ śīghragaṃ śabdayonijam \|*  
*sa vāyuḥ sarvabhūtāyuruddhataḥ svena tejasā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vavau pravyathayandaityānpratilomaṃ satoyadaḥ \|*  
*māruto devagaṃdharvairvidyādharagaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 30 \|\|*

*cikrīḍa raśmibhiśśubhrairnirmuktairiva pannagaiḥ \|*  
*sṛjaṃtaḥ sarpapatayastīvraṃ roṣamayaṃ viṣam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śarabhūtā vilagnāśca cerurvyāttānanā divi \|*  
*parvatāśca śilāśṛṃgaiḥ śataśākhaiśca pādapaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*upatasthuḥ suragaṇānprahartuṃ dānavaṃ balam \|*  
*yaḥ sa devo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābhastrivikramaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yugāṃte kṛṣṇavartmā ca viśvasya jagataḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*sarvayoniḥ samadhuhā havyabhukkratusaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhūmyambuvyomabhūtātmā śyāmaḥ śāṃtikarorihā \|*  
*avighnamamarādīnāṃ cakre cakragadādharaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

21-22a. The Sun, of twelve forms, heating the unchangeable world with heat by means of the orb at the gate of the heaven which had a thousand rays and which had illuminating lustre, moved among the gods.

22b-23a. Soma (i.e. the Moon), of white horses, having cool rays, delighting the world with lustre full of cool water, shines (i.e. shone) in his chariot.

23b-26a. The demons saw that Soma, who was accompanied by Stars, whose rays were cool, who was the lord of brāhmaṇas, whose form was marked with the shadow of a hare, who removed the nocturnal darkness, who was the lord of the Stars in the sky, who gave nectar, who was the immutable lord, who was the store of pure herbs and of nectar, who was the great lot of the world, who was agreeable, who was full of nectar, who had the snow-weapon, and who remained (in his chariot).

26b-30a. The Wind, that is the life of the beings, and has divided himself into five in men (i.e. remains in five forms in the bodies of men), who went along seven tracts, who supports and has fashioned the three worlds, whom they call Agni, the creator of the worlds, and the lord, the source of all, whose origin, found in the seven notes (of the gamut), is proclaimed by words, whom they describe as a moving element and as one having no body, whom they call as moving in the sky, as quick moving, and as being produced from the source of sound, who is the life of all beings, who was stirred up by his own lustre, blew, with clouds, in a hostile manner and troubled the Daityas.

30b-31a. The Wind, along with the gods, Gandharvas, and hosts of Vidyādharas, sported with the rays white like serpents that had lately cast their skins.

31b-32a. Lords of serpents, producing strong poison of wrath, being thin and turning themselves into arrows and with their mouths wide open moved (there).

32b-33a. The mountains also stood with their rocky peaks and trees having hundred branches, by the gods in order to strike the army of the demons.

33b-35. He, god Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha, Trivikrama, who is the fire at the end of the yuga, who is the lord of the entire world, who is the source of all, who killed (the demon) Madhu, who enjoys the oblations, who is the soul of the elements like earth, water and ether, who is dark, who brings about peace, who kills the enemies, who holds the mace and the disc, getting well-settled, caused absence of danger among the gods and others.

## \|\| 41.36-37 \|\|

*savyenālabhya mahatīṃ sarvāyudhavināśinīṃ \|*  
*kareṇa kālīṃ vapuṣā śatrukālapradāṃ gadāṃ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śeṣairbhujaiḥ pradīptābhairbhujagāridhvajaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*dadhārāyudhajālāni śārṅgādīni mahābalaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The very powerful lord, having the enemy of the serpents (i.e. Garuḍa) as his banner, held, in his right hand, the great mace, destroying all weapons, fatal in nature and bringing destruction to the enemies, and held in his other bright hands, the multitudes of other weapons like (his bow) Śārṅga etc.

## \|\| 41.38-47 \|\|

*sa kaśyapasyātmabhavaṃ dvijaṃ bhujagabhojanam \|*  
*bhujageṃdreṇa vadane niviṣṭena virājitam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*amṛtāraṃbhasaṃyuktaṃ maṃdarādrimivocchitam \|*  
*devāsuravimardeṣu bahuśo dṛṣṭavikramam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*maheṃdreṇāmṛtasyārthe vajreṇa kṛtalakṣaṇam \|*  
*vicitrapatravasanaṃ dhātumaṃtamivācalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*sphītakrodhāvalaṃbena śītāṃśusamatejasā \|*  
*bhogibhogāvasaktena maṇiratnena bhāsvatā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pakṣābhyāṃ cārupatrābhyāmāvṛtaṃ divi līlayā \|*  
*yugāṃte seṃdracāpābhyāṃ toyadābhyāmivāṃbaram \|\| 42 \|\|*

*nīlalohitapītābhiḥ patākābhiralaṃkṛtam \|*  
*aruṇāvarajaṃ śrīmānāruhya samare prabhuḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*suvarṇavarṇavapuṣaṃ suparṇaṃ khecarottamam \|*  
*tamanvayuḥ suragaṇā munayaśca samāhitāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*gīrbhiḥ paramamaṃtrābhistuṣṭuvuśca gadādharam \|*  
*tadvaiśravaṇasaṃśliṣṭaṃ vaivasvatapuraḥsaram \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vārirājaparikṣiptaṃ devarājavirājitam \|*  
*pavanābaddhanirghoṣaṃ saṃpradīpta hutāśanam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*viṣṇorjiṣṇoḥ sahiṣṇośca bhrājiṣṇostejasāvṛtam \|*  
*balaṃ balavadudrikte yuddhāya samavartata \|\| 47 \|\|*

38-44a. On the battlefield, the lord, having mounted upon the best bird (i.e. Garuḍa), who was the offspring of Kaśyapa, who was the younger brother of Aruṇa, who had serpents as his food, who shone with the lord of serpents put into his mouth, who was (formerly) connected with the activity of (carrying) nectar, who was lofty like Mandara, whose valour was many times seen in the war between gods and demons, who was used like the thunderbolt for (securing) the nectar by Indra, who had put on a garment in the form of variegated wings, who was like a mountain full of minerals, who was, in the sky, covered beautifully with the brightest gem with its lustre like the moon and (as it were) a prop of increased wrath, adhering to the hood of a serpent, and with two wings having charming feathers, like the sky being covered with two clouds with the rainbow, at the time of the destruction of the world, who was adorned with dark and reddish banners, whose wings were golden (was ready to fight).

44b-45a. All the hosts of gods and sages, calm in mind, followed him and praised the mace-holder with words couching great sacred texts.

45b-47. That mighty army of Viṣṇu, who was victorious, who was tolerant and bright, (the army) which was joined by Kubera, led by Yama, encircled by Varuṇa, adorned by the lord of gods, in which great sound was made by Vāyu, which was blazing with Agni was arranged for the battle.

## \|\| 41.48 \|\|

*svastyastu devebhya iti bṛhaspatirabhāṣata \|*  
*svastyastu daityebhya iti uśanā vākyamādade \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Bṛhaspati said: “Well-being to the gods.” Uśanas (i.e. Śukra) said these words: “Well-being to the demons”.

## \|\| 41.49 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ balābhyāṃ saṃjajñe tumulo vigrahastathā \|*  
*surāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca parasparajayaiṣiṇām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Then a fierce battle took place between the two armies of gods and demons who were desirous of conquering each other.

## \|\| 41.50 \|\|

*dānavā daivataiḥ sārddhaṃ nānāpraharaṇodyamāḥ \|*  
*samīyuryudhyamānā vai parvatā iva parvataiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The demons, with many weapons raised, went to fight with the gods, like mountains with mountains.

## \|\| 41.51 \|\|

*tatsurāsurasaṃyuktaṃ yuddhamatyadbhutaṃ babhau \|*  
*dharmādharmasamāyuktaṃ darpeṇa vinayena ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. That was a very wonderful fight between the gods and the demons, charged with piety and impiety and pride and politeness.

## \|\| 41.52-54 \|\|

*tato hayaiḥ prajavitairvāraṇaiśca pracoditaiḥ \|*  
*utpatadbhiśca gagane sāsihastaiḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kṣipyamāṇaiśca musalaiḥ saṃpatadbhiśca sāyakaiḥ \|*  
*cāpairvisphāryamāṇaiśca pātyamānaiḥ sudāruṇaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tadyuddhamabhavadghoraṃ devadānavasaṃkulam \|*  
*jagatastrāsajananaṃ yugasaṃvartakopamam \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. Then with the very speedy horses, and with elephants that were goaded, and with warriors having swords in their hands and jumping, with pestles being thrown, with falling arrows, with stretched bows, and with very fearful missiles being dropped, that battle, in which gods and demons had crowded, and which produced fear to the world and which resembled the fire of destruction, took place.

## \|\| 41.55 \|\|

*svahastamuktaiḥ parighairmudgaraiścaiva parvataiḥ \|*  
*dānavāssamare jaghnurdevāniṃdrapurogamān \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The demons struck the gods led by Indra in the battle with iron bars, mallets and rocks.

## \|\| 41.56 \|\|

*te vadhyamānā balibhirdānavairjitakāśibhiḥ \|*  
*viṣaṇṇavadanā devā jagmurārtiṃ parāṃ mṛdhe \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. The gods, who were being killed by the strong demons behaving like conquerors, whose faces were dejected, were very much afflicted in the war..

## \|\| 41.57-58 \|\|

*te cāstraśūlamathitāḥ parighairbhinnamastakāḥ \|*  
*bhinnoraskā ditisutaiḥ sravadraktā raṇe bahu \|\| 57 \|\|*

*sūditāḥ śarajālaiśca niryatnāśca śaraiḥ kṛtāḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭā dānavīṃ māyāṃ na śekuste viceṣṭitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. They, crushed down by missiles and spears, and with their heads broken with iron bars, with their chests pierced by the sons of Diti (i.e. the demons), and bleeding profusely, were killed with volleys of arrows; their exertion was rendered useless, and getting (caught) into the illusion of the demons, they were unable to move.

## \|\| 41.59 \|\|

*uttaṃbhitamivābhāti niṣprāṇa sadṛśākṛti \|*  
*balaṃ surāṇāmasurairniṣprayatnāyudhaṃ kṛtam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. The exertion of the army of the gods which as it were appeared to be arrested by the demons and which was (almost) lifeless, was rendered useless by the demons.

## \|\| 41.60 \|\|

*daityacāpacyutānghorāṃśchitvā vajreṇa tānśarān \|*  
*śakro daityabalaṃ ghoraṃ viveśa bahulocanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Indra, of many (i.e. a thousand) eyes, cutting off the terrible arrows discharged from the bows of the demons, entered the fierce army of the demons.

## \|\| 41.61 \|\|

*sa daityapramukhānsarvānhatvā daityabalaṃ mahat \|*  
*tāmasenāstrajālena tamobhūtamathākarot \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. He, having killed all important demons rendered the army of the demons covered with darkness by a multitude of darkening missiles.

## \|\| 41.62 \|\|

*te'nyonyaṃ nānvabudhyaṃta daityānāṃ vāhanāni ca \|*  
*ghoreṇa tamasāviṣṭāḥ puruhūtasya tejasā \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. They, overpowered by darkness due to the prowess of Indra, did not recognize one another nor the vehicles of demons.

## \|\| 41.63 \|\|

*māyāpāśairvimuktāstu yatnavaṃtaḥ surottamāḥ \|*  
*śirāṃsi daityasaṃghānāṃ tamobhūtānyapātayan \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. The gods, freed from the nooses of illusion, exerted, and felled (on the ground) the heads of the hosts of demons which were (covered with) darkness.

## \|\| 41.64 \|\|

*apadhvastā visaṃjñāśca tamasā nīlavarcasā \|*  
*petuste dānavāssadyaśchinnapakṣā ivādrayaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. The wretched demons, who became unconscious due to the darkness of a black colour, instantly fell down like mountains with their wings cut off.

## \|\| 41.65 \|\|

*tatrābhibhūtadaityaiṃdramaṃdhakāramivāṃtaraṃ \|*  
*dānavaṃ dehasadanaṃ tamobhūtamivābhavat \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. There (i.e. on the battlefield) the body of the lord of demons, who was overcome (with darkness) was, as it were, full of internal darkness.

## \|\| 41.66 \|\|

*tathā'sṛjanmahāmāyāṃ mayastāṃ tāmasīṃ dahan \|*  
*yugāṃtodyotajananīṃ sṛṣṭā maurveṇa vahninā \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Maya, burning the illusion (produced by gods) produced a great illusion like the one at the time of the destruction of the world produced by the Aurva fire.

## \|\| 41.67 \|\|

*sa dadāha ca tāṃ śākrīṃ māyā mayavikalpitā \|*  
*daityāścādityavapuṣā sadya uttasthurāhave \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. That illusion produced by Maya burnt the illusion created by Indra; and the demons instantly rose (taking up) the forms ofgods in the battle.

## \|\| 41.68 \|\|

*māyāṃ maurvīṃ samāsādya dahyamānā divaukasaḥ \|*  
*bhejire caṃdraviṣayaṃ śītāṃśusalilahradam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Reaching (i.e. being covered by) the Aurvī illusion, the gods being burnt (by the fire produced by it) resorted to the pond of water cool (with) the rays of the moon on the region of tbe moon.

## \|\| 41.69 \|\|

*te dahyamānā aurveṇa vahninā naṣṭacetasaḥ \|*  
*śaśaṃsurvajriṇaṃ devāḥ saṃtaptāḥ śaraṇaiṣiṇaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The gods, being burnt by that Aurva fire and being insensible and afflicted, seeking the refuge of Indra, praised him.

## \|\| 41.70 \|\|

*saṃtapte māyayā sainye hanyamāne ca dānavaiḥ \|*  
*codito devarājena varuṇo vākyamabravīt \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. When the army (of gods) was (thus) distressed and was being killed by the demons, Varuṇa, impelled by the lord of gods, said (these) words:

## \|\| 41.71 \|\|

*purā brahmarṣijaḥ śakra tapastepe sudāruṇam \|*  
*urvaḥ sa pūrvaṃ tejasvī sadṛśo brahmaṇo guṇaiḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

Varuṇa said:

71\. O Indra, formerly, Urva the son of a brāhmaṇic sage, and bright due to qualities similar to those of Brahman, practised a very severe penance.

## \|\| 41.72 \|\|

*taṃ tapaṃtamivādityaṃ tapasā jagadavyayaṃ \|*  
*upatasthurmunigaṇā devā devarṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. Hosts of sages and gods with divine sages approached him, who was as it were tormenting the world with his penance, like the sun.

## \|\| 41.73 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipuścaiva dānavo dānaveśvaraḥ \|*  
*ṝṣiṃ vijñāpayāmāsa purā paramatejasam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. The demon, Hiraṇyakaśipu, the lord of demons, also formerly requested that sage (Urva) of a great lustre.

## \|\| 41.74-75 \|\|

*ūcurbrahmarṣayaste tu vacanaṃ dharmasaṃhitam \|*  
*ṝṣivaṃśeṣu bhagavaṃśchinnamūlamidaṃ kulaṃ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*ekastvamanapatyaśca gotrā yā'nyo na vidyate \|*  
*kaumāraṃ vratamāsthāya kleśamevānuvartase \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. The brāhmaṇic sages spoke words conforming to dharma: “O revered sir, this family has its root cut off among the families of sages. You are all alone, without a child. There is on one else (to continue) the family. Practising the vow of abstinence you are following (i.e. suffering from) affliction only.”

## \|\| 41.76-78 \|\|

*bahūni vipragotrāṇi munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām \|*  
*ekadehāni tiṣṭhaṃti viviktāni vinā prajāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*evaṃbhūteṣu sarveṣu putrairme nāsti kāraṇam \|*  
*bhavāṃśca tāpasaśreṣṭhaḥ prajāpati samadyutiḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tatpravartasva vaṃśāya vardhayātmānamātmanā \|*  
*samādhatsvorjitaṃ tejo dvitīyāṃ kuru vai tanuṃ \|\| 78 \|\|*

76-77a. “Many brāhmaṇa families, those of sages of purified souls remain all alone and secluded and without progeny. When all of them are like that, I have nothing to do with sons.”

77b-78. “You are the best among ascetics and are bright like the creator. Therefore proceed to continue your family and multiply your self by yourself. Put together your mighty lustre and make your body a second (i.e. generate a son)”.

## \|\| 41.79 \|\|

*sa evamukto munibhirmunirmanasi tāḍitaḥ \|*  
*jagarha tānṛṣigaṇānvacanaṃ cedamabravīt \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The sage thus addressed by the sages being hurt in the mind censured all those and said these words to them:

## \|\| 41.80-81 \|\|

*yathā hi vihito dharmo munīnāṃ śāśvataḥ purā \|*  
*ārṣaṃ hi kevalaṃ karma vanyamūlaphalāśinaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*brahmayonau prasūtasya brāhmaṇasyātmavartinaḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ sucaritaṃ brahmāṇamapi cālayet \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. “As the eternal duty of the sages, it was laid down formerly that the only duty approved by seers, of a brāhmaṇa who eats (i.e. subsists on) wild roots and fruits, and who is born in a brāhmaṇa family and who lives by himself, (is celibacy). If celibacy is well-practised it would even move Brahmā.

## \|\| 41.82-83 \|\|

*janānāṃ vṛttayastisro ye gṛhāśramavāsinaḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ ca vane vṛttirvanāśramanivāsināṃ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāśca daṃtolūkhalinastathā \|*  
*aśmakuṭṭādayo yatra paṃcāgnitapasaśca ye \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. There are three courses of conduct of people: (One is that of those) who live as householders; (there is another) of those like us who live in the forest; and those who live in hermitages, eating (i.e. drinking) water, eating (i.e. living on) air, using their teeth as the mortar (i.e. the anchorites) and those who break things on stones, and there is the one of those who practise penance with five fires.

## \|\| 41.84 \|\|

*ete tapasi tiṣṭhaṃto vratairapi suduścaraiḥ \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ puraskṛtya prārthayaṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. These remaining in penance, and giving importance to celibacy (by performing) vows very difficult to perform, desire the highest position.

## \|\| 41.85 \|\|

*brahmacaryādbrahmaṇasya brāhmaṇatvaṃ vidhīyate \|*  
*evamāhuḥ pare loke brāhmacaryavido janāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. The brāhmaṇa-hood of a brāhmaṇa is occasioned by (i.e. is due to) his celibacy. This is what people knowing (the importance of) celibacy say in the other world.

## \|\| 41.86 \|\|

*brahmacarye sthito dharmo brahmacarye sthitaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*ye sthitā brahmacarye tu brāhmaṇā divi te sthitāḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Piety resides in celibacy; penance resides in celibacy. Those brāhmaṇas who remain in celibacy, reside in heaven.

## \|\| 41.87 \|\|

*nāsti yogaṃ vinā siddhirnāsti yogaṃ vinā yaśaḥ \|*  
*nāsti loke yaśomūlaṃ brahmacaryātparaṃtapaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Perfection is not possible without yoga (deep and abstract meditation); glory is not possible without yoga. O you tormentor of the enemies in this world, there is no better means of glory than austerity (in the form of) celibacy.

## \|\| 41.88 \|\|

*yo nigṛhyeṃdriyagrāmaṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ ca paṃcakam \|*  
*brahmacaryaṃ samādhatte kimataḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. For him, who restrains the group of the organs of sense and the group of the five elements, and concentrates on celibacy what greater penance than that is there?

## \|\| 41.89 \|\|

*ayogakeśadharaṇamasaṃkalpa vrata kriyā \|*  
*abrahmacaryā caryā ca trayaṃ syāddaṃbhasaṃjñitaṃ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. Having (i.e. growing) hair without yoga (a deep and abstract meditation), performing a vow without (proper) volition and religious mendicant’s life without celibacy—these three are called religious hypocrisy.

## \|\| 41.90 \|\|

*kva dārāḥ kva ca saṃyogaḥ kva ca bhāvaviparyayaḥ \|*  
*nanviyaṃ brahmaṇā sṛṣṭā manasā mānasī prajā \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. Where is (the need of) a wife and of union (with her)? Where again is the need of the perverse (i.e. unnatural) condition (viz. that of a householder etc.)? Indeed these mind-born offsprings were created by Brahmā with his mind.

## \|\| 41.91 \|\|

*yadyasti tapaso vīryaṃ yuṣmākaṃ vijitātmanām \|*  
*sṛjadhvaṃ mānasānputrānprājāpatyena karmaṇā \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. If you, who are self-subdued, have the power of penance then by the act like that of Brahmā, create mind-born sons.

## \|\| 41.92 \|\|

*manasā nirmitā yonirādhātavyā tapasvibhiḥ \|*  
*no dārayogaṃ bījaṃ ca vratamuktaṃ tapasvināṃ \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. The ascetics should have mentally produced offspring. There is no union with a wife, no (depositing of) seed (i.e. semen)—this is said to be a vow of the ascetics.

## \|\| 41.93 \|\|

*yadidaṃ luptadharmākhyaṃ yuṣmābhiriha nirbhayaiḥ \|*  
*vyāhṛtaṃ sadbhiratyarthamasadbhiriva saṃmataṃ \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. What you, the good and fearless persons have said here, is indeed like that which is very much liked by bad persons.

## \|\| 41.94 \|\|

*vapurdīptāṃtarātmānameṣa kṛtvā manomayaṃ \|*  
*dārayogaṃ vinā srakṣye putramātmatanūruhaṃ \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. This I, making by body blazing with the soul, will produce a mind (-born) son without copulation with a wife.

## \|\| 41.95 \|\|

*evamātmānamātmā me dvitīyaṃ janayiṣyati \|*  
*prājāpatyena vidhinā didhakṣaṃtamiva prajāḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Thus, with the act like that of the creator my soul (i.e. I) will produce another self (i.e. a son), as itwere desiring to burn the beings”.

## \|\| 41.96 \|\|

*varuṇa uvāca \|*  
*urvastu tapasāviṣṭo niveśyoruṃ hutāśane \|*  
*mamaṃthaikena darbheṇa putrasya prasavāraṇiṃ \|\| 96 \|\|*

Varuṇa said:

96\. (Then) Urva engrossed in penance, put his thigh into the fire, and shook with one darbha the fire-producing wooden stick (for) generating a son.

## \|\| 41.97 \|\|

*tasyoruṃ sahasā bhitvā varo'sau hyagnirutthitaḥ \|*  
*jagato dahanākāṃkṣī putrognissamapadyata \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Suddenly breaking his thigh, an excellent fire came up. The son—the fire, became desirous of burning the world.

## \|\| 41.98 \|\|

*urvasyoruṃ vinirbhidya aurvo nāmāṃtako'nalaḥ \|*  
*didhakṣuriva lokāṃstrīnjajñe paramakopanaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Breaking open the thigh of Urva a destructive fire called Aurva, very angry and as it were desiring to burn the three worlds, was produced.

## \|\| 41.99 \|\|

*utpadyamānaścovāca pitaraṃ dīnayā girā \|*  
*kṣudhā me bādhate tāta jagadbhakṣetyajasva māṃ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. While being produced he said to his father in piteous words: “O father, hunger is oppressing me; I shall swallow the world; leave me.”

## \|\| 41.100 \|\|

*tridivārohibhirjvālairjṛmbhamāṇo diśo daśa \|*  
*nirdahansarvabhūtāni vavṛdhe soṃtakopamaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. He, resembling Yama, spreading in the ten quarters with his flames going up to the heaven, and consuming all beings, grew.

## \|\| 41.101-102 \|\|

*etasminnaṃtare brahmā munimurvaṃ samāgataḥ \|*  
*uvāca vāryatāṃ putro jagatastvaṃ dayāṃ kuru \|\| 101 \|\|*

*asyāpatpasyate vipra kariṣye sāhyamuttamaṃ \|*  
*tathyametadvacaḥ putra śṛṇu tvaṃ vadatāṃ vara \|\| 102 \|\|*

101-102. In the meanwhile, Brahmā came to the sage Urva, and said (to him): “(Please) ward off your son; show pity for the world. O brāhmaṇa, I shall give excellent help to this your son. O you son, O you best among the speakers, listen to these true words of me.”

## \|\| 41.103 \|\|

*aurva uvāca \|*  
*dhanyosmyanugṛhītosmi yanme tvaṃ bhagavanśiśoḥ \|*  
*matimetāṃ dadāsīha paramātmanhitāya vai \|\| 103 \|\|*

Aurva said:

103\. I am blessed, I am favoured that you, revered sir, O highest soul, are giving this idea to this child (viz. me).

## \|\| 41.104 \|\|

*prabhātakāle saṃprāpte kāṃkṣitavye samāgame \|*  
*bhagavaṃstarpitaḥ putraḥ kairhavyaiḥ prāpsyate sukham \|\| 104 \|\|*

104\. When the morning time has arrived, and when his association is to be desired, revered sir, satisfied with what oblations would my son obtain happiness?

## \|\| 41.105 \|\|

*kutra cāsya nivāsaḥ syādbhojanaṃ tu kimātmakam \|*  
*vidhāsyatīha bhagavānvīryatulyaṃ mahaujasaḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Where will be his residence? What will be the nature of the mighty food of him of great lustre that the lord will give?

## \|\| 41.106 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*baḍavāmukhe ca vasatiḥ samudre vai bhaviṣyati \|*  
*mamayonirjalaṃ vipra taccāmeyaṃ vrajatvayaṃ \|\| 106 \|\|*

Brahma said:

106\. His residence will be in the mare’s mouth in the ocean. O brāhmaṇa, my source is water that is immeasurable. Let him go there.

## \|\| 41.107 \|\|

*tatrā'yamāste niyataṃ pibanvārimayaṃ haviḥ \|*  
*tadvārivistaraṃ vipra visṛjāmyālayaṃ ca tam \|\| 107 \|\|*

107\. There he will certainly live, drinking the oblation of the form of water. I am giving him that residence, viz. that expanse of water (i.e. the ocean).

## \|\| 41.108 \|\|

*tato yugāṃte bhūtānāmeṣa cāhaṃ ca putraka \|*  
*sahito vicariṣyāvo niṣpurāṇakarāviha \|\| 108 \|\|*

108\. Then, O son, he and I removing things of the past will move together at the end of the Yuga.

## \|\| 41.109 \|\|

*eṣogniraṃtakāle tu salilāśī mayā kṛtaḥ \|*  
*dahanaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sadevāsurarakṣasām \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. This fire, who is made by me to eat (i.e. subsist on) water, will, at the time of the deluge, burn all being along with the demons and goblins.

## \|\| 41.110 \|\|

*evamastviti taṃ sogniḥ saṃvṛtajvālamaṃḍalaḥ \|*  
*praviveśārṇavamukhaṃ natvorvaṃ pitaraṃ prabhum \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. Saying, “Let it be so”, that fire, having suppressed the circle of flames, entered the mouth of the ocean and not his father, the lord, viz. Urva.

## \|\| 41.111 \|\|

*pratiyātastato brahmā te ca sarve maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*aurvasyāgneḥ prabhāvajñāḥ svāṃsvāṃ gatimupāgatāḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Then Brahmā returned, and also the great sages. Knowing the prowess of the fire Aurva they took their respective courses.

## \|\| 41.112 \|\|

*hiraṇyakaśipurdṛṣṭvā tadā tanmahadadbhutam \|*  
*urvaṃ praṇatasarvāṃgo vākyametaduvāca ha \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. Then, seeing that great wonder, Hiraṇyakaśipu, saluting Urva by touching the ground with all the limbs of his body (i.e. prostrating himself before Urva), said these words (to him):

## \|\| 41.113 \|\|

*bhagavannadbhutamidaṃ saṃvṛttaṃ lokasākṣikam \|*  
*tapasā te muniśreṣṭha parituṣṭaḥ pitāmahaḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. “O revered sir, this wonder has taken place in the presence of the world. O greatest sage, the grandsire is quite pleased with your penance.

## \|\| 41.114 \|\|

*ahaṃ tu tava putrasya tava caiva mahāvrata \|*  
*bhṛtya ityavagaṃtavyaḥ ślāghyastvamiha karmaṇā \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. O you of a great vow, I should be looked upon as the servant of your son and you. You are fit to be praised due to (your having done) this deed.

## \|\| 41.115 \|\|

*tanmāṃ paśya samāpannaṃ tavaivārādhane ratam \|*  
*yadi sīdenmuniśreṣṭha tavai vasyātparājayaḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Then see me to be distressed and engaged in propitiating you. If, O greatest sage, I sink into distress, that would be your defeat.”

## \|\| 41.116 \|\|

*urva uvāca \|*  
*dhanyosmyanugṛhītosmi yasya te'haṃ gururmataḥ \|*  
*nāsti te tapasānena bhayaṃ caiveha suvrata \|\| 116 \|\|*

Urva said:

116\. I am blessed, I am favoured since you have looked upon me as your preceptor. O you of good vow, you have no fear due to this penance.

## \|\| 41.117 \|\|

*tāmeva māyāṃ gṛhṇīṣva mama putreṇa nirmitām \|*  
*niriṃdhināmagnimayīṃ duḥsparśāṃ pāvakairapi \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Accept that illusion only, which is created by my son, which is fuel-less and full of fire, which is difficult to be touched even by fires.

## \|\| 41.118 \|\|

*eṣā te svasya vaṃśasya vaśagāri vinigrahe \|*  
*rakṣiṣyatyātmapakṣaṃ ca vipakṣaṃ ca pradhakṣyati \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. While subduing the enemy it will be under the control of you and (the members) of your family. It will protect your side and will burn (i.e. destroy) the enemy.

## \|\| 41.119 \|\|

*varuṇa uvāca \|*  
*eṣā durviṣahā māyā devairapi durāsadā \|*  
*aurveṇa nirmitā pūrvaṃ pāvakenorvasūnunā \|\| 119 \|\|*

Varuṇa said:

119\. This illusion unassailable even by gods, was formerely created by Aurva, the fire, the son of Urva.

## \|\| 41.120 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu vyathite daitye nirvīryaiṣā na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śāpo hyasyāḥ purā dattaḥ sṛṣṭā yenaiva tejasā \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. When the demon was afflicted it would become powerless; there was no doubt about it. That was the curse given by him who had created it with his lustre.

## \|\| 41.121 \|\|

*yadyeṣā pratihaṃtavyā kartavyo bhagavānsukhī \|*  
*dīyatāṃ me sakho śakra toyayonirniśākaraḥ \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. O Śakra, if this (illusion) is to be set aside and the lord is to be made happy, then give me, as my companion, the Moon, born of water (of the ocean).

## \|\| 41.122 \|\|

*tenāhaṃ sahasaṃ gamya yādobhiśca samāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*māyāmetāṃ haniṣyāmi tvatprasādānna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. There is no doubt that united with him and surrounded by the aquatic animals, I shall destroy this illusion through your favour.

## \|\| 41.123 \|\|

*evamastvitisaṃhṛṣṭaḥ śakrastridaśavardhanaḥ \|*  
*saṃdideśāgrataḥ somaṃ yuddhāya śiśirāyudham \|\| 123 \|\|*

123\. Śakra, who helped the gods to prosper, being delighted, said, “Let it be so,” and ordered Soma, having cold weapons, to fight at the head (of the army):

## \|\| 41.124 \|\|

*gaccha soma sahāyantvaṃ kuru pāśadharasya vai \|*  
*asurāṇāṃ vināśāya jayārthaṃ tridivaukasām \|\| 124 \|\|*

124\. “O Soma, help Varuṇa for the destruction of the demons and the victory of the gods.

## \|\| 41.125 \|\|

*tvaṃ mataḥ prativīryaśca jyotiṣāmapi ceśvaraḥ \|*  
*tvanmayānsarvalokeṣu rasānvedavido viduḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. You are regarded as being of matchless prowess and the lord of the luminaries. Those well-versed in the Vedas know that all juices are full of you.

## \|\| 41.126 \|\|

*tvayā samo na lokesminvidyate śiśirāyudhaḥ \|*  
*kṣayavṛddhītavāvyaktesāgarecaivacāṃbare \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. None like you having cold weapons is (to be found) in the world. Your waning and waxing are uncreated in the ocean as well as in the sky.

## \|\| 41.127 \|\|

*pravartayasyahorātrātkālaṃ saṃmohayanjagat \|*  
*lokacchāyāmayaṃ lakṣma tavāṃkaḥ śaśavigrahaḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Deluding the world you cause the time through day and night. Your characteristic is reflected in the world and the spot on you is of the form of a hare.

## \|\| 41.128 \|\|

*na viduḥ soma te māyāṃ ye ca nakṣatrayonayaḥ \|*  
*tvamādityapathādūrdhvaṃ jyotiṣāṃ coparisthitaḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. O Soma, those who are not born of kṣatriya wombs do not know your illusory power. You remain above the course of the Sun, and above the luminaries.

## \|\| 41.129 \|\|

*tamaḥ protsārya sahasā bhāsayasyakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*śītabhānurhimatanurjyotiṣāmadhipaḥ śaśī \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Driving away darkness suddenly, you illumine the entire world. You are cool-rayed, snow-bodies, the lord of the luminaries and have the form of the hare on your body.

## \|\| 41.130-134 \|\|

*api tatkālayogātmā ijyo yajñaratho'vyayaḥ \|*  
*oṣadhīśaḥ kriyāyonirapāṃ yoniranuṣṇaguḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*śītāṃśuramṛtādhāraścapalaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ kāṃtiḥ kāṃtavapuṣāṃ tvaṃ somaḥ somapāyinām \|\| 131 \|\|*

*saumyastvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ timiraghnastvamṛkṣarāṭ \|*  
*tadgaccha tvaṃ mahāsena varuṇena varūthinā \|\| 132 \|\|*

*śamayasvāsurīṃ māyāṃ yayā dahyāmahe raṇe \|*  
*soma uvāca \|*  
*yanmāṃ vadasi yuddhārthaṃ devarājavaraprada \|\| 133 \|\|*

*eṣa varṣāmi śiśiraṃ daityamāyāpakarṣaṇaṃ \|*  
*etānme śītanirdagdhānpaśyasva himaveṣṭitān \|\| 134 \|\|*

130-133a. You are also of the nature of destiny; you are fit to be offered a sacrifice to; you are the sacrifice; and you are the unmanifest one; you are the lord of the herbs; you are the source of rites; also of water and you are cool-rayed; your rays are cool; you are the prop of nectar; you are smart and have a white vehicle; you are the loveliness of the lovely bodies; you are the Soma of those who drink Soma. You are agreeable to all beings; you destroy the darkness; you are the lord of the constellations. Therefore, O you commander of a large army, go with Varuṇa, wearing an armour. Put an end to the demonish illusion, by which we are being burnt.”

Soma said:

133b-134. Since, O king of gods, O giver of boons, you tell me to fight I shall shower hoarfrost which would remove the demonish illusion. See these my cool and tormenting rays, covered with snow.

## \|\| 41.135 \|\|

*tathā himakarotsṛṣṭāḥ sapāśā himavṛṣṭayaḥ \|*  
*veṣṭayaṃti ca tāndaityānvāyurmeghagaṇāniva \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. So the snow-showers discharged by the Moon, with nooes (of Varuṇa) surrounded the demons as the wind surrounds the multitudes of clouds.

## \|\| 41.136 \|\|

*tau pāśaśītāṃśudharau varuṇeṃdū mahābalau \|*  
*jaghnaturhimapātaiśca pāśapātaiśca dānavān \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. The two mighty (heroes), Varuṇa and Indu (i.e. the Moon). holding nooses and cool rays, killed the demons by sending down snow and nooses.

## \|\| 41.137 \|\|

*dvāvaṃbunāthau samare tau pāśahimayodhinau \|*  
*mṛdhe ceraturaṃbhobhiḥ kṣubdhāviva mahārṇavau \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. The two lords of water—the two warriors fighting with nooses and snow moved with water in the army like two agitated great oceans.

## \|\| 41.138 \|\|

*tābhyāmāpūritaṃ sarvaṃ taddānavabalaṃ mahat \|*  
*jagatsaṃvarttakāṃbhodaiḥ pravarṣairiva saṃvṛtaṃ \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The entire great army of the demons was filled, as the entire world is covered by the showering destructive clouds (at the time of deluge).

## \|\| 41.139 \|\|

*tāvudyatāvaṃbunāthau śaśāṃkavaruṇāvubhau \|*  
*śamayāmāsatustāṃ tu māyāṃ daityendranirmitāṃ \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. The two lords of water, viz. Soma and Varuṇa, getting ready, destroyed that illusion created by the lord of demons.

## \|\| 41.140 \|\|

*śītāṃśujālanirdagdhāḥ pāśaiścāskaṃditā raṇe \|*  
*na śekuścalituṃ daityā viśiraskā ivādrayaḥ \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Consumed by the multitudes of the cool rays, and assailed by (Varuṇa’s) nooses, the demons could not move in the battle like topless mountains.

## \|\| 41.141 \|\|

*śītāṃśu nihatāste tu daityāssarve nipātitāḥ \|*  
*himaplāvita sarvāṃgānirūṣmāṇa ivāgnayaḥ \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. All the demons struck down by Soma, were destroyed. Their bodies were flooded with snow like fires that were not hot (i.e. that were extinguished).

## \|\| 41.142 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu divi daityānāṃ nipataṃti śubhāni vai \|*  
*vimānāni vicitrāṇi nipataṃtyutpataṃti ca \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. The variegated and auspicious heavenly cars of those demons fell down. They fell down and again came up.

## \|\| 41.143 \|\|

*tānpāśahastagrathitānchāditānśītaraśmibhiḥ \|*  
*mayo dadarśa māyāvī dānavāndivi dānavaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. Maya, the demon skilled in magic, saw,in the heaven, the demons bound by the groups of nooses and covered over with the lunar rays.

## \|\| 41.144-146 \|\|

*saśailajālāṃ vitatāṃ khaḍgapaṭṭasahāsinīm \|*  
*pādapotkarakūṭasthāṃ kaṃdarākīrṇakānanāṃ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*siṃhavyāghragaṇākīrṇāṃ nadadbhirdevayūthapaiḥ \|*  
*īhāmṛgagaṇākīrṇāṃ pavanāghūrṇitaddrumām \|\| 145 \|\|*

*nirmitāṃ svena putreṇa kūjaṃtīṃ divikāmagāṃ \|*  
*prathitāṃ pārvatīṃ māyāṃ sasṛje sa samaṃtataḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

144-146. He released the celebrated, mountainous illusion with a group of mountains, with swords and sharp-edged spears, with heaps of trees standing at the top, crowded with groups of lions and tigers when the hosts of gods were making noise, crowded with herds of wolves, with trees shaken by wind; it was created by his own son, it was warbling and it moved freely in the heaven everywhere.

## \|\| 41.147 \|\|

*sāsiśabdaiśśilāvarṣaiḥ saṃpatadbhiśca pādapaiḥ \|*  
*jaghāna devasaṃghāṃste dānavānabhyajīvayat \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. The demons struck the gods with showers of rocks accompanied by sounds of swords and with falling trees (i.e. trees that fell) and did not allow them to live.

## \|\| 41.148 \|\|

*naiśākarī vāruṇī ca māye aṃtarhite tadā \|*  
*abhavadghorasaṃcārā pṛthivī parvatairiva \|\| 148 \|\|*

148\. The two illusions—that of the demons and that of Varuṇa—then disappeared. Movement on the earth became fearful as it were with mountains (everywhere).

## \|\| 41.149-150 \|\|

*na cāruddho drumagaṇairdevo dṛśyata kaścana \|*  
*tadapadhvastadhanuṣaṃ bhagnapraharaṇāvilam \|\| 149 \|\|*

*niṣprayatnaṃ surānīkaṃ varjayitvā gadādharaṃ \|*  
*sa hi yuddhagataḥ śrīmānīśo na sma vyakaṃpata \|\| 150 \|\|*

149-150. No god was seen as (each one) was screened by multitudes of trees. Except the Mace-holder (i.e. Viṣṇu) all other (soldiers in) the army of gods had their bows destroyed, had become loathsome due to the weapons being broken, and had discontinued their exertion. That majestic lord, who had entered the war, did not tremble at all.

## \|\| 41.151-152 \|\|

*sahiṣṇutvājjagatsvāmī na cukrodha gadādharaḥ \|*  
*kālajñaḥ kālameghābhaḥ samīkṣankālamāhave \|\| 151 \|\|*

*devāsuravimardaṃ ca draṣṭukāmastadā hariḥ \|*  
*tato bhagavatādiṣṭau raṇe pāvakamārutau \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. The lord of the world, Hari, who resembled the (dark) destructive cloud, who knew the occasion, and who realized (imminent) death in the war, who desired to witness the fight between gods and demons, did not get angry because of his forbearance. Then the lord ordered Fire and Wind to fight.

## \|\| 41.153-155 \|\|

*coditau viṣṇuvākyena tato māyāṃ vyakarṣatāṃ \|*  
*tābhyāmudbhrāṃtavegābhyāṃ prabuddhābhyāṃ mahāhave \|\| 153 \|\|*

*dagdhā sā pārvatī māyā bhasmībhūtā nanāśa ha \|*  
*sonilonalasaṃyuktassonalaścānilākulaḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

*daityasenāṃ dadahaturyugāṃteṣviva mūrcchitau \|*  
*vāyuḥ prajavitastatra paścādagniśca mārutāt \|\| 155 \|\|*

153-155. Impelled by the words of Viṣṇu they drew the illusion. That mountainous illusion perished (when) it was burnt by the two, who had been roaming about and had commenced to exert themselves. That Wind accompanied by Fire and that Fire in the company of Wind, augmented as it were at the time of deluge, burnt the army of demons. Wind became speedy there; and then Agni also became like that due to Māruta (i.e. Wind).

## \|\| 41.156-172 \|\|

*ceraturdānavānīke krīḍaṃtāvanalānilau \|*  
*bhasmībhūteṣu bhūteṣu prapatatsūtpatatsu ca \|\| 156 \|\|*

*dānavānāṃ vimāneṣu nipatatsu samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*vātaskaṃdhāpaviddheṣu kṛtakarmaṇi pāvake \|\| 157 \|\|*

*māyāvadhe pravṛtte tu stūyamāne gadādhare \|*  
*niṣprayatneṣu daityeṣu trailokye muktabaṃdhane \|\| 158 \|\|*

*prahṛṣṭeṣu ca deveṣu sādhusādhviti jalpiṣu \|*  
*jaye daśaśatākṣasya daityānāṃ ca parājaye \|\| 159 \|\|*

*dikṣu sarvāsu śuddhāsu pravṛtte dharmavistare \|*  
*apāvṛte caṃdrapathe svasthānasthe divākare \|\| 160 \|\|*

*pravṛttistheṣu bhūteṣu nṛṣu cāritravatsu ca \|*  
*abhinnabaṃdhane mṛtyau hūyamāne hutāśane \|\| 161 \|\|*

*yajñaśobhiṣu deveṣu svargamārgaṃ diśatsu ca \|*  
*lokapāleṣu sarveṣu dikṣu saṃdhānavartiṣu \|\| 162 \|\|*

*bhāve tapasi siddhānāmabhāve pāpakarmaṇām \|*  
*devapakṣe pramudite daityapakṣe viṣīdati \|\| 163 \|\|*

*tripādavigrahe dharme'dharme pādaparigrahe \|*  
*apāvṛtte mahādvāre vartamāne ca satpathe \|\| 164 \|\|*

*lokeṣu dharmavṛtteṣu pravṛtteṣvāśrameṣu ca \|*  
*prajārakṣaṇayukteṣu rājamāneṣu rājasu \|\| 165 \|\|*

*praśāṃteṣu ca lokeṣu śāṃte tamasi dānave \|*  
*agnimārutayostasminvṛtte saṃgrāmakarmaṇi \|\| 166 \|\|*

*tanmayā vimalā lokāstābhyāṃ jayakṛtakriyāḥ \|*  
*tīvraṃ daityabhayaṃ śrutvā mārutāgnikṛtaṃ mahat \|\| 167 \|\|*

*kālanemīti vikhyāto dānavaḥ pratyadṛśyata \|*  
*bhāskarākāramukuṭaḥ śiṃjitābharaṇāṃgadaḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

*maṃdarādripratīkāśo mahārajatasaṃvṛtaḥ \|*  
*śatapraharaṇodagraḥ śatabāhuḥ śatānanaḥ \|\| 169 \|\|*

*śataśīrṣaḥ sthitaḥ śrīmānśataśṛṃga ivācalaḥ \|*  
*kakṣe mahati saṃvṛddho nidāgha iva pāvakaḥ \|\| 170 \|\|*

*dhūmrakeśo hariśmaśrurdaṃturo vikaṭānanaḥ \|*  
*trailokyāṃtaravistāraṃ dhārayanvipulaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

*bāhubhistulayanvyoma kṣipanpadbhyāṃ mahīdharān \|*  
*īrayanmukhaniḥśvāsairvṛṣṭikārānbalāhakān \|\| 172 \|\|*

156-166a. Fire and Wind who were amusing themselves, moved in the army of the demons. Then the beings were (being) reduced to ashes and they were rising and falling. Everywhere the aeroplanes of the demons were falling. The branches (of trees) were being thrown off by Wind, and Fire was doing his duty. The killing by Māyā (i.e, illusion) was going on; the Mace-holder (i.e. Viṣṇu) was being praised; the exertion ofthe demons had stopped; the three worlds were free from bondage; gods were pleased. Good people said: ‘Well (done), well(done).’ The thousand-eyed one (i.e. Indra) achieved victory, and the demons were defeated. All the directions were pure; the righteous began to increase. The course of the Moon was uncovered, and the Sun remained steady in his own place. Beings were taking an active part in worldly affairs; people were endowed with good character; the bonds of death were unaffected. Oblations were offered into fire; gods shone with sacrifices and they showed the path to heaven. All the regents of the quarters supported their quarters; the perfect ones remained in penance; the sinful ones did not exist. The side of the gods was glad and the side of the demons was dejected. Righteousness had the three feet, and unrighteousness had just one foot (i.e. righteousness was very much predominant). The great gate (to righteousness etc.) was open, and good path existed; people were inclined to piety, and the hermitages proceeded with their activity uninterruptedly (i.e. the hermits led a peaceful life). Kings were engaged in protecting their subjects and shone; the worlds were calm (and) the dark demon was subdued.

166b-172. When that (great) deed of Agni and Vāyu took place in the war, all worlds were wholly interested in them, were bright and performed acts (celebrating) their victory. Hearing about the great fear caused to the demons by Agni and Vāyu, the well-known demon Kālanemi took notice (of what was happening). He was having a crown of the shape of the sun, and tinkling ornaments and armlets. He resembled the Mandara mountain. He was covered with great pearl-ornaments, and looking fearful due to having hundreds of weapons, a hundred arms and a hundred faces, and a hundred heads. He stood like a majestic mountain having a hundred peaks and augmented in the great side, (looking) like fire in the summer. He had smoky hair, ruddy moustache, projected teeth, and a hideous face. He had a large body expanding in the three worlds, lifting up the sky with his arms, and throw ing off the mountains with his two feet, and setting in motion showering clouds with his breaths.

## \|\| 41.173-177 \|\|

*tiryagāyataraktākṣaṃ maṃdarodagravarcasām \|*  
*didhakṣaṃtamivāyāṃtaṃ sarvāndevagaṇānmṛdhe \|\| 173 \|\|*

*tarjayaṃtaṃ suragaṇāṃśchādayaṃtaṃ diśo daśa \|*  
*saṃvartakāle hṛṣitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mṛtyumivotthitam \|\| 174 \|\|*

*sutalenocchrayavatā vipulāṃguliparvaṇā \|*  
*laṃbābharaṇapūrṇena kiṃciccalitakarmaṇā \|\| 175 \|\|*

*ucchritenāgrahastena dakṣiṇena vapuṣmatā \|*  
*dānavāndevanihatānbruvantaṃ tiṣṭhateti ca \|\| 176 \|\|*

*taṃ kālanemiṃ samare dviṣatāṃ kālaneminam \|*  
*vīkṣaṃte sma surāḥ sarve bhayavihvalalocanāḥ \|\| 177 \|\|*

173-177. All gods, with their eyes afflicted with fear, saw Kālanemi, whose broad red eyes were (looking) obliquely, whose exalted lustre was like (the) Mandara (mountain), who was, while approaching the groups of gods, as it were desiring to burn them in the battle, who was threatening the hosts of gods, and covering the ten quarters, who was seen like Death risen and delighted at the time of deluge, and who said to the demons, struck by gods, ‘Wait, wait!’ with his strong right hand lifted up, which had a raised nice palm, the fingers of which had large joints, which was long and full of ornaments, which did not move at all.

## \|\| 41.178 \|\|

*taṃ vīkṣaṃte sma bhūtāni grasaṃtaṃ kālaneminam \|*  
*trivikramaṃ vikramaṃ taṃ nārāyaṇamivāparam \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. Beings observed that Kālanemi destroying (the gods), like another Trivikrama Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) overcoming e verything.

## \|\| 41.179 \|\|

*sobhyucchrayaṃ punaḥ prāpto mārutāghūrṇitāṃbaraḥ \|*  
*prakrāmadasuro yoddhuṃ trāsayansarvadevatāḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. That demon, having shaken the sky with wind, and rising again, came and started to fight causing fear to all gods.

## \|\| 41.180-181 \|\|

*sameyivānsureṃdreṇa pariṣvakto bhramanraṇe \|*  
*kālanemirbabhau daityaḥ saviṣṇuriva maṃdaraḥ \|\| 180 \|\|*

*atha vivyathire devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*kālaneminamāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā kālamivāparam \|\| 181 \|\|*

180-181. That demon Kālanemi, while moving (on the battlefield), being encircled by Indra, came near him, and shone like Mandara with Viṣṇu. Seeing Kālanemi, like another death, coming to them, all the gods, led by Indra were very much frightened.

## \|\| 41.182 \|\|

*dānavānanupiprīṣuḥ kālanemirmahāsuraḥ \|*  
*vyavardhata mahātejāstapāṃte jalado yathā \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. That great demon, desiring to do what was agreeable to the demons, and of great lustre, increased (in size) like a cloud at the end of the summer.

## \|\| 41.183 \|\|

*taṃ trailokyāṃtaragataṃ dṛṣṭvā te dānaveśvarāḥ \|*  
*uttasthurapariśrāṃtāḥ pītvevāmṛtamuttamam \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. The lordly demons, seeing him to have entered the three worlds, stood up unfatigued (i.e. enthusiastically) as if after having drunk the excellent nectar.

## \|\| 41.184 \|\|

*te vītabhayasaṃtrāsā mayatārapurogamāḥ \|*  
*tārakāmayasaṃgrāme satataṃ jitakāśinaḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. The demons, desiring to fight, free from fear and alarm, led by Maya and Tāra, behaving like conquerors in the Tārakāmaya war, and going (out) to fight, shone.

## \|\| 41.185 \|\|

*rejurāyodhanagatā dānavā yuddhakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*maṃtramabhyasatāṃ teṣāṃ vyūhaṃ ca paridhāvatām \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. They who were repeating (magic) formulas, who were running through the army became glad when they saw the demon Kālanemi.

## \|\| 41.186 \|\|

*prekṣatāṃ cābhavatprītirdānavaṃ kālaneminam \|*  
*ye tu tatra mayasyāsanmukhyā yuddhapurassarāḥ \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. All those chief (soldiers) of Maya, who were leaders in the battle, gave up their fear (and) stood (near him) to fight.

## \|\| 41.187-195 \|\|

*te tu sarve bhayaṃ tyaktvā hṛṣṭā yoddhumupasthitāḥ \|*  
*mayastāro varāhaśca hayagrīvaśca dānavaḥ \|\| 187 \|\|*

*vipracittisutaḥ śvetaḥ kharalaṃbāvubhāvapi \|*  
*ariṣṭo baliputraśca kiśorākhyastathaiva ca \|\| 188 \|\|*

*surbhānuścāmaraprakhyaścakrayodhī mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*ete'stravedinaḥ sarve sarve tapasi susthitāḥ \|\| 189 \|\|*

*dānavāḥ kṛtino jagmuḥ kālaneminamuddhatam \|*  
*te gadābhissugurvībhiścakrairathaparaśvadhaiḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

*kālakalpaiśca musalaiḥ kṣepaṇīyaiśca mudgaraiḥ \|*  
*aśmabhiścāstrasadṛśaistathā śailaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 191 \|\|*

*paṭṭiśairbhiṃḍipālaiśca parighaiścottamāyasaiḥ \|*  
*ghātinībhiśca gurvībhiḥ śataghnībhistathaiva ca \|\| 192 \|\|*

*yugairyaṃtraiśca nirmuktairlāṃgalairugratāḍitaiḥ \|*  
*dorbhirāyatamānaiśca pāśaiśca parighādibhiḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*bhujaṃgavaktrairlelihānairvisarpadbhiśca sāyakaiḥ \|*  
*vajraiḥ praharaṇīyaiśca dīpyamānaiśca tomaraiḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

*vikośairasibhistīkṣṇaiḥ śūlaiśca śitanirmalaiḥ \|*  
*daityaiḥ saṃdīpyamānaiśca pragṛhītaśarāsanaiḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*

187-195. These successful demons, knowing the (art of the use of) missiles, well-settled in penance, viz. Maya, Tāra, Varāha, Hayagrīva, Vipracitti’s son Śveta, both Khara and Lamba, Bali’s son Ariṣṭa, so also the one known as Kiśora, and the great demon Surbhānu, famous like gods and as (an expert) fighter in a circular military array, went to Kālanemi, with (i.e. taking with them) very heavy maces, discs, chariots, hatchets, pestles resembling death, slings, mallets, stones like missiles, so also terrible rocks, sharp-edged weapons, small javelins and bars of excellent iron, heavy destructive śataghnī missiles, pairs of fetters, so also ploughs that struck fiercely when discharged, with long arms, nooses and (weapons) like iron-bars, with arrows having the licking and spreading mouths of serpents, with destructive weapons and shining iron-clubs, with sharp unsheathed swords, with sharp and bright lances, and with bright demons holding bows.

## \|\| 41.196 \|\|

*tataḥ puraskṛtya tadā kālaneminamāhave \|*  
*sā dīptaśastrapravarā daityānāṃ ruruce camūḥ \|\| 196 \|\|*

196\. That army of the demons, excellent on account of shining weapons, then led by Kālanemi, shone in the battle.

## \|\| 41.197 \|\|

*yairnimīlitasarvāṃgā vanālīvāṃbudāgame \|*  
*devatānāmapi camūrmumude śakrapālitā \|\| 197 \|\|*

197\. The army of the gods, which was closed (i.e. encircled) on all sides by them (i.e. the demons) like a thicket of trees at the time of the advent of the clouds, also became glad (as) it was protected by Indra.

## \|\| 41.198-205 \|\|

*upetā śiśiroṣṇābhyāṃ tejobhyāṃ caṃdrasūryayoḥ \|*  
*vāyuvegavatī saumyā tārāgaṇapatākinī \|\| 198 \|\|*

*toyadā baddhavasanā grahanakṣatrahāsinī \|*  
*yameṃdradhanadairguptā varuṇena ca dhīmatā \|\| 199 \|\|*

*sā pradīptāgnipavanā nārāyaṇaparāyaṇā \|*  
*sāsamudraughasadṛśī dīpyamānā mahācamūḥ \|\| 200 \|\|*

*rarājāstravatī bhīmā yakṣagaṃdharvaśālinī \|*  
*tayoścamvostadānīṃ tu babhūva sa samāgamaḥ \|\| 201 \|\|*

*dyāvāpṛthivyossaṃyogo yathā syādyugaparyaye \|*  
*tadyuddhamabhavadghoraṃ devadānavasaṃkulaṃ \|\| 202 \|\|*

*kṣamāparākramaparaṃ sadarpavinayasyadaṃ \|*  
*niścakramurbalābhyāṃ tu bhīmābhyāṃ ca surā'surāḥ \|\| 203 \|\|*

*pūrvāparābhyāṃ saṃrabdhāḥ sāgarābhyāmivāṃbudāḥ \|*  
*tābhyāṃ balābhyāṃ saṃhṛṣṭāśceruste devadānavāḥ \|\| 204 \|\|*

*vanābhyāṃ pārvatīyābhyāṃ puṣpitābhyāṃ yathā nagāḥ \|*  
*samājaghnustathā bherīḥ śaṃkhāndadhmuranekaśaḥ \|\| 205 \|\|*

198-202a. That great shining (divine) army, which was endowed with cold and hot lustre (respectively) of the Moon and the Sun, which was speedy like the wind, which was agreeable, which was having the banners of stars, which had put on the garments of clouds, which was smiling with the planets and constellations, which was protected by Yama, Indra, Kubera, and also by intelligent Varuṇa, which was having (in it) blazing fire and wind, which was devoted to Nārāyaṇa, and which resembled a current in the ocean, which had missiles which are fearful and had (in it) Yakṣas and Gandharvas, shone. At that time, the encounter between the two armies took place like the union of the heaven and earth at the time of the expiration of a Yuga.

202b-204a. That war in which gods and demons had thronged, in which forgiveness and valour were excessive, which had arrogance, politeness and speed, was fierce. The gods and demons set out with terrible armies like the excited clouds from the eastern and the western oceans.

204b-205. The gods and demons were delighted with the two armies, as the mountains with the blossomed thickets on them. They beat the drums and blew the conches repeatedly.

## \|\| 41.206-207 \|\|

*brahmāṃḍaṃ ca bhuvaṃ caiva diśaśca samapūrayan \|*  
*jyāghātatalanirghoṣa dhanuṣāṃ kūjitāni ca \|\| 206 \|\|*

*duṃdubhīnāṃ ca nirhrādo daityamaṃtardadhuḥ svanam \|*  
*te'nyonyamabhisaṃpeturyātayaṃtaḥ parasparam \|\| 207 \|\|*

206-207.
