75-76. In the Kali-yuga, void of piety, and a bad time, people everywhere touch these (Mlecchas) through greed for wealth. The bird (i.e. Garuḍa) freed the Mlecchas and being oppressed by hunger, said again: ‘O father, hunger is oppressing me more’.

## \|\| 47.77-78 \|\|

*punarāha dvijastāta kṣudhā me bādhatetarām \|*  
*avadadgaruḍaṃ tatra kaśyapaḥ kṛpayā drutam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhaṃtau vipulau tatra jighāṃsū gajakacchapau \|*  
*aprameyau mahāsatvau sāgarasyaikadeśataḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Kaśyapa there said to Garuḍa who was melted with tenderness: In one region of the ocean, there are a big elephant and a tortoise desiring to kill (each other); they are immeasurable (i.e. of a very huge size) and are very energetic.

## \|\| 47.79-80 \|\|

*tāvapsu ca drutaṃ vatsa kṣudhāṃ te vārayiṣyataḥ \|*  
*sa piturvacanaṃ śrutvā tatra gatvābhipadya tau \|\| 79 \|\|*

*nakhairbhitvā kūrmagajau mahāsatvau mahājavaḥ \|*  
*khamutpapāta tau dhṛtvā vidyudvego mahābalaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. Those (two remaining) in the water, will, O son, quickly satiate your hunger’. Hearing the words of his father, he, very powerful, and of a great speed, went there, attacked the elephant and the tortoise and tearing them with his nails, flew into the sky with the speed of lightning after seizing them.

## \|\| 47.81-83 \|\|

*ādhāratāṃ na gacchaṃti nagāśca maṃdarādayaḥ \|*  
*tato yojanalakṣe dve gatvā mārutaraṃhasā \|\| 81 \|\|*

*mahatyāṃ jaṃbuśākhāyāṃ nipapāta mahābalaḥ \|*  
*bhagnā sā sahasā śākhā tāṃ pataṃtīṃ khageśvaraḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*gobrāhmaṇavadhādbhīto dadhāra tarasā balī \|*  
*dhṛtvā tāṃ ruciraṃ vegāddravaṃtaṃ khe mahābalam \|\| 83 \|\|*

81-83. The Mandara and other mountains could not serve as a prop for him. Then the very mighty (Garuḍa) going with wind’s speed for (a distance of) two lakh yojanas, dropped (himself with them) on a huge branch of a jambu-tree. Suddenly the branch gave way. The powerful (Garuḍa), fearing the death of cows and brāhmaṇas, quickly supported that falling branch.

## \|\| 47.84-86 \|\|

*gatvā viṣṇuruvācedaṃ nararūpadharo hariḥ \|*  
*kastvaṃ bhramasi cākāśe kimarthaṃ patageśvara \|\| 84 \|\|*

*vidhṛtya mahatīṃ śākhāṃ mahāṃtau gajakacchapau \|*  
*tamuvāca dvijastasminnararūpadharaṃ harim \|\| 85 \|\|*

*garuḍohaṃ mahābāho khagarūpaḥ svakarmaṇā \|*  
*kaśyapasya munessūnurvinatāgarbhasaṃbhavaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-85a. Viṣṇu, taking up a human form, went to the charming and mighty (Garuḍa) who was moving fast holding the branch and said to him: ‘O best of birds, who are you? Why are you moving in the sky, holding the huge branch and the huge elephant and tortoise?’

85b-86. Then the bird (i.e. Garuḍa) said to Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu) in human form; ‘O you of mighty arms, I am Garuḍa, having the form of a bird due to my deeds. I am the son of Kaśyapa, born from the womb of Vinatā.

## \|\| 47.87 \|\|

*paśyaitau ca mahāsatvau bhakṣaṇārthaṃ mayā dhṛtau \|*  
*na dharā ca mamādhāro na vṛkṣā na ca parvatāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. See these great animals seized by me for eating them up. Neither the earth, nor the trees and mountains can support me.

## \|\| 47.88 \|\|

*anekayojanānyūrdhvaṃ dṛṣṭvā jaṃbūmahīruham \|*  
*apataṃtasya śākhāyāṃ sahemau paribhakṣituṃ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Seeing the jambu-tree after (having flown for) many yojanas, I fell on its branch with these two to eat them up (after sitting on the branch).

## \|\| 47.89-91 \|\|

*bhagnā sā sahasā śākhā tāṃ ca dhṛtvā bhramāmyaham \|*  
*koṭikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ vadhāt \|\| 89 \|\|*

*bhayaṃ tatra viṣādo me sahasā prāviśadbudha \|*  
*kiṃ karomi kathaṃ yāmi ko me vegaṃ sahiṣyati \|\| 90 \|\|*

*ityukte patagaśreṣṭhaṃ provācedaṃ haristadā \|*  
*asmadbāhuṃ samāruhya bhakṣemau gajakacchapau \|\| 91 \|\|*

89-90a. That branch suddenly broke. Holding the branch, I am wandering. O wise one, fear and dejection have entered me (i.e. my mind), as a result of the murder of crores of brāhmaṇas and cows.

90b-91. ‘What should I do? How should I go? Who would put up with my speed?’ When (Garuḍa) had said this, Hari then said to that best of birds: ‘Mounting on my arm, you eat up these elephant and tortoise’.

## \|\| 47.92-93 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*mamādhāraṃ na gacchaṃti sāgarāśca nagottamāḥ \|*  
*atha caivaṃ mahāsatvaṃ kathaṃ tvaṃ dhārayiṣyasi \|\| 92 \|\|*

*ṛte nārāyaṇādanyaḥ ko māṃ dhārayituṃ kṣamaḥ \|*  
*trailokye kaḥ pumāṃstiṣṭhedyo vegaṃ me sahiṣyati \|\| 93 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

92-93. ‘(Even) the oceans and best mountains are not able to support me; then how can you hold (i.e. support) a strong being like me? Who else except Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) is able to hold (i.e. support) me? He alone is the man in the three worlds, who can put up with my force.’

## \|\| 47.94 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*svakāryamuddharetprājñaḥ svakāryaṃ kuru sāṃpratam \|*  
*kṛtvā kāryaṃ khagaśreṣṭha vijānīṣe ca māṃ dhruvam \|\| 94 \|\|*

Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu) said:

94\. ‘A wise one should save his own affair first; do (i. e. get) your work (done) now; having done (i.e. having got done) your work you will certainly know me’.

## \|\| 47.95 \|\|

*mahāsatvaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā vimṛśya manasā khagaḥ \|*  
*evamastviti coktvā sa papāta ha mahābhuje \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Having seen that very mighty (Viṣṇu) and having mentally reflected, the bird (i.e. Garuḍa), saying, ‘Let it be so’, jumped on his great arm.

## \|\| 47.96 \|\|

*na cacāla bhujastasya sannipāte khageśituḥ \|*  
*tatra sthitvā sa tāṃ śākhāṃ mumoca parvatālaye \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. When the lord of the birds fell upon his (i.e. Viṣṇu’s) arm, it did not move. Remaining there, he dropped the branch on the abode of the mountains (i.e. the earth).

## \|\| 47.97 \|\|

*śākhāpatanamātreṇa sacarācarakānanā \|*  
*cacāla vasudhā caiva sāgarāḥ pracakaṃpire \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. Just at the fall of the branch, the earth, with the mobile, the immobile and the forests, trembled. The oceans also trembled (i.e. were agitated).

## \|\| 47.98 \|\|

*tataśca khāditau sattvau sahasā gajakacchapau \|*  
*tṛptiṃ na prāptavānsopi kṣudhā tasya na śāmyati \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. Then he rashly ate up the two animals, the elephant and the tortoise. He was not satisfied. His hunger was not satiated.

## \|\| 47.99 \|\|

*etajjñātvā tu goviṃdastamuvāca khageśvaram \|*  
*bhujasya mama māṃsaṃ tu bhakṣayitvā sukhī bhava \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. Knowing (i.e. seeing) this Govinda (i.e. Viṣṇu) said to the lord of birds: ‘Eat the flesh of my arm and be happy.’

## \|\| 47.100 \|\|

*ityukte pracuraṃ māṃsaṃ bhujasya tasya tena hi \|*  
*khāditaṃ kṣudhayā putra vraṇaṃ tasya na vidyate \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. When he said this, O son, he, through hunger, ate a lot of flesh of his arm; but there was no wound on his (arm).

## \|\| 47.101 \|\|

*tamuvāca mahāprājñaścarācaraguruṃ harim \|*  
*kastvaṃ kiṃ vā priyaṃ tedya kariṣyāmi ca sāṃpratam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Then the highly intelligent one said to Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu) the lord of the mobile and immobile: ‘Who are you? What proper thing dear to you should I do today?’

## \|\| 47.102-104 \|\|

*nārāyaṇa uvāca \|*  
*viddhi nārāyaṇaṃ māṃ hi tvatpriyārthaṃ samāgatam \|*  
*rūpaṃ svaṃ darśayāmāsa pratyayārthaṃ ca tasya vai \|\| 102 \|\|*

*pītavastraṃ ghanaśyāmaṃ caturbhujamanoharam \|*  
*śaṃkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ sarvasureśvaram \|\| 103 \|\|*

*taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā garutmāṃśca praṇamya śirasā harim \|*  
*priyaṃ kiṃ te kariṣyāmi vada naḥ puruṣottama \|\| 104 \|\|*

Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu) said:

102a. ‘Know me to be Nārāyaṇa, who has come here to do what is dear to you.’

102b-104. And for convincing him he showed him his own form. Seeing him who had put on a yellow garment, who was dark like a cloud, who had four arms, who was pleasing, who had held a conch, a disc, a mace and a lotus, and who was the lord of gods, Garuḍa, saluting him by bowing his head (said to him): ‘O best man (i.e. Viṣṇu), tell me what thing dear to you should I do?’

## \|\| 47.105 \|\|

*tamabravīnmahātejā devadeveśvaro hariḥ \|*  
*bhava me vāhanaṃ śūra sakhe tvaṃ sārvakālikam \|\| 105 \|\|*

105\. Viṣṇu, the lord of the lords of gods and very lustrous, said to him: ‘O brave one, O friend, be my vehicle for all times’.

## \|\| 47.106-108 \|\|

*tamuvāca khagaśreṣṭho dhanyohaṃ vibudheśvara \|*  
*saphalaṃ janma me nātha tvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvādya me prabho \|\| 106 \|\|*

*prārthayitvā ca pitarāvāgamiṣyāmi te'ntikam \|*  
*prīto viṣṇuruvācedaṃ bhava tvamajarāmaraḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ karma tejaśca matsamam \|*  
*sarvatra te gatiścāstu nikhilaṃ tu sukhaṃ dhruvam \|\| 108 \|\|*

106-107a. To him the greatest among the birds said: ‘O lord of gods, I am fortunate. O lord, O master, on having seen you my life is fruitful. Having requested my parents, I shall approach you.’

107b-108. Viṣṇu, being pleased, said this: ‘Be ever young and immortal; you will not be killed by any being; your deeds and lustre will be like mine. May you (have the power to) move at all places; may you certainly have all happiness.

## \|\| 47.109 \|\|

*saṃmilatu drutaṃ sarvaṃ yatte manasi vartate \|*  
*yatheṣṭaṃ prītimāhāramakaṣṭena pralapsyase \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. May you obtain whatever you have in mind. You will easily obtain food desired by you and to your liking.

## \|\| 47.110 \|\|

*vyasanānmātaraṃ sadyo mocayiṣyasi nānyathā \|*  
*evamuktvā hariḥ sadyastatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. You will instantly deliver your mother from her calamity. (What I say will not be) otherwise.’ Saying so Hari (i.e. Viṣṇu) instantly disappeared there only.

## \|\| 47.111 \|\|

*tārkṣyopi pitaraṃ gatvā kathayaccākhilaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*sa tacchrutvā prahṛṣṭātmā tanayaṃ punarabravīt \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Then Garuḍa also, having gone to his father, told him everything. Hearing that, and with his heart pleased, he (i.e. Kaśyapa) again said to his son (i.e. Garuḍa):

## \|\| 47.112 \|\|

*dhanyohaṃ ca khagaśreṣṭha dhanyā te jananī śivā \|*  
*dhanyaṃ kṣetraṃ kulaṃ caiva yasya putrastvamīdṛśaḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. ‘O greatest among birds, I am fortunate; so also is your auspicious mother. The wife and family of him whose son you are like this, are blessed.

## \|\| 47.113 \|\|

*yasya putraḥ kule jāto vaiṣṇavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*kulakoṭiṃ samuddhṛtya viṣṇusāyujyatāṃ vrajet \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. He in whose family such an excellent male, devoted to Viṣṇu is born, will having emancipated a crore (of members of his) family go to the same heaven as of Viṣṇu.

I 14-115. He who worships Viṣṇu everyday, who meditates upon him, who sings (songs in is praise), who always mutters Viṣṇu’s hymn, who recites his eulogy, who eats food offered to him, who fasts on the day of (i.e. auspicious to) Viṣṇu, is relieved after the destruction of all his sins—there is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 47.116 \|\|

*yasya tiṣṭhati goviṃdo mānase ca sadaiva hi \|*  
*sa eva ca labheddāsyaṃ sapuṇyaiḥ puruṣottamaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. That best man in whose mind Viṣṇu resides, alone would always get Viṣṇu’s servitude (i.e. would always become his humble devotee) by means of his religious merit.

## \|\| 47.117 \|\|

*janmakoṭisahasrebhyaḥ kṛtvā satkarmasaṃcayam \|*  
*kṣayācca sarvapāpānāṃ viṣṇoḥ kiṃkaratāṃ vrajet \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Having collected good deeds (i.e. merit due to good deeds) for thousands of crores of existence, he would, due to the exhaustion of all his sins, be the servant of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 47.118-120 \|\|

*dhanyosau mānavo loke viṣṇossādṛśyamāvrajet \|*  
*nityaḥ suravaraiḥ pūjyo lokanātho'cyuto'vyayaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

*suprasanno bhavedyasya sa eva puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*tapobhirbahubhirdharmairmakhairnānāvidhairapi \|\| 119 \|\|*

*viṣṇurna labhyate devaistvayāsau vipra labhyate \|*  
*sapatnīvyasanāddhorānmātaraṃ te pramocaya \|\| 120 \|\|*

118-119a. Such a man is fortunate in the world and would get the likeness of Viṣṇu. That man is the best with whom Viṣṇu, the immutable lord of the worlds, always worshipped by excellent gods, is well-pleased.

119b-120. Viṣṇuis not obtained (even) by gods with (i.e. after practising) austerities, and with many and various kinds of sacrifices; you are getting (i.e. you have obtained) him. Relieve your mother from the terrible calamity caused by her co-wife.

## \|\| 47.121-122 \|\|

*tato yāsyasi deveśaṃ kṛtvā mātuḥ pratikriyām \|*  
*gṛhītvā janakasyājñāṃ labdhvā viṣṇorvaraṃ mahat \|\| 121 \|\|*

*aṃbāpārśvaṃ gato hṛṣṭastāṃ praṇamyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vinatovāca \|*  
*abhavadbhojanaṃ te'dya putra dṛṣṭaḥ pitāpi ca \|\| 122 \|\|*

121-122. Having retaliated for your mother, you will go to that lord of gods.’

Securing his father’s order and having received a great boon from Viṣṇu, Garuḍa, being delighted, went to his mother and remained before her after having saluted her.

## \|\| 47.122-132 \|\|

*aṃbāpārśvaṃ gato hṛṣṭastāṃ praṇamyāgrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*vinatovāca \|*  
*abhavadbhojanaṃ te'dya putra dṛṣṭaḥ pitāpi ca \|\| 122 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ vā vilaṃbaste ciṃtayā vyathitā hyaham \|*  
*sa māturvacanaṃ śrutvā garuḍaḥ prahasanniva \|\| 123 \|\|*

*kathayāmāsa vṛttāṃtaṃ sā śrutvā vismitā'bhavat \|*  
*kathaṃ ca duḥṣkaraṃ karma śiśubhāvāttvayā kṛtam \|\| 124 \|\|*

*dhanyāhaṃ me kulaṃ dhanyaṃ yastvaṃ viṣṇusakho'bhavaḥ \|*  
*labdhvā varaṃ mahātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā me hṛṣyate manaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

*pauruṣeṇa tvayā vatsa uddhṛtaṃ me kuladvayam \|*  
*suparṇa uvāca \|*  
*mātaḥ kiṃ te kariṣyāmi priyameva taducyatām \|\| 126 \|\|*

*kāryaṃ kṛtvātha yāsyāmi pārśvaṃ nārāyaṇasya ca \|*  
*etacchrutvā tu sā prāha garuḍaṃ vinatā satī \|\| 127 \|\|*

*mahadduḥkhaṃ ca me cāsti kuru tāta pratikriyām \|*  
*bhaginī me sapatnī sā paṇitahaṃ tayā purā \|\| 128 \|\|*

*tasyā dāsyamahaṃ prāptā kastārayati māmitaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇaṃ kṛtvā viṣairaśvaṃ tasyāḥ putrairmahoragaiḥ \|\| 129 \|\|*

*uṣaḥkāle'vadatsā ca aśvoyaṃ kṛṣṇatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*tatohamavadaṃ tatra sadā cāyaṃ rucāsitaḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

*mithyā te vacanaṃ mātaḥ pratijñāṃ sā'karottadā \|*  
*tatohamabruvaṃ kadrūṃ śapathaṃ nāgamātaram \|\| 131 \|\|*

*yadīmaṃ kṛṣṇatābhyeti hareraśvamahaṃ tadā \|*  
*kṛtā bhavāmi te dāsītyahametattadā'vadam \|\| 132 \|\|*

Vinatā said:

122b-123a. O son, you had your food today; you also met your father. Why (then) are you late? I am afflicted with anxiety.

123b-124a. Hearing these words of his mother, Garuḍa, laughing a little, told her the account. Having heard it she was amazed:

124b-126a. ‘(Though) a child how did you do that feat difficult to perform? I am blessed; my family is blessed since you became the friend of Viṣṇu. Seeing that (you have) obtained a great boon (from Viṣṇu) my mind is delighted. O you (my) son, by your valour you have emancipated both my families (i.e. of my father and of my husband).’

Suparṇa (i.e. Garuḍa) said:

126b-127a. O mother, tell me what I should do that is dear to you? Having done that mission (entrusted to me by you) I shall go to the vicinity of Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu).

127b-129a. Hearing this, that chaste Vinatā said to Garuḍa: ‘I am suffering from a great calamity. Adopt a remedy against it. My sister is my co-wife. She has formerly purchased me. I have become her servant. Who will save me from it (i.e. her servitude)?

129b-130a. When her sons—the great serpents—had rendered (the Sun’s) horse black by means of poison, she said to me that the horse would become black at dawn.

130b-131a. Then I said (i.e. to this I replied)—‘This (horse) is always white in colour. Your words are untrue.’ Then she made a solemn declaration.

131b-132. Then I swore at Kadrū, the mother of the serpents. At that time I said to her: ‘If this horse of the Sun becomes black, then I shall be your servant.’

## \|\| 47.133-134 \|\|

*tatastasminhareraśve kṛte kṛṣṇe ca kṛtrimaiḥ \|*  
*tasyāḥ putraiśca dhūrtaiśca dāsītvamagamaṃ tadā \|\| 133 \|\|*

*yasminkāle hyabhīṣṭañca tasyā dravyaṃ dadāmyaham \|*  
*tasminkāle hyadāsītvaṃ yāsyāmi kulanaṃdana \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. Then when her clever sons rendered the Sun’s horse black, I became her servant. O you delighting the family, when I shall give her wealth as desired by her, I shall be free from her servitude.’

## \|\| 47.135 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*pṛccha śīghraṃ ca mātastāṃ kariṣyāmi pratikriyām \|*  
*bhakṣayiṣyāmi tānnāgānpratijñāme yathārthataḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

135\. O mother, ask her quickly; I shall retaliate. I shall eat up those serpents; this is my proper pledge.

## \|\| 47.136 \|\|

*tataḥ kadrūmuvācedaṃ vinatā duḥkhitā satī \|*  
*abhīṣṭaṃ vada kalyāṇi yena mucyeya kṛcchrataḥ \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. Then that unhappy Vinatā said this to Kadrū: ‘O you auspicious one, tell me what you desire, so that I shall be free from the difficulty.’

## \|\| 47.137 \|\|

*abravītsā durācārā pīyūṣaṃ dīyatāmiti \|*  
*etacchrutvā tu vacanamabhavatsā ca niṣprabhā \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. That wicked one said: ‘Give me nectar’. Hearing these words, she became gloomy.

## \|\| 47.138 \|\|

*tataḥ śanairupāgamya tanayaṃ prāha duḥkhitā \|*  
*amṛtaṃ prārthayatpāpā tāta kiṃ vā kariṣyasi \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. Then that miserable (Vinatā) slowly came to her son, and said to him: ‘The sinful one asked for nectar; O son, what will you do (now)?’

## \|\| 47.139 \|\|

*śrutvā vākyaṃ garutmāṃśca mahākrodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*amṛtaṃ cānayiṣyāmi mātarmā vimukhī bhava \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Hearing these words, Garuḍa, getting excessively angry (said:) ‘O mother, I shall bring nectar; do not be grieved’.

## \|\| 47.140 \|\|

*evamuktvā tu tarasā sa gataḥ pituraṃtikam \|*  
*amṛtaṃ cānayiṣyāmi māturarthe'dhunā'nagha \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Saying so, he speedily went to his father. ‘O sinless one, now I shall get nectar for my mother’.

## \|\| 47.141-143 \|\|

*sa tasya vacanaṃ śrutvā muniḥ prāha khageśvaram \|*  
*satyalokasya vai cordhve viśvakarmavinirmitā \|\| 141 \|\|*

*purī cāsti sabhā ramyā devānāṃ hita hetave \|*  
*vahniprākāradurlabhyā durdharṣā cāsuraiḥ suraiḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

*rakṣārthaṃ nirmito devaḥ suraistatra mahābalaḥ \|*  
*yaṃ yaṃ paśyati vīraḥ sa sa eva bhasmatāṃ vrajet \|\| 143 \|\|*

141-143. That sage, after hearing these words uttered by him, said to the lord of birds: ‘Above Satyaloka there is a city fashioned by Viśvakarman for the good of the worlds. It is beautiful with an assembly; it is inaccessible due to fire and ramparts; it is unassailable by demons and gods. Gods have fashioned there a mighty god for its protection. He, whom the hero sees, would be reduced to ashes.’

## \|\| 47.144 \|\|

*suparṇa uvāca \|*  
*nārāyaṇādvaro labdho mayā ca munisattama \|*  
*bhayaṃ nāstīha me tāta surāsuragaṇādapi \|\| 144 \|\|*

Suparṇa (i.e. Garuḍa) said:

144\. O best of sages, I have obtained a boon from Nārāyaṇa (i.e. Viṣṇu); O father, I have no fear even from the host of demons or of gods.

## \|\| 47.145 \|\|

*emamuktvā garutmānsa uddhṛtya sāgarājjalam \|*  
*jagāmākāśamāviśya khagaścordhvaṃ manojavaḥ \|\| 145 \|\|*

145\. Saying so, and taking the water of the ocean the bird having the speed of mind, entered the sky, and moved (up).

## \|\| 47.146 \|\|

*pakṣavātena tasyaiva rajaḥ samudgataṃ bahu \|*  
*tasyāṃtikaṃ na ca tyaktamagamattasya tacca yaḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. By the wind produced due to (the movement of) his wings much dust was raised; the heap of dust left (behind by him) did not come near him.

## \|\| 47.147 \|\|

*gatvā caṃcūjalenāpi vahniṃ nirvāpayadbalī \|*  
*rajobhiḥ paripūrṇākṣo na surastaṃ ca paśyati \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. Having gone (to the city), the mighty one put out the fire with the water in his beak. The god (the protector of the city), with his eyes full of dust, did not see him.

## \|\| 47.148-150 \|\|

*jaghāna rakṣivargāṃstānamṛtaṃ cāharadbalī \|*  
*ānayaṃtaṃ ca pīyūṣaṃ khagaṃ gatvā śatakratuḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

*airāvataṃ samārūḍho vākyametaduvāca ha \|*  
*khagarūpadharaḥ kastvaṃ pīyūṣaṃ harase balāt \|\| 149 \|\|*

*apriyaṃ sarvadevānāṃ kṛtvā jīve ratiḥ katham \|*  
*viśikhairagnisaṃkāśairnayāmi yamamaṃdiram \|\| 150 \|\|*

148-149a. The powerful one, killed the group of protectors and snatched the nectar. Indra, mounted upon Airāvata, going to the bird, bringing the nectar, said these words:

149b-150. ‘Who are you, that having taken up the form of a bird, are forcibly snatching nectar? Doing what is not liked by all gods, how do you (still) have attachment for life? I shall take you to Yama’s abode (by striking you) with arrows resembling fire.’

## \|\| 47.151 \|\|

*śrutvā vākyaṃ hareḥ kopāduvāca sa mahābalaḥ \|*  
*nayāmi tava pīyūṣaṃ darśayasva parākramam \|\| 151 \|\|*

151\. Hearing the words of Hari (i.e. Indra) the mighty (bird) angrily said: ‘I shall carry (away) your nectar; show (me) your valour’.

## \|\| 47.152 \|\|

*etacchrutvā mahābāhurjaghāna viśikhaiḥ śitaiḥ \|*  
*yathāmerugireḥ śṛṃgaṃ toyavarṣeṇa toyadaḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. Hearing this, the mighty-armed (Indra) struck (him) with sharp arrows, as a cloud would strike the peak of mountain Meru with the shower of water.

## \|\| 47.153 \|\|

*nakhairaśanisaṃkāśairbibheda garuḍo gajam \|*  
*mātali ca rathaṃ cakraṃ tathā devānpurassarān \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Garuḍa, with his nails like the thunderbolt, pierced the elephant (i.e. Airāvata), and also Mātali (the charioteer of Indra), (Indra’s) chariot, (his) disc, and the advancing gods.

## \|\| 47.154 \|\|

*vyathitosau mahābāhurmātalirgajapuṃgavaḥ \|*  
*vimukhāḥ pakṣavātena sarve devagaṇāstadā \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. That Mātali of great arms was afflicted; (and also) the best elephant. Then all the hosts of gods were made to turn away their faces with the wind produced by his wings.

## \|\| 47.155 \|\|

*tatastu kopito jiṣṇurjaghānakuliśena tam \|*  
*kuliśasyāvapātena na ca kṣubdho mahākhagaḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. Then angry (Indra), desiring to win, struck him with his thunderbolt; (but) the great bird was not disturbed by the fall of the thunderbolt.

## \|\| 47.156 \|\|

*svaṃ moghaṃ bhiduraṃ dṛṣṭvā harirbhīto'bhavattadā \|*  
*saṃnivṛtya tato yuddhāttatraivāṃtaradhīyata \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Noticing that his thunderbolt was ineffective Indra became afraid. Withdrawing from the battle then, he disappeared there only.

## \|\| 47.157 \|\|

*sutarāmapigacchaṃtaṃ vegādbhūtalamāgataḥ \|*  
*abravītsa suraśreṣṭhaḥ sarvadevagaṇāgrataḥ \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. Moving speedily, he came down to the earth. The best of gods (i.e. Indra again) said to (Garuḍa) in front of the entire host of gods:

## \|\| 47.158-159 \|\|

*śakra uvāca \|*  
*yadi dāsyasi pīyūṣamidānīṃ nāgamātari \|*  
*bhujagāścāmarāḥ sarve kriyaṃte hi dhruvaṃ tayā \|\| 158 \|\|*

*pratijñā te bhavennaṣṭā na phalaṃ jīvitasya te \|*  
*tasmādidaṃ hariṣyāmi saṃmatena tavānagha \|\| 159 \|\|*

Śakra (i.e. Indra) said:

158-159. If you now give the nectar to the mother of serpents, she will certainly make all serpents immortal. Your pledge will be null and void; (and) you will not get the fruit of your life. Therefore, O sinless one, with your consent I shall take it away.

## \|\| 47.160 \|\|

*garutmānuvāca \|*  
*yasminkāle hyadāsī sā mātā me duḥkhitā satī \|*  
*viditā sarvalokeṣu hare'mṛtaṃ hariṣyasi \|\| 160 \|\|*

Garuḍa said:

160\. O Indra, you will take away the nectar at that time when it will be known in all the worlds that that unhappy mother of me is free from servitude.

## \|\| 47.161 \|\|

*evamuktvā mahāvīryo gatvovāca prasūṃ tadā \|*  
*ānītamamṛtaṃ mātastasyā eva pradīyatām \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. Saying so, the very powerful (Garuḍa), having gone to his mother, said to her: ‘O mother, I have brought the nectar. Give it to her only.’

## \|\| 47.162 \|\|

*protphullahṛdayā sā ca dṛṣṭvā putraṃ sahāmṛtam \|*  
*tāmāhūyāmṛtaṃ datvā cādāsītāṃ tadā gatā \|\| 162 \|\|*

162\. With her heart blooming (with joy), and seeing her son with the nectar, she called her (i.e. Kadrū), and having given it to her, then became free from servitude.

## \|\| 47.163 \|\|

*tṛṇakāṣṭhāni bhūtāni paśavaśca sarīsṛpāḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā savismayāssarve devā maharṣayastadā \|\| 163 \|\|*

163\. Seeing that grass, wood, beings, beasts and reptiles, as well as gods with great sages were amazed.

## \|\| 47.164-166 \|\|

*mocayitvā tu tāmaṃbāṃ garuḍaḥ suṣṭhutāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare śakro jahāra sahasā sudhām \|\| 164 \|\|*

*nidhāya garalaṃ tatra tayā cānupalakṣitaḥ \|*  
*prahṛṣṭahṛdayā kadrūḥ putrānāhūya saṃbhramāt \|\| 165 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ mukhe dadau hṛṣṭā kṣveḍaṃ cāmṛtalakṣaṇam \|*  
*tānuvāca prasūḥ putrānyuṣmākaṃ ca kule sadā \|\| 166 \|\|*

164-165a. Having freed his mother (from bondage) Garuḍa was well (-disposed). In the meanwhile, Indra suddenly took away nectar and put poison there (i.e. in its place) without being noticed by her (i.e. Kadrū).

165b-166. Kadrū, with her heart pleased, hastily called her sons, and put the poison, having the characteristics of (i.e. resembling) nectar, into their mouths.

## \|\| 47.166-169 \|\|

*teṣāṃ mukhe dadau hṛṣṭā kṣveḍaṃ cāmṛtalakṣaṇam \|*  
*tānuvāca prasūḥ putrānyuṣmākaṃ ca kule sadā \|\| 166 \|\|*

*mukhe tiṣṭhantvamī daivā biṃdavaścastanirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*maharṣayastato devāḥ siddhagaṃdharvamānuṣāḥ \|\| 167 \|\|*

*ūcuḥssantu kule mātarasmākaṃ ca prasādataḥ \|*  
*nāgairvisarjitā devāḥ sasiddhā munayastathā \|\| 168 \|\|*

*jagmuḥ svamālayaṃ hṛṣṭā nāgāḥ pramuditāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare nāgāṃścakhāda garuḍo balāt \|\| 169 \|\|*

166b-167a. The mother (i.e. Kadrū) said to her sons: ‘Let these divine drops always remain in the mouths (of the members) of your family.’ They were happy.

167b-169. Great sages, gods, Siddhas, Gandharvas and human beings said: ‘O mother, let (these drops) be in (your) family by (i.e. as) our favour.’ Gods, with Siddhas and sages, dismissed by the serpents, gladly went home. The serpents were happy. In the meanwhile, Garuḍa forcibly ate up the serpents.

## \|\| 47.170-171 \|\|

*dikṣu palāyitāḥ śeṣāḥ parvateṣu vaneṣu ca \|*  
*sāgareṣu ca pātāle bileṣu tarukoṭare \|\| 170 \|\|*

*nibhṛteṣu nikuñjeṣu sthitāḥ sarpāśca nirvṛtāḥ \|*  
*bhujagāstasya bhakṣyāśca sadaiva vidhinirmitāḥ \|\| 171 \|\|*

170-171. The remaining serpents ran and remained in various directions, mountains and forests, oceans, the nether worlds, holes and hollows of trees, and lonely bowers. The serpents are always his (Garuḍa’s) food, created by the creator.

## \|\| 47.172 \|\|

*sa khādayitvā nāgāṃśca saṃbhāṣya pitarāvatha \|*  
*vibudhānpūjayitvā tu jagāma harimavyayam \|\| 172 \|\|*

172\. He (i.e. Garuḍa) having eaten the serpents, and having worshipped the gods, went to the immutable Hari (i.e. (Viṣṇu)

## \|\| 47.173 \|\|

*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi suparṇacaritaṃ śubham \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ suraloke mahīyate \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. He, who reads or listens to this auspicious account of Garuḍa, will be free from all sins and honoured in heaven.”

## Chapter 48 - Importance of Bull (and Cow)

## \|\| 48.1-4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ tu viprarṣe cāṃḍālapatito dvijaḥ \|*  
*pralapya ca bahūnśokānjagāma kaśyapaṃ munim \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gatvovāca muniśreṣṭha vadāsmākaṃ hitaṃ vacaḥ \|*  
*yathā pāpādvimucyehaṃ muniśreṣṭha tathā kuru \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tamuvāca mahātejā īṣaddhāsyaḥ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*kaśyapa uvāca \|*  
*saṃdarśanācca mlecchānāmupaśāṃtosi vai svayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gāyatryāśca japairhomairvrataiścāṃdrāyaṇadibhiḥ \|*  
*smara nityaṃ hareḥ pādamupoṣya harivāsaram \|\| 4 \|\|*

Brahma said:

1-3a. O brāhmaṇic sage (Nārada), and hereafter, that brāhmaṇa who had fallen among the cāṇḍālas, lamented in various ways and went to sage Kaśyapa. Having gone to him, he said: “O best sage, tell me words beneficial to me (i.e. Instruct me in such a way that I would fare well in life). O greatest sage, act in such a way that I would be free from sin.”

The (sage) of great lustre, smiling a little said:

Kaśyapa said:

3b-4. After having seen the Mlecchas you yourself have become calm. Fasting on the day sacred to Hari, always remember Hari (i. e. Viṣṇu) by muttering the Gāyatri (hymn), (other) hymns, and by vows like Cāṇḍrāyaṇa.

## \|\| 48.5 \|\|

*aharniśaṃ harerdhyānaṃ praṇāmaṃ kuru taṃ prabhum \|*  
*tīrthasnānena maṃtreṇa paṃkasyāṃtaṃ gamiṣyasi \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Day and night meditate upon Śaṅkara, and salute that lord. By means of a bath at a sacred place and by means of (reciting) hymns, you will see end of the mud (of sin).

## \|\| 48.6 \|\|

*tataḥ pāpakṣayādeva brāhmaṇatvaṃ ca lapsyase \|*  
*vratairvṛṣādhikairmokṣaṃ nāśayankalmaṣaṃ dvija \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then O brāhmaṇa, destroying your sins by means of vows with more virtue, you will get (back) your brāhmaṇahood and salvation as a result of the destruction of sins.

## \|\| 48.7 \|\|

*munestasya vacaḥ śrutvā kṛtakṛtyo'bhavattadā \|*  
*puṇyaṃ sa vividhaṃ kṛtvāpunarbrahmatvamāptavān \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hearing the words of the sage, he then became satisfied. Having done various deeds of merit, he again obtained brāhmaṇahood.

## \|\| 48.8-9 \|\|

*tatastaptvā tapastīvraṃsvarlokaṃ ciramabhyagāt \|*  
*sadvṛttasyākhilaṃ pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti dine dine \|\| 8 \|\|*

*asadvṛttasya puṇyaṃ hi kṣayaṃ yātyaṃjanopamam \|*  
*anācārāddhato vipra ācārātsuratāṃ vrajet \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then having practised a severe penance he obtained heaven after a long time. All sin of a virtuous person perishes day by day; (but) the merit of a man of bad conduct perishes like collyrium. A brāhmaṇa miserable due to bad conduct, would go to (i.e. obtain) godhead by (good) conduct.

## \|\| 48.10 \|\|

*tataḥ kaṃṭhagataiḥ prāṇairācāraṃ kurute dvijaḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasāṃgena sadācāraṃ sadā kuru \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then a brāhmaṇa (even) with his life at the point of departing, practises (good) deeds. So always do good deed mentally and physically.

## \|\| 48.11-12 \|\|

*kaśyapasyopadeśena sa vinīto'bhavaddvijaḥ \|*  
*ācāraṃ tu punaḥ kṛtvā tapastaptatvā divaṃ gataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*anācārī hato vipraḥ svargalokeṣu garhitaḥ \|*  
*ācāraṃ tu punaḥ kṛtvā suraloke mahīyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. By the advice of Kaśyapa, that brāhmaṇa became disciplined; and again conducting himself well, and having practised penance, he went to heaven. A brāhmaṇa of a bad conduct is doomed and condemned in heaven; but conducting himself well he is honoured.

## \|\| 48.13 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti gatiṃ lokāḥ pūjayitvā dvijottamān \|*  
*dvijānāṃ pīḍanaṃ kṛtvā gatiṃ gacchati kāṃ prabho \|\| 13 \|\|*

Nārada said:

13\. People get a good position (like salvation) after having worshipped best brāhmaṇas. O lord, what position does one get by troubling brāhmaṇas?

Brahmā said;

## \|\| 48.14 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*kṣudhā saṃtaptadehānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*nārcayecchaktito bhaktyā sa yāti narakaṃ naraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. That man, who does not devoutly and according to his capacity worship great-souled brāhmaṇas whose bodies are tormented by hunger, goes to hell.

## \|\| 48.15 \|\|

*paruṣeṇa krośayitvā krodhādyastu visarjayet \|*  
*sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ mahārauravakṛcchrakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. He, who, having made (a brāhmaṇa) scream by using harsh (words), dismisses him angrily, goes to the painful and terrible hell like Mahāraurava.

## \|\| 48.16 \|\|

*sannivṛttastataḥ kīṭādyantyajātiṣu jāyate \|*  
*tato rogī daridrastu kṣudhayā paripīḍitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Returning from there he is born in the lowest species, like the insects. Then he becomes a diseased, poor person oppressed by hunger.

## \|\| 48.17-20 \|\|

*nāvamanyettato vipraṃ kṣudhayā gṛhamāgatam \|*  
*na dadāmīti yo brūyāddevāgnibrāhmaṇeṣu saḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tiryagyoniśataṃ gatvā cāṃḍālyamupagacchati \|*  
*pādamudyamya yo vipraṃ haṃti gāṃ pitarau gurum \|\| 18 \|\|*

*raurave niyato vāsastasya nāstīha niṣkṛtiḥ \|*  
*yadi puṇyādbhavejjanma sa eva paṃgutāṃ vrajet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*atidīno viṣādī ca duḥkhaśokābhipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ janmatrayaṃ prāpya bhavettasya ca niṣkṛtiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-18a Therefore one should not insult a brāhmaṇa who being oppressed with hunger, has come to his house. He, who says, ‘I shall not give’ to gods, fire and brāhmaṇas, having gone through a hundred of animal-births, becomes (i.e. is born as) a cāṇḍāla.

18b-19a. He who kicks a brāhmaṇa, or a cow or his preceptor, certainly lives in the Raurava hell; for him there is no acquittal.

19b-20. If through merit he gets (a human) birth (i.e. is born as a human being), he would be crippled. He becomes very wretched, is dejected and oppressed by grief. Getting three births like this, he may then get acquittal.

## \|\| 48.21 \|\|

*muṣṭicapeṭakīlaiśca hanyādvipraṃ tu yaḥ pumān \|*  
*tāpane raurave ghore kalpāṃtaṃ sopi tiṣṭhati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. That man too who strikes a brāhmaṇa with fists, or with blows, with elbows or open hands remains till the end of the Kalpa in the burning Raurava hell.

## \|\| 48.22 \|\|

*atha janma samāsādya kukkuraḥ krūracaṃḍakaḥ \|*  
*aṃtyajātiṣu jātopi daridraḥ kukṣiśūlavān \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Then he getting the birth (of) a cruel and violent dog, is after that born in the low castes as a poor man, suffering from pain in the belly.

## \|\| 48.23-25 \|\|

*pādamudyacchate vā yastasya pāde śilīpadaḥ \|*  
*khaṃjo vā maṃdajaṃgho vā khaṇḍapādo bhavennaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pakṣavātena cāṃgāni prakaṃpaṃte sadaiva hi \|*  
*mātaraṃ pitaraṃ vipraṃ snātakaṃ ca tapasvinam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*hatvā gurugaṇaṃ krodhātkuṃbhīpāke ciraṃ bhavet \|*  
*uṣitvā caiva jāyeta kīṭajātiṣu tatparam \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-24a. The man who raises his foot (to kick a brāhmaṇa) has śilīpada (i.e. elephantiasis) on his foot. Such a man becomes lame, or short-legged or has his foot amputated; or his limbs tremble due to paralysis.

24b-25. He, who, through anger, strikes his mother, father, a brāhmaṇa who has just returned from his preceptor’s house or an ascetic or a group of preceptors would live in the Kumbhīpāka hell for a long time; and having lived there, would thereafter be born in the species of worms.

## \|\| 48.26-27 \|\|

*viruddhaṃ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ yo vadeddhi dvijātiṣu \|*  
*aṣṭau kuṣṭhāḥ prajāyaṃte tasya dehe dṛḍhaṃ suta \|\| 26 \|\|*

*vicarcikātha dadrūśca maṃḍalaḥ śukti sidhmakau \|*  
*kālakuṣṭhastathā śuklastaruṇaścātidāruṇaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. He, who would talk hostile or harsh words to brāhmaṇas, would definitely have eight kinds of leprosy on his body, O son. They are: itch\[3\], cutaneous eruption\[4\], leprosy with circular spots\[5\], types of leprosy called Śukti\[6\] and Sidhmaka, Kālakuṣṭha, Śukla, and the very terrible progressive leprosy.

## \|\| 48.28 \|\|

*tato bhiṣakprayoge ca pāpātpuṇyaṃ palāyate \|*  
*apuṇyājjalarekheva tenaiva nidhanaṃ vrajet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Then after use of drugs, merit runs away due to sin; and due to want of merit he would die as a line on water (disappears).

## \|\| 48.29 \|\|

*eṣāṃ madhye mahākuṣṭhāstraya eva prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kālakuṣṭhastathā śuklastaruṇaścātidāruṇaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Among these (various kinds of leprosy) only three are said to be major (forms of) leprosy: Kālakuṣṭha, Śukla and the very terrible Taruṇa (i.e. progressive).

## \|\| 48.30 \|\|

*mahāpātakabhāvānāṃ jñānātsaṃsargatopi vā \|*  
*atipātakināmeva trayo dehe bhavaṃti vai \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. These three appear on the body of great sinners only due to the presence of great sins or due to contagion (with lepers).

## \|\| 48.31 \|\|

*saṃsargātsahasaṃbaṃdhādrogaḥ saṃcarate nṛṇām \|*  
*dūrātparityajeddhīraḥ spṛṣṭvā snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. People contract (this) disease by contagion or contact. A wise man should avoid (the lepers) from a distance; (and) should bathe after having touched (i.e. if he touches) them.

## \|\| 48.32 \|\|

*patitaṃ kuṣṭhasaṃyuktaṃ cāṃḍālaṃ ca gavāśinam \|*  
*śvānaṃ rajasvalāṃ bhillaṃ spṛṣṭvā snānaṃ samācaret \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A man should bathe after having touched (i.e. if he touches) a fallen man, or a leper, or a cāṇḍāla eating the flesh of cows, or a dog, or a woman in her menses, or a bhilla.

## \|\| 48.33 \|\|

*duritasyānurūpeṇa dehe kuṣṭhā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*ihaloke paratraivāpyatra nāsti tu saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The various kinds of leprosy settle on the body, here or in the next world, according to the sin (committed by a person). There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 48.34 \|\|

*nyāyenopārjitāṃ vṛttiṃ brahmasvaṃ harate tu yaḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ narakaṃ prāpya punarjanma na vidyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He who snatches a brāhmaṇa’s wealth—his livelihood earned justly—gets unfailing hell (i.e. certainly goes to hell), and is not reborn (i.e. permanently lives in hell).

## \|\| 48.35 \|\|

*piśuno yastu viprāṇāṃ raṃdhrānveṣaṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*taṃ dṛṣṭvāpyathavā spṛṣṭvā sacelo jalamāviśet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Having seen or touched a wicked man, who is intent upon finding the weak points of brāhmaṇas, a man should enter water (i.e. should bathe) with his clothes on.

## \|\| 48.36 \|\|

*brahmasvaṃ praṇayādbhuktaṃ dahatyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|*  
*vikrameṇa tu bhuṃjāno daśapūrvāndaśāparān \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. (If) a brāhmaṇa’s wealth (deposited with one) in confidence is enjoyed by one, it would burn one’s family upto the seventh (generation). A man who enjoys it after having snatched it by overpowering a brāhmaṇa burns ten preceding and ten succeeding (generations).

## \|\| 48.37 \|\|

*na viṣaṃ viṣamityāhurbrahmasvaṃ viṣamucyate \|*  
*viṣamekākinaṃ haṃti brahmasvaṃ putrapautrakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. It is not poison that is called poison; but it is a brāhmaṇa’s wealth that is called poison. Poison kills one man only; but a brāhmaṇa’s wealth kills his sons and grandsons (also).

## \|\| 48.38 \|\|

*mohācca mātaraṃ gatvā brāhmaṇīṃ ca gurostriyam \|*  
*patitvā raurave ghore punarutpattidurlabhaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. A man, who through ignorance cohabits with his mother or a brāhmaṇa woman or his preceptor’s wife, falls into the terrible Raurava (hell) and finds rebirth difficult.

## \|\| 48.39-44 \|\|

*pataṃti pitarastasya kuṃbhīpāketha tāpane \|*  
*avīcikālasūtre ca mahārauravaraurave \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kadācidapi vā teṣāṃ niṣkṛtiṃ nānumenire \|*  
*prāṇaṃ hatvā dvijātīnāṃ svayaṃ yātyapunarbhavam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pataṃti puruṣāstasya raurave ca sahasraśaḥ \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva viprāṇāṃ vadhe ca pātakaṃ samam \|\| 41 \|\|*

*viṣamaṃ vā kutastiṣṭhettattvato vaktumarhasi \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*hatvā vipraṃ dhruvaṃ putra pātakaṃ yadudāhṛtam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*labhate brahmahā ghoraṃ vaktavyaṃ cāparaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*lakṣakoṭisahasrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vadhaṃ bhajet \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vedaśāstrayutaṃ hatvā śrotriyaṃ vijiteṃdriyam \|*  
*vipraṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ hatvā tasmāddaśaguṇottaram \|\| 44 \|\|*

39-40a. His manes fall into the (hells called) Kumbhipāka, Tapana, Avīci, Kālasūtra, Mahāraurava and Raurava; and they (i.e. great sages) have never granted acquittal from these.

40b-41a. He who takes away the life of a brāhmaṇa (goes to hell and) is never reborn (i.e. permanently slays in hell). Thousands of his men (i.e. relatives) fall into the Raurava hell.

Nārada said:

41b-42a. Please tell me if the sin for the murder of all brāhmaṇas is the same or why some sin becomes fearful.

Brahmā said:

42b-43a. O son, listen to the fearful sin; that is said to be a sin, which a brāhmaṇacide obtains by killing a brāhmaṇa and which is to be told hereafter.

43b-44. The sin that a man would get due to having killed a learned, restrained brāhmaṇa, who is endowed with (the knowledge of) the Vedas, is equal to the sin that he would have by killing lakhs of crores of thousands of brāhmaṇas. It would be tenfold of this by killing (i.e. if a man kills a brāhmaṇa who is) a Viṣṇu’s devotee.

## \|\| 48.45 \|\|

*svavaṃśānpātayitvā tu punarjanma na viṃdate \|*  
*trivedaṃ snātakaṃ hatvā vadhasyāṃtaṃ na vindate \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Causing the members of his family to fall he does not get rebirth (i.e. lives in hell permanently). There is no end to (the sin accrued by) the killing of (a brāhmaṇa) well-versed in three Vedas.

## \|\| 48.46 \|\|

*śrotriyaṃ ca sadācāraṃ tīrthamaṃtraprapūtakam \|*  
*īdṛśaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ hantuḥ pāpasyāṃto na vidyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. There is no end to the sin of a man who kills a brāhmaṇa who is learned, whose conduct is good and who is purified by sacred hymns and (bathes at) sacred places.

## \|\| 48.47 \|\|

*apakāraṃ samuddiśya dvijaḥ prāṇānparityajet \|*  
*dṛśyate yena cānyena brahmahā sa bhavennaraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. That man, who sees a brāhmaṇa who ends his life on account of an injury, would be the killer of a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 48.48 \|\|

*vacobhiḥ paruṣairvṛttaiḥ pīḍitastāḍito dvijaḥ \|*  
*yamuddiśya tyajetprāṇāṃstamāhurbrahmaghātinam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. That man, on account of whom, a brāhmaṇa is harassed with harsh words or behaviour or is beaten up is called the killer of a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 48.49 \|\|

*ṛṣayo munayo devāḥ sarve brahmavidastathā \|*  
*deśānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca sa ca vadhyo bhavediha \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Here (i.e. in this world) that killing would be the killing of all the sages, ascetics, gods, the knowers of Brahman of (various) countries and kings.

## \|\| 48.50-52 \|\|

*ato brahmavadhaṃ prāpya pitṛbhiḥ saha pacyate \|*  
*prāyopaveśakaṃ vipraṃ budhaḥ saṃmānayeddhruvam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*doṣaiścāpi vinirmuktamuddiśya prāṇamutsṛjet \|*  
*sa pralipto vadhairghorairna tu yaṃ parikīrtayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ātmaghātaṃ drumārohaṃ koṭarai rūpajīvinaṃ \|*  
*yaḥ kuryādātmanoghātaṃ svavaṃśe brahmahā bhavet \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. So a man who gets (i.e. commits the sin of) killing a brāhmaṇa is roasted (in a hell) with (his) dead ancestors. A man should certainly honour a brāhmaṇa fasting himself unto death; and if he, free from sins, casts, his life for that man, he is smeared with (the sin of) terrible murders and not he whom he would tell about committing suicide, climbing up a tree or living by hollows of trees. He who would commit suicide would be the killer of a brāhmaṇa in his (own) family.

## \|\| 48.53 \|\|

*bhrūṇaṃ ca ghātayedyastu śiśuṃ vā āturaṃ gurum \|*  
*brahmahā svayameva syānna tu yaṃ parikīrtayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. He who causes abortion or kills a child or his sick preceptor, is himself the killer of a brāhmaṇa, and not he whom he mentions.

## \|\| 48.54 \|\|

*mārayecca sagotraṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ brāhmaṇādhamaḥ \|*  
*tasyaiva tadbhavetpāpaṃ na tu yaṃ parikīrttayet \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. That mean brāhmaṇa, who kills a brāhmaṇa with his family, alone gets the sin and not he whom he mentions.

## \|\| 48.55 \|\|

*pīḍayitvā dvijaṃ śūdraḥ svakāryaṃ cāpi sādhayet \|*  
*tatrāpāpe ca śūdrasya pātakaṃ nānyathā bhavet \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The sin of a Śūdra, who accomplishes his object by killing a Brāhmaṇa does not become otherwise (i.e. does not lessen) since the Brāhmaṇa is innocent.

## \|\| 48.56 \|\|

*tātkālika vadhaṃ hatvā haṃtāramātatāyinaṃ \|*  
*na ca haṃtā ca tatpāpairlipyate dvijasattama \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. O best of brāhmaṇas, the killer, who kills a desperado (ātatāyin) instantly appearing, is not smeared (i.e. tainted) with sins.

## \|\| 48.57 \|\|

*ātatāyinamāyāṃtamapi vedāṃtagaṃ raṇe \|*  
*jighāṃsaṃtaṃ jighāṃsecca na tena brahmahā bhavet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A man may kill in battle a brāhmaṇa desperado, desiring to kill, even though the desperado is a master of Vedanta. By (doing) that (act) he does not become the killer of a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 48.58 \|\|

*agnido garadaścaiva dhanahārī ca suptaghaḥ \|*  
*kṣetradārāpahārī ca ṣaḍete hyātatāyinaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. These six are desperados: One who sets fire, one who administers poison, one who snatches (anothers’ wealth), one who kills a person who is asleep, one who usurps another’s field or one who kidnaps another’s wife.

## \|\| 48.59 \|\|

*khalo rājavadhodyogī pitṝṇāṃ ca vadhe rataḥ \|*  
*anuyāyī nṛpo rājñaścatvāraścātatāyinaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. These four (also) are desperados: a wicked man, one who undertakes to kill a king, one who is intent on killing one’s forefathers, a king who is a follower of another king.

## \|\| 48.60 \|\|

*tatkṣaṇānna mṛtaṃ vipraṃ punarhaṃtuṃ na yujyate \|*  
*purnahatvā vadhaṃ ghoraṃ jñānātprāpnoti niścitaṃ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. If a brāhmaṇa is not killed instantly it is not proper (to strike) to kill him again. By killing (i.e. by striking him again to kill) him a man definitely obtains sin due to his knowledge (that the brāhmaṇa was not instantly killed).

## \|\| 48.61 \|\|

*loke viprasamo nāsti pūjanīyo jagadguruḥ \|*  
*hatvā taṃ yadbhavetpāpaṃ tatparaṃ ca na vidyate \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. In the world there is none else, who, being the preceptor of the world, is fit for being worshipped. There is no greater sin than the sin which one gets by killing him.

## \|\| 48.62 \|\|

*devavatpūjanīyosau devāsuragaṇairnaraiḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya samo nāsti triṣu lokeṣu niścitaṃ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. He is fit to be worshipped like a deity by the hosts of gods and demons and by men. It is certain that there is none else who is equal to a brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 48.63 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*kāṃ vṛttiṃ samupāśritya jīvitavyaṃ dvijena hi \|*  
*apānena suraśreṣṭha tatvato vaktumarhasi \|\| 63 \|\|*

Nārada said:

63\. O best of gods, tell me accurately, following which profession a sinless brāhmaṇa should live.

## \|\| 48.64-65 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ayācitā ca yā bhikṣā praśastā sā prakīrtitā \|*  
*uñchavṛttistato bhadrā subhadrā sarvavṛttiṣu \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yāmāśritya muniśreṣṭhā gacchaṃti brahmaṇaḥ padam \|*  
*dakṣiṇā yajñaśeṣāṇāṃ grāhyā yajñagatena hi \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. That alms which is got without asking for is said to be commendable. Living by gleaning grains is better than that; it is the best of all kinds of livelihood, resorting to which the best sages go to the position of Brahman. A brāhmaṇa visiting a sacrifice should accept the fees offered as a remnant of (i e. offered at the end of) the sacrifice.

## \|\| 48.66 \|\|

*pāṭhanaṃ yājanaṃ kṛtvā grahītavyaṃ dhanaṃ dvijaiḥ \|*  
*pāṭhayitvā paṭhitvā ca kṛtvā svastyayanaṃ śubhaṃ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Brāhmaṇas should get money by reciting (Vedic texts) to others and by acting as priests at sacrifices. Reciting (Vedic texts to others), reciting them to themselves and averting evil by means of reciting sacred texts—this is the way of the life of brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 48.67 \|\|

*brāhmaṇānāmidaṃ jīvyaṃ śiṣṭā vṛttiḥ pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*śāstropajīvino dhanyā dhanyā vṛkṣopajīvinaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Accepting presents is a respectable way of life. Those who maintain themselves by the study of religious texts are blessed; so also are those who live by (eating the fruits of) trees.

## \|\| 48.68-69 \|\|

*dhanyā vṛkṣalatājīvyā vāṭīsasyopajīvinaḥ \|*  
*anna jaṃtu vadhe pāpaṃ tasya doṣopaśāṃtaye \|\| 68 \|\|*

*navadhānyāni śastāni viprebhyaḥ saṃpradāpayet \|*  
*na cetprāṇivadhe hyatra kṣīyaṃte cāyuṣo dhruvaṃ \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Those who live on the products of trees and creepers are blessed; so also are those who live on the crop (growing by the side) of roads. Killing for food is a sin. For its alleviation one should give excellent fresh grains to brāhmaṇas. Otherwise, here i.e. in the case of the murder of a being, there is the shortening of one’s life.

## \|\| 48.70 \|\|

*tasmāddadyātsubahūni pitṛdevadvijātiṣu \|*  
*abhāvātkṣattriyāvṛttirbrāhmaṇairūpajīvyate \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Therefore one should give profusely to the manes, deities and brāhmaṇas. In the absence (of a brāhmaṇa’s profession), the profession of a kṣatriya is followed by brāhmaṇas.

## \|\| 48.71-75 \|\|

*nyāyayuddheṣu yoddhavyaṃ caredvīravrataṃ śubham \|*  
*sa tayā ca dvijo vṛtyā yaddhanaṃ labhate nṛpāt \|\| 71 \|\|*

*pitṛyajñādidāneṣu medhyaṃ taddhanamucyate \|*  
*samabhyaseddhanurvidyāṃ vedayuktāṃ sadānaghaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*śaktikuṃtagadākhaḍga parighāṇāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*aśvārohaṃ gajārohamaiṃdrajālamamānakaṃ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*rathabhūmigataṃ yuddhaṃ yuktaṃ sarvatra kārayet \|*  
*dvija deva dhruvāṇāṃ ca strīṇāṃ vṛttaṃ tapasvinām \|\| 74 \|\|*

*sādhu sādhvī gurūṇāṃ ca nṛpāṇāṃ rakṣaṇāddhruvam \|*  
*yatpuṇyaṃ labhyate śūraiḥ kathaṃ tadbrahmavādibhiḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

71-72a. A brāhmaṇa should fight in righteous battles (and thus) should practise the auspicious vow of a hero. The wealth which a brāhmaṇa gets from the king by following that profession (ofa warrior), is said to be pure (when spent) in giving presents at sacrifices in honour of manes (i.e. at śrāddhas) etc.

72b-74a. An innocent brāhmaṇa should always study archery along with the Vedas. He should fully (use) the missile called Śakti, a spear, a mace, a sword, and an iron bar; he should everywhere fight by mounting a horse, or an elephant or by using war-tricks, or fight by mounting upon a chariot or standing on ground.

74b-75. How can that religious merit be obtained by the expounders of Veda, (which merit) is certainly obtained by the brave men by protecting brāhmaṇas, gods, heaven, women, ascetics, good men and women, preceptors and kings?

## \|\| 48.76-79 \|\|

*sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā sokṣayaṃ svargamaśnute \|*  
*sammukhe nyāyayuddhe ca pataṃti brāhmaṇā raṇe \|\| 76 \|\|*

*te vrajaṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ na gamyaṃ brahmavādināṃ \|*  
*dharmayuddhasya yadvṛttaṃ śṛṇu puṇyaṃ yathārthataḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*saṃmukhena prayudhyaṃte na ca gacchaṃti kātaraṃ \|*  
*na bhagnaṃ pṛṣṭhato ghnaṃti niḥśastraṃ prapalāyitam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*ayudhyamānaṃ bhīruṃ ca patitaṃ gatakalmaṣaṃ \|*  
*asacchūdraṃ stutiprītamāhave śaraṇāgatam \|\| 79 \|\|*

76-77a. Having exhausted all his sins, he obtains heaven permanently. The brāhmaṇas who fall (i.e. are killed) in a battle (while fighting) face to face, go to the highest place, inaccessible to the expounders of Veda.

77b-79. Now listen to the proper description of a righteous war. They (who fight justly) fight face to face, do not attack a coward, do not pursue the enemy who is vanquished, or who does not have a weapon, or who flees (from the battlefield), or who does not fight, who is afraid, who has fallen or who is sinless, who is a bad śūdra, who is pleased with praise, or who has sought shelter or who has surrendered in a battle.

## \|\| 48.80-81 \|\|

*hatvā ca narakaṃ yāṃti durvṛttā jayakāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*eṣā ca kṣattriyā vṛttiḥ sadācāraistu gīyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

*yāmāśritya divaṃ yāṃti sarvakṣatriyakuṃjarāḥ \|*  
*dharmayuddhe śubho mṛtyuḥ saṃmukhe kṣattriyasya ca \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Those of a bad conduct, who, desiring victory kill (such a person) go to hell. This is the kṣatriya way of life and is praised by people of good conduct, resorting to which all best kṣatriyas go to heaven. The death of a kṣatriya (while fighting) face to face in a just war is auspicious.

## \|\| 48.82-83 \|\|

*atra pūto bhavetsopi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*sa tiṣṭhetsvargaloke ca prāsāde ratnabhūṣite \|\| 82 \|\|*

*jāṃbūnadamayastaṃbhe ratnabhūṣitabhūtale \|*  
*iṣṭadravyaiḥ susaṃpūrṇe divyavastropaśobhite \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. He who is pure here, is also free from all sins, and dwells in heaven which is adorned with jewels, which has golden pillars, the ground of which is adorned with jewels, which is full of desired things, which is decorated with divine cloth.

## \|\| 48.84-87 \|\|

*purataḥ kalpavṛkṣāśca tiṣṭhaṃti sarvadāyinaḥ \|*  
*vāpīkūpataṭākādyairudyānairupaśobhite \|\| 84 \|\|*

*yauvanāḍhyāśca sevaṃte taṃ devapurakanyakāḥ \|*  
*tasyāgrato mudā nityaṃ nṛtyaṃtyapsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*gītaṃ gāyaṃti gaṃdharvā devāśca stutipāṭhakāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ krameṇa kalpāṃte sārvabhaumo bhavennṛpaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*sarvabhogaikakartā ca nīruṅmanmathavigrahaḥ \|*  
*tasya patnyaḥ prarūpāḍhyāḥ sadaiva yauvanānvitāḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

84-87. In front of it stand the desire-yielding trees giving everything. It is adorned with wells, tanks, etc. and gardens. Divine damsels endowed with youth wait upon him. Hosts of the celestial nymphs always joyfully dance before him. Gandharvas sing songs and gods praise him. Thus, in due course a man would become a sovereign emperor; he would all alone enjoy all pleasures, would be free from diseases, and would have Cupid’s body (i.e. would be very handsome). His wives would have excellent beauty and would always be endowed with youth.

## \|\| 48.88 \|\|

*dharmaśīlāḥ sutāḥ śubhrāḥ samṛddhāḥ pitṛsaṃmatāḥ \|*  
*evaṃ krameṇa bhuṃjaṃti saptajanmasu kṣatriyāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. His sons would be righteous, fair, rich and liked by parents. Thus good kṣatriyas enjoy (these pleasures) in due order for seven births.

## \|\| 48.89-93 \|\|

*anyāyena tu yoddhārastiṣṭhaṃti narake ciram \|*  
*evaṃ ca kṣatriyā vṛttirbrāhmaṇairupajīvyate \|\| 89 \|\|*

*vaiśyaiḥ śūdraistathānyaiśca aṃtyajairmlecchajātibhiḥ \|*  
*ye ca yodhāḥ prayudhyaṃte nyāyayuddhena sarvadā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*tepi yāṃti paraṃ sthānaṃ sarve varṇā dvijātayaḥ \|*  
*na śūro yo dvijo bhīrurastraśastravivarjitaḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

*vipattau vaiśyavṛtiṃ ca kārayeddvijasattamaḥ \|*  
*vaiśyavṛttiṃ vaṇigbhāvaṃ kṛṣiṃ caiva tathāparaiḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*kārayetkṛṣivāṇijyaṃ viprakarma na ca tyajet \|*  
*vaṇigbhāvānmṛṣātyuktau durgatiṃ prāpnuyāddvijaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

89-91 a. The warriors (fighting) unjustly dwell in hell for a long time. In this way the kṣatriya mode of life is practised by brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, by the low-born and by other mleccha-castes. All warriors of all castes (including) brāhmaṇas, who always fight justly, also go to the highest place.

9lb-93. That brāhmaṇa, the best one, who is not brave, who is timid and does not have (the knowledge of wielding) missiles and weapons, should follow the vaiśya way in a difficulty. Others may also follow the vaiśya way, or practise trade. A brāhmaṇa should practise agriculture or trade, but should not give up his duties as a brāhmaṇa. A brāhmaṇa will be meeting with a sad plight by telling false things and exaggerating on account of (i.e. for profit in) trade.

## \|\| 48.94-96 \|\|

*ārdradravyaṃ parityajya brāhmaṇo labhate śivam \|*  
*samutpādya tato vṛttiṃ dadyādviprāya sarvaśaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*pitṛyajñe tathā cāgnau juhuyādvidhivaddvijaḥ \|*  
*tule'satyaṃ na karttavyaṃ tulādharmapratiṣṭhitā \|\| 95 \|\|*

*chalabhāvaṃ tule kṛtvā narakaṃ pratipadyate \|*  
*atulaṃ cāpi yaddravyaṃ tatra mithyā parityajet \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. A brāhmaṇa, by giving up wet money (i.e. dakṣiṇā) gets an auspicious (place). Making his livelihood from that (i.e. trade), he should by all means give it (i.e. wealth gained by practising trade) to a brāhmaṇa. A brāhmaṇa should duly offer (oblations) at a śrāddha and into fire. He should not indulge in falsehood in balance (i.e. while weighing things), for balance (i.e. weighing correctly) is settled in (i.e. leads to) righteousness. Practising fraud in weighing he (i.e. one who practises fraud in weighing) goes to hell. In the case of those things also which are not weighed, he should avoid falsehood.

## \|\| 48.97-98 \|\|

*evaṃ mithyā na karttavyā mṛṣā pāpaprasūtikā \|*  
*nāsti satyātparodharmo nānṛtātpātakaṃ param \|\| 97 \|\|*

*ataḥ sarveṣu kāryeṣu satyameva viśiṣyate \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasraṃ tu satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam \|\| 98 \|\|*

97-98. Thus one should not practise falsehood, because falsehood produces sin. There is no greater merit than truth, (and) there is no greater sin than falsehood. Therefore in all acts truth alone is important. (If) the merit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and truth are weighed (together), truth is superior to a thousand horse-sacrifices.

## \|\| 48.99-100 \|\|

*aśvamedhasahasrāddhi satyameva viśiṣyate \|*  
*yo vadetsarvakāryeṣu satyaṃ mithyā parityajet \|\| 99 \|\|*

*sa nistarati durgāṇi svargamakṣayamaśnute \|*  
*vāṇijyaṃ kārayedvipro mithyā'vaśyaṃ parityajet \|\| 100 \|\|*

99-100. He, who, in all his acts, speaks the truth and avoids falsehood, crosses (i.e. overcomes) difficulties and eternally obtains (i.e. lives in) heaven. A brāhmaṇa should practise trade, (but) should certainly avoid falsehood.

## \|\| 48.101-105 \|\|

*vṛddhiṃ ca nikṣipettīrthe svayaṃ śeṣaṃ tu bhojayet \|*  
*dehakleśāttatsahasraguṇaṃ bhavati sarvadā \|\| 101 \|\|*

*arthārjanavidhau martyā viśaṃti viṣame jale \|*  
*kāṃtāramaṭavīṃ caiva śvāpadaiḥ sevitāṃ tathā \|\| 102 \|\|*

*giriṃ giriguhāṃ durgāṃ mlecchānāṃ śastrapātinām \|*  
*gṛhaṃ pratibhayaṃ sthānaṃ dhanalobhātsamaṃtataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

*sutadārānparityajya dūraṃ gacchaṃti lobhinaḥ \|*  
*skaṃdhe bhāraṃ vahaṃtyanye taryāṃ cakre nipātanaiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*kṣepaṇībhirmahāduḥkhaissadā prāṇavyayena ca \|*  
*arthasya saṃcayaḥ putra prāṇātpriyataro mahān \|\| 105 \|\|*

101-105. He should deposit the profit into (i.e. with) sacred places, and should himself eat the remaining (i.e. enjoy himself with what remains). It is thousandfold more meritorious than troubling the body. In the act of earning (i.e.for earning) money men, through greed for wealth, enter dangerous water, a forest and a jungle resorted to by wild beasts, a mountain, or an inaccessible mountain-cave, and also the house—a fearful abode—of mlecchas. Abandoning their sons and wives, the greedy go away (from their residences). Others carry burdens on their shoulders, or in a boat or on a wheel (i.e. a carriage); others (earn money) by killing (others) or by (using) slings, (thus suffering from) great agony, and always at the cost of their life. O son, hoarding money is dearer to men than their own life.

## \|\| 48.106 \|\|

*ebhirnyāyārjitaṃ vittaṃ vaṇigbhāvena yatnataḥ \|*  
*pitṛdevadvijātibhyo dattaṃ cākṣayamaśnute \|\| 106 \|\|*

106\. He, who, having carefully and justly earned money by (practising) these (vocations), gives it to the manes, deities and brāhmaṇas, gets eternal (happiness).

## \|\| 48.107-108 \|\|

*etau doṣau mahāṃtau ca vāṇijye lābhakarmaṇi \|*  
*lobhānāmaparityāgo mṛṣā grāhyaśca vikrayaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*etau doṣo parityajya kuryādarthārjanaṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*akṣayaṃ labhate dānādvaṇigdoṣairna lipyate \|\| 108 \|\|*

107-108. These two are great sins in trading, fraudulent purchase and sale. A wise man should make money by avoiding these two sins. He obtains eternal (happiness) and is not smeared (i.e. tainted) with the trader’s sins.

## \|\| 48.109 \|\|

*puṇyakarmarato vipraḥ kṛṣiṃ hi parikārayet \|*  
*vāhayeddivasasyārdhaṃ balīvardacatuṣṭayam \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. A brāhmaṇa engaged in doing virtuous acts, may (also) practise agriculture. He should drive four bulls for half the (part of a) day.

## \|\| 48.110 \|\|

*abhāvāttritayaṃ caiva aviśrāmaṃ na kārayet \|*  
*cārayecca tṛṇe'cchinnai coravyāghravivarjite \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. In the absence of four (he should employ) three. He should give them rest. He should graze them on uncut grass in a a place free from thieves and tigers.

## \|\| 48.111-112 \|\|

*dadyādghāsaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ ca nityamātarpayetsvayam \|*  
*goṣṭhaṃ ca kārayettasya kiṃcidvighnavivarjitam \|\| 111 \|\|*

*sadā gomayamūtrābhyāṃ vighasaiśca vivarjitam \|*  
*na malaṃ nikṣipedgoṣṭhe sarvadevaniketane \|\| 112 \|\|*

111-112. He should give (the bulls) an abode as desired (i.e. agreeable), and should himself gratify them. For a bull he should get prepared a cowpen free from trouble, and always free from cowdung, cow urine and leavings of food eaten. He should not put filth in the cowpen which is the abode of all gods.

## \|\| 48.113 \|\|

*ātmanaḥ śayanīyasya sadṛśaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*samaṃ nirvāpayedyatnācchītavātarajastathā \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. A wise man should get fashioned a cowpen like his own couch. He should make it completely free from cold air and dust.

## \|\| 48.114 \|\|

*prāṇasya sadṛśaṃ paśyedgāṃ ca sāmānyavigraham \|*  
*asya dehe sukhaṃduḥkhaṃ tathā tasyaiva kalpate \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. He should look upon the bull as his own life, and the bull’s body similar to his own. Pleasure and pain are possible in the bull’s body as in his own body.

## \|\| 48.115-116 \|\|

*anena vidhinā yastu kṛṣikarmāṇi kārayet \|*  
*sa ca govāhanairdoṣairna lipyeta dhanī bhavet \|\| 115 \|\|*

*durbalaṃ pīḍayedyastu tathaiva gadasaṃyutam \|*  
*atibālātivṛddhaṃ ca sa gohatyāṃ samālabhet \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. He, who practises agriculture in this manner, would not be smeared with the sins involved in driving bulls; he would be wealthy. He, who would trouble a weak bull or a sick one, and also a very young or a very old one, would kill (i.e. commit the sin of killing) a bull.

## \|\| 48.117 \|\|

*viṣamaṃ vāhayedyastu durbalaṃ sabalaṃ tathā \|*  
*sa gohatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ prāpnotīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. There is no doubt that he, who drives an uneven pair—a weak one and a strong one—commits the sin equal to that of (i.e. equal to that obtained by) killing a bull.

## \|\| 48.118 \|\|

*yo vāhayedvinā sasyaṃ khādaṃtaṃ gāṃ nivārayet \|*  
*mohāttṛṇaṃ jalaṃ vāpi sa gohatyāsamaṃ labhet \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. He who drives a bull without (feeding him with) grass, or he who prevents a bull who is eating (grass, from doing so), or keeps away through folly grass or water, commits a sin equal to that (of having killed a bull).

## \|\| 48.119 \|\|

*saṃkrāṃtyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ cāmāvāsyāyāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*halasya vāhanātpāpaṃ gavāmayutahatyayā \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Driving a plough on a saṃkrānti day or a full-moon day, or a new-moon day, brings in sin to one which is (equal to that brought in by) the murder of a myriad (bulls).

## \|\| 48.120 \|\|

*amūṣu pūjayedyastu sitaiścitrādibhirnaraḥ \|*  
*kajjalaiḥ kusumaistailaiḥ sokṣayaṃ svargamaśnute \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. The man, who, on these days, worships (a bull) with various kinds of sandals, collyriums, flowers and oils goes to (i.e. lives in) heaven eternally.

## \|\| 48.121-122 \|\|

*ghāsamuṣṭiṃ paragave yo dadāti sadāhnikam \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayasyasya svargaṃ cākṣayamaśnute \|\| 121 \|\|*

*yathā viprastathā gauśca dvayoḥ pūjāphalaṃ samam \|*  
*vicāre brāhmaṇo mukhyo nṛṇāṃ gāvaḥ paśau tathā \|\| 122 \|\|*

121-122. He who everyday gives a handful of grass to a bull, has all his sins destroyed and he obtains (i.e. lives in) heaven eternally. As a brāhmaṇa is, so is a bull; the fruit ofthe worship of both is the same. On thinking (it is clear that) a brāhmaṇa is the chief among men, and a bull among beasts.

## \|\| 48.123 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*vipro brahmamukhe jātaḥ kathito me tvayānagha \|*  
*kathaṃ gobhiḥ samo nātha vismayo me vidhe dhruvam \|\| 123 \|\|*

Nārada said:

123\. O innocent one, you had told me that a brāhmaṇa was born from the mouth of Brahmā. O lord, O creator, how is he then equal to bulls (i.e. a bull)? I have certainly a doubt.

## \|\| 48.124-125 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*śṛṇu cātra yathātathyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāṃ yathā \|*  
*ekapiṃḍakriyaikyaṃ tu puruṣairnirmitaṃ purā \|\| 124 \|\|*

*purā brahmamukhodbhūtaṃ kūṭaṃ tejomayaṃ mahat \|*  
*caturbhāgaprajātaṃ tadvedognirgaurdvijastathā \|\| 125 \|\|*

Brahmā said:

124-125. Listen to the fact about brāhmaṇas and bulls. Formerly men brought about the unity (between the two) by offering the funeral rice-ball to them. Formerly a great lustrous projection sprang up from the mouth of Brahmā. It became divided into four parts: Vedas, Agni (i.e. fire), Bull and Brāhmaṇa.

## \|\| 48.126 \|\|

*prāktejaḥ saṃbhavo vedo vahnireva tathaiva ca \|*  
*parato gaustathā vipro jātaścaiva pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. From the lustre the Veda rose first, and also Agni. Then Brāhmaṇa and Bull separately sprang up.

## \|\| 48.127 \|\|

*tatra sṛṣṭā mayā cādau vedāścatvāra ekaśaḥ \|*  
*sthityarthaṃ sarvalokānāṃ bhuvanānāṃ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. At that time, I first fashioned together the four Vedas for the stability of all the people and worlds everywhere.

## \|\| 48.128 \|\|

*agnirhavyāni bhuṃjīta devahetostathā dvijaḥ \|*  
*ājyaṃ goprabhavaṃ viddhi tasmādete prasūtakāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. Agni, and also the brāhmaṇa should enjoy the oblations (meant) for gods. Know that clarified butter is a product of the cow. Therefore they are begotten (from the same source).

## \|\| 48.129 \|\|

*na saṃti yadi lokeṣu catvāromī mahattarāḥ \|*  
*tadākhilaṃ ca bhuvanaṃ naṣṭaṃ sthāvarajaṃgamam \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. If these four more important ones are not there in the worlds, then the entire world and the immobile and the mobile are doomed.

## \|\| 48.130 \|\|

*ebhirdhṛtāḥ sadā lokāḥ pratiṣṭhaṃti svabhāvataḥ \|*  
*svabhāvo brahmarūposāvete brahmamayāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. The worlds always supported by these, remain in their natural condition. Natural condition is the nature of brahman. (So) they are said to be of the nature of Brahman.

## \|\| 48.131 \|\|

*tasmādgauḥ pūjanīyosau vipra devāsurairapi \|*  
*udāraḥ sarvakāryeṣu jātastathyo guṇākaraḥ \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. Therefore a bull should be worshipped even by gods and demons. He, the noble one, is born as the mine of excellences in all acts.

## \|\| 48.132 \|\|

*sarvadevamayaḥ sākṣātsarvasatvānukaṃpakaḥ \|*  
*asya kāryaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ puraiva poṣaṇaṃ prati \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. He is actually of the form of all gods. He feels compassion for all beings. I have formerly only made (i.e. laid down) his work with reference to nourishing.

## \|\| 48.133 \|\|

*ataeva mayā dattaṃ varaṃ cātisuśobhanam \|*  
*ekajanmani te mokṣastavāstviti viniścitam \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Therefore only I have given him a very auspicious boon. “It is certain that only in (i.e. after) one birth you will attain salvation.”

## \|\| 48.134 \|\|

*atraiva ye mṛtā gāvastvāgacchaṃti mamālayam \|*  
*pāpasya kaṇamātraṃ tu teṣāṃ dehena tiṣṭhati \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. All bulls that die here only will come to my abode. There will not be even an iota of sin on their bodies.

## \|\| 48.135 \|\|

*devī gaurdhenukā devāścādidevī triśaktikā \|*  
*prasādādyasya yajñānāṃ prabhavo hi viniścitaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. A cow is a goddess, (while) the bulls are gods; the first goddess has three powers. The rise of the sacrifices is certainly due to his favour.

## \|\| 48.136 \|\|

*gavāṃ sarvapavitrāṇi punaṃti sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*mūtraṃ gorgomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhisarpistathaiva ca \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. All (the products) of cows, viz. urine, dung, milk, curd, ghee, which are pure, purify the entire world.

## \|\| 48.137 \|\|

*amīṣāṃ bhakṣaṇe pāpaṃ na tiṣṭhati kalevare \|*  
*tasmādghṛtaṃ dadhi kṣīraṃ nityaṃ khādaṃti dhārmikāḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Sin does not remain in the body on eating (or drinking) these. Therefore the religious people always eat (or drink) ghee, curd and milk.

## \|\| 48.138 \|\|

*viśiṣṭaṃ sarvadravyeṣu gavyamiṣṭaṃ paraṃ śubham \|*  
*yasyāsye bhojanaṃ nāsti tasya mūrtistu pūtikā \|\| 138 \|\|*

138\. The product of cows is the best of all things, is desirable and is most auspicious. He, in whose mouth there is no food (containing the product of a cow), has a stinking figure.

## \|\| 48.139 \|\|

*annādyaṃ paṃcarātreṇa saptarātreṇa vai payaḥ \|*  
*dadhi viṃśatirātreṇa ghṛtaṃ syānmāsamekakam \|\| 139 \|\|*

139\. Food eaten is (effective) for five nights; milk for a month, curd for twenty nights; and ghee for a month.

## \|\| 48.140 \|\|

*agavyairyastu bhuṃkte vai māsamekaṃ niraṃtaram \|*  
*bhojane tasya martyasya pretāḥ khādaṃti caiva hi \|\| 140 \|\|*

140\. Evil spirits eat the meal of him (i.e. while he is eating), who eats his meals continuously for one month without using the products of cow.

## \|\| 48.141 \|\|

*paramānnaṃ paraṃ śuddhaṃ svinnaṃ cātapataṇḍulaiḥ \|*  
*bhuktvā tu yatkṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ koṭikoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 141 \|\|*

141\. That merit done (i.e. collected) by eating the best and purest food, moistened with hot rice is crore-fold.

## \|\| 48.142-146 \|\|

*anyaccāpi ca yaddravyaṃ haviṣyaṃ śāstranirmitam \|*  
*tadbhuktavā yatkṛtaṃ karma sarvaṃ lakṣaguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 142 \|\|*

*nirāmiṣaṃ ca yatkiṃcittasmādyadyatphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*tasmādgauḥ sarvakāryeṣu śasta eko yugeyuge \|\| 143 \|\|*

*sarvadā sarvakāmeṣu dharmakāmārthamokṣadaḥ \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*keṣu kiṃ vā prayogeṇa paraṃ puṇyaṃ prakīrtitaṃ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*vada tatsarvalokeśa yathā jānāmi tatvataḥ \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*sakṛtpradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā godhanaṃ cābhivaṃdayet \|\| 145 \|\|*

*sarvapāpairvinirmuktaḥ svargaṃ cākṣayamaśnute \|*  
*surācāryo yathā vaṃdyaḥ pūjyosau mādhavo yathā \|\| 146 \|\|*

142-143a. All acts done after having eaten even other food, which is made fit for oblations by the sacred precepts, would be a lakh times more effective than the fruit one would get from whatever is vegetarian food.

143b-144a. Therefore a bull alone is recommended for all acts in every yuga. In all desired objects he always is the giver of the (fruit of) pious acts, love of worldly prosperity and sensual enjoyments and salvation.

Nārada said:

144b-145a. O lord of all worlds, tell me, so that I follow correctly: In (the performance of) whichacts or by (following) which procedure great merit is known to follow?

Brahma said:

145b-146. Having gone round once, a man should salute the wealth in the form of kine. Being free from all sins he obtains heaven for ever. As the preceptor of gods is adorable or as Viṣṇu is adorable (so is a bull).

## \|\| 48.147-148 \|\|

*saptapradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā caiśvaryātpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*kalya utthāya gomadhye pātraṃ gṛhya sahodakam \|\| 147 \|\|*

*niṣiṃcedyo gavāṃ śṛṃgaṃ mastakenaiva tajjalam \|*  
*pratīccheta nirāhārastasya puṇyaṃ nibodhata \|\| 148 \|\|*

147-148. Indra went round him seven times in grandeur. Listen to the religious merit of him, who, observing a fast, and having got up at day-break, takes a pot with water (and moves) among bulls, and sprinkles the water on the bull’s horns and then receives it on his head.

## \|\| 48.149-153 \|\|

*śrūyaṃte yāni tīrthāni triṣu lokeṣu nārada \|*  
*siddhacāraṇayuktāni sevitāni maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

*abhiṣekassamasteṣāṃ gavāṃ śṛṃgodakasya ca \|*  
*prātarutthāya yo martyaḥ spṛśedgāṃ ca ghṛtaṃ madhu \|\| 150 \|\|*

*sarṣapāṃśca priyaṃgūṃśca kalmaṣātpratimucyate \|*  
*ghṛtakṣīrapradā gāvo ghṛtayonyo ghṛtodbhavāḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

*ghṛtanadyo ghṛtāvartāstā me saṃtu sadā gṛhe \|*  
*ghṛtaṃ me sarvagātreṣu ghṛtaṃ me manasi sthitam \|\| 152 \|\|*

*gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvaḥ pṛṣṭhata eva ca \|*  
*gāvaśca sarvagātreṣu gavāṃmadhye vasāmyaham \|\| 153 \|\|*

149-150a. The bath taken at the places known to be sacred and thronged by Siddhas and Cāraṇas and resorted to by great sages, is equal to the sprinkling done with the water from a cow’s horn.

150b-151a. That mortal, who, having got up in the morning, would touch a cow, ghee, honey, mustard and priyaṅgu (i.e. saffron) gets free from sin.

151b-153. ‘Cows are the givers of ghee and milk; they are the source of ghee; ghee is their product; they are the rivers of ghee, and the eddies of ghee. Let them always remain in my house. Ghee (remains) in all my limbs, ghee resides in my mind. Cows are always in front of me and behind me. Cows are (present) in all (my) limbs; I live among cows.’

## \|\| 48.154 \|\|

*ityācamya japenmaṃtraṃ sāyaṃprātaridaṃ śuciḥ \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayastasya svarloke pūjito bhavet \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. All the sin of him, who, (every) morning and evening, having sipped water, recites this sacred hymn, perishes; and he is adored in heaven.

## \|\| 48.155 \|\|

*yathā gauśca tathā vipro yathāviprastathā hariḥ \|*  
*hariryathā tathā gaṃgā etena hyavṛṣāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. As is the bull, so is a brāhmaṇa; as is a brāhmaṇa, so is Hari, so is the Ganges; these are not said to be non-bulls.

## \|\| 48.156 \|\|

*gāvo baṃdhurmanuṣyāṇāṃ manuṣyā bāṃdhavā gavām \|*  
*gauśca yasmingṛhe nāsti tadbaṃdhurahitaṃ gṛham \|\| 156 \|\|*

156\. Bulls are the kinsmen of men; men are the kinsmen of bulls. That house in which there is no bull is without kinsmen.

## \|\| 48.157 \|\|

*gomukhe cāśritā vedāḥ saṣaḍaṃgapadakramāḥ \|*  
*śṛṃgayośca sthitau nityaṃ sahaiva harikeśavau \|\| 157 \|\|*

157\. The Vedas with their six limbs and the pada and krama, reside in the mouth of cow. On the horns Hari and Keśava always stay together.

## \|\| 48.158 \|\|

*udare'vasthitaḥ skaṃdaḥ śīrṣe brahmā sthitaḥ sadā \|*  
*vṛṣaddhvajo lalāṭe ca śṛṃgāgra iṃdra eva ca \|\| 158 \|\|*

158\. In the belly lives Skanda; and Brahmā always remains in the head. Śaṅkara lives in the forehead and Indra on the tip of the horn.

## \|\| 48.159-168 \|\|

*karṇayoraśvinau devau cakṣuṣośśaśibhāskarau \|*  
*daṃteṣu garuḍo devo jihvāyāṃ ca sarasvatī \|\| 159 \|\|*

*apāne sarvatīrthāni prasrāve caiva jāhnavī \|*  
*ṛṣayo romakūpeṣu mukhataḥ pṛṣṭhato yamaḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

*dhanado varuṇaścaiva dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvamāśritau \|*  
*vāmapārśve sthitā yakṣāstejasvaṃto mahābalāḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

*mukhamadhye ca gaṃdharvā nāsāgre pannagāstathā \|*  
*khurāṇāṃ paścime pārśve'psarasaśca samāśritāḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

*gomaye vasate lakṣmīrgomūtre sarvamaṃgalā \|*  
*pādāgre khecarā vedyā haṃbhāśabde prajāpatiḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

*catvāraḥ sāgarāḥ pūrṇā dhenūnāṃ ca staneṣu vai \|*  
*gāṃ ca spṛśati yo nityaṃ snāto bhavati nityaśaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*ato martyaḥ prapuṣṭaistu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*gavāṃ rajaḥ khuroddhūtaṃ śirasā yastu dhārayet \|\| 165 \|\|*

*sa ca tīrthajale snātaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*nārada uvāca \|*  
*gavāṃ ca daśavarṇānāṃ kasya dāne ca kiṃphalam \|\| 166 \|\|*

*brūhi tattvaṃ guruśreṣṭha parameṣṭhinpriyaṃ yadi \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*śvetāṃ gāṃ brāhmaṇe datvā mānavaśceśvaro bhavet \|\| 167 \|\|*

*prāsāde vasate nityaṃ bhogī ca sukhamedhate \|*  
*dhūmrā tu svargakāṃtāra saṃsāre pāpamokṣiṇī \|\| 168 \|\|*

159-164a. The deities, Aśvins, live in the ears; the Moon and the Sun live in the eyes. God Garuḍa lives in the teeth, and Sarasvatī in the tongue. All the sacred places remain in the anus, and the Ganges in the urine. The sages live in the pores of the skin, and Yama lives in the backside of the face. Kubera and Varuṇa have resorted to the right side; the lustrous and very powerful Yakṣas reside in the left side. Gandharvas reside in the centre of the face, and the serpents on the tip of the nose. The celestial nymphs have resorted to the hind parts of the hoofs. The all-auspicious Lakṣmī resides in the cow-dung and cow-urine. Those who move in the sky reside on the tips of the feet; Prajāpati lives in the bellowing sound. The full four oceans reside in the udders of the cows.

164b-166a. A mortal who everyday bathes and touches a cow, gets relieved from all major sins. He who holds by (i.e. on) his head the dust raised by the hoofs of the cows, has (indeed) bathed in all the sacred places and is free from all sins.

Nārada said:

166b-167a. O best of preceptors, O Brahman, if you like, (please) tell me which fruit is obtained by presenting which (kind of) cow out of the cows of ten colours.

Brahmā said:

167b-168a. By giving a white cow to a brāhmaṇa, a man becomes wealthy. He always lives in a palace, and enjoying pleasure, becomes happy.

168b. A grey cow (i.e. presenting a grey cow) relieves (a man) from sins in (this) wilderness of the mundane existence and (takes him to) heaven.

## \|\| 48.169 \|\|

*akṣayaṃ kapilādānaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ datvā na sīdati \|*  
*pāṃḍurā durlabhā loke gaurī ca kulanaṃdinī \|\| 169 \|\|*

169\. The gift of a tawny cow (gives) an inexhaustible (fruit). By giving a black cow, a man does not sink. A yellowish white cow is difficult to get in the world. A yellowish cow delights the family.

## \|\| 48.170 \|\|

*raktākṣī rūpakāmasya dhanakāmasya nīlikā \|*  
*ekāṃ ca kapilāṃ datvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. A cow (i.e. the gift of a cow) with red eyes (is recommended) for (a man) who desires handsomeness. A black cow (i.e. the gift of a black cow) (is recommended) for (a man) who desires wealth. By presenting only a tawny cow a man is free from all sins.

## \|\| 48.171-177 \|\|

*yattu bālyakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yauvane vārdhake kṛtam \|*  
*vācākṛtaṃ karmakṛtaṃ manasā yatpraciṃtitaṃ \|\| 171 \|\|*

*agamyāgamanaṃ caiva mitradrohe ca pātakam \|*  
*mānakūṭaṃ tulākūṭaṃ kanyānṛtaṃ gavānṛtam \|\| 172 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ ca nāśayetkṣipraṃ kapilāṃ yaḥ prayacchati \|*  
*daśayojanavistīrṇā mahāpārā mahānadī \|\| 173 \|\|*

*nārā ca jalakāṃtāre prasṛte codakārṇave \|*  
*yāvadvatsasya dvau pādau mukhaṃ yāvanna jāyate \|\| 174 \|\|*

*tāvadgauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muṃcati \|*  
*suvarṇaśṛṃgīṃ vastrāḍhyāṃ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitām \|\| 175 \|\|*

*tāmrapṛṣṭhīṃ raupyakhurāṃ tathā kāṃsyopadohanām \|*  
*śobhitāṃ gaṃdhapuṣpaiśca sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitāṃ \|\| 176 \|\|*

*īdṛśīṃ kapilāṃ dadyāddvijātau vedapārage \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayastasya viṣṇuloke'cyuto bhavet \|\| 177 \|\|*

171-173a. All the sin, such as committed in childhood, youth or old age, or by words, deeds, or conceived by mind, and the sin due to cohabitation with one with whom it is prohibited, or the sin of treachery towards a friend, and also (the sin due to) fraud in measuring or weighing, or falsehood with reference to a girl or a cow, of him, who presents a tawny cow, perishes.

173b-175a. A cow should be looked upon as the earth, having a big river extending over ten yojanas, and having large banks, with water-elephants in the water-forest—the extended ocean of water—as long as she does not release her embryo (i.e. does not bring forth a calf)—as long as the two feet and the face of the calf have not come out.

175b-1 77. A man should give a tawny cow with golden horns, endowed (decorated) with a piece of cloth and with all ornaments, with a reddish back, silver hoofs and bell-metal udders, adorned with sandal and flowers and with all ornaments, to a brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas. All his sins perish, and he does not fall from the world (i.e. heaven) of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 48.178 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tu duhyamānāyāṃ bhūmau pataṃti biṃdavaḥ \|*  
*ārāmādi vijāyaṃte bahupuṣpaphalottamāḥ \|\| 178 \|\|*

178\. When she is being milked drops (of milk) fall on the earth. (From them) excellent gardens with many flowers, are produced.

## \|\| 48.179 \|\|

*yatra kāmaphalā vṛkṣā nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ \|*  
*prāsādāścāpi sauvarṇāstatra gacchaṃti gopradāḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

179\. Those who give cows (to brāhmaṇas) go there, where there are desire-yielding trees, where the rivers have thick milk, and where there are golden palaces also.

## \|\| 48.180 \|\|

*daśadhenūśca yo dadyādekaṃ caiva dhuraṃdharaṃ \|*  
*samānaṃ tu phalaṃ proktaṃ brahmaṇā samudāhṛtam \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. Brahmā has said that the fruit is the same (to him) who gives ten cows or one bull.

## \|\| 48.181 \|\|

*ekaṃ ca daśabhirdadyātsahasrāṇāṃ śataṃ phalam \|*  
*tasyānusārato vedyaṃ phalaṃ nārada yatnataḥ \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. He should give one (bull) with ten (cows); the fruit of giving thousand is hundred (-fold). O Nārada, the fruit is to be carefully understood accordingly.

## \|\| 48.182 \|\|

*pitṝnuddiśya yaḥ putro vṛṣaṃ ca mokṣayedbhuvi \|*  
*pitaro viṣṇulokeṣu mahīyaṃte yathepsitam \|\| 182 \|\|*

182\. The ancestors of that son, who releases a bull on the earth dedicating it to those manes, are honoured in Viṣṇu’s world (i.e. heaven) as desired (by them).

## \|\| 48.183 \|\|

*catasro vatsataryaśca ekasyaiva vṛṣasya ca \|*  
*mokṣyaṃte sarvataḥ putra vidhireṣa sanātanaḥ \|\| 183 \|\|*

183\. Four weaned female calves for one bull are released. O son, this is the old rule everywhere.

## \|\| 48.184 \|\|

*yāvaṃti caiva romāṇi tasya tāsāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaṃ bhujaṃti mānavāḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Men enjoy heaven for thousands of years i.e. for as many years as there are hairs on (the bodies of) them.

## \|\| 48.185 \|\|

*lāṃgūlena vṛṣo yacca jalaṃ cotkṣipati dhruvaṃ \|*  
*tattoyaṃ tu sahasrābdaṃ pitṝṇāmamṛtaṃ bhavet \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. That water which a bull tosses up with his tail would be (i.e. would serve as) nectar to the manes for a thousand years.

## \|\| 48.186 \|\|

*khureṇa karṣayedbhūmiṃ tato loṣṭhaṃ ca kardamaḥ \|*  
*pitṛbhyaśca svadhā tatra lakṣakoṭiguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. The ground or the clod that he tears—and also the mud (trodden by him) is Svadhā for the manes having a crore-fold effect.

## \|\| 48.187 \|\|

*vidyamāne ca janake yadi mātā vinaśyati \|*  
*caṃdanenāṃkitā dhenustasyāḥ svargāya dīyate \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. If a man’s father is alive, (but) his mother is dead, a cow marked with sandal is given for her (going to the) heaven (i.e. the gift of such a cow takes the mother to heaven).

## \|\| 48.188 \|\|

*dātā caiva pitṝṇāṃ ca ṛṇaṃ caiva pramuṃcati \|*
